items.title: Wear seat belts, both in the front and back seats
items.core: Wear seat belts in the front seat of a car, and the probability of being killed in a car accident is reduced by more than 40%. Riding in the front seat of a light truck costs 60% less. Half of the people who died in cars in the United States in 2022 were not wearing belts.
body: Cost: No money. It takes an extra 2 seconds each time you get in the car.

Benefits: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) estimates that wearing seat belts reduces the risk of fatal injury to front-seat passengers in cars by 45%. The front row of light trucks is down 60 percent. Among the people who died in passenger cars (cars carrying people) in the United States in 2022, 50% were found to be wearing belts or not. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), seat belts reduce the risk of death for vehicle occupants by up to 50%. The WHO estimates that 248,099 people will die in road traffic accidents in China in 2021, equivalent to 17.4 deaths per 100,000 people. According to the yearbook of the National Bureau of Statistics, 62,218 people died in road traffic accidents in 2021
Level of Evidence: A

Source: NHTSA (2024). Occupant Protection in Passenger Vehicles: 2022 Data (DOT HS 813 573): “Among killed passenger vehicle occupants with known restraint use, 48 percent of those in the front row and 60 percent of those in the second row were unrestrained.》<https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/ViewPublication/813573> ; WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. <https://ghoapi.azureedge.net/api/RS_196?$filter=SpatialDim%20eq%20%27CHN%27> ; National Bureau of Statistics (2022). China Statistical Yearbook 2022, Table 24-5 Road traffic accidents (2021): 62,218 fatalities. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/ndsj/2022/html/C24-05.jpg>

Note: The rear row must also be tied. In the same report, it was found that 60% of the deceased in the second row were not wearing belts. The two figures of 45% and 60% are estimates calculated by the U.S. Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) using the accident database (cited in Kahane 2015). They were not randomized trials. The number of deaths in China calculated by the WHO is about four times the 62,218 people in the statistical yearbook. The scope of statistics on both sides is different, and only the WHO caliber is used here.

Case: A family took a car back to their hometown on the weekend. The driver reminded the children and the elderly in the back seat to fasten their seat belts. On the way, he was rear-ended by a car from behind. The occupants of the car did not hit the front row and only suffered minor scratches.

items.title: Wear a helmet and buckle it up when riding a motorcycle or electric bicycle
items.core: When a motorcycle rider has an accident, wearing a helmet and buckling it up has significantly fewer deaths and head injuries. The buckle should be fastened tightly, not hanging loosely on the head is not considered wearing.
body: Cost: 100 to 300 yuan to buy one. Spend 5 seconds putting it on each time.

Benefit: Cochrane combines multiple studies together. Motorcyclists who wear helmets experience significantly fewer deaths and head injuries. The odds ratio for death was 0.58 (OR 0.58), confidence range 95% CI 0.50 to 0.68. The odds ratio for head injury was 0.31 (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.38)
Level of Evidence: A
Source: Liu BC et al (2008). Helmets for preventing injury in motorcycle riders. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004333.pub3>

Remarks: The helmet must be fastened, and hanging on the handlebars does not count as wearing. The data above is from motorcycles. There is no direct study on electric bicycles, but they are pushed here because the head injuries after a collision are the same. Wearing a helmet when skiing, snowboarding, and biking is described in Section 22, Article 12 (Wearing a helmet when skiing and mountain biking). The age threshold for children to ride on the road is set out in Section 30, Article 20 (Passengers under 16 years of age riding electric bicycles on the road).

Case: Takeaway riders deliver food on a rainy day and tighten their helmet straps before going out. He fell while trying to avoid a car that suddenly opened its door at an intersection. His helmet did not fly off. He only suffered scratches and continued to work the next day.

items.title: Install smoke alarms; install carbon monoxide alarms if you burn coal or gas for heating indoors in winter
items.core: If you have a functioning smoke alarm at home, fewer people will die in residential fires. In 40% of residential fires in the United States that killed people, people were sleeping when the fire started. If you burn coal or gas in the house in winter, add a carbon monoxide alarm. In China, 11,500 people died of carbon monoxide poisoning in 2018, and about 70% of them died at home during the three months of winter.
body: Cost: A smoke alarm costs 30 to 100 yuan. A carbon monoxide alarm costs 50 to 150 yuan. After installation, replace the battery once a year.

Benefits: North Carolina in the United States studied a number of residential fires and compared the families that were involved in the accident with those that were not. With a functioning smoke alarm in your home, significantly fewer people die in a fire. The odds ratio for death was 0.39 (OR 0.39), confidence range 95% CI 0.18 to 0.83. In the United States, 24% of fatal fires in occupied homes from 2018 to 2020 did not have smoke alarms, and 41% occurred while people were sleeping when the fire started. China reported 11,523 deaths from carbon monoxide poisoning in 2018. Of these deaths, 72.59% in December, 67.42% in January, and 66.48% in February occurred at home
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Marshall SW et al (1998). Fatal residential fires: who dies and who survives? JAMA. <https://www.usfa.fema.gov/downloads/pdf/statistics/v22i2.pdf> ; You J et al (2020). Number of Deaths due to Carbon Monoxide Poisoning by Month and by Place of Death — China, 2018. China CDC Weekly. <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2020.008>

Remarks: To B The reason: There is only one study on smoke alarms. The method was to compare households with and without accidents. It was not a randomized trial. Carbon monoxide alarms themselves have not been studied to reduce mortality. The income here is derived based on "poisoning deaths are concentrated in winter and at home".

Case: Northern residents use gas for heating in winter, install smoke alarms in bedrooms, and install carbon monoxide alarms next to the furnace. Insufficient combustion triggered the alarm at night, and the family immediately closed the valves and opened the windows to evacuate, thus avoiding poisoning.

items.title: Replace gas hoses and stoves when due. If you do not change the pipes yourself, the gas company can directly refuse the door-to-door sales
items.core: Replace hoses and stoves when due. This is the user's obligation stated in the "Urban Gas Management Regulations". Changing pipes and dismantling gas meters by yourself is expressly prohibited by regulations. The same regulation also states that gas companies cannot require you to buy products and services specified by it. If you come to the door and say "you must change", you can directly refuse.
body: Cost: A few dozen yuan for a compliant gas hose. The stove should be replaced every few years. When changing, check to see if it has expired.

Benefits: The regulations make it the user's obligation to "timely replace gas burning appliances and connecting pipes that are obsolete by the state or have expired": you must replace stoves and hoses when they reach their expiration date or are eliminated by the state. The regulations also list "unauthorized installation, modification, and dismantling of indoor gas facilities and gas metering devices" as prohibited activities, including modifying pipelines and dismantling gas meters by yourself. The regulations also clarify that gas operators shall not require users to purchase products designated by it, nor require users to accept services provided by it
Evidence level: C

Source: State Council (2010). Urban Gas Management Regulations (State Council Order No. 583 No.) Article 27: "Gas users should abide by the rules for safe gas use, use qualified gas burning appliances and gas cylinders, and promptly replace gas burning appliances, connecting pipes, etc. that have been eliminated by the state or have expired."; Article 28 prohibited behaviors include "(1) Operating public gas valves without authorization" "(2) Using gas pipelines as load-bearing brackets or grounding leads" "( 4) Installing, modifying, or dismantling indoor gas facilities and gas metering devices without authorization"; Article 20: Gas operators shall not "(6) require gas users to purchase their designated products or accept the services they provide"; Article 29: Users may complain to gas management and other departments regarding charges and services, and "the relevant departments shall handle the complaint within 15 working days from the date of receipt of the complaint." <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2010/content_1758214.htm>; Shenzhen Municipal Housing and Construction Bureau (2024). Tips on safe gas use (2): "Turn off the main gas valve at home immediately" "Open doors and windows quickly for ventilation" "Be sure not to turn on or off lights, range hoods and other electrical appliances at home" "People should evacuate quickly, move to a safe place, and call the gas company's alarm number in a timely manner". <https://zjj.sz.gov.cn/zcjzts/content/post_11882410.html>; Zhangjiagang Emergency Management Bureau (2024). Gas safety usage knowledge: "Don't turn on the exhaust fan for ventilation in a hurry" "You should stay away from the scene before calling for help." <https://www.zjg.gov.cn/zjgszwz/yjaqzs/202411/72b4fad7399c48378302460c6ce2d55b.shtml>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Gas appliance product quality and safety risk warning (reprinted by Ezhou Urban Construction Committee): "Users are encouraged to install and use gas smart meters, gas leakage safety protection devices, self-closing valves, independent smoke fire detectors, combustible gas detection alarms and other protection devices." <https://cjw.ezhou.gov.cn/zxzx/gzdt/202308/t20230821_569108.html>

Note: The original text of the regulations can be verified word for word, but it only states that it is your obligation to change the pipe when it is due, and does not explain how many accidents can be avoided by changing it. There is no official statistics on how much gas accidents can be reduced by pipe replacement based on age, so we only give it a C grade. The person who comes to the door for security inspection asks you to buy the self-closing valve and alarm specified by him. You can refuse, or you can complain, because Article 20, Item 6 of the Regulations does not allow the gas company to make such a request. Self-closing valves and alarms themselves are encouraged to be installed by the State Administration for Market Regulation. If you want to install them, you must choose qualified products yourself. If you smell gas, first turn off the main gas valve, and for bottled gas, turn off the cylinder valve. Open doors and windows for ventilation, but don't turn on the exhaust fan. Do not turn on or off electrical appliances such as lights and range hoods, and do not touch lighters. Then the people evacuated, left the scene and called the gas company's police. Carbon monoxide poisoning is another matter, see Section 13.

Case: The old man’s gas hose has been used for many years. After checking the service life, his son asked for regular repair and replacement, and refused the high-priced stove specified by the door-to-door personnel. Later inspection revealed that the old pipe was cracked and leaking.

items.title: If you don’t pick, buy, or eat wild mushrooms, any “indigenous identification methods” will not be valid
items.core: In 2025 alone, the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention investigated 828 cases of mushroom poisoning, 2,165 people were infected, and 13 people died. That year also saw the identification of 34 new species of mushrooms that had not previously been documented to be poisonous. Silver needles test for poison, bugs are not poisonous if eaten, and they are poisonous only if they are brightly colored. None of these are true.
body: Cost: No money. The hard part is giving up a seasonal game meat.

Benefits: The Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention investigated 828 cases of mushroom poisoning in 2025, involving 2,165 people and 13 deaths. The case fatality rate is 0.6%, which means that 0.6% of people who are poisoned die. From 276 to 676 cases per year from 2019 to 2024, the case fatality rate ranges from 0.87% to 2.86%. In 2025 alone, 138 species of poisonous mushrooms were identified, 34 of which were recorded in the country for the first time as causing poisoning. The popular science of the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention has rejected the folk identification method one by one. Only brightly colored ones are poisonous: Wrong, whether they are poisonous or not has nothing to do with color. Those that have been eaten by bugs and have maggots are not poisonous: Wrong, many highly poisonous mushrooms will also be eaten by bugs when they mature. Poisonous substances that will change color when cooked with silverware and garlic: Wrong, mushroom toxins do not contain sulfur, and silver needles turn black due to sulfur. High-temperature frying can remove toxins: it’s not reliable either. It concluded that "there is currently no simple, easy, fast and effective way to identify whether mushrooms are poisonous". The 2026 reminder from the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation is that if you feel unwell after ingestion, "please seek medical attention immediately and do not handle it yourself." Keep the remaining mushrooms and food residues to facilitate doctors to identify poisons
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Mushroom Poisoning Outbreaks — China, 2025. China CDC Weekly (2026): "In 2025, China CDC investigated 828 mushroom poisoning incidents across 27 provincial-level administrative divisions (PLADs), affecting 2,165 individuals and causing 13 deaths - a case fatality rate of 0.6%, the lowest of the past six years. In total, 138 poisonous mushroom species were identified, including 34 newly recorded in poisoning incidents in China. "From 2019 to 2024, the annual number of incidents ranged from 276 to 676, and the case fatality rate ranged from 0.87% to 2.86%." <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2026.120>; 2024 Annual Report of the same issue <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2025.106>; Institute of Occupational Health, Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention Yin Yu, Li Haijiao (2019). There is still a long way to go to prevent and control mushroom poisoning: "Method 4: Mushrooms that eat insects or maggots are not poisonous. Wrong!" "Method 6: Mushrooms that can change color by cooking them with silverware, green onions, garlic, and rice are poisonous. Wrong!" "Therefore, there is currently no simple, easy, fast and effective way to identify whether mushrooms are poisonous." <https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkkp/zyjk/zdzs/201908/t20190802_301109.html>; Beijing Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2023). Stay away from poisonous mushrooms and do not be a "mushroom warrior": "The folk methods of identifying poisonous mushrooms, such as looking at the color and shape, looking at the growth environment, using silverware to identify poisons, looking at secretions, looking for maggots and insects, etc. are all unreliable." <https://www.bjcdc.org/cdcmodule/jkfw/yyyspjk/jkyf/swzdyf/2023/35518.shtml>; Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (2026). Tips on preventing the risk of poisoning by accidentally eating wild mushrooms: "Please seek medical attention immediately and do not handle it yourself to avoid delaying diagnosis and treatment. Properly preserve samples of remaining wild mushrooms, food residues, etc." <https://scjgj.beijing.gov.cn/zwxx/scjgdt/202606/t20260625_4715961.html>

Note: If you suspect you have eaten something wrong, go to the hospital immediately. Do not deal with it at home. Bring leftover mushrooms, food scraps, or photos you’ve taken. There are several types of poisonous mushroom poisoning. Doctors can identify the type of mushroom and treat it accordingly. Every year, new species are recorded that can poison people, so the premise that "locals recognize them clearly" itself is untenable. Silver needles are used to detect poisons, boiling with garlic, bugs are not poisonous after being eaten, and they are poisonous only if they are brightly colored. These statements are all untrue. Fungus and white fungus that have been soaked for too long and wet rice noodles that have been left out for a long time are another poison, see Article 48 (Soaked fungus).

Case: During an outing, my colleague picked wild mushrooms that were not brightly colored and said that they were not poisonous if they were bitten by insects. Instead of cooking, everyone ate mushrooms from the supermarket. Later, many people in that mountain were poisoned, but they escaped.

items.title: Electric bicycles do not push down the corridor, do not enter the elevator, and do not charge at home
items.core: Parking or charging electric vehicles in the foyers, walkways, or stairwells of high-rise residences is expressly prohibited by Department of Emergency Management regulations. Those who fail to make corrections will be fined 500 to 1,000 yuan for individuals, and 2,000 to 10,000 yuan for businesses. The fine is a trivial matter, but the important thing is that these places are exactly the way to evacuate and escape in the event of a fire.
body: Cost: Nothing. The difficult part is that every time I park at the centralized charging point downstairs, I have to walk dozens of meters more.

Benefits: The regulations of the Department of Emergency Management expressly prohibit: "It is prohibited to park or charge electric bicycles in public foyers, evacuation corridors, stairwells, and emergency exits of high-rise civil buildings." Neither parking nor charging is allowed in the foyer, walkways, stairwells, and emergency exits of the building. Those who refuse to make corrections will be fined 500 to 1,000 yuan for units and individuals not doing business, and 2,000 to 10,000 yuan for doing business. This regulation does not cover elevators and rooms. The Ministry of Emergency Management said in a reply to the National People's Congress deputies that illegal parking and charging of electric vehicles and batteries indoors should be listed as a key focus of rectification of major fire hazards. What it reminds the society is the dangers of "cars entering the building, wires leaving the home, and self-demolition and modification". Elevators are regulated by local laws: Beijing will ban electric bicycles and rechargeable batteries from being brought into elevator cars from May 1, 2025. Individuals who refuse to correct will be fined 500 to 1,000 yuan.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Emergency Management (2021). Regulations on Fire Safety Management of High-Rise Civil Buildings (Ministry of Emergency Management Order No. 5, Articles 37 and 47). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-08/01/content_5628815.htm>; Ministry of Emergency Management (2023). Letter regarding the reply to Proposal No. 00969 of the Fifth Session of the 13th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference: "In 2021, a total of 18,000 electric bicycle fires were reported across the country, causing 65 deaths, 222 injuries, and direct property losses of 221 million yuan, of which 3,782 occurred in buildings, causing 60 deaths and 175 injuries." <https://www.mem.gov.cn/gk/jytabljggk/zxwytadfzy/2022zx/202301/t20230119_440918.shtml>; Ministry of Emergency Management (2025). Press conference on January 15, 2025: "The number of fires per million electric bicycles dropped from 5.6 in 2023 to 3, the number of fires dropped by 42.2% year-on-year, and the number of casualties dropped by more than 90%." <https://www.mem.gov.cn/xw/xwfbh/2025n01y15xwfbh_6337/>; Ministry of Emergency Management (2024). Reply to Recommendation No. 7187 of the First Session of the 14th National People's Congress: "Illegal parking or charging of electric vehicles (battery) indoors, failure to set up fire protection zones as required, etc., as the focus of the 2023 special investigation and rectification of major fire safety risks and hidden dangers" "Promote to the public the fire hazards of "cars entering the building, wires leaving the house, and self-demolition and modification"." <https://www.mem.gov.cn/gk/jytabljggk/rddbjydfzy/2023_5984/202401/t20240130_476731.shtml>; Reprinted by Beijing Dongcheng District People’s Government, Beijing Fire Protection (2025). Beijing Fire Regulations: If electric bicycles or batteries enter the elevator, an individual may be fined up to 1,000 yuan: "It is prohibited to bring electric bicycles and rechargeable batteries into the elevator car. If the violation is refused to be corrected, the unit may be fined not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan, and the individual may be fined not less than 500 yuan but not more than 1,000 yuan." <https://www.bjdch.gov.cn/ztzl/aqsczbgjsnxd/zdgz/202504/t20250410_4061604.html>

Note: Don’t buy modified batteries, don’t use off-brand chargers, and don’t leave them charging all night. Once a lithium battery catches fire, the entire piece will boil within tens of seconds, and highly toxic smoke will emit at the same time. If a car catches fire while parked in the corridor, the path you take to escape will be burned downstairs. Figures released by the Department of Emergency Management are that there were 18,000 e-bike fires nationwide in 2021, killing 65 people. Among them, 3,782 were burned in buildings, and 60 people died, almost all of them indoors. After rectification in 2024, the number of fires dropped by 42.2% compared with the previous year, and casualties dropped by more than 90%. Fires per million vehicles fell from 5.6 to 3. The press conference did not give an absolute number for the whole year.

Case: Residents of the community parked their electric vehicles in the charging shed downstairs and did not push them upstairs. At night, a battery in the building next door caught fire in the corridor. The stairs were blackened by smoke. However, the passageway to the building where his house was located was clear and the residents were evacuated smoothly.

items.title: Take your blood pressure and if it’s high, take medicine to bring it down to the standard
items.core: For every 10 mmHg drop in high blood pressure, the probability of major cardiovascular problems drops by 20%, and the risk of stroke drops by 27%. Heart failure was reduced by 28%, and the probability of death was reduced by 13%. Among Chinese people aged 35 to 75, 44.7% have high blood pressure, and only 7.2% have it under control.
body: Cost: 100 to 200 yuan for an electronic blood pressure monitor. Measure once for 1 minute. Most antihypertensive drugs cost a few yuan to dozens of yuan per month. The difficult part is to continue eating even if you don’t have symptoms.

Gains: 123 trials, more than 610,000 people combined. For every 10 mmHg decrease in systolic blood pressure, major cardiovascular events are reduced by approximately 20%. Original value RR 0.80, confidence range 95% CI 0.77 to 0.83. Systolic blood pressure is the two-digit higher blood pressure. Stroke (stroke) was about 27% lower (RR 0.73). Heart failure was about 28% lower (RR 0.72). Overall mortality decreased by 13% (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.84 to 0.91). China has screened 1.7 million people aged 35 to 75: 44.7% had high blood pressure. Among these people, 44.7% knew they had it, 30.1% were in treatment, and only 7.2% had it under control.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ettehad D et al (2016). Blood pressure lowering for prevention of cardiovascular disease and death: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32478-9>

Note: Take your blood pressure first. Less than 1 out of 10 people in China who have high blood pressure have it under control, so taking this measure is one of the most cost-effective actions in this book. There is still discussion on how low the blood pressure should be to reach the standard (130 or 140), but the matter of "knowing one's high blood pressure and lowering it" itself is not controversial.

Case: A middle-aged man’s blood pressure was found to be 158 during a physical examination at work. After that, he regularly measured his blood pressure at home every week and took medicine according to the doctor’s instructions to reduce his high blood pressure to about 130. Two years later, the reexamination indicators were stable, and doctors found no heart or brain damage.

items.title: After the age of 35, as long as you are overweight, you should check your fasting blood sugar once. Normally, you should check again every three years.
items.core: Spending tens of dollars to draw a tube of blood can detect prediabetes without any symptoms. The official recommendation for screening in the United States is that people aged 35 to 70 who are overweight or obese should get tested. If it is found to be normal, it will be checked again every three years. In the United States, a body mass index of 25 is considered overweight. For Asians, it is reduced to 23. In China, a body mass index of 24 is considered overweight.
body: Cost: Fasting blood sugar is more than ten yuan. Glycated hemoglobin is tens of yuan. Just go to the hospital for a blood draw.

Benefits: The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force is the official U.S. agency that recommends screening. Its current recommendation: Screen adults ages 35 to 70 who are overweight or obese for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, even if they don’t have any symptoms. Overweight refers to a body mass index of ≥25, and obesity refers to a body mass index of ≥30. For Asian Americans, it recommends lowering the cutoff to a body mass index of ≥23, because Asians have a higher risk of diabetes at the same body mass index. China's industry standard is: a body mass index between 24.0 and 28.0 is considered overweight, and a body mass index ≥28.0 is considered obese. The recommendation grade for this piece of advice is B. It also states: "Screening every 3 years is reasonable for normoglycemic adults."
Level of Evidence: A

Source: US Preventive Services Task Force (2021). Screening for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes. <https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/screening-for-prediabetes-and-type-2-diabetes>: "at a lower BMI (≥23) if the patient is Asian American"; General Office of the National Health Commission (2024). The core knowledge of resident weight management (2024 edition) explains: "According to the "Adult Weight Determination" (WS/T 428-2013) industry standard... 24.0≤BMI<28.0 is overweight, and BMI≥28.0 is obese." <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202407/P020240703481519509521.pdf>; Wang L et al (2021). Prevalence and Treatment of Diabetes in China, 2013-2018. JAMA: "In 2018, among adults with diabetes, 36.7% (95% CI, 34.7%-38.6%) reported being aware of their condition" "These rates did not change significantly from 2013." <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2021.22208>

Note: Being diagnosed with prediabetes does not mean that you need to take medicine. By eating less, moving more, and losing some weight, the risk of diabetes can be reduced by 30 to 60%. In a national survey in 2018, only 36.7% of Chinese adult patients with diabetes knew they had the disease, which was no significant improvement compared with 2013. Please see Section 2, Article 45 (Detection of Pre-Diabetes) for this drop and how to correct it and how often it needs to be reviewed after detection.

Case: A 38-year-old colleague’s body mass index was over 24. He had no symptoms such as thirst and frequent urination, but he still checked his fasting blood sugar and was found to have prediabetes. The doctor arranged for repeated examinations, and the index returned to the normal range six months later.

items.title: Don’t speed, don’t drink and drive, don’t look at your phone, and stop and take a rest when you feel sleepy.
items.core: For every 1% increase in average vehicle speed, the probability of crashing and killing someone increases by about 4%. There is no safe line for alcohol that says “a little bit is fine”. The risk of an accident is about 3.6 times higher when you are fiddling with your phone while driving than when you are concentrating on driving, and about 12.2 times when you are dialing a number. When you're visibly sleepy, the risk is about 3.4 times higher.
body: Cost: No money. Drive slower and take a few extra minutes each way. The difficult part is to drink less at dinner and not to read the news when it comes. Stop and rest for at least 20 minutes every 4 hours on long drives.

Benefit: According to the World Health Organization (WHO): for every 1% increase in average vehicle speed, the risk of fatal accidents increases by 4%. The risk of drunk driving increases from very low blood alcohol concentrations. The WHO also says that drivers who use mobile phones while driving are about four times more likely to be involved in an accident than those who do not, and using hands-free is not much safer. A US study installed cameras in the cars of more than 3,500 drivers and captured 905 accidents in which people were injured or their cars were damaged. The comparison was with driving clips while sober, attentive, and not drinking. The combined odds of having an accident with the various movements of the phone in hand were 3.6 (OR 3.6). Accident is a rare outcome, and the odds ratio and relative risk are similar. The odds ratios were 12.2 for dialing, 6.1 for typing a message, 4.8 for reaching for the phone, 2.7 for swiping the phone, and 2.2 for holding a phone call. Those who were obviously sleepy in the video had an odds ratio of 3.4 (OR 3.4)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet: "Drivers using mobile phones are approximately 4 times more likely to be involved in a crash than drivers not using a mobile phone." "Hands-free phones are not much safer than hand-held phone sets.》<https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traffic-injuries> ; Dingus TA et al. (2016). Driver crash risk factors and prevalence evaluation using naturalistic driving data. PNAS 113(10):2636-2641. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1513271113> ; Paragraph 2 of Article 22 of the Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (amended in 2021): "If excessive fatigue affects safe driving, no motor vehicle shall be driven"; Article 90: "A warning or a fine of not less than 20 yuan but not more than 200 yuan". <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab231eb017abd617ef70519>; Article 62 of the Implementation Regulations of the Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2017): Driving a motor vehicle shall not engage in "(3) Making and answering handheld phones, watching TV, etc. that hinders safe driving" and "(7) Driving a motor vehicle continuously for more than 4 hours without stopping to rest or stopping and resting for less than 20 minutes." <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f40f566c10e23> ; Ministry of Public Security (2021). Measures for the Management of Points for Road Traffic Safety Violations (Ministry of Public Security Order No. 163) Article 11: One demerit 3 Points include "(6) Driving a motor vehicle and making and answering hand-held phones and other behaviors that hinder safe driving" and "(14) Driving a truck continuously for more than 4 hours without stopping to rest or stopping and resting for less than 20 minutes." Article 9: 9 points are recorded at one time for "(7) Driving a medium-sized or larger passenger vehicle or dangerous goods transport vehicle for more than 4 hours without stopping or taking a rest for less than 20 minutes." <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5679697.htm>

Note: The 1% and 4% groups of speed and death are calculated based on the accident model and are not random group experiments. Regarding drunk driving, WHO only gave directions, not numbers. For the question "how much you drink, how much the risk increases", this section has not verified the original documents. The odds ratios between mobile phones and sleepiness are calculated as accidents that hurt people or crashed cars, not deaths. The control group is the "optimal driving state" that has been selected, so these numbers are higher than when compared with normal driving. The law governs making phone calls while holding the phone in hand, with a fine of 20 to 200 yuan and 3 points. It's not illegal to use a hands-free device, but the WHO says it's not much safer. It is also illegal to drive for more than 4 hours without taking a 20-minute break. Driving a truck will be worth 3 points, driving a medium-sized or larger passenger car or dangerous goods vehicle will be worth 9 points. If you feel sleepy, go into the service area and park your car to rest for a while. You may also feel drowsy after taking cold medicines or anti-allergy medicines containing chlorpheniramine or diphenhydramine. See Section 34, Article 12 (Chlorpheniramine). Always sleepy while driving and snoring loudly, see Section 3, Item 27 (Sleep Apnea).

Case: Before running a long distance, the driver put his mobile phone in the passenger seat, maintained the speed limit on the road, and did not touch a sip of wine after the meal. When I felt sleepy after driving, I went to the service area and slept for 20 minutes, and finally got home safely.

items.title: Use a safety seat for children under 4 years old when riding in a car, and do not hold them in your arms
items.core: Using a safety seat for babies under one year old when riding in a car is about 70% less likely to be fatally injured in a car accident. Children ages 1 to 4 are about half as low. Holding him in his arms has no such effect.
body: Cost: 300 to 2,000 yuan each, can be used for several years. Spend an extra minute strapping your child in every time you get in the car.

Benefits: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) estimates that using safety seats reduces the risk of fatal injury to infants under 1 year old in a car by 71%. The decline was 54% among young children aged 1 to 4 years. The World Health Organization (WHO) claims that infant deaths dropped by 71%
Level of Evidence: A
Source: NHTSA (2024). Occupant Protection in Passenger Vehicles: 2022 Data (DOT HS 813 573). <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traffic-injuries>

Note: Fix the seat according to the instructions. If it is installed incorrectly, it means it is not installed. For children under 1 year old, install it in reverse so that the child faces the rear of the vehicle. The above figures are estimated by U.S. officials based on accident data.

Case: A two-year-old child went on the highway with his parents, and his family members fastened him in the rear safety seat. Sudden braking in the lane next to the car caused a rear-end collision, and the luggage in the car flew into the front seat. The child was held firmly by the seat belt and was not injured.

items.title: If you have children at home, install limiters or guardrails on windows and balconies. Screen windows do not count as protection
items.core: A pair of limiters costs tens of dollars. New York City installed window guardrails for high-risk residents for free and provided door-to-door explanations. The number of reported child falls in one district dropped by half in three years. Later, New York simply enacted legislation requiring landlords to install guardrails in homes with children 10 years old and younger. Screens do not count as protection.
body: Cost: A few dozen yuan for a window limiter or child safety lock. Put it on for ten minutes.

Income: New York City has run a project called "Children Can't Fly" since 1972, which provides free window guardrails in high-risk urban areas and provides door-to-door explanations. The number of reported falls in the Bronx fell 50 percent from 1973 to 1975. Since then, New York City has amended its health code to force landlords to install window guards in apartments with children 10 years and younger
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Spiegel CN, Lindaman FC (1977). Children can't fly: a program to prevent childhood morbidity and mortality from window falls. American Journal of Public Health: "Significant reduction in falls resulted, particularly in the Bronx, where reported falls declined 50 percent from 1973 to 1975", the 1976 New York City Health Code amendment "to require that landlords provide window guards in apartments where children ten years old and younger reside". <https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.67.12.1143>; (2021). Unintentional Window Falls in Children and Adolescents. Academic Pediatrics: January 2007 to August 2017 Monthly National Electronic Injury Surveillance System 38,840 emergency department visits, "The majority of falls occurred in children under the age of 6 and were related to falls from a second story or below". <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.acap.2020.07.008>

Note: The above study was equipped with window guardrails. The limiter allows the window to be pushed open only a short distance. The principle is the same, but there is no separate research number. Do not place beds, sofas, boxes or other things that children can climb on near windows or balconies. The screen window only blocks mosquitoes and will fall off when pushed. Don't use it as a guardrail. It’s not just those who live in high-rise buildings who need to wear them: According to the US data, most falls occur on the second floor or lower. If a child falls down the stairs in a walker, see Section 20, Item 15 (Don’t buy a walker with wheels).

Case: There is a two-year-old child in a renting house. The parents installed limiters on the living room windows, guardrails on the balcony, and the screen windows are only used to prevent mosquitoes. The child was blocked when he climbed up the window sill to play and did not fall.

items.title: Keep children out of sight when near water, and wear life jackets when boating or swimming.
items.core: Wearing a lifejacket when you fall into the water on a boat is about half as likely to drown as not wearing one. Drowning is still the leading cause of death among children aged 1 to 14 in China. The drowning death rate in rural areas is approximately twice that of urban areas.
body: Cost: $50 to $200 for a life jacket. In addition, it is necessary to catch up on the attention of looking at the child.

Benefit: Research using U.S. Coast Guard data, comparing people with similar conditions. For people who fall into the water on a recreational boat, wearing a life jacket reduces the risk of drowning by about half. The original value was adjusted RR 0.51, confidence range 95% CI 0.35 to 0.74. China's drowning mortality rate for people under 20 years old dropped from 6.60 per 100,000 people in 2013 to 3.28 per 100,000 people in 2021. The rural area is about twice that of the urban area. In 2021, the rate was 3.84 per 100,000 people in rural areas and 2.01 in urban areas. Drowning remains the leading cause of death in children ages 1 to 14. The drowning death rate for 1 to 14 years old in 2021 was 3.23 per 100,000 people, which was 0.99 higher than the next highest number of road traffic injuries. In 2021, drowning accounted for 31.1% of injury deaths among those aged 0 to 19 years, and road traffic accounted for 27.9%. The highest drowning mortality rate is among those aged 15 to 19, at 3.95 per 100,000 people, including 5.99 males.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Cummings P et al (2011). Association between wearing a personal floatation device and death by drowning among recreational boaters. Injury Prevention. <https://doi.org/10.1136/ip.2010.028688> ; Li Z et al (2023). Unintentional Drowning Mortality Among Individuals Under Age 20 — China, 2013–2021. China CDC Weekly: "In China, it is deemed the primary cause of death for children between the ages of 1 and 14. According to 2021 data, the rate of unintentional drowning in this age group is 3.23 per 100,000, surpassing road traffic injuries, the second leading cause of fatalities, by 0.99 per 100,000." "rural areas exhibited roughly double the mortality rate found in urban areas". <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2023.198> ; Zhou J et al (2024). Injury Mortality of Children and Adolescents Aged 0–19 Years — China, 2010–2021. China CDC Weekly: "drowning and road traffic crashes were the top two causes of child injury deaths, explaing 31.1% and 27.9% of total injury deaths". <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2024.057>

Note: Level A only corresponds to this half of the life jacket. "Keep sight" is the consensus of everyone. In single calculation, it is only grade C. There is no random trial and there will never be in the future. Drowning deaths in China are concentrated in rural areas and among men aged 15 to 19 years. When playing on the ice in winter, see Article 41 (measure the thickness of the ice in the wild first).

Case: Taking a 6-year-old child for a picnic by the reservoir on the weekend, the parents always kept a close eye on the child and put on and fastened the life jacket before getting on the boat. The child slipped and fell into the water and was immediately pulled back to the boat without choking.

items.title: Over 60, practice balance and leg strength, renovate bathrooms and stairs at home
items.core: By practicing balance, such as Tai Chi, two or three times a week, the number of falls among elderly people is reduced by about 23%, and the number of falls is reduced by 15%. Having someone come to your home to assess and modify your home has reduced the number of falls by about 20%. Falls are the number one cause of injury death among people over 65 in China, and more than half of them occur in their own homes.
body: Cost: 30 minutes of Tai Chi or balance training two to three times a week. Bathroom anti-slip mats, handrails, and night lights cost tens to hundreds of dollars. The difficult part is to practice for a long time.

Yield: Cochrane combined 108 trials, 23,407 people. Exercise reduces falls in older adults by 23%. The original value was the ratio of fall rates, RaR 0.77, with a confidence range of 95% CI 0.71 to 0.83. The number of people who had a fall decreased by 15% (RR 0.85). Inviting people to do safety assessments and modifications at home reduced the fall rate by about 20% (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.97). Practicing Tai Chi reduces the risk of falling by approximately 29% (RR 0.71). Falls are the number one cause of injury death among people over 65 in China. In 2018, 55.97% of falls among the elderly occurred at home
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Sherrington C et al (2019). Exercise for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007146.pub3> ; Lu Z et al. (2021). Characteristics of Falls Among Older People — China, 2018. China CDC Weekly. <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2021.013>

Note: This applies to people over 60 who live in their own homes and not in nursing homes. The above study counts falls, not deaths. The journey from fall to hip fracture to death is short. If you can't see the road clearly, you will fall more often. If cataracts affect your vision, see Section 17, Article 9 (Cataract Surgery). If an old man is dragged down while taking his dog for a walk, see Section 17, Article 10 (Old Man Walking Dog). Whether bones can withstand being dropped, see Article 39 of this section (Bone Density Examination).

Case: 72-year-old Grandma Chen used to get up at night and often walk around in the dark, and the bathroom became slippery. After the community visited her for evaluation, handrails and non-slip mats were installed, and she practiced Tai Chi three times a week. I haven’t fallen once in half a year, and I feel much safer going to the bathroom by myself at night.

items.title: Check for two and a half hepatitis B, and judge whether to take up the vaccine based on the vaccination record
items.core: In the Qidong study, those who were vaccinated against hepatitis B at birth were 84% less likely to develop liver cancer later in life. Adults cannot copy this decrease, nor can they take three additional shots just because their antibodies are low. People who have completed the entire course, had protective antibodies, and have normal immunity usually do not need boosting. If you are not sure whether you have been vaccinated or not, bring the test sheet to the vaccination clinic for evaluation.
body: Cost: A check costs tens of dollars. For adults who need to be vaccinated, the total cost of 3 shots of hepatitis B vaccine is about 100 to 300 yuan, and the cost is determined by the local outpatient clinic. Usually given at 0, 1, and 6 months.

Benefits: The Qidong trial was randomized by group, not by individual, and followed for 30 years. Hepatitis B vaccination in newborns reduces primary liver cancer by 84%. The confidence range is 95% CI 23% to 97%. There was a 72% (95% CI 68% to 75%) decline in the positivity rate for the hepatitis B surface antigen HBsAg, which is the proportion of people who are found to have the virus. 67.8% of the control group received catch-up vaccinations between the ages of 10 and 14 years. The efficacy of follow-up vaccination on HBsAg positivity in early adulthood was only 21% (95% CI 10% to 30%), much weaker than vaccination at birth. The HBsAg-positive proportion of the entire population in China dropped by 52% from 1992 to 2014, and by 97% among those under 5 years old. These numbers cannot be directly applied to adult re-inoculation. People with normal immunity, who have completed the entire course and have produced protective antibodies will still have immune memory after the antibodies drop, and usually do not need to be boosted. Immune memory is the body's ability to quickly mobilize defenses when it encounters a virus again. Whether to re-vacculate should be judged based on vaccination records, surface antigens, surface antibodies and core antibodies. If the vaccination history is unclear, go to the vaccination clinic for evaluation.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Qu C et al (2014). Efficacy of neonatal HBV vaccination on liver cancer and other liver diseases over 30-year follow-up of the Qidong hepatitis B intervention study. PLoS Medicine: "The estimated efficacy of catch-up vaccination on HBsAg seroprevalence in early adulthood was 21% (95% CI 10%-30%), substantially weaker than that of the neonatal vaccination (72%, 95% CI 68%-75%).》<https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1001774> ; Cui F et al (2017). Prevention of Chronic Hepatitis B after 3 Decades of Escalating Vaccination Policy, China. Emerging Infectious Diseases. <https://doi.org/10.3201/eid2305.161477>; China Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Hepatitis B (Vaccine Immunization Prevention, FAQ No. 4). <https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkyj/mygh02/ymkyfjb/yxgy/>; CDC. Pink Book, Chapter 10: Hepatitis B (Immunogenicity and Vaccine Efficacy, Serologic Testing of Vaccine Recipients). <https://www.cdc.gov/pinkbook/hcp/table-of-contents/chapter-10-hepatitis-b.html>; CDC (2023). Screening and Testing for Hepatitis B Virus Infection: CDC Recommendations — United States, 2023 (Table 1, Persons Who Are Fully Vaccine Against HBV Infection). <https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/rr/rr7201a1.htm>

Remarks: Adults who have not been vaccinated, have not completed vaccination, or have unclear vaccination history should bring vaccination records and laboratory test sheets to the vaccination clinic. If the doctor confirms that the infection is still possible, vaccination or catch-up will be carried out according to the procedure. Just because the antibody is negative once many years later, it cannot be concluded that the original vaccination failed. After the average person completes the entire process, there is no need to repeatedly check for antibodies in order to decide whether to strengthen. If it is found that there is no protective antibody within the specified time after the full vaccination, the doctor must arrange for re-vaccination and re-examination. People on dialysis, those with low immune function, and those with occupational exposure to blood should also be evaluated individually. Positive core antibodies may indicate previous infection, but cannot be directly regarded as never being infected and requiring revaccination. The vaccine does not treat an existing infection. If the surface antigen HBsAg is positive, go to the hepatology department for evaluation, see Section 16, Article 11 (If the hepatitis B surface antigen is positive, have a liver B-ultrasound every six months).

Case: 42-year-old Mr. Zhang’s physical examination revealed that hepatitis B antibody was weak. He found out his old vaccination book and it showed that he had received three injections. He took the test form to the community clinic and the doctor determined that no further enhancement was needed. He saved the money for three injections and no longer worried about the arrows on the form.

items.title: If you are stabbed by a nail or a wooden thorn or the wound is stained with mud, go and get it treated on the same day. By the way, ask if you need a tetanus shot
items.core: In the United States, once tetanus occurs, about 1 in 10 people will die. Deep wounds and wounds stained with soil are at the highest risk. If the wound is dirty and it has been more than 5 years since the last injection, a booster injection is required. It won't cost more than a few dozen dollars to get it processed on the same day, so don't delay.
body: Cost: Registration and wound treatment are tens of yuan. The doctor said that if you want to take a shot, the vaccine or immune globulin will cost tens to hundreds of yuan.

Benefits: Tetanus kills approximately 1 in 10 cases in the United States. Deep wounds, wounds contaminated with soil, are at higher risk. China’s 2024 diagnosis and treatment standards divide wounds into two levels. Shallow wounds that are treated within 6 hours and are not stained with soil, feces or animal saliva are considered low risk. Those that have been handled for more than 6 hours, are stained with these things, or have puncture wounds, avulsion injuries, crush injuries, burns, frostbite, or foreign bodies remaining in the wounds are considered high risks. Those who have received more than 3 injections and the last injection was less than 5 years ago do not need to take any injections. 1 booster shot for high-risk wounds at 5 to 10 years. For those who are over 10 years old, no matter which level they are, they will receive one booster shot. If you have not received all 3 shots or cannot remember clearly, you must complete the vaccinations. High-risk wounds should also receive passive immune preparations (injections such as immune globulin or antitoxin that directly deliver antibodies)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Tetanus: "Tetanus bacteria can get into someone's body through broken skin, usually through injuries." "Tetanus can lead to death (1 in 10 cases in the United States are fatal)." Shots are also at increased risk." "Vaccination also helps prevent tetanus in people with wounds, depending on their tetanus vaccination history." 16 pages, see page 20 for Table 4). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/content_6982262.htm>; Attachment PDF (scanned copy). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/P020241023483425528555.pdf>

Note: Let the doctor make a decision when you get to the hospital. Don’t make up your own mind, and don’t bother asking. Not all wounds need to be punched. The doctor will look at the category of the wound, ask you when was your last injection, and then make a decision. It is wrong to say that if you get beaten as a child, it will be effective for life. If the wound is dirty, it should be strengthened 5 years after the last injection. So before you go, think about the year you last had a tetanus shot.

Case: Lao Zhou stepped on a rusty nail while repairing a flower stand in the yard, and the wound was deep and stained with soil. He went to the hospital that afternoon for debridement and asked about tetanus. It had been seven years since his last injection, and the doctor gave him an injection that saved him from the risk of subsequent infection.

items.title: Women get the HPV vaccine, the sooner the better
items.core: Sweden tracked 1.67 million women. People who received the HPV vaccine before the age of 17 had about one-eighth the risk of later developing invasive cervical cancer. For those aged 17 to 30, only about half are available. The earlier you hit, the more you will drop.
body: Cost: Domestic products cost about 300 yuan per shot, and imported products cost about 1,300 yuan per shot. Give a total of 2 to 3 shots. One trip at a time, half a day.

Income: Sweden tracked 1.67 million women for statistics: those who have been vaccinated have a lower incidence of invasive cervical cancer than those who have not been vaccinated. Vaccination before age 17 years was about 88% lower (IRR 0.12, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.34, original value and its confidence range in brackets). Vaccination was approximately 53% lower among those aged 17 to 30 years (IRR 0.47, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.75). The World Health Organization sets priority vaccination targets for girls aged 9 to 14 who have not yet been sexually active
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Lei J et al (2020). HPV Vaccination and the Risk of Invasive Cervical Cancer. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1917338>; WHO. Cervical cancer fact sheet: "HPV vaccination is a priority for all girls aged 9–14 years, before they become sexually active.》<https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/cervical-cancer>

Note: The World Health Organization gives priority to girls aged 9 to 14 who have not yet been sexually active. Playing from 17 to 30, there is still more than half a drop. The Swedish study only looked at the 30-year-old. There was no figure on how much the number of people with HIV would be reduced after the age of 30. Even if you have been vaccinated, you still need to undergo cervical cancer screening. Vaccines cannot replace screening. See Article 18 (Cervical cancer screening for women over 30 years old).

Case: Li’s mother’s daughter received the HPV vaccine at school when she was 14 years old. There was a girl in the same class whose family hesitated to wait until she was an adult before beating her, but she didn't wait. Later, the whole school was screened and the vaccination team found no abnormalities. She was fortunate to have completed the vaccination before the recommended age.

items.title: Women should undergo breast cancer screening starting at the age of 40, with mammography every two years
items.core: Women aged 40 to 74 should have mammography every two years, which is clearly recommended in the official screening recommendations of the United States. Over the age of 75, and with the addition of ultrasound and MRI for dense breasts, the official conclusion is that the evidence is not enough. When you add money to the physical examination package, you don’t have to buy it.
body: Cost: Two to three hundred yuan for each mammography target. Many areas have free screening programs. Take half a day every two years.

Benefits: The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force is the official U.S. agency that recommends screening. Its current recommendation is: "It is recommended that women aged 40 to 74 years have a screening mammogram every two years." Mammography is commonly known as mammography. The recommendation grade for this piece of advice is B. It concluded there was "insufficient evidence" for women aged 75 and older and for replacement ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging of dense breasts. China’s 2021 Breast Cancer Screening Guidelines recommend that women at average risk start being screened at age 45 and every 1 to 2 years. High-risk women start at age 40, once a year
Level of Evidence: A

Source: US Preventive Services Task Force (2024). Breast Cancer: Screening. Chinese Journal of Oncology, 43(4), 357-382: "Recommendation 8.1: For average-risk groups, breast cancer screening is recommended to begin at the age of 45." "Recommendation 8.2: For high-risk groups, breast cancer screening is recommended to begin at the age of 40." "Recommendation 9.1: For average-risk groups, breast cancer screening is recommended every 1 to 2 years." <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.cn112152-20210119-00061>

Note: The age at which to start checking varies from country to country. China’s 2021 guideline is that for general risk, it starts from the age of 45. Those whose parents, children or siblings have had breast cancer, as well as those with BRCA mutations, are at high risk and need to find a doctor to decide on a plan separately. This article does not apply

Case: After Aunt Wang turned 45, she had a mammogram every two years. The physical examination center always recommended breast ultrasound and magnetic resonance at her own expense. She only did mammography as recommended by the United States. In the past two years, she had not missed a diagnosis, saved thousands of dollars in additional fees, and felt more at ease.

items.title: Women over 30 years old should be screened for cervical cancer, giving priority to HPV testing
items.core: In the trial in rural India, women who had only one HPV test had about half the risk of dying from cervical cancer. The risk of detecting late-stage cervical cancer is also about 50% lower. One to two hundred dollars at a time, and checked every 5 years as recommended by the United States.
body: Cost: An HPV test costs 100 to 300 yuan. If the result is negative, just check once every 5 years. Take the sample for a few minutes.

Benefits: The trial in rural India was randomized by group, not by individual. The subjects were women aged 30 to 59 years. The risk of dying from cervical cancer is about 48% lower with just one HPV test screening. Original HR 0.52, confidence range 95% CI 0.33 to 0.83. The risk of detecting advanced cervical cancer was approximately 53% lower (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.69). For the check interval, see the 2018 recommendations of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force: Women aged 30 to 65 who are tested for high-risk HPV alone should be tested every 5 years
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Sankaranarayanan R et al (2009). HPV screening for cervical cancer in rural India. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0808516>; US Preventive Services Task Force (2018). Cervical Cancer: Screening: "For women aged 30 to 65 years, the USPSTF recommends screening every 3 years with cervical cytology alone, every 5 years with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing alone, or every 5 years with hrHPV testing in combination with cytology (cotesting)." <https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/cervical-cancer-screening>

Note: People who have received the HPV vaccine should also be screened, because the vaccine cannot cover all virus types. What is rare about this study is that it is a randomized screening test, with the number of deaths directly used as the result, and only one round of screening was conducted.

Case: 38-year-old Ms. Liu took an HPV test in the community and it was negative. The doctor told me that according to the guidelines, I can check again after five years. She did not undergo TCT every year, and the reexamination after five years was still negative. During this period, no cervical lesions appeared, which saved her worries and money.

items.title: Colorectal cancer screening at the age of 45 to 50, fecal immunochemical test or colonoscopy to detect fecal occult blood
items.core: Doing dozens of fecal occult blood tests every two years, the probability of dying from colorectal cancer is about 16% lower, and the probability of dying from colorectal cancer is 25% lower for those who have at least one test. For people who were called for a colonoscopy, the probability of developing colorectal cancer in the next ten years dropped from 1.20% to 0.98%.
body: Cost: Stool testing costs tens of dollars and should be done every 1 to 2 years. A colonoscopy costs several hundred to more than a thousand yuan, and if the result is negative, it can be done once every 10 years. Allow one day for bowel cleansing before having a colonoscopy.

Benefit: Cochrane combines multiple studies together. People screened for fecal occult blood had about a 16% lower risk of dying from colorectal cancer. Original value RR 0.84, confidence range 95% CI 0.78 to 0.90. It was about 25% lower among those who participated in at least one round (RR 0.75). Look again at that randomized trial from NordICC. Among people invited for colonoscopies, the incidence of colorectal cancer dropped from 1.20% to 0.98% over 10 years. Original value RR 0.82, confidence range 95% CI 0.70 to 0.93
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Hewitson P et al (2007). Screening for colorectal cancer using the faecal occult blood test, Hemoccult. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001216.pub2> ; Bretthauer M et al (2022). Effect of Colonoscopy Screening on Risks of Colorectal Cancer and Related Death. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2208375>

Remarks: Controversy. NordICC counts people who are "invited for colonoscopy". Colorectal cancer deaths were 0.28% versus 0.31% (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.16), a difference within the margin of error. This suggests that the mortality benefit of colonoscopy has previously been overestimated. The evidence from fecal testing on mortality is even stronger. At what age should you start checking? The guideline in various countries is between 45 and 50 years old. If someone in your family has had the disease, start earlier. For those who have had colon cancer and have undergone surgery and chemotherapy, please refer to Section 16, Article 14 (After Surgery and Chemotherapy for Colon Cancer) for exercise.

Case: Zhao started taking fecal occult blood tests every year at the age of 50, and it was negative for two consecutive years. It was positive once in the third year, and early-stage adenoma was found and removed by colonoscopy. The doctor said that if only one colonoscopy was performed, it would last ten years, so he chose to continue having stool tests yearly.

items.title: People with cardiovascular disease and the elderly get annual flu vaccination
items.core: In the trial of flu vaccination after a heart attack, the proportion of deaths within one year dropped from 4.9% to 2.9%. People with cardiovascular disease should take a supplemental injection every autumn. The number of healthy elderly people who got vaccinated dropped from 6% to 2.4% in one season, but this number is not reliable, and it is unclear whether it will lead to fewer deaths.
body: Cost: 50 to 150 yuan per shot. Give it once a year in the fall.

Benefits: One trial was done after myocardial infarction, 2571 people were randomized. Neither the doctor nor the patient knew which shot was given. Among people who got the flu shot, the overall mortality rate over 12 months was 2.9%. The placebo shot was 4.9%. Original HR 0.59, confidence range 95% CI 0.39 to 0.89. A placebo is a control shot that contains no active ingredient. The HR for cardiovascular death was 0.59. Another study combined multiple studies together. Major cardiovascular events were 3.6% among those who received the influenza vaccine and 5.4% among controls. Original value RR 0.66, confidence range 95% CI 0.53 to 0.83. The RR for cardiovascular death was 0.74 (95% CI 0.42 to 1.30; this difference was within the margin of error and not statistically significant). For otherwise healthy elderly people, please read Cochrane’s 2018 review: After vaccination, the incidence of influenza in one season dropped from 6% to 2.4%. The review rated the credibility of this evidence as "low" and the evidence on mortality as "very low"
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Fröbert O et al (2021). Influenza Vaccination After Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Trial. Circulation. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.121.057042>; Behrouzi B et al. (2022). Association of Influenza Vaccination With Cardiovascular Risk: A Meta-analysis. JAMA Network Open. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.8873>; Demicheli V et al. (2018). Vaccines for preventing influenza in the elderly. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004876.pub4> (The Cochrane summary mentioned in the remarks)

Note: Controversy. Class A only corresponds to people with cardiovascular disease. For otherwise healthy older people, the Cochrane review could only come up with one conclusion: the incidence of influenza fell from 6% to 2.4% in one season. It rated the credibility of this evidence as "low" and the evidence on mortality as "very low." The source of the review is the 2018 article by Demicheli V et al. For pregnant women, see Section 27, Section 18 (Inactivated influenza vaccine during pregnancy), and for patients with COPD, see Section 16, Section 12 (Inhalants for COPD).

Case: Uncle Sun, three years after his myocardial infarction, gets a flu shot every autumn. A patient in the same ward thought it was troublesome and did not treat him. That winter, he was hospitalized for heart failure caused by influenza. Uncle Sun didn't catch a cold throughout the quarter, and his reexamination indicators were stable.

items.title: Get the shingles vaccine after the age of 50
items.core: In the third phase trial, this vaccine prevented 97% of shingles, which was similar for all age groups. The disadvantage is that two injections cost 3,000 to 4,000 yuan, all at your own expense.
body: Cost: The recombinant herpes zoster vaccine requires two shots, totaling about 3,000 to 4,000 yuan. All the money was paid for by myself.

Benefits: A Phase 3 trial spanning 18 countries and 15,400 people. The trial randomly divided people into two groups, one group received the vaccine and the other group received a control injection, and were followed for an average of 3.2 years. Results: Herpes zoster occurred in 6 cases in the vaccine group and 210 cases in the placebo group. Converted to 0.3 versus 9.1 per 1,000 person-years, which means the number of cases that occur in one year with 1,000 people observing. The original article reads "The overall vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster is 97.2% (95% CI 93.7–99.0, P<0.001)." Efficacy ranged from 96.6% to 97.9% across age groups. Injection site and systemic reactions within 7 days of injection were more common in the vaccine group. Level 3 symptoms (the most severe level) were reported by 17.0% of the vaccine group and 3.2% of the placebo group. The proportion of serious adverse events and deaths was similar between the two groups
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Lal H, Cunningham AL, Godeaux O, et al. (2015). Efficacy of an adjuvanted herpes zoster subunit vaccine in older adults. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(22), 2087-2096: "There were solicited or unsolicited reports of grade 3 symptoms in 17.0% of vaccine recipients and 3.2% of placebo recipients. The proportions of participants who had serious adverse events or potential immune-mediated diseases or who died were similar in the two groups.》<https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1501184>

Note: It is not cost-effective because it is expensive. Shingles itself is rarely fatal, but post-herpetic neuralgia is the real thorn in the side, which can last from months to years. Within a week of receiving the vaccine, there were more reactions at the injection site and throughout the body than with the placebo. The most severe level (third-level symptoms) reported was 17.0% versus 3.2%. The two groups of serious adverse events were almost the same

Case: 56-year-old Aunt Zhou took two shots of herpes zoster vaccine at her own expense, which cost more than 3,000 yuan. A friend of her own age got herpes zoster and had pain for two months, but she had no symptoms. She said it was money well spent as it saved her pain and missed work.

items.title: Pneumococcal vaccine for those over 65 years old
items.core: In a trial of 84,500 elderly people, the 13-valent pneumococcal vaccine blocked about 46% of the types of pneumonia that the vaccine can control. Blocks 75% of the most dangerous invasive infections. However, it has no effect on "all causes of pneumonia", so don't expect it to control all pneumonia.
body: Cost: several hundred yuan. Free for seniors in some areas.

Income: The Netherlands randomly divided 84,500 people over the age of 65 into two groups for comparison. The 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine was used. Its efficacy against vaccine-covered pneumonia was 45.6%. The confidence range is 95.2% CI 21.8–62.5. Vaccine coverage refers to the bacterial types that the vaccine can control. Efficacy against invasive pneumococcal disease, the most dangerous type of infection, was 75.0% (95% CI 41.4–90.8). It has no effect against all causes of pneumonia combined
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Bonten MJ, Huijts SM, Bolkenbaas M, et al. (2015). Polysaccharide conjugate vaccine against pneumococcal pneumonia in adults. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(12), 1114-1125. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1408544>

Note: It only protects against the types covered by the vaccine. It does not prevent you from pneumonia if you take it. The 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine commonly used by Chinese elderly people is not the same as the 13-valent conjugate vaccine used in this trial. The above efficacy data cannot be directly applied

Case: 68-year-old Grandpa Wu received the 13-valent pneumococcal vaccine in the community as recommended. In the winter of the same year, several elderly people in the same building were hospitalized for invasive pneumonia. He only suffered from ordinary bronchitis, which healed in a week. The doctor said it was not covered by the vaccine.

items.title: Check for Helicobacter pylori, and if it is positive, it will be eradicated
items.core: In the 22-year follow-up trial in Linqu, Shandong, those who eradicated Helicobacter pylori had about half the risk of developing gastric cancer later on. The risk of dying from gastric cancer is about 40% lower. A check-up costs one to two hundred yuan, and eradication requires two weeks of medication.
body: Cost: Carbon 13 or Carbon 14 breath test $100 to $200. Eradication requires taking four kinds of medicine at the same time, and the cost of medicine is 200 to 500 yuan for two weeks. The difficult part is to take all the medicines for these two weeks on time.

Benefits: The randomized trial in Linqu, Shandong, followed for 22 years. For people who had undergone Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy, the odds ratio of developing gastric cancer was 0.48 (OR 0.48), with a confidence range of 95% CI 0.32 to 0.71. Gastric cancer is a rare outcome, and the odds ratio and relative risk are similar, so the risk of gastric cancer is about half lower. About 38% lower risk of dying from gastric cancer (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.99)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Li WQ et al (2019). Effects of Helicobacter pylori treatment and vitamin and garlic supplementation on gastric cancer incidence and mortality: follow-up of a randomized intervention trial. BMJ. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.l5016>

Note: Re-infection may occur after eradication, so the family members should check and treat the disease together. The population of this trial is residents of areas with high incidence of gastric cancer. People who live in low-incidence areas will actually receive much smaller benefits. Eradication cannot replace gastroscopy. For those over 45 years old who are at high risk, see Article 47 (go for gastroscopy screening).

Case: Lao Chen was found positive for Helicobacter pylori during his physical examination. After taking medicine for two weeks, the reexamination turned negative. In the family, my brother had never been cured and was later diagnosed with gastric cancer. Lao Chen said that luckily he checked it out and now he has a good appetite and has less worries.

items.title: Heavy smokers who have a low-dose chest CT every year
items.core: Eligible heavy smokers who have a low-dose CT every year are 20% less likely to die from lung cancer than if they only have a chest X-ray. The overall probability of death is 6.7% lower. The price is a re-examination after suspicious results are found, and a period of worry.
body: Cost: 200 to 400 yuan per time, completed in 10 minutes. In addition, we need to include the re-examination after the false alarm and the fear during that period.

Benefits: The U.S. NLST randomized trial enrolled 53,454 people, all 55 to 74 years old, with a smoking history of 30 or more pack-years and no smoking cessation for 15 years or less. A pack-year is a unit used to calculate the amount of cigarettes consumed. Smoking a pack a day for one year counts as a pack-year. The result is this. People who had low-dose CT scans had a relative 20.0% lower risk of lung cancer deaths than those who only had chest X-rays. Confidence range 95% CI 6.8 to 26.7. The relative reduction in overall mortality was 6.7%, confidence range 95% CI 1.2 to 13.6. Each person was examined for three consecutive years. Taken together, 24.2% of low-dose CT examination results were suspicious. 96.4% of suspicious results were false alarms (false positives)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National Lung Screening Trial Research Team (2011). Reduced Lung-Cancer Mortality with Low-Dose Computed Tomographic Screening. New England Journal of Medicine: "The rate of positive screening tests was 24.2% with low-dose CT and 6.9% with radiography over all three rounds. A total of 96.4% of the positive screening results in the low-dose CT group and 94.5% in the radiography group were false positive results.》<https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1102873>

Note: Only applicable to high-risk smokers. In the same trial, 24.2% of the results of three rounds of low-dose CT were suspicious, of which 96.4% were false alarms (false positives). Non-smokers are not included in this trial. If we check whether there are any benefits, this trial cannot answer the question.

Case: Lao Han has been smoking for 40 years, one pack a day, and has had low-dose chest CT every year since the age of 55. In the second year, early-stage pulmonary nodules were detected, and the surgical pathology was carcinoma in situ. An old friend of the same age only had a chest X-ray and was discovered at an advanced stage. He was thankful that the screening was timely.

items.title: Call 12356 when you are depressed or having suicidal thoughts, and don’t stockpile sleeping pills and pesticides at home
items.core: Take things that can kill you away from your hands. The evidence for this practice is getting stronger all the time. After controlling analgesics, related suicides dropped by 43%, and installing protection in places where people often jump from buildings dropped by 86%. Therefore, we do not stockpile sleeping pills and pesticides at home. When you have trouble thinking, call 12356 first. It is available nationwide and is open at least 18 hours a day.
body: Cost: No money. Make a phone call. In addition, lock up the medicine and keep pesticides away from home.

Benefit: A review that systematically sorts out the research in the past 10 years: the evidence for restricting people’s access to lethal means has been increasing. After painkillers were controlled, suicides related to painkillers fell by 43%. After protection was added to locations where people often jump from buildings, the drop dropped by 86% (79% to 91%, the range of confidence in brackets is the range of this number). For cognitive programs in schools, the odds ratio for suicide attempts was 0.45 (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.24 to 0.85). Suicide attempt is an uncommon outcome, and the odds ratio and relative risk are similar, so about 55% lower. Medications and psychological treatments for depression are an important part of preventing suicide. Starting from May 1, 2025, the psychological assistance hotline can be reached nationwide by dialing 12356, which will be open for no less than 18 hours a day
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Zalsman G et al. (2016). Suicide prevention strategies revisited: 10-year systematic review. Lancet Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2215-0366(16)30030-X> ; National Health Commission (2024). Notice on the application of "12356" national unified psychological assistance hotline number (National Health Medical Administration Letter [2024] No. 259). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6994470.htm>

Remarks: To B The reason: Most of the evidence on restrictive measures comes from ecological studies, which compare numbers before and after the policy is introduced. The hotline itself has no evidence of reducing mortality. Suicidal impulses often last only a few minutes to a few hours, and moving the thing that can kill you away is an intervention in itself. Data on this time scale, as well as long-term outcomes after an attempt, are provided in Item 32 of this section (Tell someone close to you as soon as you have suicidal thoughts). What will be left after being rescued, see Article 33 of this section.

Case: Xiao Li couldn't sleep all night during that time, always thinking about getting it over with. He first emptied the sleeping pills in the medicine box and then dialed 12356. The operator chatted with him for 40 minutes, and he took the initiative to go to the psychological clinic the next day, and now returns as scheduled.

items.title: Prepare fire extinguishers, fire blankets, escape masks and first aid kits, and check them once a year
items.core: Fire extinguishers, fire blankets, escape masks, and first aid kits are all included in the 11-type home emergency list from the Department of Emergency Management. A set costs a few hundred yuan and can be purchased once. In studies where home safety coaching has been conducted at homes, injury rates were about a quarter lower.
body: Cost: Fire extinguisher, fire blanket, one breathing mask per person, plus a first aid kit, a set of several hundred yuan. Just buy it once and spend ten minutes checking it every year.

Benefits: There are 11 items in total in the "National Basic Home Emergency Supplies Stockpile Recommendations List" from the Department of Emergency Management. Among them, "fire extinguishers and fire blankets" are used to "fight the first fire", and the list also states that "the fire blanket can be worn on the body to escape." "Respiratory mask" refers to "fire-fighting filtering self-rescue respirator, used for fire escape." "External medicines" are "hemostatic powder, hemostatic patches, gauze bandages, etc., used to treat wounds." Cochrane combined 98 studies and 2,605,044 people.
