The ratio of injury rates between the home safety intervention and control groups was 0.89 (IRR 0.89). The confidence range is 95% CI 0.78 to 1.01. Among them, door-to-door interventions have an injury incidence rate of about 25% lower (IRR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.91)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Ministry of Emergency Management (2020). National basic version of household emergency material reserve recommended list. <https://www.mem.gov.cn/kp/shaq/202011/t20201129_372149.shtml> ; Kendrick D et al. (2012). Home safety education and provision of safety equipment for injury prevention. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD005014.pub3>; Wusheng County Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (2025). Consumption tips for portable fire extinguishers, fire doors (windows), and point temperature (smoke) fire detectors. <https://www.wusheng.gov.cn/gasylbzj/c109568/zzzq/content/content_1988424970198126592.html> ; Guizhou Fire Rescue Corps (2025). A complete guide to the functions and usage of the essential fire-extinguishing blanket at home (reprinted from Beijing Fire Protection). <https://gz.119.gov.cn/xfkp/xfcs/202503/t20250313_87157898.html> ; NVWA (2014). Blusdekens oktober 2014 (Dutch Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority inspection report, the original page has been offline, the link is to the web archive on October 20, 2021). <https://web.archive.org/web/20211020154732/https://www.nvwa.nl/binaries/nvwa/documenten/consument/consumentenartikelen/non-food/overige-non-food/blusdekens-oktober-2014/Factsheet+Blusdekens+Oktober+2014.pdf>

Note: Dispute. In the same Cochrane summary, the type of intervention that did not distribute equipment had an injury rate about 20% lower. Original value IRR 0.78, confidence range 95% CI 0.66 to 0.92. The group that was given equipment didn't do any better. The main thing that reduces damage is household education and modification, so the income from equipment is recorded as "medium" and not as "large". When buying a fire extinguisher, look for the CCC mark. The pressure-storage pointer should stop in the green zone. Most fire-extinguishing blankets are made of fiberglass. Only hold the two straps and don't touch the blanket surface with bare hands. Using it to cover oil pans is also controversial: Dutch regulatory agencies tested 22 brands in 2014, and none of them could be used by ordinary people to reliably extinguish the oil. When the oil pan is on fire, turn off the heat and cover the pan. Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms are listed in Article 3 of this section. Use of tourniquets is described in Section 13.12. How to choose each item, where to put it, and how to replace it every few years, see [docs/Home Emergency Equipment List.md](../docs/Home Emergency Equipment List.md)

Case: When the community came to do a safety inspection, Aunt Zhang spent 398 yuan to buy a fire extinguisher, a fire blanket and an escape mask. Half a year later, a frying pan caught fire in the kitchen. She put it out with a fire blanket without using a fire extinguisher or calling the police. The whole family was unscathed.

items.title: If there is visible blood in the urine, even if it doesn't hurt or it is clean the next day, you still need to check it
items.core: In the outpatient medical records of the United Kingdom, about 2.8% of people over 60 years old have visible hematuria, and bladder cancer is finally diagnosed. About 1.2% among those 40 to 59 years old. This number is not high, but it is high enough that I need to check it once. Even if it only occurs once, is in small amounts, and is not painful, you should get it checked out.
body: Cost: A routine urine test costs tens of yuan, and a urinary tract ultrasound costs one to two hundred yuan. If the doctor thinks it is necessary, he can add a cystoscope, which costs around a thousand yuan.

Income: The UK conducted a study using electronic medical records from community general clinics (primary care), 4915 cases of bladder cancer versus 21718 controls. This is the proportion of people who develop gross hematuria who are eventually diagnosed with bladder cancer. For those over 60 years old it was 2.8%, confidence range 95% CI 2.5 to 3.1. For those aged 40 to 59 years it was 1.2%, confidence range 0.6 to 2.3. The scientific name of this ratio is positive predictive value. Hematuria, visible only under a microscope, is equally significant. Odds ratio 20, confidence range 95% CI 12 to 33. In those over 60 years the proportion was 1.6%, confidence range 1.2 to 2.1. The British National Health Service (NHS) says blood in the urine may be a sign of cancer and must be checked. Even if there are no other symptoms, it is the first time, and the amount is small, make an appointment with your doctor as soon as possible
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Price SJ, Shephard EA, Stapley SA, Barraclough K, Hamilton WT (2014). Non-visible versus visible haematuria and bladder cancer risk: a study of electronic records in primary care. British Journal of General Practice, 64(626), e584-e589. <https://doi.org/10.3399/bjgp14X681409>; NHS. Blood in urine: "Blood in your pee must be checked out because it can be a sign of cancer." "But do not self-diagnose." "It may not be blood in your pee if: you've recently eaten beetroot … you're taking a new medicine … it's happening during your period". <https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/blood-in-urine/>; NHS. Symptoms of bladder cancer: "You have blood in your pee, even if: you do not have any other symptoms; it's the first time it's happened; there's only a small amount of blood; you're not sure if it's blood". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/bladder-cancer/symptoms/>

Note: "It doesn't hurt" is not a reason to let it go. The British National Health Service (NHS) states that if you have blood in your urine, you should make an appointment with a doctor as soon as possible, even if you have no other symptoms, it is your first time, the amount is small, and you are not sure whether it is blood. Painful urination, frequent urination, and fever may be a urinary tract infection. Severe pain from the waist to the groin, and restlessness. It may be stones. But the NHS also says don't draw your own conclusions, let your doctor see. The redness you see during your period, if you have just eaten beetroot, if you have just taken a new medication, or if your urine is red, it may not be blood. Those who are taking anticoagulants should not assume that it is caused by the medicine. This is the author's suggestion. The above study did not separately count this type of people. The benefit is recorded as "small" because there is only the detection rate and there is no effect size of "how many deaths can early detection reduce".

Case: Lao Chen is 62 years old. One day his urine was completely red, but it didn’t hurt and was clear the next day. His children forced him to go to the urology department. A B-ultrasound found a 1.2-centimeter bladder tumor, which was performed by electric resection on the spot. The pathology was in the early stage, and there was no recurrence after three years of follow-up.

items.title: If you have erectile function problems, go for a cardiovascular check first, don't treat it as just "that thing"
items.core: Men with erectile dysfunction are about 40% more likely to develop cardiovascular disease and about 60% more myocardial infarction than others. The younger the person, the greater the difference. So check your blood pressure, blood sugar, and blood lipids first, and don’t buy your own medicine.
body: Cost: Registration is tens of yuan. Measuring blood pressure, drawing blood to check blood sugar and blood lipids costs one to two hundred yuan. Go to the hospital and wait a few days for the results.

Benefits: A meta-analysis combined 14 follow-up studies, totaling 92,757 men, followed for an average of 6.1 years. Compared with those without erectile dysfunction, the later risks of men with this problem are as follows. Overall cardiovascular events were approximately 44% higher (RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.27 to 1.63, confidence range). Myocardial infarction was approximately 62% higher (RR 1.62, 1.34 to 1.96). Cerebrovascular events were approximately 39% higher (RR 1.39, 1.23 to 1.57). All-cause death was approximately 25% higher (RR 1.25, 1.12 to 1.39). Cardiovascular death did not widen the gap (RR 1.19, 0.97 to 1.46). The younger the age, the higher the multiple. The group of people with moderate cardiovascular risk originally had a higher multiple than those with high and low risks. For studies using questionnaires, the calculated multiple was 1.61 (1.38 to 1.86). Studies that asked just one sentence were 1.27 (1.18 to 1.37)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Vlachopoulos CV, Terentes-Printzios DG, Ioakeimidis NK, Aznaouridis KA, Stefanadis CI (2013). Prediction of cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality with erectile dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes, 6(1), 99-109. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCOUTCOMES.112.966903>; DailyMed. VIAGRA (sildenafil citrate) tablet, CONTRAINDICATIONS. <https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=d905dc8d-917f-4ea3-a4ee-a1ecf6967d4e>; NHS. Erectile dysfunction (impotence): "Most men occasionally fail to get or keep an erection. This is usually caused by stress, tiredness or drinking too much alcohol, and it's nothing to worry about." GP or go to a sexual health clinic if: erection problems keep happening". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/erection-problems-erectile-dysfunction/>

Note: These 14 studies follow a group of people to see the results, not randomized trials. Therefore, "40% more" is a correlation and cannot be regarded as cause and effect. The British National Health Service (NHS) says that most men have trouble getting erect from time to time, usually because they are tired, stressed, or drunk, so there is nothing to worry about. If it happens repeatedly, you should see a doctor. The things to be checked are the same as those in items 7 and 8 of this section: measuring blood pressure, checking fasting blood sugar, plus blood lipids, smoking and waist circumference. Don’t buy “impotence” supplements online. The regular drugs are prescription drugs, and the instructions list nitrates as contraindications. People who are taking nitroglycerin and other drugs cannot take them. Taking them together will cause the blood pressure to drop sharply. For how to improve, see Article 29 of this section (weight loss and quitting smoking can improve erectile function). The income is recorded as "medium" but not "large": 44% is the risk difference between the two groups of people, not "checking how many deaths can be reduced at one time". Don't remember "small": the signal in Article 27 of this section (visible blood in urine) only has a detection rate. Hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia found here all have ready-made treatments.

Case: 42-year-old Mr. Wang found it difficult to have an erection, so he bought health pills to take. During the physical examination at the unit, the doctor asked him to check his blood pressure and blood lipids. The results showed that his systolic blood pressure was 158 and his low-density lipoprotein was 5.2. After he started taking antihypertensive statins, those aspects gradually recovered.

items.title: Lose weight, quit smoking, and control blood pressure and blood sugar, and your erectile function will improve accordingly
items.core: If you control cardiovascular risk factors, your erectile function itself will improve. Using a questionnaire gives you an average of 2 to 3 more points. The total score of this questionnaire is 25 points, and a score of 22 or above is considered normal.
body: Cost: No money, and you may save money. What is difficult is long-term persistence: eat less, exercise, and quit smoking.

Benefits: A meta-analysis combining 6 randomized controlled trials and 740 men. Intervention is lifestyle modification or medication to control cardiovascular risk factors, with follow-up for at least 6 weeks. Results: Scores on the Erectile Function Questionnaire (IIEF-5) improved by an average of 2.66 points (95% CI 1.86 to 3.47, confidence range). After removing the 2 trials (143 people) that used statins, the remaining 4 trials (597 people) purely relying on lifestyle changes still improved by 2.40 points (1.19 to 3.61). The IIEF-5 is a 5-question questionnaire with an overall score of 5 to 25 points. The original article is divided into five grades according to the score, with scores of 22 to 25 considered as no disorder and scores of 5 to 7 considered as severe
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Gupta BP, Murad MH, Clifton MM, Prokop L, Nehra A, Kopecky SL (2011). The effect of lifestyle modification and cardiovascular risk factor reduction on erectile dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Archives of Internal Medicine, 171(20), 1797-1803. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archinternmed.2011.440>; Rosen RC, Cappelleri JC, Smith MD, Lipsky J, Peña BM (1999). Development and evaluation of an abridged, 5-item version of the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5) as a diagnostic tool for erectile dysfunction. International Journal of Impotence Research, 11(6), 319-326. <https://doi.org/10.1038/sj.ijir.3900472>; State Food and Drug Administration (2016). The Food and Drug Administration: Be wary of the illegal addition of "sildenafil" to some products: "criminals, driven by profit, mix sildenafil, the main component of Viagra, into corn flour to produce a large number of illegal products claiming to have aphrodisiac effects." "my country has never approved and registered health foods that can "improve male sexual function." "Using sildenafil without the guidance of a doctor will pose a serious threat to the health and life safety of users." <http://app.www.gov.cn/govdata/gov/201605/16/380625/article.html>

Note: The interventions in these 6 trials are different, some are weight loss plus exercise, and some are medication to control blood pressure and blood lipids. There were only 740 people in total. So the direction is clear, and how much better it can be depends on the individual. The profit is recorded as "small" because the end point only has questionnaire scores, and there is no number of "how many diseases were avoided later". Similarly, these actions have hard end points elsewhere. To quit smoking, see Section 2, Item 1 (Stop smoking, the sooner the better). For weight loss, see Section 2, Item 32 (Keeping a BMI of 20–25). For blood pressure, see Article 7 of this section (measure your blood pressure and take medicine if it is high). Taking medicine itself is not a restricted area, provided it is prescribed by a doctor. The former State Food and Drug Administration reminded in 2016 that the country has never approved health foods that can "improve male sexual function." Some criminals mix sildenafil, an ingredient of this type of medicine, into illegal products that are claimed to be aphrodisiacs. If they are taken without the guidance of a doctor, health and life will be in danger. How to distinguish health products purchased online, see Section 28, Item 4 (Do not buy weight loss pills that promise to lose weight quickly).

Case: Lao Zhou quit smoking and walked briskly for 40 minutes every day. He lost 8 kilograms in three months, and his blood pressure and blood sugar returned to normal values. During the re-examination, the doctor asked him to fill out the 25-point questionnaire. The score rose from 18 to 23, which was beyond the normal line, and the medication was reduced.

items.title: Use condoms throughout sexual intercourse and do not share needles with others
items.core: Wear them throughout every sexual activity, and the probability of HIV infection between opposite sexes is reduced by about 70%. The effect of "wearing it most of the time" is not much different from not wearing it. It also protects against other sexually transmitted diseases, but it cannot protect against syphilis and herpes that grow in places that cannot be covered by condoms.
body: Cost: one or two yuan each. The hard part isn't the money, it's using it every time and wearing it from the beginning.

Gains: One study combined 25 studies, 10,676 opposite-sex couples. These couples have one partner infected with HIV and one partner uninfected, which is known as serodiscordance. People who consistently use condoms every time have about a 71% lower risk of HIV transmission compared to people who never use them. Original value RR 0.29, confidence range 95% CI 0.20 to 0.43. About 77% lower (RR 0.23, 95% CI 0.13 to 0.40) than those who used intermittently. The authors concluded that while condoms are not perfect, "consistent use reduces HIV transmission by more than 70 percent." The World Health Organization says that correct and consistent use of condoms is one of the most effective ways to prevent sexually transmitted infections, including HIV. But ulcers that grow in places that condoms cannot cover, such as syphilis and genital herpes, cannot be stopped by condoms
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Giannou FK, Tsiara CG, Nikolopoulos GK, et al. (2016). Condom effectiveness in reducing heterosexual HIV transmission: a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on HIV serodiscordant couples. Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research, 16(4), 489-499. <https://doi.org/10.1586/14737167.2016.1102635>; Fonner VA et al (2016). Effectiveness and safety of oral HIV preexposure prophylaxis for all populations. AIDS. WHO (2025). Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) fact sheet: "When used correctly and consistently, condoms offer one of the most effective methods of protection against STIs, including HIV. Although highly effective, condoms do not offer protection for STIs that cause extra-genital ulcers (i.e., syphilis or genital herpes)."<https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/sexually-transmitted-infections-(stis)>

Note: The difference between "irregular use" and "not using" is very small. It must be used every time and throughout the process to be effective. Sharing needles is another independent and efficient route of transmission, which has nothing to do with sexual behavior. Injecting drugs, tattoos, and piercings also count. High-risk groups can also use pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), which involves taking medicine in advance to block infection. Taking 18 studies together, in all trials in which more than 70 adults took the medicine on time, the risk of HIV infection was about 70% lower for people taking PrEP than for those taking a placebo. The original value was a relative risk of 0.30, with a confidence range of 95% CI of 0.21 to 0.45. In trials where fewer people took the medicine on time, no protective effect was seen. PrEP is a prescription drug. Go to the infectious disease department or disease control department to ask, don't buy it online. See Section 13 for what to do after you have been exposed

Case: Couple Xiao Li insists on using condoms every time. During the physical examination, the HIV screen was negative. The doctor told him that consistent use of condoms can greatly reduce the risk of infection. Therefore, Xiao Li pays more attention to protection.

items.title: If you have engaged in high-risk behaviors, go for an HIV test. The CDC is free and the results are confidential
items.core: Go to the CDC for an AIDS test at no cost. Without your consent, no organization or individual may disclose your name, address, workplace and medical history. Finding out is not a death sentence: people who insist on taking medicine to suppress the virus until it is undetectable will not pass it on to their sexual partners. In the study, there was not a single case of such transmission between couples.
body: Cost: No money. Go to a disease control or designated medical institution and get a blood draw. The hard part is opening your mouth to investigate.

Income: Article 23 of the "Regulations on the Prevention and Treatment of AIDS" states. The health authorities of local people's governments at or above the county level will designate some medical and health institutions. These institutions "should provide free counseling and preliminary screening tests to those who voluntarily receive HIV counseling and testing." The significance of early detection is not psychological comfort: current antiviral treatments can suppress the virus until it is undetectable. The World Health Organization states that "infected individuals who receive antiretroviral treatment and have an undetectable viral load cannot transmit HIV to their sexual partners." The PARTNER study tracked 782 same-sex couples, each with one partner infected and one partner uninfected, known as serodiscordance. Total 1593 pairs of years (number of tracked years for each pair added together). There were a total of 76,088 condom-less sexual intercourses and 15 new infections during this period. After phylogenetic analysis comparing viral genes, it was found that none of these 15 cases came from partners, and there was zero transmission between partners. Article 39 of the "Regulations on the Prevention and Treatment of AIDS" stipulates: "Without the consent of the person or his/her guardian, no unit or individual may disclose the name, address, workplace, portrait, medical history, or other information that may infer their specific identity of persons infected with HIV, AIDS patients, and their family members."
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2006). Regulations on the Prevention and Treatment of AIDS (Articles 3, 23, 38, and 39). <https://wjw.beijing.gov.cn/zwgk_20040/zcwj2022/flfg/202304/t20230408_2992986.html> (Reprinted by Beijing Municipal Health Commission); Rodger AJ, Cambiano V, Bruun T, et al. (2019). Risk of transmission HIV through condomless sex in serodifferent gay couples with the HIV-positive partner taking suppressive antiretroviral therapy (PARTNER): final results of a multicentre, prospective, observational study. The Lancet, 393(10189), 2428-2438. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(19)30418-0>; Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Science popularization of HIV testing window period. <https://web.archive.org/web/20260915151957/https://cdcp.gd.gov.cn/jkjy/kpydjwjxz/content/post_3441820.html> (The number during the window period; the original page has been offline, and the link is the web archive of 2026-09-15)

Note: The window period determines when the check counts. According to the Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention, nucleic acid testing takes about 1 week, fourth-generation antigen-antibody combined testing takes about 2 weeks, and third-generation antibody testing takes about 3 weeks. It is recommended to check again after at least 2 weeks and every 2 to 4 weeks. More than 99.99% of the time 3 months after the last high-risk behavior, infection can be ruled out. A positive result from the self-test does not mean a confirmed diagnosis, and must be reviewed by the disease control or formal institution. Article 3 of the regulations stipulates that no unit or individual may discriminate against infected persons and their families, and that rights and interests such as marriage, employment, medical treatment, and schooling are protected by law. Article 38 also stipulates that infected persons have the obligation to "timely inform those with whom they have sexual relations of the fact of infection or illness." For screening of three diseases during pregnancy and mother-to-child transmission, see Section 27

Case: After Ms. Zhang engaged in high-risk behavior, she went to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention for HIV testing. The entire process was free and the information was strictly confidential. After being diagnosed, she immediately received antiviral treatment. Now her viral load is undetectable and the doctor told her that she is no longer contagious.

items.title: As soon as the suicidal idea comes up, tell someone around you first and hand over these tens of minutes
items.core: In an interview, nearly half of the people who attempted suicide said that it took no more than 10 minutes from the idea to the action. Three-quarters of the people had contact with someone close to them during that time. About 2% of people who have been admitted to the hospital due to self-injury died of suicide one year later, and about 7% more than nine years later. The vast majority of people did not die of suicide later.
body: Cost: No money. The hard part was opening up and admitting that I couldn't be alone for a few hours.

Income: 82 suicide attempters were interviewed within 3 days of admission: 47.6% (39 people) said that it took no more than 10 minutes from the first time they had suicidal thoughts to the time they actually took action. People who took longer to do this had significantly higher suicidal intent scores. There was no relationship between impulsivity scale scores and procedure length. 76.8% (63 people) said they had some kind of contact with a partner, family member or friend during this period. The authors concluded that the time window for intervention is usually very short, and professionals have limited scope to intervene at this stage. The author therefore advocates making signal recognition and intervention methods available to ordinary people. Another systematic review summarized 90 follow-up studies. Among those who presented themselves for self-injury, the median proportion of those who self-injured themselves again without dying 1 year later was 16%. 2% died by suicide after 1 year. About 7% of those followed for more than 9 years died by suicide
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Deisenhammer EA, Ing CM, Strauss R, Kemmler G, Hinterhuber H, Weiss EM (2009). The duration of the suicidal process: how much time is left for intervention between consideration and accomplishment of a suicide attempt? Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, 70(1), 19-24. <https://doi.org/10.4088/JCP.07m03904>; Owens D, Horrocks J, House A (2002). Fatal and non-fatal repetition of self-harm: systematic review. British Journal of Psychiatry, 181, 193-199. <https://doi.org/10.1192/bjp.181.3.193>

Remarks: Reason for B: Deisenhammer's item only had 82 people, from a hospital, and relied on the parties' subsequent recollections. Owens's article gave a ratio in the middle of 90 studies with different approaches, rather than combining them into one number. The same article also clearly states that the suicide risk of self-injurers is still hundreds of times higher than that of the general population. Therefore, "the vast majority of people did not die of suicide" refers to the overall situation of this group of people, and cannot be regarded as a guarantee for a specific person. You still need to see the medical treatment that should be seen. To remove the means of causing death and 12356 See Article 25 of this section. See Section 3, Item 18 for some first things to do when you’re feeling down. For the sequelae after rescue, see Article 33 of this section. If you suspect that someone around you has such thoughts, you can ask directly. See Article 43 of this section (directly ask people around you who are not feeling well). What you can do when people around you express such thoughts, see Section 8, Article 15

Case: Xiao Liu stood on the balcony for more than ten minutes, with only the thought of jumping down in his mind. He sent a message to his roommate saying "I am in danger now", and his roommate rushed in and pulled him back into the house, where they sat with him all night. A week later he started seeing a psychiatrist and never stood on that balcony again.

items.title: Don’t take "rescue" as a guarantee: emergency treatment after drinking pesticides or inhaling gas can only save your life, but it may not save your lungs and brain
items.core: There is no effective antidote for paraquat, and more than 40% of a group of patients in Bangladesh were not saved. It causes the lungs to become inflamed and slowly harden, and the kidneys and liver to be damaged. Nearly half of the brains of people who were rescued from gas poisoning and who only breathed ordinary oxygen were not as good as before six weeks later, and only a quarter of those who had undergone hyperbaric oxygen.
body: Cost: No money. Just know this first.

Benefit: A systematic review of paraquat poisoning: the mortality rate is extremely high because of its strong toxicity and lack of effective treatment. It is actively moved into the lung tissue against the concentration difference, which is called active uptake against the concentration gradient. The result is pneumonia and pulmonary fibrosis. It also causes kidney damage and liver damage. The review states: Gastric lavage should not be performed. Hemodialysis and hemoperfusion are unlikely to alter the clinical course. Evidence for the efficacy of hormones and immunosuppressants is weak. The review also states: "The mortality rate was high in all centers, although treatment varied widely." Ten tertiary hospitals in Bangladesh admitted 1,420 cases from 2013 to 2024, of which 257 cases were analyzable: the case fatality rate was 43.2%. Common manifestations were lower limb swelling caused by acute renal failure in 71.2%, vomiting in 65.8%, and abdominal pain in 58.0%. The trial of acute carbon monoxide poisoning was a double-blind randomized study with 76 people in each group. Neither the doctor nor the patient knew which group they were admitted to. Cognitive sequelae at six weeks were observed in 19/76 (25.0%) of the hyperbaric oxygen group. Normobaric oxygen group 35/76 (46.1%), P=0.007. After adjustment for other factors, the odds ratio was 0.45 (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.22 to 0.92, confidence range in parentheses). Another study looked at 73 consecutive cases: 30% had cognitive sequelae and 12% had white matter hyperintensities. China revoked the registration and production license of paraquat aqueous agent on July 1, 2014, and stopped production. Starting from July 1, 2016, the sale and use of aqueous agents in the country will be stopped. Starting from September 26, 2020, the sale and use of soluble colloidal agents in China will be prohibited. The document states that "suicide incidents from taking paraquat frequently occur" is the direct reason for the strengthening of supervision.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Gawarammana IB, Buckley NA (2011). Medical management of paraquat ingestion. British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 72(5), 745-757. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2125.2011.04026.x>; Chowdhury FR et al (2026). Clinical and Laboratory Profile of Paraquat Poisoning: A Toxicological Crisis in Bangladesh. American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene, 115, 176-182. <https://doi.org/10.4269/ajtmh.25-0719>; Weaver LK, Hopkins RO, Chan KJ, et al. (2002). Hyperbaric oxygen for acute carbon monoxide poisoning. New England Journal of Medicine, 347(14), 1057-1067. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa013121>; Parkinson RB, Hopkins RO, Cleavinger HB, et al. (2002). White matter hyperintensities and neuropsychological outcome following carbon monoxide poisoning. Neurology, 58(10), 1525-1532. <https://doi.org/10.1212/wnl.58.10.1525>; General Office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (2018). Notice on effectively strengthening the supervision and management of paraquat (Nongbanong [2018] No. 17). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-12/31/content_5442594.htm>

Remarks: Reason for B: The subjects of these studies are poisoning patients, not a single suicide attempt group. The carbon monoxide test also included people who were accidentally poisoned. Therefore, the above proportion of sequelae cannot be directly regarded as the "probability of consequences for suicide attempts." There is only one thing that is certain: no method can guarantee that there will be no sequelae. On-site disposal of carbon monoxide is provided in Section 13.19. If you accidentally take pesticides or medicines, do not induce vomiting and bring a bottle with you to see a doctor. See Section 13, Article 20. Please refer to Article 25 of this section for not hoarding pesticides and sleeping pills at home. This book does not compare the fatality rates of different methods, nor does it write down any specific practices

Case: Lao Chen drank half a bottle of paraquat after an argument with his wife and was still conscious when he was sent to the county hospital for gastric lavage. Two weeks after he was transferred to the ICU in the provincial capital, his lungs began to develop fibrosis. After he returned home, he could barely breathe even when he went upstairs. He passed away three months later. The wife said that at that time she just wanted to go to the hospital and everything would be fine.

items.title: Don't bet "just lie down for a few days" on falling from a height: most people who enter the trauma ICU survive, and the cost is calculated in years
items.core: In a hospital in Xinjiang, only 5.5% of people who fell from a height and entered the trauma ICU died, but the injuries were serious and the treatment lasted a long time. Nearly half injured more than three parts at the same time, more than a third were put on a ventilator, and the longest one stayed in the ICU for 132 days. Half fell less than 3 meters. Less than 60% of those who were seriously injured were able to return to work.
body: Cost: No money. Just look at this account clearly first.

Income: A trauma ICU (intensive care unit) in southern Xinjiang has done statistics. From April 2020 to July 2024, a total of 289 falls were reported here. The average age of this group was 40.3 years. The median fall height was 3 meters, with 26.6% falling from more than 5 meters and 11.4% falling from more than 10 meters. The median injury score ISS was 24. The higher the score, the more serious the injury. 63.3% of people had an ISS greater than 20. 47.1% injured more than 3 parts, and 18.3% injured more than 4 parts. 36% required placement on a ventilator (mechanical ventilation), with a median duration of 103.5 hours. The median length of ICU stay was 8 days, the minimum was 1 day, and the maximum was 132 days. In-hospital or 30-day mortality was 5.5% (16/289). A trauma center in Germany admitted 84 patients with polytrauma with ISS ≥ 25. Polytrauma refers to injuries to multiple parts at the same time. Return to work during the follow-up period was 58%. Age, length of ICU treatment, and self-rated health were predictors. In 2024, the average hospitalization cost of hospitals across the country (the average amount spent per hospitalization) was 9,870.0 yuan, a decrease of 4.3% from the previous year based on current prices. In the same year, the total national health expenditure was 9.08955 billion yuan, of which personal health expenditure was 2.50075 billion yuan, accounting for 27.5%
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Chen Y, Li W, Wang Medicine, 18, 142. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12245-025-00959-4>; Simmel S, Wurm S, Drisch S, Woltmann A, Coenen M (2020). Die Rehabilitation, 59(2), 95-103. <https://doi.org/10.1055/a-0977-6853>; National Health Commission (2025). Interpretation of the 2024 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of my country's Health Careers. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202512/content_7050025.htm>

Remarks: Reason given to B: The falling group was compiled from old medical records by a hospital, and accidents and self-injury were not separated. The return-to-work group consisted of only 84 people, and that was in Germany. Neither group should be treated as "what will happen to a person after jumping off a building". The average hospitalization cost per hospitalization is the average calculated from all hospitalizations in the country, not the cost of fall injuries. It is quoted only to give a lower limit that can be checked. The original text only gives the height distribution of this group of people, so the correspondence between height and consequences is not written here. The most important pressure ulcers to watch out for during prolonged bed rest are listed in Section 17, Item 8. Deep Vein Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolism See Section 13, Item 11 (Sudden swelling of a leg). See Item 32 of this section for what to do when thoughts pop up. For the consequences of poisoning, see Article 33 of this section (don’t take “rescue” as a cover-up). The following is the author's own experience: I fell from the fourth floor and thought beforehand that "it would be fine in ten days." In fact, he was hospitalized for a year, had four surgeries, had a steel plate, and couldn't stand up on his own for half a year, so his family borrowed money for it

Case: Worker Xiao Sun slid down from a scaffolding more than 2 meters high and lay there for two days feeling fine. On the third day, I was sent to the hospital with abdominal pain. I suffered a ruptured spleen and a fractured lumbar spine. I stayed in the ICU for 11 days and received a blood transfusion of 2000 ml. Half a year later, he could only sit in an office and never been on the shelf again.

items.title: Don't exchange "one less kidney is nothing" for money: the remaining one has to work for two, and 86% of people who sold kidneys said that their health has become worse
items.core: For regular donors in the United States who have been screened before kidney donation, the number of uremia cases after 15 years is 31 per 10,000 people. The number of equally healthy people who did not donate was 4 per 10,000 people. Of a group of people who sold their kidneys in India, 86% said they were in poor health six years later, and three-quarters were still in debt.
body: Cost: No money. Just look at this account clearly first.

Benefits: The United States compared 96,217 living kidney donors with 20,024 comparable healthy non-donors. The latter comes from the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III). Look again at the estimated risk of developing uremia 15 years after donation. Donors were 30.8 per 10,000 people, confidence range 95% CI 24.3–38.5. The number of healthy non-donors was 3.9 per 10,000 people, confidence range 95% CI 0.8–8.9, P<0.001. The scientific name of uremia is end-stage renal disease (ESRD). At this stage, it must be maintained by dialysis or transplantation. Estimated lifetime risk of developing ESRD: 90 per 10,000 donors, 326 per 10,000 people in the unscreened general population, and 14 per 10,000 healthy non-donors. Norway also made a comparison. On one side were 1901 kidney donors with a median follow-up of 15.1 years. On the other side were 32,621 donor-eligible controls with a median follow-up of 24.9 years. All-cause death was approximately 30% higher among kidney donors (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11–1.52). Cardiovascular death was about 40% higher (HR 1.40, 1.03–1.91). Walking up to about ten times higher ESRD (HR 11.38, 4.37–29.6). The overall incidence of ESRD in this cohort of donors was 302 cases per million. An additional 3,698 kidney donors in the United States developed ESRD in 11 of them, equivalent to 180 cases per million people observed for one year, compared with 268 cases in the general population during the same period. Of this group, 255 individuals returned for review an average of 12.2 ± 9.2 years after donation. 85.5% of them had renal filtration function GFR ≥ 60 ml/min/1.73 m². 60 is the lower limit of clinical normality. 32.1% had hypertension. 12.7% had proteinuria (leaking of protein in the urine). A survey of 305 kidney sellers in Chennai, India, took place an average of 6 years after selling their kidneys: 96% sold to pay off debt, receiving an average of $1,070. After kidney removal, the average household income dropped by one-third (P<0.001), the number of people living below the poverty line increased, and three-quarters were still in debt at the time of the survey. 86% reported that their health status was worse than before kidney transplantation, and 79% did not recommend that others sell their kidneys
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Muzaale AD, Massie AB, Wang MC, Montgomery RA, McBride MA, Wainright JL, Segev DL (2014). Risk of end-stage renal disease following live kidney donation. JAMA, 311(6), 579-586. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2013.285141>; Mjøen G, Hallan S, Hartmann A, et al. (2014). Long-term risks for kidney donors. Kidney International, 86(1), 162-167. <https://doi.org/10.1038/ki.2013.460>; Ibrahim HN, Foley R, Tan L, et al. (2009). Long-term consequences of kidney donation. New England Journal of Medicine, 360(5), 459-469. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0804883>; Goyal M, Mehta RL, Schneiderman LJ, Sehgal AR (2002). Economic and health consequences of selling a kidney in India. JAMA, 288(13), 1589-1593. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.288.13.1589>

Note: Controversy: Ibrahim’s study used ordinary people as the comparison object. It concluded that kidney donors' survival and risk of developing ESRD are similar to those of the general population. When Muzaale and Mjøen changed the comparison subjects to people who were "equally healthy and equally qualified to donate kidneys," the risk was significantly higher. The difference lies in who is being compared, not the donor. All three studies agree that the absolute risk is small (30.8 per 10,000 people over 15 years). So the focus is not on "kidney donation is dangerous", but on two other things. The remaining kidney is indeed paying the price, and the ratio of high blood pressure and proteinuria is there. These figures all come from people who have been screened before surgery, have someone review them after surgery, and can return to the hospital in case of an accident. There are none of these three things: selling kidneys on the black market. The return interview in India gave a different ending. The original study only provided the incidence of self-reported health deterioration, proteinuria, hypertension and uremia, but did not include figures such as "how many people are bedridden", so I will not fill in those figures here. Family restrictions, fines and penalties for legal donation are found in Section 9, Article 22 (Do not sell your own organs). For those who are already undergoing dialysis, please refer to Section 16, Articles 1 and 2 for direct settlement across provinces and long-term medication (medication must be taken as prescribed by the doctor, and outpatient chronic and special diseases must be registered in another location)

Case: 23-year-old Xiao Wang sold a kidney to repay an online loan and received 32,000 yuan. Six years later, during the Visit India survey, he said that now his back hurts when he does heavy work, his creatinine exceeds the standard, and his debts have not been paid off. The doctor said his remaining kidney was overworked.

items.title: Do not pick up, dismantle, or sell metal parts of unknown origin, and stay away from those with clover warning signs
items.core: Rays are invisible to the naked eye, and the radioactive source is a solid piece sealed in a small metal shell, so "seeing to be fine" cannot be used as a judgment. The probability of an ordinary person being hit is extremely low, with less than 1 accident per 10,000 radioactive sources per year. But once it hits, the consequences will be serious. In 1987, someone in Brazil took apart a radiotherapy machine in an abandoned clinic, and four people died.
body: Cost: Nothing. If you see unfamiliar metal cylinders, lead cans, or parts removed from equipment, walk around them without picking them up, taking them apart, or putting them in your pocket.

Income: Popular science from the National Nuclear Security Administration says that radioactive sources are solid radioactive materials that are permanently sealed in a container or have a tight coating. Industrial material level gauges, flaw detectors, and gamma knives in hospitals all use this type of instrument. Without protection, exposure to Class III radioactive sources can cause permanent damage within a few hours, and can lead to death within days to weeks. X-rays are invisible to the naked eye, and gamma rays are electromagnetic waves like them. There are three ways to prevent external exposure: shorten the time, increase the distance, and add shielding. Gamma rays have strong penetrating power and require thick concrete walls or lead to block them. As of 2025, there are approximately 178,000 radioactive sources and 355,000 radioactive devices (sets) in use across the country. The annual incidence rate of radiation accidents from radioactive sources has remained stable at less than 1 incident per 10,000 radioactive sources. The grading is like this. If a Class I or II radioactive source is lost, stolen, or out of control, it constitutes a major radiation accident. Category III is a major radiation accident. Loss and theft of Category IV and V equipment, or causing personnel to be exposed to exposure exceeding the annual dose limit, are general radiation accidents. Official case: In June 2020, the ironmaking plant of Ningxia Iron and Steel Group conducted gamma-ray flaw detection operations on the blast furnace pipeline renovation project. Three workers were exposed to a Class II iridium-192 radioactive source. Chen Moumou's left hand suffered acute radiation-induced skin damage of III degree. Liu Moumou's left thumb and index finger had IV degrees, and the middle finger, ring finger, and little finger had III degrees. Fan Moumou’s left hand has degree I-II. The doses to which the three people were exposed seriously exceeded the dose limits stipulated in national standards, and the two responsible units had their radiation safety licenses revoked and fined 70,000 yuan. International example: Teletherapy machine dismantled in an abandoned clinic in Goiânia, Brazil, 1987. The 50.8 TBq cesium-137 radioactive source inside was removed, and the sealed capsule containing the source was broken. About 112,000 people are being monitored. Of these, 249 had internal or external contamination. Of these 249 people, 129 are moderately to severely contaminated, and 50 require close medical monitoring. Last 4 deaths (National/International)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (2025). 2024 China Ecological Environment Status Bulletin. <https://www.mee.gov.cn/ywgz/sthjjcgl/hjzljcypj/202506/t20250605_1120773.shtml>; National Nuclear Safety Administration (2026). The effectiveness of my country's nuclear and radiation safety supervision in 2025. <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/tpxw/202601/t20260107_1140062.html>; Ministry of Ecology and Environment (2021). Notification on the handling of a radiation accident case caused by illegal and illegal gamma-ray flaw detection operations. <https://www.mee.gov.cn/xxgk2018/xxgk/xxgk06/202101/t20210121_818216.html>; State Council (2019). Regulations on the Safety and Protection of Radioisotopes and Ray Devices (Revised in 2019, Articles 34, 42, and 68). <https://www.mee.gov.cn/ywgz/fgbz/xzfg/201909/t20190918_734315.shtml>; Ministry of Environmental Protection (2009). Notice on establishing a hierarchical handling and reporting system for radiation accidents of radioisotopes and ray devices (Radiation Accident Grading Standards). <https://www.mee.gov.cn/gkml/zj/wj/200910/t20091022_172414.htm>; National Nuclear Safety Administration. [Use of Nuclear Technology] What is a radioactive source?: "Radioactive sources refer to radioactive materials, other than materials in the nuclear fuel cycle of research reactors and power reactors, that are permanently sealed in containers or tightly clad and are solid." "Such as material level gauges, gamma flaw detectors, etc. are all sealed sources." Class III radioactive sources "Without protection, exposure to such sources can cause permanent damage to humans within a few hours, and can cause death within days to weeks of exposure." <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076670.html>; National Nuclear Safety Administration (reprinted from Shandong Environmental, Nuclear and Radiation Division). Nuclear and radiation science knowledge: "Cesium-137 used in industrial level gauges, iridium-192 used in flaw detectors, and cobalt-60 used in hospital gamma knives, etc." <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076991.html>; National Nuclear Safety Administration. Miraculous Nuclear Technology (16) - Radiation Protection and Management: "There are generally three basic protection measures for external exposure: time protection, distance protection and shielding protection". <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076933.html>; National Nuclear Safety Administration. [Radiation Protection] What are the types of radiation? : "Gamma rays, like X-rays, are electromagnetic waves." "Gamma rays have strong penetrating ability and require thicker materials to shield them. Thick concrete walls or lead and other materials are often used for protection." <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076595.html>; National Nuclear Safety Administration. Nuclear knowledge in life - X-ray security inspection machine: "X-rays are also called Roentgen rays, which are invisible to the naked eye." <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076874.html>; Hunan Provincial Institute of Geology (2023). Radiation devices used in nuclear technology (excerpted from "Nuclear Safety Comprehensive Knowledge Tutorial"): "The core part of the X-ray machine is the X-ray tube" "Slow-emission radiation will still exist after the accelerator is shut down" "After the accelerator is shut down, the impact of induced radioactivity must be considered when entering the accelerator hall or target hall". International Atomic Energy Agency (1988). The Radiological Accident in Goiânia. IAEA, Vienna. <https://www-pub.iaea.org/MTCD/Publications/PDF/Pub815_web.pdf>; Wang Furu, Wang Jin, Yu Ningle, et al. (2019). Post-irradiation medical follow-up observation of patients exposed to the “5.7” radioactive source loss accident in Nanjing. Chinese Journal of Radiation Medicine and Protection, 39(11), 859-863. <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.issn.0254-5098.2019.11.011>; China Environmental News (2014-05-15). The 48 hours when the radioactive source was lost (Xu Xiaoyi, Shao Yi, Chu Fangqiao, Tang Jingru). <http://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hjbzl/202406/P020240624472937009953.pdf> (Web archive <https://web.archive.org/web/20261005044102/http://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hjbzl/202406/P020240624472937009953.pdf>)

Note: If you really encounter it: stay away, remember the location, don’t move, call 110. The regulations require reporting to the ecological environment department, public security department, and health department. The only protection that ordinary people can do is to stay away and stay less. Pockets and plastic bags cannot block γ rays. X-ray machines and CT generate rays by energizing the X-ray tube and do not contain radioactive sources. This is derived from the principle of ray devices. The accelerator is different. After shutdown, there is still induced radioactivity in the structural materials and the air in the machine room. The real danger is the sealed radioactive source in the equipment. Gamma knives, gamma flaw detectors, and material level gauges all contain sources. In the accident in Goiania, someone took apart the machine and took out the source. So don’t expect to identify the radioactive source, and equipment parts of unknown origin will not be dismantled, sold, or taken home. There have also been incidents in China of people picking up radioactive sources without knowing it. In May 2014, an iridium-192 radioactive source was lost during flaw detection operations at a factory in Nanjing Chemical Industry Park. A warehouse manager picked it up during inspection and put it in his overalls pocket. He was later diagnosed with mild acute radiation sickness and acute radiation skin damage to his right leg. He was hospitalized for a year and still had to walk with crutches a few years later. Two other workers said they had seen it. One of them thought it was a necklace on the way to work, picked it up, looked at it and threw it away. The source of the loss is Tianjin Hongdi Engineering Inspection and Development Co., Ltd. No official accident report was found. The injuries of the person who picked up the source were taken from a follow-up paper published by a doctor from the Jiangsu Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention. The part about picking up and throwing away was only reported by a reporter from China Environment News. People who work in scrap recycling, dismantling, hardware and construction sites are more likely to encounter this. This is derived from the two accidents in Goiania and Nanjing. If you see a warning zone with a clover sign on the construction site, go around it. What we are talking about here is an out-of-control radioactive source. Nuclear power plant leakage is another type of accident, which will not be discussed here. The beneficiaries are mainly yourself and your family members who are present at the scene.

items.title: When you have borrowed money to repay your gambling and are feeling depressed, call 12356 first, and then give your bank card and payment password to your family members
items.core: In Sweden, people who go to a specialist for gambling problems are 15 times more likely to die by suicide than their peers, and the total death rate is 1.8 times. The telltale sign that someone is going to commit suicide is depression. So when you borrow money to pay back your gambling and feel depressed all the time, call 12356 first.
body: Cost: No money. Make a phone call. Leave bank cards, payment passwords and lending apps in the hands of family members. The difficulty is to first admit that you can't control it.

Benefits: A Swedish national registry study identifying 2,099 people diagnosed with gambling disorder in specialist settings between 2005 and 2016. Gambling disorder is uncontrollable gambling that affects your life. Compared with Swedes of the same age, people aged 20 to 74 years had 1.8 times the overall mortality rate and 15 times the suicide mortality rate (both numbers are the standardized death ratio (SMR)). There were 67 deaths during the follow-up period, 21 of which were due to suicide. What predicts death by suicide is depression. The author issued a correction in 2023: Suicide is 12.1 times more common in men and 16.1 times more common in women. Starting from May 1, 2025, China's psychological assistance hotline can be reached nationwide by dialing 12356, which is open for no less than 18 hours a day (Sweden/National)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Karlsson A, Håkansson A. (2018). Gambling disorder, increased mortality, suicidality, and associated comorbidity: A longitudinal nationwide register study. Journal of Behavioral Addictions, 7(4), 1091–1099. <https://doi.org/10.1556/2006.7.2018.112>; Karlsson A, Håkansson A. (2023). Corrigendum to: Gambling disorder, increased mortality, suicidality, and associated comorbidity. Journal of Behavioral Addictions, 12(1), 302. <https://doi.org/10.1556/2006.2023.10000>; National Health Commission (2024). Notice on the application of "12356" national unified psychological assistance hotline number (National Health Medical Policy Letter [2024] No. 259). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6994470.htm>

Note: It is given B because there is only one study, and it only counts people who went to specialists. These people are more seriously ill, so 15 times cannot be applied to everyone who plays cards. Putting money in the hands of family members is an empirical approach. Without direct research, it is simply considered a C-level approach. The legal red line for gambling is found in Section 9, Article 13 (No tapping, no online gambling). Whether a family member should pay gambling debts for him or not, see Section 8, Article 44 (gambling debts are not considered joint debts between husband and wife). What to do when suicidal thoughts arise, see Article 32 of this section (tell someone close to you first). The main beneficiary is yourself, and your family members can also force them to do this when they find signs of it.

Case: Lao Zheng lost 800,000 in gambling, all his credit cards were overdue, and he had insomnia every day. The daughter noticed that he was not in a good mood, so she called 12356 with him and took away his bank card. Three months later, he joined a gambling mutual aid group and found a new job after debt reorganization.

items.title: Men who have sex with men who have high-risk sexual behaviors should go to a designated AIDS hospital to ask for pre-exposure prophylaxis. Taking it on time can reduce infection by about 70%
items.core: Those who have not been infected yet should take an antiviral drug in advance, called pre-exposure prophylaxis. People who eat on time can reduce the risk of infection by about 70%. People who eat intermittently have basically no effect. It is a prescription drug and must be checked in the hospital before being prescribed, and then reviewed regularly.
body: Cost: This is a prescription drug, most places pay for it by themselves, and the price ranges from a few hundred to several thousand yuan. Check HIV, kidney function and hepatitis B before prescribing medication. Thereafter, review every 3 months. The hard part is eating on time every day.

Benefits: This drug is a combination of emtricitabine and tenofovir. The iPrEx trial gave 2,499 men who have sex with men and transgender women a daily pill or a placebo. The pill group had 44% fewer infections (95% CI 15–63). People who can detect the drug in their blood have a much stronger protective effect. The UK PROUD trial included 544 men who have sex with men. The group who took the drug immediately had 86% fewer infections than the group who delayed it for a year (90% CI 64–96, 90% confidence range). The French IPERGAY trial, which took the pill as needed before and after sex, resulted in 86% fewer infections (95% CI 40–98). The World Health Organization used a meta-analysis to combine the trials. Overall RR 0.49 (0.33–0.73, ~51% lower). In trials where the medication taking rate exceeded 70%, the RR was 0.30 (0.21–0.45, about 70% lower). If the medication taking rate is less than 40%, the RR is 0.95, which is basically ineffective. The State Food and Drug Administration approved this drug for pre-exposure prophylaxis in August 2020. Available to adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg (Multiple Countries/China)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Grant RM, Lama JR, Anderson PL, et al. (2010). Preexposure chemoprophylaxis for HIV prevention in men who have sex with men. New England Journal of Medicine, 363(27), 2587–2599. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1011205>; McCormack S, Dunn DT, Desai M, et al. (2016). Pre-exposure prophylaxis to prevent the acquisition of HIV-1 infection (PROUD): effectiveness results from the pilot phase of a pragmatic open-label randomized trial. The Lancet, 387(10013), 53–60. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)00056-2>; Molina JM, Capitant C, Spire B, et al. (2015). On-demand preexposure prophylaxis in men at high risk for HIV-1 infection. New England Journal of Medicine, 373(23), 2237–2246. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1506273>; Fonner VA, Dalglish SL, Kennedy CE, et al. (2016). Effectiveness and safety of oral HIV preexposure prophylaxis for all populations. AIDS, 30(12), 1973–1983. <https://doi.org/10.1097/QAD.0000000000001145>; in China. Chinese Medical Journal, 133(23), 2840–2846. <https://doi.org/10.1097/CM9.0000000000001181> (Chinese version of "Expert Consensus on HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis in China"); World Health Organization (2019). What's the 2+1+1? Event-driven oral pre-exposure prophylaxis to prevent HIV for men who have sex with men (WHO/CDS/HIV/19.8). <https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/what-s-the-2-1-1-event-driven-oral-pre-exposure-prophylaxis-to-prevent-hiv-for-men-who-have-sex-with-men>; General Office of the State Council (2024). China’s AIDS Containment, Prevention and Treatment Plan (2024-2030). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6992033.htm>

Note: The people in the experiment were mainly men who have sex with men, so this is the group of people you should ask the most. Other people who have high-risk sexual behaviors can also ask their doctor whether it is appropriate. Before prescribing the medicine, you must first confirm that you are not infected. Taking it by someone who is already infected will make the virus drug-resistant. The results of the self-test paper cannot be used as a basis. For people with hepatitis B, discontinuing medication may cause hepatitis to flare up, so check before prescribing medication. The World Health Organization only recommends eating as needed for men who have sex with men, and is suitable for those who eat less than 2 times a week on average. The recommended way to take it is to take 2 tablets 2 to 24 hours before sexual intercourse, and 1 tablet each 24 hours and 48 hours afterward. Women and people with hepatitis B can only take it every day. In the on-demand eating trial, the medication group had more gastrointestinal and renal adverse reactions than the placebo group, so reexamination cannot be omitted. Domestically, it will be piloted among men who have sex with men starting in 2019, and the plan for 2024 calls for "standardized implementation." The nationwide free policy was not found. Go to the infectious disease department or STD/AIDS clinic of the local designated AIDS hospital. First, call the local disease control number and ask which hospital can provide it. It does not protect against sexually transmitted diseases such as syphilis and gonorrhea. Condoms must still be used. See Article 30 of this section (use condoms throughout sexual intercourse). High-risk behavior has occurred. For remediation, see Section 13, Article 38 (Get blocking medication within 72 hours). The main beneficiary is yourself, but also protects your partner.

Case: Xiao Chen is a man who has sex with men and has multiple partners. After a liver and kidney function test at a designated hospital, he was prescribed pre-exposure prophylaxis, which he took at a fixed time every day. A year later, the HIV negative test was confirmed. The doctor said that the drug concentration in his body was stable and the protective effect reached more than 70%.

items.title: Women over 65 years old should have a dual-energy X-ray bone density test. Postmenopausal women with risk factors for osteoporosis do not need to wait until the age of 65.
items.core: Women over 65 and postmenopausal women with risk factors for osteoporosis should have their bone density checked. By checking the risks first and then giving medication to those at high risk, hip fractures can be reduced by about 17%. Calculated, for every 1,000 people who go for a check-up, about 5 fewer people will suffer a hip fracture. No change was seen in overall mortality.
body: Cost: Go to the hospital for a dual-energy X-ray bone density test (DXA), which checks your lumbar spine and hip. It can be done in a few minutes while lying down. The self-pay is usually one to two hundred yuan, and prices vary from place to place. The ultrasound of the calcaneus that was stepped on during the physical examination can only be used for preliminary screening, but not for diagnosis.

Benefits: The 2025 recommendation from the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force is that women aged 65 and older should be screened for osteoporosis (level B recommendation). Screening is also recommended for postmenopausal women younger than 65 years of age who are at high risk for fracture based on risk assessment (Grade B). The man had insufficient evidence and did not take a position. The evidence review for this recommendation pooled 3 randomized trials involving 42,009 older European women. The screening method is to first assess the risk of fracture, then check the bone density if the risk is high, and take medication if the high risk is found. Hip fractures were about 17% lower in the screening group. Original value RR 0.83, confidence range 95% CI 0.73 to 0.93. In absolute terms, screening results in 5 fewer hip fractures per 1,000 people. Among them, the British SCOOP trial looked at 12,483 women aged 70 to 85 years. The screening group had about 28% lower hip fractures (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.89), and no difference in mortality was seen. The 2017 edition of the diagnosis and treatment guidelines of the Chinese Medical Association recommends that women over the age of 65 and men over the age of 70 undergo bone density examinations. People who are younger than this age but have one or more risk factors for osteoporosis are also recommended to be checked. In the national survey from 2017 to 2018, the prevalence of osteoporosis among women over 40 years old was 20.6%, and that among men was 5.0% (China)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: US Preventive Services Task Force, Nicholson WK, Silverstein M, et al. (2025). Screening for Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement. JAMA. Screening for Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures: A Systematic Evidence Review for the US Preventive Services Task Force. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2024.21653>; Shepstone L, Lenaghan E, Cooper C, et al. (2018). Screening in the community to reduce fractures in older women (SCOOP): a randomized controlled trial. The Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32640-5> ; Osteoporosis and Bone Mineral Diseases Branch of the Chinese Medical Association (2017). Diagnosis and Treatment Guidelines for Primary Osteoporosis (2017). Chinese Journal of Osteoporosis and Bone Mineral Diseases, 10(5), 413-443 (Table 5 Clinical indications for bone density measurement). <https://html.rhhz.net/GUSS/html/cc825127-29a3-47c1-9a95-7a212fdcce55.htm>; Wang L, Yu W, Yin X, et al. (2021). Prevalence of Osteoporosis and Fracture in China: The China Osteoporosis Prevalence Study. JAMA Network Open. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2021.21106>

Note: Controversy: The predetermined primary outcome of SCOOP was all osteoporotic fractures. There was no significant reduction in the screening group (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.03), except for hip fractures. All three trials "assess risk first, then check bone density." None of the separate comparisons only looked at bone density. The review of evidence also estimated that between 11.8% and 24.1% of people diagnosed were overdiagnosed, meaning they would not have broken a bone in their lifetime. Should men be tested? The United States says there is insufficient evidence, and China’s guidelines set it at age 70 or older. Follow the doctor’s advice. This section is about whether the bones can withstand the fall. To avoid a fall, rely on section 13 (balance and leg strength). Do both together. What to do after osteoporosis is detected, see Article 40 (Take medication when osteoporosis is detected). The beneficiary is mainly yourself, but also your parents.

Case: During a community physical examination, 72-year-old Aunt Li suffered from pain in her lower back after bending down to move flower pots. Her daughter accompanied her to do a dual-energy X-ray bone density test and found osteoporosis in her hip. After the doctor's assessment, he prescribed medication in a standardized manner. After one year of follow-up, no hip fracture occurred and he walked more steadily.

items.title: If you are diagnosed with osteoporosis, or if you have broken a bone after a slight fall, ask your doctor to prescribe anti-osteoporosis drugs and insist on taking them. Do not take calcium supplements instead.
items.core: For postmenopausal women who have been diagnosed with osteoporosis or have had fractures, taking alendronate can reduce hip fractures by about half. Symptomatic spinal fractures were more than half as likely to occur. Elderly people who start receiving medication once a year after surgery for a hip fracture are about 35% less likely to have another fracture within two years. Calcium supplementation alone cannot replace these drugs.
body: Cost: Requires a prescription and lasts for several years. Commonly used medications include oral medications that are taken once a week, and injections that are infused once a year. Bone density should be checked every year when you first start taking medication, and every 1 to 2 years after stabilization. The hard thing is to keep using it even if you don’t feel it.

Benefits: Fragility fractures are fractures that occur due to minor trauma or during daily activities. There are three categories of medication targets identified in the 2017 edition of the Chinese Medical Association’s guidelines. One is people who have had a fragility fracture of the spine or hip. The second is people whose bone density T-score is -2.5 or below, regardless of whether they have had a fracture or not. The third is people with low bone mass, who have had fragility fractures in their wrists, upper arms or pelvis, or who are calculated to have a high risk of fractures. The guidelines also state that "there is currently insufficient evidence to suggest that calcium supplementation alone can replace other anti-osteoporosis drug treatments." Cochrane updated its review of alendronate in 2025. Among postmenopausal women with existing osteoporosis or fractures, hip fractures were about 51% lower in the drug group. Original value RR 0.49, confidence range 95% CI 0.25 to 0.96. Symptomatic spinal fractures were approximately 55% lower (RR 0.45, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.73). The HORIZON trial looked at 2,127 people who had had surgery for a hip fracture, with an average age of 74.5 years. Annual infusions of zoledronic acid were started within 90 days of surgery and followed for a median of 1.9 years. New fractures dropped from 13.9% to 8.6%, a decrease of about 35%. Deaths dropped from 13.3% to 9.6%, a decrease of about 28%. About 20 percent of people die from complications within a year of a hip fracture, the guidelines write. In the national survey from 2017 to 2018, only 1.4% of women diagnosed with osteoporosis or fractures were taking medication, and only 0.3% of men (China)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Osteoporosis and Bone Mineral Diseases Branch of the Chinese Medical Association (2017). Diagnosis and Treatment Guidelines for Primary Osteoporosis (2017). Chinese Journal of Osteoporosis and Bone Mineral Diseases, 10(5), 413-443 (Table 10 Indications for anti-osteoporosis drug treatment; section for calcium; section for efficacy monitoring). <https://html.rhhz.net/GUSS/html/cc825127-29a3-47c1-9a95-7a212fdcce55.htm> ; Wells GA, Hsieh SC, Peterson J, et al. (2025). Alendronate for the primary and secondary prevention of osteoporotic fractures in postmenopausal women. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001155.pub3> ; Lyles KW, Colón-Emeric CS, Magaziner JS, et al. (2007). Zoledronic acid and clinical fractures and mortality after hip fracture. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa074941>; Cummings SR, Lui LY, Eastell R, Allen IE (2019). Association Between Drug Treatments for Patients With Osteoporosis and Overall Mortality Rates: A Meta-analysis. JAMA Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2019.2779>; LC, Kistler CE, Booth G, et al. (2025). Screening for Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures: A Systematic Evidence Review for the US Preventive Services Task Force. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2024.21653> ; Wang L, Yu W, Yin China: The China Osteoporosis Prevalence Study. JAMA Network Open. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2021.21106>

Note: Controversy: A meta-analysis combining 38 trials did not find that this class of drugs can reduce overall mortality (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.05). Zoledronic acid alone was also not significant (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.13). The authors concluded that these drugs should only be used to reduce fractures. Cochrane also rated the confidence of those figures as low to moderate. In women who had not yet fractured and were at low risk for fracture, alendronate had no significant effect on hip fracture (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.43 to 1.32). Rare side effects such as osteonecrosis of the mandible and atypical femoral fracture cannot be completely covered by several years of trials, so it is necessary to review the medication on time and do not add or stop the medication yourself. Some people are suitable for injections, and some people are suitable for taking medicine. The doctor decides which one to choose. How to detect osteoporosis, see Article 39 (Bone Density Examination). Menopausal hormone therapy can also reduce fractures, but is generally only considered when other medications are not suitable. For use of hormones for hot flashes and night sweats, see Section 2, Item 43 (Evaluation of hormone therapy for premenopausal hot flashes). The beneficiary is mainly yourself, but also your parents.

Case: 68-year-old Aunt Wang fractured her wrist after slipping at home, and her bone density was diagnosed as osteoporosis. At first, she only drank milk to supplement calcium. One year later, she suffered a slight fall and suffered a compression fracture. She switched to alendronate sodium and insisted on reexamination. No more fractures occurred in two years.

items.title: Punch a hole to measure the thickness before going on the ice in the wild. Don't go on ice if it is less than 15 cm. Don't go near the ice on the river or ice fishing holes
items.core: The official domestic saying is that only adults can go skating when the ice is 15 cm thick. The bottom line in the U.S. and Canada is 10 centimeters, and that only counts new clear ice. The whitish ice is only half as strong and twice as thick. The same piece of ice, a foot thick here, may be only an inch or two a few steps away, so measure as you go.
body: Cost: The easiest thing is to go to a regular ice rink that is managed by someone, so you don’t have to spend extra money. If you have to go out onto the ice in the wild, bring an ice auger or ice trowel to drill holes to measure the thickness. Buy another pair of life-saving ice picks, which are two spikes with handles and hang them on your chest. These add up to tens to one or two hundred yuan. Measure each section of the walk and take extra time.

Benefits: According to popular science from the China Meteorological Administration, the ice layer is 15 centimeters thick and adults can skate on it. The ice level of open-air rinks must also reach 15 centimeters before they can be opened. The Beijing Municipal Water Affairs Bureau said that a regular natural ice rink can only be opened if the ice thickness is 15 centimeters, the temperature remains between -8°C and 1°C, and there is no strong wind for a week. There are often ice holes dug by fishermen on the wild ice. Once dug, it is difficult to freeze again. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources guidelines are for new clear ice only: less than 4 inches (about 10 centimeters) to pin, 4 inches for walking and ice fishing. White ice that has melted and frozen on top of the snow is only about half as strong as transparent ice, and its thickness is twice as thick. On the same stretch of water, the ice may be a foot thick here and only an inch or two a few feet away. Ice on flowing water is often dangerous, especially near streams, bridges and culverts. The ice may also be thinner on the shore than further away. The National Weather Service threshold for walking, ice fishing, and skating is also 4 inches. The Canadian Center for Occupational Health and Safety relayed advice from the Canadian Red Cross. 15 centimeters for skating and walking with several people, and 20 centimeters for skating parties with a large number of people. These are safety guidelines, and there is no study that has calculated how many people will die if you follow them (nationwide/United States, Canada)
Evidence level: C

Source: China Meteorological Administration (2019). How thick is the ice for safe walking on ice? <https://www.cma.gov.cn/kppd/kppdqxyr/kppdtyqx/201901/t20190124_513302.html>; Beijing Water Affairs Bureau (2024). Beijing's regular river and lake ice rinks have not yet reached the opening standards, so don't risk skating on "wild ice": "After the beginning of spring, as the temperature warms up, the ice surface becomes thinner day by day, melting and seeping in some places, and there is a risk of rupture at any time, so you cannot go on the ice after the beginning of spring." "If the lower part of the ice layer looks like icicles, you should pay special attention, because these vertical stubbles indicate that the inside of the ice layer has become crispy." <https://swj.beijing.gov.cn/swdt/ztzl/fnsbaqztxc/fnszlxx/202412/t20241226_3973959.html>;Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. General ice thickness guidelines. safety. <https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/safety/ice/index.html>; Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. Steps for surviving immersion. <https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/safety/ice/survival.html>; National Weather Service. Winter Weather Safety: Ice and Frost. Working on or near Ice Covered Water - Basic Information. <https://www.ccohs.ca/oshanswers/hsprograms/work_ice.html>

Note: The official guidelines say that there is no 100% safe ice. The enough thickness is only a threshold, not a guarantee. The Beijing Municipal Water Affairs Bureau said that after the beginning of spring, the temperature has warmed up, and the ice surface has become thinner day by day. In some places, water has melted and water seeped. After the beginning of spring, it is no longer possible to go on the ice. The lower half of the ice layer looks like icicles standing vertically, indicating that the ice has become crispy, and it looks dangerous when it is thick. If you really fall in, don't take off your clothes. The air trapped in thick clothes will help you float. Turn around and face the direction you came from, where the ice is the strongest. He put his arms on the ice, dug the ice pick into the ice, kicked his feet back, and dragged his body up. Don't stand up after you come up, lie down and roll out of the ice cave, and get warm as soon as possible. If you are severely cold, you need to go to the hospital. If you see someone falling into a hole in the ice, don’t run over to pull them out. Please refer to Section 13, Article 25 (don’t go into the water if you see someone drowning). Call someone first and call 110, then pass the pole and throw the rope. The main beneficiaries are yourself and the children you take to play ice.

Case: During wild fishing on New Year’s Day, Lao Zhang first drilled a hole in the river bend to measure the ice. The white ice on the shore was only 9 cm, and the edge of the hole was even thinner. He did not get on the thin ice and took his companions to the regular ice rink. Ten minutes later, the original spot cracked and the two of them avoided falling into the water.

items.title: Install the protective cover, put on goggles and a visor before using the angle grinder, hold it firmly with both hands, do not install a woodworking saw blade to cut wood
items.core: The angle grinder rotates very fast, and if the piece is broken, it will fly out and hurt people, and it will rebound suddenly when the woodworking saw blade is installed.
