In the two accidents in China, saw blades were installed but no guards were installed. One person cut his femoral artery and the other cut his carotid artery, but neither was saved. A shield, goggles plus a visor, and a steady hand hold all cost little money.
body: Cost: A pair of goggles plus a visor costs dozens of yuan. Take a look at the shield and film every time before turning it on, and unplug it before changing films. Spend an extra minute or two. The difficulty lies in not removing the protective cover or working with one hand even when it is too troublesome.

Benefits: The Canadian Center for Occupational Health and Safety and the safety agency in Queensland, Australia, list the practices below. Check the protective cover and film before starting the machine. If there are cracks, chips, or deformations, do not use them. The maximum speed marked on the film cannot be lower than the speed marked on the machine, and the diameter and middle hole must also match the machine. Disconnect the power supply before changing the film. The thing you want to grind or cut must first be fixed. Wear protective glasses or goggles with a visor on top. Hold the two handles with both hands and stand firm on your feet. The cutting blade cannot be polished, as it will break more easily. Do not put the machine down until the film has completely stopped. Keep sparks and debris out of the way and keep flammable things away. Queensland's advisory says the design speed of the cutting blade edge is approximately 70 meters per second. Loading a 356mm film onto a 230mm machine, with an edge speed of at least 120 meters per second, the film will break easily. In February 2016, a local worker was hit in the chest by debris while using a 230 mm angle grinder and died from internal injuries. There are two domestic accident investigation reports. In 2019, a worker in Harbin changed the cutting blade to a toothed saw blade and cut wooden boards without a guard. The saw blade caught his pants and severed his femoral artery, causing him to bleed to death. In 2024, a worker in Futian, Shenzhen, used an angle grinder equipped with a woodworking saw blade and without a guard or auxiliary handle to cut a wooden door frame. The machine rebounded and cut the carotid artery, causing death. The national standard cited in the report states "Do not attach saw chains, wood carving blades or toothed saw blades." In South Korea's emergency injury monitoring from 2011 to 2018, 8,697 people were injured by high-speed rotating cutting tools, of which 4,603 were using tools such as grinders. 46.4% of their injuries were on their hands, and 23.0% of their injuries were on their heads. Grinders were more likely to cause serious injuries than other similar tools, with an odds ratio of 2.07 (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.88–2.29). A hospital in Mianyang, Sichuan, treated 36 inpatients with eye injuries caused by angle grinders over two years. There were 10 people whose best visual acuity was still less than 0.05 with glasses after surgery. Angle grinders were responsible for 82 of 742 cases of acute traumatic injuries to the hands and forearms in one year in a Turkish hospital. All but eight were injured while not at work, and 44% were retired people. Among the 15 angle grinder injuries at a trauma center in Japan from 2017 to 2018, 9 were misused such as attaching a saw blade to cut wood. 2 of them had their entire fingers broken, and 1 had a section of their fingers broken (Canada, Australia/China/Korea, Turkey, Japan)
Evidence level: C

Source: Canadian Center for Occupational Health and Safety (2025). Abrasive Wheels - Use of Portable Grinders. <https://www.ccohs.ca/oshanswers/safety_haz/abrasive_wheels/safeuse1.html>; (2025). Powered Hand Tools - Use of Grinder Attachments. <https://www.worksafe.qld.gov.au/news-and-events/alerts/workplace-health-and-safety-alerts/2017/guards-and-discs-on-angle-grinders>; Harbin Songbei District People's Government (2019). Harbin Sanfa Loading and Unloading Transportation Co., Ltd. "8.28" Mechanical Injury Accident Investigation Report. <https://www.songbei.gov.cn/hebsbq/tzgg/201910/c01_797872.shtml>; Futian District People's Government Shatou Xinzhou Nancun House Decoration Project "3·14" General Machinery Injury Accident Investigation Team (2024). Do Not Cut Wood with an Angle Grinder, or You Might Lose a Finger: A Retrospective Study. Journal of Hand Surgery Asian-Pacific Volume. <https://doi.org/10.1142/s2424835521500053>

Remarks: C is given because these practices come from safety agency guidelines and accident investigations, and there is no study to calculate how many fewer people can be injured if you follow them. Injury data only indicate how severe the injuries were, and they are all cases from one hospital or one country. The magnitude of the benefit is set as medium, based on judgment: the consequences can be death, blindness, or severed fingers, but only for the person using the angle grinder. The instruction manual for the Harbin machine originally said that toothed saw blades should not be installed and that a guard must be installed. The worker had a hand saw at hand, a carpentry tool like this that should be used to cut wood. Keep loose clothes, hanging jewelry and long hair away as they can get caught in them. There is a lot of dust and noise when grinding. For details on masks and earplugs, see Section 19, Article 10 (protective equipment must be provided by the unit). If you really cut a major blood vessel, apply firm pressure to the wound first. See Section 13, Article 12 (If there is heavy bleeding, apply firm pressure to the wound with your hands first). The main beneficiary is yourself, but also your family members who are standing by to help. How to preserve a severed finger? See Section 13, Article 47 (Amputated fingers and toes).

Case: When repairing a wooden cabinet at home, Xiao Chen replaced the woodworking saw blade on the angle grinder and removed the guard. The saw blade got stuck and rebounded during cutting, and his wrist was scratched and required stitches. Later, he put the shield back on, put on goggles and a visor, and held it steady with both hands before finishing the job.

items.title: Directly asking someone who is emotionally unwell around you "Have you ever thought about suicide?" will not make him think more
items.core: I am afraid that mentioning suicide will bring out the idea. I have not seen this in the research. When the question about suicide was added to the questionnaire for middle school students, the people asked did not feel more uncomfortable, and the number of people who wanted to commit suicide did not increase. Children who already had depressive symptoms felt less uncomfortable when asked, and children who had attempted suicide were less likely to want to commit suicide.
body: Cost: No money. Ask a question and take a moment to listen. The difficulty lies in opening the mouth. Many people are afraid that asking will bring out their thoughts.

Profit: 2342 students from 6 high schools in New York State were randomly divided into two groups by class. One group had suicide questions on their questionnaire, and the other group didn't. There was no difference in discomfort between the two groups on the spot and 2 days after completing the questionnaire (P = .66 and P = .41, P greater than 0.05 means no difference was seen). Two days later, 4.7% of the group who were asked said they had thought about suicide, and 3.9% of the group who were not asked, no difference was seen (P = .49). Students who originally had depressive symptoms felt less uncomfortable when asked (P = .01). Students who had attempted suicide before were less suicidal when asked (P = .02). A 2022 meta-analysis reviewed 17 studies and combined eight of the “asked” and “not asked” comparisons. After questioning, there was no significant increase in suicidal thoughts and behaviors, self-injury not seeking death, and psychological pain on the spot and afterwards. The strongest evidence was eight randomized controlled trials with low or unclear risk of bias. Another literature review in 2014 also stated that no study found a significant increase in suicidal thoughts after being asked
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Gould MS, Marrocco FA, Kleinman M, Thomas JG, Mostkoff K, Cote J, Davies M (2005). Evaluating iatrogenic risk of youth suicide screening programs: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA, 293(13), 1635-1643. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.293.13.1635>; Polihronis C, Cloutier P, Kaur J, Skinner R, Cappelli M (2022). What's the harm in asking? A systematic review and meta-analysis on the risks of asking about suicide-related behaviors and self-harm with quality appraisal. Archives of Suicide Research, 26(2), 325-347. <https://doi.org/10.1080/13811118.2020.1793857>; Dazzi T, Gribble R, Wessely S, Fear NT (2014). Does asking about suicide and related behaviors induce suicidal ideation? What is the evidence? Psychological Medicine, 44(16), 3361-3363. <https://doi.org/10.1017/S0033291714001299>

Remarks: Reason for B: These studies only prove that there is no harm in asking, and no study has calculated how much suicide deaths can be reduced by asking. The magnitude of the benefit is set to be small because there is no mortality figure, only the surrogate endpoint of "no increase in thoughts." The methods of asking questions in research are mostly questionnaires and research interviews. They are not asked in person by family members and friends. When asked in person, it is inference. When asked, he really thought about it, don’t walk away yet, call 12356 with him, and move medicines and pesticides away, see Article 25 of this section (call 12356 when you have suicidal thoughts). He said that he should bring others with him, or that he had prepared means. Close relatives could be sent to the hospital directly, or they could call 110. See Section 8, Article 15 for the procedure (close relatives can be sent to the doctor directly). Nearly half of the time from the thought to taking action does not exceed 10 minutes, see Article 32 of this section (as soon as the thought of suicide occurs, tell someone around you first). The beneficiaries are mainly spouses and immediate family members, but friends and colleagues can also be asked.

Case: After evening self-study, the head teacher noticed that Xiao Zhou was silent and negative in his signature, and asked him alone, "Have you ever thought about committing suicide?" Xiao Zhou was silent at first, and then told the plan. The teacher contacted the parents and the school psychologist that day, and received timely intervention.

items.title: Go for an electrocardiogram if you have palpitation or irregular heartbeat. If you find atrial fibrillation, ask your doctor to evaluate you. Take anticoagulants to prevent stroke. Do not take aspirin instead.
items.core: Atrial fibrillation is when the heartbeat becomes chaotic. Blood pools in the heart and easily forms blood clots. If it rushes into the brain, it is a stroke. According to the doctor's assessment, taking anticoagulants can reduce strokes by about 60% and deaths by about 30%. Drugs such as aspirin are only about 20% less and cannot be replaced. In a survey from 2014 to 2016, only 6% of Chinese people with high-risk atrial fibrillation were taking anticoagulants.
body: Cost: tens of yuan for an electrocardiogram. Warfarin is cheap, but requires regular blood tests to adjust the dose. Newer anticoagulants do not require frequent blood draws and are more expensive. The difficulty is that you have to take it every day even if you don’t have symptoms. Before tooth extraction or surgery, you have to tell the doctor that you are taking anticoagulants.

Benefits: When atrial fibrillation occurs, the heart trembles wildly, and blood pools in the atrium, easily forming blood clots. A blood clot that breaks into a blood vessel in the brain is a stroke. The most common symptoms are palpitation, feeling tired after activity, and chest discomfort. About 25% of people say they have no symptoms. The diagnosis can be confirmed by taking a single-lead ECG lasting more than 30 seconds, or a regular 12-lead ECG taking more than 10 seconds. A 2007 meta-analysis combined 29 randomized trials with 28,044 people. Adjusted-dose warfarin reduced strokes by approximately 60% (64%, confidence range 49% to 74%) compared with no medication. Antiplatelet drugs such as aspirin were only about 20% less effective (22% less, confidence range 6% to 35%). When comparing the two classes of drugs directly, warfarin was 39% less effective than antiplatelet drugs. For major extracerebral hemorrhage, the absolute annual increase is no more than 0.3%. One Cochrane review looked at only 2,313 people who had not had a stroke. The odds ratio for death in the warfarin group was 0.69 (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.94). Death is a rare outcome, and the odds ratio and relative risk are similar, so death is about 30% lower. Four large trials involving 71,683 people compared newer oral anticoagulants with warfarin. The new drug reduces strokes and embolisms by 19% (RR 0.81) and deaths by 10% (RR 0.90). Intracranial bleeding was 52% less (RR 0.48), but gastrointestinal bleeding was 25% greater (RR 1.25). Aspirin cannot replace anticoagulants. Among 5599 people who were not candidates for warfarin, apixaban was associated with 55% fewer strokes and embolisms than aspirin (HR 0.45). Major bleeding was 1.4% versus 1.2% per year, with no discernible difference (HR 1.13, CI 0.74 to 1.75). Another trial only enrolled 973 people over the age of 75. The combined risk of fatal and disabling stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, and arterial embolism was 52% lower with warfarin than with aspirin (RR 0.48). Bleeding outside the brain was 1.4% versus 1.6% per year. Chinese 2023 atrial fibrillation guidelines were scored with CHA2DS2-VASc-60. 1 point each for heart failure, hypertension, diabetes, vascular disease, 60 to 64 years old, female gender, 2 points each for those over 65 years old, and stroke. For men with a score of 2 or above and for women with a score of 3 or above, oral anticoagulants are recommended. 1 point for men and 2 points for women. Consider the risk of bleeding and personal preference. Guidelines do not recommend the use of antiplatelet drugs to prevent stroke caused by atrial fibrillation. The 2023 U.S. guidelines state that whether or not to eat depends on the risk of stroke, regardless of whether atrial fibrillation attacks in fits or continues. It also states that the bleeding risk score cannot be used alone to decide not to eat, but must be used to identify bleeding factors that can be modified. A survey of people over 45 years old in China from 2014 to 2016 found that atrial fibrillation accounted for 1.8%, or about 7.9 million people. Those who knew they had atrial fibrillation were 78.3% in urban areas and only 35.3% in rural areas. Only 6.0% of people with high-risk atrial fibrillation were taking anticoagulants. In the national survey from 2020 to 2021, 43.8% of the atrial fibrillation detected was discovered this time. Among those previously diagnosed, 32.1% were taking anticoagulants, while only 19.8% in rural areas
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Hart RG, Pearce LA, Aguilar MI. (2007). Meta-analysis: antithrombotic therapy to prevent stroke in patients who have nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. Annals of Internal Medicine, 146(12), 857-867. <https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-146-12-200706190-00007>; Aguilar MI, Hart R. (2005). Lancet, 398(10310), 1498-1506. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(21)01637-8>; Svendsen JH, Diederichsen SZ, Højberg S, et al. (2021). Implantable loop recorder detection of atrial fibrillation to prevent stroke (The LOOP Study): a randomized controlled trial. Lancet, 398(10310), 1507-1516. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(21)01698-6>

Note: The controversy lies in screening. There is no controversy in taking anticoagulants after atrial fibrillation is detected. There is insufficient evidence whether people without symptoms should be specifically checked for atrial fibrillation. The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force concluded in 2022 that there was insufficient evidence to determine benefit or harm. Sweden asked people aged 75 to 76 to undergo electrocardiograms for two weeks. After about seven years, the combined number of deaths, strokes, and bleeding was only 4% lower, which is just enough to make a statistical difference. Denmark buries people between the ages of 70 and 90 with small devices that record their heartbeats over a long period of time. Atrial fibrillation was detected in 31.8% versus 12.2%, but strokes were not so rare that the difference was noticeable. China's 2023 guidelines say people over 65 can consider feeling their pulse or doing an electrocardiogram when seeing a doctor. Therefore, people with symptoms should be checked, and those over 65 years old should ask the doctor to feel their pulse when seeing a doctor. There is no need to buy special equipment to screen. After taking anticoagulants, do not add analgesics such as ibuprofen to yourself, see Section 34, Item 3 (ask your doctor before taking ibuprofen for people taking anticoagulants). The medicine should be taken for a long time, and do not stop when you think it is okay. See Section 16, Article 1 (Take the medicine as directed by the doctor). High blood pressure is also a scoring item, see Article 7 of this section (blood pressure measurement). People with atrial fibrillation do not have to give up coffee altogether, see Section 2, Item 26 (Drink three to four cups of coffee a day). If your mouth suddenly becomes crooked and one side of your arm feels weak, call 120 immediately whether or not you have taken medicine. See Section 13, Item 3 (Sudden mouth crooked and one arm feels weak). The beneficiaries are mainly yourself and the elderly in your family.

Case: 65-year-old Chen suffered from paroxysmal palpitation for half a month, and atrial fibrillation was detected on the community electrocardiogram. The doctor recommended anticoagulation based on the score. He initially wanted to take only aspirin. After a follow-up visit, he received standardized medication. He had no stroke in one year and the follow-up results were stable.

items.title: Adults should check the hepatitis C antibody once, and then check the nucleic acid if it is positive. If confirmed, take oral medicine for 8 to 12 weeks, and most of them can be cured
items.core: There may be no symptoms for decades after hepatitis C infection. Check the antibody once, and then check the nucleic acid if it is positive. After being diagnosed, taking oral medicine for 8 to 12 weeks will clear the virus more than 95% of the time. People who clear the virus have a 60% lower risk of later death and a 70% lower risk of liver cancer. This type of medicine was included in medical insurance in 2019, with an average price reduction of more than 85%.
body: Cost: Draw a tube of blood to test for hepatitis C antibodies. The cost is usually several dozen yuan at your own expense. Prices vary from place to place. Those who are positive for antibodies will have their blood drawn again for nucleic acid testing to see if the virus is still present. Those who are diagnosed should go to the local designated hospital for hepatitis C to get medicine. Most plans are to take one tablet a day for 8 to 12 weeks, and the cost of the medicine will be reimbursed by medical insurance. The difficulty is that you can’t remember to get checked when you don’t have symptoms.

Benefit: Hepatitis C is spread through blood and there is no vaccine. The World Health Organization says that chronic hepatitis C often has no symptoms for decades, and by the time symptoms appear, the liver has been severely damaged. Positive antibodies only mean that you have been infected, and you need to check the nucleic acid to know whether the virus is still there. About 30% of people infected do not need treatment and clear the virus within 6 months. The World Health Organization says that almost all patients can be cured by taking oral direct-acting antivirals for 8 to 12 weeks. An evidence review for the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force combined 49 treatment studies and found cure rates above 95% for each genotype. Cure means no virus can be detected in the blood 12 weeks after stopping the drug. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 1.9% of patients, and 0.4% discontinued treatment due to side effects. In the same review, all follow-up studies were combined without group comparison. Overall mortality was approximately 60% lower among those who were cured than among those who were not cured (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.28–0.56, 13 studies). About 71% lower for liver cancer (HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.23–0.38, 20 studies). France followed 9895 patients with chronic hepatitis C for a median of 33.4 months. After deducting factors such as age, degree of liver fibrosis, and alcohol consumption, the overall mortality rate was approximately 52% lower among those taking the drug (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.33–0.70). Liver cancer was about 34% lower (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.46–0.93). Among U.S. veterans, 15,059 hepatitis C patients with advanced liver disease took these drugs. The average follow-up was about 1.6 years. For every 100 people who were cured, 2.6 people died during one year of follow-up, and 12.3 people who were not cured died. After adjusting for other factors, the risk of death was approximately 74% lower (HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.22–0.31). The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force in 2020 recommended that all adults ages 18 to 79 be screened (level B recommendation). For most people, checking once in a lifetime is enough. China's 2022 version of prevention and treatment guidelines recommends that all adults be screened for antibodies, those at high risk should be checked regularly, and those with positive antibodies should be tested for nucleic acid. In the 2006 national survey, the antibody positivity rate among people aged 1 to 59 was 0.43%. Combining multiple studies, it was 0.60% for the general population, 48.67% for drug users, and 6.59% for hemodialysis patients. The National Medical Insurance Administration said that before the negotiations, the cost of a course of hepatitis C drugs was more than 50,000 yuan. The three hepatitis C drugs negotiated to enter medical insurance in 2019 have an average price reduction of more than 85% (United States, France/China)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: US Preventive Services Task Force, Owens DK, Davidson KW, et al. (2020). Screening for Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Adolescents and Adults: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement. JAMA, 323(10), 970-975. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2020.1123>; Chou R, Dana T, Fu R, Zakher B, Wagner J, Ramirez S, Grusing S, Jou JH (2020). Screening for Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Adolescents and Adults: Updated Evidence Report and Systematic Review for the US Preventive Services Task Force. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2019.20788>; Carrat F, Fontaine H, Dorival C, et al. (2019). Clinical outcomes in patients with chronic hepatitis C after direct-acting antiviral treatment: a prospective cohort study. The Lancet, 393(10179), 1453-1464. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(18)32111-1>; Backus LI, Belperio PS, Shahoumian TA, Mole LA (2019). Impact of Sustained Virologic Response with Direct-Acting Antiviral Treatment on Mortality in Patients with Advanced Liver Disease. Hepatology, 69(2), 487-497. <https://doi.org/10.1002/hep.29408>; Jakobsen JC, Nielsen EE, Feinberg J, et al. (2017). Direct-acting antivirals for chronic hepatitis C. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, CD012143.pub3. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012143.pub3> (Contra); World Health Organization (2026). Hepatitis C (Fact Sheet, 2026-07-28). <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/hepatitis-c>; Chinese Medical Association Hepatology Branch, Chinese Medical Association Infectious Disease Branch (2022). Guidelines for the prevention and treatment of hepatitis C (2022 edition). Chinese Journal of Hepatology, 30(12), 1332-1348. <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.cn501113-20221220-00605>; Nine departments including the General Office of the National Health Commission (2021). Notice on the issuance of the action plan (2021-2030) to eliminate the public health hazards of hepatitis C (National Health Office Disease Control and Prevention Letter [2021] No. 492). <https://www.nhc.gov.cn/jkj/c100062/202109/6bf87bfeb2f0424e8d6efc0425b91699.shtml>; National Medical Insurance Administration (2019). Policy interpretation of "Notice on Including Drugs Negotiated in 2019 into Category B". <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2019/11/28/art_53_2057.html>

Note: Controversy: The Cochrane 2017 review only recognized randomized trials. Most of the 138 it found were short-term trials and could not tell whether the drugs would reduce deaths and liver disease. It believes that the "cure" only means that the virus cannot be found in the blood, and the relationship between it and fewer deaths has not been confirmed by randomized trials. The death and liver cancer figures above come from tracking records. There are also no studies directly comparing censorship with no censorship. Among the people named in the national plan for investigation, there are those who are preparing for surgery, blood transfusions, endoscopy, and dialysis, and there are those who have unexplained abnormalities in liver function tests. Those who have used intravenous drugs, sold plasma, had multiple sexual partners, and had sex with men are also included. Spouses and sexual partners of HIV-infected and hepatitis C patients should also be screened. The plan also proposes to mobilize people over 40 years old to check. The guidelines state that most of today's patients had received blood transfusions or sold plasma before 1993. Tattoos, piercings, and sharing razors and toothbrushes can also spread the disease. Hugging, sharing dishes and drinking glasses generally do not spread the disease. After treatment, the antibody is still positive, and you need to check the nucleic acid to know whether there is reinfection. People who are cured can still be infected again, and people who are still sharing needles will have their nucleic acid tested at least once a year. If you are diagnosed with pregnancy, you should treat it after giving birth or stopping breastfeeding. You should use contraception during treatment. Those who have cirrhosis should also be checked for liver cancer on a regular basis after being cured. See Article 30 of this section for not sharing needles (not sharing needles with others). Hepatitis B needs to be checked for another set of indicators, see Article 14 of this section (check for hepatitis B in two and a half pairs). For AIDS, see Article 31 of this section (check for AIDS once). The guidelines state that hepatitis C combined with excessive alcohol consumption may develop into liver failure, and for alcohol consumption, see Section 2, No. 19 (Drink less or no alcohol). The main beneficiary is yourself, but your spouse and sexual partners are also protected.

Case: During the physical examination at the work unit, 45-year-old Master Liu was found to be positive for hepatitis C antibodies. Further nucleic acid testing confirmed the infection. He was asymptomatic and took 12 weeks of oral medication as prescribed by the doctor. The virus was not detectable in the retest; his family was also reminded to undergo screening.

items.title: Before entering limited spaces such as septic tanks, manholes, sewage pools, vegetable cellars, fermentation tanks, etc., ventilate them, inspect them to be qualified, and implement protection and supervision. Do not enter if conditions are not sufficient. If someone falls, don't follow him. Call 119 and 120
items.core: Places such as septic tanks, manholes, and vegetable cellars will accumulate poisonous gas and lack oxygen. People can collapse in a few seconds. Before entering, you must ventilate, pass inspections, and take protective measures. There will be people outside watching the whole process, and don't enter anything less. After opening the lid and waiting for a while, I couldn't confirm that it was safe inside. If you see someone fall, don’t follow him, call 119 or 120.
body: Cost: Ventilation, detection, protection and monitoring all require money to buy equipment, hire people, and time. Families will give priority to hiring a team with equipment and training. Please ask the local service provider for the cost. If the conditions are not good enough, don’t go down by yourself. It's hard not to jump down when someone falls inside.

Income: "Limited space" refers to closed or semi-closed places such as septic tanks, manholes, cesspools, cellars, and tanks, which are not places where people can wait for a long time. The Department of Emergency Management analyzed larger incidents since 2013 in limited spaces at industrial and trade businesses. Poisoning and suffocation accounted for 96.8% of accidents and 96.9% of fatalities. The main ones that harm people are hydrogen sulfide, carbon monoxide, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide. Accidents in which protective measures were not taken and rescue was performed blindly accounted for 87.4% of the accidents and 86.8% of the fatalities. The Department of Emergency Management's 2020 safety guidance manual said that nearly 80% of accidents resulted in more casualties due to blind rescue efforts. More than 50% of people who died in a confined space were rescuers. In 2018, the State Council Safety Commission reported eight accidents. In each of the 8 cases, only one person was in danger at the beginning, but due to blind rescue efforts, 3 to 4 people died in each case. In 2019, three people fainted after inhaling hydrogen sulfide while cleaning a sewage pool at a paper mill in Dongguan. Six people went into the pool to save him, and seven died in the end. In 2020, at a noodle product factory in Jiaozuo, a worker fell into a material tank in the fermentation workshop. Others rescued blindly, and a total of six people died. The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health investigated 70 confined space fatal accidents from 1983 to 1993, resulting in 109 fatalities. Of those, 39 (36%) went in to save people. Among these 39 people, only 4 were professional rescuers such as police and fire fighters. Its 1986 warning said about 60 percent of those who died were people trying to save others. The manual says that hydrogen sulfide smells like rotten eggs, but when the concentration is high, your nose can no longer smell it. Concentrations exceeding 1,000 milligrams per cubic meter can kill within seconds. When carbon dioxide concentration is high, a person will fall unconscious within seconds. The manual requires that if you are unable to save yourself at the scene, you should call 119 and 120 in time, and "forced rescue will never be allowed." Stand outside and pull the person out, provided that the trapped person is wearing a full-body safety belt and the safety rope is connected to the outside. Order No. 13 of the Ministry of Emergency Management requires industrial and trade enterprises to "ventilate first, then inspect, and then operate." Enterprises should be equipped with detection, ventilation, protection and rescue equipment according to risks, and monitoring personnel should be present throughout the process. Ventilation and inspection must also be continued during the operation. If the conditions do not meet safety requirements, no entry is allowed. Guardians should stop blind rescuers who fail to take safety measures. The Anshun Municipal Health Bureau reminds that if the cellar where vegetables are stored is sealed for a long time, the vegetables will consume oxygen and release carbon dioxide. Open the vents for adequate ventilation before entering the cellar. This ventilation tip is not a substitute for gas detection, protection and monitoring (Nationwide/U.S.).
Evidence level: C

Source: Ministry of Emergency Management (2023). Interpretation of "Safety Regulations for Operations in Limited Spaces of Industrial and Trade Enterprises". <https://www.mem.gov.cn/gk/zcjd/202312/t20231212_471584.shtml>; Ministry of Emergency Management (2023). Special press conference on "Safety Regulations for Operations in Limited Spaces of Industrial and Trade Enterprises". <https://www.mem.gov.cn/xw/xwfbh/2023n12y12rxwfbh/wzsl_4260/202312/t20231212_471598.shtml>; Emergency Management Ministry Order No. 13 (2023). Remarks: C is given because these are accident statistics and safety regulations. There is no study to calculate how many fewer people will die if followed. The magnitude of the benefit is set as medium, based on judgment: the consequence is death, often several at a time, but only for those who want to go to such a place. What we often encounter at home is cleaning our own septic tank and biogas tank, and getting vegetables from the vegetable cellar and cellar. Don't rely on the smell to judge whether it is safe or not. Not smelling the odor does not mean there is no hydrogen sulfide. If you are asked to go into wells or pools while working without ventilation, testing, supervision and safety belts, you can refuse. The grounds for refusal are given in Section 19, Article 10 (work without protective measures may be refused). If someone falls inside, call someone first and call 119 and 120. What you can do is open the lid from the outside and blow air inside. After the person is pulled up and moved to a place with fresh air, and the person is not breathing normally, the pressure is applied. See Section 13, Article 1 (Someone falls to the ground and is not breathing normally). It does not matter whether the person who falls is a colleague, a neighbor or a stranger. The principle is the same as Section 13 and Article 25 (Don’t go into the water if you see someone drowning). Carbon monoxide from burning coal in the house is described in Article 3 of this section (carbon monoxide alarm). The main beneficiary is yourself, because you are often the one who wants to save others, followed by your family members who work together.

Case: Next to the manhole cover of the septic tank in the community, a worker fainted after smelling a strange smell. His companion did not go down the well, so he immediately called 119 and 120 and ventilated the workers outside. The workers were rescued after testing their firefighting equipment, and medical care was provided at the scene, and the workers were saved from danger.

items.title: If you are over 45 years old, live in an area with a high incidence of gastric cancer and esophageal cancer, have a family history or are Helicobacter pylori positive, go for a gastroscopy screening
items.core: People over 45 years old, who are at high risk of gastric cancer and esophageal cancer, and have had a gastroscopy, the probability of dying from these two cancers is about half lower. However, people who take the initiative to check themselves tend to pay more attention to their health, so this number will be on the higher side. According to the most stringent method, the death rate from esophageal cancer is only about 20% lower, which is still within the error range. For people who are not at high risk, the guidelines do not recommend checking.
body: Cost: A few hundred yuan for an ordinary gastroscopy, and an additional several hundred yuan for a painless gastroscopy. Prices vary from place to place. Go on an empty stomach and take half a day before and after. If you choose a painless gastroscopy, someone should accompany you. The uncomfortable part was the few minutes the tube passed through my throat.

Benefits: The National Health Commission’s 2024 plan identifies high-risk groups in this way. You must first be over 45 years old and then meet any of the following conditions. One is living in a county with a high incidence of gastric cancer or esophageal cancer. Gastric cancer is calculated as an age-standardized incidence rate exceeding 20 cases per 100,000 people, and esophageal cancer is calculated as an age-standardized incidence rate exceeding 15 cases per 100,000 people. The second is that parents, children, brothers and sisters have had this cancer. The third is a positive test for Helicobacter pylori, which only counts gastric cancer. The fourth is smoking, heavy drinking, eating salty foods, and liking to eat pickled foods. Esophageal cancer also includes eating hot foods. The fifth is to have suffered from diseases such as atrophic gastritis, gastric ulcer, gastric polyps, Barrett's esophagus, and reflux esophagitis. The screening age is generally between 45 and 74 years old. Gastroscopy is the first choice and is done in principle every 5 years. The 2022 national guidelines clearly do not recommend gastric cancer screening for people other than those at high risk. One study in six high-incidence areas in China followed about 637,500 people aged 40 to 69 years. People who had a gastroscopy had a 57% lower risk of dying from upper gastrointestinal cancer than those who had not. Original value RR 0.43, confidence range 95% CI 0.40 to 0.47. The incidence of upper gastrointestinal cancer was approximately 23% lower (RR 0.77). Only 33.53% of those invited actually did it. Counting all those invited, death was about 31% lower (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.72). Another study was conducted in a village with a high incidence of esophageal cancer, without randomization, and followed for 10 years. The cumulative mortality from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma was 3.35% in the screening group and 5.05% in the control group. In the Korean National Screening Program, the odds ratio of dying from gastric cancer among those who had a gastroscopy was 0.53 (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.56). Death from gastric cancer is a rare outcome, and the odds ratio and relative risk are similar, so about 47% lower. No difference was seen in those who had a barium meal (OR 0.98). The more times you have a gastroscopy, the lower the risk. Taking 10 Asian studies together, the death rate from gastric cancer is about 40% lower in people who have had a gastroscopy. Original RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.73. There is no change in the number of people getting gastric cancer. There was a trial in northern China that randomized 33,800 people aged 45 to 69 and followed them for 9 years. Death from esophageal cancer was about 18% lower among those assigned to the screening group (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.53 to 1.26), which was within the margin of error. Incidence was approximately 19% lower (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.60 to 1.09), also not significant. A 2023 meta-analysis corrected the bias of "people who take the initiative to check are inherently healthier." People who actually go for gastroscopy are about 48% less likely to die from gastric cancer (RR 0.52, confidence range 0.39 to 0.79). Calculated based on the entire screening project, only RR is 0.94 (confidence range 0.71 to 1.28), and no effect is visible (China/South Korea/Asia)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: General Office of the National Health Commission (2024). Notice on the issuance of the Esophageal Cancer Screening, Early Diagnosis and Early Treatment Plan (2024 Edition) and the Gastric Cancer Screening, Early Diagnosis and Early Treatment Plan (2024 Edition) (National Health Office Medical Emergency Letter [2024] No. 200). <https://www.nhc.gov.cn/wjw/c100378/202406/7008ffe1c77d4457ac73361be75760c7.shtml> (Full text reprinted in the attachment: Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention <https://cdcp.gd.gov.cn/jkjy/jkzt/mxfcrxjbfz/content/mpost_4444507.html>); He Jie, Chen Wanqing, Li Zhaoshen, et al (2022). Chinese Oncology, 31(7), 488-527 (Clinical Issues 7, 13). <https://doi.org/10.11735/j.issn.1004-0242.2022.07.A002> (The same article was published in Chinese Journal of Oncology, 44(7), 634-666. <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.cn112152-20220617-00430>); Chen R, Liu Y, Song G, et al. (2021). Effectiveness of one-time endoscopic screening program in prevention of upper gastrointestinal cancer in China: a multicentre population-based cohort study. Gut, 70(2), 251-260. <https://doi.org/10.1136/gutjnl-2019-320200>; Wei WQ, Chen ZF, He YT, et al. (2015). Long-Term Follow-Up of a Community Assignment, One-Time Endoscopic Screening Study of Esophageal Cancer in China. Effectiveness of the Korean National Cancer Screening Program in Reducing Gastric Cancer Mortality. Gastroenterology, 152(6), 1319-1328.e7. <https://doi.org/10.1053/j.gastro.2017.01.029>; Zhang <https://doi.org/10.1053/j.gastro.2018.04.026>; Liu M, Yang W, Guo C, et al. (2024). Effectiveness of Endoscopic Screening on Esophageal Cancer Incidence and Mortality: A 9-Year Report of the Endoscopic Screening for Esophageal Cancer in China (ESECC) Randomized Trial. Journal of Clinical Oncology, 42(14), 1655-1664. <https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.23.01284>; Hibino M, Hamashima C, Iwata M, Terasawa T. (2023). Radiographic and endoscopic screening to reduce gastric cancer mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet Regional Health – Western Pacific, 35, 100741. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.lanwpc.2023.100741>

Note: Controversy. The evidence that gastroscopy reduces deaths is mostly based on comparing those who voluntarily undergo the examination with those who do not. People who go for the check-up are already paying more attention to their health, so the benefits will be considered great. The 2023 meta-analysis assessed that the risk of bias in these studies ranged from moderate to very serious, and all studies done in existing screening projects were very serious. In the village-based trial of esophageal cancer, the nine-year difference in death was within the margin of error. The harms listed in the 2022 guidelines are overdiagnosis, false positives and missed diagnoses, as well as bleeding, perforation, cardiorespiratory accidents, aspiration pneumonia and infection. Overdiagnosis refers to the detection of cancer that will never occur again in your lifetime. For those who cannot tolerate ordinary gastroscopy, the plan states that it can be done under anesthesia or sedation. People over 45 years old who are positive for Helicobacter pylori are considered to be at high risk for gastric cancer. For eradication, see Article 23 (check for Helicobacter pylori, eradicate if positive), but eradication cannot replace gastroscopy, both must be done. Barium meal, single examination of pepsinogen, tumor markers and PET examination are not recommended for screening. Tumor marker panels are provided in Section 6, Item 7 (Whole-body PET-CT and Tumor Marker Panels). If atrophic gastritis, intestinal metaplasia, or intraepithelial neoplasia is detected, reexamination should be more frequent and follow the doctor's instructions. You can ask the local CDC or county hospital whether the county where you live is considered a high-risk area. If you already have difficulty swallowing, you should go to the doctor, not for screening. See Section 34, Article 6 (if you have difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, or melena, go directly to the hospital). If you have vomited blood or had tarry black stools, go to the emergency room on the same day. See Section 13, Article 49 (tarry). For those who like to drink hot tea, see Section 2, Item 30 (leave hot things on for a while before drinking). The beneficiary is mainly yourself, but also your parents.

Case: 52-year-old Uncle Zhao’s father had gastric cancer, and he was Helicobacter pylori positive but asymptomatic. During the physical examination, he underwent a gastroscopy and found early gastric cancer. After endoscopic resection, the pathology was still limited to the mucosa, and he was reviewed regularly thereafter.

items.title: Eat the soaked fungus and white fungus in one meal and don't stay overnight. Wet rice noodles such as river noodles and rice rolls are eaten on the same day you buy them. If you don't make your own fermented rice noodles at home
items.core: The fungus and white fungus that have been soaked for too long, the wet rice noodles that have been stored for a long time, and the cornmeal that is fermented at home may develop a poison called rice fermentation acid. It cannot be removed even if it is boiled, and there is no antidote. This kind of poisoning has been reported across the country for eleven years, and about 30% of the people who fell ill died.
body: Cost: No money. Soak as much fungus and white fungus as you eat, and throw away the rest. Only buy the amount of wet rice noodles you can eat on the day. The difficulty is that you can’t bear to pour it out after soaking too much. Some people are used to making their own sour soup.

Income: In the national foodborne disease outbreak surveillance, a total of 19 cases of rice yeast acidosis were reported from 2010 to 2020. 146 people became ill, 43 died, and the case fatality rate was 29.5% (meaning that 29.5% of those who became ill died). Broken down by food: Home-fermented cornmeal products 9 cases, 33 deaths. Wet rice noodles 5 cases, 7 deaths. There were 3 cases of fungus, 5 people got sick and 3 people died. In 2020, there were 143 reported deaths from food poisoning nationwide, of which 12 were attributed to oryzoin. Ahead of it are poisonous mushrooms (80 people) and methanol (14 people). A note from the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation states: Rice fermentation acid cannot be destroyed by boiling at 100°C or steaming in a pressure cooker, and there is currently no specific antidote. From 2018, Guangdong requires small packages of wet rice noodles to be sealed and have a standard-definition shelf life. Before and after comparison, the number of cases per year in the province dropped from an average of 6.25 to 0.5
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Zhang H et al (2023). Epidemiology of foodborne bongkrekic acid poisoning outbreaks in China, 2010 to 2020. PLoS One 18(1):e0279957: "From 2010–2020, a total of 19 BA poisoning outbreaks were reported to the China National Foodborne Disease Outbreak Surveillance System. These outbreaks involved 146 illnesses, 139 hospitalizations, and 43 deaths, with a case-fatality rate of 29.5%.》<https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0279957> ; Li H et al. (2021). Characteristics of Settings and Etiologic Agents of Foodborne Disease Outbreaks — China, 2020. China CDC Weekly 3(42):889-893. <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2021.219> ; Yuan Y et al. (2020). A Foodborne Bongkrekic Acid Poisoning Incident — Heilongjiang Province, 2020. China CDC Weekly 2(51):975-978: "In October 2020, 9 persons in Jidong County, Heilongjiang Province died after consuming a homemade fermented corn flour product — sour soup — with a case fatality rate of 100%.》<https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2020.264> ; Liu Z et al. (2026). Controlling the Storage Time Is an Effective Measure to Reduce the Risk of Bongkrekic Acid Poisoning Caused by Wet Rice Noodles. Foodborne Pathog Dis 23(7):468-472 (first published online on 2025-05-12): "The annual average number of BKA poisoning cases in Guangdong Province dropped from 6.25 before implementing the code to 0.5 after implementing the code." <https://doi.org/10.1089/fpd.2024.0131>; Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Warnings about the risk of food poisoning caused by rice fermentation acid: "Ricee fermentation acid is stable to heat and cannot be destroyed by boiling at 100°C and high-pressure cooking." "Currently, there is no specific detoxification drug for rice fermentation acid." "Tremella, fungus and their processed products brewed the next day cannot be eaten." "Ear pieces that are shapeless, sticky, inelastic, or have a peculiar smell cannot be eaten." "Induce vomiting as soon as possible to expel gastric contents and reduce the amount of toxins absorbed; send to hospital for treatment in time." <https://scjgj.beijing.gov.cn/hdjl/xfts/202309/t20230904_3248296.html> ; Hunan Provincial Administration for Market Regulation (2025). [Food Safety Science] Fatal warning about rice fermentation acid: "Soak Tremella fungus in cold water (room temperature) for 3 to 4 hours, and soak fungus in cold water for 1 to 2 hours. Change the water 1 to 2 times to remove microorganisms. The maximum soaking time should not exceed 8 hours." "If Tremella fungus and fungus feel sticky and have poor elasticity after soaking, , has a sour smell, and the soaking water is turbid, which is a sign of spoilage and should be discarded immediately." "When poisoning occurs, vomiting should be induced as soon as possible to reduce the absorption of toxins; try to save suspected pathogenic foods and seek medical treatment in time." "People who have eaten the same food, regardless of whether they have symptoms or not, should be sent to the hospital for examination." <https://amr.hunan.gov.cn/amr/xxx/xtdtx/202506/t20250630_33725786.html> ; Guizhou Provincial Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Food safety warning on preventing rice yeast acidosis: "When purchasing Tremella, fungus and other related foods, choose formal channels, do not soak them overnight, and process them in time for consumption." <https://amr.guizhou.gov.cn/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/tzgg_5626971/tzgg_5626972/202307/t20230728_81318622.html>

Note: In October 2020, several families in Jidong County, Jixi City, Heilongjiang ate homemade sour soup for breakfast. All nine people who ate it died. Soaking the fungus in cold water for one or two hours is enough. The soaking time varies from place to place. In Hunan, the longest time is no more than 8 hours. The ear pieces are sticky, inelastic, and have a sour smell, or the soaking water is turbid and the entire basin should be thrown away. If you experience vomiting, dizziness, and general lack of energy after eating, induce vomiting immediately and take the remaining food to the hospital. People who eat with you should also get tested if they don’t have symptoms. Wild Mushrooms See No. 5 (Don’t Eat Wild Mushrooms).

Case: The summer night market stall served fungus mixed with cold dishes that had been soaked for two days. After eating, many customers vomited and suffered abdominal pain and were sent to the hospital; the same batch of fungus was detected with rice fermentation acid. The adjacent stalls were used up on the same day they were renovated, and similar situations did not occur again after that.

items.title: If you have a cough or expectoration that lasts for more than two weeks or there is blood in the sputum, go to a designated tuberculosis hospital for a check-up. If you are diagnosed, take all the medicine according to the plan, and don’t stop when you feel better
items.core: If you have a cough that lasts for more than two weeks or there is blood in the sputum, go to a designated tuberculosis hospital for a check-up. If tuberculosis, the bacteria found in sputum, is not cured, approximately 70% of the patients will die within ten years. About 95% of new patients and relapsed patients who started treatment in China were cured or finished taking the medicine on schedule. You need to take enough medicine. Stopping the medicine on your own can easily make bacteria resistant. Only about 70% of domestic multi-drug-resistant patients are successfully treated.
body: Cost: Go to the local designated tuberculosis hospital to take a chest X-ray and check sputum, which takes half a day. Designated hospitals provide free examinations and treatment for some items. It is up to each region to decide which items are free. You can call the local CDC before going. Once diagnosed, you need to take medicine every day. For ordinary tuberculosis, you need to take medicine for 6 to 8 months. In the meantime, you need to go back for review as required by the doctor. The difficulty is that after the cough is cured, I have to take medicine for several months.

Benefits: The World Health Organization says that in 2024, approximately 10.7 million people around the world will get tuberculosis, and 1.23 million people will die from it. China accounts for 6.5% of new cases worldwide. According to estimates from the World Health Organization, about 696,000 people will be newly diagnosed with tuberculosis in China in 2024, and about 28,000 people will die from tuberculosis. About 76% of estimated new cases are diagnosed and reported. The "Measures for the Management of Tuberculosis Prevention and Treatment" states that coughing, sputum production for more than 2 weeks, hemoptysis or blood in the sputum are considered suspicious symptoms of tuberculosis. The consequences of not treating tuberculosis come from a systematic review of studies that preceded the advent of anti-tuberculosis drugs. The proportion of patients with untreatable sputum smear-positive tuberculosis who died over 10 years ranged from 53% to 86%, with a weighted mean of 70%. A positive sputum smear means that bacteria can be found directly in the sputum. About 20% of those with sputum smear-negative and culture-positive cases died within 10 years. The results of treatment can be found in the Chinese data released by the World Health Organization. About 549,000 new and relapsed patients started treatment in 2023 (548,839 people). About 95% of them are successfully treated, with success referring to being cured or taking the medicine on schedule, and about 2.9% die. In 2024, approximately 2.9% of new patients in China will be resistant to rifampicin, and 17% of treated patients will be resistant to rifampicin. Rifampicin is the main first-line anti-tuberculosis drug. A total of 9,927 multidrug-resistant patients started treatment in 2022, and 6,783 patients were successfully treated, or about 68%. The World Health Organization now recommends three types of drug-resistant TB regimens: two six-month regimens, several nine-month regimens, and longer courses of 18 to 20 months. Nine months is only given to people who are not resistant to fluoroquinolones. In 2024, more than half of China's multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant patients will still use long courses of treatment. The World Health Organization says that stopping medication early or not following medical advice can cause tuberculosis bacteria in the body to become drug-resistant. National promotional materials state that the full course of treatment for common tuberculosis takes 6 to 8 months, and for drug-resistant tuberculosis, it takes 18 to 24 months. The promotional materials also state that non-standard treatment can easily lead to drug resistance, and after drug resistance, the cure rate is low and the cost is high. A Cochrane review summarized 5 randomized trials. The trial reduced the standard 6-month treatment course to 4 months and added moxifloxacin. The relative risk of recurrence after treatment was RR 3.56 (95% CI 2.37–5.37). The probability of recurrence is approximately 3.6 times greater after 6 months of treatment (Global/China)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Health Order No. 92 (2013). Note: If someone in the family is diagnosed with infectious tuberculosis, the people who live with him and colleagues and classmates who often live together should also go to a designated hospital for a check-up. The "Tuberculosis Prevention and Management Measures" require designated hospitals to screen these close contacts. One analysis compiled 95 studies in low- and moderate-income areas. About 3.1% of close contacts had TB, and about 51.5% had latent infection. Latent infection means the bacteria are present in the body but are not causing illness and are not contagious. The national plan for 2024 requires that close contacts be tested for tuberculosis infection and those found to be latent infected are given preventive treatment. Practices vary from place to place, so ask the designated hospital when the time comes. National propaganda materials say that people with HIV infection, diabetes, pneumoconiosis patients, the elderly and people with low immunity are more susceptible to the disease and should be checked regularly every year. For AIDS, see Article 31 of this section (check AIDS once), and for blood sugar, see Article 8 of this section (check fasting blood sugar). If you want to go out of town during treatment, you should first inform the doctor in charge and find a local designated hospital for further treatment when you arrive in the new place. The common course of tuberculosis treatment written by the World Health Organization is to take medicine every day for 4 to 6 months, and domestic promotional materials state that it is 6 to 8 months. How long to take depends on the designated hospital, don’t shorten it yourself. For the general principle of taking the full amount of medicine as prescribed by the doctor, see Section 16, Article 1 (Take the full amount of medicine as prescribed by the doctor). The main beneficiary is yourself, but also your family members and people around you.

Case: Lao Wu had been coughing for more than a month, and his sputum was stained with blood. Taking medicine as a cold was ineffective. After going to a designated tuberculosis hospital to take X-rays and check sputum, he was diagnosed with tuberculosis. He took the full course of treatment according to the plan, and the sputum bacteria turned negative after re-examination, and the people living with him were also screened.

items.title: Quit smoking, the sooner the better
items.core: According to American studies, smokers live on average more than ten years less than non-smokers. Quitting before the age of 40 can eliminate about 90% of the risk of death caused by subsequent smoking. The earlier you quit, the more you will get back. If you continue to have a fracture after a fracture, the bone will more likely not grow back, so don't have a fracture until the bone has grown back.
body: Cost: No money, and in turn, you save money. A pack of cigarettes a day costs about 20–30 yuan, and if you quit, you will keep the money. The difficulty lies in enduring the withdrawal period, which usually lasts from a few weeks to a few months.

Benefits: A study in the United States that followed a group of people (only recorded, not grouped) found that people who are still smoking have a life expectancy that is more than 10 years shorter than those who have never smoked. Quitting before age 40 eliminates about 90% of the risk of death associated with continuing to smoke. Quitting smoking is associated with approximately 10 additional years of life at age 25–34, approximately 9 additional years at age 35–44, and approximately 6 additional years at age 45–54 (originally reported in life-years). Similar studies in China: In the 2010s, the risk of death for urban male smokers was 1.65 times that of non-smokers (RR 1.65), and for rural men it was 1.22 times. After 10 years of quitting, the risks associated with smoking are nearly gone. The same goes for after a fracture. Nineteen recording-only, no grouping studies were combined. The odds ratio for a fracture that did not heal (the bone failed to grow) was about 2.3 in smokers compared with nonsmokers (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.76–3.06, after adjusting for other factors). Tibial fractures and open fractures of the lower leg are equally high. In a Swedish randomized trial of 50 people who participated in a six-week smoking cessation program after emergency surgery for fractures, 20% experienced at least one postoperative complication. The 55 who did not participate were 38%. If the surgery is scheduled in advance, you can start quitting smoking 4 to 8 weeks before the surgery, with weekly counseling and nicotine replacement. Doing so resulted in about 58% fewer postoperative complications (RR 0.42, 95% CI 0.27–0.65, 2 trials, 210 people).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Jha P et al (2013). 21st-century hazards of smoking and benefits of cessation in the United States. NEJM. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)00340-2>; Oberg M et al (2011). Worldwide burden of disease from exposure to second-hand smoke: a retrospective analysis of data from 192 countries. Lancet. Cigarette smoking increases complications following fracture: a systematic review. J Bone Joint Surg Am. (2010). Effect of smoking cessation intervention on results of acute fracture surgery: a randomized controlled trial. J Bone Joint Surg Am. <https://doi.org/10.2106/JBJS.I.00627>; Thomsen T et al. (2014). Interventions for preoperative smoking cessation. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002294.pub4> (Numbers of fractures and surgeries)

Note: Smoking other people’s cigarettes can also kill people: In 2004, about 603,000 people died from second-hand smoke worldwide, accounting for about 1% of the total global deaths that year. If you don’t smoke yourself, you should also avoid other people’s cigarettes, especially your children. How to quit? The specific methods are in the following four items: Article 3 (smoking cessation medicine), Article 4 (setting a quit date), Article 5 (going to a smoking cessation clinic), and Article 6 (e-cigarettes). The number of bone non-union comes from a study that only records and does not group people into groups. Smokers may also be different from non-smokers in other aspects, so it cannot be fully deducted. That smoking cessation trial after fracture had only 105 people. The author converted to odds ratio and calculated it again, and the difference was not significant (OR 2.51, 95% CI 0.96–6.9).

Case: A 39-year-old driver smokes a pack of cigarettes a day. During the physical examination, the doctor reminded that the greatest benefit would be gained from quitting smoking before the age of 40. He threw away his smoking utensils that day and relied on the supervision of smoking cessation clinics and family members to persist. The morning cough disappeared half a year later, and the cough no longer occurred during the review of the fractured calf.

items.title: Don’t smoke at home or in the car, and don’t let guests smoke at home
items.core: In 2004, about 600,000 people around the world died from smoking other people’s cigarettes, nearly 30% of whom were children. People who breathe secondhand smoke are more likely to suffer from high blood pressure, heart disease and stroke. What you inhale at home is more harmful than what you inhale outside.
body: Cost: No money or time. The difficulty lies in asking family members and guests not to smoke at home.

Benefits: In 2004, 603,000 people died worldwide from secondhand smoke, accounting for approximately 1.0% of global deaths, 28% of whom were children. Taking the 57 studies combined, the odds ratio for high blood pressure was about 1.28 for people who were exposed to secondhand smoke compared to those who were not exposed to it. The odds ratios were 1.39 for heart disease, 1.50 for myocardial infarction, and 1.36 for stroke. The risk of secondhand smoke at home is higher than outside the home
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Öberg M, Jaakkola MS, Woodward A, Peruga A, Prüss-Ustün A (2011). Worldwide burden of disease from exposure to second-hand smoke: a retrospective analysis of data from 192 countries. Lancet: "603,000 deaths were attributable to second-hand smoke in 2004, which was about 1·0% of worldwide mortality. 47% of deaths from second-hand smoke occurred in women, 28% in children, and 26% in men", "61% of DALYs were in children". <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(10)61388-8>; (2026). The Associations Between Secondhand Smoke Exposure and Various Cardiovascular Diseases: A Meta-Analysis. Nicotine & Tobacco Research: 57 Study, "hypertension (OR: 1.28, 95% CI: 1.15 to 1.40), heart disease (OR: 1.39, 95% CI: 1.28 to 1.50), myocardial infarction (OR: 1.50, 95% CI: 1.17 to 1.84), stroke (OR: 1.36, 95% CI: 1.18 to 1.54)" "Home exposure has a higher risk of CVD than non-home exposure". <https://doi.org/10.1093/ntr/ntaf111>

Note: Take care of your home first, because you stay at home for a long time, and multiple studies have shown that secondhand smoke at home is more harmful than outside the home. 61% of the health losses caused by second-hand smoke fall on children. To quit smoking on your own, see No. 1 of this section.

Case: Mr. Zhang often smokes in the living room. His daughter, who is in elementary school, has been passively exposed to second-hand smoke for a long time and coughs frequently. Physical examination revealed that the respiratory tract is sensitive. The doctor clearly stated that it is directly related to the second-hand smoke environment at home.

items.title: Don’t just rely on tolerance to quit smoking, get the medicine first: the success rate of taking varenicline can more than double
items.core: The rate of quitting for people who take varenicline is more than twice that of taking a placebo. Those who use nicotine patches, chewing gum and other substitutes have about 50% higher rates than those who don’t use drugs. Using the patch and chewing gum together can increase the cost by more than 20%.
body: Cost: Nicotine patches and chewing gum are over-the-counter and available at pharmacies. A course of treatment lasts for 8 to 12 weeks and costs from a few hundred yuan to more than a thousand yuan. Varenicline and bupropion are prescription drugs and should be prescribed by a smoking cessation clinic or respiratory medicine department. This amount of money was roughly offset by the fewer cigarettes purchased during the same period.

Benefits: 41 randomized trials, 17,395 people combined, varenicline was 2.32 times more likely to quit smoking than placebo (RR 2.32, 95% CI 2.15–2.51, confidence range; high-certainty evidence). Varenicline was also higher than bupropion (RR 1.36, approximately 36% higher) and a nicotine replacement alternative alone (RR 1.25, approximately 25% higher). Nicotine replacement versus no drug: 133 trials, 64,640 people, approximately 55% more successful (RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.49–1.61). Adding the patch to a fast-acting dosage form (chewable gum, lozenge) was about 27% more effective than using one alone (RR 1.27, 95% CI 1.17–1.37, 16 trials, 12,169 people, high-certainty evidence). Side effects: Compared with placebo, people who took varenicline were about 2.6 times more likely to experience nausea (RR 2.61), about 37% more likely to have insomnia (RR 1.37), and more dreams. The review says that the most common symptom is nausea, which is mostly mild to moderate and usually subsides slowly. The instructions for a nicotine patch in the United States describe reducing dosage in three steps. Start with 21 mg for 6 weeks, then 14 mg for 2 weeks, and finally 7 mg for 2 weeks, then stop.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Livingstone-Banks J, Fanshawe TR, Thomas KH, et al. (2023). Nicotine receptor partial agonists for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 5, CD006103. Adverse events section); Hartmann-Boyce J, Chepkin SC, Ye W, Bullen C, Lancaster T (2018). Nicotine replacement therapy versus control for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 5, CD000146. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000146.pub5>; Theodoulou A, Chepkin SC, Ye W, et al. (2023). Different doses, durations and modes of delivery of nicotine replacement therapy for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 6, CD013308. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013308.pub2>; Shanghai Municipal Health Commission (2021). Choose the right medicine to make quitting smoking easier: "There are three main types of smoking cessation medicines on the market, namely nicotine replacement therapy drugs, bupropion, and varenicline." "Nicotine replacement therapy drugs are over-the-counter drugs (OTC) and can be purchased over the counter in pharmacies; while bupropion and varenicline are prescription drugs and must be seen in the hospital's smoking cessation clinic or respiratory medicine department, and can only be obtained after being prepared by a pharmacist with a doctor's prescription." <https://wsjkw.sh.gov.cn/jtyx/20211119/df50681e01ba49f896d54f771d8176ae.html>; Haleon (2025). NICODERM CQ (nicotine) patch, extended release. DailyMed instructions: "use according to the following 10-week schedule: STEP 1 … 21 mg patch/day … Weeks 1-6 … 14 mg … Weeks 7-8 … 7 mg … Weeks 9-10”. <https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=93b2d1b9-83c1-40b5-b6af-90c38c8d6cef> (the sentence about patch reduction)

Note: The smoking cessation drugs sold in China are of the above three categories, and only nicotine replacement drugs are over-the-counter drugs. Common reactions to varenicline are nausea, dreaminess, and inability to sleep. If you have a history of mental illness, you should inform your doctor. This is the author's recommendation. The course of nicotine replacement treatment generally lasts for 8 to 12 weeks. The patch should be gradually reduced and stopped according to the instructions or the doctor's instructions. Medication only solves the discomfort during the few weeks of withdrawal, but does not solve the problem of "wanting to smoke", so it should be used together with Article 4 (Set a quit date) and Article 5 (Go to a smoking cessation clinic) in this section.

Case: Lao Zhou has been smoking for 20 years. He tried hard to quit smoking twice but failed. Later, he took varenicline under the guidance of a doctor and made simple behavioral adjustments. After three months, he stopped smoking completely.

items.title: Set a date to quit smoking. You can stop all at once, or you can first slowly reduce it to no smoking at all.
items.core: Stop all at once, or first slowly reduce it to no smoking at all. You can choose either method. In a British study, 22% of those who stopped smoking stopped smoking after six months, and only 15.5% of those who gradually reduced their smoking. But taking more studies together, it’s still unclear which one is better in the long run. Choose one that reduces slowly, and the goal is not to smoke a single ounce.
body: Cost: No money. Just pick a day on your calendar and tell your family and colleagues in advance.

Benefits: In 2016, 697 smokers in the UK were randomly divided into two groups. One group stopped all at once on the quit day, and the other group cut back 75% of their cigarettes two weeks before the quit day. Both groups received behavioral support from nurses and used nicotine replacement before and after the quit date. At week 4, 49.0% (95% CI 43.8–54.2, which is the confidence range) of the once-off group had not relapsed, and 39.2% (34.0–44.4) of the slow-down group had a relative risk of 0.80 (0.66–0.93). By month 6, the one-off group was 22.0% (18.0–26.6) and the slow-down group was 15.5% (12.0–19.7), with a relative risk of 0.71 (0.46–0.91). People who originally preferred a gradual taper also had a lower success rate at week 4 than those who preferred a one-stop approach (38.3% vs. 52.2%). A 2019 Cochrane review combined 22 studies, involving 9,219 people, comparing success rates in quitting smoking after at least 6 months. The relative risk of tapering and then quitting compared with stopping was RR 1.01 (95% CI 0.87–1.17). The evidence is moderately certain and does not yet show which approach is better in the long term, nor does it suggest that either approach is equally effective.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Lindson-Hawley N, Banting M, West R, Michie S, Shinkins B, Aveyard P (2016). Gradual Versus Abrupt Smoking Cessation: A Randomized, Controlled Noninferiority Trial. Annals of Internal Medicine, 164(9), 585–592. <https://doi.org/10.7326/M14-2805>; Lindson N, Klemperer E, Hong B, Ordóñez-Mena JM, Aveyard P (2019). Smoking reduction interventions for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 9, CD013183. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013183.pub2>; Theodoulou A, Chepkin SC, Ye W, et al. (2023). Different doses, durations and modes of delivery of nicotine replacement therapy for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 6, CD013308 (the section on the use of nicotine replacement therapy in advance). <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013308.pub2>

Note: Controversy. The 2016 trial supported a single stop but was not a substitute for the combined judgment of more studies in the 2019 review. The review's estimates remain uncertain, and the long-term success rate of tapering first may be slightly higher or lower. Choose to reduce slowly first. The goal is to quit smoking completely, not to smoke less cigarettes all the time. In addition, in that trial, both groups started using nicotine replacement before the quit date. There is also evidence for this practice: using it in advance is about 25% more successful than starting on the quit date (RR 1.25, 95% CI 1.08–1.44, 9 trials, 4395 people, moderate certainty evidence). The evidence for early dosing does not mean that stopping all at once is better than reducing the dose first.

Case: Ms. Li chose New Year's Day as the day to quit smoking. Instead of suddenly stopping smoking, she reduced one cigarette a day and stopped smoking completely after two and a half months. When she was reviewed at the end of the year, her lung discomfort symptoms were significantly reduced.

items.title: Go to the smoking cessation clinic, or call 12320 to ask if there are any local smoking cessation services
items.core: Medicine and "someone asking you regularly" are two different things, and they are more effective together. The rate of quitting for people who took medicine while having someone follow them up was nearly twice as high as for people who only listened to a brief piece of advice. Phone calls also count: the quit hotline has taken the initiative to call back many times, and the success rate is as high as 25% to nearly 40%.
body: Cost: A few yuan to dozens of yuan for registering a number. Behavioral support typically consists of 4 to 8 interviews, lasting from half an hour to an hour each, and up to 5 hours in total. There is no cost to call the hotline.

Benefits: 52 trials, 19,488 people combined, medication plus behavioral support was 1.83 times more likely to quit smoking than usual care or brief advice (RR 1.83, 95% CI 1.68–1.98, confidence range; high-quality evidence). Among the 43 trials recruiting from healthcare settings it was 1.97 times (1.79–2.18). Telephone consultation is calculated separately: among those who have called the quit hotline themselves, those who have received multiple proactive follow-up interviews are about 38% higher than those who only received materials or had only one conversation (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.19–1.61, 14 trials, 32484 people); those who have not actively called the hotline and are provided with telephone consultation by the researcher, the rate is about 25% higher (RR 1.25, 95% CI 1.15–1.35, 65 trials, 41233 people). Both were moderately certain evidence.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Stead LF, Koilpillai P, Fanshawe TR, Lancaster T (2016). Combined pharmacotherapy and behavioral interventions for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 3, CD008286. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008286.pub3>; Matkin W, Ordóñez-Mena JM, Hartmann-Boyce J (2019). Telephone counseling for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 5, CD002850. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002850.pub4>; Chinese Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (2021). "China Smoking Smoking Platform" WeChat applet is officially launched: "Under the guidance of the Healthy China Action Tobacco Control Action Working Group, the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention and the World Health Organization Representative Office in China jointly produced China's authoritative smoking cessation resource library "China Smoking Smoking Platform" WeChat applet. The content of the applet mainly includes: smoking cessation hotline, detailed information on smoking cessation clinics, and online smoking cessation service resources, etc."; the footer of the same site is marked with "Health consultation hotline: 12320". <https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkyj/yckz/gzdt/202203/t20220310_296389.html>

Remarks: How to find it in China: Search the "China Smoking Smoking Platform" applet on WeChat, which has a list of smoking cessation hotlines and smoking cessation clinics in various places; you can also call 12320 to ask if there are any local smoking cessation clinics. Most of the above experiments were conducted abroad, and the service intensity of smoking cessation clinics in different places varies greatly, so the numbers can only be used as a guide. The medicines to be dispensed are listed in Section 3 of this section (Smoking Cessation Medicines).

Case: Mr. Wang set up a file in the smoking cessation clinic and received regular check-ups and medication. The nurse followed up by phone every week. Even though he wanted to relapse many times, he was promptly dissuaded. He successfully quit smoking six months later and his weight has not rebounded significantly.

items.title: If you can’t quit, then consider e-cigarettes. People who don’t smoke should not try them.
items.core: If you switch cigarettes to nicotine-containing e-cigarettes, about 60% more people will quit than if you use nicotine substitutes. This conclusion is very reliable. However, there is not enough safety data on long-term smoking to treat it as harmless. These trials compare people who want to quit smoking, and should not be used by non-smokers.
body: Cost: Equipment and cartridges cost tens to hundreds of yuan per month. You can only buy tobacco-flavored ones in China, and you can only buy them in stores with a tobacco retail license.

Benefits: An ongoing review including 80 randomized trials, 29,861 people. Nicotine-containing e-cigarettes are about 61% more likely to quit smoking than nicotine replacement therapy (RR 1.61, 95% CI 1.23–2.12, confidence range; high-certainty evidence, 11 trials, 4114 people). In absolute terms, it is about 4 more people taking ordination for every 100 people (1 to 7 more people). The proportion of serious adverse events was approximately similar in both groups (risk difference 0.01, 95% CI −0.01 to 0.02, moderate-certainty evidence). and behavioral support only or no support, approximately 75% higher (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.39–2.20, low-certainty evidence).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Lindson N, Livingstone-Banks J, Butler AR, et al. (2026). Electronic cigarettes for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 8, CD010216. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD010216.pub11>; State Tobacco Monopoly Administration (2022). E-cigarette Management Measures (State Tobacco Monopoly Administration Announcement No. 1 of 2022, effective on May 1, 2022) Article 18: To engage in e-cigarette retail business, you must apply for a tobacco monopoly retail license from the tobacco monopoly administrative department. Article 22: "It is prohibited to sell e-cigarette products to minors." Paragraph 2 of Article 23: "Any individual, legal person or other organization shall not sell e-cigarette products, aerosols and nicotine for e-cigarettes through information networks other than the e-cigarette transaction management platform stipulated in these Measures." Article 26: "It is prohibited to sell flavored e-cigarettes other than tobacco flavors and e-cigarettes that can add aerosols by themselves.". <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5697988.htm>; World Health Organization (2023-12-14).
