Urgent action needed to protect children and prevent the uptake of e-cigarettes: "E-cigarettes as consumer products are not shown to be effective for quitting tobacco use at the population level" "it is not recommended that governments permit sale of e-cigarettes as consumer products in pursuit of a cessation objective" "Whilst long-term health effects are not fully understood". <https://www.who.int/news/item/14-12-2023-urgent-action-needed-to-protect-children-and-prevent-the-uptake-of-e-cigarettes>; Department of Health and Social Care (2023-04-11). Smokers urged to swap cigarettes for vapes in world first scheme: "almost 1 in 5 of all smokers in England will be provided with a vape starter kit alongside behavioral support”. <https://www.gov.uk/government/news/smokers-urged-to-swap-cigarettes-for-vapes-in-world-first-scheme>; Supreme People’s Procuratorate (2021). Wujiang District, Suzhou, Jiangsu: The prosecutor handling the case revealed a new type of drug disguised as a trend: "This "top" e-cigarette contains synthetic cannabinoid ingredients that are listed as a whole category by the state." <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202110/t20211011_531831.shtml>

Remarks: Controversy. The World Health Organization said in 2023 that e-cigarettes are sold as ordinary commodities and there is no evidence that they can help people quit smoking. It does not recommend that the government liberalize the sale of e-cigarettes for the purpose of quitting smoking, but treat them as medicine if they are to be used. It also said the long-term health effects were not fully understood and it was concerned children and young people would start smoking as a result. Starting in 2023, England will go in the opposite direction and issue e-cigarette starter kits to about one million smokers, along with smoking cessation counseling. There is not a complete ban on the sale of e-cigarettes in China, but the regulations are very strict, and the rules are written in the "E-Cigarette Management Measures". Only tobacco-flavored ones are allowed to be sold, fruit-flavored ones and those that can add your own e-liquid are not allowed to be sold. You can only buy it at physical stores with a tobacco retail license. In addition to the national unified e-cigarette transaction management platform, selling on other websites, online stores and social software is illegal. It is also not allowed to be sold to minors. Therefore, the fruit-flavored e-cigarettes that can still be purchased are through illegal channels and are not under supervision. This is how the "top e-cigarette" mixed with synthetic cannabinoids comes out, see Section 22, Article 4 (Do not accept cigarette cartridges from others). The products tested in the review are all regulated nicotine-containing products, and e-liquids of unknown origin are not included. In order, try item 3 of this section (smoking cessation drugs) first, as the evidence there is stronger and cheaper.

Case: Lao Chen failed to quit smoking many times. After evaluation, he switched to compliant e-cigarettes, gradually reduced the nicotine concentration, and stopped using them completely after a year. His colleagues who had never smoked followed suit and soon developed throat discomfort.

items.title: Not drinking sugary drinks or switching to sugar-free ones is not a solution
items.core: According to American studies, people who drink more than two sweet drinks a day have a risk of death that is about 20% higher than those who hardly drink. One to two servings per day is more than 10% higher. There is no benefit in switching to sugar-free drinks: those who drink more than two cups of sugar-replacement drinks a day are about a quarter more likely to drink sugar-free drinks.
body: Cost: No money or time. You can also save money by switching to plain water or sugar-free tea. The difficulty lies in breaking the habit of drinking sweet drinks, including sugar-free ones.

Benefits: There are two large studies in the United States that follow a group of people. These two items are only recorded without grouping, and there are about 118,000 people and 36,000 deaths. People who drank more than 2 servings per day had about a 21% higher risk of death (HR 1.21) than those who drank less than 1 serving per month. Drinking 1–2 servings per day was about 14% higher (HR 1.14). The European EPIC tracking study only records, without grouping, 450,000 people in 10 countries. Sugary soft drinks were about 8% more common among those who drank more than 2 cups per day compared with those who drank less than 1 cup per month (HR 1.08, 95% CI 1.01–1.16). Artificially sweetened drinks (sugar-free version) were about 26% higher (HR 1.26, 1.16–1.35). All soft drinks combined were about 17% higher (HR 1.17, 1.11–1.22).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Malik VS et al. (2019). Long-Term Consumption of Sugar-Sweetened and Artificially Sweetened Beverages and Risk of Mortality in US Adults. Circulation. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.118.037401>; Mullee A, Romaguera D, Pearson-Stuttard J, et al. (2019). Association Between Soft Drink Consumption and Mortality in 10 European Countries. JAMA Internal Medicine, 179(11), 1479-1490. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2019.2478>

Note: The controversy is over sugar-free drinks. The association with sugar-substitute drinks is stronger than that with sugar-containing drinks. This may be because the cause and effect are reversed: only people who are already overweight or have diabetes switch to the sugar-free version. So don’t use this to say that sugar substitutes are more poisonous. But it at least shows that there is no evidence to support the statement "it will be fine if you switch to sugar-free". It is safest to switch to plain water or sugar-free tea. In addition, this type of research is only a follow-up record and does not conduct group experiments. People who drink more sweet drinks have worse lifestyles, so the numbers may be on the high side.

Case: Xiao Zhou, a college student, drinks two cups of fruity soda every day, and later switched to sugar-free sugar-substitute drinks. During the physical examination, he still found that his blood sugar fluctuated greatly. The doctor reminded him that sugar-substitute drinks also have metabolic risks and should not be taken lightly.

items.title: Do not chew betel nut
items.core: People who chew betel nut are about 20% more likely to die during the same period than those who do not chew it. The risk of diabetes and metabolic syndrome is about 50% higher. The risks of oral cancer and esophageal cancer are additional.
body: Cost: It doesn’t cost money, it doesn’t take up time, and it also saves money on buying betel nuts. The hard part is breaking the habit of chewing.

Revenue: 17 Asian studies, 388,000 people combined. People who chewed betel nut had an approximately 21% higher risk of death than those who did not chew it (relative risk 1.21, P=0.02). Deaths are counted among those 179,600. The risk of developing diabetes was about 47% higher (1.47). The risk of developing metabolic syndrome was about 51% higher (1.51). Betel nut itself is also a known risk factor for oral and esophageal cancer. Oral cancer: Combining 50 studies, chewing betel nut without tobacco in the Indian subcontinent was associated with approximately 2.56 times the risk of oral and oropharyngeal cancer (95% CI 2.00–3.28). About 7.74 times (5.38–11.13) with added tobacco. Taiwanese betel nut chewed without tobacco is about 10.98 times (4.86–24.84). In India and Taiwan, the more people chew each day and the longer they chew, the higher the risk. Esophageal cancer: When 12 Asian studies were combined, the odds ratio for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma among betel nut chewers was approximately 3.05 (2.41–3.87). The odds ratio for chewing betel nut and smoking was approximately 6.79 (4.71–9.79). This outcome is rare in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, and the odds ratios and relative risks are similar. After quitting: 13 studies combined showed that the risk of head and neck cancer in people who quit tobacco-spiked betel nut was about 34% lower than those who still chewed it (RR 0.66, 0.54–0.81). Those who quit smoking were about 27% lower (RR 0.73, 0.56–0.95). Those who had been abstaining for more than 20 years were about 63% lower (RR 0.37, 0.22–0.61).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Yamada T, Hara K, Kadowaki T (2013). Chewing betel quid and the risk of metabolic disease, cardiovascular disease, and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis. PLoS One, 8(8), e70679. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0070679>; Guha N, Warnakulasuriya S, Vlaanderen J, Straif K (2014). Betel quid chewing and the risk of oral and oropharyngeal cancers: a meta-analysis with implications for cancer control. International Journal of Cancer, 135(6), 1433-1443. <https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.28643>; Akhtar S (2013). Areca nut chewing and esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma risk in Asians: a meta-analysis of case-control studies. Cancer Causes & Control, 24(2), 257-265. Shah K, Boffetta P, Seyyedsalehi MS (2025). Reversal of head and neck cancer risk after the cessation of use of smokeless tobacco and betel quid use: meta-analysis. Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 34(5), 619-626. <https://doi.org/10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-24-1502>

Note: The longer you chew and the more you chew every day, the higher the risk of oral cancer. After you quit, the risk will go down over time. In an Indian study, betel nut mixed with tobacco was more dangerous than those without tobacco. Most of the chewing in Taiwan is without tobacco, and the risk is also very high.

Case: A middle-aged man in Hunan has been chewing betel nut for ten years, at least one pack a day. Later, he developed oral mucosal fibrosis and was diagnosed as a precancerous lesion. The doctor clearly told him that this was directly related to long-term chewing of betel nut.

items.title: Change the salt at home to low-sodium salt (potassium salt)
items.core: People in rural China who have had a stroke or have high blood pressure over the age of 60 have changed the salt at home to low-sodium salt for nearly five years. The probability of death is about 12% lower and the probability of stroke is about 14% lower.
body: Cost: A bag is a few yuan more expensive than ordinary salt. You can change it easily when you buy it, so it doesn’t take up any extra time. The taste remains almost unchanged.

Benefits: A trial in which people were randomly divided into two groups was conducted in rural China. 20,995 people were all people who had suffered a stroke or patients with hypertension over 60 years old. They were followed for 4.74 years. Results: The risk of death was about 12% lower in the low-sodium salt group than in the regular salt group (RR 0.88). Stroke was about 14% lower (RR 0.86). Major cardiovascular events were approximately 13% lower (RR 0.87). In terms of hyperkalemia events, no statistical difference was seen between the two groups.
Level of Evidence: A
Source: Neal B et al. (2021). Effect of Salt Substitution on Cardiovascular Events and Death. NEJM. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1311889>(Disputing Party PURE)

Remarks: Disputed. This PURE study only has long-term follow-up records and does not group groups. It reports: People who excreted less than 3 grams of sodium a day had about a 27 percent higher risk of death and cardiovascular events. For people who excrete more than 7 g of sodium a day, the level is about 15% higher. According to its results, neither too little nor too much is good, and the middle is best. However, in the randomized trial in rural China cited in this article, low-sodium salt only replaced part of the diet and did not reduce the sodium level so low. Also note that the test subjects are high-risk elderly people. Healthy young people gain much less benefit from salt switching. People with renal insufficiency, or those taking potassium-sparing drugs, should ask their doctor before changing salt.

Case: An elderly man with high blood pressure in a northern rural area changed the daily iodized salt used at home to low-sodium salt. He persisted for nearly five years. During this period, he did not have a stroke. The physical examination showed that his blood pressure was more stable, and he no longer had to worry about excessive salt intake.

items.title: Brush your teeth carefully, clean between your teeth once a day, and go to the dentist if you have missing teeth
items.core: In a Japanese study, people who flossed or brushed between their teeth had about a 10% lower risk of death. Elderly people who have lost all their teeth and have less than 20 teeth left have a significantly higher risk of death. An electric toothbrush removes 10% to 20% more plaque than a manual toothbrush, and the gum inflammation is less severe, but it is unclear how useful this difference is.
body: Cost: flossing or interdental brushing costs tens of yuan a year, and teeth cleaning costs one or two hundred yuan each time. Spend an extra two or three minutes every day. The hard part is turning teeth cleaning into something you do every day. If the manual toothbrush is not clean, you can replace it with an electric toothbrush, which costs a few hundred yuan. The brush head should be replaced regularly.

Benefits: There is a study in Japan, 9676 people, followed for 6 years. People who used interdental cleaning tools had about an 11% lower risk of death (hazard ratio 0.89). Those who used tongue cleaning tools were about 23% lower (0.77). In addition, multiple studies were combined and the subjects were elderly people living in the community. For those without a single tooth, the odds ratio for death was about 1.87 (95% CI 1.35–2.59, which is the confidence range). For those with fewer than 20 teeth, the odds ratio was approximately 2.04 (1.67–2.49). Odds ratios cannot be read directly as multiples of the probability of death. Electric vs. manual: Combining 51 randomized trials, electric brushes removed about 11% less plaque when used for 1 to 3 months, and about 21% less after 3 months. Gingivitis was milder by about 6% and 11% respectively. How important these differences are for health is unclear, the review authors say
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Wang K, Matsuyama Y, Kiuchi S, et al. (2026). Routine oral health practices and all-cause mortality. Journal of Dentistry. Deteriorated oral health and function as risk factors for physical disability and mortality in community-dwelling older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. European Geriatric Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s41999-025-01319-4>; Yaacob M, Worthington HV, Deacon SA, et al. (2014). Powered versus manual toothbrushing for oral health. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002281.pub3>; Deacon SA, Glenny AM, Deery C, et al. (2010). Different powered toothbrushes for plaque control and gingival health. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004971.pub2>

Note: Controversy. This type of research is just a track record. People with bad teeth often have poor overall health and financial status. Whether it is the teeth that are dragging down the body or poor health that is dragging down the teeth, I can’t tell. But this is extremely low cost, and periodontitis and missing teeth themselves affect eating. Among electric toothbrushes, the round head that rotates the brush head back and forth has the most tests (27 tests). Compared with manual brushes, plaque and gingivitis are significantly reduced in both the short and long term. No research has been conducted to determine whether filling missing teeth can reduce deaths. It is recommended that fillings be made because missing teeth affect eating, and this is the author’s judgment. Among different types of electric toothbrushes, an independent review could not draw a conclusion because there were too few trials. How much does it cost to implant a tooth and which dental care items are covered by medical insurance? See Section 24, Article 12 (ask about the lump sum price before dental implantation)

Case: An old man in Japan insists on cleaning the gaps between his teeth with an interdental brush every day, brushes his teeth carefully in the morning and evening, and fills his teeth regularly. At the age of 80, he still has 22 natural teeth, good chewing function, and his physical condition is much better than that of his peers.

items.title: Walk 7,000–8,000 steps a day, or briskly walk for 150–300 minutes a week
items.core: People who walk about 7,800 steps a day have a risk of death that is about 45% lower than those who only walk 3,500 steps. The same applies in terms of time. Brisk walking for 150-300 minutes per week is about 30% lower than no exercise. When it reaches a certain amount, it will no longer go down. For those over 60 years old, walking to 6000-8000 steps is enough. Just one of the two numbering methods meets the standard.
body: Cost: No money. In terms of steps, walking is 60–90 minutes a day, which can be divided into commuting and grocery shopping. In terms of exercise time, 20–45 minutes per day. The difficulty lies in persisting for a long time.

Benefit: Combined 15 studies that tracked a group of people, only records, not groups. These 15 cases totaled 47,471 people and 3,013 deaths. People are divided into four categories according to the number of steps per day. The median of the lowest category is 3553 steps/day. The medians for the other three grades were 5801, 7842, and 10901 steps/day. The risk of death in these three brackets is approximately 40%, 45%, and 53% lower than the lowest bracket, respectively (HR 0.60, 0.55, 0.47). For people over 60 years old, after walking 6,000–8,000 steps, the benefits level off from taking more steps. For people under 60 years old, levels level off after 8,000–10,000 steps. Another analysis combined multiple studies and found it effective starting at about 3867 steps/day. For every additional 1,000 steps/day thereafter, the risk of death decreased by approximately 15%. Calculated by exercise time: Taking multiple tracking studies together (recording only, not grouping), people who exercise 1–2 times the lower limit of the guideline have a mortality risk about 31% lower than those who do not exercise (HR 0.69). This amount is 7.5–15 MET·h/week, which is approximately equivalent to brisk walking for 150–300 minutes/week. Those who did not reach the lower limit were also about 20% lower (HR 0.80). Those who reached 3–5 times the lower limit were about 39% lower (HR 0.61), which was the peak of the decline. Going higher won't get any lower, but there's no harm in it (10 times more is HR 0.69). Another pooled study using accelerometer measurements: The quartile of people with the most moderate-to-vigorous activity had about a 48% lower risk of death than the quartile with the least (HR 0.52). An accelerometer is an instrument worn on the body to measure activity. The pooled data included 8 studies and 36,383 people, with an average age of 62.6 years and a median follow-up of just 5.8 years. The authors of the paper removed those who died within the first two years and recalculated, and the results were basically unchanged. However, they also said that the bias caused by "people who move less when they are sick" may still be there.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Paluch AE et al (2022). Daily steps and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis of 15 international cohorts. Lancet Public Health. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-2667(21)00302-9>; Banach M et al (2023). Cardiology. <https://doi.org/10.1093/eurjpc/zwad229>; Arem H et al. (2015). Leisure time physical activity and mortality: a detailed pooled analysis of the dose-response relationship. JAMA Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2015.0533>; Ekelund U et al. (2019). Dose-response associations between accelerometry measured physical activity and sedentary time and all cause mortality: systematic review and harmonised meta-analysis. BMJ. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.l4570>

Note: The number of steps and exercise time say the same thing, they just change the counting method, and one of them is enough. The most cost-effective step is to add from 4,000 steps to 7,000 steps. You don’t have to go to 10,000 steps. It should be noted that this kind of research is just a follow-up record: among the people who walked the least and moved the least, there were also people who were sick and unable to walk. They move less because they are dying, not because they move less so they die early. Therefore, the calculated gap is often too large. For those items that use instruments to measure activity, the tracking time is short and the participants tend to be older. Therefore, "risk ratio 0.52, about 48% lower" may be too high. This is the inference of this book. But the trend of more movement is clear.

Case: Retired Uncle Zhao used to only walk more than 3,000 steps a day. Later, he insisted on walking briskly for 40 minutes every evening, about 7,500 steps. Six months later, he had a physical examination and found that his blood pressure and blood lipids had dropped. The doctor said that the risk of death was significantly reduced.

items.title: Check your blood lipids regularly in adulthood, once every 2 to 5 years before the age of 40 and once a year from the age of 40. If you have high blood pressure or high blood lipids, take medicine as prescribed by your doctor and do not stop on your own
items.core: For every 10 mmHg drop in blood pressure, the probability of death is reduced by about 13%, and the probability of stroke is reduced by about 27%. Statins lower LDL cholesterol by 1 unit, and the probability of death is reduced by about 10%. People who take medicine on time are 30% to 45% less likely to die than those who often miss it. Blood lipids should be checked every 2 to 5 years before the age of 40, and every year starting from the age of 40.
body: Cost: Centrally purchased antihypertensive drugs and statins range from a few yuan to dozens of yuan per month. It doesn’t take much time to eat once a day. The difficulty is that you have to keep eating, and you can't stop just when you think it's okay. To check your blood lipids, you need to draw a tube of blood. People over 65 years old have a free physical examination every year, which includes blood lipids, see Section 6, Item 18 (Universal Physical Examination Package).

Benefits: Combining multiple randomized trials: for every 10 mmHg decrease in systolic blood pressure, the risk of death is reduced by approximately 13% (RR 0.87). Systolic blood pressure is the high pressure in blood pressure. Major cardiovascular events were approximately 20% lower (RR 0.80). Stroke was about 27% lower (RR 0.73). heart failure was about 28% lower (RR 0.72). Taking statins lowers low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL). For each 1.0 mmol/L decrease in LDL, the risk of death was approximately 10% lower (RR 0.90). For the same reduction, major vascular events were approximately 22% lower (RR 0.78). In addition, multiple tracking studies are combined and only recorded, not grouped. People who eat ≥80% of what their doctor recommends have a lower risk of death than those who regularly skip meals. This was about 45% lower for statins (RR 0.55). Antihypertensive medication was about 29% lower (RR 0.71). How often should blood lipids be checked? According to the recommendations of Healthy China Action: People under 40 years old with normal blood lipids should have their blood lipids checked every 2 to 5 years. People 40 and older should get tested at least once a year. People at high risk of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases should be screened every 6 months. The 2023 version of China's Blood Lipid Management Guidelines is written in the same way for people around the age of 40. For high-risk people, it is changed to check according to individual needs.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ettehad D et al (2016). Blood pressure lowering for prevention of cardiovascular disease and death: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Lancet. a meta-analysis of data from 170 000 participants in 26 randomized trials. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(10)61350-5>; Chowdhury R et al (2013). Adherence to cardiovascular therapy: a meta-analysis of prevalence and clinical consequences. European Heart Journal. <https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/eht295>; Healthy China Action Promotion Committee (2019). Healthy China Action (2019-2030), (11) Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Disease Prevention and Control Action (Reprinted by Hunan Provincial Health Commission). <https://wjw.hunan.gov.cn/wjw/ztzl/knowledge/tzggzcfg/202003/t20200303_11359594.html>; Joint Committee on the Chinese Guidelines for Lipid Management (2023). Chinese Journal of Cardiovascular Disease, 51(3), 221-255. <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.cn112148-20230119-00038>; Li JJ et al. (2023). 2023 Chinese guideline for lipid management. Frontiers in Pharmacology, 14, 1190934 (The English version of the previous guideline, the original Chinese text is not available, and the relevant content is checked against the English version). <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2023.1190934>

Note: Only those whose doctors judge that they should take medicine should do so. Healthy people do not need to take it. How often to check blood lipids is the official recommendation. There is no test that is better than checking once every few years. If someone in the family suffers from familial hypercholesterolemia (a hereditary disease in which people are born with extremely high cholesterol), their first- and second-degree relatives will have their blood lipids checked. If the parents’ total cholesterol is ≥6.2 mmol/L, the children should also be checked. If a first- or second-degree relative has had a myocardial infarction, stroke or sudden death before the age of 55 for a male or 65 for a female, the children should also be checked. The numbers for "Insisting on taking medicine" come from tracking records. People who can insist on taking medicine are more self-disciplined, so they will maximize the benefits. The numbers from the first two randomized trials are more reliable. This section does not include a separate article on blood sugar control: the evidence of the benefits of lowering blood sugar on total mortality is not as consistent as that of blood pressure and blood lipids. Those with high blood pressure and diabetes should have their kidneys checked every year, see Section 16, Item 13 (urinary albumin to creatinine ratio).

Case: An old man with a 40-year history of hypertension insists on taking antihypertensive drugs and statins regularly every day, and his blood lipids and blood pressure are controlled to meet the standards. He is reviewed regularly and has never stopped taking medication on his own because his indicators have improved.

items.title: Sleep about 7 hours a night with a fixed schedule
items.core: People who sleep less than 7 hours for a long time have a 10% higher chance of dying during the same period. The more chaotic the routine, the higher the risk. Compared with the group of people with the most chaotic work and rest schedules, other people’s income levels are 20% to nearly 50% lower. Irregular sleep schedules are a greater indicator of mortality risk than how much sleep you get.
body: Cost: No money. To take time to sleep, most people switch the time they use to check their phones to sleep. The difficulty lies in fixing the point of going to bed and getting up.

Income: Taking the 16 tracking studies together, only recording without grouping, there were 1.38 million people and 113,000 deaths. People who slept short had about a 12% higher risk of death (RR 1.12). About 30% higher among those who slept longer (RR 1.30). Another summary was broken down into sleep duration bins: the seven-hour bin had the lowest risk. Less than 7 hours, about 6% higher for every hour less (RR 1.06). Each additional hour above 7 hours was about 13% higher (RR 1.13). The British Biobank has watch records of about 61,000 people, which are only recorded and not grouped. Divide people into five levels according to their work and rest patterns. The four more regular brackets had a 20%–48% lower risk of death than the least regular bracket. An irregular sleep schedule is a better predictor of death than how much sleep you get. Another study by the British Biobank used watches to measure the sleep duration of 51,562 people, of which 3,853 had new cardiovascular diseases. Social jet lag refers to the difference between sleep middays on weekdays and weekends. People with a social jet lag of more than 2 hours had about a 30% higher risk of cardiovascular disease (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11–1.54). This association also existed among people who slept for normal hours.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Cappuccio FP et al (2010). Sleep duration and all-cause mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective studies. Sleep. of Prospective Cohort Studies. JAHA. <https://doi.org/10.1161/JAHA.117.005947>; Windred DP et al. (2024). Sleep regularity is a stronger predictor of mortality risk than sleep duration: A prospective cohort study. (2026). Social jet lag is associated with incident cardiovascular disease independent of sleep duration and cardiac genetic risk. Journal of Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1111/joim.70133>

Note: What needs to be changed is sleeping too little and having a disorderly schedule. There is no need to deliberately compress sleep time. People who sleep longer are at higher risk, and it's probably the other way around: depression, chronic illness, and sleep apnea make people sleep more. In addition, work and rest patterns are currently supported by two follow-up studies, both of which only record and do not group people. Taken alone, they are Level B evidence. How to catch up on sleep after staying up late, see Article 38 of this section (catching up on sleep the next night after staying up late). How to treat long-term insomnia, see Section 3, Item 26 (Cognitive behavioral therapy first for long-term insomnia).

Case: Xiao Lin, an office worker, used to only sleep for more than five hours a day and crazily catch up on sleep on weekends. Later, he changed to a fixed seven hours of sleep a day and went to bed at 11 o'clock at night. After half a year, he felt better during the day and his physical examination indicators were more stable.

items.title: People who often play racket sports such as tennis, badminton, and table tennis
items.core: People who often play tennis, badminton, and table tennis have a death risk about half lower than those who do not play, and cardiovascular death is about 56% lower. Swimmers were about 28% lower. There is no difference between running and football in this data.
body: Cost: Venue fee is tens of yuan each time. About 2 hours per week. The difficulty is getting the people and the venue together, and having to go every week.

Benefits: A UK study that followed 80,300 people, comparing people who did a certain sport to those who didn't. People who played racket sports had an approximately 47% lower risk of death (hazard ratio 0.53, 95% CI 0.40–0.69, confidence range). Cardiovascular death was approximately 56% lower (0.44, 0.24–0.83). Rackets refer to tennis, badminton, and table tennis. For swimmers the numbers were 0.72 and 0.59, for aerobics 0.73 and 0.64, and for bikers 0.85. No statistical difference was seen between running and football
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Oja P, Kelly P, Pedisic Z, et al. (2017). Associations of specific types of sports and exercise with all-cause and cardiovascular-disease mortality: a cohort study of 80 306 British adults. British Journal of Sports Medicine, 51(10), 812-817. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2016-096822>

Note: Controversy. This type of research is just a track record. People who play are healthier and socialize more. There was no difference in the running group, which also shows that what matters may be "what kind of people choose which exercise." Don’t think that running is useless just because of this. There are other items in this section that are calculated based on the total amount of exercise.

Case: After Lao Zhou retired, he went to the community court to play badminton every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday afternoon for one hour each time. After two years of persistence, a physical examination showed that his blood lipids and blood pressure were better than those of his peers, and he no longer breathed when climbing stairs.

items.title: Save up sporadic strenuous activities such as climbing stairs and walking briskly to four or five minutes a day
items.core: For people who do not exercise at all, as long as they have one or two minutes of strenuous activity three times a day, the risk of death is about 40% lower than that of people who do not do it at all, and cardiovascular death is nearly half lower. Exertional activities include climbing stairs and walking quickly.
body: Cost: No money, no extra time to exercise. The difficulty is to remember to take the stairs and walk faster, don't try to save trouble.

Benefits: The British Biobank conducted a study of 25,200 people who did not regularly exercise. During an average follow-up of 6.9 years, 852 individuals died. Some people engage in sporadic strenuous activity for 1–2 minutes three times a day. Their risk of death and cancer death was 38%–40% lower than those who had none. The risk of cardiovascular death is reduced by 48%–49%. People who accumulated 4.4 minutes of such activity per day had a 26%–30% lower risk of death and cancer death. 32%–34% lower risk of cardiovascular death
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Stamatakis E, Ahmadi MN, Gill JMR, et al. (2022). Association of wearable device-measured vigorous intermittent lifestyle physical activity with mortality. Nature Medicine, 28, 2521-2529. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-022-02100-x>

Note: Controversy. This study used wearable devices to actually measure activity levels, which is more reliable than having people fill out questionnaires and recall them. But it was still just a follow-up record, without group trials, and it only followed for 6.9 years. The subjects of the study are people who do not exercise at all. This rule does not apply to people who are already exercising regularly.

Case: Xiao Li, an office worker, deliberately gets off the bus two stops early and walks briskly for ten minutes when commuting. During his lunch break, he climbs the stairs of the office building to and from the fifth floor. Six months later, he found that he had more energy and the cardiovascular indicators on his physical examination report had also improved.

items.title: Perform strength training for 30-60 minutes per week
items.core: People who practice strength training for 30-60 minutes per week have a 10 to 20% lower risk of death than those who do not exercise. No more practice will make it better. Strength and aerobics work best together.
body: Cost: Freehand squats and push-ups are free. Practice 1–2 times a week for 20–30 minutes. The hard part is fitting it into your weekly schedule.

Benefits: Combining multiple follow-up studies (only records, not groups): people who do strength training have a 10%–17% lower risk of death than those who don’t. It's not that the more you practice, the better. The biggest drop is about 10%-20% at about 30-60 minutes a week. Practicing more will not bring more benefits. People who did both strength and cardio had a lower risk of death than people who did neither.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Momma H et al (2022). Muscle-strengthening activities are associated with lower risk and mortality in major non-communicable diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. British Journal of Sports Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2021-105061>

Note: This type of study is only a tracking record, and the amount of exercise is reported by the participants themselves. The evidence for "overtraining will make you worse" is very weak, so there is no need to limit the amount of training for this reason. Strength training also has fall-prevention and muscle-preserving benefits for the elderly, and those are listed in Section 1. For people with degenerative knee pain, thigh muscle training is more effective than arthroscopy. See Section 6, Item 33 (Arthroscopic Cleaning).

Case: 45-year-old Ms. Wang practices dumbbell exercises twice a week for twenty minutes each time, combined with brisk walking. One year later, not only did she have a tighter body, but her annual physical examination also maintained excellent bone density and muscle mass.

items.title: Don’t sit for too long, get up and move every once in a while
items.core: People who sit for the longest have a risk of death that is more than one and a half times higher than those who sit for the least. Sitting for a long time at a time is another risk. But with 60–75 minutes of moderate-intensity activity each day, the risks of sitting for too long are largely offset.
body: Cost: No money, it doesn’t take much time to stand up a few times. The difficulty is that you forget the time after sitting in, so you have to set a reminder.

Income: There is a tracking study in the United States, which only records, does not group, and uses accelerometers for actual measurement. Divide people into four groups based on the total amount of time they sit for a day. Those who sat the most had about a 163% higher risk of death (HR 2.63) than those who sat the least. Divide it into four parts based on how long you sit continuously: the people who sit for the longest period of time have about 96% higher scores (HR 1.96) than the people who sit for the shortest period of time. So the total amount of sitting and how long you sit at one time are each independently related. Another summary combined studies of millions of people, only recording, not grouping. People who sat for more than eight hours a day and did little exercise had about a 59% higher risk of death (HR 1.59) than those in the other group. The other group of people are those who sit for less than 4 hours a day and are the most active. About 60–75 minutes a day of moderate-intensity activity can offset the risks of sitting for long periods of time. Even if the most active group sat for more than 8 hours a day, the HR was only 1.04, and no statistical difference was seen.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Diaz KM et al (2017). Patterns of Sedentary Behavior and Mortality in U.S. Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A National Cohort Study. Annals of Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.7326/M17-0212>; Ekelund U et al (2016). Does physical activity attenuate, or even eliminate, the detrimental association of sitting time with mortality? A harmonised meta-analysis of data from more than 1 million men and women. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(16)30370-1>

Note: The reliable conclusion is: how long you sit is not as important as how much you move. When you exercise enough, the risk of sitting for a long time basically disappears. It should be noted that this type of research is only a follow-up record. A large number of people who sit the most are already sick. The "hazard ratio 2.63" obviously implies "you must be sick first before sitting for a long time". In addition, in the same summary, the risk of watching TV for more than 3 hours a day existed in people of all levels of exercise, and the most active group just pushed the starting point to 5 hours.

Case: Programmer Xiao Zhao sets an hourly reminder on his mobile phone. When the time is up, he stands up and does a few minutes of stretching or goes to the tea cup to drink water. After three months of persistence, his back pain was significantly reduced, and he had more energy to work out after get off work.

items.title: Eat less processed meat (ham, bacon, sausage, luncheon meat)
items.core: People who eat the most ham, bacon, and sausages are about 20% more likely to die during the same period than those who eat the least. Eating one more serving of processed meat per day increases the risk by 20%.
body: Cost: No money, even money, and no time required. The difficulty lies in eating less of what you like.

Benefits: Combining multiple follow-up studies (recording only, not grouping): the group that ate the most processed meat had about a 23% higher risk of death than the group that ate the least (RR 1.23). Red meat was approximately 29% higher overall (RR 1.29). Unprocessed red meat was about 10% higher (RR 1.10), but no statistical difference was seen in this term. Another summary is based on the amount eaten per day. Eating one additional serving of processed meat per day was associated with an approximately 23% higher risk of death (RR 1.23). Eating 1 additional serving of red meat per day was about 10% higher (RR 1.10).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Larsson SC, Orsini N (2014). Red meat and processed meat consumption and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis. American Journal of Epidemiology. <https://doi.org/10.3945/ajcn.117.153148>; Johnston BC et al (2019). Unprocessed Red Meat and Processed Meat Consumption: Dietary Guideline Recommendations From the NutriRECS Consortium. Annals of Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.7326/M19-1621> (disputing party NutriRECS Guide)

Note: Disputed. The NutriRECS guidelines rated these studies as "less reliable" using a generally accepted scoring of evidence (GRADE) approach. It only gave a very weak suggestion: just eat as you are now. What the two sides are arguing about is whether the evidence is strong enough, not the direction. There are no studies saying processed meat is beneficial. Unprocessed red meat had a small effect and no statistical difference was seen. What needs to be controlled is processed meat.

Case: Aunt Zhang used to eat ham sausage with toast for breakfast and bacon for lunch. After learning about the risks, she switched to eggs and fresh tomatoes for her sandwiches and avoided sausages when eating out. Six months later, her blood pressure became more stable.

items.title: Drink less or no alcohol
items.core: After drinking 100 g of pure alcohol per week, the more you drink, the sooner you will die. 100 g of pure alcohol is approximately 2.5 L of beer. People who drink 100–200 g per week at age 40 lose about half a year; those who drink 200–350 g lose one or two years; and those who drink more than 350 g lose four to five years. In terms of overall health, the most cost-effective amount is not to drink.
body: Cost: It doesn’t cost money, saves money, and doesn’t take up time. It's a little awkward when trying to push a drink in a social setting.

Income: 83 follow-up studies were combined, only recorded and not grouped, 600,000 people who drank alcohol. The risk of death was lowest at no more than 100 g of pure alcohol per week. This amount is approximately 2.5 L of 5% beer, or 300 mL of 40-proof liquor. People who drank 100–200 g per week at age 40 had about 6 months less life expectancy. Drink 200–350 g per week for less than 1–2 years. Less than 350 g 4–5 years. The above three items were originally reported in life-years. Global Burden of Disease Study GBD 2016 When all types of health losses are combined, the lowest risk alcohol consumption is 0 drinks/week. There was also a summary that corrected for biases in study design. People who drank 1.3–24 g per day had about a 7% lower risk of death (RR 0.93) than people who had never drank in their lifetime. However, no statistical difference was seen in this item. Drinking 45–64 g per day was approximately 19% higher (RR 1.19). Approximately 35% higher above 65 g per day (RR 1.35).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Wood AM et al. (2018). Risk thresholds for alcohol consumption: combined analysis of individual-participant data for 599 912 current drinkers in 83 prospective studies. Lancet. 195 countries and territories, 1990–2016: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2016. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(18)31310-2>; Zhao J et al. (2023). Association Between Daily Alcohol Intake and Risk of All-Cause Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-analyses. JAMA Network Open. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.6185>; Di Castelnuovo A et al (2006). Alcohol dosing and total mortality in men and women: an updated meta-analysis of 34 prospective studies. Archives of Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archinte.166.22.2437>(Disputing Party)

Remarks: Dispute. The one who believes that "drinking less is good" is a summary of 34 long-term follow-up studies. It reports: Overall mortality was up to 17%–18% lower among light drinkers. The amount it gives is no more than 4 cups a day for men and no more than 2 cups for women. Within this amount, people who drank more had a lower mortality rate. Opponents believe that the "no drinking" group includes people who quit drinking due to illness and people who are already in poor health. There is a summary that specifically deducts these interferences. After that, the protective effect is gone. The Global Burden of Disease Study also gives 0 as safest. A safe way to read it is: drinking less will not significantly harm your life span, but drinking more will. "Starting drinking for health reasons" has no basis. What to do if you want to drink less, see item 21 of this section (count the number of drinks first and then see a doctor). People who drink every day should not quit on their own. See Article 20 of this section (Don’t quit on your own).

Case: Lao Chen originally drank two bottles of beer every night to help him sleep. After learning about the long-term harm of alcohol, he gradually changed to drinking non-alcoholic drinks and soaking his feet. After a few months, he was sleeping more deeply, was more alert during the day, and his physical exam parameters returned to normal.

items.title: People who drink every day and have trembling hands and panic when they stop, don’t quit on their own.
items.core: People who drink a lot every day and stop suddenly will have withdrawal reactions. Mild symptoms include trembling hands, sweating, palpitation, and inability to sleep; severe symptoms include convulsions or delirium tremens, which are potentially life-threatening emergencies. Norway tracked more than 30,000 people, and among those who suffered from delirium tremens, 8% died each year. If you want to quit, go to the hospital first and explain how much you drink every day.
body: Cost: A call to the psychiatry or addiction medicine department costs a few yuan to dozens of yuan. In severe cases, you may need to stay in the hospital for several days.

Benefits: A 2026 clinical review states: People who drink heavily for a long time will develop withdrawal syndrome after sudden cessation or significant reduction in drinking. The symptoms include tremor, autonomic nervous excitement, anxiety, insomnia, abnormal perception, epileptic seizures and delirium tremens, which are "common and potentially life-threatening" in general medical diagnosis and treatment. The Norwegian National Register Cohort included 36,287 people diagnosed with alcohol dependence, alcohol withdrawal state, or delirium tremens from 2009 to 2015: annual mortality rates were 8.0% in the delirium tremens group, 5.0% in the withdrawal state group, and 3.6% in the alcohol dependence group. The standardized death ratio in the delirium tremens group was 9.8 (95% CI 8.9–10.7, which is the confidence range), meaning the risk of death was approximately 9.8 times higher than in the general population of the same age.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Caputo F, Lungaro L, Costanzini A, De Giorgio R, Addolorato G (2026). Alcohol withdrawal syndrome in hospitalized patients: a practical review. European Journal of Internal Medicine, 107103. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejim.2026.107103>; Bramness JG, Heiberg IH, Høye A, Rossow I (2023). Mortality and alcohol-related morbidity in patients with delirium tremens, alcohol withdrawal state or alcohol dependence in Norway: A register-based prospective cohort study. Addiction, 118(12), 2352–2359. <https://doi.org/10.1111/add.16297>

Note: How to judge by yourself: if you drink it almost every day, if you don’t drink it for a day, your hands will shake, you will sweat, your heart will be flustered and you will be unable to sleep. You need to drink a little in the morning to feel comfortable. Don’t stop yourself if you have one. The normal practice in the hospital is to use benzodiazepines to tide over the past few days, and to supplement thiamine (vitamin B1) at the same time. The reason for the B level is that the Norwegian cohort said "what happens to people who have suffered from delirium tremens", not "what will happen if they quit hard on their own". The difference between the two is an inference. I am not advising you to continue drinking, but I am asking you to change your method of stopping and go to the hospital to quit. How much you drink per week is considered too much, see item 19 of this section (drink less or not drink at all), and what to do if you want to drink less, see item 21 of this section (count the number of drinks first and then see a doctor).

Case: Lao Liu drank a pound of liquor every day. After he suddenly stopped drinking, his hands shook, his heart palpitated, and he suffered from insomnia all night. His family immediately sent him to the hospital. After evaluation, the doctor gave him alternative drugs and gradually reduced the dosage, and he safely passed the dangerous withdrawal period.

items.title: If you want to drink less, count how much you drink in a week, and then talk to your doctor for a few minutes.
items.core: The doctor takes a few minutes to look at your drinking, explain the risks, and help you set a goal. After a year, you will drink an average of 20 grams less pure alcohol per week, which is about half a liter of beer. Talking longer does no more good. We can no longer stop drinking. There are two drugs abroad that have been proven to be effective. For every 12 people treated, one more person will no longer drink too much.
body: Cost: No money. Just count the number of cups and write them down once a day. It doesn't cost extra to ask casually at the clinic.

Benefits: 34 randomized trials, 15,197 people combined, people who received a brief intervention drank 20 grams less of pure alcohol per week after one year than people who received minimal or no intervention (95% CI, 12 to 28 grams less, confidence range; moderate-certainty evidence). Baseline alcohol consumption among participants in these studies averaged 244 grams per week. Brief interventions are defined as no more than five sessions of advice or lifestyle counseling totaling less than 60 minutes; longer sessions have no additional benefit. Drugs: 122 randomized trials, 22,803 people combined, acamprosate prevented one more person from returning to any drinking for every 12 people treated (95% CI 8 to 26); oral naltrexone 50 mg daily, one more person treated from 12 people (8 to 26), did not return to heavy drinking.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Kaner EF, Beyer FR, Muirhead C, et al. (2018). Effectiveness of brief alcohol interventions in primary care populations. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2, CD004148. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004148.pub4>; Jonas DE, Amick HR, Feltner C, et al. (2014). Pharmacotherapy for adults with alcohol use disorders in outpatient settings: a systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA, 311(18), 1889–1900. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2014.3628>

Note: The benefit magnitude is set as "small" because the two pieces of evidence measure the amount of drinking, not the mortality rate. According to the rules of this book, only the surrogate endpoint is recorded as "small". Most of the drug trials are conducted abroad, and most of the subjects have met the diagnostic criteria for alcohol dependence, and psychosocial intervention is also given in the trials. The numbers are "additional benefits on this basis." The domestic indications and whether these two drugs can be prescribed are subject to the doctor and the drug instructions. Do not buy online by yourself. If you have already experienced withdrawal reactions, please refer to Article 20 of this section (don’t force yourself to quit).

Case: Xiao Wu spent two minutes in the physical examination center checking the amount and frequency of drinking per week. After reading the records, the doctor suggested that he set a goal of drinking at most twice a week. A reexamination six months later showed that his self-reported drinking had indeed dropped significantly.

items.title: Eat a handful of nuts every day
items.core: People who regularly eat nuts have a risk of death that is about 20% lower than those who don’t. You can see the difference by eating it once a week, which is about 10% lower. Eat a handful a day and the difference will be most obvious.
body: Cost: 28 grams per day, about two to three hundred yuan a year. Eat as you go, it doesn't take up time.

Benefits: Two US follow-up studies, 119,000 people, more than 3 million person-years. Person-years are the number of people multiplied by the number of years each was tracked. Compared with people who did not eat nuts: those who ate them less than once a week had about a 7% lower risk of death (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% CI 0.90–0.96, confidence range). Eating once a week was about 11% lower (0.89, 0.86–0.93). 2–4 times per week was about 13% lower (0.87, 0.83–0.90). 5–6 times per week was about 15% lower (0.85, 0.79–0.91). About 20% lower for more than 7 times per week (0.80, 0.73–0.86)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Bao Y, Han J, Hu FB, et al. (2013). Association of nut consumption with total and cause-specific mortality. New England Journal of Medicine, 369(21), 2001-2011. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1307352>

Note: Buy the original flavor without added salt. Nuts are high in calories, so don’t eat them as snacks. It should be noted that this type of study only follows a group of people for a long time. People who eat nuts have a better overall lifestyle, so the numbers have to be discounted

Case: Grandma Li grabs a handful of walnuts or unsalted almonds as snacks every day while watching TV series, replacing the previous biscuits. After persisting for more than a year, her constipation improved, and the good cholesterol in her blood lipid test also increased.

items.title: Replace some of the red meat with fish and poultry
items.core: Eating two more servings of processed meat or red meat per week has a higher risk of death by about 3%. If you replace it with the same amount of fish or poultry, there will be no increase. The effect of changing meat is relatively small in this section, so it is easy to change without any effort.
body: Cost: No money or time. This is changing the type of meat, not buying more. The hard part is changing your taste preferences.

Income: Combined 6 tracking studies in the United States and nearly 30,000 people. Eating two more servings of processed meat per week was associated with an approximately 3% higher risk of death (hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 1.02–1.05, confidence range). Eating two more servings of unprocessed red meat per week was also about 3% higher (1.03, 1.01–1.05). The same eating method is 0.99 (0.97–1.02) when replaced with poultry; replaced by fish, it is 0.99 (0.97–1.01). No statistical difference was seen in either of these items
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Zhong VW, Van Horn L, Greenland P, et al. (2020). Associations of Processed Meat, Unprocessed Red Meat, Poultry, or Fish Intake With Incident Cardiovascular Disease and All-Cause Mortality. JAMA Internal Medicine, 180(4), 503-512. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2019.6969>

Note: The difference between two servings per week is very small, so don’t expect to live a few more years by exchanging meat. If you also spend money on eating meat, you can give priority to fish and poultry

Case: Xiao Chen used to eat sausage rice or braised pork for lunch, but now she will give priority to grilled fish and skinless chicken legs when they are available in the canteen. This simple replacement made her feel less greasy and lighter.

items.title: Replace some of the polished rice and white flour with whole grains
items.core: People who eat 90 g more of whole grains a day are about 17% less likely to die during the same period. 90 g is about three servings. I ate about 200 g per day and continued to decrease.
body: Cost: Brown rice, oats, and whole wheat flour are more expensive than polished rice and white flour, and do not take up time. The difficulty is that the taste has to be adapted slowly.

Benefits: Combining multiple follow-up studies (recording only, not grouping): Eating 90 g more whole grains per day reduced the risk of death by about 17% (RR 0.83). 90 g is about 3 servings. This benefit continues up to 210–225 g per day. In another summary, eating one more serving per day was about 8% lower (RR 0.92).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Aune D et al (2016). Whole grain consumption and risk of cardiovascular disease, cancer, and all cause and cause specific mortality: systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective studies. BMJ. Journal of Clinical Nutrition. <https://doi.org/10.3945/ajcn.117.153148>

Note: You don’t have to replace all of them with whole grains, just half of them will already have the most obvious benefits. It should be noted that this kind of research is only a tracking record. People who eat whole grains are inherently healthier, so the numbers are on the higher side. The results between the various studies are also far apart (I² 83%, the larger the number, the more inconsistent the conclusions of the studies).

Case: Lao Zhou’s breakfast changed from white rice porridge to oatmeal porridge, and half of the white rice at lunch was replaced by brown rice. A few months later, he found that his blood sugar after meals was more stable, he was less hungry, and his weight gradually dropped.

items.title: Drink tea more than three times a week
items.core: People who have the habit of drinking tea have a lower risk of death by about 15%. Starting from the age of 50, people live an average of 1.26 years longer and are free from cardiovascular disease for 1.41 years.
body: Cost: tens to hundreds of yuan a year. Brewing a cup for a few minutes doesn't take up much time.

Benefits: A study of 100,900 people in China (China-PAR), half of whom were followed for 7.3 years. People who drank tea had about a 15% lower risk of death (hazard ratio 0.85, 95% CI 0.79–0.90, confidence range). Taking the age of 50 as the starting point: People with the habit of drinking tea have 1.41 more years of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease-free years and 1.26 more years of life expectancy
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Wang 1956-1963. <https://doi.org/10.1177/2047487319894685>; Mycotoxins in tea: Cui P et al (2020). Quantitative analysis and dietary risk assessment of aflatoxins in Chinese post-fermented dark tea. Food and Chemical Toxicology. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fct.2020.111830>; Zhou H et al (2022). Mycotoxins in Tea (Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze): Contamination and Dietary Exposure Profiling in the Chinese Population. Toxins. <https://doi.org/10.3390/toxins14070452>; Green tea extract and liver injury: Hu J et al (2018). The safety of green tea and green tea extract consumption in adults - Results of a systematic review. Regulatory Toxicology and Pharmacology. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.yrtph.2018.03.019>

Note: The controversy lies in the fact that this type of research is only a tracking record. A high proportion of Chinese male tea drinkers smoke and drink alcohol. The author has deducted some of these effects, but not completely. One more thing, don’t drink scalding tea. For the temperature of hot drinks, see Article 30 of this section (Do not drink scalding tea). Some people are worried about mycotoxins in tea. Aflatoxin was found in 2 of 158 dark teas tested in China. Based on the amount of tea consumed, the amount consumed was lower than the internationally acceptable value. Another study examined 352 teas and 16 types of mycotoxins, and only the average content of ochratoxin A in black tea exceeded the limit. Calculated based on the amount of tea consumed by Chinese people, dietary risks were not calculated in either category. Store the tea in a dry place. Do not drink the tea if it becomes damp or moldy. Green tea extract capsules are different: high-concentration catechins can damage the liver if swallowed in large quantities at one time, but brewed tea does not have this problem. So what I’m talking about here is just brewed tea, don’t use extract health products instead

Case: Teacher Lin has been drinking tea for more than 20 years, making a cup of green tea in the morning and afternoon every day. Although she is over sixty, her blood pressure is normal, and during the physical examination, the doctor also said that her blood vessels are younger than they actually are.

items.title: Drink three to four cups of coffee a day, with a total caffeine content of no more than 400 mg, no sugar or milk caps; except for pregnant women, women with a high risk of fractures, and people with palpitation, anxiety, and insomnia
items.core: People who drink three to four cups of coffee a day have a risk of death about 17% lower than those who don’t drink it. On the day of drinking coffee, there will be more premature ventricular contractions, and patients with hypertension will have elevated blood pressure within a few hours after drinking it. But people who drink coffee regularly do not have more new arrhythmias over the years. The amount of caffeine in one cup varies greatly, but the total amount per day is limited to no more than 400 mg.
body: Cost: One or two yuan per day. It only takes a few minutes to make a cup, and it doesn’t take up much time. If you buy a large cup, pay attention to how many milligrams of caffeine you drink in a day.

Benefit: A review combines 201 summary analyzes together. The original studies under these summaries are only recorded and not grouped. For overall mortality, the review cited one of the meta-analyses of dose-effect relationships. People who drank 3–4 cups of coffee per day had a 17% lower risk of death than those who drank no coffee (relative risk 0.83, 95% CI 0.79–0.88, confidence range). At 7 cups per day, the decrease narrowed to 10% (relative risk 0.90, 95% CI 0.85–0.96), and no increase in risk was seen. A study by the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) in the United States tracked 40,725 adults, half of whom were followed for 9.8 years. It was also only recorded and not grouped. Research divides coffee drinkers into two categories. The morning type refers to people who drink coffee mainly between 4:00 and 11:59, but rarely drink coffee in the afternoon and evening, accounting for 36%. They had a 12% lower risk of all-cause death than noncoffee drinkers (hazard ratio 0.88, 95% CI 0.81–0.96). After subtracting the effects of sleep deprivation and sleep difficulties, it was 16% lower (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.74–0.95). The risk of cardiovascular death was 19% lower (hazard ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.70–0.94). 31% lower after accounting for sleep effects (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.55–0.87). All-day types are those who drink in the morning, afternoon and evening, accounting for 14%. No difference was seen in their risk of all-cause death (hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.90–1.10). There was no discernible difference in the risk of cancer death between the two groups. There is an official daily limit for caffeine. Both the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) and Health Canada set the upper limit for healthy adults at 400 mg per day. This is all sources combined, including tea, cola and energy drinks. EFSA also requires drinking it spread throughout the day, with no more than 200 mg in a single serving. The content of a cup of coffee varies greatly. According to EFSA, a 200 mL cup of filter coffee contains approximately 90 mg. According to Health Canada, an 8-ounce (237 mL) cup of freshly brewed coffee averages 135 mg. According to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), 12 ounces (approximately 355 mL) of freshly brewed coffee contains 113–247 mg. So the FDA breaks 400 mg down to about 2 to 3 12 ounce cups of coffee, and the review breaks down into about 4 cups. Within a few hours of drinking it, the heart and blood pressure did respond. One randomized trial had 100 adults wear an ECG recorder for 14 days. Each day, they were randomly assigned via text message to have caffeinated coffee or no caffeine that day. There were an average of 154 premature ventricular contractions (an early beat of the ventricles) per day on coffee-drinking days and 102 on non-caffeine days (rate ratio 1.51, 95% CI 1.18–1.94). The number of premature atrial contractions was 58 versus 53, with no visible difference. On coffee days, you lose 36 minutes of sleep at night. Another meta-analysis looked only at patients with hypertension. When they consumed 200–300 mg of caffeine in one sitting, their systolic blood pressure increased by an average of 8.1 mmHg and their diastolic blood pressure increased by 5.7 mmHg. The increase occurs within an hour of drinking and lasts for at least 3 hours. In three studies where coffee was consumed for two weeks, blood pressure was no higher than when no coffee was consumed. In the long term, the British Biobank has tracked 386,258 people for an average of 4.5 years. It also only records and does not group people. Each additional cup of coffee consumed on a daily basis was associated with a 3% lower risk of new arrhythmia (hazard ratio HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96–0.98). The American Heart Association's 2026 scientific statement summarizes randomized trials among regular coffee drinkers. These trials showed that caffeinated coffee led to fewer episodes of atrial fibrillation and more premature ventricular contractions.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Poole R, Kennedy OJ, Roderick P, et al. (2017). Coffee consumption and health: umbrella review of meta-analyses of multiple health outcomes. BMJ, 359, j5024. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.j5024>, with corrections BMJ (2018), 360, k194. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.k194> (Confidence range for overall mortality in abstract changed from 0.83–0.88 to 0.79–0.88); Wang X, Ma H, Sun Q, et al. (2025). Coffee drinking timing and mortality in US adults. European Heart Journal, 46(8), 749-759. <https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehae871>; Yang R, Lei Q, Liu Z, et al. (2024). Relationship between timing of coffee and tea consumption with mortality (total, cardiovascular disease and diabetes) in people with diabetes: the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2003–2014. BMC Medicine, 22, 526. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12916-024-03736-x>; EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (2015). Scientific Opinion on the safety of caffeine. EFSA Journal, 13(5), 4102. Caffeine topic page (table of contents per serving) <https://www.efsa.europa.eu/en/topics/topic/caffeine>; FDA. Spilling the Beans: How Much Caffeine Is Too Much? <https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/spilling-beans-how-much-caffeine-too-much>; Health Canada. Caffeine in foods. Association of Sugar-Sweetened, Artificially Sweetened, and Unsweetened Coffee Consumption With All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality. Annals of Internal Medicine, 175(7), 909-917. <https://doi.org/10.7326/M21-2977>; Treskes RW, Clausen J, Marott JL, et al. (2023). Use of sugar in coffee and tea and long-term risk of mortality in older adult Danish men. PLOS ONE, 18(10), e0292882. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0292882>; Atrial Fibrillation: Wong CX, Cheung CC, Montenegro G, et al. (2026). Caffeinated Coffee Consumption or Abstinence to Reduce Atrial Fibrillation. JAMA, 335(4), 317-325. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2025.21056>; Joglar JA, Chung MK, Armbruster AL, et al. (2024). 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation. Circulation, 149(1). <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001193>; Heart rhythm and blood pressure: Marcus GM, Rosenthal DG, Nah G, et al. (2023). Acute Effects of Coffee Consumption on Health among Ambulatory Adults. New England Journal of Medicine, 388(12), 1092-1100. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2204737>; Mesas AE, Leon-Muñoz LM, Rodriguez-Artalejo F, Lopez-Garcia E. (2011). The effect of coffee on blood pressure and cardiovascular disease in hypertensive individuals: a systematic review and meta-analysis. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 94(4), 1113-1126. <https://doi.org/10.3945/ajcn.111.016667>; Kim EJ, Hoffmann TJ, Nah G, et al. (2021). Coffee Consumption and Incident Tachyarrhythmias: Reported Behavior, Mendelian Randomization, and Their Interactions. JAMA Internal Medicine, 181(9), 1185-1193. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2021.3616>;Marcus GM, Hu FB, van Dam RM, et al. (2026). Caffeine and Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation, 154(9), e345-e355. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001454>; Hyppönen E, Zhou A. (2021). Cardiovascular symptoms affect the patterns of habitual coffee consumption. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 114(1), 214-219. <https://doi.org/10.1093/ajcn/nqab014>

Note: The controversy lies in the fact that the review author states that most of the evidence comes from studies that only follow-up records, and reliable randomized controlled trials are needed to determine whether there is cause and effect. A study by the British Biobank found that people with high blood pressure, angina, and cardiac arrhythmia were less likely to drink caffeinated coffee. Genetic analysis also supports that people with high blood pressure drink less, and people with high resting heart rates are more likely to drink decaf. The authors of this study cautioned that comparing coffee drinkers with non-drinkers may account for this difference as a benefit of coffee. There is only one American study on the fact that drinking in the morning is better, so it was not included in the title. The authors note that the results cannot be interpreted as cause and effect, and it could simply be that people who drank coffee in the morning were healthier overall. In another U.S. study that only included people with diabetes, those who drank coffee from dawn to mid-morning had a 25% higher risk of death, while those who drank coffee from mid-morning to mid-morning had a 20% lower risk. The results were opposite. None of these studies compared whether 12 o'clock or 14 o'clock was more appropriate. Section 3, Item 4 (No caffeine after 2 p.m.) talks about sleep. You should push it forward according to your own bedtime, and it does not conflict with this article. 400 mg is the upper limit of safety, not a beneficial dose. Decaffeinated coffee has similar benefits, but in a slightly smaller size, so there’s no need to drink more to make up for it. Not to exceed 200 mg (EFSA) or 300 mg (Health Canada) per day for pregnant women. Women with a high risk of fractures do not apply to this rule. It is not suitable for people with anxiety and insomnia. This is the judgment of this book. There is no conclusion for these two types of people in the review. People who feel flustered after drinking should drink less, or switch to decaf. This is also the judgment of this book. People with atrial fibrillation do not have to give up coffee altogether. In one trial, people who drank about one cup of coffee a day after cardioversion for sustained atrial fibrillation had fewer relapses than those who abstained from coffee (47% vs. 64%). The 2023 U.S. Guidelines for Atrial Fibrillation also do not recommend abstaining from coffee to prevent attacks, but do so for people who drink it if it triggers symptoms. There is no evidence for other arrhythmias, so listen to your doctor. Mortality did not see added sugar negating the benefit. However, there is no research on syrup and milk cap drinks, and they contain a lot of sugar, so it is still recommended not to add them.

Case: An office worker drinks two cups of unsweetened black coffee every day to refresh himself. He found that he would occasionally feel flustered and suffer from insomnia when he drank the fourth cup, so he decisively cut back to two cups, which not only refreshed his mind but also ensured the quality of his sleep.

items.title: Eat enough 5 servings (about 400 g) of fruits and vegetables every day
items.core: Eat 200 g more of fruits and vegetables every day, the risk of death is reduced by about 10%. People who ate five servings a day ate about 13% less than those who ate just two. According to American research, if you eat more, it will not get lower.
body: Cost: A few yuan to more than ten yuan per day. Spend some time washing and cutting every day. The difficulty lies in buying and eating enough every day.

Benefits: Combining multiple follow-up studies (only recording, not grouping): eating 200 g more fruits and vegetables per day reduces the risk of death by about 10% (RR 0.90). This benefit continues up to 800 g per day. A summary of two large U.S. follow-up studies plus 26 studies found that people who ate five servings a day had about a 13% lower risk of death (HR 0.87) than those who ate only two. The best combination is 2 servings of fruit and 3 servings of vegetables, no more.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Aune D et al (2017). Fruit and vegetable intake and the risk of cardiovascular disease, total cancer and all-cause mortality: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective studies. International Journal of Epidemiology. <https://doi.org/10.1093/ije/dyw319>; Wang DD et al (2021). Fruit and Vegetable Intake and Mortality: Results From 2 Prospective Cohort Studies of US Men and Women and a Meta-Analysis of 26 Cohort Studies. Circulation. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.120.048996>

Note: The two studies have different opinions on the optimal amount to eat. The American study stops decreasing after 5 servings. It should be noted that this type of research is only a tracking record, and the interference is obvious: people who eat more vegetables have different income, education, and exercise than others. So "the risk is about 10% lower" is already the upper limit.

Case: An office worker who didn’t like vegetables before only ate meat for lunch. Recently, he eats one meat and two vegetables every day in the workplace cafeteria, plus an apple after each meal. After six months of persistence, a physical examination revealed that his blood lipid levels have improved significantly and his bowel movements have become smoother.

items.title: Eat less ultra-processed foods (potato chips, instant noodles, pastries, fast food)
items.core: People who eat the most ultra-processed foods have a 20% higher probability of death during the same period than those who eat the least, and cardiovascular death is 50% higher. However, this type of evidence is rated as less certain, and the figures need to be discounted backwards.
body: Cost: No money, just buy it instead. Cooking your own meals, or taking the time to pick out less processed ingredients, takes up some time every day. The difficulty lies in resisting the inertia of “convenience is good” for a long time.

Benefits: A review combines multiple summarized studies together. The original studies under these summaries are only recorded and not grouped. Results: People who ate more ultra-processed foods had about a 21% higher risk of death (RR 1.21) and a 50% higher risk of death from cardiovascular disease (RR 1.50) than those who ate less. The evidence ratings for these two items are "highly suggestive" and "convincing" respectively. However, according to the general evidence scoring method (GRADE), the certainty is low or very low.
Level of Evidence: A
Source: Lane MM et al. (2024). Ultra-processed food exposure and adverse health outcomes: umbrella review of epidemiological meta-analyses. BMJ. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-077310>

Remarks: The controversy lies in three points. This classification (NOVA) groups foods with widely different nutritional values ​​into one category. It overlaps heavily with sugary drinks and processed meats (Articles 7 and 18), and it’s unclear which one is responsible. According to the general evidence scoring method (GRADE), the grade is also low. So after doing those two things, I don’t know how much more benefits this one will bring. The evidence against this is the low rating given by the same review itself, and there is currently no original research that reaches the opposite conclusion. So first do items 7 and 18 (avoid drinking sugary drinks and eat less processed meat), and then look at this item.

Case: Xiao Li used to eat potato chips and fast food as a midnight snack. Later, he switched to buying fresh ingredients and cooking simple noodles by himself. Although it took a few minutes to prepare, he lost five pounds in a few months and became less sleepy during the day at work.

items.title: Stop burning coal and firewood for cooking and heating, and switch to electricity or gas
items.core: Those who burn coal or firewood for cooking have a 10% higher risk of death; those who burn coal for heating have a 14% higher risk. People who have switched to electricity or gas have a 13%–33% lower risk of death than those who still burn coal.
body: Cost: Rural families need to replace their stoves, plus fuel costs, which can cost several hundred to thousands of yuan a year. Just change it once and it's done, it won't take up time in the long run. Most people in the city already have electricity or gas.

Income: There is a study on chronic disease follow-up in China, which only records, without grouping, 271,000 adults without cardiovascular disease. People who used solid fuels such as coal for cooking had about an 11% higher risk of death than people who used electricity or gas (HR 1.11). Use of solid fuels for heating was about 14% higher (HR 1.14). People who had switched from solid fuels to cleaner fuels were about 13% less likely to cook (HR 0.87) than those who were still burning. Heating was about 33% lower (HR 0.67). There is another account for outdoor PM2.5. Taking 104 follow-up studies combined, each 10 µg/m³ higher long-term exposure was associated with an approximately 8% higher risk of death from natural causes (RR 1.08). Natural causes are non-accidental death.
Level of Evidence: A
Source: Yu K et al. (2018). Association of Solid Fuel Use With Risk of Cardiovascular and All-Cause Mortality in Rural China. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envint.2020.105974>

Note: This type of research is only a tracking record. Families that switch to fuel tend to be wealthier, and the "risk ratio 0.67" is mixed with the impact of family circumstances. As for outdoor PM2.5, there is a limit to what individuals can do, which is to move, wear masks, and use purifiers. There are no studies of air purifiers with mortality as the endpoint, so numbers are not given in this section.

Case: Uncle Zhang in the northern countryside always burned a coal stove to keep warm in the winter. Last year, my son installed an electric heater, and the house no longer smelled of soot. Uncle Zhang said he no longer coughed at night, and his throat felt much better when he woke up in the morning.
