items.title: Put hot things away before drinking, and avoid drinking hot tea, soup and coffee
items.core: In a study in an area with a high incidence of esophageal cancer in Iran, drinking very hot tea was about 8 times more likely to get esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (a type of esophageal cancer) than drinking warm tea. Even if it's just "hot", the risk is about 2 times higher. Drinking it within two minutes after pouring it is about five times more risky than waiting more than four minutes before drinking it.
body: Cost: No money, just wait two or three minutes more each time. It's hard not to drink when you're hungry.

Benefits: Comparing 300 patients with 571 people who did not have the disease in an area with a high incidence of esophageal cancer in northern Iran. The following are compared with those who drink warm tea. For those who drank "hot" tea, the odds ratio for developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma was approximately 2.07 (95% CI 1.28–3.35, confidence range). The odds ratio for drinking "very hot" was approximately 8.16 (3.93–16.9). The odds ratio for those who drank less than 2 minutes after pouring compared with those who waited more than 4 minutes before drinking was approximately 5.41 (2.63–11.1). Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is a rare outcome, with odds ratios and relative risks similar
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Islami F, Pourshams A, Nasrollahzadeh D, et al. (2009). Tea drinking habits and oesophageal cancer in a high risk area in northern Iran: population based case-control study. BMJ, 338, b929. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.b929>;Loomis D, Guyton KZ, Grosse Y, et al. (2016). Carcinogenicity of drinking coffee, mate, and very hot beverages. Lancet Oncology, 17(7), 877-878. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(16)30239-X>; Yu C, Tang H, Guo Y, et al. (2018). Hot tea consumption and its interactions with alcohol and tobacco use on the risk for esophageal cancer: a population-based cohort study. Annals of Internal Medicine, 168(7), 489-497. <https://doi.org/10.7326/M17-2000>

Note: The International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies hot drinks above 65 ℃ as Category 2A, which means they are likely to cause cancer. The same review concluded that coffee itself does not cause cancer. One domestic study followed 456,000 people for a median of 9.2 years. People who drink very hot tea and more than 15 grams of alcohol per day have the highest risk of esophageal cancer. Compared with people who rarely drank tea and drank less than 15 grams of alcohol per day, the hazard ratio was 5.00 (HR 5.00, 3.64–6.88). For those who smoke and drink hot tea every day, the risk ratio is 2.03 (1.55–2.67). The authors of the paper concluded that when scalding tea is combined with excessive drinking or smoking, the risk of esophageal cancer is higher.

Case: Lao Chen has the habit of drinking scalding Kung Fu tea, and he feels stuffy as soon as it is brewed with boiling water. After listening to the doctor's advice, he now poured the tea into a fair cup and waited for five minutes to drink it. Although it took an extra minute or two, the burning sensation in his esophagus no longer existed.

items.title: Go out and soak up the sun during the day, don’t stay out of the sun all day long
items.core: In a Swedish study, women who deliberately avoided the sun had a life expectancy 0.6 to 2.1 years shorter than those who got the most sun. People who don't smoke but stay out of the sun have about the same life span as smokers who get the most sun.
body: Cost: Nothing. Ten minutes a day on the way to and from get off work and during lunch break are enough.

Earnings: Swedish study, 29,500 women, followed for 20 years. Those who avoided the sun had a life expectancy of 0.6 to 2.1 years less than those who spent the most time in the sun. "Non-smokers who avoided the sun had life expectancies similar to those of smokers in the group with the most sun exposure," the authors wrote.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Lindqvist PG, Epstein E, Nielsen K, et al. (2016). Avoidance of sun exposure as a risk factor for major causes of death: a competing risk analysis of the Melanoma in Southern Sweden cohort. Journal of Internal Medicine, 280(4), 375-387. <https://doi.org/10.1111/joim.12496>

Note: The controversy lies in the fact that Sweden has a high latitude and less sunshine, so the conclusion cannot be directly transferred to China. Moreover, people who avoid the sun may be weak and do not like to go out. This is the author's speculation. The authors of the paper themselves stated that women who spend a lot of time in the sun have a higher risk of skin cancer. So don’t get sunburned. You still need to cover yourself when exposed to strong sunlight at noon.

Case: Ms. Zhang, an office worker, used to use sun protection so airtight that she could hardly see the sun. Recently, she walked downstairs for fifteen minutes every day at noon to soak up the sun. Not only did she feel more cheerful, but she also fell asleep much faster at night than before.

items.title: Keep your BMI between 20–25 and lose weight if you are overweight
items.core: The risk of death is lowest at BMI 20–25. A BMI of 27.5–30 is about 20% higher, a BMI of 30–35 is about 45% higher, and a BMI of 35–40 is about 90% higher. For East Asians whose BMI is above 25, for every 5 points higher, the risk is about 40% higher.
body: Cost: Nothing. Diet and exercise take up time every day. This is the most persevering part of the whole festival: you have to keep your mouth shut and open your legs for a long time. After losing weight, maintaining it is more difficult than losing weight.

Gains: Individual data from 239 follow-up studies combined (record only, not grouped). This analysis only retained three categories of people: those who had never smoked, those who did not have chronic diseases at the time of enrollment, and those who lived more than 5 years after enrollment. Results: The risk of death was lowest at BMI 20–25. BMI 25–27.5 was approximately 7% higher (HR 1.07). 27.5–30 about 20% higher (HR 1.20). 30–35 about 45% higher (HR 1.45). 35–40 was about 94% higher (HR 1.94). 40–60 was about 176% higher (HR 2.76). For every 5 kg/m² above BMI 25, the risk was approximately 39% higher in East Asians (HR 1.39).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Global BMI Mortality Collaboration (2016). Body-mass index and all-cause mortality: individual-participant-data meta-analysis of 239 prospective studies in four continents. Lancet. using standard body mass index categories: a systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2012.113905> (disputing party)

Note: Controversy. One party believes that "being fatter will help you live longer." When they added up, they got: Overweight people had about a 6 percent lower risk of death, and those who were mildly obese had about a 5 percent lower risk. The main disagreement between the two sides is whether to exclude three types of data: smokers, people who have already been sick, and data from the first few years of enrollment. The reason for trimming is because people who are seriously ill will lose weight first. After the analysis, which compiled 239 studies, eliminated these three categories, the risks of being overweight emerged again. Also note that there are no randomized trials demonstrating that weight loss alone reduces overall mortality. The above benefits are compared side by side with people of different fat and thin profiles. It does not mean that you can reduce so much by losing weight. People who want to lose weight don’t have to worry about meal times. Breakfast and 16:8 fasting have no additional benefits. See Section 6, Item 26 (don’t expect breakfast or 16:8 to help you control your weight).

Case: Lao Liu is 170cm tall and weighs 160kg, with a BMI close to 28. He insists on eating less than half a bowl of rice for dinner every day and walking briskly for half an hour. He has lost 10 pounds in three months, his blood pressure has dropped significantly, and he is no longer out of breath when climbing stairs.

items.title: Eat chili peppers more than four times a week
items.core: In an Italian study, people who ate chili peppers more than four times a week had a 23% lower risk of death and a one-third lower risk of cardiovascular death than those who rarely ate it.
body: Cost: No money and no time required.

Benefits: An Italian study of 22,800 people, half of whom were followed for 8.2 years, with a total of 1,236 deaths. People who ate chili peppers more than four times a week had about a 23% lower risk of death than those who rarely ate them (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.66–0.90, confidence range). Cardiovascular death was approximately 34% lower (0.66, 0.50–0.86)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Bonaccio M, Di Castelnuovo A, Costanzo S, et al. (2019). Chili Pepper Consumption and Mortality in Italian Adults. Journal of the American College of Cardiology, 74(25), 3139-3149. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2019.09.068>

Note: The controversy lies in the fact that this is a tracking record made in the context of the Mediterranean diet. People who eat spicy food may have an overall diet that is closer to the local traditional way of eating. Also note that for people with gastroesophageal reflux, hemorrhoids, and irritable bowel, eating spicy food may aggravate the symptoms, so there is no need to force it. This is the author’s experience and no specific research has been found.

Case: Uncle Wang from Sichuan has homemade chili sauce with every meal, and he eats spicy food more than four times a week. Although he is older, his cardiovascular examination results have always been very healthy, and specialists praised his eating habits for protecting his heart.

items.title: Drink one or two servings of milk or yogurt every day
items.core: People who drank more than two servings of milk or yogurt a day had about a 17% lower risk of death than those who didn't.
body: Cost: A few yuan per day, no time required.

Benefits: The PURE tracking study covered 136,000 people in 21 countries, followed for an average of 9.1 years, and resulted in a total of 6,796 deaths. People who ate more than two servings of dairy products per day had about 17% lower risk of death than those who did not eat them (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.72–0.96, confidence range), P for trend=0.0052
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Dehghan M, Mente A, Rangarajan S, et al. (2018). Association of dairy intake with cardiovascular disease and mortality in 21 countries from five continents (PURE): a prospective cohort study. Lancet, 392(10161), 2288-2297. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(18)31812-9>

Note: The controversy lies in the fact that PURE includes a large number of low- and middle-income countries, where being able to drink milk every day is an indication of a good family background. This layer of interference is difficult to eliminate. In addition, people with lactose intolerance can switch to yogurt or low-lactose milk instead of drinking milk

Case: Professor Li, a college teacher, drinks a glass of milk for breakfast every day and eats a small box of sugar-free yogurt as a snack in the afternoon for more than two years. Physical examination results show that his bone density is among the best among his peers, and his gastrointestinal digestive function has always been very good.

items.title: There is no need to give up eggs, just one a day
items.core: If you eat half an extra whole egg a day, your risk of death will be about 7% higher. Replace this half with egg whites, fish, poultry or nuts, and the risk of death will be lower. However, another batch of studies found that eating less than one egg a day has no relationship with cardiovascular disease, so there is no need to give up eggs.
body: Cost: No money and no time required.

Benefit: A follow-up study of 521,000 people in the United States, with a total of 129,000 deaths. Eating half an extra whole egg per day was associated with about a 7% higher risk of death (hazard ratio 1.07, 95% CI 1.06–1.08, confidence range). Replace half a whole egg with an equal amount of egg white, poultry, fish, dairy products or nuts and beans, and the risk of death will be lower, as will the risk of death from cardiovascular, cancer, and respiratory systems. Opponent: Three major studies in the United States, with a total of 216,000 people, followed for a maximum of 32 years. There was no difference in cardiovascular disease risk between those who ate at least one egg a day and those who ate less than one egg a month (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.82–1.05). The same article combined 33 sets of data and 1.72 million people. If you eat one more egg a day, the risk of cardiovascular disease will not change (RR 0.98, 0.93–1.03). The authors of the paper concluded that there was no association between eating up to one egg per day and cardiovascular disease.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Zhuang P, Wu F, Mao L, et al. (2021). Egg and cholesterol consumption and mortality from cardiovascular and different causes in the United States: A population-based cohort study. PLoS Medicine, 18(2), e1003508. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1003508>; Drouin-Chartier JP, Chen S, Li Y, et al. (2020). Egg consumption and risk of cardiovascular disease: three large prospective US cohort studies, systematic review, and updated meta-analysis. BMJ, 368, m513. U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, U.S. Department of Agriculture (2015). 2015–2020 Dietary Guidelines for Americans, Chapter 1: "The Key Recommendation from the 2010 Dietary Guidelines to limit consumption of dietary cholesterol to 300 mg per day is not included in the 2015 edition, but this change does not suggest that dietary cholesterol is no longer important to consider" "individuals should eat as little dietary cholesterol as possible while consuming a healthy eating pattern". <https://www.dietaryguidelines.gov/sites/default/files/2019-05/2015-2020_Dietary_Guidelines.pdf>

Note: Very controversial: There are also studies that have followed a large number of people for a long time, as well as a summary of multiple studies, and have not found that one egg a day is related to cardiovascular disease. The 2015 Dietary Guidelines for Americans removed the 300 mg daily limit for cholesterol. But it also said that this does not mean that cholesterol is not important, and that you should eat as little as possible while eating healthily. One a day, currently there is no correlation with cardiovascular disease. The title "within one a day" refers to this result, and there are more studies that have not directly measured it

Case: 52-year-old Aunt Chen is worried about high cholesterol and has never eaten eggs before. After listening to the doctor's advice, she changed to eating a hard-boiled egg every morning and removed part of the yolk. A reexamination six months later found that all blood lipid indicators remained within the normal range.

items.title: Take a bath if you can, don't just take a shower
items.core: In a Japanese study, people who took a bath almost every day had a risk of cardiovascular events that was about 28% lower than those who took a bath less than twice a week, and a risk of cerebral hemorrhage that was about 46% lower.
body: Cost: Spend more on water and electricity. Half an hour each time.

Benefits: A Japanese study of 30,000 people, aged 40 to 59 years, followed for 19 years, with a total of 2,097 cardiovascular events. People who bathed almost every day had about a 28% lower risk of cardiovascular events than those who bathed no more than twice a week (hazard ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.62–0.84, confidence range). Coronary heart disease was about 35% lower (0.65, 0.45–0.94). Stroke was about 26% lower (0.74, 0.62–0.87). Cerebral hemorrhage is about 46% lower (0.54, 0.40–0.73)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Ukai T, Iso H, Yamagishi K, et al. (2020). Habitual tub bathing and risks of incident coronary heart disease and stroke. Heart, 106(10), 732-737. <https://doi.org/10.1136/heartjnl-2019-315752>; Consumer Affairs. At the end of the year and the beginning of the year, the accident of the high-spirited person should be noted (the page does not write the release date, the number is quoted from the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare 2024 Annual Vital Statistics): ""Drowning in the bathtub and drowning in the bathtub"にThe number of people who died was 7,776 in the 6th year of Reiwa. Undressing room, bathroom, temperature difference, rapid stimulation, blood pressure, and hot water bath The temperature inside the tank is long and the temperature rises and the body temperature rises and the consciousness is impaired. <https://www.caa.go.jp/policies/policy/consumer_safety/caution/caution_084/>

Note: The controversy lies in the fact that this is the result of the Japanese people and bathtub culture. Most Chinese families do not have the conditions to take a bath every day. Also, don’t make the water too hot and don’t soak it for too long. For the elderly and people with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, water temperature that is too high or soaking for too long can be dangerous. In Japan, 7,776 people drowned in bathtubs in 2024. The Japan Consumer Agency said that common causes are the large temperature difference between the house and the bathroom in winter and soaking in hot water for too long. Do not take baths, hot springs or saunas after drinking alcohol, see Section 22, Article 11 (Do not take hot springs after drinking alcohol).

Case: Fitness enthusiast Xiao Lin used to take a cold shower after exercising. Recently, he has made a habit of taking a hot bath in the bathtub for fifteen minutes before going to bed every night. He has found that his muscle soreness is relieved faster and his sleep becomes deeper at night.

items.title: Keep naps within half an hour and not more than one hour. If you have to sleep for an hour or two before you can survive, go check out the cause
items.core: People who nap for less than one hour do not have an increased risk of death or chronic disease, and their brains are clearer. People who sleep for more than an hour have a 30% higher risk of coronary heart disease, and a 20% higher risk of diabetes and obesity. So set an alarm and wake yourself up in half an hour. If you have to sleep for an hour or two every day to survive, that's a sign that you should check your body.
body: Cost: No money. Just set an alarm before going to bed, it requires almost no willpower.

Benefits: An umbrella review summarizing 16 meta-analyses, 244 health outcomes. An umbrella review is a summary of existing summary research. The bottom line: People who napped for less than 60 minutes had no increased risk of overall mortality or chronic disease and had the greatest improvement in brain function (SMD 0.69, 95% CI 0.37–1.00, which is the confidence range). Short naps of 20 to 30 minutes produced the greatest improvement in exercise performance (SMD 0.99, 0.67–1.31). People who nap for more than 60 minutes have about a 30% higher risk of coronary heart disease and about a 20% higher risk of diabetes and obesity. Another study asked 1,338 people over the age of 56 to wear wristwatches to measure their naps instead of filling out questionnaires on their own. It was followed for a maximum of 19 years, during which 926 people died. Each additional hour of napping was associated with an approximately 13% higher risk of death (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.04–1.23). Sleeping once more per day was about 7% higher (HR 1.07, 1.02–1.13). Those who took a nap in the morning were about 30% more likely to do so than those who slept in the early afternoon (HR 1.30, 1.03–1.64).
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Du P, Li J, Hua Z, et al (2026). Multiple Health Outcomes of Daytime Napping: A Comprehensive Umbrella Review. Public Health Reviews. All-Cause Mortality in Older Adults. JAMA Network Open. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.7938>; Dashti HS et al. (2021). Genetic determinants of daytime napping and effects on cardiometabolic health. Nature Communications. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-20585-3>

Note: Controversy. The above two are studies that only record and do not group. People who take long naps are more likely to have sleep apnea, anemia, hypothyroidism, depression, or other chronic conditions. Therefore, it is unclear how much of "people who sleep longer die more often" is caused by the nap itself. Causal inference using genes (Mendelian randomization, 453,000 people plus 541,000 people) supported only one thing: more frequent naps were associated with slightly higher blood pressure and waist circumference. It found no causal effect of napping on coronary heart disease and diabetes. So don’t think of “taking less naps” as a means to reduce mortality. "Check the cause" is the author's suggestion, and it belongs to level C: If you feel sleepy during the day and must sleep for a long time, check your sleep at night first. Check for sleep apnea if you are snoring or holding your breath during sleep, and then check blood routine and thyroid. How to take a short nap to refresh yourself, see Section 3, Item 11 (Take a 10-minute nap if you feel sleepy in the afternoon). See No. 13 of this section for how much sleep you should get at night (7 hours of sleep per night). How to detect and treat snoring and breath holding, see Section 3, Item 27 (Sleep Apnea).

Case: I used to take a two-hour nap after lunch and always wake up with a headache. Recently, Xiao Wang set an alarm clock for 25 minutes and got up at that time. He was clear-headed at work in the afternoon and no longer had insomnia at night. His overall mental state was much better.

items.title: After staying up late, catch up on sleep the next night, don’t save it until the weekend
items.core: People who slept less and didn't make up for it the next night had a risk of death that was about 15% higher than people who had a regular sleep schedule, and those who slept too little and didn't catch up on it were about 42% higher. People who catch up do not see an increased risk. So I stayed up late and went to bed early the next night.
body: Cost: Nothing. I wanted to sleep during those one or two hours.

Income: UK Biobank 85,618 people, average age 61.8 years old, wore watches to record daily sleep, with a median follow-up of 8 years. The study first calculated each person's "sleep-less nights" based on their own sleep needs, which refers to sleeping more than 2.5 hours less than they need. The first night after the period of less sleep is considered a "catch-up night". If you sleep more than you need this night, you will be considered as making up for it. According to this, it is divided into five modes. Compared with those who had a regular sleep schedule, those who slept little and did not get enough sleep had about a 15% higher risk of all-cause death (HR 1.15, 95% CI 1.01–1.31, which is the confidence range). Those who accumulated more than 3.5 hours of sleep without catching up were about 42% higher (HR 1.42, 1.24–1.63). There was no significant association between the two groups of catch-up, with the HR after sleep loss being 1.12 (0.98–1.28). Among people who were already short sleepers, about 19% (1.19, 1.01–1.40) slept less and did not make up for their sleep, and about 38% (1.38, 1.17–1.63) of those who slept too little did not make up for their sleep. This result was replicated in another group of 4,586 people in the American Health Survey.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Li X, Zhang M, Li Z, et al (2026). Acute sleep rebound following sleep restriction is associated with reduced mortality risk. Nature Communications. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-72461-1>

Note: This is a record-only study without grouping. People who cannot make up for it may be busier and in poorer health, so this layer cannot be cleared. "The two groups that were supplemented did not see an increase in risk." It was just that no difference was found. Their point estimates were still greater than 1, and supplementing them does not mean that there is nothing wrong. So if you stay up late, you have to pay it back as soon as possible, and you can't just stay up late because of it. In this study, catching up on sleep refers to sleeping more on the first night after sleeping less, and does not include catching up on the weekend. It’s another thing to fix “sleep on weekdays and catch up on weekends” into a weekly rhythm. It’s called social jet lag, which itself is related to cardiovascular disease. See Article 13 of this section (sleep about 7 hours a night, fixed schedule). Regarding the article about getting up at a fixed time on weekends, see Section 3, Item 2 (fixed wake-up time, same on weekends), which does not conflict with this article: this article tells you to go to bed early that night, not to sleep until noon the next day.

Case: Programmer Xiao Li stayed up until 3 a.m. on Friday to catch up on a project, and went to bed at 9 p.m. on Saturday for a full 9 hours of sleep. He didn’t feel dizzy or weak on Monday, nor did he feel more tired after catching up on sleep on the weekend like before.

items.title: The longer you work the night shift, the higher your risk of cardiovascular disease. If you can, switch to another job as soon as possible.
items.core: People who work night shifts have about 13% more cardiovascular disease and about 27% more cardiovascular deaths than people who don't work night shifts. And the longer you work, the worse: for every five additional years of night work, there's about a 7 percent increase in cardiovascular disease. Therefore, this account is calculated on an annual basis, so you should transfer as soon as possible.
body: Cost: If you transfer or change jobs, you may get less money, and your night shift allowance will be gone. Finding a job takes time and can be difficult to make up your mind. If this account is taken into account when choosing a job, the cost will be zero.

Benefits: 23 follow-up studies combined, only recorded, not grouped. People who worked the night shift had about a 13% higher risk of cardiovascular events (RR 1.13, 95% CI 1.10–1.16, confidence range). Cardiovascular death was approximately 27% higher (RR 1.27, 1.18–1.36). Looking at the number of years: for each additional five years of working night shifts, the incidence of cardiovascular disease is about 7% higher (RR 1.07, 1.04–1.09), and the cardiovascular death is about 5% higher (RR 1.05, 1.03–1.06). Broken down by disease, the incidence of coronary heart disease was about 22% (1.22, 1.16–1.28), the death from coronary heart disease was about 22% (1.22, 1.10–1.36), the death from ischemic heart disease was about 39% (1.39, 1.06–1.84), and the death from stroke was about 49% (1.49, 1.04–2.12). The incidence of stroke was not significant (1.06, 0.95–1.18).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Xi J, Ma W, Tao Y, et al (2025). Association between night shift work and cardiovascular disease: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis. Frontiers in Public Health. workers: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Occupational Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1093/occmed/kqaf040>; Shen QM, Li ZY, Tan YT, et al (2026). Night shift work and risk of total and site-specific cancer: results from a prospective cohort study among Chinese men. Scandinavian Journal of Work, Environment & Health. <https://doi.org/10.5271/sjweh.4290>; Czeisler CA, Johnson MP, Duffy JF, et al (1990). Exposure to bright light and darkness to treat physiologic maladaptation to night work. New England Journal of Medicine, 322(18), 1253-1259. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM199005033221801>; Eastman CI, Stewart KT, Mahoney MP, Liu L, Fogg LF (1994). Dark goggles and bright light improve circadian rhythm adaptation to night-shift work. Sleep, 17(6), 535-543: "Both bright light and goggles were significant factors for producing circadian rhythm phase The combination of bright light plus goggles was the most effective" "Goggles were necessary for producing phase delays". <https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/17.6.535>; Crowley SJ, Lee C, Tseng CY, Fogg LF, Eastman CI (2003). Combinations of bright light, scheduled dark, sunglasses, and melatonin to facilitate circadian entrainment to night shift work. Journal of Biological Rhythms, 18(6), 513-523: "With bright light during the night shift, almost all of the earlier participants complete achieved re-entrainment, and the phase delay shift was so large that darker sunglasses and melatonin could not increase its magnitude". <https://doi.org/10.1177/0748730403258422>

Note: These are record-only studies, not grouping. People who work the night shift are inherently different from others in terms of smoking, weight, and income, and the correction is not clean. The evidence that night shifts cause cancer is much softer than the popular belief. In an analysis pooling 12 studies and 12,132 breast cancer cases, those who worked night shifts had only about a 5% higher risk, with a confidence interval spanning 1 (RR 1.05, 0.96–1.14). The 20-year bracket is about 25% higher (1.25, 1.01–1.55). But after the author did impact analysis, this item was not significant. After adjusting for possible publication bias, it is close to 1. The author's words are that this association is "far from established." In another study that followed 8,202 cancer cases in Chinese men for 16.1 years, night shifts were not associated with total cancer or most common cancers. Only pancreatic cancer had a 59% higher risk between 11 and 20 years (HR 1.59, 1.09–2.31). Therefore, this calculation is based on cardiovascular disease, not cancer. This book does not advocate that anyone should leave the night shift. It just lays out the annual calculation for you to calculate by yourself. For those who are already doing it, first change what can be changed: For quitting smoking, see item 1 of this section (quit smoking, the sooner the better), for blood pressure and blood lipids, see item 12 of this section (if you have high blood pressure and high blood lipids, take medicine as prescribed by your doctor), for how to catch up on sleep after a night shift, see item 38 of this section (catch up on sleep the next night after staying up late). There are two other strategies that can be tried: concentrating eating during the day, and using strong light and strict shading during the day to move the biological clock. The latter really moved the biological clock in the experiment. After working six consecutive night shifts under ordinary indoor lighting, the biological clock remained motionless; when switched to strong light of 7,000 to 12,000 lux and almost total darkness during the day, the entire clock was reversed in four days. **The light at night should be bright enough, the light should be strictly blocked when sleeping during the day, and sunglasses should be worn on the way to work to block the morning light. Researchers recommend doing these three things together. ** In an experiment with 50 people on a simulated night shift, bright lights at night and sunglasses after get off work worked best on their own, but together they worked best. For people who do not wear sunglasses, the biological clock only moves in the direction of advance and cannot move in the direction of delay. The author believes that the sunlight on the way to get off work is blocking it. In another experiment of 67 people, those whose biological clocks were originally on the early side almost all turned upside down when exposed to strong light at night, and even after changing their sunglasses to darker ones, they did not move any further. For indoor lighting only, the darker the sunglasses, the more useful they are. The end points of both strategies are only metabolic indicators and sleep, and no experiments have tested whether following these measures can reduce cardiovascular risk. If you go back to your daytime life on your rest day, the clock will still be turned back. Dosage, raw numbers, and other sources, along with how the body tells time, are at [docs/Biological Clocks and the Night Shift.md](../docs/Biological Clocks and the Night Shift.md).

Case: Sister Chen, who worked the night shift in an electronics factory for 8 years, was transferred to the day shift quality inspection position last year. Half a year later, her blood pressure dropped from 145/95 to 128/82 during a physical examination. The doctor said that the work and rest routine played a role.

items.title: Buy pre-packaged edible oil with SC number, do not buy self-pressed peanut oil in bulk from small workshops
items.core: Peanuts that become damp and moldy will produce aflatoxin, which is a clear carcinogen and mainly damages the liver. After Guangzhou took control of small workshops, the liver function abnormalities of residents who often ate self-pressed oil decreased by about 35%. Pregnant women in Guangxi who eat self-pressed peanut oil are more likely to have low birth weight and premature birth.
body: Cost: Buy somewhere else, the money is about the same. Just take a look at the packaging to see if there is a food production license number starting with SC. The difficulty lies in convincing the elders who are accustomed to buying self-pressed oil.

Benefits: Aflatoxins are classified as Class 1 carcinogens by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (determined to cause cancer in humans), mainly liver cancer. A study in Guangzhou measured aflatoxin B1 in self-pressed peanut oil from small workshops from 2010 to 2022. The median was 1.29 μg/kg, with the middle half of the samples ranging from 0.12 to 6.58. After the local small workshop management regulations were introduced, the toxins in the oil immediately dropped to 2.865 μg/kg, and then dropped to 2.593 μg/kg every year. The proportion of abnormal liver function among residents who regularly consumed self-pressed oil decreased (PR 0.650, 95% CI 0.469–0.902, confidence range), which was about 35% lower. In a study following 1,611 pregnant women in Guangxi, 81.7% consumed self-pressed peanut oil. The odds ratio for low birth weight among those who ate was 1.9 (aOR 1.9, 1.1–3.2). The odds ratio for preterm birth was 1.8 (aOR 1.8, 1.1–3.0).
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Lei J, Li Y, Wang Y, et al (2024). The impact of small food workshops management regulations on aflatoxin B1 in home-made peanut oil and the liver function of high-consumption area residents: an interrupted time series study in Guangzhou, China. Frontiers in Public Health, 12. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2024.1484414>; Zhong Y, Lu H, Jiang Y, et al (2024). Effect of homemade peanut oil consumption during pregnancy on low birth weight and preterm birth outcomes: a cohort study in Southwestern China. Global Health Action, 17. <https://doi.org/10.1080/16549716.2024.2336312>; IARC (2012). Chemical Agents and Related Occupations. IARC Monographs on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans, Vol 100F. <https://publications.iarc.fr/123>; National Health and Family Planning Commission, State Food and Drug Administration (2017). National Food Safety Standards Limits of Mycotoxins in Food (GB 2761-2017)

Note: Both studies are only tracking records and there is no group control. The end point of the Guangzhou project was liver function tests, not liver cancer and death. The median toxin content of self-pressed oil is actually lower than the national standard limit of 20 μg/kg for peanut oil. The risk comes from long-term consumption and individual batches with high levels. The national standard limit applies to all peanut oil, but pre-packaged oil must pass production license and factory inspection. Small workshops are controlled according to the management methods of each province, and random inspections are much less. What to do if the peanuts, corn, and nuts stored at home become moldy? See Article 46 of this section (throw away the entire package if it becomes moldy). The beneficiaries of this article are mainly you and your family members who eat together.

Case: Aunt Zhang from Guangxi often buys self-pressed peanut oil in bulk from the market for cooking, and her transaminase was high in her physical examination. Three months after switching to bottled oil with an SC number from the supermarket, her liver function reexamination returned to normal.

items.title: Use vegetable oil instead of lard and butter for cooking. There is no need to buy oil for health reasons, and don't expect flaxseed oil to protect your heart.
items.core: Eating less saturated fats such as lard and butter and replacing it with vegetable oil can reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke by about 17%, but the overall risk of death has not changed. I eat more of the main ingredients of soybean oil and corn oil, but I don’t see any benefits or harms. If you eat too much flaxseed oil, your risk of heart disease will not decrease.
body: Cost: Not much money. Vegetable oil is already the workhorse of most households. The difficulty lies in getting rid of the taste habit of using lard for cooking and mixing rice.

Benefits: Cochrane compiled 15 randomized trials, 56,675 people, each conducted for at least two years. Eating less saturated fat was associated with approximately 17% lower overall cardiovascular events (RR 0.83, 0.70–0.98). Overall mortality was almost unchanged (RR 0.96, 0.90–1.03), as was cardiovascular death (RR 0.95, 0.80–1.12). Switching to polyunsaturated fat (the main component of soybean oil and corn oil) and switching to carbohydrates, no difference in effect was seen. The data on switching to monounsaturated fat (the main component of rapeseed oil and olive oil) are too sparse to tell. Another Cochrane article summarized 19 randomized trials and 6461 people. Eating more omega-6 (linoleic acid) had an RR of 1.00 (0.88–1.12) for total mortality and a RR of 0.97 (0.81–1.15) for cardiovascular events. No benefits or harms could be seen. The third article summarized 86 randomized trials and 162,796 people. Eating more plant-derived omega-3 (the main component of flaxseed oil and perilla oil) had an overall mortality rate of RR 1.01 (0.84–1.20) and a coronary heart disease event RR of 1.00 (0.82–1.22), which basically had no effect.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Hooper L, Martin N, Jimoh OF, et al (2020). Reduction in saturated fat for cardiovascular disease. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (5), CD011737. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD011737.pub3>; Hooper L, Al-Khudairy L, Abdelhamid AS, et al. (2018). Omega-6 fats for the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (11), CD011094. Abdelhamid AS, Brown TJ, Brainard JS, et al. (2020). Omega-3 fatty acids for the primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (3), CD003177. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD003177.pub5>; Chinese Nutrition Society (2022). Dietary Guidelines for Chinese Residents (2022). People's Medical Publishing House

Note: Controversy: Some people advocate that omega-6 in soybean oil and corn oil Too much can be pro-inflammatory, so eat less and change your oil. The randomized trial of the omega-6 article above found no harm, and the author rated the quality of the evidence as low. The magnitude of benefit was rated as moderate based on 17% lower cardiovascular events and no change in overall mortality. The amount of oil should be controlled. Dietary guidelines recommend 25 to 30 grams of cooking oil per person per day.

Case: Uncle Wang, who is accustomed to cooking with lard, followed the advice and switched to peanut oil, which is common in supermarkets. A year later, his physical examination showed that his LDL dropped by 0.8, and he did not bother buying expensive niche oils as before.

items.title: Turn on the range hood when cooking or frying, and keep it on from the beginning to the end
items.core: Chinese women who do not smoke, do not turn on the range hood or seldom turn it on when cooking, the risk of lung cancer is about twice that of the normal range hood. The risk is about 50% higher if you live in a house with poor kitchen ventilation, especially if you live in a coal-burning house.
body: Cost: If you have a range hood installed in your home, you will only have to pay a little more for electricity. If it is not installed, it will cost several hundred to thousands of yuan to buy one and install it. The difficulty is to remember to turn it on every time and don't turn it off if it's too noisy.

Benefits: 10 case-control studies combined, all in non-smoking Chinese women. Case control is to compare lung cancer patients with people without the disease, and then look back and ask about their past habits. The odds ratio for developing lung cancer among those exposed to cooking fumes was approximately 1.74 (95% CI 1.57–1.94, confidence range). Four of them compared people who were exposed to cooking fumes but did not use range hoods, and the odds ratios were approximately 2.11 (1.54–2.89). A study in Taiwan compared 1,302 non-smoking female lung cancer patients with 1,302 people who did not have the disease. Only look at people who have been cooking for more than ten years. The odds ratio is approximately 0.49 (0.32–0.76) for those who have used range hoods for more than two-thirds of the years, compared with those who have used range hoods for less than one-third of the years. Lung cancer is a rare outcome, and the odds ratios and relative risks are similar. There was a study in Shanghai that followed 71,000 non-smoking women from 1996 to 2009, and 429 cases of lung cancer were detected. Those who said they had lived in a house with poor kitchen ventilation were about 49% more likely to develop lung cancer (HR 1.49, 1.15–1.95). Those who burned coal and had poor ventilation for more than 20 years had about a 103% higher risk (HR 2.03, 1.35–3.05). Just looking at whether coal was burned or not, no difference was seen (HR 1.03, 0.84–1.26). I don’t see any difference in what kind of oil I use for cooking.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Xue Y, Jiang Y, Jin S, Li Y (2016). Association between cooking oil fume exposure and lung cancer among Chinese nonsmoking women: a meta-analysis. OncoTargets and Therapy, 9, 2987-2992. <https://doi.org/10.2147/OTT.S100949>; Chen TY, Fang YH, Chen HL, et al. (2020). Impact of cooking oil fume exposure and fume extractor use on lung cancer risk in non-smoking Han Chinese women. Scientific Reports, 10, 6774. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-63656-7>; Kim C, Gao YT, Xiang YB, et al (2015). Home kitchen, ventilation cooking fuels, and lung cancer risk in a prospective cohort of never smoking women in Shanghai, China. International Journal of Cancer, 136(3), 632-638. <https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.29020>

Note: Controversy: The figures supporting the use of range hoods mainly come from case-control studies. After patients are diagnosed, they tend to underreport the number of times they opened the range hood when recalling the past, and the number may be too high. In the follow-up study in Shanghai, the increased risk mainly fell on households that burned coal and had poor ventilation. The study couldn't give an independent number on how much difference it would make if people only burned gas. Therefore, the level of evidence is only B, and the benefit is considered to be as large as approximately twice the risk. Do not burn coal and firewood for cooking, see Article 29 of this section (Do not burn coal and firewood for cooking and heating). The beneficiaries of this article are mainly the people who often cook at home.

Case: Aunt Li, a non-smoker, always found the range hood to be noisy and only turned on for one minute when cooking. After turning it on for the entire process from turning on to loading, the smell of cooking fumes in the kitchen was reduced, and the lung nodules during the annual physical examination did not increase in size.

items.title: If hot flashes and night sweats before and after menopause affect your life, go to the gynecologist to evaluate hormone therapy. Don't take it and don't buy your own medicine, let alone use it to prevent heart disease
items.core: If you have hot flashes and night sweats before and after menopause, if you use hormone therapy, the number of hot flashes will be about 75% less than if you take a placebo. The cost is slightly more breast cancer, blood clots, and strokes, each around 8 per 10,000 women per year. There was no increase in overall mortality among people who started taking it between 50 and 59 years of age. It cannot be used to prevent heart disease or Alzheimer's disease.
body: Cost: One visit to the gynecologist or menopause clinic. The doctor will ask about your medical history to see if you are not suitable for taking hormones, and then prescribe a prescription if appropriate. After use, follow the doctor's instructions for review. The hard thing is to let go of the fear that "hormones will cause cancer when you touch them", and don't buy them just because you heard they can fight aging.

Benefits: Cochrane pooled 24 randomized trials, 3329 people, comparing oral steroids to placebo. People taking hormones had about 75% fewer hot flashes per week than placebo (95% CI 64.3–82.3, confidence range). The severity of hot flashes was also significantly reduced, with an odds ratio of 0.13 (OR 0.13, 0.07–0.23). People who took the placebo also had about 57.7% fewer hot flashes, so anything that can cure hot flashes must be compared with a placebo before it counts. Risks look at the US WHI randomized trial. 16,608 women aged 50 to 79 years with a uterus were followed for an average of 5.2 years on estrogen plus progestin. Coronary heart disease was approximately 29% higher (HR 1.29, 1.02–1.63). About 26% higher for invasive breast cancer (HR 1.26, 1.00–1.59). Stroke was approximately 41% higher (HR 1.41, 1.07–1.85). Pulmonary embolism was approximately 113% higher (HR 2.13, 1.39–3.25). In absolute terms, there are 7 more cases of coronary heart disease, 8 more cases of stroke, 8 more cases of pulmonary embolism, and 8 more cases of invasive breast cancer per 10,000 women per year. At the same time, there were 6 fewer cases of colorectal cancer and 5 fewer hip fractures. Women who had their uterus removed and only used estrogen had a 21% lower risk of breast cancer over 13 years of follow-up (HR 0.79, 0.65–0.97). Over a combined 18 years of follow-up in both trials, there was no change in overall mortality (HR 0.99, 0.94–1.03). By age at drug initiation, the group aged 50 to 59 years had approximately 31% lower overall mortality in those years of drug use (HR 0.69, 0.51–0.94). It was 1.04 (0.87–1.25) for those aged 60 to 69 years and 1.13 (0.94–1.36) for those aged 70 to 79 years, both of which were significant. After 18 years of age, the value for the 50- to 59-year-old group is 0.89 (0.79–1.01), which is no longer significant. A 2017 review by Cochrane looked at women aged 50 to 59 years alone. The only significant increase was in blood clots when combined with estrogen and progestin, with an absolute risk of less than 1 in 500. In women over 65 years old who took combined estrogen and progestin, dementia rose from 9 to 11 to 30 cases per 1,000 people over 4 years. The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force 2022 recommended against the use of hormones to prevent chronic disease (level D recommendation), concluding that there is no net benefit.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: MacLennan AH, Broadbent JL, Lester S, Moore V (2004). Oral oestrogen and combined oestrogen/progestogen therapy versus placebo for hot flushes. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (4), CD002978. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002978.pub2>; Writing Group for the Women's Health Initiative Investigators, Rossouw JE, Anderson GL, Prentice RL, et al (2002). Risks and benefits of estrogen plus progestin in healthy postmenopausal women: principal results from the Women's Health Initiative randomized controlled trial. JAMA, 288(3), 321-333. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.288.3.321>; Manson JE, Chlebowski RT, Stefanick ML, et al (2013). Menopausal hormone therapy and health outcomes during the intervention and extended poststopping phases of the Women's Health Initiative randomized trials. JAMA, 310(13), 1353-1368. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2013.278040>; Manson JE, Aragaki AK, Rossouw JE, et al (2017). Menopausal hormone therapy and long-term all-cause and cause-specific mortality: the Women's Health Initiative randomized trials. JAMA, 318(10), 927-938. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2017.11217>; Marjoribanks J, Farquhar C, Roberts H, et al (2017). Long-term hormone therapy for perimenopausal and postmenopausal women. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (1), CD004143. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004143.pub5>; US Preventive Services Task Force, Mangione CM, Barry MJ, et al (2022). Hormone therapy for the primary prevention of chronic conditions in postmenopausal persons: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA, 328(17), 1740-1746. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.18625>

Note: Controversy: Women in WHI were an average of 63 years old and were on a fixed oral regimen. Nowadays, most people in their 50s and just after menopause use it for symptoms, which is not exactly the same as the people in the experiment. The low mortality rate in the 50 to 59-year-old group can be seen by age group, but it is not significant after 18 years, so it cannot be said that hormones can extend life. Cochrane also wrote that the trial was not large enough to see the risks in women within 10 years of menopause. The following types of people are generally not suitable for use: those who have had breast cancer, those who have had blood clots, those with a high risk of cardiovascular disease, and those who are very obese. The specific judgment is left to the doctor. If a person with a uterus only uses estrogen, endometrial cancer will increase, so progesterone must be used at the same time. Only those who have had their uterus removed can only use estrogen. Hormones can also reduce fractures, but are generally only considered when other anti-osteoporosis drugs are not suitable. For osteoporosis, please first read Section 1, Item 39 (Bone Density Examination) and Section 1, Item 40 (Take medication if osteoporosis is detected). The magnitude of benefit was rated as approximately 75% fewer hot flashes, and the endpoint was symptoms, not total mortality. The beneficiary of this article is mainly yourself, but also your mother and spouse.

Case: After menopause, 52-year-old Ms. Liu woke up three or four times a night with hot flashes. After going to the gynecologist for evaluation, she took low-dose hormones. After a week, her hot flashes were reduced to once. She slept well and stopped buying health care products.

items.title: If you want to keep a dog, count walking the dog every day as walking, and don’t raise a dog specifically for longevity
items.core: The probability of death for people who own a dog during the same period is on average about a quarter lower, and the probability of death for people who have had coronary heart disease is even lower. But after deducting other differences, large studies in the UK and Norway could not find any difference, and there was no correlation between keeping cats. So don’t raise a dog specifically for longevity. If you originally wanted to raise a dog, treat walking the dog every day as walking.
body: Cost: Keeping a dog always costs money, including dog food, vaccines, deworming, medical treatment, and certificates. The dog must be cared for until it dies of old age. You have to find time to walk your dog every day, and you have to find someone to look after your dog when you go on business trips. The difficulty is that you have to persist every day, and you can’t stop whenever you want. There are no official statistics on how much it costs to raise a dog in China, so we won’t include numbers here.

Income: Taking the 10 follow-up studies together, approximately 3.84 million people were followed for an average of 10.1 years. Dog owners had about a 24% lower risk of death (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.67–0.86, confidence range). Cardiovascular death was approximately 31% lower (RR 0.69, 0.67–0.71). Among those who had coronary heart disease, the risk was about 65% lower among those who had dogs at home (RR 0.35, 0.17–0.69). The author states that this summary does not exclude other factors. The study, based on a registry of about 3.43 million people across Sweden, adjusted for income, marriage and other factors. All people combined, dog ownership was associated with approximately a 20% lower risk of death (HR 0.80, 0.79–0.82). People who lived alone had an approximately 33% lower risk of death if they owned a dog (HR 0.67, 0.65–0.69). Living with others was about 11% lower (HR 0.89, 0.87–0.91). Among Swedish patients after myocardial infarction, the risk of death was about 33% lower for those who lived alone with a dog (HR 0.67, 0.61–0.75), and about 15% lower for those who lived with a partner or children (HR 0.85, 0.80–0.90). It was approximately 27% (HR 0.73, 0.66–0.80) and 12% lower (HR 0.88, 0.83–0.93) respectively after ischemic stroke. Opposition: There were 6 batches of health surveys in the UK with a total of 59,352 people followed for an average of 11.5 years. After all adjustments, dog ownership was not associated with death (HR 1.03, 0.98–1.09), nor with cardiovascular death (HR 1.07, 0.96–1.18). A Norwegian study followed dog owners for a median of 18.5 years and found that the risk of death was almost the same among dog owners (HR 1.00, 0.91–1.09). People who keep dogs there are not more active than others. In the Swedish twin registry, where 34,202 people were asked about their lifestyle habits, the relationship between dog ownership and a lower risk of cardiovascular disease and death could not be replicated. In an Australian study of 15,735 people followed for 4 years, the odds ratio for death among dog owners was 0.77 (OR 0.77, 0.59–0.99). Part of this difference can be explained by higher levels of activity. Raising cats, birds, and fish is not associated with death. The American Heart Association's 2013 statement said that keeping pets, especially dogs, "may be reasonable" to reduce cardiovascular risk, which is the weakest recommendation. The same statement explicitly opposes adopting, rescuing, or buying pets primarily for the purpose of reducing cardiovascular risk.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Kramer CK, Mehmood S, Suen RS (2019). Dog ownership and survival: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes, 12(10), e005554. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCOUTCOMES.119.005554>; Mubanga M, Byberg L, Nowak C, et al. (2017). Dog ownership and the risk of cardiovascular disease and death – a nationwide cohort study. Scientific Reports, 7, 15821. Mubanga M, Byberg L, Egenvall A, Ingelsson E, Fall T (2019). Dog ownership and survival after a major cardiovascular event: a register-based prospective study. Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes, 12(10), e005342. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCOUTCOMES.118.005342>; Ding D, Bauman AE, Sherrington C, et al (2018). Dog ownership and mortality in England: a pooled analysis of six population-based cohorts. American Journal of Preventive Medicine, 54(2), 289-293. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.amepre.2017.09.012>; Torske MO, Krokstad S, Stamatakis E, Bauman A (2017). Dog ownership and all-cause mortality in a population cohort in Norway: the HUNT study. PLoS ONE, 12(6), e0179832. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0179832>; Taniguchi Y, Ikeuchi T, Yong J (2024). Dog, cat, bird, fish, and other pet ownership and mortality: evidence from the HILDA cohort. PLoS ONE, 19(8), e0305546. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0305546>; Mubanga M, Byberg L, Egenvall A, et al (2019). Dog ownership and cardiovascular risk factors: a nationwide prospective register-based cohort study. BMJ Open, 9(3), e023447. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2018-023447>; Levine GN, Allen K, Braun LT, et al (2013). Pet ownership and cardiovascular risk: a scientific statement from the American Heart Association. Circulation, 127(23), 2353-2363. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0b013e31829201e1>

Note: Controversy. The above are all tracking records and there is no group comparison, so we cannot deduce "raising a dog for longevity". People who know how to keep dogs may be healthier and more active, while people who are sick or disabled may not be good at raising dogs. These differences cannot be accounted for. The 24% in the summary did not deduct any factors. In several studies that asked about living habits, the difference was gone. In another Swedish study, dog owners were slightly more likely to start taking antihypertensive and lipid-lowering drugs. So even if the risk of death is really low, it is not due to lowering blood pressure and blood lipids. There is only one thing that can be realized: if you already have a dog or want to have one, count walking a dog every day into the amount of walking. If it is enough, please refer to Article 11 of this section (walk 7000–8000 steps a day). Regarding leashes, vaccinations, and compensation for dog injuries, see Section 8, Article 30 (Dogs must be leashed). How to hold the leash to prevent falls when the elderly are walking their dogs, see Section 17, Article 10 (Elderly Dogs Walking). The magnitude of the income is determined as large based on the aggregated 24% of the machine, but this number does not deduct other factors. The beneficiary of this article is mainly yourself.

Case: Xiao Zhou, an office worker who originally wanted to keep a dog, walked his dog for half an hour in the morning and evening every day. In three months, his average daily steps increased from 4,000 to 8,000, and he lost 3 pounds in weight. He did not force a dog for exercise.

items.title: If you are diagnosed with pre-diabetes (high blood sugar, but not yet diabetic), you can push back diabetes by eating less, losing weight, and moving more. Check your blood sugar every six months
items.core: For those with high blood sugar but not yet diabetes, if you eat less, move more, and lose a little weight, your risk of developing diabetes can be reduced by 30 to 60%. The experiment in Daqing, China, followed for 30 years, found that people who did this had about a quarter lower risk of death and lived about a year and a half longer on average. But similar trials in the United States and Finland found no difference in mortality.
body: Cost: No money, you can save a little by eating less. Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity such as brisk walking each week, spread out to about 20 minutes each day. Eat 400 to 500 kcal less per day than before. The difficulty lies in persisting and maintaining the weight after losing it. A blood test is done every six months, and the fasting blood sugar is more than ten yuan.

Benefits: The Daqing study is a randomized group trial conducted in Daqing, Heilongjiang, and is divided into clinics. 577 adults with impaired glucose tolerance, a form of prediabetes, were assigned to either a control group or one of three intervention groups: diet alone, exercise alone, or both. The intervention was done for 6 years. The cumulative proportion of diabetes in the 6 years in the control group was 67.7%. 43.8% in the diet group, 41.1% in the exercise group, and 46.0% in the diet plus exercise group. After deducting the differences in body mass index and fasting blood sugar, the risk of diabetes in the three groups was approximately 31%, 46%, and 42% lower respectively. Thin and overweight people (a body mass index cutoff of 25) experienced similar decreases. At follow-up to 23 years, cardiovascular death was approximately 41% lower in the intervention group (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.36–0.96, confidence range). Overall death was approximately 29% lower (HR 0.71, 0.51–0.99). The risk of developing diabetes was about 45% lower (HR 0.55, 0.40–0.76). At 30 years, the time to diabetes in the intervention group was delayed by 3.96 years (based on a median calculation). Cardiovascular events were approximately 26% lower (HR 0.74, 0.59–0.92). Serious small vascular complications of fundus, kidney, and nerves were approximately 35% lower (HR 0.65, 0.45–0.95). Cardiovascular death was approximately 33% lower (HR 0.67, 0.48–0.94). Overall death was approximately 26% lower (HR 0.74, 0.61–0.89). Lived an average of 1.44 years longer (0.20–2.68). The US DPP trial randomized 3234 people with high blood sugar. The goals for the lifestyle group were to lose at least 7% of body weight and be active for at least 150 minutes per week. After an average of 2.8 years of follow-up, the lifestyle group had a 58% lower risk of developing diabetes than the placebo group (95% CI 48%–66%). The group taking metformin had a 31% lower rate (17%–43%), which was worse than changing lifestyle. Following an average of 15 years, the lifestyle group was still 27% lower (HR 0.73, 0.65–0.83), but the gap narrowed year by year. At a median follow-up of 21 years, overall mortality did not differ between the lifestyle group and the placebo group (HR 1.02, 0.81–1.28). There was also no difference in cardiovascular death (HR 1.18, 0.77–1.81). The Finnish DPS trial randomized 522 overweight people with impaired glucose tolerance. The cumulative incidence of diabetes in 4 years was 11% in the intervention group and 23% in the control group. The risk was 58% lower during the trial. After discontinuing one-on-one coaching and then continuing it, it was still 43% lower at a median of 7 years. At mean follow-up of 10.6 years, there was no significant difference in total mortality (HR 0.57, 0.21–1.58). Neither did cardiovascular disease (HR 1.04, 0.72–1.51). The boundary set by the Healthy China Action is: a fasting blood glucose of 6.1 to 7.0 mmol/L (excluding 7.0) is considered prediabetes. Blood sugar between 7.8 and 11.1 mmol/L (excluding 11.1) 2 hours after drinking sugar water also counts. It recommends that people who are overweight or obese lower their body mass index to or near 24, or lose at least 7 percent of their body weight. Eat at least 400 to 500 fewer calories per day and engage in moderate-intensity activity for at least 150 minutes per week. Check fasting blood glucose or 2-hour postprandial blood glucose every six months.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Pan XR, Li GW, Hu YH, et al (1997). Effects of diet and exercise in preventing NIDDM in people with impaired glucose tolerance. The Da Qing IGT and Diabetes Study. Diabetes Care, 20(4), 537-544. <https://doi.org/10.2337/diacare.20.4.537>; Li G, Zhang P, Wang J, et al. (2014). Cardiovascular mortality, all-cause mortality, and diabetes incidence after lifestyle intervention for people with impaired glucose tolerance in the Da Qing Diabetes Prevention Study: a 23-year follow-up study. Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, 2(6), 474-480. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-8587(14)70057-9>; Q, Zhang P, Wang J, et al (2019). Morbidity and mortality after lifestyle intervention for people with impaired glucose tolerance: 30-year results of the Da Qing Diabetes Prevention Outcome Study. Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, 7(6), 452-461. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-8587(19)30093-2>; Knowler WC, Barrett-Connor E, Fowler SE, et al (2002). Reduction in the incidence of type 2 diabetes with lifestyle intervention or metformin. NEJM, 346(6), 393-403. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa012512>; Diabetes Prevention Program Research Group (2015). microvascular complications over 15-year follow-up: the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study. Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, 3(11), 866-875. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-8587(15)00291-0>; Lee CG, Heckman-Stoddard B, Dabelea D, et al (2021). Effect of Metformin and Lifestyle Interventions on Mortality in the Diabetes Prevention Program and Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study. Diabetes Care, 44(12), 2775-2782. <https://doi.org/10.2337/dc21-1046> (disputing party); Tuomilehto J, Lindström J, Eriksson JG, et al (2001). Prevention of type 2 diabetes mellitus by changes in lifestyle among subjects with impaired glucose tolerance. NEJM, 344(18), 1343-1350. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM200105033441801>; Lindström J, Ilanne-Parikka P, Peltonen M, et al (2006). Sustained reduction in the incidence of type 2 diabetes by intervention: follow-up of the Finnish Diabetes Prevention Study. Lancet, 368(9548), 1673-1679. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(06)69701-8>; Uusitupa M, Peltonen M, Lindström J, et al (2009). Ten-year mortality and cardiovascular morbidity in the Finnish Diabetes Prevention Study—secondary analysis of the randomized trial. PLoS ONE, 4(5), e5656. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0005656> (disputing party); Healthy China Action Promotion Committee (2019). Healthy China Action (2019-2030), (14) Diabetes Prevention and Control Action (Reprinted by Hunan Provincial Health Commission). <https://wjw.hunan.gov.cn/wjw/ztzl/knowledge/tzggzcfg/202003/t20200303_11359594.html>

Remarks: Dispute. All three trials saw fewer people developing diabetes and developing it later. But whether it can lead to fewer deaths can only be seen in the Daqing experiment. There were only 577 people in Daqing, and the author himself said the number was small because the trial was originally designed to look at diabetes. After the U.S. DPP trial ended, everyone was sent to a modified lifestyle class, including the placebo group. The authors of the Finnish trial wrote that the numbers may not have been large enough to see small differences. Therefore, delaying diabetes is certain, but extending life is not yet certain. The average body mass index of people in the American and Finnish trials was above 30. The average number of people in Daqing is only 25.7. The trial only advised people with a body mass index over 25 to lose weight, and they didn't lose much weight. The author believes that it mainly depends on changing the way you eat and being more active. Therefore, people who are not fat still need to change their eating habits and move more. Cut out sweet drinks first, see No. 7 in this section (No sugary drinks). If you exercise enough, refer to item 11 in this section (reach 7000–8000 steps a day). To determine how much weight to lose, refer to item 32 of this section (control your BMI to 20–25). How to find out, see Section 1, Item 8 (check fasting blood glucose). Metformin can also reduce the risk of diabetes, but the effect is not as good as changing your lifestyle. Whether you should take it or not is decided by your doctor. The magnitude of the benefit was rated as large based on an overall mortality rate of approximately 26% lower in Daqing, but was not replicated in the US and Finnish trials. The beneficiary of this article is mainly yourself.

Case: Uncle Zhao’s physical examination found that his fasting blood sugar was 6.3. He cut half of his rice at dinner and walked briskly for 40 minutes every day. After half a year, his blood sugar dropped to 5.6. He did not develop diabetes. During the reexamination, the doctor said he was doing well.

items.title: If the peanuts, corn, nuts and rice flour at home are moldy, throw away the whole package. Do not pick out the moldy ones and eat the leftovers; chew the nuts until they become bitter and spit them out immediately
items.core: Moldy peanuts and corn will produce aflatoxin, which can cause liver cancer. In a study in Shanghai, people who had this toxin in their urine had a risk of liver cancer that was about 3.4 times higher than those who didn't. The number of people who had hepatitis B virus and were found to have toxins was about 59.4 times more likely than those who had neither. This toxin is difficult to remove by frying, boiling, or frying.
body: Cost: Throwing away a bag of peanuts, nuts or a bag of rice noodles costs a few yuan to dozens of yuan. Usually, keep grains and nuts in a dry, ventilated, and cool place, buy small packages, and stock up less. The difficulty lies in not wanting to throw it away, especially when convincing the elders in the family.

Benefits: Aflatoxin is a Class 1 carcinogen determined by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (definitely can cause cancer in humans) and causes liver cancer. It is most common in peanuts and corn, and it is difficult to destroy it in general cooking such as stir-frying, boiling, and frying. A study in Shanghai followed 18,244 middle-aged men since 1986, and each had a urine sample when they were enrolled. Following approximately 70,000 person-years, 55 cases of liver cancer were detected. Compare 50 of those cases with the 267 people in the same group who didn't get the disease. The risk of liver cancer for those with aflatoxins detected in urine was approximately 3.4 times (RR 3.4, 95% CI 1.1–10.0, confidence range). Hepatitis B surface antigen positivity was approximately 7.3 times higher (2.2–24.4). Those who had both earned about 59.4 times more (16.6–212.0) than those who had neither. In an earlier analysis of the same group of people, excluding hepatitis B, smoking, drinking, and educational level, the number of toxins detected was about 3.8 times (1.2–12.2). Qidong, Jiangsu Province, used to be an area with a high incidence of liver cancer. Since the 1980s, the local staple food has been changed from corn to rice. The median level of toxin markers in residents' blood dropped from 19.3 pg/mg in 1989 to undetectable (less than 0.5) in 2009. The liver cancer death rate among residents under 35 years old fell by more than half among the cohorts born between the 1960s and 1980s. These groups of people were born before hepatitis B vaccination was universally administered to newborns. The authors estimate that about 65% of the reduction in liver cancer deaths can be attributed to eating less toxins, with 83% of that falling among people infected with hepatitis B. According to global estimates, hepatitis B carriers eat the same amount of toxins, and the carcinogenic potential is about 30 times that of people without the virus. A batch of liver cancers in China every year can be attributed to this toxin. About 5,300 to 14,400 of these cases occur in people who are carriers of hepatitis B, and about 1,990 to 4,430 cases occur in people who do not carry the virus.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: IARC (2012). Aflatoxins. In: Chemical Agents and Related Occupations. IARC Monographs on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans, Vol 100F, 225-248. <https://publications.iarc.fr/123>; Qian GS, Ross RK, Yu MC, et al. (1994). A follow-up study of urinary markers of aflatoxin exposure and liver cancer risk in Shanghai, People's Republic of China. Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 3(1), 3-10. <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8118382/>; Ross RK, Yuan JM, Yu MC, et al (1992). Urinary aflatoxin biomarkers and risk of hepatocellular carcinoma. Lancet, 339(8799), 943-946. <https://doi.org/10.1016/0140-6736(92)91528-G>; Chen JG, Egner PA, Ng D, et al (2013). Reduced aflatoxin exposure presages decline in liver cancer mortality in an endemic region of China. Cancer Prevention Research, 6(10), 1038-1045. <https://doi.org/10.1158/1940-6207.CAPR-13-0168>; Liu Y, Wu F (2010). Global burden of aflatoxin-induced hepatocellular carcinoma: a risk assessment. Environmental Health Perspectives, 118(6), 818-824. <https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.0901388>; Oil Products Quality and Safety Risk Assessment Laboratory of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (Wuhan) (2020). Identification and prevention of aflatoxin contamination in agricultural products and food. Popular science world of the Department of Agricultural Products Quality and Safety Supervision, Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs. <https://jgs.moa.gov.cn/kptd/202011/t20201110_6356097.htm>; Guangdong Provincial Health Commission (2015). Do not eat moldy food and beware of aflatoxin poisoning. <https://wsjkw.gd.gov.cn/gkmlpt/content/2/2129/post_2129622.html>; USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service. Molds on Food: Are They Dangerous? <https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/molds-food-are-they-dangerous>

Note: The number in the income column calculates the relationship between "how many toxins you eat" and liver cancer. No research has directly measured how much liver cancer can be reduced by "throwing away moldy things at home". The Shanghai study only had one urine test at the time of enrollment. There is no correlation between the intake estimated by the dietary questionnaire and liver cancer, indicating that the questionnaire estimate is not accurate and must rely on laboratory testing. Toxin markers among Qidong residents could no longer be detected by 2009. The amount most families eat now is likely to be much lower than it was back then. This is a judgment, and there are no national figures. Therefore, the magnitude of the income is not determined as large based on 3.4 times mechanically, but is determined as medium based on judgment. Why throw away the whole bag: The Guangdong Provincial Health and Medical Commission reminds you to throw away the whole bag of nuts and peanuts as soon as they smell smelly after opening, to avoid the mold spores scattering after shaking open. Musty food must be discarded. The USDA's food safety guidelines state that peanut butter, beans and nuts should be thrown away if they become moldy, as should cooked rice, noodles, and bread. Only hard vegetables with low water content such as cabbage and carrots can be cut off at least 2.5 centimeters around the moldy spots before eating. The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs reminds that moldy peanuts will have a bitter and peculiar smell in your mouth. If you eat them by mistake, you should spit them out immediately and rinse your mouth. The risk superposition for hepatitis B carriers is the most obvious. For those who have not been tested for hepatitis B, see Section 1, Article 14 (check for hepatitis B in half and half). For information about buying oil, see Article 40 of this section (do not buy bulk self-pressed peanut oil from small workshops). This article takes care of the grain and nuts stored at home. Acute poisoning such as soaked fungus and fermented rice noodles is another type of toxin, see Section 1, Item 48 (You don’t make your own fermented rice noodles at home). Nuts that are not moldy are still worth eating, see No. 22 in this section (eat a handful of nuts every day). The beneficiaries of this article are mainly you and your family members who eat together.

Case: Uncle Sun in Henan found that a few peanuts in the grain storage were covered with green mold. He threw away the whole bag and refused to eat it. However, his neighbor picked out the moldy grains and ate the rest. Later, he was found to have excessive aflatoxin and was hospitalized.

items.title: Don’t eat raw fish, sashimi, fish porridge and drunken shrimp made from freshwater fish and shrimp. If you eat it frequently, go to the hospital to check for liver flukes. If found out, take praziquantel according to the doctor’s advice
items.core: Eating raw freshwater fish and shrimp will cause liver fluke infection. It is a confirmed cancer-causing parasite, and the risk of cholangiocarcinoma in people infected with it is about four to five times that of those without it. Vinegar, wine, and mustard are not effective at killing it. If you take medicine for two days, more than 90% of the symptoms can be cured.
body: Cost: It doesn’t cost anything to not eat yusheng. It’s difficult to change the taste that has been there for many years. You have to turn it down during dinner parties. If you have eaten often, go to the hospital for a stool test to check for insect eggs. The cost varies from place to place. After checking out, take praziquantel according to the dosage prescribed by the doctor, usually for 1 to 2 days.

Profit: Clonorchis sinensis is commonly known as liver fluke. The International Agency for Research on Cancer, a subsidiary of the World Health Organization, held a meeting in 2009 and concluded that long-term infection with it causes cancer in humans. It can cause cholangiocarcinoma and is classified as category 1. That 1994 assessment gave it only Category 2A (probably carcinogenic). Combining published studies, people infected with liver flukes have about a 4.8-fold risk of developing cholangiocarcinoma. The original article was a relative risk of 4.8 (95% CI 2.8–8.4, confidence range). This number also includes another liver fluke found in Southeast Asia. In the same article, hepatitis B is 2.6 times, hepatitis C is 1.8 times, and liver fluke is the strongest one. Another summarized 36 studies. In case-control studies, the odds ratio for cholangiocarcinoma was approximately 4.37 (OR 4.37, 2.84–6.72). The follow-up study was approximately 10.43 times (RR 10.43, 2.90–37.47). Cholangitis and cholecystitis were about 7.80 times (RR 7.80). Gallstones were approximately 2.42 times more likely (RR 2.42). The odds ratio for hepatocellular carcinoma was approximately 4.69 (OR 4.69). Cholangiocarcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma are both rare, with similar odds ratios and relative risks. No significant association was seen for cirrhosis. The more severe the infection, the more these diseases occur. According to a national survey from 2014 to 2015, the infection rate was 0.47%, approximately 6 million people. The four provinces with infection rates exceeding 1% are Guangdong, Guangxi, Heilongjiang and Jilin. Using monitoring data from 2016 to 2021, it is estimated that in 2020, the number nationwide will be approximately 0.67%, or approximately 9.46 million people. Among them, Guangxi accounts for about 8.92% and Guangdong accounts for about 2.99%. Fifteen departments including the National Administration for Disease Control and Prevention issued prevention and control plans in 2024. The plan is based on the average infection rate at surveillance sites from 2018 to 2022. Guangxi 8.75%, Jilin 4.38%, Heilongjiang 3.16%, and Guangdong 2.95%. National Center for Food Safety Risk Assessment 2026 Tip: Seasonings such as wine, vinegar, and mustard are not effective in killing liver flukes. Freeze at temperatures below minus 20°C for at least 7 days. Heating should bring the center of the food to above 70°C for more than 10 minutes. The International Agency for Research on Cancer also states that salted and smoked freshwater fish can also be contagious. For treatment, see a summary in 2022, with a total of 26 trials and 3340 people. The recommended dosage of praziquantel by the World Health Organization is 25 mg per kilogram of body weight, three times a day for 2 days. The predicted cure rate for Clonorchis sinensis is 98.5% (85.4%–99.9%).
Level of Evidence: B

Source: IARC Working Group on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans (2012). Opisthorchis viverrini and Clonorchis sinensis. In: Biological Agents. IARC Monographs on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans, Vol. 100B, 341-370. <https://publications.iarc.who.int/119>; Shin HR, Oh JK, Masuyer E, et al. (2010). Epidemiology of cholangiocarcinoma: an update focusing on risk factors. Cancer Science, 101(3), 579-585. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1349-7006.2009.01458.x>; pathological changes: a systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS ONE, 10(7), e0132673. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0132673>; Qian MB, Chen J, Bergquist R, et al (2019). Neglected tropical diseases in the People's Republic of China: progress towards elimination.
