Infectious Diseases of Poverty, 8, 86. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s40249-019-0599-4>; Qian MB, Huang JL, Wang L, et al (2025). Clonorchiasis in China: geospatial modeling of the population infected and at risk, based on national surveillance. Journal of Infection, 91(1), 106528. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jinf.2025.106528>; National Bureau of Disease Control and Prevention and other 15 departments (2024). Notice on the issuance of the National Comprehensive Prevention and Control Implementation Plan for Hydatid Disease and Other Key Parasitic Diseases (2024-2030), Appendix 7. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202405/content_6950309.htm>; National Food Safety Risk Assessment Center (2026). Risk tips on eating fresh fresh water fresh food with caution to prevent liver fluke disease (reprinted by Chongqing Center for Disease Control and Prevention). <https://www.cqcdc.org/index.php?a=shows&catid=179&id=3861>; Qian MB, Patel C, Palmeirim MS, et al (2022). Efficacy of drugs against clonorchiasis and opisthorchiasis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis. The Lancet Microbe, 3(8), e616-e624. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2666-5247(22)00026-X>; Institute of Parasitic Disease Prevention and Control, Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2020). Knowledge on prevention and control of clonorchiasis (liver fluke) (Reprinted by Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention). <https://cdcp.gd.gov.cn/jkjy/jkzt/jscbfz/content/post_3439516.html>; Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2023). Will you lose your life if you eat raw fish? Be wary of the “murderer” liver fluke lurking in fish and fish! <https://cdcp.gd.gov.cn/jkjy/jkts/content/post_4274108.html>; Hong Kong Center for Food Safety. Food Safety of Freshwater Fish Sashimi. <https://www.cfs.gov.hk/sc_chi/multimedia/multimedia_pub/multimedia_pub_fsf_148_01.html>

Note: The above risk figures are from case-control and follow-up records, and there is no group control. There are no studies that have directly compared whether "check-up and then treatment" can reduce the risk of cholangiocarcinoma. Cholangiocarcinoma is rare, so although the multiple is high, the risk of it affecting everyone is not high. The grade of evidence is therefore assigned to B. The ratio of about 4.8 times refers to those who are infected and those who are not infected. It does not mean that this method can reduce the number of diseases, so the magnitude of the benefit is determined as medium based on judgment, which is the same as Article 46 of this section (throw away the whole package if it is moldy). Guangdong CDC says liver flukes can live in humans for 20 to 30 years. Mild cases often have no symptoms, so people who often eat raw fish should not wait until they feel uncomfortable to get checked out. Testing stool to look for worm eggs is the only way to confirm the diagnosis, and B-ultrasound, CT, and blood drawing can only assist. Praziquantel should be dosed by a doctor based on body weight and severity of infection. The Parasitology Department states that a medical history should be obtained before using large doses in areas where cysticercosis is present. If you are cured and continue to eat fish, you will get it again. Keep raw fish knives and cutting boards separate from cooked food. Parasites such as Anisakis are commonly found in marine fish sashimi. The Hong Kong Center for Food Safety recommends that the elderly, children, and pregnant women not eat raw fish if purchased from licensed stores. If a child is infected, it will affect his growth. Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C can also damage the liver and cause cancer. See Section 1, Item 14 (Check for hepatitis B twice and half) and Section 1, Item 45 (Check for Hepatitis C antibodies once). The beneficiaries of this article are mainly yourself and your family members who eat together.

Case: A Qiang from Guangdong often eats raw fish. His physical examination revealed that he was positive for liver fluke. He took praziquantel for two days as directed by the doctor. After a re-examination, the eggs turned negative. The doctor told him to only eat cooked freshwater fish and shrimp in the future.

items.title: Turn off non-essential notifications and put your phone out of sight when working
items.core: If your phone rings, even if you don’t look at it or touch it, your score on attention tasks will be lost. The drop is about the same as if you actually answered the phone or sent a text message. There is another situation: if your mobile phone is placed on the table and you resist looking at it, the amount of brain space you can use will also decrease. The more people can't live without their mobile phones, the more they lose.
body: Cost: No money. Taking a few minutes to change the settings requires little perseverance.

Benefits: Just receiving a notification without looking at it or touching it significantly worsened the performance of the attention task. The magnitude of the deterioration is comparable to actually making phone calls or sending text messages. This was done in a laboratory, and the subjects were college students. Two other experiments show that even if you successfully restrain yourself from looking at your phone, leaving your phone next to you will reduce the amount of brain space you can use. People with strong cell phone dependence experienced the greatest decline.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Stothart, Mitchum & Yehnert (2015). The attentional cost of receiving a cell phone notification. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance. Capacity. Journal of the Association for Consumer Research. <https://doi.org/10.1086/691462>

Note: These are single tasks in the laboratory. No one has measured the results of accumulating this every day. For positions that really require on-call availability, you can leave notifications for only a few contacts.

Case: Xiao Zhang, a copywriter, put his mobile phone in a drawer while working and turned off WeChat and short video push. The plan that originally took two hours to write was handed in in one and a half hours, and he no longer lost his mind frequently.

items.title: Set your wake-up time, even on weekends
items.core: The fifth of people with the most chaotic schedules have their biological clocks about 2.5 hours later than the fifth of people with the most regular schedules. It's like living in jet lag for a long time. Students who have a more regular schedule have better grades.
body: Cost: No money. It takes a little perseverance to sleep less on weekends.

Benefits: 61 college students logged 30 days. In the quintile with the most irregular schedules, the biological clock (circadian rhythm) is about 2.5 hours later than in the quintile with the most regular schedules. Specifically, the moment when melatonin begins to be secreted is 00:08 vs. 21:32. The period when you are most sleepy and want to sleep is about 1.8 hours later. The more regular the routine, the better the academic performance (correlation coefficient r = 0.37).
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Phillips et al. (2017). Irregular sleep/wake patterns are associated with poorer academic performance and delayed circadian and sleep/wake timing. Scientific Reports. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-03171-4>

Remarks: This is the only study with a small number of people and no group control. The researchers used a model to deduce that the difference in biological clocks is mainly due to the different light seen every day. They suggested that you could try using light to adjust it, but there was no experimental verification. Therefore, in addition to the fixed wake-up time, go out more and see the light during the day. This is derived from their calculations. How to catch up on sleep after occasionally staying up late, see Section 2, Item 38 (Catch up on sleep the next night after staying up late): The method is to go to bed early that night instead of sleeping until noon the next day.

Case: Xiao Chen, a college student, used to sleep until noon on weekends and always felt sleepy in class on Mondays. He changed to getting up at 7 o'clock every day, including weekends. After two weeks, he no longer naps in morning classes and his endorsement efficiency has become higher.

items.title: Sleep 7 to 8 hours a night, don't think 6 hours is enough
items.core: If you only sleep 6 hours a night for two weeks, your brain's performance will drop to a level equivalent to two days and two nights without sleep. The trouble is that I can't feel it. Self-rated sleepiness stopped rising after the first few days, and people who slept for 6 hours rated themselves as sleepy as those who slept for 4 hours. So the feeling of "I sleep for 6 hours is enough" is unreliable.
body: Cost: No money. Allow an extra 1 to 2 hours for sleep every day. Going to bed earlier requires a little perseverance.

Benefits: 48 healthy adults, ages 21 to 38, slept only 6 hours per night for 14 days. Their mental performance declined cumulatively, to levels equivalent to two consecutive nights of no sleep at all. However, self-rated sleepiness only increased in the first few days and then almost stopped increasing. There was no difference in self-rated sleepiness between the 6-hour and 4-hour groups. This is a controlled trial (RCT) in which people are randomly divided into two groups. Additionally, short periods of sleep deprivation (acute sleep deprivation, no more than 48 hours) had effect sizes of g = -0.776 for simple mind wandering and g = -0.125 for reasoning accuracy. This part is calculated by combining 70 studies.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Van Dongen, Maislin, Mullington & Dinges (2003). The cumulative cost of additional wakefulness. Sleep. <https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/26.2.117>; Lim & Dinges (2010). A meta-analysis of the impact of short-term sleep deprivation on cognitive variables. Psychological Bulletin. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0018883>

Note: The most important point is that "I don't feel sleepy" is not evidence that I have slept enough. People who sleep for 6 hours for a long time just feel used to it, and their performance does not keep up. The part that summarizes multiple studies talks about staying up all night. There is only one randomized controlled trial to support "chronic sleep deprivation". The relationship between how long you sleep and the risk of death is calculated separately. See Section 2, Item 13 (about 7 hours of sleep every night): When calculating the mortality rate, the 7-hour period has the lowest risk.

Case: Xiao Chen only slept 6 hours a night for two weeks in a row to work on a project, claiming that he was used to it. He responded slowly at the regular meeting, and added two wrong columns of data to the report. After changing back to sleeping for 7.5 hours, similar errors were significantly reduced.

items.title: No caffeine after 2 pm
items.core: Drink 400 mg of caffeine 6 hours before going to bed, which is almost three or four cups of coffee. That night, the instrument measured that I lost more than 1 hour of sleep. But I couldn’t see any difference at all in my sleep diary. A 250 mL cup of coffee (107 mg) should be consumed at least 8.8 hours before bedtime to avoid affecting sleep. For those who go to bed at 11 o'clock, 2 o'clock in the afternoon is the limit.
body: Cost: No money. For those who are used to drinking coffee in the afternoon, it takes a little perseverance to resist drinking.

Benefits: Taking a 400 mg caffeine pill six hours before bed resulted in 1.1 to 1.2 hours less total measured sleep time than taking a placebo pill. Assuming that a 250 mL cup of coffee contains 107 mg, 400 mg is approximately the amount of three or four cups of coffee. The placebo tablets look the same but contain no caffeine. However, the sleep diaries written by the subjects themselves did not report the difference and they were not aware of it. Putting the studies together (meta-analysis): caffeine reduces total sleep time by an average of 45 minutes. The proportion of people actually asleep in bed (sleep efficiency) decreased by 7%. A 250 mL cup of coffee (107 mg) should be consumed at least 8.8 hours before bedtime to avoid affecting sleep.
Level of Evidence: A
Source: Drake, Roehrs, Shambroom & Roth (2013). Caffeine effects on sleep taken 0, 3, or 6 hours before going to bed. Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.smrv.2023.101764>

Note: Only one laboratory has done the Drake study, and the 400 mg used is too large, which is equal to the upper limit of drinking one day at a time. The upper limit is shown in Section 2, Article 26 (three to four cups of coffee). For people who metabolize caffeine slowly, the cutoff time is even earlier. What you get back by drinking less caffeine is sleep duration, which stacks up with number 3 (get enough 7 to 8 hours of sleep every night).

Case: Xiao Lin ordered another American drink at three o'clock in the afternoon. After lying down at eleven o'clock in the evening, his mind was clear. His bracelet showed that he slept one hour less than usual. After switching to drinking coffee after lunch and only drinking water in the afternoon, I fell asleep much easier.

items.title: Change emails and messages to be processed in batches a few times a day
items.core: Compared with the same group of people for two weeks. The week I limited my email checking to just three times a day, I experienced significantly lower daily stress while sending and receiving the same amount of email. Without restrictions, people check an average of 15.5 times a day.
body: Cost: No money. Take the time to clarify with colleagues how often you will be back. It takes a little perseverance to resist checking emails at any time.

Benefits: 124 adults, before and after comparison of the same group of people over two weeks (self-control). Daily stress was significantly lower in the week when checking email was limited to three times per day than in the week when checks were unlimited (effect size Cohen's d = 0.37). There was no difference in the number of emails received and responded to over two weeks. When we started without restrictions, people checked email an average of 15.5 times a day.
Level of Evidence: B
Source: Kushlev & Dunn (2015). Checking email less frequently reduces stress. Computers in Human Behavior. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chb.2014.11.005>
Note: There is only one study, the effect is medium to small, and the measurement is stress, not the work done. No one has directly studied instant messaging, so this is just a recommendation.

Case: Xiao Wang used to refresh his mailbox every ten minutes during meetings and work, and felt disturbed all day long. He fixed checking mails three times in the morning, afternoon, and before get off work. After finishing all the mails that day, his stress was reduced.

items.title: When doing work that requires continuous thinking, block out even a few seconds of interruption
items.core: An average interruption of 2.8 seconds doubles the probability of errors in the following operations. 4.4 seconds of interruption tripled. On-site tracking also found that it took an average of 25 minutes to get back to the interrupted thing, and two other things were inserted in the middle. People who were interrupted worked faster, but with higher levels of stress, frustration, and effort.
body: Cost: No money. Close the door, put on headphones, or put up a "Do Not Disturb" sign.

Benefits: An average interruption of 2.8 seconds will double the step error rate of tasks done step by step in order (sequence tasks). A 4.4 second break triples that. This is done in a laboratory. The other was an on-site observation of 24 white-collar office workers (information workers). On average, they switch work topics every 11 minutes. 57% of work topics were interrupted. Returning to the interrupted activity during the day took an average of 25 minutes and 26 seconds. 2.26 other things were inserted in between. There was also an experiment with 48 people: People who were interrupted worked faster but reported higher levels of stress, frustration, time pressure, and effort.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Altmann, Trafton & Hambrick (2014). Momentary interruptions can derail the train of thought. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0030986>; Mark, Gonzalez & Harris (2005). No task left behind? Examining the nature of fragmented work. CHI 2005. <https://doi.org/10.1145/1054972.1055017>; Mark, Gudith & Klocke (2008). The cost of interrupted work: More speed and stress. CHI 2008. <https://doi.org/10.1145/1357054.1357072>

Note: That field study divided interruptions into two categories: those that come to you from others, and those that are initiated by yourself. Closing the door only blocks the former category. The latter category should be used in conjunction with Item 1 (Turn off non-essential notifications) and Item 5 (Batch processing of messages).

Case: When designer Lao Zhou was writing a plan, his colleagues frequently poked their heads in to ask for details. They only spoke for a few seconds each time, but he always had to re-examine his ideas. After putting on earplugs and setting the status to Do Not Disturb, the half-day rework was reduced by more than half.

items.title: Do one thing at a time, don’t answer messages while in a meeting
items.core: Once tasks are switched, responses are slower and more error-prone. People who often use several media at the same time have not developed the ability to do several things at the same time, but perform worse on task switching tests.
body: Cost: Nothing. It takes a little perseverance to refrain from replying to messages during a meeting.

Benefits: After task switching, the response is significantly slower and more error-prone. This section comes from a review of multiple studies. Another laboratory study involved college students. People who frequently use several media at the same time (heavy media multitaskers) are more likely to be distracted by irrelevant things and irrelevant memories. They actually performed worse on the task-switching test.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Monsell (2003). Task switching. Trends in Cognitive Sciences. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S1364-6613(03)00028-7>; Ophir, Nass & Wagner (2009). Cognitive control in media multitaskers. PNAS. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0903620106>

Note: How much more it costs to switch back and forth varies greatly depending on the work you do, so we won’t give a unified number here. Ophir's study was a comparison at the same time point. It's unclear whether "multitasking makes attention worse" or "people with poor attention tend to multitask more."

Case: At the department meeting, Xiao Li was listening to the budget discussion while replying to the group message. He missed the final amount and asked his colleagues after the meeting. Later, he put his cell phone on the table and only took notes, recording the meeting's conclusions all at once.

items.title: Do not look at light-emitting screens one hour before going to bed. If you want to read, read a paper book or an ink screen with no screen light on.
items.core: In the experiment, I turned the iPad to the brightest and read for about 4 hours before going to bed. I fell asleep about 10 minutes later than reading a paper book. Melatonin is suppressed by 55%. The next day, the biological clock is pushed back by more than 1.5 hours, making me sleepier in the morning and taking longer to wake up.
body: Cost: Nothing. Put down your phone one hour before going to bed. It takes perseverance to fight against inertia for a long time.

Benefit: Let the same group of people take turns to do two conditions in the laboratory (crossover experiment). One is to read e-books on the iPad before going to bed, adjust the brightness to the highest level, and read for about 4 hours, for 5 nights. The other is to read a paper book in an equally dark room. Reading a glowing e-book before bed was about 10 minutes slower than falling asleep from a paper book (25.7 minutes vs. 15.8 minutes). Melatonin is suppressed by 55% in the evening. The next day's biological clock (circadian rhythm) is delayed by more than 1.5 hours, with melatonin secretion starting at 22:31 versus 21:01. The next morning I was even sleepier and took longer to fully wake up.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Chang, Aeschbach, Duffy & Czeisler (2015). Evening use of light-emitting eReaders negatively affects sleep, circadian timing, and next-morning alertness. PNAS. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1418490112>

Note: The number of people is small and the conditions are controlled in the laboratory. Depending on the daily brightness and usage time of mobile phones, the impact may not be so great. This study didn't test how useful a phone's night mode is. It didn't test the ink screen either. The ink screen without the screen light relies on reflecting the light in the room just like the paper book, so it is classified as the paper book. This is deduced from this research. The ink screen with the screen light on is also glowing and has no data.

Case: Xiao Wu lay in bed and used the brightest tablet to watch TV dramas before going to bed. His eyes became clearer and clearer as he watched, and it was very difficult to get up the next morning. After switching to paper books, she felt sleepy before the usual time and didn't feel so heavy when she woke up.

items.title: Go to bed when the time comes and don’t stay up late watching games, short videos, or pornographic content
items.core: In 2025, Chinese people will sleep an average of 6.97 hours at night and fall asleep at an average of 0:10. Among children and teenagers, those who use mobile phones and tablets before going to bed are significantly more likely to not get enough sleep and feel sleepy during the day. The equipment is just placed in the bedroom and not used, so that's about it. If you want to change it, the easiest way is to keep your cell phone out of the bedroom.
body: Cost: Nothing. The difficulty lies in resisting the inertia of "watching just one more episode" for a long time. Keeping your cell phone out of the bedroom saves the most effort.

Benefits: In 2025, Chinese residents will sleep an average of 6.97 hours at night, with an average sleep time of 0:10 (Chinese Sleep Research Association). Those who used portable devices before bed had an odds ratio of not getting enough sleep (OR 2.17). The numbers in this paragraph are odds ratios and cannot be read directly as multiples of probability. The odds ratio for poor sleep quality was 1.46 (OR 1.46). The odds ratio for daytime sleepiness was 2.72 (OR 2.72). The odds ratios for devices that are just placed in the bedroom and not used are similar, 1.79, 1.53, and 2.27 respectively (OR 1.79/1.53/2.27). This part is calculated by combining 20 surveys at the same time point and 125,198 children and adolescents. Another survey at the same time point included 844 adults aged 18 to 94 years. Among them, people who still use their mobile phones after turning off the lights are slower to fall asleep, have a lower proportion of actually falling asleep in bed, and are more tired during the day.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Carter et al. (2016). Association Between Portable Screen-Based Media Device Access or Use and Sleep Outcomes. JAMA Pediatrics. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2016.2341>; Exelmans & Van den Bulck (2016). Bedtime mobile phone use and sleep in adults. Social Science & Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2015.11.037>; Chinese Sleep Research Association (2026). 2026 China Sleep Health Research White Paper (Reprinted by the Fujian Provincial Health Commission as reported by the Health News). <https://web.archive.org/web/20261001203506/https://wjw.fujian.gov.cn/jggk/csxx/xcc/mtbd/202603/t20260323_7114382.htm> (The original page has been offline, the link is the web archive on October 1, 2026); Grubbs JB et al. (2018). Pornography Problems Due to Moral Incongruence: An Integrative Model with a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Archives of Sexual Behavior. Responsiveness, Not Erectile Dysfunction. Sexual Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1002/sm2.58> (the second controversial party in the remarks)

Note: Controversy. The price of staying up late itself is shown in No. 3 of this section (get enough 7 to 8 hours of sleep every night). There is currently no reliable evidence to say whether pornography is responsible for the impact it has on the energy and brain power of ordinary people. An analysis that compiled multiple studies concluded that the so-called "pornography problem" stems more from a mismatch between a person's ideas and his or her behavior than from the content itself. Another study compiled data from 280 men. The results showed that there was no relationship between the duration of watching and erectile function during sex with a partner. Let’s just focus on the fact that it takes up sleep time. The two numbers 6.97 hours and 0:10 are not published on the official website of the Chinese Sleep Research Association (checked in September 2026). This is based on the health newspaper report reproduced by the Fujian Provincial Health Commission.

Case: Xiao Zheng, a second-year high school student, puts his mobile phone on the bedside and watches short videos until midnight at night. He always lies on his desk during class during the day. After his parents moved his mobile phone to charge in the living room, he went to bed at midnight and could keep up with his early reading.

items.title: Do not make important decisions or send important news late at night
items.core: When people get enough sleep, they quickly learn to avoid high-risk options. After not sleeping for two nights in a row, the risk increases again and again. The older I get, the more obvious it becomes. The impact of missing a few hours of sleep has not been directly measured, but the important decision must be postponed until after waking up.
body: Cost: Nothing. Just push things off until after you wake up.

Earnings: 34 healthy people did the Iowa Gambling Task after 49.5 hours without sleep. It's an experiment in measuring risky decisions. When well-rested, they quickly learn to avoid high-risk options. After being deprived of sleep, they tend to choose high-risk options more often. Older people are more affected. This is an experiment and only this study.
Level of Evidence: B
Source: Killgore, Balkin & Wesensten (2006). Impaired decision making following 49 h of sleep deprivation. Journal of Sleep Research. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2869.2006.00487.x>

Note: The study is about the extreme situation of not sleeping for two consecutive nights. There is no direct measurement of what would happen if ordinary people stayed up until two o'clock in the morning. "Not sending a message" is half of the author's experience (level C), and it's not too late to send it the next day.

Case: Lao Zhang had an argument with his wife after working overtime for two nights in a row, and wanted to make an angry statement in the middle of the night. He first saved the draft and rewrote it when he woke up, leaving only one thing to resolve the next day without escalating the conflict.

items.title: If you feel sleepy in the afternoon, take a nap for 10 minutes instead of half an hour.
items.core: When you didn't get enough sleep the night before, a 10-minute nap can refresh you on the spot, and some of the effects can last up to two and a half hours. Five minutes of sleep is basically useless. It takes 35 minutes for 20 minutes of sleep to take effect. After sleeping for 30 minutes, I would feel dazed for a while when I woke up, and my performance during that period would be worse than if I hadn't slept.
body: Cost: Nothing. Take 10 minutes and find another place to lie down or tummy.

Benefits: After not getting enough sleep the night before, a 10-minute nap can immediately improve sleepiness, fatigue, energy, and mental performance, with some of the benefits lasting 155 minutes later. There is little benefit from sleeping for 5 minutes. The benefits of a 20-minute nap don’t appear until 35 minutes later. After sleeping for 30 minutes, there is a period of sleep inertia: the performance is worse when I first wake up, and then improves.
Level of Evidence: B
Source: Brooks & Lack (2006). A brief afternoon nap following nocturnal sleep restriction: Which nap duration is most recuperative? Sleep. <https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/29.6.831>

Note: There is only one laboratory study in healthy young adults. Don’t force yourself if you can’t sleep. There is no research to support whether lying with your eyes closed for 10 minutes is helpful. Napping for more than an hour is linked to higher mortality and risk of coronary heart disease, see Section 2, Item 37 (naps should be limited to half an hour).

Case: After lunch, Xiao Liu was so sleepy that he read the wrong form. He tried to sleep for 30 minutes, but when he woke up, he was confused and slowed down. Later, he set an alarm for 10 minutes and woke up after lying down for a while. In the afternoon, he checked the data much more smoothly.

items.title: Use earplugs when working in an open-plan office or find a quiet room to do memory-intensive tasks
items.core: As the background noise increases from 39 decibels to 51 decibels, fewer words can be remembered, and people become more tired and less inclined to work. Watching nature videos with sound during your break can help you regain your energy more than listening to office noise.
body: Cost: Earplugs cost several dozen yuan. Take the time to reserve a quiet conference room.

Benefits: Let students work in simulated open offices. When background noise was raised from 39 to 51 decibels (dB, LAeq), they remembered fewer words, rated themselves as more tired, and felt less inclined to work. Watching nature videos with sound during breaks can bring back your energy score more than just listening to the sound of the river or office noise.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Jahncke, Hygge, Halin, Green & Dimberg (2011). Open-plan office noise: Cognitive performance and restoration. Journal of Environmental Psychology. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvp.2011.07.002>
Note: Only one laboratory study. The most annoying thing among the noise is the sound of voices. White noise headphones can help with this, but this study did not test headphones.

Case: In the open office, when Xiao He was memorizing the customer list, there were always people chatting next to him, and he couldn't remember it even after reading it over and over. She put on earplugs and went to the small conference room to recite the name for ten minutes. After returning, she was able to name most of the names.

items.title: Don’t just keep adding more hours to your weekly working week: after about 49 hours, an extra hour of extra work will produce less and less work.
items.core: Records from British armaments factories during World War I show that workers were given as much work as they could work within a 49-hour week. Over 49 hours, an extra hour adds less and less work. Working 70 hours a week produces almost the same amount of work as working 56 hours, and the extra 14 hours are wasted.
body: Cost: You may get less overtime pay. You may also have to put in the effort to talk to your superiors.

Earnings: Record output of British munitions factory workers during World War I: within 49 hours per week, output proportional to hours worked. Beyond 49 hours, the rate of increase in output begins to slow. Maximum is reached around 63 hours. The output of working for 70 hours is almost the same as that of working for 56 hours. The extra 14 hours is equivalent to working in vain.
Level of Evidence: B
Source: Pencavel (2015). The Productivity of Working Hours. The Economic Journal. <https://doi.org/10.1111/ecoj.12166>

Note: The data comes from factories a hundred years ago, where manual labor was done, and the workers were mainly women. This threshold may not be the same when it comes to mental work. The author himself said that it may be higher or lower in other types of work. What is reliable is the direction: after a certain point, no matter how hard you work, you will get almost no extra work. The exact number of 49 is unreliable.

Case: Before the project went online, the team leader asked the team to work continuously for 65 hours a week. In the next few days, review errors increased and the progress was not much faster. After changing to about 49 hours per week, deliveries were completed as usual and there was less rework.

items.title: When you find that you are thinking about the same bad thing over and over again, change to something that requires hands-on work
items.core: Remembering the same bad thing over and over will aggravate your depression, nail the negative thoughts more firmly, make it harder for people to solve the problem, and make it harder to actually take action. It also drains you of people around you who are willing to listen to you. When you realize you're going around in circles, go do some hands-on work.
body: Cost: No money. The difficulty lies in first noticing that you are thinking over and over again (this is called rumination), and the awareness itself requires practice.

Benefits: A review of multiple studies says that repeatedly thinking about the same bad event (rumination) can worsen depression. It also reinforces negative thinking and weakens problem-solving abilities. It gets in the way of actual action and drains you of people around you who are willing to listen to what you have to say. It is associated with anxiety, overeating, alcoholism, and self-harm.
Level of Evidence: B
Source: Nolen-Hoeksema, Wisco & Lyubomirsky (2008). Rethinking Rumination. Perspectives on Psychological Science. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1745-6924.2008.00088.x>

Note: The review only gives directions, no numbers. "Changing jobs" is the author's own approach. There is only one sentence that the literature can support: it is better to divert attention than to continue to go around in circles. As for what kind of job to change, no one has compared it.

Case: After Xiao Zhao was criticized, he thought about the same sentence repeatedly at night, and even after telling his friends twice, he still couldn't get around it. She got up to wash the dishes and tidy the table. After getting busy, she finally wrote a short remedial email.

items.title: Consider thoughts such as "Things will definitely be worse" as symptoms rather than facts
items.core: In a twin study that followed for 20 years, the higher the pessimism score, the higher the risk of death. For each higher score, the risk of death was about 13% higher and the risk of death from cardiovascular disease was about 20% higher. In turn, high optimism scores did not confer corresponding benefits. So what we need to deal with is pessimism, not "not enough positive energy".
body: Cost: No money. The difficulty lies in seeing this thought as a symptom rather than a fact.

Yields: 2978 Australian twins aged 50 and over were followed for an average of 20 years, during which 1068 died. For each standard deviation higher on the pessimism scale, the risk of death was approximately 13% higher (hazard ratio 1.134). The confidence range for this number is 95% CI 1.065–1.207, P=8.85×10⁻⁵. Cardiovascular death was approximately 20% higher (1.196, 1.045–1.368, P=0.0093). Not associated with cancer death. Optimism scores were also not significantly associated with mortality.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Whitfield JB, Zhu G, Landers JG, Martin NG (2020). Pessimism is associated with greater all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, but optimism is not protective. Scientific Reports, 10, 12609. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-69388-y>

Remarks: Controversial. This is just observation, no grouping. Some people may say, "In fact, pessimism comes from the disease first." The author retorts that if that is the case, cancer deaths should also be related. But there may still be unmeasured factors. Optimism is not protective, so there is no need to force yourself to "think positive." What needs to be done is not to regard pessimistic expectations as accurate predictions of the future.

Case: Mr. Li is worried that the project will fail and has trouble sleeping and eating. He dismissed this thought as a symptom of pessimism rather than a fact and went to the hospital. After psychological counseling and antidepressant treatment, his mood improved and the project was successfully completed.

items.title: Reduce the relationships that consume you and learn to say no to unwanted requests
items.core: In a survey of widowed women aged 60 to 89, the relationship between uncomfortable interactions and happiness was stronger and more consistent than comfortable interactions. So do subtraction first, then addition.
body: Cost: No money. There will be social friction in the short term, and some relationships may be lost. It takes considerable perseverance to say no.

Benefits: Survey of 120 widowed women aged 60 to 89: The association between unpleasant relationships and psychological well-being is more consistent and stronger than comfortable relationships. According to this result, the loss caused by a person who consumes you is greater than the benefit brought by a person who supports you.
Evidence level: C
Source: Rook (1984). The negative side of social interaction: Impact on psychological well-being. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.46.5.1097>

Note: The respondent population is special, and it is a one-time questionnaire, so the order cannot be seen. What is measured is happiness, not energy. The placement in this section is the author's inference. There is no objective standard for which relationships are considered "consumption", you can only judge by yourself.

Case: Aunt Wang often helps neighbors take care of their children, but she is exhausted. She began to refuse unreasonable requests and reduce consumptive social interactions. Half a year later, she had time to join her favorite choir, and her happiness improved significantly.

items.title: When you are angry, leave the scene first and treat the other person as the weather rather than the enemy
items.core: Look at what just happened from another angle, or think about it from the other person's point of view, which can lower your emotions. The latter is more effective. Just not showing your emotions has some effect. But it's useless to suppress the feelings in my heart and try not to think about it. People who punished the offender thought about the incident longer afterwards, while people who did not retaliate turned over the story more quickly.
body: Cost: No money. You should refrain from replying on the spot, turn around and walk away, and decide whether to deal with it later. This takes a little practice.

Benefits: Comparing 306 experimental comparisons combined (meta-analysis): The effect size on mood of explaining what happened from another perspective (cognitive reappraisal) was d = 0.36. Put yourself in the opponent's shoes and see d = 0.45. Shifting attention d = 0.27. Suppressing external displays of emotion (not showing it) was effective, d = 0.32. Trying to suppress the feeling doesn't work (d = -0.04), nor does trying not to think about it (d = -0.12). These numbers are calculated from the sum of the indicators of inner feelings, external performance and physical reactions, and are not given separately in the summary. Another three experiments showed that people who punished the offender thought about the offender longer afterwards; people who did not punish the offender were quicker to "turn over". People overestimate the pleasure of revenge in advance.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Webb TL, Miles E, Sheeran P (2012). Dealing with feeling: A meta-analysis of the effectiveness of strategies derived from the process model of emotion regulation. Psychological Bulletin. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0027600>; Carlsmith KM, Wilson TD, Gilbert DT (2008). The paradoxical consequences of revenge. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0012165>

Note: The portion that summarizes multiple studies measures emotional intensity, not energy, and the effect size is small to moderate. There is only one set of experiments for the revenge part, so it is rated B. "The Empty Ship" is a fable in Zhuangzi's "Mountain Trees": An empty ship will not be angry if it collides with it, but only if there are people on board it will be angry, but the collision is the same. The title says "when the weather" means the same thing: just like the rain is not directed at you, don't take the other person's attention as it is directed at you. This is an analogy, not evidence. If you really have a loss, take the Section 8 and 9 legal route, which is much cheaper than having an attack on the spot.

Case: Xiao Zhang was criticized in public by his colleagues and became angry. He immediately left the scene and went to the tea room to calm down, thinking that his colleagues might be under pressure. Ten minutes later, he returned calmly, communicated with his colleagues, and resolved the misunderstanding.

items.title: When you are depressed, do the most cost-effective things first: move, see more light, go to bed on time, talk to someone, and take a phone call. 12356
items.core: Brisk walking, jogging, yoga and strength training can all reduce depression. The greater the intensity, the more effective it is. For details, see Section 22, Item 6 (walk or run when you are in a bad mood). Light therapy has a strong effect on seasonal depression and is also effective on depression regardless of season. Online self-help cognitive behavioral courses are effective, and it is better to have someone with you when symptoms are severe. If you can’t think of it, call 12356 first.
body: Cost: No money, or very little. Go for a brisk walk, jog, or strength training a few times a week. Go out and bask in the sun during the day. The routine is fixed. Make a phone call when you're stuck.

Benefits: 218 randomized controlled trials, 14,170 people combined (network meta-analysis). The control group was people who were also doing other activities. Compared with them, walking or jogging had an effect size on depression of g = -0.62 (95% confidence interval -0.80 to -0.45). Yoga -0.55, strength training -0.49. The greater the intensity, the better the effect. Combining multiple light therapy studies: effect sizes were 0.84 (0.60 to 1.08) for seasonal depression and 0.53 (0.18 to 0.89) for nonseasonal depression. There was also an analysis that combined patient-by-patient data from each study. It looks at Internet Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (online self-help courses). Both guided and unsupervised conditions performed better than the control group. At moderate to severe levels (PHQ-9 greater than 9 points), it is better to have someone to guide you. 12356 is the national psychological assistance hotline, open no less than 18 hours a day.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Noetel M et al (2024). Effect of exercise for depression: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. BMJ. <https://doi.org/10.1176/appi.ajp.162.4.656>; Karyotaki E et al (2021). Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Depression: A Systematic Review and Individual Patient Data Network Meta-analysis. JAMA Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2020.4364>; National Health Commission (2024). Notice on the application of the "12356" national unified psychological assistance hotline number (National Health Medical Administration Letter [2024] No. 259). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6994470.htm>

Note: These are auxiliary means for mild to moderate depression. If you are seeking medical treatment for moderate to severe suicidal thoughts, please call 12356 first (see Section 1, Article 25). Most exercise trials involve a small number of people, and there is no way to hide who is exercising like in drug trials. The illumination study only lasted until 2003, and the number of people was small. Those studies used specialized lighting lamps, not sunlight. Changing it to going out to bask in the sun during the day is derived from phototherapy. "Go to bed on time" and "find someone to tell you" are the author's experiences and there is no separate literature. Don't think of "moving" as a requirement for depressed people. If you can walk for ten minutes, it counts.

Case: Xiao Chen was depressed due to a broken relationship and was unable to work. He insists on running for 30 minutes every morning, getting more sun, going to bed on time, and talking to his friends. Three weeks later, my mood improved significantly and I returned to work.

items.title: Think of police officers, doctors, and tellers as people who work according to rules, not as roles: it is documents and deadlines that can push things forward, not emotions
items.core: Police officers, doctors, and tellers are all people who work according to job rules, and are governed by documents, deadlines, and supervision. It is written in the rules whether the matter should be completed within a few days and what paperwork should be given if it cannot be completed. So get a receipt, note the deadline, and appeal through channels, and don’t think about explaining the truth until the other party agrees.
body: Cost: No money. What changes is your expectations and sequence of actions. For the first time, you have to resist the urge to "talk the truth to the other person until they agree."

Benefits: Change your actions in dealing with organizations: from "asking for help, getting angry, and repeating your grievances over and over again" to "getting documents, recording deadlines, and appealing through channels." What is saved is the time of repeated communication and repeated recall. This is a one-time adjustment of mindset and does not save time every day. What can be checked are the deadlines themselves, which are written down in the document. The time limit for handling a public security case shall not exceed 30 days from the day it is accepted; if the case is serious and complex, it may be extended by 30 days with the approval of the higher-level public security agency. If a case involving an accuser is decided not to be filed, the notice of disapproval must be served within 3 days. The accuser can apply for reconsideration within 7 days, and the public security organ will make a decision within 30 days. If you are not satisfied, you can apply for review to the next higher level within 7 days.
Evidence level: C

Source: Ministry of Public Security (2020). Provisions on the procedures for handling criminal cases by public security organs (Ministry of Public Security Order No. 159, as amended, Articles 171, 178, and 179). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5549884.htm>; Ministry of Public Security (amended in 2013/2019). Procedures for handling administrative cases by public security organs (Ministry of Public Security Order No. 125, No. 149). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2013/content_2321117.htm>

Remarks: Reason for setting C: "Many people regard the person behind the window as a character and not as a working person." There is no literature to cite for this judgment itself. Only half of the rules can be quoted: deadlines, documents and relief channels are all clearly stated. The figures quoted in this article all come from the two Ministry of Public Security regulations in Section 8, Article 39 (Process after reporting the alarm). Just following the process can't control "the other party's bad attitude", and it doesn't guarantee that it will be done. What you can change is your expectations and first step. The same goes for bank tellers and government affairs counters: their operations leave traces, need to be reviewed, and mistakes must be held accountable. So what you should do is to leave a receipt, ask for a reply, and complain according to the channel. Don't make blind guesses about "will he cheat me?" Legal priorities are clearly written, for example, emergency services are graded according to condition, not on a first-come, first-served basis (Section 24, Article 7, Emergency Pre-screening Triage). If you want to thank the doctor who saved your life, write a thank you letter and satisfaction rating, see Section 24, Item 11. If you want to "give something so that people can have more snacks", it is a crime of bribery for those who handle the case and law enforcement, and it is expressly serious, see Section 8, Article 40. If you encounter obvious differential treatment, it is the object of complaints and supervision, not an unspoken rule to be imitated.

Case: Mr. Wang ran many errands to no avail when applying for procedures to go abroad. Later, he organized all the materials in accordance with the service guidelines, asked for an acceptance receipt and noted down the commitment period. When the application was overdue, he successfully completed the appeal with the receipt.

items.title: Don’t regard “how other people are doing” as a daily must-read: set limits or turn off apps that check the status of peers
items.core: People who are used to comparing themselves to others who are doing better online tend to have worse moods and lower self-esteem. People who deactivated Facebook for four weeks experienced a small increase in happiness, but also lost some knowledge of current events. People who limited each of the three social platforms to 10 minutes a day were less lonely and depressed after three weeks.
body: Cost: Nothing. It only takes a few minutes to set a time limit for an application or to deactivate an account. The hard thing is not to open it again, and you have to fight against inertia for a long time.

Benefits: Combining studies (meta-analysis): 54 independent samples, 94 effect sizes, N = 36,583, using a three-level random effects model. The mean correlation between online upward social comparison and psychological maladjustment was r = 0.330 (95% CI 0.289–0.370, credible range). Look at the specific results separately. The negative social evaluative emotions of fear of being looked down upon were 0.438, and anxiety was 0.382. Depression 0.306, low happiness 0.268, and low self-esteem 0.263. Age, cultural background, and year of data collection did not affect the strength of this association. The results from long-term follow-up studies are also no stronger than those from surveys at the same time point. There was also a randomized, controlled trial of 2,743 U.S. Facebook users. 61% of them were willing to accept deactivation for less than $102. These people were randomly divided into a four-week discontinuation group and a control group. Deactivation frees up 60 minutes per day for the average subject. The subjective well-being index increased by 0.09 standard deviations. The sub-categories are life satisfaction 0.12, anxiety 0.10, depression 0.09, and happiness 0.08. After deducting the random elements of multiple comparisons, these still count. The author gives a reference, which is a psychological intervention that makes people more positive. This type of intervention affects subjective well-being by about +0.34 standard deviations and depression by about -0.23 standard deviations. So the effect is about 25 to 40 percent of conventional psychological interventions. The price over the same period was a 0.19 standard deviation drop in the current affairs knowledge index and a 0.16 standard deviation drop in political opposition. After the experiment, Facebook use in the deactivated group was still 12 minutes/day lower than the control (0.31 standard deviations, a 23% decrease). There was also a randomized controlled trial with 143 undergraduate students who were randomly divided into two groups. One group limited each platform to Facebook, Instagram, and Snapchat to 10 minutes a day, while the other group used them as usual. After three weeks, loneliness and depression in the time-limited group dropped significantly. Anxiety and FOMO were lower in both groups than at the beginning.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Lei Y, Hu S, Sun Y, Zheng L (2026). "Looking up" linked to feeling down: a meta-analysis of online upward social comparison and psychological maladjustment. Frontiers in Psychology. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1825169>; Allcott H, Braghieri L, Eichmeyer S, Gentzkow M (2020). The Welfare Effects of Social Media. American Economic Review, 110(3), 629–676. <https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20190658>; Allcott H, Braghieri L, Eichmeyer S, Gentzkow M (2019). The Welfare Effects of Social Media. NBER Working Paper No. 25514 (The specific numbers quoted in this article are checked verbatim according to this edition, and the published abstract does not include numbers). <https://www.nber.org/papers/w25514>; Hunt MG, Marx R, Lipson C, Young J (2018). No More FOMO: Limiting Social Media Decreases Loneliness and Depression. Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology, 37(10), 751–768. <https://doi.org/10.1521/jscp.2018.37.10.751>

Note: The "related" half only means that two things occurred together, and cannot be read as who caused whom. The author himself said that more long-term follow-up research is needed. The half of the random group can tell cause and effect, but the subjects were Facebook users before the 2018 U.S. midterm elections, and moving to the Chinese platform was considered a trick. Hunt has only 143 undergraduate students, and that's it. The effect sizes are not large, so don’t expect that turning off the app will solve your emotional problems. What should be blocked is the use of "seeing how other people are doing", which does not include contacting family and friends, checking information, or looking for a job. If you really can't hold it down, start by turning off push notifications, "people you may know" and homepage recommendations. For an account of total screen time, see Section 4, Items 15 and 16 (hard cap on short videos, no scrolling news). What to do first when you feel down, see No. 18 in this section (get moving, get some sunshine, go to bed on time). Regaining a sense of identity by buying things See Section 6, Item 23. To pay more to "move up a notch" see Section 6, Item 24.

Case: Mr. Liu checks Moments and sees his peers showing off their houses and cars, which makes him increasingly anxious. She set her WeChat Moments to be unavailable and limited the time she could use Douyin. After a month, she stopped comparing herself to others and felt more relaxed.

items.title: When you think "everyone has seen me make a fool of myself", divide that estimate by two
items.core: Wear an embarrassing T-shirt into the house, thinking that nearly half of the people will recognize who is printed on the shirt, but in fact, less than a quarter. Changing to a decent t-shirt is just as overrated. After group discussions, people also think that their wrong words will be more conspicuous in the eyes of others. After chatting, they often underestimate how much the other person likes them. So when I think "everyone saw me making a fool of myself", the reality is often half or less.
body: Cost: No money. Just ask yourself one more thing when you are nervous: Did they really see it?

Benefits: Experiment 1: Have participants wear T-shirts with Barry Manilow’s face on them and walk into a room with other participants. On average, wearers estimated that 46% of bystanders could correctly identify who was wearing the clothing. Bystanders were actually correct 23% of the time, and their estimate was exactly twice the actual value. Subtracting the actual values ​​from the estimates on a game-by-game basis, the average overestimation was 23 percentage points (95% CI 9–38, credible range). Excluding the two games with only two and three bystanders, it was 27 percentage points (11–43). Experiment 2: Wearing a T-shirt that the participant selected and considered positive. The average estimate was 48%, and bystanders were actually correct 8% of the time, a six-fold increase. The authors note in a footnote that the estimates of wearers in both experiments were almost identical (48% and 46%), with the difference being only the accuracy of bystanders (8% and 23%). The author suspects that the main reason is that the questionnaire given to bystanders in Experiment 2 is more laborious, and non-decent clothes are more likely to be overestimated. Experiment 3: Undergraduate students were divided into groups of 3 to 7 people, discussed a designated topic for 20 minutes, and then wrote a policy proposal together. Just after the discussion, each person separately estimated how others in the group would rank everyone. The smaller the number, the higher the ranking. In terms of "number of wrong things said", the average estimated ranking was 2.30, and the actual ranking given by others was 2.96, with a difference of −0.66 (p < .01). So people think that what they say wrong will be more conspicuous in the eyes of others. The same goes for "Words that may offend others" (2.35 vs. 2.90, p < .01), and the difference is smaller for "Words that may be criticized by others" (2.61 vs. 2.82, p < .05). Another series of studies had three settings: stranger pair conversations, college freshman roommates, and adult workshops. The result is that people systematically underestimate how much the person they are talking to likes them, and how much they enjoy the conversation. The author calls it "like difference". It's present in conversations of varying lengths, lasting for months between freshman roommates.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Gilovich T, Medvec VH, Savitsky K (2000). The spotlight effect in social judgment: An egocentric bias in estimates of the salience of one's own actions and appearance. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 78(2), 211–222. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.78.2.211>; Boothby EJ, Cooney G, Sandstrom GM, Clark MS (2018). The Liking Gap in Conversations: Do People Like Us More Than We Think? Psychological Science, 29(11), 1742–1756. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797618783714>

Remarks: Reason for setting B: They are all laboratory and campus studies with a small number of people. Scenarios were getting dressed, chatting with strangers or roommates, and student group discussions, asking just after the discussion. Moving to "being discussed by colleagues" and "does anyone still remember the wrong thing I said in a meeting a few days later?", there is no direct evidence. These numbers only indicate the direction and approximate multiple of overestimation, and cannot be used as a set of coefficients. The opinions of others are not unimportant. In situations where you are really being evaluated, such as interviews, defenses, assessments, and physical examination reports, the evaluation is real, so prepare when you need to. What you have to discount is just the daily feeling of "everyone is looking at me". What you have to deal with in that part is your own estimation bias.

Case: Xiao Chen attended a party wearing a T-shirt with a cartoon pattern printed on it. He felt that it was very eye-catching and felt ashamed. Afterwards, he asked his friends and found that almost no one noticed the pattern on the clothes. This confirms that people often overestimate their conspicuousness in the eyes of others.

items.title: See "Others ask me to be perfect" as a symptom instead of a fact
items.core: People who always feel that "people around me ask me to be perfect, and if I can't do it, I will be denied" are more likely to have suicidal thoughts. The relationship between "I demand perfection from myself" and suicidal thoughts is much weaker, only about one-third of the former. Deducting the original thoughts, the former feeling is still related to the increase in the number of thoughts later, but the magnitude is not large.
body: Cost: No money. The difficulty is treating this thought as something to be dealt with rather than as an accurate measurement of what the other person really wants.

Benefits: Combining multiple studies (meta-analysis): 45 studies, N = 11,747, the population was undergraduates, medical students, community adults and psychiatric patients, using a random effects model. Below are the weighted average correlations with suicidal ideation. Perfectionistic worries r = .28 (95% CI .24–.32, credible range; 42 studies, 7,936 people). Perfectionism worries are a collection of socially prescribed perfectionism, concerns about making mistakes, doubts about actions, and gaps between reality and standards. Socially prescribed perfectionism, counted separately, also had r = .28 (.25–.32, 30 studies, 3,640 people). Perfectionism strivings r = .10 (.07–.13, 31 studies, 4,588 people), which is a composite of self-oriented perfectionism and personal standards. Parental criticism r = .20 (.11–.29). Let’s look at the relationship with suicide attempts. Perfectionism worries r = .12 (.07–.17, 15 studies, 5,275 people). Socially prescribed perfectionism r = .19 (.08–.29, 8 studies, 689 people). Let’s look at the part about tracking for a while. After deducting the suicidal thoughts at the beginning, socially prescribed perfectionism still changed in the same direction as the suicidal thoughts at subsequent follow-up, but the amplitude was not large. No correlation was seen between self-directed and other-directed perfectionism.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Smith MM, Sherry SB, Chen S, Saklofske DH, Mushquash C, Flett GL, Hewitt PL (2018). The perniciousness of perfectionism: A meta-analytic review of the perfectionism-suicide relationship. Journal of Personality, 86(3), 522–542. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jopy.12333>

Remarks: Reason for setting B: Most of the included studies are one-time questionnaires, and the order cannot be seen. The correlation strength was moderate (r about .28), explaining roughly only a few to 10% of the variance. What is measured is suicidal thoughts and suicide attempts, not death itself, so the magnitude of the benefit is recorded as "surrogate endpoint only". The authors themselves said that the grouping of perfectionistic worries and suicide attempts was subject to publication bias. Publication bias means that studies with unfavorable results are not published. After filling in the missing research in the estimation, the direction of the conclusion remains unchanged. High standards are not a problem in themselves, nor do they necessarily lead to lower requirements. The difference lies in where the standards come from, and whether you feel like "I'm finished as a person" when you fail to meet them. It’s something that can be treated as a symptom, just like the pessimistic expectations in #15 (treating thoughts like “Things will definitely be worse” as a symptom). If you have suicidal thoughts, call 12356 first. Move the means of death away. See Section 1, Article 25. What you can do when someone around you expresses such thoughts, see Section 8, No. 15. Screening for depression in children is provided in Section 30, Item 8.

Case: Xiao Zhao has high demands from his parents and is always afraid of being rejected for not being perfect, so he often wants to commit suicide. After being guided by a psychiatrist, he realized that this was a misunderstanding. After accepting that I am not perfect, my suicidal thoughts gradually disappear.

items.title: When you are angry, don’t vent your anger by punching a sandbag or running a lap. Let your body slow down first
items.core: Punching a sandbag, riding a bike, or going for a run. These methods of venting to make the body more excited will not relieve your anger as a whole. Methods such as slow breathing, mindfulness, and meditation to calm the body can significantly suppress anger and the urge to take action.
body: Cost: No money. When you are angry, do something to slow down your heartbeat for a few minutes: breathe slowly, sit down, and be quiet. The difficulty was that what I wanted to do most at that time was to vent.

Yield: 154 studies combined (meta-analysis), 184 samples, 10,189 people. Techniques to calm the body, such as deep breathing, mindfulness, and meditation, can reduce anger and aggression. Effect size g = -0.63, 95% CI -0.82 to -0.43 (confidence range). The results were stable across gender, race, age and culture. Methods to make the body more excited, such as playing sandbags, jogging, and cycling, are generally ineffective. Its effect size was g = -0.02, 95% CI -0.13 to 0.09. The author's conclusion is: venting anger and going for a run are not effective ways to relieve anger.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Kjærvik SL, Bushman BJ (2024). A meta-analytic review of anger management activities that increase or decrease arousal: What fuels or douses rage? Clinical Psychology Review. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpr.2024.102414>

Note: Measures anger and aggression, not energy. Caliber is recorded as time, which is the author's classification: one less quarrel means one less time to clean up the mess. For methods that can be used on the spot, see Section 22, Item 8 (cyclic sighing), and Section 17 of this section (Leave the scene first when angry). Running is not useless. In the long term, it works for low moods, see Section 22, No. 6 (Go for a walk or run when you’re in a bad mood). It's just not suitable for on-the-spot relief. Don't drive, don't send messages, don't make decisions when you're angry. If someone is hitting you, leave first and call the police. It’s not your emotions that need to be dealt with at that time, see Section 8, Item 43 (Domestic Violence).

Case: When faced with the complex PPT production task, Xiao Zhao, a newcomer in the workplace, no longer generally estimates the time, but splits the collection of information, typesetting, and beautification into three sub-tasks to estimate separately. In the end, it was not only completed within the deadline, but also avoided delays.

items.title: If you have something pressing in your mind, you can write down your thoughts and feelings for several days, but don’t expect it to cure your illness.
items.core: Writing down bad things will have a little benefit on average, but it is very small. The conclusions of the summary are also inconsistent, and there are two summaries that do not show obvious effects. It costs next to nothing and can be tried. If you have serious emotional problems, don't use them as a substitute for seeing a doctor.
body: Cost: No money. A common practice in research is to write three to four times for 15 to 20 minutes each time. Write about something that makes you uncomfortable. Write about your deepest thoughts and feelings.

Benefits: An analysis pooled 146 studies of randomization (meta-analysis). People in the study wrote or talked about things that were important to them. The average effect was positive and significant, but small, with an effect size of r = .075. Another summary only included randomized controlled trials, and 30 trials combined showed no significant effects on either physical health or mental health. Taken together, 16 randomized trials of cancer patients and survivors found no significant effects on psychological, physical, or quality of life outcomes. where psychological aspect g = 0.04, 95% CI -0.06 to 0.14 (credible range).
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Frattaroli J (2006). Experimental disclosure and its moderators: a meta-analysis. Psychological Bulletin. Psycho-Oncology. The effect of expressive writing intervention on psychological and physical health outcomes in cancer patients--a systematic review and meta-analysis. Psycho-Oncology. <https://doi.org/10.1002/pon.3802>

Note: Controversy. In favor is a pooling of 146 studies that found the effect to be positive but small. The opposing side is a summary of two randomized controlled trials, neither of which found a significant effect. The number of times and how long each time is written in the cost column comes from the earliest experimental design, which was written in Mogk's summary. I included it because it costs almost nothing and doesn't take much time, and can be done by one person. You can use it when you don’t want to talk to anyone and there is no one around you to talk to. What is measured is not energy, the caliber is recorded as time, which is the author's classification. As you write and feel more and more uncomfortable, stop and type 12356 instead. See Section 1, Article 25 (12356).

Case: Xiao Sun was depressed due to high work pressure. She kept a journal for a week, recording her thoughts and feelings. My mood was slightly relieved, but it was not cured. Later, she sought psychological counseling and finally solved the problem.

items.title: Take analgesics like ibuprofen for dysmenorrhea, don’t take it hard; if the pain is so severe that you have to miss work and school, and you can’t take medicine for three months, go to a gynecologist for a checkup
items.core: The number of people who have dysmenorrhea who take ibuprofen and other painkillers has significantly reduced their pain has increased from less than 20% to about half. It is more effective than acetaminophen and has more side effects. If the pain is so severe that you miss work or school, or if the pain persists during intercourse, or if the pain cannot be suppressed after taking medicine for three months, go to the gynecologist to check for endometriosis. In a ten-country study, the average delay from symptom onset to diagnosis was 6.7 years.
body: Cost: A box of ibuprofen costs more than ten yuan. I only take it on the days when I feel pain. If you need to go to the gynecology department, it will cost some money and half a day to register and do a B-ultrasound.

Benefits: A Cochrane systematic review compiled 80 randomized controlled trials involving 5820 women with primary dysmenorrhea. Primary dysmenorrhea refers to dysmenorrhea that cannot be diagnosed with other diseases. NSAIDs were more effective at relieving pain than placebo (OR 4.37, 95% CI 3.76–5.09, confidence range). That translates to 18% of people taking the placebo experiencing moderate or better relief, and 45% to 53% of those taking the drug. The trade-off is more side effects (OR 1.29, 1.11–1.51). 10% of people who took the placebo experienced side effects, and 11% to 14% of those who took the drug. The excess was mainly gastrointestinal discomfort (OR 1.58) and neurological reactions (OR 2.74). They were also more effective at relieving pain than acetaminophen (OR 1.89, 1.05–3.43), although there were only three trials. There is no difference between which type of medicine is best. UK NICE guidance (updated 2024) lists several conditions in which to suspect endometriosis. They are long-term pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea affecting daily activities and quality of life, and deep pain during or after intercourse. There are also painful defecation during menstruation, blood in the urine or painful urination during menstruation, and infertility accompanied by these symptoms. Girls 17 and under also count. The guidelines recommend starting with a trial of acetaminophen or a drug like this for, say, 3 months. If the pain relief is not enough, I will go for further examination. Gynecological examination and B-ultrasound were normal, but this disease could not be ruled out. One study looked at 1,418 women undergoing laparoscopy at 16 hospitals in 10 countries. From the onset of symptoms to the surgical diagnosis of endometriosis, it took an average of 6.7 years, mainly during the period of medical treatment at the grassroots level. Women diagnosed with the disease work an average of 10.8 hours less work per week. Most of them are at work and their efficiency is reduced. A Dutch online survey asked 32,748 women aged 15 to 45. 13.8% took time off due to menstruation, an average of 1.3 days per year. 80.7% of people are at work during menstruation but their efficiency decreases, which is equivalent to 8.9 days less work per year.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Marjoribanks J, Ayeleke RO, Farquhar C, Proctor M (2015). Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for dysmenorrhoea. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (7):CD001751. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001751.pub3>; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2017, updated 2024). Endometriosis: diagnosis and management (NG73), recommendations 1.3.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3, 1.5.4. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng73/chapter/Recommendations>; Nnoaham KE, Hummelshoj L, Webster P, et al.; World Endometriosis Research Foundation Global Study of Women's Health consortium (2011). Impact of endometriosis on quality of life and work productivity: a multicenter study across ten countries. Fertility and Sterility, 96(2):366-373.e8. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fertnstert.2011.05.090>; Schoep ME, Adang EMM, Maas JWM, De Bie B, Aarts JWM, Nieboer TE (2019). Productivity loss due to menstruation-related symptoms: a nationwide cross-sectional survey among 32 748 women. BMJ Open, 9(6):e026186. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2018-026186>; Haleon (2026). Advil (ibuprofen) capsule, liquid filled), OTC drug label: Warnings. DailyMed. <https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=1f01c10a-9434-91a4-2ee4-352315a6b610>

Remarks: 60 People over the age of 18, who have had gastric bleeding, or are taking anticoagulants or hormones, should ask their doctor before taking such drugs. See section 34, item 3 (pain relievers such as ibuprofen) for details. The U.S. instructions for ibuprofen state that it may cause severe allergies, and people who are allergic to aspirin are more likely to have asthma attacks. People with asthma should also ask their doctor before use. If you are pregnant, ask your doctor first. Do not take it by yourself after 20 weeks of pregnancy. See Section 34, Item 5 (After 20 weeks of pregnancy). If you are unable to take this type of medicine, you can use acetaminophen instead. The upper limit for one day is shown in Section 34, Item 1 (Acetaminophen). If you have dysmenorrhea, take medicine only on the days when you have your period. The threshold of Section 34, Article 9 (Don’t take painkillers for more than 15 days a month) covers headaches, and the number of days for menstrual cramps cannot be reached even if you take painkillers. A was chosen because the analgesic effect comes from a large number of randomized trials. The authors rated the quality of evidence for most comparisons as low, mainly because the trial methods were not clearly written, and 59% of the trials were funded by pharmaceutical companies. Setting the income as "medium" is a judgment: the review only measures whether it hurts or not, and does not allow for a few days off. In the Dutch survey, the loss caused by menstruation is equivalent to about 10 days per year, which is divided into hours per week. The endometriosis group had already undergone laparoscopy, which does not mean that most people with dysmenorrhea have this disease. The main beneficiary is yourself.

Case: Xiao Liu, a college student, suffered from severe menstrual cramps for a long time. The pain was significantly relieved after taking ibuprofen. But then she developed non-menstrual pain and went to the doctor to be diagnosed with endometriosis. The doctor reminded her that if taking painkillers for three months didn't work, she needed to get checked out in time.

items.title: Long-term insomnia (more than three nights a week for more than three months) should first undergo cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia. Do not take sleeping pills for a long time as soon as it starts.
items.core: After this treatment, you can fall asleep 19 minutes faster on average and stay awake for 26 minutes less in the middle of the night. The effects slowly fade but are still there after 12 months. Online self-help courses are almost as effective as face-to-face courses. Sleeping pills are less helpful for people over 60 years old. 1 in 6 people who take the medicine will have side effects, and only 1 in 13 people can sleep well.
body: Cost: Going to the hospital’s sleep clinic, psychiatry department or psychology department will cost registration and treatment fees. Online self-help courses are much cheaper. A course of treatment usually lasts 6 to 8 weeks, and a daily sleep diary is required. What you can do first is stimulus control: go to bed when you are sleepy, and get up when you can't fall asleep while lying down. The bed is only used for sleeping and sex. Get up at the same time every day and don't nap during the day. The difficulty lies in sleep restriction: you need to shorten the time you spend in bed in the first few weeks, which will make you feel more sleepy during the day.

Benefits: The National Health Commission’s 2020 diagnosis and treatment specifications write down the key points for diagnosis of insomnia disorders according to international classifications. First, it is difficult to fall asleep, easy to wake up after falling asleep, or wake up early. The second is feeling tired and sleepy during the day, which affects work. Third, these conditions occur at least 3 times a week for at least 3 months. Less than 3 months is called short-term insomnia disorder. Norms designate cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia as first-line treatment. It includes 5 parts: sleep restriction, stimulus control, cognitive therapy, relaxation training and sleep hygiene, usually in a cycle of 6 to 8 weeks. Standards say it has the same short-term effect as taking medicine, but is better than taking medicine in the long term. The regulations also state that sleeping pills should generally not be taken continuously for more than 4 weeks. If you continue to take sleeping pills, you will be evaluated once a month. The American College of Physicians’ 2016 guidelines strongly recommend that adults with chronic insomnia should undergo this treatment first. If it doesn't work on its own, discuss with your doctor whether to add medication in the short term. One analysis combined 20 randomized controlled trials with 1162 people (meta-analysis). After treatment, the time to fall asleep was reduced by 19.03 minutes (95% CI 14.12–23.93, confidence range). The time spent awake after falling asleep was 26.00 minutes less (15.48–36.52). The proportion of people who actually fell asleep (sleep efficiency) was 9.91% higher when lying in bed (8.09%–11.73%). Total sleep time was only 7.61 minutes longer, which was not statistically significant (−0.51 to 15.74). None of the studies reported adverse outcomes. Another analysis compiled 30 randomized controlled trials to see how long the effects lasted. Improvements in insomnia severity decreased over time compared with those who did not receive treatment. g = 0.64 at 3 months, 0.40 at 6 months, and 0.25 at 12 months. The effect gradually became weaker, but the authors believe it will still be clinically significant within a year. One analysis, done online, combined 11 randomized controlled trials with 1,460 people. Improvements were seen across sleep measures, with effect sizes g ranging from 0.21 to 1.09. The authors say this is as effective as in-person treatment, and the longer the treatment and the more people following up, the greater the effect. In another online randomized trial of 1,711 people, the control group only received sleep hygiene information. For people who undergo digital therapy, their sleep-related quality of life is greatly improved, and their physical condition and mental state during the day are slightly improved.
