Let’s look at sleeping pills. One analysis pooled 24 randomized controlled trials involving 2,417 people over 60 years old with insomnia. Each trial lasted at least 5 consecutive nights. Compared with placebo, those who took the drug slept 25.2 minutes longer and woke up 0.63 fewer times during the night. For every 13 people who take the medicine, 1 person's sleep quality improves. One out of every six people taking medication will experience side effects (NNH 6, 4.7 to 7.1). Side effects on memory and thinking were more common than those taking placebo, with an odds ratio of 4.78 (OR 4.78, 1.47–15.47). There was also more daytime fatigue, odds ratio 3.82 (OR 3.82, 1.88–7.80).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: General Office of the National Health Commission (2020). Notice on the issuance of the Standards for Diagnosis and Treatment of Mental Disorders (2020 Edition) (National Health Commission Medical Letter [2020] No. 945), Appendix Chapter 12, Section 2 "Insomnia Disorder". Qaseem A, Kansagara D, Forciea MA, Cooke M, Denberg TD; Clinical Guidelines Committee of the American College of Physicians (2016). Management of Chronic Insomnia Disorder in Adults: A Clinical Practice Guideline From the American College of Physicians. Annals of Internal Medicine, 165(2):125-133. <https://doi.org/10.7326/M15-2175>; Trauer JM, Qian MY, Doyle JS, Rajaratnam SM, Cunnington D (2015). Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Chronic Insomnia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Annals of Internal Medicine, 163(3):191-204. <https://doi.org/10.7326/M14-2841>; van der Zweerde T, Bisdounis L, Kyle SD, Lancee J, van Straten A (2019). Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia: A meta-analysis of long-term effects in controlled studies. Sleep Medicine Reviews, 48:101208. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.smrv.2019.08.002>; Zachariae R, Lyby MS, Ritterband LM, O'Toole MS (2016). Efficacy of internet-delivered cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia - A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Sleep Medicine Reviews, 30:1-10. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.smrv.2015.10.004>; Espie CA, Emsley R, Kyle SD, et al (2019). Effect of Digital Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia on Health, Psychological Well-being, and Sleep-Related Quality of Life: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA Psychiatry, 76(1):21-30. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2018.2745>; Glass J, Lanctôt KL, Herrmann N, Sproule BA, Busto UE (2005). Sedative hypnotics in older people with insomnia: meta-analysis of risks and benefits. BMJ, 331(7526):1169. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.38623.768588.47>; Edinger JD, Arnedt JT, Bertisch SM, et al (2021). Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline. Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 17(2):255-262. <https://doi.org/10.5664/jcsm.8986>

Note: The five stimulus control items in the cost column are taken from the 2021 guidelines of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine. Sleep restriction is to first reduce the time you spend in bed to the length of time you actually fall asleep, and then slowly add it back according to your sleep efficiency. The guide says it will make you more sleepy during the day, and people who drive or operate machines should use it with caution. People with manic tendencies, uncontrolled epilepsy, and people who are particularly sleepy during the day should also use it with caution. It is best to follow up with a doctor. It only talks about sleep common sense such as work, rest, diet, and environment. It is not effective when used alone, and the guideline does not recommend it. A few nights without sleep is not considered an insomnia disorder. At this time, fix the wake-up time first, see Article 2 of this section (fixed wake-up time). Look at number 4 (no caffeine after 2 p.m.) and number 8 (no glowing screens an hour before bed). For those who snore, hold their breath while sleeping, or feel extremely sleepy during the day, the regulations require that sleep apnea be ruled out first. How to check Item 27 of this section (sleep apnea). If you feel depressed and can’t sleep well, see No. 18 in this section (a few things to do first when you feel depressed). Sleeping pills are prescription drugs, and that analysis only looked at people over 60 who were taking them for a short period of time. Targeted income: The time to fall asleep quickly and the time to wake up less in the middle of the night add up to about 45 minutes every night, which is hourly in a week. Total sleep duration remained almost unchanged. The 20-trial article excluded insomniacs who also had other medical conditions. Which department to go to in China depends on the author’s experience (level C). Each hospital is different. Please ask if this treatment is available before registering. The main beneficiary is yourself. Don’t expect to rely on melatonin to cure long-term insomnia. See Section 6, Item 34 (Relying on melatonin to cure long-term insomnia).

Case: Lao Zhou suffered from insomnia for half a year and relied on sleeping pills to fall asleep, but the effect gradually deteriorated. He attended cognitive behavioral therapy classes for insomnia and learned sleep hygiene and relaxation techniques. Three months later, I fell asleep faster and stopped taking sleeping pills.

items.title: Snoring loudly, someone sees you holding your breath while sleeping, and you are so sleepy during the day that you feel sleepy while driving. Go to the hospital for sleep monitoring to check for sleep apnea. If it is moderate to severe, wear a ventilator at night
items.core: Sleep apnea is when breathing stops or becomes shallower after falling asleep. People will wake up and feel sleepy during the day. After wearing the ventilator, my sleepiness during the day was significantly reduced, and my driving accidents were reduced by about 70%. But experiments have not shown that it can prevent heart disease or prevent people from dying. They wear it to stay awake during the day.
body: Cost: Go to the hospital’s sleep clinic, respiratory department or otolaryngology department first. Once the diagnosis is confirmed, you need to have one night of sleep monitoring, sleep in the hospital, or borrow the device at home and wear it to sleep. If you need to wear a ventilator, you usually have to buy the machine yourself, which costs a lot of money. The difficulty is persistence: I have to wear a mask to sleep every night. In the first few weeks, I don’t get used to it. Many people wear it for a few hours and then take it off.

Benefits: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine’s 2017 diagnostic guidelines address who is more likely to have moderate to severe sleep disorders. Extremely sleepy during the day most days, plus at least two of the following three. First, you often snore loudly, second, someone sees you stop breathing, gasping for breath, or wake up with a choke while sleeping, and third, you have been diagnosed with high blood pressure. The guidelines require sleep monitoring to be used for diagnosis, not questionnaires alone. If your breathing stops or becomes shallow more than 5 times per hour and you have symptoms, you are considered to have this disease. 15 or more times counts regardless of symptoms. A 2019 systematic review from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine compiled 38 randomized controlled trials. Self-rated sleepiness scores decreased by 2.4 points (95% CI 1.9–2.8, confidence range) in those on ventilators compared with no treatment. This score is called the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, with a maximum score of 24, with the higher the score, the sleepier you are. Counting only people who were not sleepy in the first place, 5 tests dropped by 1.0 points, which the authors considered to be of no clinical significance. The same review included 10 studies comparing before and after treatment. Compared with before treatment, the relative risk of car accidents after wearing a ventilator was 0.3 (RR 0.3, 0.2–0.4), which was about 70% less. Another analysis in 2010 combined nine similar studies and found a RR of 0.278 (0.22–0.35). It also says that daytime sleepiness is significantly reduced after just one night of wearing it, and simulated driving performance improves within 2 to 7 days. A 2009 analysis by the same group of authors showed that the risk of a car accident among untreated patients was roughly 1.21 to 4.89 times higher than that of others. Let’s look at the heart and life span. The SAVE trial looked at 2,717 moderately to severely ill patients aged 45 to 75, all with coronary heart disease or stroke. Follow-up lasted an average of 3.7 years after randomization. Among those who suffered cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, 17.0% were on ventilators and 15.4% were not on ventilators. There was no difference between the two groups (HR 1.10, 0.91–1.32). Those who wore them only wore them for an average of 3.3 hours a night. Their snoring, daytime sleepiness, quality of life, and mood improved. A 2017 analysis combined 10 randomized trials with 7266 people. There was also no difference in overall mortality (RR 1.13, 0.99–1.29). An estimate in 2019 said that about 176 million people aged 30 to 69 in China have this disease, accounting for 23.6%. Among them, there are about 65.52 million, accounting for 8.8%, moderate to severe cases, the largest number in the world.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Kapur VK, Auckley DH, Chowdhuri S, et al (2017). Clinical Practice Guideline for Diagnostic Testing for Adult Obstructive Sleep Apnea: An American Academy of Sleep Medicine Clinical Practice Guideline. Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 13(3):479-504. <https://doi.org/10.5664/jcsm.6506>; Patil SP, Ayappa IA, Caples SM, Kimoff RJ, Patel SR, Harrod CG (2019). Treatment of Adult Obstructive Sleep Apnea With Positive Airway Pressure: An American Academy of Sleep Medicine Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and GRADE Assessment. Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 15(2):301-334. <https://doi.org/10.5664/jcsm.7638>; Tregear S, Reston J, Schoelles K, Phillips B (2010). Continuous positive airway pressure reduces risk of motor vehicle crash among drivers with obstructive sleep apnea: systematic review and meta-analysis. Sleep, 33(10):1373-1380. <https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/33.10.1373>; Tregear S, Reston J, Schoelles K, Phillips B (2009). Obstructive sleep apnea and risk of motor vehicle crash: systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 5(6):573-581. <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20465027/>; McEvoy RD, Antic NA, Heeley E, et al (2016). CPAP for Prevention of Cardiovascular Events in Obstructive Sleep Events Apnea. New England Journal of Medicine, 375(10):919-931. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1606599>; Yu J, Zhou Z, McEvoy RD, et al (2017). Association of Positive Airway Pressure With Cardiovascular Events and Death in Adults With Sleep Apnea: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. JAMA, 318(2):156-166. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2017.7967>; Benjafield AV, Ayas NT, Eastwood PR, et al (2019). Estimation of the global prevalence and burden of obstructive sleep apnoea: a literature-based analysis. The Lancet Respiratory Medicine, 7(8):687-698. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-2600(19)30198-5>; US Preventive Services Task Force (2022). Screening for Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Adults: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement. JAMA, 328(19):1945-1950. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.20304>

Note: Controversy. Randomized trials have not shown whether ventilators can prevent heart disease and allow people to live longer. Most of the people in SAVE are not very sleepy and wear less. But the 2017 analysis did not see any difference when the wear was separated by length of time. The numbers in the car accident are from the comparison before and after treatment, not random grouping. The people in the study may have been more careful after treatment. The number in China was only extrapolated from a 2005 study of 3,648 people, an estimate funded by ventilator manufacturers. The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force said in 2022 that screening people without symptoms would have both advantages and disadvantages. Therefore, people who do not snore and are not sleepy during the day do not need to check specifically. The profit determination is a judgment: the sleepiness score dropped by 2.4 points, which did not measure the number of hours more awake every day. Which department to choose is based on the author’s experience (level C) and varies from hospital to hospital. If you feel sleepy while driving, stop the car first. See Section 1, Article 9 (Stop and take a rest if you feel sleepy). If you need to take a long nap during the day, see Section 2, Item 37 (check the reason if you take a nap for more than one hour). For long-term insomnia, see Article 26 of this section (Chronic Insomnia). The main beneficiary is yourself, but others in the car and on the road will also benefit.

Case: Lao Zhang snores loudly and often feels sleepy while driving during the day. I went to the hospital for sleep monitoring and was diagnosed with moderate to severe sleep apnea. After wearing a ventilator at night, I feel better during the day and no longer doze off while driving.

items.title: Write “plan to do” into “What time, where, and do whatever comes up”
items.core: Rewrite “I want to do this” into “Sit down at the desk at 8 a.m. on Tuesday and write the introduction first.” Taking the 94 tests together, people who write like this have a significantly higher proportion of achieving their goals, which is a medium to large effect. All that is changed is the way a sentence is written, which costs no money or effort.
body: Cost: No money. Spend 1 to 2 minutes on each item and write an "if... then..." sentence. For example, “Sit down at your desk at 8 a.m. on Tuesday and write the introduction first.”

Benefits: Taking the 94 independent tests together, people who first write down their plans as "if...then..." have a higher goal achievement rate. This way of writing is called implementation intention in psychology. The effect size, d = 0.65, is considered medium to large. There are three steps that work: start taking action, endure when interrupted, and withdraw from things that are destined to fail.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Gollwitzer, P. M., & Sheeran, P. (2006). Implementation intentions and goal achievement: A meta-analysis of effects and processes. Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 38, 69–119. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2601(06)38002-1>

Note: This trick only works for things you really want to do. If you don’t want the goal itself, it’s useless no matter how many sentences you write. In addition, these studies mostly looked at students and looked at health habits, so they may not necessarily be equally effective in the workplace.

Case: Graduate student Xiao Li concretized his plan of "preparing a thesis" into "writing two paragraphs of literature review in the library at 7 o'clock every night." This clear time, place and execution plan enabled him to complete the writing more smoothly than other students who only had vague plans.

items.title: Write down the exit conditions before starting work
items.core: Write down a sentence before starting work: stop if a certain target is not reached by a certain day of the month. According to multiple studies, this way of writing can indeed help people avoid things they are destined to fail. What you save is all the time you would have spent digging in.
body: Cost: No money. When you start working, take 5 minutes to write down "It will stop if a certain target is not reached on a certain day of the month." The difficulty is that you have to admit your fault when the day comes, and it would be a bit embarrassing to stop in front of others.

Benefits: Combining multiple studies on implementation intentions, predetermined "if... then..." can also help people withdraw from things that are destined to fail. The original statement is disengagement from failing courses of action. The time you save is the time you would have invested in it.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Gollwitzer, P. M., & Sheeran, P. (2006). Implementation intentions and goal achievement: A meta-analysis of effects and processes. Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 38, 69–119. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2601(06)38002-1>

Note: Exit conditions should be set when work has just started and the mood is still calm. Later, it will definitely be biased by the cost that has been invested. When judging, only look at future investment and future returns, see Article 3. In addition, "willingness to withdraw" is only a sub-conclusion in a summary of multiple studies, and no one has individually calculated how much time it can save.

Case: Xiao Wu planned to open a milk tea shop, and wrote down the exit conditions before starting the project: if the daily turnover is less than 500 yuan within three months, the shop will be closed. After failing to meet the target after three months, he decisively closed the store to avoid greater losses.

items.title: When deciding whether to continue, only look at future investment and future returns, not how much has been invested
items.core: The money and time already invested will make people want to continue doing it. Taking 98 sets of data together, this tendency exists stably. Therefore, when deciding whether to continue, you only need to consider how much you have to invest in the future and how much you can get back. Don’t count what you’ve already spent.
body: Cost: No money. The hard thing is to accept one thing: the time you invested in it is gone and you can’t get it back.

Benefits: The money, energy and time invested will make people want to continue doing it. This is called the sunk cost effect in psychology. Taking 98 sets of data together, the analysis confirmed that this tendency exists stably. If you avoid this tendency, you won’t continue to invest time just because you don’t want to waste it.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Arkes, H. R., & Blumer, C. (1985). The psychology of sunk cost. Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 35, 124–140. <https://doi.org/10.1016/0749-5978(85)90049-4>; Roth, S., Robbert, T., & Straus, L. (2015). On the sunk-cost effect in economic decision-making: A meta-analytic review. Business Research, 8(1), 99–138. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40685-014-0014-8>

Note: This is what Arkes and Blumer did in their theater experiment. The Ohio University Theater sells season tickets at random prices: $15 off the original price, $2 off, or $7 off. In the first half of the season, the original price group watched an average of 4.11 games, while the other two groups watched an average of 3.32 and 3.29 games. There is no obvious difference between the three groups in the second half of the season. Roth et al found that this effect faded over time, with older people being less affected.

Case: Xiao Zheng spent 20,000 yuan to sign up for the examination class, but found out halfway through that he was not suitable. He no longer thinks about the money he has spent, but only looks at the future: he still needs to invest half a year, and the passing rate is extremely low. So he gave up decisively and turned to learning skills.

items.title: The construction period is estimated based on the actual time consumption of similar tasks in the past and is not based on the plan.
items.core: Students estimated that they would finish writing their thesis in 33.9 days, but it actually took them 55.5 days. Only 29.7% of them completed it in the time they estimated. Another group was asked to think about how long it took to do something similar last time before estimating the time. The proportion of on-time completion increased from 29.3% to 60.0%.
body: Cost: Nothing. Before estimating, take a few minutes to look up how long you actually did the last time you did something similar.

Benefit: The student expected to complete the thesis in 33.9 days, but actually took 55.5 days. Only 29.7% finished on time according to their estimate. The researchers asked another group of people to first link their past experience to the current event before evaluating it. The proportion of this group that completed on time increased from 29.3% in the control group to 60.0%. The optimism of underestimating the construction period no longer appears in this group.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Buehler, R., Griffin, D., & Ross, M. (1994). Exploring the "planning fallacy": Why people underestimate their task completion times. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 67(3), 366–381. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.67.3.366>; Flyvbjerg, B. (2006). From Nobel Prize to project management: Getting risks right. Project Management Journal, 37(3), 5–15. <https://doi.org/10.1177/875697280603700302>; Halkjelsvik, T., & Jørgensen, M. (2012). From origami to software development: A review of studies on judgment-based predictions of performance time. Psychological Bulletin, 138(2), 238–271. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0025996>

Note: Buehler's study only looked at Canadian college students. It was a single study with a small number of people, 37 people and about 40 people in each group. Estimating based on historical data of similar projects is called reference prediction. For details on how to do this in engineering, see Flyvbjerg. Halkjelsvik compiled multiple studies and showed that underestimating is more common than overestimating, but the amount varies greatly with the task and research method.

Case: Xiao Qian estimated that he could finish writing the report in one week, but it took two weeks. Next time, he would first recall that it took two weeks last time, then estimate two weeks and prepare in advance. Finally finished on time, avoiding mistakes made in a hurry.

items.title: Distribute the agenda before the meeting. If there is no agenda, the meeting will not be held. If you can stand up, do it standing up.
items.core: Participants are more likely to find this useful if the agenda is distributed before the meeting. In the experiment, driving while seated took 34% longer than driving while standing, and there was no difference in the quality of decisions made between the two driving methods.
body: Cost: Nothing. Organizers spend 5 to 10 minutes before the meeting writing an agenda. Standing meetings require the cooperation of participants.

Yield: 958 and 292 participants in the two surveys, respectively. The result is: for meetings where the agenda is distributed before the meeting, participants are more likely to think that this will be effective, and this relationship is statistically tenable. In another experiment, 55 groups sat for a meeting and 56 groups stood for a meeting, and the sitting time was 34% longer. There is no difference in the quality of the decisions made by the two methods.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Leach, D. J., Rogelberg, S. G., Warr, P. B., & Burnfield, J. L. (2009). Perceived meeting effectiveness: The role of design characteristics. Journal of Business and Psychology, 24(1), 65–76. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10869-009-9092-6>; Bluedorn, A. C., Turban, D. B., & Love, M. S. (1999). The effects of stand-up and sit-down meeting formats on meeting outcomes. Journal of Applied Psychology, 84(2). <https://doi.org/10.1037/0021-9010.84.2.277>

Note: The stand-up experiment was a task for a group of 5 people in the laboratory. Long meetings and large meetings cannot copy this conclusion. Leach measures how effective participants feel they are, not how much work was actually done.

Case: Manager Li of the project team changed the weekly meeting to issue the agenda in advance and hold it standing up. The originally scheduled one-hour discussion ended in half an hour. The quality of decision-making was not affected. Everyone felt that the meeting was more efficient.

items.title: Reduce the number of meetings and eliminate meetings that can be resolved asynchronously using text.
items.core: The more meetings there are on that day, the more tired people will be, and the more work they will feel like they have on their hands. If you cut off a meeting, the time saved is the length of the meeting itself, without any discount.
body: Cost: Nothing. Colleagues and superiors are required to cooperate. The difficulty is that writing a paragraph clearly takes more energy than opening your mouth to say a sentence.

Earnings: Two surveys looked for employees who worked more than 35 hours a week, 676 and 304 respectively. The impact of how much time meetings take up on work attitude and happiness is not fixed. It depends on two things: whether the meeting is well held and how dependent the job is on others. Another study asked people to keep diaries for a week and found that the more meetings they had during the day, the higher their fatigue and perceived workload. The time saved is equal to the meeting time itself that you cut off.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Rogelberg, S. G., Leach, D. J., Warr, P. B., & Burnfield, J. L. (2006). "Not another meeting!" Are meeting time demands related to employee well-being? Journal of Applied Psychology, 91(1). <https://doi.org/10.1037/0021-9010.91.1.83>; Luong, A., & Rogelberg, S. G. (2005). Meetings and more meetings: The relationship between meeting load and the daily well-being of employees. Group Dynamics: Theory, Research, and Practice, 9(1). <https://doi.org/10.1037/1089-2699.9.1.58>

Note: Controversy: Rogelberg 2006 found that the relationship between meeting frequency and happiness was not one-sided. In a position that is highly dependent on others at work, having too many meetings is not a bad thing. In addition, there is no research that directly compares "switching to text-based asynchronous communication" with meetings. This is the author's own inference.

Case: Xiao Zhang canceled the weekly product synchronization meeting and instead used documents to collect progress and opinions. The original two-hour meeting was saved, and the team had more time to deal with core tasks, and the fatigue was significantly reduced.

items.title: Divide big tasks into subtasks, estimate time, and start work again
items.core: When people estimate the construction period, they will not automatically break the tasks into pieces and calculate them piece by piece. If you list the subtasks first and then estimate them, you will be able to underestimate them. After taking it apart, every small step can be done immediately, so it is not so easy to delay.
body: Cost: Nothing. The split itself takes 5 to 15 minutes.

Benefits: When people estimate the duration, they don't break a multi-headed task into several pieces. For example, writing a literature review, writing a discussion, and sorting out references are just a few things. Listing the subtasks first and then estimating them will avoid the mistake of estimating the construction period too short. This mistake is called the planning fallacy. After taking it apart, every small step becomes an action that can be started immediately, and procrastination is reduced. The factors that were the strongest predictors of procrastination in the study included feelings of disgust about the task and being pushed back to the task itself.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Kruger, J., & Evans, M. (2004). If you don't want to be late, enumerate: Unpacking reduces the planning fallacy. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, 40(5), 586–598. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jesp.2003.11.001>; Steel, P. (2007). The nature of procrastination: A meta-analytic and theoretical review of quintessential self-regulatory failure. Psychological Bulletin, 133(1). <https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.133.1.65>

Note: To what extent is appropriate: "Each sub-task can be completed in one sitting" shall prevail. If it is too detailed, it will also take time. In addition, Kruger and Evans only verified the direction from the abstract, and the specific percentage was not verified to the original text.

Case: Break down "writing a report" into "making an outline, finding three pieces of information, and writing the first paragraph." Start by estimating the time required for each paragraph. A task that was originally delayed for a week has a first draft on the same day.

items.title: Set a date for things that have no external deadlines
items.core: When there is a deadline set by others, 80.6% of students can finish it before that date. Only 38.7% were completed within the time expected. When it is finished, it almost follows the deadline set by others and has little to do with my own estimation. If there is no deadline, you can follow this method to set one yourself and accept it.
body: Cost: No money. The difficulty lies in recognizing it once it has been decided, and not taking it seriously when the day comes means that it is not decided yet.

Benefits: 80.6% of students with external deadlines completed by deadline. Only 38.7% were completed within the expected time. When it is done, it almost follows the deadline. The correlation coefficient is r = 0.82. The closer this number is to 1, the closer it is. There is only a weak relationship with one's own expectations.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Buehler, R., Griffin, D., & Ross, M. (1994). Exploring the "planning fallacy": Why people underestimate their task completion times. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 67(3), 366–381. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.67.3.366>; Ariely, D., & Wertenbroch, K. (2002). Procrastination, deadlines, and performance: Self-control by precommitment. Psychological Science, 13(3), 219–224. <https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9280.00441> (Retracted 2026, Retraction Statement: Self-Control by Precommitment. Psychological Science. <https://doi.org/10.1177/09567976261488042>); Hyndman, K., & Bisin, A. (2026). Replication of "Procrastination, Deadlines, and Performance: Self-Control by Precommitment". Psychological Science: "changes in the deadlines had a negligible effect on the three performance metrics and several survey metrics used in the original study". <https://doi.org/10.1177/09567976261460772>

Note: Tell others the date you set, and it will be closer to the one set by others. What research proves is that deadlines set by others work. The ones you set for yourself, such as time boxes and Pomodoros, are recommended here. There is an experiment that directly measured self-set deadlines, the one by Ariely and Wertenbroch in 2002. It was retracted by the journal in 2026. In repeated experiments in the same year, no matter how the deadline was set, it had little impact on performance.

Case: A freelance writer wrote a book proposal without a deadline from the publishing house, so he took half a year to write only three pages. Later, I decided to send it to my wife for review every Sunday night, treating this day as the delivery day. The entire text would be completed six weeks later, and I would still follow the date I accepted the payment.

items.title: Treat procrastination as avoiding discomfort, not as not working hard enough
items.core: How uncomfortable this thing is, whether you feel that you have accomplished it, whether you can easily be taken away by what is in front of you, and whether you have strong self-control are the most closely related to procrastination. Personalities such as neuroticism and excitement-seeking are only weakly related to procrastination. Therefore, you can first change the task to be less uncomfortable and make the first step smaller. Don't just scold yourself and then force yourself to do it.
body: Cost: No money. What has changed is the direction of judgment: first ask what makes you uncomfortable about this matter, and then think of a solution.

Benefits: A meta-analysis that summarized 691 correlation coefficients found that there are several things that have a strong and stable relationship with procrastination: the degree to which the task is disgusting, how far away from the deadline, self-efficacy (feeling that you can do it), impulsivity, and conscientiousness and its underlying self-control, easily distracted, organized, and achievement motivation. Neuroticism, rebellion, thrill-seeking, and procrastination were only weakly related. The authors use temporal motivation theory to explain this set of results: the attractiveness of a thing now quickly decreases as the reward becomes further away.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Steel P (2007). The nature of procrastination: a meta-analytic and theoretical review of quintessential self-regulatory failure. Psychological Bulletin, 133(1), 65–94. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.133.1.65>

Note: The benefit magnitude is recorded as "medium" because these studies only point out the direction and do not measure how many hours can be saved. The specific actions are in Article 1 of this section (written as "What time, where, and whatever happens when you encounter it"), Article 7 (break large tasks into subtasks), and Article 8 (set a date for things that have no external deadlines). These are a summary of related studies, and it is not clear who caused whom.

Case: Faced with a report that had been delayed for a long time, Xiao Chen no longer blamed himself, but opened the document first and only wrote the title. This action made her feel that the task was not that difficult, and she successfully completed the first part ten minutes later.

items.title: Put the things you need close at hand, and move things you don’t want to touch away from you. Don’t expect to hold back on the spot
items.core: The farther away things are, the less people will take them. When the same snack is placed further away, the amount eaten is significantly reduced, which is a medium-sized effect. If there are fewer options, fewer people will take them. This method does not require you to endure on the spot, it can be arranged in a few minutes.
body: Cost: No money, just a few minutes at a time. Put your phone in another room and spread out your books and computer on the table.

Benefit: A Cochrane review of 24 randomized trials. Placing food further away reduced the amount eaten, with a standardized mean difference of −0.60 (95% CI −0.84 to −0.36, confidence range; 12 studies, 1098 people, low-certainty evidence), a medium effect. Reducing the number of options reduced the choice of that food more significantly, with a standardized mean difference of −1.13 (95% CI −1.90 to −0.37, 3 studies, 154 people, low-certainty evidence). Regression analysis shows that the further you look and the simpler the options, the stronger the effect.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Hollands GJ, Carter P, Anwer S, et al. (2019). Altering the availability or proximity of food, alcohol, and tobacco products to change their selection and consumption. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 9, CD012573. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012573.pub3>

Reasons for this level: All 24 studies included in this review were on food, and none on alcohol or tobacco; 14 were done in laboratories, all from high-income countries. Therefore, "move away and touch less" is a logical extension to mobile phones and games, and there is no direct experiment. Putting your phone out of sight has been directly tested by someone, see Section 3, Item 1 (Turn off non-essential notifications, and keep your phone out of sight while working).

Case: Xiao Wang put the snacks in the TV cabinet into the kitchen high cabinet, leaving only fruits on the coffee table. He walked a few more steps when he wanted to eat potato chips and gave up when he was too lazy to get up. Over the course of a week, his snack intake was reduced by half.

items.title: If you want to do it, bet money on it, but ask yourself first if you are willing to bet
items.core: If you want to force yourself to do it, you can get the bonus when you do it, or you can pay the deposit first and then return it and then get the bonus. Among those who were willing to participate in both, those who paid a deposit were 13 percentage points more likely to do so. But only 13.7% are willing to pay a deposit, and 90% are willing to receive a bonus, so the deposit is only useful to those who are willing to make a deposit.
body: Cost: For a deposit-type plan, you must first spend some of your own money, and if you fail to do so, it will be confiscated. The bet in the experiment was $150.

Benefits: A randomized trial of 2,538 people in the United States randomly assigned employees and their relatives and friends to four incentive programs or usual care. The acceptance rate for the bonus model (approximately $800 for making it) is 90.0%, and for the deposit model (pay $150 first, plus a $650 bonus), the acceptance rate is 13.7%. Six-month sustained abstinence rates: ranged from 9.4% to 16.0% for the four incentive programs and 6.0% for usual care. Bonus type 15.7%, deposit type 10.2%. But among the 13.7% of people who are "willing to participate in both", the six-month quit rate of the deposit type is 13.2 percentage points higher than the incentive type (95% CI 3.1 to 22.8, which is the credible range).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Halpern SD, French B, Small DS, et al. (2015). Randomized trial of four financial-incentive programs for smoking cessation. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(22), 2108–2117. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1414293>

Note: This experiment measures smoking cessation, and it is a logical extension to things like writing papers and fitness, so the benefit magnitude is recorded as "medium". When choosing a solution, first see whether you will actually use it, rather than which one is more effective. A method that most people are unwilling to accept, no matter how effective it is, will be of no use to these people. So choose the one you are willing to accept first. A smaller bet is better than no bet at all. How to quit smoking itself, see Section 2, Item 3 (Smoking Smoking Drugs).

Case: Xiao Lin paid a 200 yuan deposit on the fitness app and agreed to check in three times a week to get a full refund and an additional 50 yuan bonus. His completion rate for the month was 90%; when only bonuses were previously provided, he only completed 60%.

items.title: New habits are calculated by months, not by "21 days"
items.core: There is no basis for "21 days to form a habit". A study that followed people for 12 weeks found that it took 18 days for a person to do an action without thinking about it, and 254 days for a person to do it slowly. It's normal for it not to feel better after two or three weeks. If you miss a day in the middle, the progress will not be cleared.
body: Cost: No money. What is required is to repeat the same action in the same scenario every day for several months.

Benefits: 96 volunteers each picked an action related to eating, drinking or activities, and did it every day in a fixed scene (such as "after breakfast") for 12 weeks, and rated their automation level every day. The data of 82 people was enough for analysis, and the model was successfully fitted on 62 people. The number of days required to reach 95% of the respective automation cap, ranging from 18 to 254 days. The study also found that missing an opportunity to perform has no substantial impact on the habit formation process.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Lally P, van Jaarsveld CHM, Potts HWW, Wardle J (2010). How are habits formed: Modeling habit formation in the real world. European Journal of Social Psychology, 40(6), 998–1009. <https://doi.org/10.1002/ejsp.674>

Note: Only this study, 96 People do simple actions (such as eating a piece of fruit after a meal). No one has measured how long it takes to do complex tasks, such as running three times a week and writing every day. So if you are still struggling after two weeks, it should not be taken as evidence of failure. To make repetition really happen, tie the action to a fixed scene, see item 1 of this section (written as "what time, where, and whatever happens").

Case: Lao Zhou wanted to develop the habit of morning jogging. He gritted his teeth every day for the first 21 days. He even missed one on the 22nd day and almost gave up. I found some research and said it might take a few months, so I continued running slowly. It wasn’t until the 85th day that I felt uncomfortable not running. I missed that day and didn’t reset my progress.

items.title: If procrastination has affected your life, use self-help materials supported by randomized trials instead of having to see a therapist
items.core: Procrastination that is severe enough to be painful can be improved. After practicing according to the cognitive behavioral self-help materials for ten weeks, both doing it with someone and doing it completely by yourself are obviously better than doing nothing at all. There is no difference between someone taking care of it and no one taking care of it, so it will be effective if you follow the instructions yourself.
body: Cost: A self-help book costs tens of dollars, some are free. It takes about ten weeks to devote, reading one section and doing one exercise each week.

Income: 150 people were randomly divided into three groups: self-help with therapist guidance, self-help without guidance, and waiting list control. Ten weeks later, between-group effect sizes on the pure procrastination scale were d = 0.70 (95% CI 0.29–1.10, which is the confidence range) for the guided group and d = 0.50 (0.10–0.90) for the no-guidance group; on the irrational procrastination scale they were 0.81 (0.40–1.22) and 0.69 (0.29–1.09), respectively. The proportion achieving clinically meaningful improvement was 31.3% to 40.0% in the guided group and 24.0% to 36.0% in the unguided group. There were no significant differences between the two groups on any of the outcomes.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Rozental A, Forsell E, Svensson A, Andersson G, Carlbring P (2015). Internet-based cognitive-behavior therapy for procrastination: A randomized controlled trial. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 83(4), 808–824. <https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000023>

Remarks: The subjects are Swedish adults, and the materials used are Swedish. The same set is not readily available in Chinese, so the benefit magnitude is recorded as "medium". The ingredients in the material are the usual ones: behavioral activation, behavioral experiments, stimulus control, explanations of motivation and work methods. Stimulus control is the same as in No. 10 of this section (move away what you don’t want to touch). If procrastination is accompanied by obvious depression or anxiety, first follow Section 3, Item 18 (get moving, bask in the sun, go to bed on time, talk to someone, call 12356).

Case: Xiao Wu, a college student, was troubled by procrastination. He spent 20 minutes practicing according to the "Procrastination Self-Help Manual" every day. After ten weeks, he no longer stayed up late to hand in homework, his anxiety was significantly relieved, and he did not seek help from a psychological counselor.

items.title: Use your hourly wage to decide which chores to outsource
items.core: The Chinese spend an average of 1 hour and 17 minutes doing housework every day. The hands-on part of the day took 1 hour and 59 minutes. People who spend money to buy time have higher life satisfaction. The same amount of money spent on buying time makes people happier now than buying things.
body: Cost: It costs a sum of money to outsource. The amount depends on the service you buy. In addition, you should take the time to calculate your hourly wage clearly.

Income: Chinese residents spend an average of 1 hour and 17 minutes doing housework every day. Counting only those who did housework, the average was 1 hour and 59 minutes. This is the 2024 survey, covering 38,500 households and 107,000 people. Another study took a sample of 6,271 people in four countries and found that people who spend money to buy time have higher life satisfaction. Researchers have also conducted experiments in real life: the same money spent on buying time brings higher current happiness than buying physical goods.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Whillans, A. V., Dunn, E. W., Smeets, P., Bekkers, R., & Norton, M. I. (2017). Buying time promotes happiness. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1706541114>; National Bureau of Statistics (2024). Bulletin of the Third National Time Use Survey (No. 2). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html>

Note: Calculate the hourly wage first, and the calculation is one month’s after-tax income ÷ one month’s actual working hours. Let’s look at how much this housework outsourcing costs. If the unit price of outsourcing is lower than your hourly wage, and you will really use the time saved to earn money or rest, then outsource. Everyone’s hourly wage and outsourcing price are different, so you have to make your own conclusions. In addition, Whillans measures how happy people are after spending money to buy time, not how many hours are saved.

Case: Ms. Zhang, who earns 20,000 yuan a month, calculated her hourly wage and found that outsourcing cleaning and laundry for two hours a day cost less than one-tenth of her monthly salary. She used the time she saved to learn new skills and her life satisfaction improved.

items.title: Set a hard cap for short videos and aimless screen browsing
items.core: In 2024, Chinese people will spend an average of 5 hours and 37 minutes online every day, and the number of people who actually went online that day was 6 hours and 3 minutes. In 2018, it was only 2 hours and 42 minutes by the same calculation. This is the largest number in this section. Cutting off an hour a day adds up to 365 hours a year.
body: Cost: No money. It only takes a few minutes: turn off push notifications, delete the app, or set a daily time limit for the app. The difficulty lies in holding back and not opening it.

Revenue: Chinese residents spend an average of 5 hours and 37 minutes online every day. Counting only those who were actually online that day, the average was 6 hours and 3 minutes. 92.9% of people had used the Internet that day. These are the numbers for 2024. In 2018 it was only 2 hours and 42 minutes by the same calculation. This is the largest number in this section. Cutting one of those hours off every day equals 365 extra hours per year. According to the China Internet Network Information Center, by June 2025, netizens will spend an average of 30.6 hours online per week, 1.9 hours more than half a year ago. There are 1.068 billion short video users, accounting for 95.1% of Internet users.
Evidence level: C

Source: National Bureau of Statistics (2024). Third National Time Use Survey Bulletin (No. 2). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html>; National Bureau of Statistics (2019). 2018 National Time Use Survey Bulletin. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202302/t20230203_1900224.html>; China Internet Network Information Center (2025). The 56th "Statistical Report on the Development of China's Internet". <https://www.cnnic.net.cn/NMediaFile/2025/0730/MAIN1753846666507QEK67ZS9DH.pdf>

Note: Internet time includes work, study and social interaction, and it is not all a waste. It was designated as C level because there was no research to calculate "how much was saved after the restriction and where the time was used." I only had total statistics. Among them, in the category of "checking how other people are doing", there have been randomized experiments to measure how much money was saved and how much the mood changed. See Section 3, Item 20.

Case: Xiao Li, a college student, set a daily limit of 45 minutes for a short video app. Once the time is up, the phone will lock the app. After a week, he had fewer unfinished notifications and had more time to prepare for exams and exercise.

items.title: Instead of watching TV and scrolling news, watch the information you need regularly
items.core: People over the age of 15 in the United States watch 2.6 hours of TV every day, accounting for half of all leisure time. In 2018, Chinese people watched an average of 1 hour and 40 minutes a day, and those aged 75 to 84 watched 3 hours and 16 minutes. Change the information you want to read to concentrated viewing at regular intervals, and this is where you can save.
body: Cost: No money. It's difficult to break the habit of opening it casually, and you may miss some instant messages.

Revenue: Americans 15 and older watch 2.6 hours of television per day. Their total leisure time is 5.2 hours, half of which is spent watching TV. These are the numbers for 2025. Chinese residents watch TV for an average of 1 hour and 40 minutes a day, and those aged 75 to 84 watch 3 hours and 16 minutes. These are the 2018 numbers.
Evidence level: C

Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (2026). American Time Use Survey — 2025 Results. <https://www.bls.gov/news.release/atus.nr0.htm>; National Bureau of Statistics (2019). 2018 National Time Use Survey Bulletin. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202302/t20230203_1900224.html>

Note: There are only total statistics on hand. I have not studied and calculated how the time saved after watching less TV and news is used. The method of "concentrating on reading" is based on the author's experience.

Case: Lao Chen turned off the news scroll bar on the TV and instead spent 15 minutes each day during lunch break and after dinner to browse important information. He used to watch rolling news whenever he had free time, but now he can save nearly two hours a day.

items.title: Spend time to learn the keyboard shortcuts and automation of commonly used software
items.core: Most people who are used to Word still click on toolbar icons. In the group comparison experiment, shortcut keys were faster than menus and icons. Learning this time is a one-time expense, and every operation will pay for itself every day. The longer you do the same type of work, the more you earn back.
body: Cost: Nothing. It takes several hours to dozens of hours to study at one time. The difficulty is that when I first started using it, it was slower than using a mouse.

Benefits: The study looked at 251 experienced Word users. Most of them rarely use faster shortcut keys and still mainly click on the icon toolbar. Group comparison experiments confirmed that among the three methods of menu, icon, and shortcut keys, shortcut keys are the fastest. The time saved accumulates little by little with the number of operations per day. People who have done the same type of work for a long time will benefit the most.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Lane, D. M., Napier, H. A., Peres, S. C., & Sándor, A. (2005). Hidden costs of graphical user interfaces: Failure to make the transition from menus and icon toolbars to keyboard shortcuts. International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction. <https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327590ijhc1802_1>

Note: Only learn the operations you will use more than ten times a day. Learning too much is another waste. Also, that efficiency experiment only had six participants, and the summary didn’t give the number of seconds saved per operation.

Case: Clerk Xiao Liu spent an afternoon memorizing the 20 commonly used shortcut keys of Word. When doing layout and format adjustments later, the operation speed was twice as fast as clicking the toolbar icons one by one, saving several hours every month.

items.title: Put commuting time first when choosing a place to live and shorten one-way commuting
items.core: According to German tracking data, people who have longer commutes feel worse off, and their wages and housing do not make up for this loss. However, some scholars have compiled multiple studies and believe that the relationship between commuting length and overall life satisfaction is not stable. Saving 30 minutes each way saves 5 hours a week.
body: Cost: High cost. You may have to pay higher rent, or move to a smaller house. The move itself also takes time.

Benefits: Chinese residents spend an average of 50 minutes a day in traffic. Only counting people traveling that day, it’s 1 hour and 2 minutes. These are the numbers for 2024. Data from Germany that tracks the same group of people over a long period of time shows that people with longer commutes have steadily lower subjective well-being (how well they feel). And that loss was not compensated for in income or housing. A review that pulled together multiple studies also confirmed that the longer the commute, the more dissatisfied people are with their commute, regardless of the mode of transportation used. But the same review also said that there is no stable relationship between commuting length and overall life satisfaction. It takes 30 minutes less each way and saves about 5 hours per week.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Stutzer, A., & Frey, B. S. (2008). Stress that doesn't pay: The commuting paradox. Scandinavian Journal of Economics, 110(2), 339–366. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9442.2008.00542.x>; Chatterjee, K., et al. (2020). Commuting and wellbeing: A critical overview of the literature with implications for policy and future research. Transport Reviews, 40(1), 5–34. <https://doi.org/10.1080/01441647.2019.1649317>; National Bureau of Statistics (2024). Bulletin of the Third National Time Use Survey (No. 2). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html>

Note: Controversy: Chatterjee et al. compiled multiple studies and pointed out that there is no stable relationship between commuting length and overall life satisfaction. They argue that people can generally trade the loss of long commutes for better jobs or housing. Also note that traffic activity statistics count all trips, not just commuting. In addition, if you can stagger your commute to get off work, you can run the same distance shorter.

Case: Xiao Wang changed his residence from outside the Fifth Ring Road to near the company, and his one-way commute was shortened from 90 minutes to 30 minutes. He sleeps an extra hour a day and has more social time on weekends. Although the rent has increased, he feels it is worth it.

items.title: Turn off all automatic renewals that you don’t need and replace them with manual renewals when they expire
items.core: What you save are those subscriptions that you haven’t used for a long time and are still deducting money every month. It takes less than 20 minutes to go through the automatic deduction lists of Alipay, WeChat, Apple and Android. According to regulations, merchants must clearly remind you before deducting money, and must also provide you with an entrance to cancel at any time, and it must be easy to find.
body: Cost: No money. Go through the "automatic deduction" lists of Alipay, WeChat, Apple, and Android for 10 to 20 minutes at a time. Every time you renew in the future, you have to click one more time.

Revenue: The money saved is equal to the sum of the subscriptions you no longer use but are still being charged. Everyone is different and there is no universal number. Regulations require merchants to clearly remind you before renewing, and to give you a "simple cancellation at any time" option. Cancellation does not cost extra money (China, effective from 2021)
Evidence level: C

Source: State Administration for Market Regulation (2021, revised in 2025). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions (General Administration Order No. 37, Article 18). <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/fgs/art/2025/art_4b47c79b8d994a42bba4835997688faa.html>

Note: For services that you really use frequently, annual payment is generally cheaper than monthly payment. It is more cost-effective to keep automatic renewal. The ones you want to close are the ones you have long forgotten about but are still deducting money from. For how to remind operators of websites selling memberships, see Section 26, Article 13 (Selling Automatically Renewal Members).

Case: Xiao Zhao spent 15 minutes looking through the automatic deduction lists of Alipay and Apple. He found two music and cloud storage subscriptions that he had not used for a long time, and canceled them immediately. Over the course of a year, I saved nearly 400 yuan in wasted money.

items.title: Perform a personal tax return from March to June every year, and fill in the special additional deductions
items.core: These types of people can usually get a refund: they only worked for a few months throughout the year, changed jobs in the middle of the year, or did not fill in deductions such as children's education, mortgages, rents, and supporting the elderly. It can be done in ten minutes on your mobile phone. If your annual comprehensive income is less than 120,000 yuan, or the tax you should pay is less than 400 yuan, you don’t need to apply.
body: Cost: Nothing. It can be done on the "Personal Income Tax" App and it takes only ten minutes.

Income: Calculate the general ledger by adding together the four items of wages, salaries, labor remuneration, author remuneration, and royalties. If you pay too much, you will be refunded, and if you pay less, you will have to make up for it. There are two situations where you do not need to apply: your annual comprehensive income does not exceed 120,000 yuan, or the tax to be paid does not exceed 400 yuan. These two items were announced by the State Administration of Taxation in 2023 and will be in effect until December 31, 2027. On the other hand, the following types of people can usually get their money back: those who have income for only a few months of the year, those who have changed jobs in the middle of the year, and those who have unfilled deductions for children’s education, mortgages, rents, support for the elderly, etc.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Administration of Taxation (2025). Measures for the Administration of Comprehensive Income Settlement and Payment of Personal Income Tax (Article 6) and its Interpretation. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202502/content_7006465.htm>; Ministry of Finance and State Administration of Taxation (2023). Announcement on the continuation of policies related to the final settlement and settlement of comprehensive income of individual income tax. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202308/content_6900594.htm>

Note: The person who should pay the tax must also pay it. It is illegal not to do it. There are seven special additional deductions: children’s education, continuing education, serious illness medical treatment, housing loan interest, housing rent, supporting the elderly, and care of infants and young children under 3 years old. Among them, you can only choose one for mortgage and rent, and you cannot fill in both.

Case: Xiao Wang joined the company in July last year and changed companies in October. He has not filled out the deductions for rent and children's education. In April this year, he filled in and calculated the tax on the personal tax app, and the system calculated a refund of more than 1,800 yuan.

items.title: The provident fund is not only used to buy a house: renting, decoration, and property fees can all be raised. It will be handled according to the new regulations starting from September 20, 2026
items.core: The provident fund is not only used to buy a house. The new regulations list nine situations that can be withdrawn, including renting a house, renovating the house you live in, and paying property fees. After you submit your application, the Provident Fund Center will reply within 3 days whether you are allowed to apply.
body: Cost: No money. Just go through the withdrawal procedure once.

Income: The revised regulations list the circumstances under which withdrawals can be made to nine items. These include: paying rent, renovating the house you live in, and paying property fees for the house you live in. The provident fund management center must make a decision on whether to allow withdrawal or not within 3 days from the day it accepts your application
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2026). State Council’s Decision on Amending the “Housing Provident Fund Management Regulations” (State Council Order No. 844, State Council No. 93 on July 31, 2026 Passed by the 2020 Executive Meeting, "Effective from September 20, 2026"): The revised Article 24 "If employees have any of the following circumstances, they can withdraw the balance in the employee housing provident fund account: (1) Paying rent; (2) Purchasing, constructing, renovating, and overhauling self-occupied housing; (3) Repaying the principal and interest of home purchase loans; (4) Renovating self-occupied housing; (5) Paying property fees for self-occupied housing; (6) ) Retired or retired; (7) Completely lost the ability to work and terminated the labor relationship with the unit; (8) Settled abroad; (9) Other housing consumption situations approved by the State Council. "; Article 25 "The Housing Provident Fund Management Center shall make a decision on whether to approve the withdrawal or not within 3 days from the date of accepting the application"; Article 18 The deposit ratio "should not be less than 5% of the employee's average monthly salary in the previous year." <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12946/202608/content_7079363.html>

Note: The money in the account is your own salary, plus the part allocated to you by the unit. The money is left untouched and only accrues interest at a very low interest rate. The regulations also state that if an employee dies or is declared dead, the heirs and legatees can withdraw the account balance. What materials need to be submitted and how to handle the application are determined by the local provident fund management center. Check the local center's service guide before running. The provident fund can also be used to borrow money to buy a house, and the interest rate is lower than that of commercial loans. See Section 15, Article 16 (Use housing provident fund loan first). If a property relies on water and power outages to pay for property fees, see Section 15, Article 17 (Property Water and Power Outages).

Case: After the implementation of the new regulations, Ms. Li applied for withdrawal on the Provident Fund App based on the rental contract and uploaded the property fee invoice. The center approved the reply on the second day, and 3,600 yuan was credited to the account, which was used to pay the rent for the second half of the year.

items.title: Mobile phone and broadband packages are recalculated every year. If you don’t use it, you will downgrade it. If the operator refuses to switch networks, you will complain.
items.core: The old package you are using is often dozens of dollars more expensive than the new one. Dozens a month, hundreds of dollars a year is wasted. According to regulations, operators cannot refuse you to switch networks without legitimate reasons, nor can they delay and refuse to do so for you, nor can they set a separate set of tariffs for people who switch networks. If it gets stuck, you complain.
body: Cost: No money. It takes ten minutes to check the bill. The hard part is resisting customer service and not downshifting for you.

Income: The regulations of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology state that operators shall not "refuse, prevent, or delay the provision of number portability services to users without justifiable reasons." It is also not allowed to "use technical means such as interception and restriction to affect the quality of communication services for users who port their numbers to another network." It is also not allowed to "set up special tariff plans and marketing plans for users who port their numbers to other networks." Old packages are often dozens of yuan more expensive than packages currently on sale. If you don’t change it, you will be throwing away hundreds of dollars every year
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (2019). Regulations on the management of number portability services (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology Information Management [2019] No. 242). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-11/13/content_5451483.htm>

Remarks: First go to the business hall App Check how much data and calls you have actually used in the past six months, and then choose a package based on this usage. If the customer service says, "Downshifting needs to be done by the sales office" and "Cannot be changed during the contract period," you should ask him to provide written evidence. If he couldn't give it, he called 12300 to complain

Case: Aunt Chen’s broadband was bundled with the 129 veteran package. She wanted to port her number to another network but was repeatedly pushed back by the window. She wrote down the work order number and complained, and the operator released it within three days and changed it to a 39 yuan package, saving about a thousand yuan a year.

items.title: Don't buy lottery tickets
items.core: According to regulations, the minimum proportion of bonuses to sales is 50% for lottery numbers, 65% for instant lottery, and 73% for guessing. For every 1 yuan invested in double-color balls, the long-term average return can only be 0.51 yuan, a stable loss of 49%. In 2024, 623.486 billion yuan in lottery tickets were sold nationwide, of which 161.031 billion yuan went directly into the public welfare fund, which is not included in the prize money.
body: Cost: No money. If you don't buy it, you save money.

Earnings: The Ministry of Finance sets a minimum percentage of prizes as a percentage of sales: 50% for lotto and digital lotteries, 65% for instant tickets, and 73% for lottery tickets. Shuangseqiu provides a bonus based on 51% of sales, and only takes out 51 yuan as a bonus for every 100 yuan sold. Converted to you, for every 1 yuan invested, you can only get back 0.51 yuan on average in the long run, a loss of 49%. In 2024, 623.486 billion yuan of lottery tickets were sold nationwide, of which 161.031 billion yuan went into the public welfare fund and did not return to the hands of lottery buyers (China, 2024)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Finance (2015). Notice on standardizing and strengthening the management of lottery fund composition ratio (Caizong [2015] No. 94). <http://m.mof.gov.cn/czxw/201511/t20151113_1560814.htm>; Ministry of Finance (2025). Ministry of Finance Announcement No. 8 of 2025 (2024) Annual Lottery Public Welfare Fund Raising and Distribution). <http://zhs.mof.gov.cn/zhengcefabu/202508/t20250828_3970977.htm>; China Welfare Lottery Double Color Ball Game Rules (Article 14). <https://mzj.nc.gov.cn/ncsmzj/flcp/202111/5dccc1a5da89434e94a62f8ea0e5887e.shtml>

Remarks: On average, you will lose money in the long run. This is determined by the system and has nothing to do with luck. It’s okay to buy it, but it can only be used as an entertainment expense of 2 yuan a time, not as financial management.

Case: Lao Zhang used to buy 10 yuan double-color balls every day after get off work. He spent more than 3,600 yuan a year and won less than 500 yuan. After he stopped buying, he automatically transferred the money to deposit, and at the end of the year, his account had more than 3,000 yuan more.

items.title: Just walk away when you see "high yield", "capital protection" and "steady profit"
items.core: The former chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission said in 2018: If the rate of return exceeds 6%, there will be a question mark. If the rate of return exceeds 8%, it is very dangerous. If the rate of return exceeds 10%, you will be prepared to lose all your principal. Formal financial management is no longer allowed to promise to protect capital and profits. According to regulations, the money you lose by participating in illegal fund-raising is borne by yourself, and no one will cover it for you if something goes wrong.
body: Cost: No money. Just stop when you hear these words.

Income: The former Chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission said something at the Lujiazui Forum in 2018. The original words are: "If the rate of return exceeds 6%, there will be a question mark. If the rate of return exceeds 8%, it will be very dangerous. If the rate of return exceeds 10%, you will be prepared to lose all your principal." The new asset management regulations require financial institutions to “not promise to guarantee principal and return” and also require that “when payment difficulties arise, financial institutions shall not advance funds for redemption in any form.” Therefore, there is no such thing as capital preservation in formal financial management. Losses caused by participating in illegal fund-raising are "borne by the fund-raising participants themselves", and no one will compensate you after the accident (China, 2018, 2021)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Guo Shuqing (2018). Prevent and resolve financial risks Strive to cross major hurdles (speech at the 10th Lujiazui Forum, official website of the State Financial Supervision and Administration Bureau): "In the process of cracking down on illegal fund-raising, we strive to use various methods to make the people realize that high returns mean high risks. If the return rate exceeds 6%, there will be a question mark. If the return rate exceeds 8%, it will be very dangerous. If it exceeds 10%, you will be prepared to lose all your principal." <https://www.nfra.gov.cn/cn/view/pages/ItemDetail.html?docId=182418>; Reprinted by Tianjin Local Financial Administration Bureau. <https://jrgz.tj.gov.cn/ztlm/ztzl/jrjfwphjr/202006/t20200625_2744709.html>; People's Bank of China, etc. (2018). Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions (Yinfa [2018] No. 106, Articles 2 and 6). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2018/content_5323101.htm>; State Council (2021). Regulations on Preventing and Dealing with Illegal Fund-raising (State Council Order No. 737, Article 25). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5588815.htm>

Note: These three lines of 6%, 8%, and 10% are drawn by regulators based on experience, not legal provisions. The original words were said when talking about cracking down on illegal fund-raising, targeting financial products and investment companies that promise high returns. It does not constitute investment advice. If you need to borrow money from others or buy shares in your own business, please see Section 12, Article 26 (Finding someone to raise money to do business) as a red line.

Case: Ms. Zhao saw a financial management poster of "guaranteed capital, guaranteed profit, 12% annual return" in the group, and asked the other party to show their qualifications but did not reply. Three months later, the platform was unable to withdraw cash, and several neighbors lost their principal.

items.title: No minimum repayments on credit cards, no installment or consumer loans for consumption; if you have to borrow, first convert the interest into annualized interest rate and then compare
items.core: The minimum repayment is a loan with daily interest, which is equivalent to about 18% per year based on the upper limit before 2020. If you use it, the interest-free period will be void. When writing "monthly handling fee 0.6%" in installments, the annual calculation is about 13.8%, not 7.2%. Because the principal is repaid every month, the handling fee is always charged based on the original amount. Which loan is more expensive depends only on the annual interest rate, not on the daily interest and monthly rates.
body: Cost: No money. Have enough cash to repay the bill in full before the bill date. The hard part is not having to spread out large expenses in installments. When you must borrow, take a few minutes to ask about the APR on each loan.

Income: There are upper and lower limits on credit card overdraft interest rates before 2020: the upper limit is "daily interest rate 5/10,000", and the lower limit is 0.7 times the upper limit. Five thousandths converted into one year is 18.25%, which is simple interest: calculated at 18.25% per year, the interest is no longer rolled into the principal. Starting in 2021, the card issuer and cardholder will negotiate pricing. After the minimum repayment is made, interest will be calculated on the full amount of the unpaid principal every day, and the interest-free period will be invalidated at the same time. The central bank has required card issuers to display the annualized interest rate (the interest rate calculated based on the entire year) in an obvious way, and "should not only display the daily interest rate and daily repayment amount." Starting from 2021, all lending institutions must clearly state the annual interest rate when advertising and signing contracts. The daily interest rate and the monthly interest rate can be written together, but they cannot be more conspicuous than the annualized interest rate. The annualized interest rate takes into account interest and various expenses directly related to the loan. If you repay the principal in installments, the amount of principal you actually used will be calculated based on the remaining principal after each installment. The People's Bank of China gave an example: borrow 100,000 yuan and repay it in 12 months, and pay 0.5% of the initial principal as installment fee every month. A service fee of RMB 1,000 is required when borrowing the loan. Based on simple interest, the annualized rate is approximately 12.80%. Based on compound interest (internal rate of return method), the annualized rate is approximately 13.58%. Just looking at the rates, you would think it only costs 0.5% × 12 + 1% = 7% a year. In fact, it is almost twice that, because the principal is decreasing every month, but the installment fee is always charged at 100,000 yuan. According to the same algorithm, a credit card is divided into 12 installments, with a handling fee of 0.6% per installment and no other fees, which is nominally 7.2% per year. Based on compound interest, the annualized rate is about 13.8%, which is about 1.9 times the nominal figure. There are 6 to 36 periods, all ranging from 1.8 to 2 times. The person who lends you money is an individual or an ordinary company, which is private lending. The agreed interest rate exceeded 4 times the one-year LPR when the contract was signed, and the court did not support the excess. The one-year LPR on August 20, 2026 is 3.0%, and 4x is 12%. The interest will be deducted from the loan first, and the court will calculate the principal based on the actual money received. This line does not cover licensed financial institutions such as banks and consumer finance companies. Seven types of local financial organizations, including small loan companies, pawn shops, and financial leasing companies, are also not applicable. Therefore, you cannot use 12% to arbitrage their loans. It depends on the annualized interest rate written in the contract (China, 2020, 2021)
Evidence level: C

Source: People's Bank of China (2020). Notice on promoting the market-oriented reform of credit card overdraft interest rates (Yinfa [2020] No. 327). <https://xining.pbc.gov.cn/zhengwugongkai/4081330/4406346/4693549/4159909/index.html>; People's Bank of China (2021). People's Bank of China Announcement [2021] No. 3 (Articles 1, 3, and 4, attachment "Example of Calculating Loan Annualized Interest Rate Using Internal Rate of Return Method" Third Example). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-03/31/content_5597156.htm>; Supreme People's Court (Second Amendment in 2020). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases (Articles 1, 25, and 26). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/94b6623974526df7d2430a3c73f050.html> (Official Gazette of the Supreme People's Court); Supreme People's Court (2020). Reply on the scope of application of the new judicial interpretation of private lending (Fa Interpretation [2020] No. 27). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/285171.html>; The National Interbank Funding Center is authorized by the People's Bank of China (2026). Announcement of the Loan Prime Rate (LPR) on August 20, 2026. <https://www.chinamoney.com.cn/chinese/rdgz/20260820/3399885.html>

Remarks: 18.25% is directly multiplied by "five ten thousandths × 365", and there is no calculation of compound interest. It would be even higher on a monthly basis. Some banks have discounts, which are subject to the annualized interest rate stated on your own statement. When you are really stuck with cash flow, give priority to borrowing from formal channels with lower interest rates, and don’t drag on the minimum repayment to earn interest. When comparing two loans, ask the other party to give you an annualized interest rate based on compound interest. What the other party offers is simple interest. According to regulations, "simple interest" must be written down. Simple interest will be lower than compound interest. 13.8% and 1.8 to 2 times are calculated by this book based on the algorithm of the People's Bank of China, and the algorithm is written in the verification record. Do not engage in usury in private lending, see also Section 7, Article 15 (Do not borrow at usury). For the additional money charged by the store when buying a car and applying for a loan, please refer to Article 49 of this section (financial service fees of 4S stores). For those that have not been repaid, please see Section 7, Article 23 (credit cards and online loans have been repaid).

Case: Xiao Liu bought a computer for 8,000 yuan using his credit card. He only paid the minimum amount on the bill day, and the interest for the next month was more than 100 yuan. The customer service also recommended a 0.6% installment. He calculated it using an annualized rate of about 13.8% and changed it to a one-time payment.

items.title: Do not reward anchors, do not recharge games, and do not place impulsive orders
items.core: Domestic gamers spend an average of about 480 yuan on games a year, and it is basically impossible to get back the money spent. The law only supports parents in requesting recharges from underage children without their consent and that are disproportionate to their age and intelligence. Adults do not have this provision. The most labor-saving way is to set up defenses in advance: turn off password-free payments, set single and daily limits, and unbind payment methods.
body: Cost: No money. Take a few minutes to do three things: turn off password-free payments, set single and daily limits, and delete the payment methods tied to the platform. The hard part was not to click that button on the spot.

Benefit: This is a big expense. In 2024, the actual sales revenue of the domestic game market will be 325.783 billion yuan, with 674 million users, and an average per capita of about 480 yuan (this is calculated by dividing the first two numbers). You can basically never get back the money you spend. There is only one exception: people with limited capacity for civil conduct (here refers to minors) without the consent of their guardians, reward and recharge "expenditures that are not appropriate for their age and intelligence." In this case, "the People's Court shall support" the guardian's request for a refund. There are no such regulations for adults’ own tips and recharges. In addition, minors can only play online games on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays. You can only play for one hour from 20:00 to 21:00 every day (China, 2020, 2021)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National Press and Publication Administration (2024).
