It seems cost-effective because it costs nothing, and the intuition of "hardship is effective" is so intuitive
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Buijze GA et al. (2016). The Effect of Cold Showering on Health and Work: A Randomized Controlled Trial. PLOS ONE. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0161749>; Cain T et al. (2025). Effects of cold-water immersion on health and wellbeing: A systematic review and meta-analysis. PLOS ONE. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0317615>

Note: Controversy: The number of days absent from work due to illness is indeed 29% less. This difference does not seem to be a coincidence. But the total number of sick days is not less, so it cannot be said that there are really fewer sick days. The use of cold water by athletes to help them recover after training is another issue, which we don’t care about here. Cold showers have no obvious harm to healthy people, but don’t regard it as a health investment

Case: A middle-aged man insisted on winter swimming and cold showers for half a year in order to enhance his immunity. I still had two colds during this period, and my physical examination showed no change in immunoglobulin levels. The doctor said that cold showers may cause short-term stress to the body, which does not mean that I will get sick less often.

items.title: Don’t buy products such as detoxification, colon cleansing, enzymes, and alkaline water
items.core: The detoxification industry is huge, but there is very little clinical evidence to support it, and no one has seriously tested the detoxification diets on the market. Some people checked whether there is a relationship between dietary acid-base and alkaline water and cancer, but only one qualified study was found, and no connection was found.
body: Cost: several hundred to several thousand yuan. Those who rely on starvation to "detoxify" may also lower their blood sugar and lack nutrients.

Benefits: That review concluded that “despite the booming detox industry, there is very little clinical evidence to support these diets” and that “there are no randomized controlled trials of commercial detox diets.” Another systematic review specifically examined whether there is a relationship between dietary acid-base and alkaline water and cancer: 8,278 documents were reviewed, and only one was eligible for inclusion, and no association was found. The authors write that "it is unreasonable to promote an alkaline diet and alkaline water to the public for cancer prevention or treatment." It seems cost-effective because "there are toxins in the body that need to be excreted" and "acidity in the body can cause cancer." These two premises sound very similar to physiology
Evidence level: C

Source: Klein AV, Kiat H (2015). Detox diets for toxin elimination and weight management: a critical review of the evidence. J Hum Nutr Diet. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jhn.12286>; Fenton TR, Huang T (2016). Systematic review of the association between dietary acid load, alkaline water and cancer. BMJ Open. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2015-010438>

Remarks: We can only say "no evidence supports", so we only give it a C grade. It is the job of the liver and kidneys to remove the waste products produced by the body's metabolism. As long as these two organs are not sick, there is no need to do any additional "detoxification"

Case: A woman spent 800 yuan on an enzyme bowel cleansing product and drank it twice a day. After drinking it for three months, my bowel movements are still irregular. Physical examination shows that the intestinal function is normal. The doctor pointed out that drinking more water and eating more fiber is more effective than drinking enzymes.

items.title: Don't force yourself to drink water just to get enough "8 glasses of water a day"
items.core: Some people specifically searched for the origin of "8 glasses of water a day", but not a single study to support it was found. Food and other drinks already contain a lot of water, so you don't need to drink so much. This conclusion only applies to healthy adults who live in places with mild climates and don't move much. People who work in hot weather, exercise strenuously, or drink more to treat and prevent diseases should take the initiative to drink more.
body: Cost: No money. It takes a little time and energy to remember to drink, and you will wake up more often at night.

Benefits: There was a literature review specifically looking at the term “8×8,” which refers to eight 8-ounce glasses of water per day. It concluded that "no scientific studies supporting 8×8 were found." It also writes that "studies of food and fluid intake in thousands of adults strongly suggest that such large amounts are not needed" because food and other drinks already provide large amounts of fluids. The author specifically states that this conclusion only applies to "healthy adults in moderate climates who spend most of their time sitting." He also wrote that the treatment or prevention of some diseases requires drinking up to 8×8 or more, and that "strengthening labor and exercise, especially in hot climates" also require drinking more. This statement seems cost-effective because water costs nothing, the number 8 is neat, and "drink more water" seems harmless in any situation
Evidence level: C

Source: Valtin H (2002). "Drink at least eight glasses of water a day." Really? Is there scientific evidence for "8 x 8"? Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol. <https://doi.org/10.1152/ajpregu.00365.2002>

Note: The number that is missing is "how many cups you must drink every day", which does not mean that drinking more water is harmful. People who work in high temperatures or exercise strenuously are a different matter and should take the initiative to drink. People who have had kidney stones should drink more, see Section 16, Item 8 (if you have had kidney stones, drink water to 2.5-3 liters per day, and reduce salt to less than 6 grams). The following two sentences are common sense reminders. The article in the source column did not say: Drink when you are thirsty at ordinary times and look at the color of your urine; people who do not feel thirsty after getting older should take the initiative to drink

Case: A woman working in an office forced herself to drink 8 glasses of water every day in order to maintain her health, and ran to the toilet in less than two hours. The physical examination showed that her kidney function was normal, and the doctor told her that the water in the soup and fruits was enough, so there was no need to force-feed her.

items.title: Don't spend money to tell fortunes, read Tarot, or look at zodiac signs to make decisions
items.core: There is a classic classroom experiment: the "Personal Personality Analysis" that students received was actually identical to each other, but everyone generally thought it was accurate. Fortune telling appears to be accurate, and here’s the truth. Astrologers get it right about as often as they make blind guesses. The price is more than a few dozen yuan: The principal of the fortune-telling gang in Xixian County, Henan Province, collected incense money and a "support package" of up to 3,888 yuan, and was sentenced to eleven years in prison.
body: Cost: No money. The hard thing is to give up a shortcut to making decisions and have to think on your own in the future.

Benefits: Classic classroom experiment: The "personal analysis" students received after taking the personality test is actually the same for everyone, but it is generally considered to be accurate. The author's conclusion is that "acceptance by the person or the analyst does not prove that the interpretation is correct." Thirty-nine students rated the analysis' accuracy on a scale of 0 to 5, and 34 rated it a 4 or 5. According to the distribution in the table, the average score is about 4.26 points. This explains why fortune telling always seems accurate. This phenomenon is called the Barnum effect. Astrology has also been tested in a double-blind manner, and the results were published in Nature. The astrologer chooses the one from the three personality test results that matches the horoscope. 40 were selected out of 116. You can pick 38.5 by purely guessing, and the astrologer predicts that you can pick 58.5 in advance. Official case: The Procuratorate of Xixian County, Henan Province reported an online fortune-telling fraud gang that first lures people in with free palm readings, and then charges "incense money" and "support packages" of up to 3,888 yuan. There were more than 50 victims, and more than 2 million yuan in stolen money was recovered. The principal culprit was sentenced to 11 years in prison and fined 100,000 yuan
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Forer BR (1949). People, 18 people with 4 points, 16 people with 5 points, N=39). <https://doi.org/10.1037/h0059240>; Carlson S (1985). A double-blind test of astrology. Nature 318:419-425 (Table 2: 116 first choice, 40 picks, random expectation 38.5, astrologers expected 58.5; "The data are consistent with chance, inconsistent with astrological hypothesis"). <https://doi.org/10.1038/318419a0>, full text copy included on Richard Muller's website <https://muller.lbl.gov/papers/Astrology-Carlson.pdf>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2026). Xixian County, Henan: After three years of continuous tracking and elimination of a group of online fortune-telling fraud gangs. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/202607/t20260728_732935.shtml>

Note: These two articles are only separate studies. Forer's original article did not directly write the average score. 4.26 was calculated based on the distribution in Table 1 of the original article. Here I only say "it is not accurate" and do not comment on any beliefs. Spending tens of dollars on entertainment does not count, but using it to decide on resignation, marriage, or investment is where you lose money.

items.title: Don’t buy anti-blue light glasses to “protect your eyesight”, and don’t believe that “if you stare at the screen for a few months, your eyes will become useless.” However, pain and redness in your eyes should be treated as an emergency
items.core: There is no obvious benefit to anti-blue light lenses. If you don’t buy them, you can save hundreds to thousands in added price. Compared with ordinary lenses, studies have found no difference in whether the eyes of people wearing them are tired or how clearly they can see, and no evidence has been found that they protect the fundus of the eyes. You can recover from eye soreness and dryness while looking at the screen, and your eyes won't be permanently damaged. What can really damage your eyes is welding arc light and laser.
body: Cost: It doesn’t cost any money, and you can save hundreds to thousands of dollars in markup on the lenses.

Benefits: Cochrane's 2023 systematic review included 17 randomized controlled trials, each involving 5 to 156 people, with follow-up ranging from less than 1 day to 5 weeks. Because the data were too small, the number of people recruited in each trial was very different, and the follow-up time was inconsistent, the author did not combine them to calculate a total. The results below are compared to lenses without blue light filtering. After less than a week of follow-up, there was "probably no difference" in self-reported eye fatigue, and the certainty of the evidence was low. In one trial of 120 people, the difference between the two groups was 9.76 units. The credible range for this difference is 95% CI −33.95 to 53.47. The range spans between plus and minus, indicating that no difference can be seen. The critical flicker fusion frequency is an objective measure of eye fatigue. "There may be little difference" between the two groups, and the certainty is low. The best vision you can see with spectacle correction "probably has no effect." The two groups differed by 0.00 logMAR (95% CI −0.02 to 0.02). This one has only 1 study, 156 people, and the certainty is moderate. It is unclear whether there is any effect on daytime wakefulness (2 trials, 42 people, very low certainty). The review also found no evidence to support its ability to protect the macula. The popular science page of the American Academy of Ophthalmology states that it is "not true" that "looking at screens for a long time can permanently damage your eyes." It is just that looking at screens for a long time will make your eyes uncomfortable. The national "Classification and Catalog of Occupational Diseases" (2024 edition) lists electro-optical ophthalmia caused by welding arc light and eye damage caused by lasers as occupational diseases
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Singh S, Downie LE, Anderson AJ, Keller PR, White SJ, Ang M, Wolffsohn JS (2023). Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses for visual performance, sleep, and macular health in adults. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 8, CD013244. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013244.pub2>; American Academy of Ophthalmology (2024). Computers, Digital Devices, and Eye Strain (“You may have heard that looking at a computer, smartphone, or other digital screen for long periods of time will permanently damage your eyes. Fortunately, this is not true.”). <https://www.aao.org/eye-health/tips-prevention/computer-usage>; National Health and Health Commission and four other departments (2024). Notice on the issuance of the "Classification and Catalog of Occupational Diseases" (National Health and Occupational Health Issue [2024] No. 39, "3. Occupational eye diseases" item 2 electro-optical ophthalmia, "6. Occupational diseases caused by physical factors" item 6 Eye (cornea, lens, retina) damage caused by laser). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_11886/202502/content_7007111.html>

Note: Watching the screen causes visual fatigue and dry eyes, which are manifested as eye soreness, dryness, and blurry eyes after looking at them for a long time. Resting and blinking often can relieve it. It can be alleviated, and it does not mean "the eyes are damaged". This sentence comes from the popular science page of the American Academy of Ophthalmology and is not the conclusion of the Cochrane review in the source column, so it is only rated C. What can really cause irreversible eye damage in a short period of time are strong light sources such as arc welding, ultraviolet rays, and lasers. Eye injuries caused by welding arc light are called "electrophotophthalmia", which is a legal occupational disease. It is blocked by goggles and masks, not anti-blue light lenses, see Section 19, Article 10 (Protection from dust, noise, chemical poisons). When you stay up all night staring at the screen, what you need to guard against is not the screen itself, but an exception. If your eyes are swollen, painful and red, there is a rainbow when looking at the light, and you also have a headache, nausea and vomiting, it is an acute angle-closure glaucoma attack. It can crush the optic nerve within a few days, necessitating a trip to the eye emergency department the same day, see Section 13, No. 6 (Ophthalmological emergencies). Dilated pupils in the dark, lowering your head for a long time and pushing the lens forward are two things that are its triggers. People at high risk are those over 50 years old, farsighted, and have a shallow anterior chamber. Dry eyes caused by the screen will become a chronic disease that needs to be seen by a doctor if it lasts for a long time. It will not go away after sleeping. If your eyes have been feeling uncomfortable, or your vision is really declining, go to the ophthalmologist to find out the cause, and don't just change the lenses yourself. How to prevent myopia in children and adolescents, see Section 30, Items 4, 12, and 9 (go outdoors for 2 hours a day, have mydriasis checked, and do not buy products that “cure myopia”).

Case: A programmer spent 800 yuan on anti-blue light lenses and looked at the screen for 10 hours a day. Half a year later, my eyes were still dry and tired. An eye examination showed that my vision had not declined. The doctor explained that the dry eyes were due to less blinking and had nothing to do with blue light.

items.title: Don’t treat blood donation as health care: "Detoxification, lowering blood lipids, and preventing myocardial infarction" are not supported by randomized trials. Frequent donation can really lead to iron deficiency
items.core: It is unreliable to say that donating blood can prevent myocardial infarction and reduce deaths. People who can donate blood all the time are already in better health. If this layer is deducted, the mortality rate of donating blood once a year shrinks from nearly 20% to 7.5%. In experiments that truly compared people separately, there was no difference in the number of deaths. On the other hand, working too hard will indeed make people weak and afraid of the cold. The reason is iron deficiency.
body: Cost: No money. A blood donation takes about an hour, including filling out the form, collecting blood, and staying for observation and rest. Over the next few weeks, your body continues to replace the lost iron.

Benefits: The Finnish Kuopio study followed 2,682 men aged 42 to 60 for an average of nearly nine years. Of the 153 people who had donated blood in the 24 months before statistics were collected, one (0.7%) had an acute myocardial infarction. It occurred in 316 out of 2529 people (12.5%) who had never donated (difference between the two proportions P<0.0001). After deducting the influence of age and other risk factors for coronary heart disease, people who have donated blood have an approximately 88% lower risk of heart attack. Relative risk 0.12 (95% CI 0.02–0.86, P=0.035). But this is only a tracking record, without group comparison. There are 1,182,495 blood donors in the Nordic SCANDAT database, with a cumulative follow-up of 9,526,627 person-years, including 15,401 deaths. When only characteristics such as age and gender were excluded, donating blood once more per year was associated with an 18.6% lower mortality rate (95% CI 16.8%–20.4%). If we also deduct the layer "you are always allowed to donate blood only if you are healthy", the decrease is only 7.5% (5.7%-9.4%). The authors concluded that "cannot be interpreted as conclusive evidence of health benefits." The FeAST randomized controlled trial found 1,277 patients with symptomatic lower extremity arterial disease and randomly divided them into two groups. One group received regular bloodletting every 6 months to reduce iron, and the other group received control. The main focus was on all-cause death, 125/636 (20%) versus 148/641 (23%). HR 0.85 (HR is the hazard ratio, 1 means both sides are the same). 95% CI 0.67–1.08, P=0.17. The odds of death plus non-fatal myocardial infarction and stroke were 180 (28%) versus 205 (32%), with an HR of 0.88 (0.72–1.07, P=0.20). No difference was seen in either item. The INTERVAL randomized trial found 45,263 people who donated whole blood. These people are divided into three blood donation intervals. Men are 12 weeks, 10 weeks, 8 weeks, women are 16 weeks, 14 weeks, 12 weeks. After shortening the interval, significantly more blood was drawn over two years (1.69 units more in men in the 8-week group than in the 12-week group, 95% CI 1.59–1.80). No differences were found between the groups in quality of life, physical activity, and cognitive function. But donating blood brings more discomfort, including fatigue, shortness of breath, dizziness, dizziness and restless legs (legs are so uncomfortable that you can't lie down at night). Mean values ​​of hemoglobin and ferritin were also lower, and the number of blood donations postponed because of low hemoglobin was also greater (P < 0.0001 for each). Iron deficiency affects the body's heat production: 10 women with iron deficiency anemia, 8 people whose iron stores had been depleted but not yet anemic, and 12 control women were soaked in water at 28°C for 100 minutes. The rectal temperature was 36.0±0.2 ℃ in the anemia group and 36.2±0.1 ℃ in the control group (P=0.001). Oxygen consumption 5.28±0.26 vs. 5.99±0.29 mL·min⁻¹·kg⁻¹ (P=0.04). Thyroxine and triiodothyronine, two thyroid hormones, were also lower (P<0.002). This statement seems to be valid because the people who donate blood are healthy people who have been screened repeatedly, and the hypothesis that "removing iron can protect the heart" has not been tested in randomized trials.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Salonen JT, Tuomainen TP, Salonen R, Lakka TA, Nyyssönen K (1998). Donation of blood is associated with reduced risk of myocardial infarction. The Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor Study. American Journal of Epidemiology, 148(5), 445-451. <https://doi.org/10.1093/oxfordjournals.aje.a009669>; Ullum H, Rostgaard K, Kamper-Jørgensen M, et al. (2015). Blood donation and blood donor mortality after adjustment for a healthy donor effect. Transfusion, 55(10), 2479-2485. <https://doi.org/10.1111/trf.13205>; Zacharski LR, Chow BK, Howes PS, et al. (2007). Reduction of iron stores and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with peripheral arterial disease: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA, 297(6), 603-610. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.297.6.603>; Di Angelantonio E, Thompson SG, Kaptoge S, et al. (2017). Efficiency and safety of varying the frequency of whole blood donation (INTERVAL): a randomized trial of 45 000 donors. Lancet, 390(10110), 2360-2371. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)31928-1>; Beard JL, Borel MJ, Derr J (1990). Impaired thermoregulation and thyroid function in iron-deficiency anemia. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 52(5), 813-819. <https://doi.org/10.1093/ajcn/52.5.813>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (1997). Blood Donation Law of the People's Republic of China (Articles 2, 9, and 14). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf5e71801f9>; National Health Commission, etc. (2024-01-08). Notice on further improving the incentives and rewards for unpaid blood donors. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202401/content_6924875.htm>

Note: What you want to say is "donate blood for your own body", not the blood donation itself. Blood is for others, and according to the beneficiary classification of this book, it falls into the fourth category (strangers). What can really come back to you is the share given by the system. Article 14 of the "Blood Donation Law" stipulates that people who donate blood for free use the blood themselves in the hospital and are exempt from the fees for collection, storage, separation and testing. Spouses and immediate family members may be exempted from or reduce payment according to provincial government regulations. A notice from the National Health Commission in January 2024 stated that 28 provinces have directly reduced the cost of blood used by unpaid blood donors and relatives in provincial hospitals when they are discharged. Those who receive the voluntary blood donation award can also take public transportation for free according to the local "three exemptions" policy, visit parks sponsored by the government for free, and be exempted from paying general outpatient examination fees in public hospitals. If you want to offer, please do so at the legal intervals. Article 9 of the Blood Donation Law stipulates that each donation is generally 200 ml, with a maximum of 400 ml. The interval between two visits should be no less than 6 months. Recommended ages are 18 to 55 years. Don't keep the interval as short as possible just to get honors or collective targets. Women, people with low body weight, and people with heavy menstrual flow have low levels of iron in their bodies. People who donate blood repeatedly can check their ferritin at their own expense. After donating, if you feel weak, afraid of the cold, or feel uncomfortable in your legs when you lie down at night (this is called restless legs), don’t assume that your vitality is damaged. Go get your blood routine and ferritin checked. If you are found to be deficient in iron, follow the doctor's instructions and take iron supplements, and at the same time extend the interval between blood donations. There is only 10 human evidence that people are afraid of the cold. It is used to explain why this is the case, not to say how many people will be like this.

Case: A middle-aged man heard that donating blood can prevent myocardial infarction and lower blood lipids, so he donated more than a dozen times in two years. Later, he often felt weak and was extremely afraid of cold. He went to the hospital for examination and was diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia. The doctor clearly told him that this was caused by frequent blood donation and had nothing to do with health care.

items.title: Don't rely on universal physical examination packages to prevent diseases, do the few evidence-based screenings based on age and gender
items.core: People who do regular universal health examinations have the same mortality rate as those who don't, and the same number of deaths from cardiovascular disease and cancer. It is enough to do the few evidence-based screenings based on age and gender. Those over 35 years old can have their blood pressure measured once a year for free, and those over 65 years old can have a free physical examination once a year.
body: Cost: No money, and you can save hundreds to thousands of yuan in package fees every year. The obligation in exchange is to remember which items to check and how often to check them.

Benefit: The 2019 update of the Cochrane Systematic Review included 17 randomized controlled trials. To calculate overall mortality, 11 trials, 233,298 participants, and 21,535 deaths were combined. The group that did the general health check had the same RR as the control group, RR 1.00. RR is relative risk, 1 means both sides are the same. The 95% CI 0.97–1.03 is the confidence range. When counting deaths from cardiovascular disease, combining 9 trials, 170,227 people, and 6,237 deaths, the RR was 1.05 (95% CI 0.94–1.16). When counting deaths from cancer, combining 8 trials, 139,290 people, and 3,663 deaths, the RR was 1.01 (95% CI 0.92–1.12). No difference was seen in either of these two items. The authors concluded that "universal health screening is unlikely to be beneficial." The National Basic Public Health Service provides permanent residents aged 35 and over with a free blood pressure measurement once a year. It also gives seniors 65 and older a free annual wellness exam. This free physical examination includes physical examination, blood routine, urine routine, fasting blood glucose and electrocardiogram. Liver function tests include aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and total bilirubin. Renal function tests include serum creatinine and blood urea. Blood lipids were checked for total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. and finally abdominal B-ultrasound of the liver, gallbladder, pancreas and spleen (national)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Krogsbøll LT, Jørgensen KJ, Gøtzsche PC (2019). General health checks in adults for reducing morbidity and mortality from disease. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 1, CD009009. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD009009.pub3>; National Health and Family Planning Commission (2017). National Basic Public Health Service Specifications (Third Edition) (Health Management Services for the Elderly, Health Management Services for Patients with Hypertension). <https://www.nhc.gov.cn/ewebeditor/uploadfile/2017/04/20170417104506514.pdf>

Note: What you need to consider is "use the annual package as a means of disease prevention", which does not mean that you should not do all examinations. In addition, free blood pressure measurement once a year for those over 35 years old and free physical examination once a year for those over 65 years old are provided by the national basic public health service project, so there is no need to pay out of pocket. Check items that should be checked if there is reason to do so. For blood pressure, blood sugar, and hepatitis B, see Section 1, Items 7, 8, and 14. For breast, cervix and colorectum, see Section 1, Items 17, 18 and 19. Helicobacter pylori and low-dose CT See Section 1, Items 23 and 24. For bone density testing in women over 65 years of age, see Section 1, Item 39 (Bone Density Testing). Check if you have engaged in high-risk behavior, see Section 1, Article 31. From what age you started checking, and how often you check, are written there. If you go for a physical examination organized by your work unit and paid for by others, the only thing that will stop you is spending your own money to buy a package and adding items yourself. People who already have chronic diseases, people with symptoms, or examinations prescribed by doctors based on their condition are not included. They are medical consultations, not screening. The most common items in packages without evidence are tumor markers and whole-body imaging, see Item 7 of this section (Whole-body PET-CT and tumor marker packages). What to do if you are diagnosed with high uric acid but never have pain, or have gallbladder stones but never have pain. See Article 19 (Asymptomatic High Uric Acid) and Article 20 (Asymptomatic Gallbladder Stone) in this section. In addition, most of the trials included in Cochrane were conducted in high-income countries, where it is convenient to see a doctor. Areas with limited medical resources should not directly copy this conclusion.

Case: 45-year-old Mr. Zhang undergoes an expensive full-body physical examination package every year, and the report shows that everything is normal. However, he has been a smoker for a long time and has never had targeted low-dose lung CT screening. Last year, when he was diagnosed with lung cancer due to persistent cough, he was already in the advanced stage and missed the best treatment period.

items.title: Don’t start taking uric acid-lowering drugs just because physical examination shows high uric acid but you have never had pain
items.core: For people with excessive uric acid, but have never had gout or tophi, the American College of Rheumatology conditionally recommends not taking uric acid-lowering drugs first. 24 people took it for 3 years to prevent a gout attack. The attempt to rely on it to protect the kidneys was in vain. Patients with kidney disease took the medicine and their kidney function continued to decline, just as fast as those who took fake medicine. Treat the real attack after it has passed.
body: Cost: It does not cost money, and it also saves money on long-term medication and regular review, and also eliminates the risk of unnecessary medication.

Benefit: The American College of Rheumatology’s 2020 gout guidelines address asymptomatic hyperuricemia. It refers to blood uric acid >6.8 mg/dL, and there has been no previous attack of gout or tophi under the skin. The guidelines conditionally recommend that these individuals not start taking any urate-lowering medications. Medications include allopurinol, febuxostat, and probenecid. The certainty of the evidence was rated "high." The footnote below the table states, “Based on attributable risk, 24 patients would need to be treated for 3 years to prevent one gout attack.” The CKD-FIX randomized controlled trial enrolled 363 people. They have stage 3 or 4 chronic kidney disease with no history of gout but are at risk for worsening. One group received 100–300 mg of allopurinol daily, and one group received a placebo. The trial was conducted for 104 weeks. eGFR is an indicator of kidney function, measured in mL/min/1.73 m². Group year-to-year change was -3.33 (95% CI -4.11 to -2.55). The other group varied -3.23 per year (-3.98 to -2.47). The two groups differed by -0.10 (-1.18 to 0.97), P=0.85, and kidney function declined equally rapidly. Serious adverse events 46% vs. 44%. The PERL randomized controlled trial looked at 530 people with type 1 diabetes and early to mid-stage diabetic nephropathy. They took allopurinol for 3 years and then stopped taking it for 2 months to wash away the effects of the drug. Allopurinol did lower serum uric acid from 6.1 to 3.9 mg/dL. However, after stopping the drug, the difference in renal function index GFR between the two groups was only 0.001 mL/min/1.73 m². The confidence range for this difference is 95% CI -1.9 to 1.9, P=0.99. The amount of albumin leaked in urine was 40% higher in the allopurinol group (0 to 80). It seems cost-effective because the intuition that "if the indicator exceeds the standard, you should take medicine to suppress it" is too smooth
Level of Evidence: A

Source: FitzGerald JD, Dalbeth N, Mikuls T, et al. (2020). 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout. Arthritis Care & Research, 72(6), 744-760 (Table 1 and its footnotes). <https://doi.org/10.1002/acr.24180>; Badve SV, Pascoe EM, Tiku A, et al. (2020). Effects of Allopurinol on the Progression of Chronic Kidney Disease. New England Journal of Medicine, 382(26), 2504-2513. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1915833>; Doria A, Galecki AT, Spino C, et al. (2020). Serum Urate Lowering with Allopurinol and Kidney Function in Type 1 Diabetes. New England Journal of Medicine, 382(26), 2493-2503. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1916624>

Note: What is wrong is that "I have never had an attack and started taking uric acid-lowering drugs for the rest of my life." This does not mean that high uric acid does not matter. The same guide also lists exceptions. You can consider starting to eat in the following situations. One is that the first attack is accompanied by chronic kidney disease of stage 3 or above. The second is serum uric acid >9 mg/dL (approximately 535 µmol/L). The third is having urinary tract stones. For those who have tophi, whose bones have been eroded on the radiograph, and who have attacks more than twice a year, the guidelines strongly recommend taking medicine; for those who have more than one attack but less than two times a year, it is conditionally recommended. For details, see Section 16, Item 9 (if gout is diagnosed, take uric acid-lowering drugs for a long time). About 7.4% of Han people carry a genotype called HLA-B\*5801, while only 0.7% of white people carry it. People with this type of drug are more likely to develop severe, life-threatening drug rashes when taking allopurinol. Asians are three times more likely to develop hypersensitivity syndrome than white people. This is medicine that you can skip taking for now, there is no need to take this extra risk. Before you really start taking it, check the genotype first. See Section 16, Item 9 (if gout is diagnosed, take uric acid-lowering drugs for a long time). Those two kidney trials were conducted on patients with chronic kidney disease and type 1 diabetes, so they cannot be directly generalized as "high uric acid is completely harmless to the kidneys." What they deny is just the idea that "taking medicine to lower uric acid can protect the kidneys"

Case: Lao Li’s physical examination found that uric acid was high, but his joints were never red, swollen or painful. He listened to the rumors and started taking uric acid-lowering drugs for a long time. Three years later, not only was he unable to prevent gout once, but his kidney function also declined due to the side effects of the drugs. During the reexamination, the doctor immediately asked him to stop taking the drugs.

items.title: Don't go for preventive gallbladder removal just because gallbladder stones have been detected during physical examination but have never hurt
items.core: About 80% of people who have stones in their gallbladders but have never had pain have had no symptoms in the past nine years. Without it, approximately one to three thousand percent of emergencies such as cholecystitis and pancreatitis will occur every year. Removing the gallbladder is not without risk; about 1.5% of people experience injury to their bile ducts. Therefore, guidelines from Europe and the UK say that patients should not be cured until there are no symptoms.
body: Cost: No money, but also saves a general anesthesia operation and a hospitalization. The obligation in exchange is to remember which signals require you to go to the hospital as soon as they appear.

Benefits: The Italian MICOL census performed ultrasound on 11,229 people aged 29 to 69 years. 856 people were found to have gallstones, 580 of whom were asymptomatic and followed for an average of 8.7 years. Among these 580 people, 453 (78.1%) have been asymptomatic, 61 (10.5%) have mild symptoms, and 66 (11.4%) have severe symptoms. A total of 189 cholecystectomies were performed during the follow-up period, 41.3% of which were performed on asymptomatic individuals. The author concluded that "expectant treatment is still an effective treatment method for most patients." Expectant treatment means observation first and no surgery. An HMO (a managed care organization) in the United States conducted follow-up statistics on 691 people diagnosed with gallstones, with an average follow-up period of 78±61.6 months. Of the 135 asymptomatic individuals who were followed for 58±50.2 months (median 46.3 months), only 10% developed symptoms of gallstones and 7% underwent surgery. Only 2 of the 50 deaths in the entire group were related to the biliary tract, and both were in the symptomatic group. The author's conclusion is that "patients with silent stones do not need surgery before symptoms appear." Silent stones are stones that do not make a sound or attack. This is what Article 1.2.1 of the UK NICE Guideline CG188 says. "People with normal gallbladders and bile ducts who are incidentally found to have asymptomatic gallbladder stones should be informed that they do not need treatment until symptoms develop." The European Society of Liver Diseases' 2016 gallstone guidelines put the risks on both sides together. About 0.7% to 2.5% of asymptomatic people develop symptoms each year. The annual incidence of acute cholecystitis, acute pancreatitis, obstructive jaundice (blockage of the bile duct, yellowing of the person) or cholangitis is 0.1% to 0.3%. After the first colic, complications only rise to 1% to 3% per year, so most people have a bout of pain before something big happens. On the surgical side, of the 51,041 cholecystectomies registered nationwide in Sweden, 1.5% injured the bile duct. About one-fifth (0.3%) of these are partial or complete disconnections of the bile duct. The mortality rate within one year was 3.9% for those with bile duct injuries and 1.1% for those without. The guideline also states that 10% to 40% of patients still experience discomfort after surgery, or may feel better for a while and then return. The conclusion of the guideline is that surgery on asymptomatic people, whether open or laparoscopic, will not prolong life. Because the risk of death and complications from the surgery itself outweighs the risk of not doing it. The total cost will be lower if symptoms are treated before treatment occurs. A 1983 calculation gave specific figures: A 30-year-old male who undergoes prophylactic resection will live an average of 4 days less than those who are first observed, and a 50-year-old man will live 18 days less. There has been no randomized trial comparing cutting and not cutting. Preventive resection seems cost-effective because of the intuition that "sooner or later it will hurt, so it is better to do it while you are young."
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Festi D, Reggiani ML, Attili AF, et al. (2010). Natural history of gallstone disease: Expectant management or active treatment? Results from a population-based cohort study. Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, 25(4), 719-724. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1440-1746.2009.06146.x>; McSherry CK, Ferstenberg H, Calhoun WF, Lahman E, Virshup M (1985). The natural history of diagnosed gallstone disease in symptomatic and asymptomatic patients. Annals of Surgery, 202(1), 59-63. <https://doi.org/10.1097/00000658-198507000-00009>; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2014). Gallstone disease: diagnosis and management. NICE guideline CG188, clauses 1.2.1, 1.3.1. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg188/chapter/Recommendations>; European Association for the Study of the Liver (2016). EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of gallstones. Journal of Hepatology, 65(1), 146-181. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhep.2016.03.005>; Törnqvist B, Strömberg C, Persson G, Nilsson M (2012). Effect of intended intraoperative cholangiography and early detection of bile duct injury on survival after cholecystectomy: population based cohort study. BMJ, 345, e6457. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.e6457>; Ransohoff DF, Gracie WA, Wolfenson LB, Neuhauser D (1983). Prophylactic cholecystectomy or expectant management for silent gallstones. A decision analysis to assess survival. Annals of Internal Medicine, 99(2), 199-204. <https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-99-2-199>; Gurusamy KS, Samraj K (2007). Cholecystectomy versus no cholecystectomy in patients with silent gallstones. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, CD006230. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD006230.pub2>; Counter: Venneman NG, Buskens E, Besselink MG, et al. (2005). Small gallstones are associated with increased risk of acute pancreatitis: potential benefits of prophylactic cholecystectomy? American Journal of Gastroenterology, 100(11), 2540-2550. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1572-0241.2005.00317.x>; Biliary Surgery Group of the Surgery Branch of the Chinese Medical Association, Biliary Surgery Committee of the Surgery Branch of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association (2022). Expert consensus on the surgical treatment of benign gallbladder diseases (2021 edition). Chinese Journal of Surgery, 60(1), 4-9. <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.cn112139-20210811-00373> (Full text requires subscription, not available); Ibid. (2022). Interpretation of "Expert Consensus on Surgical Treatment of Benign Diseases of the Gallbladder (2021 Edition)". Chinese Journal of Surgery, 60(4), 337-342. <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.cn112139-20220119-00031>

Remarks: Controversy. The 2021 edition of the expert consensus on domestic biliary tract surgery lists some asymptomatic gallbladder stones as surgical indications. An interpretation article in the same magazine stated that one of the core points of the controversy lies here. You need to subscribe to the full text of the consensus. This book failed to check which situations it lists specifically. Another counter-argument concerns small stones: stones smaller than 5 mm are more associated with pancreatitis. A Dutch calculation said that such people may live longer or shorter after preventive resection, depending on how common and fatal pancreatitis is. European guidelines also list exceptions: calcification of the gallbladder wall (porcelain gallbladder) and the presence of gallbladder polyps greater than 1 cm should be removed. When undergoing other major abdominal surgeries, you may consider cutting it off. This article only talks about one situation: a stone grows in the gallbladder, and it never hurts. **Stones in the common bile duct are another story**. Article 1.3.1 of the same guideline clearly states that regardless of whether there are symptoms of common bile duct stones, the stones in the bile duct must be removed and the gallbladder must be removed. Go to the hospital on the same day if any of the following conditions occur. Don't take this conclusion for granted: persistent cramping in the right upper abdomen or upper abdomen, fever and chills, yellowing of the whites of the eyes or skin, and dark urine. When the doctor recommends surgery after viewing the images, ask him for the reasons, such as bile duct involvement, polyps, or gallbladder wall abnormalities. Don't use this conclusion to refute him. What it blocks is "cutting without any reason, just because the stone is found." The above two studies followed a group of people looking backwards, without group control. But what they want to answer is "What will happen if you don't move it?" rather than "Which treatment is better?", so it is appropriate to use it here. In addition, the two tracking years are 4 to 9 years. The longer the years are, the proportion of symptoms will go up

Case: Lao Liu found gallbladder stones during physical examination but he never felt any pain. The surgeon said it could be cut. He found the European and British guidelines that said not to cut if there were no symptoms. In the past nine years, about 80% of the cases had no symptoms, so he chose to observe. I haven't had a seizure in the past eight years, and I haven't taken any specialized medicine.

items.title: Don't quit calcium to prevent kidney stones
items.core: People who have had calcium oxalate stones are often advised to eat less calcium, but the results of the test are just the opposite. Men who repeatedly develop stones and have high urinary calcium eat calcium normally and eat less animal protein and salt. The number of men who relapse within five years is only half of those who eat a low-calcium diet. UK guidelines also state not to limit calcium.
body: Cost: No money. In turn, it saves trouble, as you don’t have to be wary of things containing calcium every day.

Benefits: There was a 5-year randomized controlled trial, looking at 120 men who had repeatedly developed calcium oxalate stones and had high levels of calcium in their urine (called idiopathic hypercalciuria). They were randomly divided into two groups. One group ate normal calcium, 30 mmol per day. This group also ate less animal protein (52 g per day) and less salt (50 mmol sodium chloride per day). The other group ate a traditional low-calcium diet, 10 mmol per day. Relapses over 5 years were 12/60 vs 23/60. The unadjusted relative risk was 0.49 (95% CI 0.24–0.98, which is the confidence range), P = 0.04, and the risk of recurrence in the normal calcium group was only half. During the follow-up period, urinary calcium dropped by approximately 170 mg per day in both groups. But the oxalic acid excreted in urine is different. The low calcium group increased by an average of 5.4 mg per day, and the normal calcium group decreased by an average of 7.2 mg per day. Article 1.8.1 of the British NICE guideline NG118 states that do not limit the amount of calcium you eat every day. Adults maintain 700 to 1,200 mg daily. Children and adolescents 350 to 1,000 mg daily depending on age. Giving up calcium seems cost-effective because of the intuition that "stones are made of calcium, so eat less calcium."
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Borghi L, Schianchi T, Meschi T, et al. (2002). Comparison of two diets for the prevention of recurrent stones in idiopathic hypercalciuria. New England Journal of Medicine, 346(2), 77-84. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa010369>; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2019). Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management. NICE guideline NG118, Article 1.8.1. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng118/chapter/Recommendations>

Note: Controversy: This trial is only done on men, and these people have repeated calcium oxalate stones and have high urinary calcium. It cannot be directly applied to all types of stones. In addition, the experimental group made three changes at the same time: eat calcium normally, eat less animal protein, and eat less salt, so all the benefits cannot be attributed to "not quitting calcium." Low salt and animal protein may also be at play. The answer is to "take the initiative to quit calcium-containing foods", not to say "you should take more calcium". What is changed here is the calcium in three meals a day. Calcium supplements are another matter. People who have had stones should ask their attending doctor whether they should take supplements. For the article on drinking more water, see Section 16, Item 8 (drink up to 2.5-3 liters of water per day after kidney stones)

Case: Uncle Wang, who repeatedly developed calcium oxalate stones, listened to advice and strictly gave up milk and soy products. As a result, the stone recurred three times within five years. Later, the doctor asked him to resume normal calcium intake and reduce salt and animal protein. The frequency of stone recurrence was significantly reduced, and his health was better.

items.title: Don’t buy crystals, bracelets, and other items for the purpose of “transferring luck,” “bringing wealth,” or “nurturing people.”
items.core: There is no verifiable evidence that wearing them can improve luck, attract wealth, or nourish people. It seems to have the same principle as fortune telling. It is said in a general enough way that you will apply it yourself. In 2026, a live broadcast room fabricated material and falsely claimed that it could prevent and cure rheumatism, and was investigated and punished as false propaganda. No problem buying it as a decoration.
body: Cost: No money. All you have to do is don't include "transportation" and "supporting people" into the reasons for buying it. The difficulty is that when everyone else is wearing it and talking about the spirit, you don’t follow suit.

Benefits: Classic classroom experiments show that everyone gets the same general "personal analysis", but generally thinks it is accurate. This phenomenon is called the Barnum effect. It explains where the experience of "it feels smooth after putting it on" comes from. That author concluded that "acceptance by myself does not prove that the interpretation is correct." Official case: On June 4, 2026, the State Administration for Market Regulation announced a number of typical cases of "anti-counterfeiting and clearing up sources" in traditional craft markets. Among them, there is a jewelry store in Sihui, Guangdong, which fabricates product materials in the live broadcast room. It also falsely claims that the product has the effects of "preventing and treating rheumatism, improving immunity, improving sleep quality, and clearing blood vessels." This store relies on scripts and acting to mislead and deceive consumers. This violates Article 9, Paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, and the case is called "Sihui City Langzhen Jewelry Store False Commercial Promotion Case" (National)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Forer BR (1949). The fallacy of personal validation: A classroom demonstration of gullibility. Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology. <https://doi.org/10.1037/h0059240>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2026). The State Administration for Market Regulation announced a number of typical cases of "anti-counterfeiting and clearing up sources" in traditional craft markets. <https://www.samr.gov.cn/xw/zj/art/2026/art_1529399cfe874b8780c4496eb0158020.html>

Note: There is only one conclusion: its efficacy cannot be verified, nor can any prediction ability be measured. It does not comment on any beliefs or customs, nor is it intended for gifts, commemorations, or family heirlooms. Two things need to be distinguished. The functions claimed by the merchants are clearly stipulated, and you can make complaints. As for the "transshipment" statement, there is neither research nor proof that it is false. You can only rely on your own budget to manage it. Before buying it, treat it as an ordinary accessory and ask yourself, "If it doesn't change anything, would I still buy it at this price?" How to check the material and certificate, and why it is not cost-effective to treat it as an investment, see Section 5, Items 33 and 34 (Bracelets and watches are calculated based on the money spent, and jewelry and jade are recognized by the CMA report). For fortune telling with money, see Article 15 of this section (Fortune Telling Tarot Horoscopes).

items.title: Don’t expect buying things to improve your mood or sense of identity
items.core: The more important people value money and material things, the less happy they feel, but the connection is very weak, and it is impossible to tell who is causing whom. Other studies have found that spending money on an experience makes people happier than buying things. So for the same amount of money, spending on an experience like going out is more likely to make people happy than filling up a shopping cart.
body: Cost: No money. The hard thing is not to place an order when you are in a bad mood.

Benefits: A meta-analysis (aggregating many studies) with 259 independent samples and 753 effect sizes. The result: The more materialistic people value things, the lower their self-reported happiness is. On the most commonly used kind of multidimensional scale, the correlation coefficient r = -0.19 (corrected ρ = -0.24). On the scale that measures only the aspect of "paying attention to money," the correlation is even weaker, r = -0.08 to -0.11. Depending on what kind of results you are looking at, the strengths and weaknesses are different. The strongest correlations were with risky health and consumption behavior and negative evaluation of oneself, r = -0.28 to -0.44. The weakest correlations were with life satisfaction and negative emotions, r = -0.13 to -0.15. The author also conducted a mediation analysis (finding what passed through the middle), and the results suggested that this negative correlation may be due to unsatisfied psychological needs. Another study: In two surveys of different groups, respondents said spending money on life experiences made them happier than buying things. In subsequent laboratory experiments, recalling a good mood after spending money on an experience was also higher than recalling a purchase (the national scale is not applicable, both items use foreign samples)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Dittmar H, Bond R, Hurst M, Kasser T (2014). The relationship between materialism and personal well-being: A meta-analysis. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 107(5), 879-924. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0037409>; Van Boven L, Gilovich T (2003). To do or to have? That is the question. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 85(6), 1193-1202. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.85.6.1193>

Note: Controversy: Most of the included studies asked a group of people at the same time point to see if two things were synchronized, and it was impossible to tell who came first and who came last. The author himself also said in the conclusion that more experiments and long-term follow-up studies are needed to see the direction clearly. Therefore, it cannot be read as "Buying things will make people unhappy", it can only be read as "There is little hope of becoming happy by buying things." And the correlation is weak: r = -0.19 probably explains only a few percentage points of the variation, which varies greatly from person to person. Both studies used foreign samples, and there is no similar data that can be quoted for the Chinese population. There is nothing against spending money on things you like. What is against using shopping as a means to regulate your mood, because that will make your first reaction the next time you are in a bad mood still be to place an order. See Section 5 for specific actions to save money. For a truly evidence-based approach when you are in a bad mood, see the second half of verse 22 and verse 29. For the budget added to "be one step better than others", see Article 24 of this section (move up one step).

Case: Xiao Zhou felt depressed after working overtime continuously. He impulsively bought limited edition sneakers and expensive skin care products. He was very excited when he opened the package, but the feeling of emptiness returned a few days later. At the end of the year, she used the same money to go hiking and camping with her best friend. The memories of that shared experience still make her feel warm.

items.title: Don’t spend more money to change houses, cars, or circles just to “move up a notch among the people around you.”
items.core: Comparing people with the same income, the more your neighbor earns, the lower the happiness reported by this person. This mainly happens to neighbors who have the same academic qualifications as themselves, and it is more obvious for people who often interact with their neighbors. So the extra money you spend to move into a place where everyone has more money than you buy is moving you down a notch. But when incomes rise together, people still feel better off.
body: Cost: No money. All I have to do is ask one more question before adding a budget: Is this increase buying the thing itself, or is it my position in this group of people. The difficulty lies in not following suit when everyone around you changes.

Income: The U.S. National Survey of Families and Households (NSFH) interviewed the same people in two rounds. The author compared this data with local average income. Average local income (PUMA) is derived from the 1990 Census 5% sample. After deducting one's own income and a series of personal characteristics, the result is: the higher the neighbor's income, the lower the self-reported happiness. This effect is large, even if another algorithm is used, it is stable and highly significant. The author’s statement is that the decrease in happiness caused by “an increase in neighbor’s income” and “a similar decrease in own income” are of the same order of magnitude. After changing to compare myself with myself before and after the same person (this is called adding individual fixed effects), the direction of the coefficient remains unchanged and the size is similar, but the significance drops to the 10% level. Restricting the comparison to the same state and the same survey round (this is called the fixed effect of California and survey round), the results are basically unchanged. This shows that it is not caused by "people who tend to move to poorer areas are inherently happier", nor is it caused by some unmeasured factors at the state level. The effect was stronger among people who frequently interacted with neighbors and was not significant among people who only interacted with friends outside the community. There is no difference between people who rent a house and those who own a house. This does not support the explanation that "the housing prices in your place are high, so the actual money you can spend is less." Happiness only decreases with the income of neighbors with the same education and has almost no response to the income of neighbors with different education. And it is mainly transmitted through "satisfaction with one's material situation", not through satisfaction with other aspects such as family life. Finally, if the income of myself and my neighbors rises in the same proportion, happiness still rises
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Luttmer EFP (2005). Neighbors as Negatives: Relative Earnings and Well-Being. The Quarterly Journal of Economics, 120(3), 963–1002. <https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/120.3.963>; Luttmer EFP (2004). Neighbors as Negatives: Relative Earnings and Well-Being. NBER Working Paper No. 10667 (The expressions and magnitudes quoted in this article are checked verbatim according to this edition). <https://www.nber.org/papers/w10667>

Note: There are several reasons for rating B: the data comes from questionnaires that repeatedly interviewed the same group of people. In this study alone, the sample is abroad. The results we look at are the respondents' self-reported happiness, not money. The author did use statistical methods to eliminate several types of interference, such as before-and-after comparisons of the same person, and comparisons between the same state and the same round, but after all, it was not a randomized experiment. There is no similar data that can be cited for the Chinese population. The income level is set as "medium", which follows the standard of Article 23 of this section (don't expect to buy things to improve your mood). The money saved may indeed amount to tens of thousands of dollars. However, there is no numerical support for "how much happiness can be gained by saving this money", so it is not recorded as "big" on a 10,000-yuan scale. There is no objection here to spending money on a bigger house, a quieter neighborhood, a shorter commute, those are the purchases themselves. What stops me is the reason "My colleagues have all changed, I can't be worse than them". See Section 4, Item 18 for the order of accommodation (put commuting time first when choosing accommodation). See item 23 of this section for buying things to improve your mood (don’t expect buying things to improve your mood). Comparisons on the Internet, Chapter 3, Item 20 (Don’t treat “How are other people doing” as a daily must-read)

Case: My neighbor traded in a Porsche, so Xiao Li gritted his teeth and traded in a BMW. Later, he found that everyone on that street had replaced their cars, but he felt shorter. Later, he realized that among people with the same income, the richer their neighbors were, the lower their happiness was, and that money bought them a step down.

items.title: Don’t believe that “willpower is like a muscle, it wears off after a while.”
items.core: The popular saying is: Do something that requires self-control first, and then it will be easier to lose power, so save your willpower. 23 laboratories and 2,141 people redid the experiment according to the same protocol, and the results were almost zero. Stop explaining yourself by saying "you ran out of willpower today", and don't spend money on courses that teach you how to build willpower.
body: Cost: No money. All that needs to be changed is a statement.

Benefits: A multilaboratory preregistered replication study with 23 laboratories and 2141 participants. They redid the sequential task paradigm according to Sripada et al.'s standardized protocol: first perform a task that consumes self-control, and then perform a second task that requires self-control. Summary results show that the ego depletion effect is small and the 95% confidence interval includes 0 (d = 0.04, 95% CI −0.07 to 0.15). Based on this, the author discusses whether the model that "self-control is a limited resource" is still valid. Another redo of the same preregistered protocol, 36 laboratories, 3531 people, had an effect size of d = 0.06, again too small to be counted.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Hagger MS, Chatzisarantis NLD, Alberts H, et al. (2016). A Multilab Preregistered Replication of the Ego-Depletion Effect. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 11(4), 546–573. <https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691616652873>; Vohs et al. (2021). A Multisite Preregistered Paradigmatic Test of the Ego-Depletion Effect. Psychological Science. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797621989733>

Remarks: If you want to drop the model "self-control is a resource that will be consumed", do not drop "people will be tired". Not sleeping enough and working continuously for too long will make people less efficient. That is another matter. It should be dealt with according to the sleep and working hours in Section 3. The approach that is truly supported by randomized trials is to change the environment and rewrite the method. See Section 4, Item 10 (move away what you don’t want to touch) and Section 4, Item 1 (written as "at what time, where, and do whatever you encounter"). It's still worth it to fix what you wear and eat because it costs next to nothing. What it saves is those few minutes and a few struggles, not willpower. Don’t expect it to make you judge better in the afternoon. The other entries in this section count money, but here they count time and energy, and there is no conversion between the two.

Case: Xiao Li controlled his appetite and did not eat dessert in the morning. When faced with a milk tea invitation from a colleague in the afternoon, he broke the habit and overeated on the grounds that he had "exhausted his willpower". Later, he participated in a repeated experiment and found that the so-called 'self-depletion' effect was almost zero, and he no longer used this theory to make excuses for indulgence.

items.title: Don’t expect breakfast or 16:8 light fasting to help you control your weight, choose a meal time that you can stick to for a long time
items.core: The popular saying is that skipping breakfast will make people overeat at lunch and dinner, and eat more in a day. This was not the case in a short trial of several weeks: People who skipped breakfast ate more than 200 fewer calories a day and weighed slightly less. 16:8 Compared with simply eating less, there is no difference in weight after one year. People who skip breakfast for a long time have more cardiovascular disease, but there is only a correlation, and there is no difference in the overall mortality rate.
body: Cost: No money. What you save is the mental effort of competing with meal time every day.

Benefits: Let’s first look at the statement “Skipping breakfast will make you eat more later.” One meta-analysis combined 13 randomized trials. People assigned to the breakfast group consumed 259.79 kcal more per day than those in the no breakfast group (95% CI 78.87–440.71, confidence range). Body weight is 0.44 kg higher (0.07–0.82). People who skipped breakfast didn’t make up for it at lunch or dinner. The trials were all followed for a short period of time, looking at weight for an average of 7 weeks and intake for an average of 2 weeks. Look at 16:8, the practice of only eating within a set number of hours. One study was conducted in 116 overweight adults for 12 weeks. The weight difference between the group that only ate from 12 noon to 8 pm and the group that ate three regular meals a day was −0.26 kg (−1.30 to 0.78), which was not significant. Another study was done in Guangzhou, with 139 obese patients followed for 12 months. Time-restricted eating plus caloric control resulted in 1.8 kg (−4.0 to 0.4) more weight loss than caloric control alone, which was also not significant. Finally, let’s see if skipping breakfast for a long time is harmful. In a pool of 2.38 million people, people who skip breakfast are more likely to suffer from cardiovascular disease, with an odds ratio OR of 1.17 (1.09–1.26). There were also more deaths from cardiovascular disease, odds ratio OR 1.49 (1.20–1.84). But these were studies that only recorded, not grouped. In the original study, which followed for 17 to 23 years, the hazard ratio for all-cause death was 1.19, with a confidence range of 0.99 to 1.42, which crosses 1 and is not considered a difference.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Sievert K, Hussain SM, Page MJ, et al (2019). Effects of breakfast on weight and energy intake: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. BMJ. Metabolic Parameters in Women and Men With Overweight and Obesity. JAMA Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2020.4153>; Liu D, Huang Y, Huang C, et al (2022). Calorie Restriction with or without Time-Restricted Eating in Weight Loss. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2114833>; Zhang H, Zhang S, Liu Y, et al (2025). The association between skipping breakfast and cardiovascular disease: a meta analysis. Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine. (2019). Association of Skipping Breakfast With Cardiovascular and All-Cause Mortality. Journal of the American College of Cardiology. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2019.01.065>; Fernandes-Alves D, Teixeira GP, Guimarães KC, Crispim CA (2026). Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials Comparing Time-Restricted Eating With and Without Caloric Restriction for Weight Loss. Nutrition Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1093/nutrit/nuaf053>; Sun T, Zhang L, Lu Y, et al. (2024). Non-linear relationship between the first meal time of the day and gallstone incidence in American adults. Frontiers in Nutrition. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fnut.2024.1521707>; Liu T, Wang Y, Wang X, et al (2023). Habitually Skipping Breakfast Is Associated with the Risk of Gastrointestinal Cancers: Evidence from the Kailuan Cohort Study. Journal of General Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11606-023-08094-7>; National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (2022). Symptoms & Causes of Peptic Ulcers (Stomach or Duodenal Ulcers) ("The most common causes of peptic ulcers are Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)."). <https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/peptic-ulcers-stomach-ulcers/symptoms-causes>

Note: Controversy. The two cardiovascular odds ratios came from studies that only recorded and did not group groups. People who skip breakfast are inherently more likely to smoke, drink alcohol, sit for long periods of time, and have low incomes, and these factors cannot be corrected cleanly. So it’s unclear how much of this correlation is due to the breakfast itself. Death from all causes would have crossed 1. 16:8 is also controversial. One article summarized 30 trials and 1,341 people. Under the premise that both groups ate the same amount, the group who ate during the time-restricted diet lost 1.46 kg more (−2.65 to −0.26). The cost is an additional 0.41 kg of lean body mass. But most of these trials were short, and the longest and most rigorous twelve-month trial said there was no difference. Prolonged fasting is also related to the gallbladder. In a cross-sectional survey of 6,547 people, the odds ratio of detecting gallstones within an hour of the first meal of the day was OR 1.05 (1.02–1.08). Compared with those who delayed their first meal until 9:00 to 14:00 compared with those who ate earlier, the odds ratio was OR 1.49 (1.24–1.77). The mechanism is that the longer bile is stored in the gallbladder, the easier it is to precipitate stones. However, this was a survey conducted at the same time, and it is possible that the eating habits were changed after the gallbladder problem first occurred. The Kailuan cohort in China was followed for 5.6 years and recorded 369 cases of gastrointestinal cancer. People who skipped breakfast had a 2.32-fold (1.34–4.01) risk of colorectal cancer and a 5.43-fold (1.34–21.93) risk of gallbladder and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The credible range of the latter number is as wide as 21.93, indicating that there are too few events and can only be used as clues. Taken together, when it comes to weight control, mealtime has a very small impact, so don’t worry about it. As for whether it is better to skip breakfast altogether for a long time, the existing evidence is all correlation and cannot prove cause and effect, but the direction is consistent and unfavorable. If you want to be on the safe side, eat normally, but don't expect it to help you lose weight. The popular science page of the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases states that the most common causes of gastric ulcers are Helicobacter pylori infection and painkillers such as aspirin and ibuprofen. Fasting is not among the other rare causes listed. For what should be checked, see Section 1, Article 23 (check for Helicobacter pylori, eradicate if positive). What to do if gallbladder stones are detected during a physical examination but you never experience pain. See Article 20 of this section (If gallbladder stones are detected during a physical examination but you never experience pain, do not perform preventive gallbladder removal). When it comes to weight control, the real evidence is about what and how much you eat, see Section 2, Item 27 (Eat enough fruits and vegetables a day), Section 2, Item 28 (Eat less ultra-processed foods), and Section 2, Item 32 (Keep your BMI between 20–25). It is not suitable for people with diabetes, those taking anti-diabetic drugs, or those who are pregnant. Missing a meal may lead to hypoglycemia, so follow your doctor's advice. Extreme fasting and vomiting are another matter, see Section 28, No. 1 (Do not use extreme dieting, fasting, or vomiting to control weight).

Case: Xiao Chen, who adheres to the 16:8 light fast and only eats at noon and evening every day, has almost no weight change in a year. She gave up the rule and switched to eating three meals a day. Half a year later, due to her long-term persistence and proper control of total calories, she gradually lost five pounds and her overall mental state was better.

items.title: Don’t believe that “masturbation harms the body” or “rebooting can make you better.” What really matters is whether it delays sleep, work, and relationships.
items.core: I haven’t seen any evidence that masturbation harms the body. Men who ejaculate frequently are about 20% less likely to develop prostate cancer, but some studies have shown that men who ejaculate frequently in their youth are at higher risk. A few people feel weak every time they ejaculate, like a cold, and it takes a few days to get better. This is a rare disease, and you can go to a urologist or andrology department. I feel that I am "addicted to watching pornography" mostly because it conflicts with my own moral values.
body: Cost: Nothing. What is saved is the money spent on "kidney-tonifying" remedies and "rehabilitation" courses, as well as the anxiety of long-term self-blame.

Benefits: Look at the body first. A US study followed 31,925 men through 2010. Individuals self-reported how many times they ejaculated per month and were grouped by frequency. The HR for prostate cancer was 0.81 (95% CI 0.72–0.92, approximately 19% lower) for those who reported 21 or more times per month compared with those who reported 4 to 7 times per month. This is based on times between ages 20 and 29. HR 0.78 (0.69–0.89, about 22% lower) for times at age 40 to 49 years. What is lost is mainly low-risk prostate cancer. The opposite was a British case-control study that compared 431 patients diagnosed before the age of 60 and 409 controls. People who masturbate frequently in their twenties and thirties are at higher risk, and people who masturbate frequently in their fifties are at lower risk. Watch porn again. A systematic review and meta-analysis concluded that many people feel that they are "addicted" because their behavior does not match the truth they believe in, not just because they watch too much. A few people do feel uncomfortable every time they ejaculate, but this is not a "body injury" but a rare disease called post-ejaculation syndrome (POIS). If you have it, you should see a doctor, not rely on rebooting. Among 45 patients in the Netherlands, 87% became ill within 30 minutes of ejaculation, 80% felt tired and had no energy, and 78% felt like they had a cold. Thirty-seven patients at a French hospital took an average of 4.7 days to recover. The cause is not clear. In the Dutch study, 29 of 33 people (88%) who took skin tests were allergic to their own semen. A study of 24 patients in China found no allergic antibodies to semen, and the patients had high anxiety and depression scores. A 2025 review found only 14 treatment studies, 12 of which were individual cases. Only 18% of 211 sexual medicine experts around the world said that more than 30% of patients can get better (US/UK/Netherlands/France/China)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Rider JR, Wilson KM, Sinnott JA, et al. (2016). Ejaculation Frequency and Risk of Prostate Cancer: Updated Results with an Additional Decade of Follow-up. European Urology, 70(6), 974–982. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eururo.2016.03.027>; Dimitropoulou P, Lophatananon A, Easton D, et al. (2009). Sexual activity and prostate cancer risk in men diagnosed at a younger age. BJU International, 103(2), 178–185. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1464-410x.2008.08030.x>; Grubbs JB, Perry SL, Wilt JA, Reid RC. (2019). Pornography Problems Due to Moral Incongruence: An Integrative Model with a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Archives of Sexual Behavior, 48(2), 397–415. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10508-018-1248-x>; Waldinger MD, Meinardi MM, Zwinderman AH, Schweitzer DH. (2011). Postorgasmic Illness Syndrome (POIS) in 45 Dutch caucasian males: clinical characteristics and evidence for an immunogenic pathogenesis (Part 1). The Journal of Sexual Medicine, 8(4), 1164–1170. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1743-6109.2010.02166.x>; Chea M, Teng M, Chesnel C, et al. (2023). Postorgasmic illness syndrome: one or several entities? A retrospective cohort study. The Journal of Sexual Medicine, 20(12), 1407–1413. <https://doi.org/10.1093/jsxmed/qdad139>; Xi GP, Yang RX, Zhang J, et al. (2023). Clinical characteristics, allergic response to autologous semen, and desensitization in patients with postorgasmic illness syndrome. Sexual Medicine, 11(6), qfad068. <https://doi.org/10.1093/sexmed/qfad068>; Ponce S, Chapalamadugu M, Levine S, et al. (2025). Treatments for postorgasmic illness syndrome: a systematic review. The Journal of Sexual Medicine, 22(7), 1236–1243. <https://doi.org/10.1093/jsxmed/qdaf112>; Duran MB, Rubin RS, Reisman Y, Serefoglu EC, et al. (2025). Recognition and practice patterns of sexual medicine experts towards postorgasmic illness syndrome. International Journal of Impotence Research, 37(6), 454–457. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41443-023-00753-x>

Note: Controversy. Both studies on prostate cancer were only records, without group control, and the times were recalled by myself, so the conclusion can only be that "no evidence of harm to the body was seen", and cannot be used to persuade people to do more. The author of the British study himself said that the period in his fifties may have been due to illness first and then less frequency. The abstract of the porn article did not give an effect size, so only the direction is included here. The benefit is set to be small because the reduction is mainly due to low-risk prostate cancer, not death. The studies on post-ejaculation discomfort have only included dozens of patients. The literature says this disease is rare, but no one has counted how many people have it in the general population. Almost every time after ejaculation, I feel like I have a cold, and it takes a few days to get better. I go to the urology department or andrology department and mention the name of the disease. The real signs that you should go to a psychiatrist or psychological department are: staying up late because of it, missing work, affecting your relationship with your partner, and being unable to stop even if you want to. Stay up late to see Section 3, Item 9 (don’t stay up late for games, short videos, or pornographic content). If you are worried that you may have erection problems due to watching porn, you should first check it out according to Section 1, Item 28 (If there is a problem with erectile function, check cardiovascular disease first). For the legal consequences of sending or selling resources to the group, see Section 9, Article 4 (pornographic videos are yours to watch). The beneficiary is yourself.

Case: Xiao Liu, a college student, was influenced by online articles and firmly believed that 'only by abstaining from sex can you get better'. Due to his occasional masturbation, he fell into deep self-denial and shame, which even affected his sleep. After consulting a psychiatrist, he understood that what he should really focus on was whether he was delaying his normal work and study, rather than moral anxiety.

items.title: Don’t spend money on “sexual orientation correction” or “homosexuality therapy”, and don’t send your family members there
items.core: After reading the research, an expert group from the American Psychological Association said that most of this type of correction cannot change sexual orientation and may even hurt people.
