items.title: Code written during working hours and using company resources belongs to the company. You can use your own open source projects on your own time and equipment without mixing company code.
items.core: For software that is mainly written using the company's equipment, intranet or business data and is the responsibility of the company, the copyright belongs to the company. You only retain the right to authorize it, and the same is true as stipulated in the contract. Written after get off work, as long as the company computers or business data are used, it may also be considered company-owned. For inventions made primarily using company resources, the patents also belong to the company.
body: Cost: No money. When joining the company, read the intellectual property clauses in the employment contract clearly. The difficulty is that personal projects and company work are often mixed on the same computer and must be separated

Benefits: Works created to complete work tasks for the unit are job works (things made while working at work). Under normal circumstances, the copyright belongs to the author, and the organization has the right to priority use within the scope of business, and the author shall not allow a third party to use it in the same way within 2 years. But there are two types of situations that are different. The first category is engineering design, software and other works that are mainly created using the material and technical conditions of the unit and for which the unit is responsible. The other category is works that are contractually stipulated to belong to the unit. These two types of authors retain only the right of authorship. The physical and technical conditions of the unit refer to the company's equipment, intranet, business data, etc. Inventions and creations that are performed to perform the tasks of the unit, or are mainly completed by utilizing the material and technical conditions of the unit, are service inventions. The right to apply for a patent and the patent rights obtained belong to the unit (nationwide)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (2020). Copyright Law (Amended in 2020, Article 18). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796.html>; National People's Congress Standing Committee (2020). Patent Law (amended in 2020, Article 6). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308800.html>

Note: Software is directly written into the category of "copyright belongs to the unit", and programmers hardly fall into the category of "copyright belongs to the author, and the unit has priority for use within two years". "Written after get off work" as long as the company computer, intranet or company business data are used, it may be counted as mainly relying on the unit's equipment and data. If you want to complete your personal project cleanly, use your own machines, do not touch the company warehouse, and do not overlap with the company's business.

Case: A programmer uses the company computer to call business data to write personal open source tools after get off work, and uploads it to GitHub after leaving the company. The company submitted development records and data usage evidence to defend its rights. The tool code was deemed to belong to the company, and he only retained his signature.
items.sourceUrl: https://github.com/eternity4719/HowToLiveBetter/blob/main/book/11-程序员和技术人容易踩的红线.md

items.title: Use open source code such as GPL to make products, open source or change the license according to the license requirements, and improperly "no one cares"
items.core: Infringement of copyright, compensation based on the other party's losses or the money you earn. If it is intentional and the circumstances are serious, the penalty can be 1 to 5 times. One company recruited former employees of an opponent to make essentially similar software, arguing that the other party's software used GPLv2 and should have been open source. The Supreme People's Court held that the other party's failure to open source would not affect its copyright, and still sentenced the infringement to a halt and compensated it with a compensation of 500,000 yuan.
body: Cost: Nothing. Before using someone else's open source code, take a look at its license (the conditions of use stated by the author). GPL requires that the source code of products using it must be released. If it conflicts with closed source selling for money, change it to another one. The difficulty lies in letting go of a library that is already in use.

Income: Infringement of copyright will be compensated based on the actual loss of the rights holder, or based on the money earned by the infringer. If you can't calculate both of these, it will be determined based on how much you would normally pay to buy this license. If the infringement is intentional and the circumstances are serious, the compensation may be 1 to 5 times the amount. If the public interest is harmed, the illegal gains may also be confiscated and fined. Official case: (2021) Supreme Court Zhiminzhong No. 51. The defendant recruited former employees of the plaintiff and developed gateway software that was substantially similar to the plaintiff's software. The defendant argued that the plaintiff's software was based on GPLv2 and should have been open source. The Supreme People's Court determined that "whether the developer himself violated the GPLv2 agreement and whether he or she enjoys software copyright are two independent issues" and ordered to stop the infringement and compensate the developer 500,000 yuan (nationwide)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (2020). Copyright Law (2020 amendment, Articles 53 and 54). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796.html>; Intellectual Property Court of the Supreme People's Court (2022). Case involving copyright infringement of "open source software" ((2021) Supreme People's Court Zhiminzhong No. 51). <https://ipc.court.gov.cn/zh-cn/news/view-3042.html>

Note: This case illustrates that "the other party used GPL code" cannot be used as a reason for you to copy it. On the other hand, GPL authors have sued commercial parties that do not open source, and there have been effective judgments in China. The original text of this section cannot be found on the Supreme Judge website, so it is not quoted. The reason for the B grade is that compliance with the open source license can only be controlled by the general provisions of the contract and copyright law, and there is no specific law.
items.sourceUrl: https://github.com/eternity4719/HowToLiveBetter/blob/main/book/11-程序员和技术人容易踩的红线.md

items.title: Only the personal information necessary for business will be collected when making an app. Those under 14 years old must have their guardian's consent. The privacy policy must be clearly written
items.core: Only the personal information necessary for business will be collected. Those under 14 years old must have their guardian's consent. Violators will be ordered to make corrections first, and the App may be suspended. Those who refuse to make corrections will be fined up to 1 million yuan, and those responsible will be fined 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. Serious fines of less than RMB 50 million or less than 5% of the previous year's turnover may be imposed, and the responsible person may be fined RMB 100,000 to RMB 1 million.
body: Cost: No money. Before going online, review the permission list and privacy policy applied for by the App, and don’t ask for permissions that you can’t use. The difficulty is that the product always wants to leave some more data that "may be used in the future"

Benefits: The processing of personal information should have a clear and reasonable purpose, be directly related to this purpose, and adopt a method that has the least impact on personal rights and interests. The processing of personal information requires the consent of the individual or meets legal circumstances. Before processing, tell the user several things in a prominent way and in clear and understandable language. You need to tell who you are, how to contact you, what information is collected, what is used for it, how to process it, how long it is stored, and how users can exercise their rights. It is informed by a processing rule (often referred to as a privacy policy). The rules should be public and easy to view and save. Those under 14 years of age must obtain parental or guardian consent. In case of violation, the regulatory authorities will order corrections, issue warnings, confiscate illegal gains, and order illegal apps to suspend or terminate services. Those who refuse to make corrections will be fined up to 1 million yuan, and the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel will be fined 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. In serious cases, a fine of less than 50 million yuan or less than 5% of the previous year's turnover may be imposed. Those responsible are fined 100,000 to 1 million yuan. These people may also be prohibited from serving as directors, supervisors, or senior executives of relevant companies within a certain period of time. If selling or providing personal information constitutes a crime, see Article 4 (National)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2021). Personal Information Protection Law (Articles 6, 13, 31, 66). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088.html>; National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2021). Personal Information Protection Law (Article 17: "Before processing personal information, personal information processors shall truly, accurately and completely inform individuals of the following matters in a conspicuous manner and in clear and easy-to-understand language"; "If personal information processors inform individuals of the matters specified in paragraph 1 by formulating personal information processing rules, the processing rules shall be made public and easy to review and save"). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088.html>

Note: The law does not specify which positions are referred to by "other directly responsible personnel". The author infers that people who write code and make products may also be counted. This book does not find any cases that can be verified verbatim. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology regularly notifies the removal of illegal apps. This section has not verified which period the notification is, so it will not be quoted.

Case: A children's learning app forces access to address books and precise locations when registering, and also collects mobile phone numbers of students under 14 years old without guardian consent. After the parents complained, the supervisor ordered rectification, but they were fined if they refused to make corrections.
items.sourceUrl: https://github.com/eternity4719/HowToLiveBetter/blob/main/book/11-程序员和技术人容易踩的红线.md

items.title: ICP filing is required before websites and apps go online, and logs must be kept for more than 6 months according to the level of protection requirements
items.core: There is no fee for filing. Domestic servers that fail to file and refuse to make corrections will be shut down. If the registration says there is no charge but actually collects money, the fine will be 3 to 5 times the illegal income, or 100,000 to 1 million yuan. The log must be kept for six months. If you refuse to make corrections or have consequences, you may be fined RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000.
body: Cost: Registration is free, following the cloud vendor's process. The author's experience is that it takes a few days to a few weeks. Level protection assessments are charged based on level. Level protection, referred to as grade protection, is a set of security management actions that the state requires websites and systems to perform based on system importance.

Benefits: Commercial Internet information services are subject to licensing, and non-commercial Internet information services are subject to filing. Those who have not obtained a license or have not filed a record are not allowed to engage in business. Those who fail to register will be ordered to make corrections by the telecommunications management agency; those who refuse to make corrections will be ordered to close the website. Those who operate without a license will have their illegal gains confiscated and be fined 3 to 5 times the illegal gains, or a fine of 100,000 to 1 million yuan. If the registration number is not marked on the homepage of the website, a fine of 5,000 yuan to 50,000 yuan will be imposed. Network operators must develop a security management system based on the hierarchical protection system (level protection), prevent attacks, retain network logs for no less than 6 months, and classify and back up data for encryption. Those who fail to perform will be ordered to make corrections and given a warning. Those who refuse to correct or cause consequences will be fined 10,000 to 100,000 yuan, and those in charge will be fined 5,000 to 50,000 yuan (nationwide)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2011). Internet Information Services Management Measures (revised in 2011, Articles 4, 19, and 22). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1860864.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Cybersecurity Law (amended in 2025, effective on January 1, 2026, Articles 23 and 61; the 2016 text is Articles 21 and 59). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm>

Note: If the domestic server is not registered, the access provider will not allow you to access it. How to register, how much the penalty will be for not registering a registration number, and how to check whether the service provider is qualified, please see Section 26, Article 4 (servers must be registered if they are placed within the country). There are two real pitfalls: filing as personal non-business, but actually charging; changing the domain name or changing the entity, but not changing the filing. The author's opinion is that keeping a diary for 6 months is both an obligation and a self-protection. If something goes wrong, it can be used to prove that it was not you. Apps and mini-programs must also be registered before being put on the shelves. The method is in the same article.

Case: A local lifestyle website rented a domestic server but did not register ICP, and continued to go online even after being notified. During the inspection, it was found that the logs were only kept for 30 days, and the website was eventually shut down and fined.

items.title: Before providing generative AI services to the public, safety assessments and algorithm filings must be carried out in accordance with regulations, and generated content must be marked
items.core: Generative AI services that are oriented to the public and can influence public opinion or mobilize people must undergo security assessments and algorithm filings before going online. If they are changed or stopped, they must be changed or cancelled. The generated pictures and videos must be tagged. Don’t worry about these gadgets that you use yourself and are not open to the public. Violations will be punished according to the Cybersecurity Law and other laws.
body: Cost: It doesn’t cost any money, but it will take some time to go through the process of the Internet Information Department. As long as the tool does not provide services to the domestic public, this method does not apply

Benefits: To provide generative artificial intelligence services with public opinion attributes or social mobilization capabilities, security assessments must be conducted in accordance with national regulations. Algorithm filing, as well as subsequent changes and cancellation procedures must also be handled in accordance with the algorithm recommendation management regulations. Public opinion attributes or social mobilization capabilities refer to the ability to influence public opinion or the ability to organize and mobilize people. Providers should identify generated content such as images and videos. The Measures state that if enterprises, scientific research institutions, etc. develop and apply generative artificial intelligence technology, "if they do not provide generative artificial intelligence services to the domestic public, the provisions of these Measures shall not apply." Anyone who violates the measures will be punished "in accordance with the provisions of the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China, the Data Security Law of the People's Republic of China, the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, the Science and Technology Progress Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws and administrative regulations." The measures will come into effect on August 15, 2023 (nationwide)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Cyberspace Administration of China and seven other departments (2023). Interim Measures for Generative Artificial Intelligence Service Management (2, 12, 17, 21). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891752.htm>

Note: This method does not specify how much the fine will be. Violations will require penalties under the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, and Personal Information Protection Law, so it is graded B. This section has not verified the original text on the Supreme Judge website and does not cite civil cases involving the use of AI-generated content to infringe other people’s copyrights and portraits. For transfer stations that resell overseas large model interfaces at low prices, see Article 19 of this section (AI transfer stations).

Case: A company launched an AI face-changing applet for the public without conducting safety assessment and algorithm registration, and the exported video was not labeled. After regulatory inspections, they are required to be removed from the shelves for rectification and punished in accordance with the law.

items.title: If you don’t make or distribute a tool that automatically skips or blocks ads from other apps, you may be accused of unfair competition for free.
items.core: If you make software that skips or blocks ads from other apps for users, you may be sued for unfair competition by the other party. It may be considered even if you don’t charge money, and the operators covered by the law include individuals who provide services. Some browsers blocked Mango TV’s pre-roll ads by default, resulting in a loss of 800,000 yuan. There is an app that allows people to skip the opening ads of Mango TV, resulting in a loss of 80,000 yuan.
body: Cost: No money. The price is giving up a popular gadget. The difficulty is that you feel that you have not made any money, but you just clicked "Skip" for the user

Profit: The law stipulates that operators shall not use technical means to hinder or destroy the normal operation of network products or services legally provided by other operators. Operators here refer to natural persons, legal entities and unincorporated organizations that provide goods or services. If you cause damage to the other party, you will be compensated based on the other party's actual losses, or based on the benefits you received as a result, plus the other party's reasonable expenses to stop the infringement. The market supervision department can also impose a fine of 100,000 to 1 million yuan, and in serious cases, a fine of 1 million to 5 million yuan. Official case: 720 The built-in function of the browser blocks pre-title ads and pause ads on the Mango TV website by default. The first instance dismissed Mango TV’s lawsuit. The Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court changed the verdict in the second instance and determined that it constituted unfair competition and awarded compensation of RMB 800,000 in economic losses and reasonable expenses. In 2021, the Supreme Court listed it as a typical case. The “Block Wizard” App allows users to directly skip the opening screen advertisements of Mango TV. At first trial, the court ordered the defendant to pay 80,000 yuan in economic losses and 10,000 yuan in reasonable expenses. In April 2024, the Beijing Intellectual Property Court upheld the second instance. The second review held that it actually blocked open-screen advertisements, not just clicked "Skip" for users (National)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (revised in 2025). Anti-Unfair Competition Law (Articles 2, 13, 22, and 29). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181971552b40197b1016efc5437>; Supreme People's Court (2021). Typical anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition cases of the People's Court (Case 5: "720 Browser" Unfair Competition Dispute, (2018) Guangdong 73 Civil Final No. 1022). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/324491.html>; Beijing Political and Legal Network (2024-04-18). "Mango TV" sued "Ban Elf" for unfair competition and won the second instance (Source: Beijing Legal Network). <https://www.bj148.org/sa1/ajbb/202404/t20240418_1664299.html>; "Finance" client (2023-09-10). App blocks open-screen advertisements, and Tencent issued a lawyer's letter requesting its removal. Is it reasonable? (Finance E Law Fan Rui). <https://www.mycaijing.com/article/detail/500930?source_id=40> (Webpage archive <https://web.archive.org/web/20261005041658/https://www.mycaijing.com/article/detail/500930?source_id=40>)

Note: The two judgments used the provisions before the amendment. After the revision in 2025, this article was moved to Article 13, and data, algorithm and platform rules were also added. The court of second instance ruled that it was blocking, and users who clicked "Skip" would not be affected. In August 2023, “Li Tiaodiao”, a free ad-skipping tool on Android, received a letter from Tencent’s lawyer. The lawyer's letter said that it had blocked advertisements on Tencent Browser, which constituted unfair competition, and ordered it to be removed from the shelves within 48 hours. The developers say it is for public benefit and not profitable, and reports say it only accepts sporadic rewards. But it still announced that it would suspend updates indefinitely, and several similar software also stopped. The matter was only reported by the media, and there was no prosecution or verdict. When individual developers receive a lawyer's letter, they must either stop or spend their own money to hire a lawyer to respond. Ordinary first-instance procedures are stipulated to be completed within 6 months, which can be extended, and the lawyer's fees are generally paid by oneself. I wrote a script just for myself, and I didn’t find any cases where I was held accountable. Those who sell ticket-grabbing software will lose money due to unfair competition, see Article 3 of this section (ticket-grabbing flash sale script). The beneficiary is yourself.
items.sourceUrl: https://github.com/eternity4719/HowToLiveBetter/blob/main/book/11-程序员和技术人容易踩的红线.md

items.title: Does not use the "AI transfer station" to resell overseas large model interfaces at low prices: a webmaster in Shanghai has been criminally detained
items.core: AI transfer station is a website that resells overseas large model interfaces at low prices. A webmaster in Shanghai said that he was criminally detained for 37 days for this reason. Now that he is out on bail pending trial, he will definitely be sentenced, and he has already returned compensation and returned the stolen goods. The Ministry of National Security also issued a reminder saying that some transfer stations do not have operating qualifications, and some even transfer user data abroad without permission.
body: Cost: No money. The price is to let go of a side job with a low threshold and good revenue. If you really want to do model aggregation, just take the right path. It will cost a lot of money and time to apply for a business license and receive officially authorized models

Benefits: The Ministry of National Security issued a risk warning in June 2026. It is suggested that the AI ​​relay station is a proxy layer sandwiched between users and official services of model manufacturers. Some transfer stations lack operating qualifications. Some have not obtained the compliance qualifications for data export and have not gone through the legal process of security assessment, so they transfer the data entered by users to overseas servers. Some also allow users to bypass restrictions on network access, official authorization and cross-border transmission. China News Weekly reported on a case in June 2026. In May 2026, a transit station manager in Shanghai issued a closure announcement in the technology community. He said that he was criminally detained by the Shanghai police for 37 days for illegally obtaining large model interfaces, and is now on bail pending trial. He said, "I will definitely be sentenced in the future." He had already returned the stolen goods and had to pay a fine. Reports say that this type of transfer station registers in batches or purchases subscription accounts for large overseas models, sets up servers overseas as a springboard, and then resells them to domestic users at low prices (nationwide/Shanghai)
Evidence level: C

Source: Ministry of National Security (2026). "AI transfer station" risks must be guarded against. <https://www.szzg.gov.cn/2026/xwzx/szkx/202606/t20260608_5331487.htm> (The official website of the Digital China Construction Summit reproduces the WeChat official account of the Ministry of National Security); China News Weekly (2026-06-22). AI transfer station faces a "storm" of rectification (reporter Meng Qian). <https://www.chinanews.com/cj/2026/06-22/10644787.shtml> (Web Archive <https://web.archive.org/web/20261005042903/https://www.chinanews.com/cj/2026/06-22/10644787.shtml>)

Remarks: There are only media reports and self-reports of the parties involved in this case. There is no verdict or police report. There is no official statement on what crime to prosecute. The specific charges and sentences circulated on the Internet come from lawyers’ articles and are not quoted in this book. Therefore, we cannot say that "being a transit center must be a crime." We can only say that some people have been criminally detained for this. For formal model aggregation, a business license is required to charge fees. See Section 26, Article 2 (chargeable websites require a license). Providing generative AI services to the public must be registered, see Article 17 of this section (Generative AI Security Assessment). There are legal conditions for transferring user data overseas, see Section 26, Article 10 (User Information Transfer Abroad). There are additional risks for persons using transfer stations, see Section 14, Article 10 (AI Transfer Stations). The beneficiary is yourself.

Case: A webmaster in Shanghai built an AI transfer station to resell overseas large model interfaces at low prices and collect membership fees. Because he had no operational qualifications and the data was transmitted through overseas channels, he was detained and returned the stolen goods.

items.title: If you don’t write, sell or distribute cracked patches, registration machines and cracked versions of the software, if you sell them for enough money, you will be charged with copyright infringement.
items.core: Registration code verification and dongle verification are all technical measures of the software. If you circumvent them without permission, even if you infringe, you will have to pay compensation if you don’t charge money. In order to make money to crack or sell cracking tools, earning 30,000 yuan or selling them for 50,000 yuan is enough to be sentenced, with the maximum sentence being 10 years. Someone made cracked dongles and sold them with pirated software. The three co-defendants were sentenced to 1 to 3 years and 2 months.
body: Cost: No money. The price is to let go of side businesses that can make money quickly, such as selling cracked versions, selling registration codes, and selling cracked dongles. Do not post cracked patches to forums or network disks. The difficulty is that cracking seems to be just a technical job, not like stealing

Profit: Let’s talk about civil matters first. Copyright law allows rights holders to add technical measures to their works. Technical measures are effective technologies, devices or components that prevent and restrict others from using works without permission. No one may deliberately avoid or destroy technical measures without the permission of the right holder. It is also prohibited to manufacture, import or provide relevant devices and components to the public in order to avoid technical measures. You are also not allowed to deliberately provide technical services for others to avoid technical measures. Computer software is a work, and any of these actions are considered infringements. The infringement must be stopped and losses must be compensated. The amount of compensation is calculated based on the actual loss of the right holder or the money you earn. If you can't figure it out, refer to the normal price to pay for a license. For intentional infringement and serious circumstances, the penalty will be 1 to 5 times. If the public interest is harmed at the same time, the copyright authorities may also confiscate the illegal gains. If the illegal business volume exceeds 50,000 yuan, a fine of 1 to 5 times that amount may be imposed. If the amount is less than 50,000 yuan or cannot be calculated clearly, a fine of not more than 250,000 yuan may be imposed. Let’s talk about criminal matters. The Criminal Law Amendment (11) includes "intentional avoidance or destruction of technical measures" as a crime of copyright infringement, provided that the purpose is to make a profit. If the illegal income is more than 30,000 yuan, or the illegal business amount is more than 50,000 yuan, he will be sentenced to not more than 3 years and be fined or only fined. Up to 10 times these amounts, the penalty is 3 to 10 years and a fine. Someone knowingly knows that someone else is committing a crime of copyright infringement and provides him with devices, components or technical services that are mainly used to circumvent or destroy technical measures. If the amount reaches the same threshold, he will also be prosecuted as this crime. Official Case 1: From March 2019 to July 2022, in order to make money, Liu Mousheng made his own “encryptor” that could circumvent software technical measures. He also copied pirated software and sold it along with dongles. His illegal business amounted to more than 1.06 million yuan. The Shanghai No. 3 Intermediate People's Court found that the circumstances were particularly serious and sentenced him to the crime of copyright infringement. The Supreme People's Procuratorate said this was the country's first copyright infringement case of "intentional avoidance or destruction of technical measures" after the implementation of the 11th Amendment to the Criminal Law. In April 2023, the Shanghai court sentenced the three defendants in this series of cases to 3 years, 2 months to 1 year, with partial probation, and fined 700,000 to 80,000 yuan. Official Case 2: Liu, a medical equipment repairman, spent 80,000 yuan in a QQ group to buy 50 sets of cracked dongles, and then resold them online for several thousand yuan each. Plug it in to bypass the medical device's authentication and enter the repair software. Shanghai Putuo Court sentenced him to one year and two months, suspended, and fined him 80,000 yuan. Official Case 3: Starting from May 2021, Xuzhou Li Moumou and others have been looking for someone to do cracking programs for game consoles and produce cracking devices for sale. The illegal business amount was more than 39 million yuan. In November 2024, 10 people were sentenced to 3 years and 6 months to 2 years and 6 months, with partial probation, and fines ranging from 11 million yuan to 1.5 million yuan (national)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (2020). Criminal Law Amendment (11) (Item 20, i.e., Article 217, Item 6 of the Criminal Law). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/202012/t20201227_503682.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Copyright Law (2020 Amendment, Article 3, Articles 49, 50, 53, and 54). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796.html>; Supreme People’s Court, Supreme People’s Procuratorate (2025). Interpretation of Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Intellectual Property Infringement (Fa Interpretation [2025] No. 5, Article 13). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202504/t20250424_693977.shtml>; Supreme People’s Court, Supreme People’s Procuratorate (2025). Typical cases of criminal protection of intellectual property rights (Case 6: Copyright infringement case of Liu Mousheng and Liu Mou). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202504/t20250424_693978.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2024). The Supreme People's Procuratorate: Guided the handling of the country's first "intentional avoidance or destruction of technical measures" copyright infringement case. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/2024zgjtzwlft/202402/t20240228_645416.shtml>; Procuratorate Daily (2023-04-18). Selling pirated dongles to unlock medical equipment security systems (reprinted from the Supreme Procuratorate’s official website). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202304/t20230418_611586.shtml>; National Copyright Administration (2025). Top ten cases of combating infringement and piracy nationwide in 2024 (Case 6: Case of copyright infringement by Li Moumou and others in Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province by destroying technical measures). <https://www.ncac.gov.cn/xxfb/ywxx/202508/t20250801_925366.html>

Note: The beneficiary is yourself. The copyright law leaves several loopholes: testing the security performance of computer systems and networks, conducting encryption research, and software reverse engineering research can avoid technical measures. However, the same article states that avoidance technology, devices or components must not be provided to others. So you can research it yourself, but you can’t send it out or sell it. Distributing crack patches for free is not a crime of copyright infringement, because this crime requires making money. However, civil infringement is still established, and the software company can send a lawyer's letter and sue you for compensation. The ordinary procedures for first-instance litigation are stipulated that the trial should be completed within 6 months, which can be extended. The lawyer's fees are generally paid by oneself. Putting the entire cracked version of the software online for people to download is considered as distributing the work without permission. The criminal threshold is found in Section 9, Article 24 (Sharing network disk resources). Game cheats bypass anti-cheating, see Article 2 of this section (Game cheats and auxiliaries).

Case: Three sellers made cracked patches for software dongles and sold pirated programs online, collecting tens of thousands of yuan. Three people were sentenced for copyright infringement after police seized the sales records.

items.title: Do not help others launch DDoS traffic attacks, do not sell or rent "stress testing" traffic platforms, and do not attack the other party's server if you lose in games
items.core: Using DDoS to prevent other people's websites, servers, and games from opening is considered a crime of damaging computer information systems. Those with serious consequences will be sentenced to less than 5 years, and those with particularly serious consequences will be sentenced to more than 5 years. Anyone who spends money to place an order for the platform to fight is also considered a joint crime. Someone opened a DDoS website to collect membership fees to receive orders, and was sentenced to 10 months to 5 years and 6 months.
body: Cost: No money. DDoS controls a large number of machines to send requests to the target at the same time, blocking the server until it cannot be used. The price is to let go of the pay-per-view and package-based business of selling traffic, and you have to hold back your anger for a while. If you have a conflict with someone in a game or in business, report, complain, or call the police. Don't spend money to find someone to fight.

Benefits: If the function of the computer information system is interfered with, causing the system to fail to operate normally, and the consequences are serious, the person will be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 5 years or criminal detention. If the consequences are particularly serious, the sentence will be more than 5 years. The court regarded DDoS as the "disruption" mentioned here. There are several criteria for "serious consequences". One is that the main software or hardware of more than 10 computer information systems cannot operate normally. One is illegal gains of more than 5,000 yuan, or economic losses of more than 10,000 yuan. There is also a system that provides services to more than 10,000 users and cannot operate normally for more than 1 hour in total. If the number of units and money is counted to 5 times these numbers, the consequences will be particularly serious. Knowing that others are engaging in such sabotage and yet providing them with procedures and tools for sabotage shall be punished as a joint crime. The threshold is illegal income of more than 5,000 yuan, or providing more than 10 people. The same applies to providing him with help such as server hosting and technical support, and illegal income of more than 5,000 yuan. Some people provide programs and tools specifically used to invade and illegally control computer information systems. If the crime is provided to more than 20 people, or the illegal income is more than 5,000 yuan, he will be sentenced to not more than 3 years and concurrently or solely fined. Those who are not serious enough to commit crimes, but those who interfere with the functions of computer information systems, provide such tools, and cause harm will be detained for less than 5 days, and if the circumstances are more serious, they will be detained for 5 to 15 days. Official Case 1 (Prosecution Case No. 69): In early 2017, Yao Xiaojie and others were hired to establish a "Dark Sky Team" overseas. They bought a large amount of server resources and used Trojan software to control them and launch DDoS. They attacked the IPs of three game companies on an Internet company's cloud server three times. The games were unable to be logged in and users were frequently disconnected. The injured company spent more than 40,000 yuan on repairs. In June 2018, the Shenzhen Nanshan Court sentenced 11 people to one to two years in prison for damaging computer information systems. Official Case 2: Tang and Wang built a DDoS website in March 2017, which allows members to recharge and submit attack tasks. They received orders to launch traffic attacks on more than 80 target IPs. Nantong Haimen Court sentenced Tang and others to 10 months to 5 years and 6 months for damaging computer information systems. Zhang, who placed an order on this website, submitted more than a hundred attack tasks to 11 IPs or domain names of peer companies in order to suppress his peers. The court found that the person who placed the order and the website operator were guilty of a joint crime. The person who placed the order is the one who initiated the order and is the principal offender. Official Case 3: Wang built a DDoS platform and sold attacks clearly based on "Bronze", "Silver", "Gold" and "Diamond" packages. He was prosecuted by the Beijing Haidian Procuratorate for the crime of illegal use of information networks. In 2020, the first trial lasted for 1 year and he was fined 50,000 yuan (national)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (amended according to the Criminal Law Amendment (11), Article 285, paragraph 3, Article 286, Article 287-1). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Supreme People’s Court, Supreme People’s Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation of Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Endangering the Security of Computer Information Systems (Fa Interpretation [2011] No. 19, Articles 2, 3, 4, 9, and 11). <https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html> (Reprinted by Shenzhen Municipal Public Security Bureau); National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2025). Public Security Management Punishment Law (revised in 2025, Article 33). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; Supreme People’s Procuratorate (2020). The 18th batch of guiding cases (Prosecution Case No. 69, Yao Xiaojie and 11 other people’s case of damaging computer information systems). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/jczdal/202004/t20200408_458415.shtml>; Jiangsu Provincial Higher People’s Court (2020-09-24). Jiangsu court released typical cases of crimes endangering network security (Case 2: Case of Tang Mou and others damaging computer information systems). <https://www.jsfy.gov.cn/article/91613.html>; People's Court News (2025-02-08). Conviction and sentencing of cyber attacks committed through DDoS websites (commentary and analysis of reference case 2024-18-1-254-001 in the People's Court case database, reprinted by Shandong Court Network). <http://www.sdcourt.gov.cn/dyzy/372897/372899/33201805/index.html>; Supreme People’s Procuratorate (2020). Beijing Haidian District: The suspect in the DDoS attack platform case was sentenced. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202009/t20200901_478510.shtml>

Note: The beneficiary is yourself. This type of platform is called "stress testing". Only when you test your own system, or a system that the other party has authorized you to test in writing, is it called a stress test. Hitting other people's servers is the same as Article 9 (not testing other people's systems without written authorization). Those who open platforms to take orders are not uniformly punished in different places. The Haimen case was sentenced to the crime of destroying computer information systems, with a maximum sentence of 5 years and 6 months; the Haidian case was charged with illegal use of information networks, and the sentence was 1 year. An analysis by the People's Court News said that judicial practice in such cases is inconsistent, and the case in the database classified it as a crime of damaging computer information systems. In Case No. 69, the Internet company that was attacked reported the case. The public security sent the electronic data it provided to the Guangdong Branch of the National Computer Network Emergency Response Technology Coordination Center for analysis, and found 14 console servers. Chat records and bank statements confirm the purchase of control of these servers. For selling Trojans that control other people's computers, see Article 8 of this section (do not run your own programs on other people's machines).

Case: Due to a losing streak in the game, a player paid to place an order on a certain platform to attack the opponent's server, causing the opponent's game to be suspended for several hours. The police traced the payment and traffic records, and both the orderer and the platform operator were held accountable.

items.title: Start a business with only the money you can afford to lose, without leaving any money or borrowing money to start a business
items.core: The money owed by a self-employed person must be paid back with money and things in your own name. If you can't tell if the whole family did it together, you can use the whole family's property to pay back. It is not safe to start a company: when the company is not repaying its debts, the creditor can ask you to withdraw the capital contribution that you originally promised but has not yet expired. Therefore, how much you invest should be determined based on the principle that "you can still pay off your mortgage and see a doctor even if you lose all your money."
body: Cost: No money. Before taking action, set a number for yourself: If you lose all your money, it will not affect your mortgage payments, raising children, or medical treatment. No investment will be made if the number exceeds this number. Family money and borrowed money are not included in this amount. The hard thing is to resist adding more money when your business seems to be improving.

Profit: Losing money is not just about losing money. For debts owed by individual industrial and commercial households, if you do the business alone, you must repay it with money and things in your own name (bear it as your personal property). If the whole family did it together, or if it is not clear who did it, the whole family’s money and things will be used to repay it (the family property will bear the responsibility). Debts signed by both husband and wife are considered joint debts repaid by both parties. If one party nods afterwards, it counts. If one party borrows money in his own name, as long as the creditor can prove that the money was used for the business the couple did together, the two people can still repay it together. The company also has one. The money that shareholders originally agreed to contribute in the registered capital is called subscribed capital contribution. When a company pays its due debts, the creditor can ask him to hand over the debts that have not yet reached the payment deadline in advance (national)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 56, 1064). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; National People's Congress Standing Committee (2023). Company Law (revised in 2023, Articles 47 and 54). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm>

Note: "You can afford to lose" means: you will lose all the money, and you don't have to sell the house or ask relatives to borrow money to repair the holes. How many companies can survive and how many years on average can they survive? This official statistics cannot be verified on the official websites of the National Bureau of Statistics and the State Administration for Market Regulation. Therefore, the text does not include numbers, only legal consequences, and is rated B.

Case: A couple used the 200,000 yuan they prepared to pay off their mortgage to open a snack bar, and used their credit cards to purchase goods. After the business suffered a loss and became insolvent, the creditors went after the family property, and the mortgage and living expenses were affected.

items.title: Don’t sign a personal guarantee for a company loan, let alone your spouse
items.core: Sign a “joint and several liability guarantee”. If the company doesn’t repay the money, the creditor can bypass the company and ask for it directly from you. You should file a "general guarantee" before suing the company first. After selling the company's property, it will be your turn to wait until the company's property is sold. If your spouse signs, the property of both people will be included together, and the "limited" of the limited company will not count for you personally.
body: Cost: No money. When banks, suppliers, or landlords ask you to sign a "shareholder personal guarantee" or a "spouse's signature," stop for a moment. By signing that page, you are giving up the protection of "the company's debts are not to be traced to anyone" (giving up limited liability). I won’t sign if I can’t. If you have to sign, just sign a "general guarantee" and write down the maximum amount of money you can guarantee. The difficulty is that the other party often says "no loan, no signing", so you have to stand up to it.

Income: The sentence in the guarantee means "If the person who owes you money doesn't pay it back, it's up to you to pay it back." If it is written as a "joint and several liability guarantee", the creditor can come to you directly to ask for it instead of going to the company. If it is written as a "general guarantee", the creditor must first sue the company or go to arbitration, and then ask the court to force the company's property to be sold to pay off the debt. How much less is left before everything is sold out, then it’s your turn to make up for it. Debts signed by both husband and wife are considered joint debts repaid by both parties. If one party nods afterwards, it counts. Once the spouse signs, the property of both people will be pooled together (National, starting from 2021)
Level of Evidence: A
Source: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 681, 687, 688, 1,064). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>

Remarks: The author’s experience is that banks often require individual shareholders to sign joint guarantees when lending to small and micro enterprises. No official statistics were found in this book. You can still get a loan, you just need to know what is signed on this page before signing. The amount of the guarantee should be within the amount you can “afford to lose” in Article 1 (use only money you can afford to lose to start a business). For general rules on IOUs and guarantees, see Section 8, Article 18.

Case: The boss asked a friend and his wife to sign a joint liability guarantee for a business loan of 500,000 yuan. The two thought they were just going through the process. After the company ceased operations, the bank directly sued the couple and the family account was frozen.

items.title: Choose the right entity before opening: self-employed individuals and partners will pay the full amount, and a limited company will be "limited"
items.core: Self-employed individuals and general partners will pay whatever they owe, and shareholders of a limited company will only pay the amount they promised when registering. But as much as you promised, you will have to pay out within 5 years: if you fill in 1 million, you may owe 1 million. If you mix company accounts with your own accounts, or use the company to hide debts, "limited" will also become invalid. If you are the only shareholder, you have to take out the accounts yourself to prove that there is no fraud.
body: Cost: Registration is done online at the local government service, which takes a few hours at a time. After opening a limited company, you have to keep accounts and file taxes every month. This is a long-term expense: it takes time to do it yourself, and it costs money to hire someone to do the accounting. The prices vary from place to place.

Income: The debts owed by individual industrial and commercial households must be repaid with personal money and things, or with the whole family's money and things. The partners of a general partnership bear unlimited joint and several liability for the debts of the partnership. This means that you have to pay whatever you owe, and it is not done until it is completed. The creditor can also seize only one of them and ask him to pay back the whole amount. A limited partnership is different. The limited partners in it will only pay out the money they promised to contribute (limited to their subscribed capital contribution). The shareholders of a limited liability company will only receive the amount of money they promised to pay (limited to the amount of capital they subscribed). But "limited" will fail in three situations. First, the promised money must be paid in full within 5 years of the company's establishment. When the company repays its due debts, the creditor can request payment in advance. Second, the money that has been invested and withdrawn (withdrawn capital) must be returned. The third is to use the company as a shell to avoid debts and seriously damage the interests of creditors. At this time, you personally have to repay the company's debts together (bearing joint liability). Companies with only one shareholder are even more strict: it is up to the shareholder to prove that the company's money and his own money are separate. If he couldn't prove it, he would have to repay the company's debt personally. The court mainly looks at whether money and accounts are not separated. Shareholders use the company's money casually without keeping accounts, and company accounts and personal accounts are not separated and are all lumped together (National, starting from July 2024)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 56). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; National People's Congress Standing Committee (2006). Partnership Enterprise Law (revised in 2006, Article 2). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2006/content_413955.htm>; National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2023). Company Law (2023 Revised in 2017, Articles 4, 23, 47, 53, and 54; Article 23, Paragraph 3: "For a company with only one shareholder, if the shareholder cannot prove that the company's property is independent of the shareholder's own property, he shall bear joint and several liability for the company's debts."). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm>; Supreme People's Court (2019). Minutes of the National Court Civil and Commercial Trial Work Conference (Point 10 "Confusion of Personalities"): "The most important manifestation is whether the company's property and the shareholder's property are mixed and indistinguishable." "The company's account books are not separated from the shareholder's account books, resulting in the company's property and the shareholder's property being indistinguishable." <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/199691.html>

Note: Company accounts and personal accounts should be used separately. Customer payments should not be received on personal cards. Company money should not be used to pay household expenses. Keep complete accounts. Don’t fill in big numbers for registered capital just to look good.

Case: Two people did not register a limited company when they opened a restaurant together. After a loss, the supplier sued. The two used their personal savings to pay off the purchase price; the other person who registered the company was only responsible for the amount subscribed.

items.title: Improperly named shareholder or holding shares on behalf of others
items.core: Once your name is registered in the register, you are legally a shareholder. The money promised during registration must be paid in full on time. If the payment is not made, the company will be compensated for losses in addition to making up the payment. When the company was founded, other shareholders didn't actually hand in the money, so you have to pay back the shortfall. The business is done by others, and the debt is in your name.
body: Cost: No money. Some people say "borrow your ID card to register as a shareholder" or "put the shares in your name first", but they all refuse.

Income: Registered shareholders are legal shareholders. You have to pay the money you promised to pay in small amounts according to the time limit specified in the company's articles of association (pay the subscribed capital in full). If you fail to pay on time, in addition to making up the payment, you will also have to compensate the company for losses. If a shareholder did not actually hand in the money when the company was founded, other shareholders at the time of the company would repay the money along with them (bearing joint and several liability). When the company fails to repay its due debt, the creditor can require the money that has not yet expired to be paid in advance. The real business person is not on the registration, but the debt is recorded in your name (National, starting from July 2024)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2023). Company Law (revised in 2023, Articles 47, 49, 50, 54). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm>; Supreme People’s Court (Amended in 2020). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the "Company Law of the People's Republic of China" (3) (Fa Interpretation [2011] No. 3, 2014 Fa Interpretation [2014] No. 2, 2020 Fa Interpretation [2020] No. 18 No. 2 amendments, Articles 24 and 25): "If there are no invalid circumstances stipulated by law, the people's court shall determine that the contract is valid." "The actual investor requests the company to change shareholders without the consent of more than half of the company's other shareholders... The people's court will not support it." "If the nominal shareholder's disposal of equity causes losses to the actual investor, and the actual investor requests the nominal shareholder to bear compensation liability, the people's court shall support it." <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181799def980179ac07a9ca117c> (National Laws and Regulations Database); Supreme People's Court (2025). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the "Company Law of the People's Republic of China" (Draft for Comments) Article 90. <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/477881.html>

Note: The holding agreement between the nominal shareholder and the person who actually contributed the money will be counted as long as there are no invalid circumstances. But if the person who actually contributed the money wants to change the name, more than half of the other shareholders must agree. If the named person sells or pledges the equity, the court shall refer to the good faith acquisition in the Civil Code to handle the matter. If the buyer is not informed, the price is reasonable, and the registration has been completed, the person who paid the money cannot get the equity back and can only ask the person in name to compensate. In September 2025, the Supreme People's Court issued a draft of the new interpretation for comments. After the new interpretation is finalized and implemented, this regulation will be abolished in its entirety. As of September 2026, the 2020 revised version is still effective, and this article shall prevail. Risks of nominal legal representative, see Section 8, Article 28.

Case: My cousin asked someone to be a named shareholder and promised not to contribute money or participate in the operation. Later, the company owed the supplier 800,000 yuan, and the creditor required the nominee to make up payment within the subscription amount, and the property under his name was traced.

items.title: Before joining, check the Ministry of Commerce for registration, obtain a written disclosure, and write the "cooling off period" into the contract
items.core: According to regulations, the brand owner must first open two directly operated stores and operate them for one year, and must go to the Ministry of Commerce for registration within 15 days after signing the contract. Before signing a contract, it must write down 12 items in writing to you, including the franchise fee, how to refund the deposit, and whether the existing store is profitable. If you can't find the record, refuse to provide materials, or ask for payment before being allowed to see the contract, just leave.
body: Cost: No money. Go to the "Commercial Franchise Information Management System" website of the Ministry of Commerce to check whether the brand owner has registered. Then ask the other party to write down the things that need to be explained to you in writing before signing the contract, together with the contract text. It can be done in a few hours.

Income: Regulations require brand owners (called franchisors in regulations) to have at least 2 self-opened and self-operated direct-operated stores that have been open for more than 1 year. Counting from the day when the franchise contract is first signed, it must be filed with the competent commercial department within 15 days. Failure to register will result in a fine of 10,000 to 50,000 yuan. Those who fail to register after the deadline will be fined 50,000 to 100,000 yuan and announced to the public. Before signing a contract, it must write down the things it needs to explain and hand them over to you in writing, 12 items in total. It includes what types of franchise fees are charged, how much each fee is, when the deposit will be refunded, how many franchise stores there are, and how the business is doing. There are also summaries of audit reports reviewed in the past two years, and lawsuits and arbitrations fought in the past five years. The contract must also state that within a period of time after signing the contract, the franchisee can withdraw at his own request (unilateral termination). If the brand owner conceals the truth or gives false information, the franchisee can terminate the contract (National, starting from May 2007)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2007). Regulations on Commercial Franchise Management (State Council Order No. 485, Articles 7, 8, 12, 22, 23, and 25). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_4179.htm>; Ministry of Commerce (2012). Measures for the Administration of Commercial Franchise Information Disclosure (Ministry of Commerce Order No. 2, 2012, Articles 5 and 9). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2012/content_2177025.htm>; Ministry of Commerce. Commercial Franchise Information Management System. <https://txjy.syggs.mofcom.gov.cn/>

Remarks: If you cannot find the record, refuse to give disclosure documents, or want to pay first and then read the contract, go directly. The "cooling off period" is the few days after signing a contract that you can withdraw at your own request. The number of days is determined by the contract. The regulations only say "a certain period of time", so the number of days is required to be written in when signing the contract. For the "average sales volume, gross profit, and net profit of existing franchise stores" disclosed by the brand, we need to ask where the numbers come from. The method requires the brand to explain the source. If it is not called franchising, but only charges service fees for "agents for operation" and "store opening training", see Article 24 (agents for operations and store opening training).

Case: The franchisee paid the milk tea franchise fee of 200,000 yuan without checking the business record or making a written disclosure. After opening the store, I discovered that the brand did not have two directly-operated stores that were more than one year old, and the contract did not include a cooling-off period, making refunds difficult.

items.title: Determine the name, business location, business scope and registered capital before registration, and you can get the license on the spot once the materials are complete
items.core: Registration itself costs nothing, and the registration fee has been suspended since 2015. Some people charge money, but it is not the registration fee. There are only five materials to be submitted: application form, proof of identity or qualifications, business location documents, articles of association or partnership agreement, plus those otherwise required by regulations. Once the materials are complete, the license will be issued on the spot. If the license cannot be issued on the spot, it will be completed within 3 working days. If it is complicated, it will take another 3 working days.
body: Cost: There is no cost to register. The registration fees for enterprises and individual industrial and commercial households will be stopped from January 1, 2015. You can do it yourself at the local government service website, or go to the government office for a few hours at a time. Engraving an official seal, hiring someone to keep accounts, and renting a registered address (address hosting) are services purchased in the market, not fees charged by the government.

Benefit: The regulations specify five items of materials to be submitted. "(1) Application form". "(2) Applicant qualification documents and natural person identity certificate." "(3) Documents related to residence or main place of business." "(4) Articles of association of a company, unincorporated enterprise legal person, farmer cooperative (union) or partnership agreement of a partnership enterprise." "(5) Other materials submitted as required by laws, administrative regulations and the market supervision and administration department of the State Council." Translated into vernacular: an application, a document proving who you are or that you are qualified to do this. Add another document that proves that the store or office belongs to you, as well as the articles of association or partnership agreement. Those who are specifically required by regulations must also be paid. The company must also submit the employment documents and identity certificates of its legal representatives, directors, supervisors and senior executives. Self-employed individuals do not need to submit articles of association. The name is "declared by the applicant independently in accordance with the law", and the name should be chosen and reported by oneself. The registered capital "implements a subscription registration system". You must first write down the amount you promise to pay, so you don't have to pay it out on the spot. The business scope is selected from the classifications announced by the registration authority. If the materials are complete and the format is correct, "confirm and register on the spot." If it cannot be completed on the spot, it will be completed "within 3 working days". If the situation is complicated, an additional 3 working days will be given. "The date of issuance of the business license is the date of establishment of the market entity": The day printed on the license is the date the company or store was established (nationwide, starting from March 2022)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2021). Regulations on the Registration and Management of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746, 10th, 13th, 14th, 16th, 19th, 21st). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5636139.htm> ; State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Implementation Rules of the Regulations on the Registration and Management of Market Entities (State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 52, Articles 12, 25, and 26). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-03/02/content_5676403.htm> ; Ministry of Finance, National Development and Reform Commission (2014). Notice on the cancellation, suspension and exemption of a batch of administrative fees (Finance and Taxation [2014] No. 101, Attachment 1). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2014-12/23/content_5023513.htm> ; General Office of the State Council (2018). Opinions on further reducing the start-up time of enterprises (Guobanfa [2018] No. 32, Part 2, Item 3). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-05/17/content_5291643.htm>

Note: There is no charge for registration itself. Some people collect money for market services such as agency services and seal engraving. The price of the engraving is determined by the market. The 2018 document from the General Office of the State Council stated that "applicants are free to choose the official seal production unit" and "designated official seal production units are strictly prohibited from producing official seals." Therefore, some people say that "the seal must be carved at a designated place." You do not have to accept it. Filling in the registered capital does not affect the appearance, it only determines the upper limit of your liability, and it must be paid in full within 5 years. See Article 3 of this section (choose the right entity before opening). Business scope with licensed items cannot be opened without a license. See Article 7 of this section (Businesses that require a license)

Case: Xiao Wang plans to open a milk tea shop. He has thought of the name in advance, rented the shop and obtained the lease contract, and clarified the business scope. He submitted all the complete materials on the APP and successfully received the business license that afternoon.

items.title: Businesses that require a license cannot be opened without a license
items.core: Opening without a license will be investigated and dealt with by the department in charge of the license according to its regulations. Those who do not even have a business license and no special penalties will be ordered to close their business, the money earned will be confiscated, and they will be fined up to 10,000 yuan. Selling specialized products, or doing securities, futures, insurance, or payment and settlement, if the circumstances are serious, it constitutes the crime of illegal business operations, and the minimum sentence is not more than 5 years.
body: Cost: No money. Before opening, check to see if the business you want to do requires a license. To cater or sell food, you need a food business license. Only sell packaged food made by others, no permission required, change to registration. Once the permit is issued, we will open for business.

Income: Anyone who opens his business without a license will be investigated and dealt with by the department designated by laws and regulations. If you operate without a license, and the law does not specify the penalties, you will be ordered to stop, the money earned (illegal income) will be taken away, and you will be fined no more than 10,000 yuan. There is also a heavier gear. Items that are franchised, sold exclusively, or restricted for sale or purchase and sale as stipulated by laws and regulations shall be operated without permission. Businesses such as securities, futures, insurance, and capital payment and settlement can be carried out without approval. These two situations, if the circumstances are serious, constitute the crime of illegal business operations. Sentence to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 5 years or short-term detention (short-term detention), and a fine of 1 to 5 times the amount of money earned. Sentences of more than 5 years for particularly serious cases (national)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2017). Measures for the Investigation and Punishment of Unlicensed and Unlicensed Business Operations (State Council Order No. 684, Articles 5, 6, and 13). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-08/23/content_5219861.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Measures for the Administration of Food Business Licensing and Registration (State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 78, Article 4). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10606/202307/content_6894763.html>; National People’s Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 225). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>

Note: Licensing conditions for finance, medical care, and education and training each have their own special laws. This article only verifies the general investigation rules and criminal law provisions. Milk tea shops and snack bars are catering services and require a food business license. Decorating first and then applying for the certificate, and trial operation before obtaining the certificate are common pitfalls. To determine which categories the food industry is divided into, and whether you need a license to sell fresh meat and vegetables, see Article 8 (when making food, first check which category you fall into).

Case: Xiao Li opened a small restaurant and was eager to open it to welcome customers without obtaining a food business license. After the market supervision department discovered it during an inspection, it immediately ordered it to stop business, confiscated the illegal gains, and imposed a fine of 10,000 yuan.

items.title: When making food, first check which category you fall into: production and catering require a license, and only selling pre-packaged food requires registration. Selling fresh meat and vegetables does not require a license
items.core: If you make your own things to sell, such as snack bars, braised food, baking, and homemade pickles, you must apply for a license. Small workshops and vendors must follow the rules of the province. Only prepackaged food that meets the standard definition is sold. There is no need to apply for a food business license, but registration is required. Selling fresh meat and vegetables does not require a license. If you fail to obtain a permit when you should, you will be fined 50,000 to 100,000 yuan if the goods are worth less than 10,000 yuan.
body: Cost: There is no charge for the license itself. However, the venue and facilities must meet the standards, and it will take several weeks for on-site verification and certification. Meat sellers must keep quarantine certificates and meat quality inspection certificates for each batch.

Income: Food Safety Law: To do food business, you must first obtain a license. If you produce, sell, or cater your own food, you must obtain a license in accordance with the law. "However, those who sell edible agricultural products and those who only sell pre-packaged food do not need a license. Those who only sell pre-packaged food should report to the food safety supervision and management department of the local people's government at or above the county level for filing." Edible agricultural products are unprocessed products such as fresh meat and vegetables. Prepackaged foods must be judged according to applicable standards, not just whether they are made by others or whether they are packaged. See Article 9 (Labeling of prepackaged foods) for specific definitions. "The specific management measures for small food production and processing workshops and food vendors are formulated by provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government." Each province sets its own rules for these two categories. Those who engage in food business without a license will have all their money, food, tools, equipment and raw materials confiscated. If the total amount of the goods calculated based on the selling price (the value of the goods) is less than 10,000 yuan, an additional fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan will be imposed. If the value of the goods exceeds RMB 10,000, the fine shall be between 10 times and 20 times the value of the goods. Pig Slaughter Management Regulations: Pigs can only be slaughtered in state-designated slaughterhouses and are subject to official centralized quarantine. "Except for individuals in rural areas who slaughter and feed themselves, slaughtering at designated points is not carried out. No unit or individual is allowed to engage in pig slaughtering activities without designated points." "The pig products produced and operated by units and individuals engaged in the sale of pig products, production and processing of meat products, as well as catering service operators and centralized dining units must be pig products that have passed quarantine and meat quality inspection at designated pig slaughtering plants (fields)." Therefore, the pork you sell and use must come from designated slaughterhouses, and must pass both quarantine and meat quality inspections. Those who slaughter pigs without permission in designated slaughterhouses will be ordered to shut down, and the pigs, slaughtering tools and equipment, and the money earned will be confiscated. The fine is the same as above for cooking food without a license. Animal Epidemic Prevention Law: Animal products sold and transported must carry quarantine certificates and quarantine marks with the goods. Those who fail to bring it will be ordered to make corrections and will be fined less than twice the value of similar qualified goods. The judicial interpretation governs punitive damages, which is the amount of compensation in addition to the refund. If the food made and sold by small workshops and food vendors does not meet food safety standards, the buyer requires ten times the compensation, and the court should support it (nationwide)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (third revision in 2025). Food Safety Law (Articles 35, 36, 122). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=7b5a76d0461745a08d3f964916b87ef3>; State Council (2021). Regulations on the Management of Pig Slaughter (State Council Order No. 742, Sections 2, 23, and 31). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-07/22/content_5626534.htm>; National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2021 revision). Animal Epidemic Prevention Law (Articles 51 and 100). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080817703add2017737395a973e31>; Supreme People's Court (2024). Interpretation of Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Food and Drug Punitive Damage Disputes (Fa Interpretation [2024] No. 9, Article 4). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/bf531a70471f10d377788f28d3d8f8.html>

Note: The thresholds for small workshops, small restaurants, and food vendors are set by each province. Specific numbers are not included in this article. Go to the official website of the Market Supervision Bureau of your province and search for "Regulations on the Administration of Small Food Workshops and Small Catering Vendors" to see the local version. Selling homemade food online does not require a license just because it is "online". Those who need permission still need permission. What to do with the entity and license, see Article 6 (Determine the name, location, and business scope before registration). For information on whether other businesses require a license, see Article 7 (Businesses that require a license). How much compensation the buyer can demand is set out in Section 5, Article 31 (tenfold compensation for food).

Case: Aunt Zhang opened a convenience store at the entrance of the community, selling only packaged snacks and drinks produced by regular manufacturers. Instead of applying for a complicated food business license, she completed the registration with the Market Supervision Bureau as required and successfully opened her business in compliance with regulations.

items.title: Check the label before selling prepackaged food: the production date, shelf life, and ingredient list are in accordance with regulations
items.core: Whether it counts as prepackaged food depends on whether it is pre-packaged in a certain amount and whether the weight or capacity is uniformly marked, not just whether there is a bag. Items that are weighed and bagged when purchased, items that are cooked and sold immediately, or food items that are taken away cannot be treated as prepackaged foods just because they have bags or lunch boxes. Prepackaged food does not have this label, and if the value of the food is less than 10,000, a fine of 5,000 to 50,000 will be imposed. Bulk foods should also be labeled with name, date and other information.
body: Cost: Printing labels costs a few cents to a few cents. It takes some time to fill in the dates and ingredients correctly for each batch.

Benefits: As of October 2026, the current GB 7718-2011 requires prepackaged foods to be pre-packaged in quantitative quantities or made in packaging materials and containers. There should be a uniform weight or capacity label on the packaging. Customers weigh and bag the food when they purchase it, and they cannot judge it as pre-packaged food just because it is bagged. This general labeling rule does not apply to foods that are prepared and sold now, and take-out meals cannot be applied just because they have lunch boxes. Food safety laws require labels on prepackaged food packages.
