Calculated directly without any adjustments, 3.9% of those who had a tourniquet on died, and 5.2% of those who did not. After leveling out other conditions (multivariate adjustment), tourniquet application was still independently associated with survival. The adjusted odds ratio OR was 5.86, with a confidence range of 95% CI 1.41 to 24.47. 232 casualties at the Baghdad field hospital: 90% of patients who had a tourniquet applied before the onset of shock survived, but only 10% of those who had a tourniquet applied after shock. All 5 people who needed a tourniquet but did not have one died, and 87% of those who had a tourniquet applied survived. The International Red Cross's 2025 First Aid Guidelines state that all severe bleeding should call for first aid. The steps it gives are to first let the injured person apply pressure to the wound, then call first aid, and then have the rescuer apply pressure. Only when the limbs that cannot be suppressed bleed will a tourniquet be considered. Once the tourniquet is applied, keep it in place until emergency personnel arrive. The sequence is: direct compression, clothing or towels are acceptable, and at the same time let someone else apply 120 → Apply tourniquet to bleeding limbs that cannot be suppressed → Do not loosen
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Teixeira PGR et al. (2018). Civilian Prehospital Tourniquet Use Is Associated with Improved Survival in Patients with Peripheral Vascular Injury. Journal of the American College of Surgeons. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jamcollsurg.2018.01.047> ; Kragh JF et al (2009). Survival with emergency tourniquet use to stop bleeding in major limb trauma. Annals of Surgery. <https://doi.org/10.1097/SLA.0b013e31818842ba> ; Chinese Medical Doctor Association Emergency Physician Branch, etc. (2020). Expert consensus on the emergency application of tourniquets. Chinese Journal of Emergency Medicine 29(6):773-779: "In pre-hospital emergency, once used, it is not recommended to loosen the tourniquet unless an alternative and complete hemostasis treatment is obtained." "The maximum use time should not exceed 2 hours. However, if the objective situation cannot be treated in the hospital or there is no alternative method to stop bleeding, the tourniquet will not be removed until formal rescue is obtained." <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.issn.1671-0282.2020.06.006>, full text <http://www.cem.org.cn/rhtml/20200606/index.htm>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 255–256: "Emergency medical services (EMS) should be accessed for all severe bleeding" "Once a tourniquet has been applied, keep it in place until EMS arrives", the steps are "1. Ask the person to apply direct pressure to their injury with their hands" "3. Access EMS" "4. Apply direct pressure to the bleed" "5. If direct pressure is ineffective and the person is bleeding from an arm or leg, consider applying a tourniquet". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>

Note: Do not use thin objects such as ropes and shoelaces as tourniquets. They will not strangle arteries and may also cut the skin. After applying the tourniquet, do not loosen it after a while to "bleed" it. Bleeding on the neck and trunk can only be applied by pressing, not pricking. In that battlefield data, the tourniquet itself did not lead to amputation, and there were 4 cases of temporary nerve paralysis. The expert consensus among Chinese emergency physicians is unanimous: once used in the pre-hospital setting, it is not recommended to loosen it unless there is another way to completely stop the bleeding. The bleeding from the upper arm was stuck in the upper third of the upper arm, and the bleeding from the thigh was stuck at the root of the thigh. Do not prick the forearms, calves, elbows, or knees. The consensus suggests that the total time before and after arriving at the hospital should not exceed 2 hours. However, if you cannot get to the hospital and have no other way to stop the bleeding, you should not wait until formal rescue. Makeshift tourniquets made from belts, ties, and sleeves are difficult to stop bleeding with alone, and must be tightened with a stick.

Case: Worker Sun’s forearm was scratched by a cutting machine, and blood spurted out. A colleague used a thick towel to firmly suppress the wound and asked another person to call 120. When he could no longer suppress the wound, he tied a tourniquet above the wound and recorded the time. He was not in shock when emergency care was taken over, and the bleeding stopped after the tourniquet was loosened.

items.title: If you are bitten or scratched by a dog or cat, first rinse with soapy water and running water for 15 minutes, and get vaccinated on the same day
items.core: Once rabies occurs, the fatality rate is almost 100%, so you cannot save on washing and vaccination after being bitten. First rinse with soapy water and running water for 15 minutes alternately, and get vaccinated on the same day. The earlier the better. If the bite or broken skin area is licked, it is a third-level exposure, and passive immunity preparations must be added. The level is determined by how exposed you are and how much exposure you have.
body: Cost: Flushing costs nothing. The rabies vaccine costs several hundred yuan. For level three exposure, passive rabies immunity preparations (directly injected with ready-made antibodies) cost several hundred to thousands of yuan. The most expensive thing is the delay.

Income: The original text of the 2023 version of the National Bureau of Disease Control and Prevention and the National Health Commission: "The case fatality rate of rabies is almost 100%." The treatment is to "wash all bites and scratches thoroughly with soapy water (or other weakly alkaline cleaner) and running water under a certain pressure for about 15 minutes." A slight bite or scratch on exposed skin without bleeding is a level II exposure and requires vaccination. Penetrating bites and licking of broken skin are Level III exposures. "The wounds should be treated and passive rabies immunity preparations and rabies vaccinations should be administered."暴露分几级，规范是「根据接触方式和暴露程度」来分。 The guidelines also state that “the sooner the rabies vaccination is administered after the first exposure, the better.” WHO: About 59,000 people die from rabies every year around the world, 99% of which are transmitted by dogs
Level of Evidence: A

Source: General Department of the National Administration of Disease Control and Prevention, General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Notice on the issuance of the Rabies Exposure Prevention and Treatment Work Specifications (2023 Edition). <https://www.ndcpa.gov.cn/jbkzzx/c100014/common/content/content_1706569159854649344.html>; WHO. Rabies Fact Report. <https://www.who.int/zh/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies>

Note: Do not ignore treatment just because it is "domesticated or vaccinated". The standard looks at the level of the wound (exposure level), not the origin of the dog. Do not bandage wounds yourself. The ten-day observation method can only decide whether to stop the injection, but not whether to start it.被野生动物、蝙蝠咬伤，同样这么处理。自己养狗的，按时给狗打狂犬病疫苗、出门系绳，见第 8 节第 30 条（养狗必须牵绳）。

Case: A 7-year-old girl was bitten on the back of her hand by a neighbor’s cat. Her parents immediately washed her with soapy water and running water for 15 minutes, and took her to the dog injury clinic to get rabies vaccination that day. The wound was a level 3 exposure, and I was given immune globulin, but I didn’t get sick later.

items.title: After being burned, rinse with cold running water for 20 minutes immediately without applying toothpaste or soy sauce
items.core: Children who rinse with cold running water for 20 minutes within 3 hours of injury are less likely to need skin grafting later. It's cold water, not ice water. Ice application will aggravate the injury.衣服粘在伤口上别硬撕，冲完拿干净的湿布或保鲜膜盖住去医院，牙膏、香油都不要抹。 It took me a while to remember that replenishing within three hours is still useful.
body: Cost: No money. Takes 20 minutes.

Benefits: 2495 children with burns and scalds were followed in Australia. Children who were exposed to cool running water for 20 minutes within 3 hours of injury had an odds ratio of later needing a skin graft of 0.6, 95% CI 0.4–0.8 (confidence range). This means fewer skin grafts are needed. But odds ratio is not a ratio of probabilities. It cannot be said that the probability of skin grafting is only 60%. The combined results of seven studies also found that "20 minutes of cool running water within three hours of injury significantly reduced the likelihood of requiring skin grafting and surgical wound management." The International Red Cross's 2025 first aid guidelines state that do not use ice water or apply ice, as this will aggravate the injury. The guidelines also say covering the burn with a clean, damp cloth or plastic wrap will protect it on the way to the hospital. The NHS states that clothing and jewelry near the burn should be removed, but any that are stuck to the wound should not be moved, and do not apply any ointment, oil or butter to the burn
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Griffin BR, Frear CC, Babl F, Oakley E, Kimble RM (2020). Cool Running Water First Aid Decreases Skin Grafting Requirements in Pediatric Burns: A Cohort Study of Two Thousand Four Hundred-five Children. Annals of Emergency Medicine, 75(1), 75-85. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annemergmed.2019.06.028>; Griffin B, Cabilan CJ, Ayoub B, et al. (2022). The effect of 20 minutes of cool running water first aid within three hours of thermal burn injury on patient outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Australasian Emergency Care, 25(4), 367-376. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.auec.2022.05.004>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, page 289: "Do not use ice-cold water" "Do not apply ice, as this may aggravate the injury", page 288: "Covering a burn with a clean wet cloth or plastic cling wrap can protect it during transit to medical care". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>; NHS. Burns and scalds: "do not remove anything that is stuck to the affected area" "do not put any creams, oils or butter on burns or scalds". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/treatment/>

Note: It is cold water, not ice water. Ice application will aggravate the injury. If the clothes are stuck to the wound, don't tear it off. After rinsing, cover it with a clean cloth and go to the hospital. Do not apply toothpaste, soy sauce, sesame oil, or flour. The NHS states that you should not apply any ointment or oil to burns. Replenishment within three hours is still useful. How to prevent scalding when bathing a baby, see Section 20, Item 17 (Put cold water first and then add hot water).

Case: A 3-year-old child knocked over a hot water cup and his right forearm became red. My mother immediately rinsed the patient with cold running water for 20 minutes without applying toothpaste. She did not tear off the sticky areas of her clothes. After rinsing, she covered the patient with a clean wet cloth and went to the hospital. The doctor's evaluation only required the application of medicine, and no scars were left after three weeks.

items.title: If a rash suddenly occurs all over the body, and you are short of breath or dizzy, treat it as anaphylactic shock. Call 120 immediately and explain clearly
items.core: If you suddenly have a rash all over the body, and you are short of breath or feel dizzy, treat it as anaphylactic shock. Call 120 immediately, say "suspected anaphylactic shock" and ask the emergency department to come with epinephrine. Anti-allergic drugs and hormones are slow-acting and cannot replace epinephrine. People who have had a severe allergy go to the doctor and ask if they can prescribe an automatic injection pen to inject the middle and outer thighs, even through thin pants.
body: Cost: No money. It is known that people with severe allergies cost money to bring their own epinephrine pen, and it is a prescription drug.

Benefit: Epinephrine is the first-line drug (first-line drug) for secondary anaphylactic shock and above, and the guideline lists it as a strong recommendation. Anti-allergic drugs and hormones are slow to take effect and cannot hold their place. The International Red Cross's 2025 first aid guidelines state that epinephrine auto-injector pens can be administered through clothing, as long as the clothing is not thick. If the doctor prescribes and local laws allow, when the patient cannot take the injection himself, others can help him/her
Evidence level: B (strongly recommended by the guideline, but the underlying evidence level is low)

Source: Chinese Medical Education Association et al. (2022). Anaphylactic Shock Emergency Clinical Practice Guidelines (2020). Frontiers in Pharmacology: "Epinephrine is the first-line medicine in GRADE II to IV anaphylaxis" "Intramuscular epinephrine should be injected in the mid-anterolateral thigh", the upper limit of intramuscular injection is 0.5 mg for adults and 0.3 mg for children under 14 years of age. If no response occurs, repeat every 5–15 minutes. "If an epinephrine pre-filled injector/auto-injector is available, they should follow the instructions written on the packaging or insert". <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2022.845689>; Muraro A, et al. (2022). EAACI guidelines: Anaphylaxis (2021 update). Allergy. <https://doi.org/10.1111/all.15032>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, p. 376: "The epinephrine auto-injection may be administered through the person's clothing if the clothes are not thick". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>

Note: This allergy guideline (EAACI) itself states that "most of the evidence in this field remains at a very low level." It is listed as a strong recommendation because the benefits far outweigh the risks, not because of large trials. Epinephrine is a prescription drug. If you don't have it on hand, what you can do is call 120 and say "anaphylactic shock is suspected" and ask the emergency department to come with the drug. If you have had a severe allergy, ask your doctor if he can prescribe epinephrine pre-filled injections or automatic injection pens. Learn how to inject on the middle and outer thighs (the outside is slightly forward), and you can do it even through pants that are not thick.

Case: 30-year-old Xiao Lin developed wheals all over his body after eating seafood, and then became short of breath and felt dizzy. When my colleague called 120, he said he was "suspected of anaphylactic shock." The emergency department brought epinephrine and gave him an injection on the outside of his thigh. He was out of danger after being sent to the hospital. The doctor prescribed an auto-injection pen and asked him to take it with him.
tags: Evidence B (strongly recommended by the guide, but the underlying evidence level is low)

items.title: If someone convulses and falls to the ground, clear the area around him, let him lie on his side, and watch the watch to time the time. Do not put anything in his mouth; the same is true for children who convulse when they have a fever
items.core: Move away things that can hurt people around him, let him lie on his side, with his mouth down, and watch the watch to mark the time. Don't hold him down or put anything in his mouth, as that will only hurt his teeth and jaw. If it doesn't stop for more than 5 minutes, if it's the first attack, or if you can't wake up after convulsing, you should call an ambulance. The same goes for children who have convulsions when they have a high fever. Don't take off your clothes or rub yourself with cold water to cool down.
body: Cost: No money.

Benefits: Avoid damage to teeth and jaws caused by mouth opening and hard objects. Avoid fractures caused by forceful pressing. Failure to stop for more than 5 minutes is the red line for calling an ambulance. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s approach is to move away things that may hurt people, and gently turn people on their sides with their mouths facing the ground to keep their airways open. If you can't breathe or wake up after the seizure, or if this is your first attack, call an ambulance. The convulsions that occur when a child has a fever are called febrile convulsions. The NHS says it is more common in children aged six months to six years. It usually lasts 2 to 3 minutes, rarely more than 10 minutes, and generally does not hurt the child or leave any sequelae. The NHS lists several situations in which you should call emergency services: first time convulsions, convulsions for more than 5 minutes, out of breath, and convulsions on only one side. There are also symptoms of feeling sleepier than usual for more than an hour after stopping, and smoking more than once in 24 hours. The American Academy of Pediatrics' 2011 guidelines say that children 6 to 60 months old who have a simple febrile seizure generally do not need an EEG, blood draw or brain imaging. Doctors mainly look for the cause of fever. The British National Health Service (NHS) also reminds children not to take off their clothes or rub themselves with cold water to cool down their children.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Seizure first aid: Remove anything near them that can cause an injury. If the person is lying down, turn them gently on their side, with their mouth pointing to the ground. This will keep their airway clear. They have trouble breathing or waking up after the seizure. Has never had a seizure before. Don't hold the person down or stop their movements. Don't put anything in their mouth. This can hurt their teeth or jaw. Don't offer water or food until they are fully alert" "Time the seizure to track if it lasts more than 5 minutes. If it does, seek immediate medical attention or call 911". <https://www.cdc.gov/epilepsy/first-aid-for-seizures/index.html> ; NHS. last more than 10 minutes" "They usually affect children between 6 months and 6 years old" "has a seizure for the first time" "has a seizure that lasts more than 5 minutes" "is more sleepy than usual for more than 1 hour after the seizure stops" "protect their head with your hands or something soft" "do not move your child or try to hold them in place" "do not try to lower your child's temperature by undressing them or sponging them with cold water" "Do not take your child to A&E if they are still having a seizure or are unconscious, call 999 instead" "your child will need to be checked in hospital after having a febrile seizure for the first time". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/febrile-seizures/>; Pediatrics, 127(2), 389-394: "In general, a simple febrile seizure does not usually require further evaluation, specifically electroencephalography, blood studies, or neuroimaging". <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2010-3318>

Note: This same page lists several other situations in which you should call an ambulance immediately. For example, you may have another attack soon after an attack, you may not be able to wake up or have difficulty breathing after an attack, you may have been injured during an attack, you may have had an attack in water, or this may be your first attack. When the attack stops, let him lie on his side with his mouth facing down, and wait until he is fully awake before giving him water. If you have epilepsy patients at home, this set of actions is most useful. When a child has a fever and convulsions, the NHS also says not to move the child around or hold him down, but to protect his head with your hands or something soft. If your child is still convulsing or cannot be woken up, don't take him to the hospital by yourself. Call 120 directly. The first time I had a febrile convulsion, I had to go to the hospital for a checkup after the seizure. If you do the same thing to a stranger, the chances of the benefits coming back to you are smaller. However, you are not civilly liable for damage caused by voluntarily rescuing others (Article 184 of the Civil Code, see Article 2 of this section, don’t be in a hurry to help someone up).

Case: A three-year-old child convulsed when he had a fever. The mother moved the water cup on the coffee table and asked him to lie on his side with his mouth down. She used her mobile phone to time the child without putting anything in his mouth or taking off his clothes to apply cold water. If she didn't stop smoking for six minutes, she would call 120 immediately. If she had a seizure for the first time or if she couldn't wake up after smoking, she would also call an ambulance.

items.title: If a diabetic patient suddenly trembles, breaks out in a cold sweat, or cannot speak clearly, but is still awake and able to swallow, give 15 grams of sugar first and retest after 15 minutes.
items.core: If the person is still awake and able to swallow, first eat 15 grams of sugar, either a sugar cube or a small box of juice. Test again after 15 minutes, and try again if it's still low. A blood sugar level below 3.0 mmol/L is considered medically serious hypoglycemia. When it reaches a level that requires help from others to deal with, it can be fatal. If the dog doesn't respond or can't swallow a bite, don't feed it. Call 120 directly.
body: Cost: Nothing. Carry a few sugar cubes or a small carton of juice with you.

Benefit: Blood sugar below 3.0 mmol/L is clinically significant hypoglycemia. Changes in consciousness or behavior that require help from others are severe hypoglycemia, which can be fatal. The standards of the American Diabetes Association state that oral glucose is the first choice when the person is still awake, but other sugars containing glucose are also acceptable. Most people eat 15 grams of sugar and then eat again 15 minutes later when the hypoglycemia is still there. The International Red Cross's 2025 First Aid Guidelines state that food and drink should only be given to people who can respond to screams and swallow. If glucose tablets are not available, you can give a sugary drink (such as juice), or a few spoons of sugar or a few candies. If you don’t respond, call first aid.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: American Diabetes Association (2025). Diabetes Care Standards 2025·Chapter 6 Blood Glucose Targets and Hypoglycemia. Diabetes Care: Grading "Level 1: Glucose <70 mg/dL (<3.9 mmol/L) and ≥54 mg/dL (≥3.0 mmol/L)" "Level 2: Glucose <54 mg/dL (<3.0 mmol/L)" "Level 3: A severe event characterized by altered mental and/or physical status requiring assistance for treatment of hypoglycemia, irrespective of glucose level"; "For most individuals, 15 g carbohydrates should be ingested" "Fifteen minutes after initial treatment, repeat the treatment if hypoglycemia persists" "Glucose is the preferred treatment for the conscious individual with glucose <70 mg/dL (<3.9 mmol/L), although any form of carbohydrate that glucose contains may be used". <https://doi.org/10.2337/dc25-S006>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 390–391: "Oral glucose administration (swallowing or eating glucose) should be used for an adult or child with suspected hypoglycaemia who is responsive and able to swallow" "If they do not, give them a sugary (non-diet) drink, such as fruit juice, or some sugar (such as three teaspoons of sugar or three pieces of candy, like jellybeans)" "Only give the person something to eat or drink if they are responsive and able to swallow" "If the person’s condition does not improve quickly (around 30 minutes) or they become unresponsive, access emergency medical services (EMS)". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>

Note: Do not feed an unconscious person as it may choke the trachea. Call 120 directly. The same standard also recommends that people taking insulin and those prone to hypoglycemia should have a copy of glucagon. The original text is "All individuals treated with insulin or who are at high risk of hypoglycemia...should be prescribed glucagon". Nasal sprays and pre-filled injections are easier to use than those that require temporary mixing of medicines. These practices are by default prepared for you or the diabetics in your family, and the candy you carry with you is also for them.

Case: Lao Chen has diabetes. He was shaking in a cold sweat before lunch and his speech was slurred, but he was awake and able to swallow. My wife gave him three sugar cubes. After 15 minutes, it measured 2.8, which was lower than 3.0. I gave him a small box of juice before it rose again. If he complained at that time or couldn't swallow it, he would just give me a 120 without feeding him.

items.title: If someone gets an electric shock, cut off the power first, then use a dry stick or the like to turn it on. Do not pull it directly with your hands.
items.core: Turn off the power first, or use a dry wooden stick or the like to disconnect it before touching anyone. Just use your hands to pull, and one injured person becomes two. If you are not breathing normally after disconnecting from the power source, immediately press item 1 (press your chest hard). Don’t be afraid to touch it just because it is an electrical injury. If high-voltage lines fall to the ground or near transformer equipment, you do not dispose of them yourself, and you move far away until the power department cuts off the power.
body: Cost: No money.

Benefit: Prevent rescuers from being electrocuted together, turning one injured person into two. If the patient is not breathing normally after disconnecting from the power source, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation according to Article 1 of this section (press the chest forcefully). The first aid procedures of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention are: Look first, don’t touch, the person may still be connected to electricity. Turn off the power first if it can be cut off; if it cannot be cut off, use non-conductive objects such as cardboard, plastic or wood to turn off the power. After disconnecting from the power source, if breathing or pulse stops, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation immediately. A review says that people who suffer cardiac arrest after being electrocuted and are rescued tend to have a good prognosis
Level of Evidence: B

Source: US CDC. What to Do to Protect Yourself From Electrical Hazards (First aid section). <https://www.cdc.gov/natural-disasters/response/what-to-do-protect-yourself-from-electrical-hazards.html>; Spies C, Trohman RG (2006). Narrative review: Electrocution and life-threatening electrical injuries. Annals of Internal Medicine 145(7):531-537. <https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-145-7-200610030-00011>

Remarks: "Turn off the power first and then touch others" is a purely self-interest rule: pull directly, and you will be the second one to fall. Do not handle it yourself near high-voltage lines or substation equipment. Move back and wait until the power department cuts off the power. For cardiac arrest caused by electric shock, just press and defibrillate as usual. Don't be afraid to do it just because it is an "electrical injury".

Case: Maintenance worker Xiao Li reached out to touch the shell of a leaking rice cooker and was sucked into it. His colleague immediately unplugged the plug and used a dry wooden stick to pick it open. Xiao Li was not breathing, so his colleagues immediately pressed his chest and 120 personnel came to the scene to take over. No one dared to go near where the high-voltage line fell, waiting for the power department to cut off the power.

items.title: If the carbon monoxide alarm goes off, or people in the room have headaches, dizziness, and nausea at the same time, go out first and then make a call.
items.core: If you suspect carbon monoxide poisoning, for example, if the alarm goes off and people in the room have headaches, dizziness, and nausea, take everyone outside first and then make a call. Symptoms are like a cold, getting worse indoors and getting better when you go out, which is an important reminder. China reported 11,523 deaths from carbon monoxide poisoning in 2018, with the highest number of deaths occurring in winter, with about 70% of deaths occurring at home during the three months of winter.
body: Cost: No money.

Benefits: China CDC’s Cause of Death Surveillance System reported 11,523 deaths from carbon monoxide poisoning in 2018. The highest numbers were in January (2845 cases), February (2321 cases) and December (2010 cases). During the three months of winter, 66% to 73% died at home. This is the number reported in the system, not calculated based on the national population. More than 400 people die in the United States each year from accidental carbon monoxide poisoning that is not related to fires. More than 100,000 people went to emergency rooms and more than 14,000 people were hospitalized. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning are often described as "flu-like." Common ones include headache, dizziness, fatigue, stomach upset, vomiting, chest pain and confusion. The NHS states that symptoms worsen when you stay in the room in question and get better when you leave or go outdoors. Nausea is also among the symptoms listed by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. It states that if you suspect carbon monoxide poisoning, go outside for fresh air immediately before calling an emergency call
Level of Evidence: B

Source: You J, Liu J, Zhou M (2020). Number of Deaths due to Carbon Monoxide Poisoning by Month and by Place of Death — China, 2018. China CDC Weekly 2(2):32: "In 2018, there were 11,523 deaths caused by carbon monoxide poisoning reported in China". <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2020.008>; U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Carbon monoxide poisoning: "More than 400 Americans die from unintentional CO poisoning not linked to fires" "More than 100,000 visit an emergency department" "More than 14,000 are hospitalized", common symptoms "headache, dizziness, weakness, upset stomach, vomiting, chest pain, and confusion" "CO symptoms are often described as "flu-like."". <https://www.cdc.gov/carbon-monoxide/about/index.html>; U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. Carbon Monoxide Information Center: "Know the symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning: headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, vomiting, sleepiness, and confusion" "If you suspect CO poisoning, get outside to fresh air immediately, and then call 911". <https://www.cpsc.gov/Safety-Education/Safety-Education-Centers/Carbon-Monoxide-Information-Center>; NHS. Carbon monoxide poisoning: "They may get worse when you spend time in an affected room or building and get better when you leave or go outside". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/carbon-monoxide-poisoning/>

Note: Symptoms are like a cold.出门就好转，是最强的提示。 It is taken seriously when people in a room feel uncomfortable at the same time. This is what the author deduced from "people in the same room breathe the same air." Don't stay in the house looking for reasons, don't go back to turn off the valve, come out first and then make a call.报警器怎么装见第 1 节第 3 条。

Case: A family was eating charcoal hot pot in a closed house in winter. The carbon monoxide alarm suddenly sounded. Everyone immediately covered their mouths and noses and ran outside. Then they called the emergency number. There were no symptoms of poisoning.

items.title: Do not induce vomiting if you accidentally take detergents, pesticides, or medicines. Bring a bottle and seek medical attention immediately; if it splashes in your eyes or skin, rinse with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes
items.core: Do not induce vomiting if you accidentally take detergents, pesticides, or medicines. Vomiting may hurt your throat and may cause choking. If you mistakenly swallow strong acid and alkali detergents, the Chinese Disease Control and Prevention says to drink an appropriate amount of milk or egg white first, take the bottle with you and go to the hospital immediately. If it splashes on your skin or eyes, rinse with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes. Open your eyelids and do not rub.消毒液和洁厕剂混着用会产生氯气。
body: Cost: No money. Keep cleaners, disinfectants, pesticides and medicines high and out of reach of children, or in locked cabinets.绝不分装进饮料瓶。

Income: There are four treatment methods provided by the Occupational Hygiene and Poison Control of the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention. If it is eaten into the mouth (ingestion from the digestive tract), drink an appropriate amount of milk or egg white immediately. "Remember, do not induce vomiting." Seek medical attention as soon as possible, and bring the packaging or instructions with you "so that doctors can quickly determine the ingredients and formulate a treatment plan." Inhalation (respiratory inhalation): Immediately move to a well-ventilated area and loosen collar to allow easy breathing. If you have severe coughing, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Skin contact: Immediately flush the exposed area with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes. Be careful not to let the flushing solution splash into your eyes or other intact skin. In case of eye contact, flush eyes immediately with plenty of water or saline for at least 15 minutes. When rinsing, open your eyelids to allow the water to fully contact the eyeballs and the inside of the eyelids. "Do not rub your eyes."冲洗后立即前往眼科。高危产品按酸碱度（pH）认。 Those with pH<3 are toilet cleaners, descalers, floor cleaners, and stainless steel brighteners.部分强力管道疏通剂还含稀硫酸。 Those with pH>11 are pipe unblockers, strong kitchen decontamination agents, dishwashing powder, explosive salt, and decontamination powder. Another combination that can cause trouble right away: Disinfectant and toilet cleaners containing hydrochloric acid produce chlorine gas when used together. Chlorine gas irritates the respiratory tract, causing severe coughing and shortness of breath, which can even be life-threatening.不催吐不只管清洁剂。 The NHS's poisoning page lists medicines, cleaning products, certain plants and mushrooms, and pesticides as common causes of poisoning. It states that if you suspect that you have swallowed something harmful, do not make people vomit. "You may choke and stop breathing," and do not give food or drink. If the patient vomits, show some vomit to the doctor. The International Red Cross's 2025 first aid guidelines state that people who have swallowed poison should not let them vomit, as "it may injure the throat." Give bottles, packaging and labels to first responders
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Institute of Occupational Health and Poison Control, Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2025). Summer vacation safety tips: Be wary of strong acid and alkali cleaners. <https://niohp.chinacdc.cn/kpdw/202507/t20250722_308659.htm>; NHS. swallowed something harmful – they could choke and stop breathing" "do not give the person anything to eat or drink" "if the person vomits, try putting some vomit in a container to give to healthcare professionals"; Common causes include "medicines" "household cleaning products" "certain plants and mushrooms" "pesticides". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/poisoning/>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 346–347: “The person should NOT be encouraged to vomit as this may damage their throat” “First aid providers should not give any diluents such as milk, water or activated charcoal to a person who has swallowed a poisonous substance unless they are instructed to do so by the poison control center or equivalent poison expert”. <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>

Remarks: Set B because the official popular science only talks about how to deal with it and how to recognize it, and there is no figure on "how many things can be avoided if you follow these instructions."喝不喝牛奶，两边说法不同。 China Disease Control and Prevention says that if you accidentally swallow strong acid and alkali detergents, drink an appropriate amount of milk or egg white first. The International Red Cross said no milk or water would be given unless asked to do so by a poisoning first aid specialist, and the NHS also said no food or drink would be given. Don’t feed yourself anything other than detergents, such as medicines and pesticides. Not sure what he had accidentally swallowed, he took the bottle, instructions, and vomit to the hospital. Prevention is much cheaper than first aid: store them in categories, don’t mix them with food and drinks, tighten the caps and throw away empty bottles after use, and never pour into mineral water bottles. Wear rubber gloves and goggles when using, open windows for ventilation, and do not mix different types. See Section 19 for carbon monoxide and Section 14 for burns. If chemicals such as acids and alkalis are splashed on your body, please refer to Article 21 (Chemicals Splashed on Your Body) on how to take off your clothes and how long you should take the bath. The child has swallowed a button battery or magnetic beads, see Article 45 (Child has swallowed a button battery).

Case: Xiao Zhao mistakenly took a sip of the toilet cleaner as a drink. His family did not induce vomiting and took the bottle directly to the doctor; the doctor asked him to drink milk first. Later, he mixed disinfectant and toilet cleaner. The chlorine fumed made his eyes hurt. He opened his eyelids and flushed them with plenty of water for twenty minutes.

items.title: If chemicals such as acids and alkalis splash on your body, take off the contaminated clothes immediately and rinse with plenty of running water. Open your eyelids and rinse for enough time before leaving.
items.core: The first step is to take off the stained clothes and shoes immediately. The areas covered by the clothes will be most seriously injured. The second step is to rinse the skin and eyes with plenty of running water at room temperature, no hot water, for at least 15 minutes. For wounds on the skin, the Hunan Provincial Department of Emergency Management gives 20 to 30 minutes, whichever is longer. The third step is to open your eyelids and go to the ophthalmologist directly after flushing.
body: Cost: No money. On your first day on the job, check the location of the eyewash station and shower unit. Don’t wait until something goes wrong to find them.

Benefit: Three steps on site. The first step is to take off the contaminated clothes and shoes immediately: the poison will continue to be absorbed through the skin, and the pockets of the clothes will be the most injured. The second step is to rinse with plenty of running water. The lower limit given by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention on Occupational Health and Poison Control is "at least 15 minutes" each for skin and eyes. The Hunan Provincial Department of Emergency Management recommends 20 to 30 minutes for wound irrigation, "with strong chemicals requiring longer." Whichever of the two calibers is longer. In the third step, the eyes should "open the eyelids and ensure that the water flow fully contacts the eyeballs and the inside of the eyelids", "do not rub the eyes", and go to the ophthalmologist immediately after flushing. Use room temperature or lukewarm water, hot water is prohibited. Do not apply ointment, red lotion or anything to the fresh wound, and do not wrap it with dirty cloth. Applying it will affect the doctor's judgment of the depth. Legally, "chemical skin burns" and "chemical eye burns" are included in the list of statutory occupational diseases. Those that occur at work are classified as occupational diseases and work-related injuries. In the event of an acute occupational hazard accident, the employer "should organize timely treatment, conduct health examinations and medical observations, and the necessary expenses shall be borne by the employer" (National)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Institute of Occupational Health and Poison Control, Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2025). Summer vacation safety tips: Be wary of strong acid and alkali detergents. <https://niohp.chinacdc.cn/kpdw/202507/t20250722_308659.htm>; Hunan Provincial Department of Emergency Management (2015). Emergency handling and treatment of common chemical poisoning accidents. <http://yjt.hunan.gov.cn/yjt/tszt/aqzs/201509/t20150919_3113778.html>; National Health Commission and four other departments (2024). Classification and catalog of occupational diseases (implemented from August 1, 2025). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6992843.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (2018). Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases (Article 37). <https://www.beijing.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengcefagui/qtwj/201711/t20171104_779851.html> (Reprinted by the Beijing Municipal People’s Government)

Note: B is set because there is no unified national standard number for how long it takes to flush. One of the two official materials takes 15 minutes to write and the other takes 20 to 30 minutes to write. Go to the hospital with the chemical's name, packaging, or safety data sheet (SDS). The doctor will rely on it to make a plan. Don't just grab another acid or alkali to "neutralize" it: mixing the two together will generate heat, and you can't control how much you pour. The "neutralizing fluid" mentioned in the Hunan material refers to the special flushing fluid prepared by the unit in advance, not something used for hedging on site. Dry powders such as lime powder and cement powder should be brushed off before flushing. According to this, some local emergency pages say that concentrated sulfuric acid should also be dried first. This point differs from place to place and is not covered in this book. Household cleaners and ingestion see section 20. For protection and physical examination before taking up the job, please refer to Section 19, Articles 9 and 10 (the unit must provide hazard notices and protective equipment before taking up the job).

Case: When a worker was repairing equipment and splashed dilute sulfuric acid on his arm, he immediately took off the contaminated shirt and rinsed it with running water for half an hour. He then sought medical treatment. His skin was only slightly red and not burned.

items.title: If you feel dizzy, nauseous, not sweating or unconscious under high temperature, immediately move to a cool place and take off your clothes and splash water to cool down. If you are unconscious, do not give water or give 120
items.core: Hot red skin, slurred speech, and confusion are symptoms of heat stroke. The body temperature can rise above 41°C in 10 to 15 minutes, and the mortality rate in severe cases is extremely high. Immediately move to a cool and ventilated place, take off your clothes, cool down with cold water and a wet towel, and call 120 degrees at the same time. Do not give a sip of water to an unconscious person.
body: Cost: No money.

Earnings: National Weather Service: Heat stroke is a 'serious medical emergency'. It is characterized by a body temperature above 103°F (39.4°C), confusion, slurred speech, and hot and red skin. The treatment is to call first aid immediately, move to a cool place, cool down with cold water and damp cloth, and "do not give liquids." The symptoms of heat exhaustion are profuse sweating, fatigue, clammy skin, and fast and weak pulse. The treatment is to move to a cool place, loosen clothes, and drink sips of water. Seek medical attention if vomiting occurs, worsens, or does not relieve for more than 1 hour. Yunnan Provincial Bureau of Disease Control and Prevention reminds: Immediately move to a cool and ventilated place, use cold wet towels to cool down, drink salty drinks if you are conscious, and call the emergency number immediately if symptoms are severe. It also said severe heat stroke has an "extremely high case fatality rate". The Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention reminds: Cool down first, then transfer, and cool down within the "golden half hour" after the patient loses consciousness. If possible, young adults without underlying diseases can soak in cold water to quickly cool down, while the elderly and those with underlying illnesses can spray water on their skin and rely on evaporation to cool down. The Wilderness Medical Society's 2024 updated heat illness guidelines say that cold water immersion is the most important way to treat severe heat stroke, as it cools the body the fastest. If you don't have ice water, use the coldest water at hand. If you can't soak it, spray water and fan it at about half the speed of soaking. The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) says that during a heat stroke attack, the body temperature can rise above 106°F (about 41°C) within 10 to 15 minutes. Among the symptoms it lists are "hot and dry skin, or heavy sweating."中国疾控 2014 年版中暑指南列的热射病表现有「皮肤红、热、且干燥无汗」，处理要求「不要给病人喝水」，病人呕吐就翻成侧躺，保持呼吸道通畅
Level of Evidence: B

Source: US National Weather Service. Heat Related Illnesses. <https://www.weather.gov/safety/heat-illness>; Yunnan Provincial Bureau of Disease Control and Prevention (2026). If you have these symptoms, you may have heatstroke. <https://ynsjkj.yn.gov.cn/html/2026/jikongkepu_0719/2606.html>; Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention. In hot weather, the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention reminds you to beware of heatstroke: "If possible, cold water immersion can be used to quickly cool down young adults without underlying diseases. The elderly and patients with underlying illnesses can spray water on the skin to cool down through evaporation. Cooling should follow the principle of "cooling first, then transporting". <https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkkp/ggws/hjyssj/202409/t20240906_296985.html> ; National Health Commission (2010). Key points of knowledge on prevention of heat stroke. <https://www.nhc.gov.cn/wjw/jbyfykz/201007/1edb19b7dd4e4bdf8da5ea45f4a64e23.shtml> ; Eifling KP et al (2024). Wilderness Medical Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of Heat Illness: 2024 Update. Wilderness & Environmental Medicine 35(1_suppl):112S-127S. <https://doi.org/10.1177/10806032241227924> (The text site refuses to be automatically crawled. For specific recommendations, check the updated summary on the official website of the Wilderness Medical Association: "cold water immersion … is the most important method of treating severe heat illness" "If CWI is unavailable, evaporative cooling is the recommended second-line treatment. … generally half as fast as CWI" <https://wms.org/magazine/magazine/1540/Heat-Illness-CPG/default.aspx>); Lipman GS et al. (2019). Same as the 2019 version of the guideline. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wem.2018.10.004>; US CDC/NIOSH. Heat-related Illnesses: "When heat stroke occurs, the body temperature can rise to 106°F or higher within 10 to 15 minutes" "Hot, dry skin or profuse sweating". <https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/about/illnesses.html>; Institute of Occupational Health and Poison Control, Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2014). Public Guidelines for Prevention and Emergency Treatment of Heat Stroke (2014 Edition). <https://niohp.chinacdc.cn/sndt/201405/t20140530_97623.htm>

Note: Don’t wait to “take it easy.” During heat stroke, the body temperature can rise to over 41°C in just ten minutes. People with heat stroke may not sweat, or they may sweat profusely. NIOSH lists both. Don’t let it go just because you are still sweating. Do not give water to an unconscious person, and let him lie on his side if he vomits. Where to put the ice pack, the two sides have different opinions. The Chinese Disease Control and Prevention said it should be applied on the neck, armpits and thighs, while the Wilderness Medical Association said that research could not show that applying it to these areas has a cooling effect. The Wilderness Medicine Society recommends covering the entire body when ice packs are available. If the ice pack is not available, place it on the cheeks, palms, and soles of the feet. Both sides said to soak it in cold water if possible.

Case: A construction worker suddenly became dizzy and confused while working in the high temperature at noon. The worker quickly moved him to a cool and ventilated place and poured cold water on him to cool down. At the same time, he called 120, and the rescue was timely and life-threatening.

items.title: As long as people with heat stroke are awake, they should drink cold salt water or sports drinks in small amounts and frequently. Do not drink too much, drink alcohol or high-sugar drinks.
items.core: Only those who are sober should drink it. Drink cold salt water or sports drinks in small amounts and frequently. Do not drink them all in one go. Skip alcohol and high-sugar drinks, which make you lose more water. Cool down first and then replenish water. If the baby is unconscious and has slurred speech, he will not feed him a mouthful.
body: Cost: Nothing. A bottle of sports drink costs a few dollars.

Benefits: The Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention has released the "Public High Temperature Heat Stroke Prevention and Emergency Treatment Guidelines (2014 Edition)". When talking about prevention, it says that those who do physical work or strenuous exercise in high temperatures should "drink at least 2 to 4 cups of cold water (500 to 1000ml) per hour. The water temperature should not be too high, and drinking water should be small and frequent." This amount is for preventive use for people who have not yet suffered from heat stroke. It also states that "excessive sweating will lead to the loss of salt and minerals in the body" and "sports drinks can help people replenish the salt and minerals needed by the body during sweating." It also says, "Do not drink drinks that contain alcohol or a lot of sugar. These drinks can cause more body fluids to be lost. At the same time, you should also avoid drinking frozen drinks that are too cold." For heat stroke, it is clearly written "Do not give water to the patient." US NIOSH: For heat exhaustion, "encourage frequent sips of cold water"; for heat cramps, drink sports drinks containing sugar and electrolytes every 15 to 20 minutes, "do not use salt tablets"
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Institute of Occupational Health and Poison Control, Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2014). Public Guidelines for the Prevention and Emergency Treatment of Heat Illness (2014 Edition). <https://niohp.chinacdc.cn/sndt/201405/t20140530_97623.htm>; US CDC/NIOSH. Heat-Related Illnesses. <https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/about/illnesses.html>

Note: The 2014 version of the Chinese Disease Control and Prevention Guidelines says that excessive sweating will lose salt and minerals, which need to be replenished. Sports drinks can help replenish them, so the water should contain a little salt. Drinking small amounts frequently is also a requirement of this guideline. "Don't drink iced drinks" also comes from this guide. The reason is that you are afraid of stomach cramps, and there is no quantitative evidence. Don't misread it as "can't use cold ones." Article 22 (Take off your clothes and splash water to cool down when you feel dizzy and nauseated at high temperatures) discusses several ways to cool down. They are cold water scrubbing, cold water immersion, and ice pack application on the head, armpits, and thighs (groin). These are for use on the body, not in the mouth. Cooling down always comes before hydration. If you are unconscious and have slurred speech, don’t feed him any food.

Case: A tourist suffered a slight heatstroke while climbing a mountain in summer and was conscious. A friend gave him a small amount of cold salt water to drink several times and moved him to the shade of a tree to cool down. The heatstroke symptoms were significantly relieved after half an hour.

items.title: In case of fire, crawl on the ground, touch the door before opening it, don't open the door if it's hot, take the stairs instead of the elevator, and don't look back when you're out.
items.core: Get down on the ground and crawl under the smoke toward the exit. Touch the doorknob and door panel before opening the door. If it is hot or if there is smoke coming from the seam of the door, don't open it. Try the second way, open it slowly, and close it if there is smoke. Take the stairs instead of the elevator, and don’t look back to get something when you go out. If your clothes catch fire, stop, fall to the ground, roll around, and protect your face with your hands.
body: Cost: Installing 1 to 2 independent smoke detectors at home costs tens of yuan. Take a look at the two exits of the corridor in advance.

Proceeds: US FEMA Escape original text: "Get down on the ground and crawl under the smoke toward the exit." Before opening the door, touch the doorknob and door panel. "If it is hot or there is smoke at the crack of the door, don't open the door. Use the second way." Open the door slowly and close it immediately if there is smoke. If your clothes catch fire, "stop, fall to the ground, or roll" and protect your face with your hands. If you can't get out, close the door, block the door cracks and vents with cloth or tape, and call to report your location. The Department of Emergency Management’s fire self-rescue tips agree. When escaping, do not take the elevator. When the fire is not severe, try to run downstairs. Cover your mouth and nose with a wet towel or mask, and evacuate lying down or bending down.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: US FEMA Ready.gov. Home Fires. <https://www.ready.gov/home-fires>; Department of Emergency Management (2019). Self-rescue methods for fires in public places: "Do not take the elevator when escaping. When the fire is not large, try to run below the floor." "You can use a wet towel or mask to cover your nose, and crawl or bend to evacuate." <https://www.mem.gov.cn/kp/shaq/201904/t20190401_366015.shtml>; Guizhou Fire Rescue Corps (2020). Fire knowledge | Three key points for escape: "Fold a wet towel in half 3 times (folded into 8 layers), the smoke removal rate is relatively high, but when the concentration of smoke and poisonous gas is too high, the filtration effect cannot be guaranteed. In addition, too wet a towel can cause breathing difficulties." <https://gz.119.gov.cn/xfkp/xfcs/202010/t20201026_71437855.html>

Note: Don’t take the elevator, you will be trapped in it if the power is cut off. Don't look back to get your property. Don't run up there unless you're sure the roof door is open. Don't jump off the building. Wet towels should be folded in half 3 times to form 8 layers. Don’t add too much water, as too wet a towel will make you unable to breathe. When the smoke and poisonous gas are too thick, even a towel can't stop it. For wildfires and wild fires, see Section 9, Article 28 (picnics are not allowed to light fires in forest areas and grasslands).

Case: A fire broke out in a residential building late at night. The resident crawled to the door with his body bent to the ground. He touched the doorknob and found it was hot, so he took the balcony to escape. Finally, he evacuated safely along the stairs without being greedy for property.

items.title: When you see someone drowning, call someone and call 110/120 first, stretch out the pole and throw floating objects, but don’t go into the water yourself
items.core: Call people and call 110/120 first, stretch out the pole or throw floating objects on the shore, but don’t go into the water yourself. If the person is unresponsive and unable to breathe normally after landing, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation immediately. Trained to perform compressions and perform artificial respiration. If you don't know, can't or don't want to blow, just keep pressing and listen to the emergency dispatcher's instructions.
body: Cost: No money. The hard thing is resisting the urge to jump.

Benefit: WHO: About 300,000 people drown every year around the world, 92% of which are in low- and middle-income countries. Drowning is the fourth cause of death in children aged 1 to 4 years old and the third leading cause of death in children aged 5 to 14 years. The intervention recommended by WHO is "safe rescue and resuscitation training", such as learning how to save people without entering the water first.先大喊叫人、打 110/120，再从岸上递长杆、绳子，或抛救生圈、空桶等漂浮物。 The 2025 International Red Cross First Aid Guidelines state that when rescuing, try not to enter the water: pass hard objects (such as poles, branches) from the shore or boat, or throw ropes or floatable objects.施救的人不要碰正在挣扎的溺水者，因为有被拖进水里的危险。 Those who are already rescuing in the water must understand the water conditions and bring floating objects. If the person is unresponsive or breathing abnormally after being fished out, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation immediately. The American Heart Association and American Academy of Pediatrics 2024 Drowning Resuscitation Guidelines emphasize that cardiac arrest in drowning is often caused by severe hypoxia. Trained rescuers should perform artificial respiration and chest compressions together. If you are unable, unable or unwilling to perform artificial respiration, continue chest compressions until rescuers arrive. When making emergency calls, speak on speakerphone and listen to the dispatcher
Evidence level: C

Source: WHO. Drowning Fact Sheets. <https://www.who.int/zh/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/drowning>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 214–215: “An attempted rescue by first aid providers should be made without entering the water, either from land or a boat, by reaching with something rigid (e.g. a pole or tree branch), or by throwing a rope or buoyant object. Providers should not touch an actively drowning person because of the risk of being pulled into the water." <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>; American Heart Association / American Academy of Pediatrics (2024). Highlights of the 2024 Focused Update on Resuscitation Followingcitation Drowning, pp. 3–4. <https://www.heart.org/-/media/CPR-Files/CPR-Guidelines-Files/Highlights/2024_Drowning/Hghlghts_2024GLFU_Drowning_240927.pdf>

Note: C is set because "do not enter the water" is only a practice recommendation in the International Red Cross Guidelines. There are no controlled studies or numbers.不要手拉手结成链子下水，这是作者从「不下水」推出来的。 Don't drag someone without training. If you encounter someone who is struggling, you may be dragged into the water. "Don't go into the water" is also a self-interested rule: the person who goes into the water drowns himself, no matter who is in the water. Most of the people who really need to be rescued are their own children. How to prevent them lies in Section 1, Article 12 (Kids should not be out of sight near water). If someone falls into an ice hole, they don’t run up to the ice to pull him out. How can the ice be protected? Section 1, Article 41 (Measure the thickness of the ice in the wild first).

Case: Mr. Wang heard calls for help at the park lake over the weekend and saw a boy drowning and struggling. He did not dive directly, but immediately shouted for help and asked others to call 110 and 120. At the same time, he and another person grabbed a long branch and stretched out to the boy, and threw him an empty plastic bucket to increase buoyancy. The boy was caught and pulled ashore. He was no longer breathing. Mr. Wang immediately performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation until the ambulance arrived. The doctor said that it was precisely because he did not enter the water rashly, called in time and received professional first aid that the boy was finally out of danger.

items.title: If someone is choked and unable to speak, stand behind him and give him 5 back slaps and 5 abdominal thrusts if he is over 1 year old. If he falls down, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
items.core: Those over 1 year old were unable to speak, so they stood behind them and received 5 back slaps followed by 5 abdominal punches. Pregnant women and very fat people would punch the chest instead. Repeatedly until something comes out or a person falls down, perform CPR and call the emergency number at the same time. Don't reach into your mouth to pick out something you can't see.
body: Cost: No money. Take a look at the action: Make a fist with one hand above the navel, wrap it with the other hand, and quickly impact inwards and upwards.

Profit: U.S. National Library of Medicine Original text: First ask, "Are you choked? Can you speak?" "If you can cough hard or speak, don't use your hands." Coughing itself can often cough up foreign objects. Unable to speak, he "repeatedly repeated 5 back pats and 5 abdominal thrusts until the foreign object came out or the person lost consciousness." "Start cardiopulmonary resuscitation as soon as you lose consciousness," and at the same time ask someone to call emergency services. Pregnant women and obese people may do chest thrusts instead. The International Red Cross's 2025 first aid guidelines state that you should not reach your fingers into your mouth to pick blindly, as this may push things deeper, and only take out visible solids with your fingers
Level of Evidence: B

Source: US National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus. Choking – adult or child over 1 year. <https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000047.htm>; Fuzhou Municipal Health Commission (2026). The Heimlich Method has been updated: "Infants, children and adults over 1 year old: changed from the old version of single abdominal shock to the cycle of "5 back slaps + 5 abdominal shocks"" "The first aid training of the Chinese Red Cross system has always been taught in the cycle of "5 back slaps + 5 abdominal shocks". <https://www.fuzhou.gov.cn/zgfzzt/swjw/fzwj/jkkp/202601/t20260108_5268351.htm>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, page 238: "First aid providers should not use a blind finger sweep in people with a foreign-body airway obstruction as this may push the object further down the person's airway". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>

Note: Do not reach into your mouth to pull out invisible things, as it will push it deeper. Don't photograph people who are still coughing. The beneficiaries are mainly family members who eat together. The teachings in China are also the same. The Fujian Provincial Red Cross Emergency Rescue Training Center said that the Chinese Red Cross system has always taught this way. For children over 1 year old and adults, do a cycle of 5 back pats and 5 abdominal thrusts. Many old tutorials on the Internet only teach abdominal thrusts, and that is an old version. For children under 1 year old, instead of pressing the belly, press the chest. See Article 43 of this section (Infant Choking).

Case: During a dinner party, a child choked on a peanut and was unable to speak. The adult immediately slapped the child five times on the back and punched the abdomen five times. The child coughed out the peanut, and the child resumed breathing. He was sent to the hospital for examination and was found to be fine.

items.title: If you get lost or your car breaks down in the Gobi, desert, or no-man’s land, stay where you are or next to the car. Report your location first, then provide shade and heat preservation, save water, and don’t wander around.
items.core: Stay where you are or next to the car. The car is the biggest shade.顺序是：有信号先发位置再打电话 → 遮阳保暖 → 省水 → 不乱走 → 用反光镜、烟、三堆火发信号。 Tell others your route, destination, return date and vehicle license plate before going in.
body: Cost: Tell others the route, destination, return date, and vehicle license plate before entering the uninhabited area. Starting from 4 liters of water per person per day. Satellite communicators or Beidou short message equipment cost thousands of yuan, and renting them costs a few hundred yuan each time. The difficult thing is to keep "staying where you are and not wandering around."

Benefit: The National Park Service's Mojave Desert page has three original sentences. One sentence is "At least 1 gallon (approximately 3.8 liters) of water per person per day, and 2 gallons per person per day for hikers and bicyclists."一句是「告诉别人你的路线、目的地、返回日期、车型和车牌」。 Another sentence is "Mobile phone signal is intermittent." Original text from Death Valley: "Don't hike at the valley bottom or at low altitudes when it's hot." There is "almost no cell phone signal" in the wilderness area. It is recommended to bring a satellite phone. Original text from the Mojave Desert Driving page: "In the event of an emergency, staying with your vehicle is the most important thing you can do." The page also says that it's not common, but people do die from exposure to heat or cold while walking back to the road. There are five steps to prioritization.第一步是报平安和坐标，有信号时先发位置再打电话。 The second step is to protect yourself from the sun and keep warm. The car is the biggest shelter. The third step is to save water. The fourth step is not to wander around. The fifth step is the signal. A reminder from the Chongqing Municipal Emergency Management Bureau: Three fires arranged in a triangle are an internationally accepted distress signal. When you get close, shout "three short, three long, three short" and repeat every 1 minute. When the sun is shining, use bright objects such as mirrors and can lids to reflect the light. The Ministry of Culture and Tourism reminds self-driving tourists to be cautious when traveling to uninhabited areas, travel with as many vehicles as possible, and rent satellite phones when necessary
Evidence level: C

Source: US National Park Service. Mojave National Preserve Safety. <https://www.nps.gov/moja/planyourvisit/safety.htm>; US National Park Service. Death Valley Safety. <https://www.nps.gov/articles/000/desertdrivingsafety.htm> ; Chongqing Emergency Management Bureau (2024). Emergency Science >> What you need to know about distress signals in the wild (long picture): "Set three flames is an internationally accepted distress signal. Arrange the fires in a triangle." "Three short beeps, three long beeps, and three short beeps; repeat after an interval of 1 minute." <https://yjj.cq.gov.cn/yjkp/scshaq/202409/t20240918_13639172.html> ; Ministry of Culture and Tourism (2018). The Ministry of Culture and Tourism reminds tourists to choose outdoor adventure travel carefully: "Be careful when going to uninhabited areas and sparsely populated areas" and "try to travel with as many vehicles as possible, prepare walkie-talkies in advance, and rent satellite phones if necessary." <https://www.mct.gov.cn/zxbs/cxts/201811/t20181127_836244.htm>

Note: The reason for level C is that these are official tips, not research data.饮水量、报备、信号覆盖、待在车旁、求救信号都是官方原话。 The official original text of the "three tones in a group" that has been circulated is not found, so the official three piles of fire and three short, three long and three short are used here. Don’t find your way on foot in the middle of the day. Don't drink urine. Don't skip drinking to save water.

Case: A self-driving tourist’s vehicle broke down in the Gobi Desert. He immediately waited beside the vehicle and sent its location. He used the car’s body to shade the vehicle and retained drinking water. He was successfully found by search and rescue personnel two days later.

items.title: Shivering, slurred speech, and swaying when walking are hypothermia. Change into wet clothes and wrap up, warm the torso first, and drink hot sweet drinks instead of alcohol
items.core: Hypothermia occurs when the body temperature drops below 35°C. People will tremble, sway when walking, and feel a little confused. If it is severe, they will not shake. Change out of wet clothes and wrap yourself in a sleeping bag, blanket, or thermal blanket to warm your torso first. If you are awake and able to swallow, give hot sweet drinks, but not alcohol. If the patient does not respond to the cry or is not breathing normally, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation according to Article 1 of this section (press the chest forcefully).
body: Cost: A few dollars for an aluminum foil thermal blanket, plus a spare dryer. It doesn't cost anything to learn to read signals.

Income: Original text from the National Weather Service: A body temperature below 95°F (35°C) is hypothermia. "If you feel cold, sluggish, or unable to think clearly, see a doctor immediately." The treatment is to "see a doctor immediately, move the person to a heated room, and rewarm the person starting from the center of the body" and give hot drinks. "Alcohol will reduce chills," so I don't drink it. "Perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation when unconscious", please refer to Article 1 of this section (not breathing normally) on how to judge whether or not to do so. Use warm water or body temperature to warm up frostbite. "Do not use hot water or radiant heat such as fireplaces." The Wilderness Medicine Society’s 2019 Hypothermia Guidelines are the guide for practitioners in this area. Symptoms of hypothermia listed in the International Red Cross's 2025 First Aid Guidelines include shivering, uncoordinated movements, slow movements, and a bit of confusion. After it gets worse, the person may no longer tremble, become confused, speak incoherently, and be unable to walk. The treatment is to have people take off wet clothes, dry them, and cover them to keep out the cold. If the person is awake and shivering, use a sleeping bag or blanket to warm himself up. Reflective materials can also be used. If you can swallow, give hot sweet drinks or high-energy foods. The guidelines also remind not to drink alcohol and not to rub his skin
Level of Evidence: B

Source: US National Weather Service. During Extreme Cold. <https://www.weather.gov/safety/cold-during> ; Dow J et al (2019). Wilderness Medical Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Out-of-Hospital Evaluation and Treatment of Accidental Hypothermia: 2019 Update. Wilderness & Environmental Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wem.2019.10.002>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 460–462: "shivering" "poor coordination" "slow movements" "mild confusion" "no shivering" "disorientation, lack of memory" "may the person cannot walk or use their hands. Have the person remove any wet clothes (or help them if they are unable to do so). Carefully dry off the person if they are wet. Cover and protect the person from the cold. If a person is responsive and shivering, let them warm up using a sleeping bag or a blanket. If they can swallow, give them a warm, sugary drink (e.g. hot chocolate) or some "high-energy food" "Alternative equipment may be used, including warm, dry clothing or reflective material" "Avoid alcohol" "Do NOT rub the person’s skin". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>

Note: Do not rub your hands and feet. Don't take a hot bath. Don't drag or drag it. People with severe hypothermia are prone to cardiac arrest. Don't think it's getting better just because "the shivering stops". The absence of shivering (the chills stop) means it's getting worse. The full text of the Wilderness Medical Society guide requires a subscription, only the abstract has been verified at this time.

Case: A hiker encountered a sudden rainfall in a mountainous area and his clothes were wet. He kept shivering and slurred his speech. His companion changed out of his wet clothes, wrapped his torso with a thermal blanket and gave him hot sugar water. His symptoms gradually improved.

items.title: If you are bitten by a snake, sit down and don't move. Take off your ring and watch. Send to the hospital as soon as possible to get antivenom. Do not cut, suck, or tie to death.
items.core: Sit down and don't move. Immobilize the bitten limb. Take off your ring and watch first to avoid swelling and strangulation. Send to a hospital with antivenom as soon as possible. Serum is the most effective way to prevent or reverse most venoms. No incision, no suction, no ice, no rubbing, no rope, and no walking. Take a photo of the snake if you can, don't catch it.
body: Cost: No money. Find out in advance which nearby hospital has antivenom. The hard thing is resisting taking care of the wound yourself.

Income: WHO The original text has three sentences. One sentence is "immediately and completely immobilize the bitten body part and quickly send it to the nearest medical institution for medical treatment." One sentence is "Avoid using tourniquets and avoid cutting wounds." Another sentence is "Treat with appropriate antivenom for the local snake species." "High-quality antivenom is the most effective treatment for preventing or reversing most of the toxic effects of snake bites." Globally, approximately 81,000 to 138,000 people die from snake bites each year, with amputations and permanent disabilities causing approximately three times the number of deaths. China's 2024 snakebite treatment guidelines estimate that there are 250,000 to 280,000 venomous snake bites in the country each year. Most of those bitten are people over 50 years old. Hospitals in the Yangtze River Basin and 11 southern provinces treated 40,817 snakebite patients from 2017 to 2021. There were 23 deaths during hospitalization (0.06%). The International Red Cross's 2025 First Aid Guidelines state: The bitten person should move as little as possible, and do not walk if the bite is on the leg. Remove jewelry, watches, and tight clothing to prevent swelling and choking of blood flow. Do not use a tourniquet, do not suction, do not apply cold compresses, do not rub, and do not cut with a knife. These methods are useless and may cause more injuries. Take photos of snakes when you can safely do so, do not catch or kill them
Level of Evidence: B

Source: WHO. Live reports on animal bites. <https://www.who.int/zh/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/animal-bites>; WHO (2023). Live reports on snake bites and poisoning. <https://www.who.int/zh/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/snakebite-envenoming> ; Lai R et al (2024). The Chinese guideline for management of snakebites. World Journal of Emergency Medicine 15(5):333-355: "An estimated 250,000–280,000 cases of venomous snakebites occur in China each year, affecting mainly aged patients. ≥50 years". <https://doi.org/10.5847/wjem.j.1920-8642.2024.076>; Yan S et al (2026). Clinical epidemiology of snakebite envenoming in hospitals 11 provinces of Yangtze River Basin and southern regions of China. PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases: "withdrawal (4346, 10.65%), and death (23, 0.06%)". <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pntd.0013247>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 339–341: "Remove jewelry, watches or tight clothing to prevent blood flow being restricted if there is swelling" "The following actions are not effective and may even cause further harm: applying a tourniquet, sucking out the venom, applying a cold compress, rubbing the bite, cutting the wound with a knife to increase bleeding" "Do not try to catch or kill the snake. Consider taking a photo". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>

Note: Take photos of snakes if you can, don’t catch them. Don't run, don't suck with your mouth, don't apply ice, and don't use a rope to strangle. There are no official statistics on snakebite deaths nationwide in China. The in-hospital mortality rate in those 11 provinces seems to be low, but more than 10% of the patients are discharged without treatment. Why are they not included in the statistics?

Case: A farmer was bitten on the ankle by a viper in the field. He sat still and took off his watch. His family sent him to a hospital with antivenom. The serum was injected in time and the swelling gradually subsided.

items.title: When there is an earthquake, first check what kind of house you are in: shelter in place in a building that meets the earthquake resistance requirements, and go out a few steps away from the door of an old house that may collapse
items.core: First check what kind of house you are in. If you have to go down the stairs or go through the hall to get out of a building built according to earthquake-resistant regulations, you should hide on the spot: protect your head and neck and get under the strong table and hold on to the table legs. Bungalows, old brick houses, self-built houses without earthquake protection, the door is just a few steps away, go out. Do not jump off the building, take the elevator, or go down the stairs while shaking under any circumstances.
body: Cost: No money. Take a look in advance at how many steps it takes to go out of your home, which way to go, and which table is sturdy.

Profit: China Earthquake Administration's popular science film "An earthquake is coming, should you hide or run?" "The mantra is "Escape nearby during an earthquake, and evacuate quickly after an earthquake" and clearly limits "this refers to buildings that meet earthquake resistance requirements." The reason is that such buildings are "less likely to collapse overall." The original article said that "falling building components and decorative items" "are the greatest threat to life safety." And "blindly running around without protective measures during an earthquake" "can easily be injured by falling ceilings, chandeliers (fans) and other objects." The method of hiding is to "protect your head and neck with your hands or other soft objects" and "hold the table legs firmly"; if there is no table, "quickly crouch close to the load-bearing wall" and "avoid external walls, windows, and balconies." "If you are outdoors," you "should evacuate to an open place to avoid shocks as soon as possible." Conversely, the 1988 Armenian earthquake was the collapse of Soviet-style prefabricated buildings in clumps. The case-control study from that time stated that "leaving the building after the first shock is a protective behavior." People who stayed indoors were more likely to be injured than those who ran outside, odds ratio 4.40, 95% CI 2.24–8.71 (credible range). The odds ratio for injury was 12.20 (3.62–63.79) when people were inside a building versus outside.
