The odds ratio for injury was 3.65 (2.12–6.33) in buildings with more than 5 floors compared with those in shorter buildings. Earthquake science popularization from the Ministry of Emergency Management states: "People living in old brick and concrete buildings should be more proactive in looking for opportunities and evacuate quickly." Those who live in bungalows, "if you are by the door or window, and there are no other dangerous buildings outside the window, you can immediately escape to the open space in the middle of the yard." During an earthquake, "never use the elevator", "don't choose to jump off the building to escape" if you live on the first or second floor, and "be careful not to go downstairs" if you are on a high floor. When outdoors, avoid buildings with glass curtain walls, overpasses, telephone poles, street lights and billboards.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: China Earthquake Administration (produced by Anhui Provincial Seismological Bureau). When an earthquake comes, should you hide or run? (Popular science video, subtitled transcription). <https://www.cea.gov.cn/cea/dzpd/dzcs/5537260/index.html>; Armenian HK, Noji EK, Oganesian AP (1992). A case-control study of injuries arising from the earthquake in Armenia, 1988. Bulletin of the World Health Organization, 70(2), 251-257. <https://europepmc.org/article/MED/1600585>; US FEMA Ready.gov. Earthquakes. <https://www.ready.gov/earthquakes>; Mahue-Giangreco M, Mack W, Seligson H, Bourque LB (2001). Risk factors associated with moderate and serious injuries attributable to the 1994 Northridge Earthquake. Annals of Epidemiology, 11(5), 347-357. <https://doi.org/10.1016/s1047-2797(01)00220-4>; Department of Emergency Management (2019). Earthquake self-rescue manual can save lives at critical moments! <https://www.mem.gov.cn/kp/zrzh/201904/t20190401_366172.shtml>; Ministry of Emergency Management (2019). Earthquake avoidance, self-rescue and mutual rescue common sense: "Never jump off the building in panic" "Avoid tall buildings or structures: buildings, especially buildings with glass curtain walls; Crossing street bridges and overpasses" "Avoid dangerous, tall or suspended objects: transformers, telephone poles, street lights, billboards, cranes, etc.". <https://www.mem.gov.cn/kp/zrzh/201902/t20190226_366163.shtml>; Emergency Management Department (2019). How to respond to earthquakes in different places: "If you are on a high-rise, be careful not to go downstairs." <https://www.mem.gov.cn/kp/zrzh/201903/t20190328_366164.shtml>

Remarks: Controversy, the two conclusions are for two types of houses. The China Earthquake Administration itself also wrote that the premise of "hiding" is "in a building that meets the requirements for earthquake resistance." It also requires "adapting measures to local conditions" and "different to each person", to see whether the building can withstand earthquakes, where you are, and whether you can run. The whole building in Armenia collapsed, and there was nowhere to hide, so you had the advantage of getting out. FEMA in the United States advises "get down on the spot, protect your head and neck, hold on tight, and don't run outside" for homes in this country. Injuries there mainly come from falling objects and falling while moving during shaking. Northridge's research also suggests that reaching for things and holding on to things that "seem stable" can worsen injuries. Therefore, it is useless to just ask "should you run?" You must judge "whether this building will collapse and whether you can reach the open space in a few seconds." For buildings that meet the requirements for earthquake resistance, if you need to go down the stairs or through the foyer, you should take shelter in place. Based on the buildings built in accordance with the regulations after 2001, this is a rough demarcation given by the author. The official text only says that "it meets the requirements for earthquake resistance." Bungalows, old brick houses, self-built houses without earthquake protection, the door is just a few steps away, go out. This Armenian study only compared the injured and uninjured survivors, but did not include the victims, nor did it explain whether the impact of floor height was deducted. People who can run out are likely to live in lower floors, so the numbers need to be discounted. Under no circumstances jump off the building, take the elevator, or go down the stairs while shaking. When outdoors, stay away from tall buildings, overpasses, telephone poles, glass curtain walls and billboards.

Case: When the earthquake occurred, the residents were in a high-rise residence that met the earthquake-resistant standards. They immediately got under the sturdy dining table to protect their heads and necks, held on to the table legs, and evacuated in an orderly manner after the shaking stopped.

items.title: If you encounter bears, wild boars, or packs of wild dogs, don’t run. Move sideways and slowly move away.
items.core: Don’t run if you encounter bears. They run up and down hills like racehorses. Don’t climb trees either. Black bears and brown bears can climb. Stop, keep talking to it in a low voice, wait for it to stop moving, and then slowly move away sideways. If a brown bear pounces on you, it will lie down and pretend to be dead, clasping the back of its neck with both hands. If a black bear pounces on you, it will run into the car or house. If it cannot escape, it will fight back. If bitten by a dog, flush and inject according to Article 13.
body: Cost: No money. Bring a hiking pole with you when you go into the mountains, and walk together and loudly to let the animals know you are coming. The hard thing is to stand still and not run away.

Benefit: The original National Park Service text about bears has six sentences. One sentence is "Don't run, a bear can run up and down hills as fast as a racehorse." One line is "Keep calm, most bears don't want to attack you, they just want to be left alone." One sentence is "Keep talking to the bear in a low voice." One sentence is "When the bear is still, turn sideways and slowly step away so that you can keep an eye on the bear without tripping." One sentence is "make yourself appear as big as possible." Another saying is "Don't climb trees, grizzly bears and black bears can climb trees." When attacked by a brown bear, he "played dead, lying down with his hands behind his neck and his legs spread apart." When attacked by a black bear, "Don't pretend to be dead. Run to a car or house. If you can't escape, fight back with whatever is at hand." Dog bites should be treated in accordance with Article 13
Level of Evidence: B

Source: US National Park Service. Staying Safe Around Bears. <https://www.nps.gov/subjects/bears/safety.htm>; General Affairs Department of the National Administration of Disease Control and Prevention, General Office of the National Health and Health Commission (2023). Rabies Exposure Prevention and Treatment Work Specifications (2023 Edition). <https://www.ndcpa.gov.cn/jbkzzx/c100014/common/content/content_1706569159854649344.html>

Note: Level B only corresponds to bears. For wild boars and wild dogs, "Don't run, retreat slowly, find high places or obstacles to block" is experience, which is considered level C. The official tips from the National Forestry and Grassland Administration and local forestry and grassland were not found this time. Don’t use food as a lure, don’t get close to take pictures, and don’t take dogs into mountains with wild boars. Most of the bears in China are black bears and brown bears. Whether they are pretending to be dead or not, it depends on these two types.

Case: A tourist came across a black bear while hiking in the mountainous area. He immediately stood still and chatted in a low voice, then slowly turned sideways and returned to the car without running. He waited for the bear to leave and drove away safely.

items.title: If you encounter a thunderstorm in the wild, get into a car or building with a hard top and avoid ridges, lone trees, water and metal
items.core: There is no safe place outdoors within the scope of a thunderstorm. Getting into a hard-top car or building, a convertible, a motorcycle, a tent, a pavilion, under a tree, or under a protruding rock does not count. Avoid open areas, ridge tops, isolated trees, water, and iron railings. If a group of people cannot walk, they should spread out and stand. Evacuate when you hear thunder. It is safe to wait 30 minutes after the last thunder.
body: Cost: No money. The cost is that the trip is interrupted for more than half an hour. The hard thing is to be willing to go back when the thunder is still far away.

Benefits: There is no safe place outdoors within the range of a thunderstorm. It is not safe until 30 minutes have elapsed since the last thunder. The National Weather Service states: Get into a sturdy building or a hard-top vehicle. A tent is completely unprotected from a lightning strike, and a picnic shelter open on all sides is unsafe. Cave entrances and small rock outcrops are also dangerous, as arcs can jump across gaps. Hiding under trees is the second leading cause of lightning casualties. When you hear thunder, you are probably within striking range. "When thunder strikes, get inside."
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National Weather Service. Outdoor lightning safety: "There is no safe place outside when thunderstorms are in the area" "Avoid open fields, the top of a hill or a ridge top. Stay away from tall, isolated trees or other tall objects" "Stay away from water, wet items, such as ropes, and metal objects, such as fences and "If you are in a group, spread out to avoid the current traveling between group members"; resume activities "Wait 30 minutes until after the last rumble of thunder"; "Remember, a tent offers NO protection from lighting" "Do NOT seek shelter under the beach picnic shelters" "Cave entrances are dangerous during thunderstorms. Small overhangs can allow arcs to cross the gap". <https://www.weather.gov/safety/lightning-outdoors>; National Weather Service. Lightning safety: "If you hear thunder, you are likely within striking distance of the storm" "When Thunder Roars, Go Indoors". casualties". <https://www.weather.gov/safety/lightning-myths>

Note: Tents, pavilions, under trees, and rock protrusions are not considered shelters. Hardtop cars count. Convertibles and motorcycles are not included. This is derived by the author from the condition of "hard top". Start evacuating when you hear thunder, don't wait for the rain to fall.

Case: A climber suddenly encountered a thunderstorm in the countryside. He quickly hid in a car with a hard top and closed the windows, staying away from the ridges and lone trees. He waited for thirty minutes after the last thunder to get out of the car.

items.title: When going to a plateau, slowly rise according to the sleeping altitude (how high you sleep that night). If your symptoms worsen, go down. Don’t push yourself.
items.core: It depends on how high you sleep, not how high you go during the day. Sleeping above 2450 meters will put you at risk of altitude sickness. After 3,000 meters, the sleeping altitude only increases by 500 meters every night, leaving one extra day to adapt to each liter of 1,000 meters. If you have a headache or nausea, don't sleep high. If it gets worse after resting, go down. I feel wobbly while walking and panting even when I don't move. Descending and inhaling oxygen are more effective than taking medicine.
body: Cost: Spend an extra day or two getting used to it. Preventive medicines are prescription medicines, so ask your doctor before departure. The hard thing is to be willing to set aside these days when your schedule is tight.

Benefits: Sleeping above 2450 meters puts you at risk of altitude sickness. High-altitude cerebral edema and pulmonary edema (water accumulation in the brain and lungs) will cause death if not evacuated to lower ground in time. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Yellow Book gives three rules for preventing severe illness: Know the early symptoms and be willing to admit them; when you have symptoms, no matter how mild they are, do not sleep at a higher altitude; if symptoms still worsen after resting or treatment at the same height, move down. Acute altitude sickness usually improves quickly when walking more than 300 meters downhill. High altitude cerebral edema requires immediate descent in remote areas and use dexamethasone and oxygen together if available. In most cases, people with high altitude pulmonary edema must descend immediately. Descending and inhaling oxygen are much more effective than taking medicine.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Yellow Book High Altitude Travel and Altitude Sickness: "Any unacclimatized traveler proceeding to a sleeping altitude of ≥2,450 m (≥8,000 ft)—and sometimes lower—is at risk for altitude illness"; ascent rate "500 m (1,650 ft) per night in sleeping altitude once above 3,000 m (9,800 ft)", every 1,000 Mega one day acclimatization day; Acetazolamide prevention "125 mg twice a day; 250 mg twice a day if >100 kg body weight"; having HACE" "Descent and oxygen are much more effective treatments than medication". <https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/environmental-hazards-risks/high-altitude-travel-and-altitude-illness.html>; Wilderness & Environmental Medicine (2024). Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Acute Mountain Sickness (2024 Update). Wilderness & Environmental Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wem.2023.05.013>

Note: The calculation is "how high you sleep", not how high you reach during the day. If you have symptoms, stop sleeping in high places. If symptoms get worse after resting, go back down. If you stagger while walking, have a change of consciousness, or can't breathe even without moving, you may have cerebral edema or pulmonary edema, and you should evacuate immediately in the wild. Taking medicine is not as good as evacuation and oxygen inhalation.

Case: Xiao Wang went from the plains to Daocheng. He slept at 3300 meters on the first night and suffered from headache and nausea. On the second day, he pushed himself to 4200 meters and slept at 4200 meters. He was so breathless that he couldn't sleep in the middle of the night. He quickly descended to 3300 meters in the morning and took oxygen. His symptoms were significantly relieved two hours later.

items.title: If you are bitten by a tick, use pointed tweezers against the skin to pull it out steadily. Do not apply oil or burn it.
items.core: Use pointed tweezers to grasp the tick as close to the skin as possible and pull it out firmly. Don't apply Vaseline or burn it with fire, as this will stimulate it to squeeze pathogen-laden body fluids into the skin. Don't twist and pull, as it can easily break the mouthparts in the flesh. After I pulled it out, I recorded the date. In the next few weeks, I had fever and rash, and when I saw a doctor, I took the initiative to say that I had been bitten by a tick.
body: Cost: A pair of pointed tweezers.

Benefits: The CDC's extraction method is to use clean pointed tweezers to hold the tick as close to the skin as possible and pull it out with steady, even force. Applying petroleum jelly, nail polish, or grilling the ticks can irritate ticks and squeeze pathogen-laden body fluids into the skin. Twisting or tugging, it is easy to break the part of the mouth (mouthparts) that is stuck in the flesh. If you develop a rash or fever within a few weeks of removal, see your doctor and tell him if you were bitten by a tick recently and when. Ticks can transmit a disease in China called fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome. There were 6,602 cases and 306 deaths reported nationwide in 2024, both the most since the disease was discovered. The average case fatality rate from 2010 to 2024 is 4.79%. The older you are, the higher it is. For those over 85 years old, it is 9.15%.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. After a tick bite: "Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible using clean fine-tipped tweezers" "Pull tick away from the skin with steady, even pressure" "Do not use petroleum jelly, heat, nail polish, or other substances to try and make the tick detach from the skin. This may agitate the tick and force infected fluid from the tick into the skin" "Don't twist or jerk the tick. This can cause the tick mouthparts to break off and remain in the skin" "If you develop a rash or fever within several weeks of removing a tick, see your doctor" "Tell the doctor about your recent tick bite" "When the bite occurred". in China, 2010–2024: a fifteen-year national surveillance analysis. BMC Infectious Diseases 26:1497: "The number of reported cases (6,602 cases) and deaths (306 cases) in 2024 were both the highest levels since the discovery of this disease" "The average CFR was 4.79%, and the CFR increased with age, reaching 9.15% among those aged 85 years and above". <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12879-026-14066-z>

Note: Write down the date after unplugging. In the following weeks, I had fever, rash, and fatigue. When I saw a doctor, I volunteered that I had been bitten by a tick. If the doctor doesn't ask or you don't tell, it's easy to be treated as if you have a cold.

Case: Lao Zhou came home from hiking and found a tick biting his armpit. He used pointed tweezers to hold the tick against the skin and pull it out steadily without applying oil or burning, and recorded the date. Three weeks later, when he developed a fever and rash and went to the doctor, he proactively informed the doctor of his tick bite history. The doctor promptly provided symptomatic treatment and he recovered quickly.

items.title: All water in the wild should be boiled before drinking. Boiling for one minute is enough. At common travel altitudes, there is no need to boil water because of the high altitude.
items.core: All microorganisms that can cause illness in drinking water die within a few seconds at boiling temperatures. Rolling for another minute is just a margin for "mistakes". At common travel altitudes, there is no need to cook more because of the high altitude. If you can't burn it, use a filter or disinfectant tablet. Each of these two has pathogens that cannot be covered. It can burn or burn. Even clear streams may contain parasites.
body: Cost: Carrying the weight of an extra stove and fuel.

Benefits: All microorganisms that can cause illness by drinking water will be killed (inactivated) in a few seconds at the boiling temperature of the water. "High-altitude water cannot be properly heated" is a common misunderstanding. The same page notes that the other two approaches have shortcomings: Most portable filters don't block viruses; chlorine and iodine barely kill the parasite Cryptosporidium at practical doses. In places where there is a lot of human and animal activity, clear surface water should also be protected against all intestinal pathogens, including Cryptosporidium. Off-the-beaten-path wild water, mainly resistant to giardia and intestinal bacteria
Level of Evidence: B

Source: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Yellow Book·Water Disinfection for Travelers: "All organisms that may cause illness from drinking water are killed within seconds at boiling temperature" "CDC recommends that travelers boil water for a full minute to account for user variability in identifying boiling points and to add a margin of safety" "Although the boiling point for water decreases with increasing elevation, at common travel elevations the temperature needed to achieve boiling is still well above the temperature required to inactivate enteric pathogens" "Many filters do not reliably remove viruses" "Cryptosporidium, is poorly inactivated by chlorine- or iodine-based disinfection at practical concentrations"; Table 1.8.3 lists the main threat to "Clear surface water near human and animal activity" as "All enteric pathogens, including Cryptosporidium". <https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/preparing-international-travelers/water-disinfection-for-travelers.html>

Note: The same page also says that it doesn’t have to actually boil: 60°C for 30 minutes is equally effective, and boiling is just an endpoint that can be seen without a thermometer. If you can't burn it, use a filter or chemical disinfectant tablets. Both of them have pathogens that cannot be covered. If you can burn it, burn it. Even streams that look clear may contain parasites, so don’t judge by their appearance.

Case: Xiao Li was hiking in a mountainous area at an altitude of 3,500 meters. He cooked noodles with clear stream water. After boiling the water for one minute, he turned off the heat and ate it. The travel companion who was traveling with him was worried that the food would not boil due to the high altitude, so Multi insisted on cooking it for ten more minutes. As a result, Xiao Li was fine, but the travel companion had diarrhea due to eating half-cooked food.

items.title: If a stranger asks for money in the wilderness, give him the money, don't do anything, remember his characteristics, and call the police after you escape.
items.core: When you are blocked and your personal safety is threatened, save your life first instead of taking risks or chasing for money. After the other party takes the money and leaves, recovering the property may still be considered legitimate self-defense, but it depends on the situation and means at the scene. After escaping, note down the physical appearance, accent, license plate and escape direction, and call 110.
body: Cost: Cash on the person. The hard part is suppressing the anger.

Benefit: Life is more valuable than money, and what the other party risked for a few hundred dollars was a serious crime. Article 263 of the Criminal Law stipulates that whoever robs public or private property by violence, coercion or other methods shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years and shall also be fined. Possessing a gun, breaking into a house, causing serious injury or death, etc. will result in a sentence of more than ten years or even the death penalty. The legitimate defense protection in Article 20 of the Criminal Law "stops ongoing unlawful infringement." The 2020 guidance of the two high-level organizations and the First Department states that although property has been taken away, if it can be recovered through chasing and blocking, it can be regarded as the infringement is still ongoing. Whether it can be considered legitimate defense depends on the situation and the purpose of stopping the infringement. To determine that the defense is excessive, it must simultaneously meet the requirements of clearly exceeding the necessary limit and causing significant damage. Just because the other party takes the money and turns around doesn't mean the defense is over. For your own safety, don't take risks or chase for money. Immediately after escaping, note down the physical appearance, accent, license plate, escape direction, and call 110
Evidence level: C

Source: National People's Congress (amended in 2020). Criminal Law (Articles 20, 263). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html> (Reprinted and integrated text by Beijing Public Security and Traffic Management Bureau); Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security (2020). Guidance on the application of the legitimate defense system in accordance with the law, points 6, 8, and 11. <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/251611.html>

Note: The reason for level C is that "it is safer to give money without confrontation" and there is no direct documentation. The law only explains the other party's risks and your boundaries. Whether it is legitimate defense still needs to be verified, and you may be investigated and detained before being determined. For process costs, see Section 8, Article 11 (You can fight back against an infringement that cannot be avoided). Don’t follow him to a remote place to “get money”. Don't hand over your mobile phone password. Don't get in the other person's car. Pay money first only when you are blocked in person and your personal safety is threatened. You can still call the police after you escape. If someone uses private photos or nude chat videos online to ask for money, the opposite is true. You cannot give a penny. See Section 8, Article 32 (the other party uses excuses to ask for money). Don’t expect to bring sling sticks, stun guns, and daggers with you. You will be punished if you take them out. See Section 9, Article 26 (Don’t buy sling sticks or stun guns for self-defense).

Case: Lao Chen was stopped by a gangster on a mountain path late at night and demanded money. He immediately handed over his wallet and mobile phone without resisting or chasing him. Afterwards, he remembered the other person’s appearance and direction of escape. After getting away, he immediately called 110 to call the police. The police quickly arrested the suspect based on clues.

items.title: If you see a group of people fighting, retreat and leave. Don't go up to start a fight, don't watch, and don't pick up people on the ground. If you want to call the police, retreat to a safe distance and call 110
items.core: If you make a move, breaking up the fight becomes joining the fight. What you should do is to retreat and leave. Those who actively participate in mass brawls will be sentenced to less than 3 years in prison. If there are a large number of people, cause serious disorder on the road, or take someone else's money, the sentence will be 3 to 10 years. If you are willing to call the police, retreat to a safe distance and call 110. Tell them clearly the location, how many people are there, whether anyone has a knife or stick, and whether anyone is lying down and not moving.
body: Cost: No money. The hard thing is to resist the urge to step forward and give someone a hand, and to stand and watch the excitement. After calling the police, you may be interviewed once to take notes, which may take up to half a day.

Profit: Article 292 of the Criminal Law: "In the event of a fight involving a crowd, the ringleaders and other active participants shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention or surveillance." Those who gather to fight many times, those who are large in number and have a bad social impact, those who cause serious disorder in public places or traffic thoroughfares, and those who are armed, "will be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years." "Those who gather to fight and cause serious injury or death will be convicted and punished as intentional injury or intentional homicide." The Public Security Administration Punishment Law also has penalties. Assaulting another person is punishable by 5 to 10 days of detention and a fine of 500 to 1,000 yuan. Those who fight in groups will be treated as picking quarrels and provoking trouble, and will be detained for up to 15 days and fined 2,000 yuan. Article 5 of the "Guiding Opinions on the Lawful Application of the Justifiable Defense System": Unlawful infringement "includes illegal infringement directed at the individual, as well as unlawful infringement that endangers national or public interests or is directed at others." Article 9 of the Opinion states that if one party strikes first and the means are obviously excessive, the fighting back should generally be considered a defensive act. The same is true if one party strikes first and continues to infringe despite the other party's efforts to avoid conflict
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Articles 232, 234, 292, 305, 310). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishment Law (revised in 2025, Articles 30 and 51). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; Supreme People’s Court, Supreme People’s Procuratorate, and Ministry of Public Security (2020). Guidance on the application of the legitimate defense system in accordance with the law (Fafa [2020] No. 31, Articles 5 and 9). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/251611.html>; National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (revised in 2018, Articles 62, 110, 111, 193). Full text reproduced by the People's Procuratorate of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region <https://www.nx.jcy.gov.cn/zwsy/qwfb/202011/t20201119_608817.html>

Remarks: B is determined because there are hard provisions on the consequences, but there is no official original text for the step of "retreating from the police and not engaging in a fight." It is deduced from the provisions and "how to identify a fight." "I'm here to break up the fight" is not a talisman. It determines whether you hit someone or not, and who you hit. If the opponent has fallen to the ground or ran away, and you catch up and fight, it is no longer considered defense. If you see someone being surrounded and being beaten unilaterally, you can indeed stop it legally. Justifiable defense protects not only yourself, but also others. But going up with bare hands would probably just add another wounded person. Calling people, recording from a distance, and calling the police are more effective. "Don't get involved, don't watch" will only benefit you. The benefits of calling 110 mainly fall on the person on the ground, who belongs to the lowest category of beneficiaries in this book. You can weigh it yourself whether you are willing to spend this time. There are a few things to know before weighing in. The obligation to testify is inherent: Article 62 of the Criminal Procedure Law states that anyone who knows the circumstances of the case has the obligation to testify, and it will not disappear if this call is not made. Even if there is serious injury or life, the police will still find the people present through surveillance. Standing around and watching is the easiest way to get registered. If the person who reports the case does not want his name to be made public, the case-handling agency "should keep him secret" (Article 111). Tell clearly the location, the number of people, and whether you have someone to take, then you can hang up without having to stay where you are. You will be reprimanded or detained for less than ten days when the court notifies you to appear in court and you refuse to testify without a valid reason (Article 193). Passers-by rarely make it this far. Failure to call the police is not illegal in itself: Article 110 of the Criminal Procedure Law says "you have rights and obligations" and there is no penalty. There is no crime in the criminal law that punishes ordinary people for failing to report information. Walking away is a legal option. There are only two red lines after walking away. One is helping Tibetans afterwards or providing false evidence to cover up (Criminal Law Article 310, less than 3 years, 3 to 10 years in serious cases). The second is intentionally giving false testimony when called to testify (Article 305, less than 3 years, or 3 to 7 years in serious cases). Silence and telling the truth are both okay, only making up words is okay. If you are involved in a conflict, see Section 8, Article 10, if you are asked for money by a stranger, please see Section 36 of this section, and if you save money after rescuing an injured person, see Section 39 of this section.

Case: Xiao Zhang encountered two groups of people fighting each other with wine bottles at the night market. He did not step forward to start a fight or watch. He immediately retreated a hundred meters away and called 110. He explained the location, the number of people and who was carrying equipment, and then left. The police arrived and quickly controlled the situation. Xiao Zhang was not injured and was not involved in the lawsuit.

items.title: If you may be exposed to HIV, get blocking medicine within 72 hours. The sooner the better
items.core: If you suspect that you may be exposed to HIV, 72 hours is the hard line. Try to take the medicine within 2 hours, preferably no more than 24 hours. The medicine must be taken for 28 days. The trail is gone after 72 hours, so don’t wait until the next day to decide.
body: Cost: A 28-day course of treatment costs thousands of dollars, and most areas pay for it themselves. I had to go to the hospital that night. The difficult thing is to admit on the spot that you may be infected and go out immediately.

Income: The Beijing Municipal People’s Government’s anti-AIDS science section states: Preventive medication after exposure is called post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), and preventive medication should be “administered within 2 hours as much as possible, preferably within 24 hours and no more than 72 hours.” Also "take it for 28 consecutive days." It is no longer recommended to start after 72 hours. This is a hard time limit. The Beijing article also stated that "taking medication regularly every day has a better blocking effect than frequently missing doses." The technical guidelines from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention state that missing doses and stopping medication on your own will reduce the preventive effect. The guidelines require follow-up for drug side effects in the second week after starting the drug, and HIV and hepatitis C antibody testing at 30 and 90 days after exposure. The Chongqing Center for Disease Control and Prevention announced in 2024 that there are 29 outpatient clinics in 26 districts and counties in the city that can prescribe pre- and post-exposure preventive drugs, 14 of which provide 24-hour services
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Beijing Municipal People's Government. Can't tell the difference between before and after? Six questions and six answers to comprehensively understand HIV pre-exposure/post-exposure prophylaxis. <https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/jhsyfwzdzx/sjazbr/fakp/202311/t20231110_3299397.html>; Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Center for STD and AIDS Prevention and Control (2020). Technical Guidelines for HIV Post-Exposure Prevention (Trial): "Drug users may stop taking the drug due to intolerance to the side effects, or miss doses for other reasons. These will reduce the preventive effectiveness of the drug." "Doctors should follow up with HIV and HCV antibody testing on the patient 30 days and 90 days after the patient is exposed." <https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkyj/crb2/yl/azb/jswj_azb/202410/t20241027_302131.html>; Chongqing Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2024). Guidelines for the construction of standardized procedures for 24-hour outpatient clinics for HIV post-exposure prophylaxis were released in Chongqing. Many hospitals have provided round-the-clock services: "The number of institutions in Chongqing that provide pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis drug services has increased to 29 outpatient clinics in 26 districts and counties." "The number of outpatient clinics that can provide 24-hour all-weather services has reached 14." <https://www.cqcdc.org/index.php?a=shows&catid=2270&id=3045>

Remarks: Where to get it: The designated AIDS medical institution designated by the local Center for Disease Control and Prevention, usually the Department of Infectious Diseases (STD and AIDS Clinic). Some cities have set up 24-hour clinics, such as Chongqing. Before going, call the local disease control number and ask which hospital has medicine. Don’t waste time in the emergency department. Situations that are considered "exposure" include unprotected sexual intercourse, broken condoms, pricks from needles, and blood on mucous membranes. Whether or not to use medication is up to the doctor's discretion. The medicine must be taken for 28 days. Missing a dose will reduce its effectiveness. Then follow medical advice at 30 and 90 days after exposure. Blocking drugs are only remedies and cannot replace usual prevention. For daily prevention and testing, see Section 1, Items 30 and 31 (use condoms at all times, and get checked if you have high-risk behaviors).

Case: Xiao Li was exposed to a high risk of HIV infection in an accident. Less than 2 hours after the incident, he immediately rushed to the emergency department of the infectious disease hospital and started taking blocking drugs (PEP) under the guidance of a doctor. He took the medicine in strict accordance with the requirements for 28 consecutive days without missing a dose. He was reexamined 1 month and 3 months later, and the results were negative. Doctors pointed out that the sooner the drug is taken after exposure, the better. It will still be effective within 72 hours, but beyond the time limit, the blocking effect will be significantly reduced.

items.title: If you save someone who is injured and you get money, first find the perpetrator and the medical insurance, and then go and declare a righteous act to confirm it
items.core: Save someone and help yourself, don’t admit that you are unlucky. Those who are brave enough to be injured will be treated first and charged later. The medical expenses will be borne by the perpetrator. If the person runs away or cannot afford compensation, the basic medical insurance will be used. If you do not harm anyone, if you bring it up, the person you saved should be given appropriate compensation in accordance with the law. At the same time, go to declare for righteousness to confirm that if you are injured and meet the conditions, you will be treated as work-related injury insurance.
body: Cost: No money. To apply, you need to submit documents and wait for certification, which can take several weeks to several months.

Income: Article 183 of the Civil Code: "If one is harmed by protecting the civil rights and interests of others, the infringer shall bear civil liability, and the beneficiary may provide appropriate compensation. If there is no infringer, the infringer has escaped or is unable to bear civil liability, and the victim requests compensation, the beneficiary shall provide appropriate compensation." The State Council issued [2012] No. 39 talks about what to do if you act bravely for the injured. Medical institutions must establish green channels and "adhere to the principle of 'treat first, charge later'". The original text of the medical expenses section is "Medical expenses incurred due to emergency treatment, if there is an infringer or responsible person, shall be borne by the infringer or responsible person; if there is no infringer or responsible person, and if the infringer or responsible person escapes or is unable to bear it, it shall be settled through the basic medical security system in accordance with regulations." Those who die, "those who meet the conditions for martyr assessment will be assessed as martyrs in accordance with the law"; "those who are treated as work-related injuries will enjoy a one-time work-related death benefit and a special survivor's benefit equivalent to 40 months' salary." For those who are disabled, "those who meet the conditions for enjoying work-related injury insurance benefits will receive corresponding benefits in accordance with the "Work-related Injury Insurance Regulations"; if they do not meet the requirements, the civil affairs department will assess the disability level and implement corresponding benefits." In terms of employment, "employment assistance will be given priority and key support will be provided", and public welfare positions will be "prioritized for those who meet the requirements and are brave enough to do justice." In terms of housing, "priority will be included in the housing security system, priority will be given to renting and allocating affordable housing or issuing housing rental subsidies"
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 183). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; forwarded by the General Office of the State Council to the Ministry of Civil Affairs and other departments (2012). Opinions on Strengthening the Protection of the Rights and Interests of Persons Who Serve as Volunteers (Guobanfa [2012] No. 39). <https://www.gov.cn/zwgk/2012-07/26/content_2191928.htm>

Note: B is determined because the treatment you can receive is determined by national documents. However, the amount of bonuses and how they are determined are determined by each province’s own regulations. The figures vary from place to place and have not been verified on a province-by-province basis this time. Generally, a report is made to the public security agency or a volunteer organization (foundation) in the place where the accident occurred. Whether it can be determined depends on the evidence: the police receipt, on-site surveillance, the names and phone numbers of witnesses, and hospital medical records, all left on the spot. If you want to litigate, the civil rights of acting bravely are within the scope of free legal aid. For the national standard of one-time work-related death benefit and how to convert the disability level into money, see Section 19, Articles 14 and 15. How to apply for legal aid is provided in Section 7, Article 3.

Case: Xiao Liu was passing by the river to rescue a child who had fallen into the water. He was scratched by a stone and needed 5 stitches. He went to the parents of the child to explain the situation, and the parents gave him appropriate compensation. He then went to apply for a voluntary act and got confirmation. The medical expenses were reimbursed by the insurance company according to work-related injury insurance benefits, and he did not pay a penny.

items.title: If a knife, steel bar, or glass is inserted into the body, apply pressure around the foreign object to stop the bleeding. Do not pull it out
items.core: Pulling it out may cause heavy bleeding and make it more difficult for doctors to judge the depth of the injury. Call 120, apply pressure around the foreign object to stop the bleeding, and secure the foreign object to prevent it from shaking. Expose the internal organs on the belly, do not tuck it back, and cover it with a clean, wet dressing. Don't seal the wounds on your chest. If there is no bleeding, leave them open. Don't cover them tightly when you apply pressure. Sealing them may deflate the lungs.
body: Cost: Nothing. The hard thing is to resist the instinct to "pull it out first" and wait for the ambulance.

Benefit: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies 2025 International First Aid Guidelines: "The person giving first aid should apply pressure around a foreign object (such as a knife) that has penetrated the body, stabilize the foreign object, and do not pull it out." "Do not pull out any foreign objects inserted into wounds in the abdomen or chest. Pulling them out may cause severe bleeding and make it more difficult for doctors to determine the severity of the injury." "Foreign objects stuck in the body should be stabilized; if the foreign object beats with the pulse, just let it beat and hold it loosely." "First aid providers should not stuff exposed internal organs back into the body." For an open wound on the stomach where the internal organs are visible, "you can cover it with a sterile or clean enough wet dressing." Open chest wall wounds that are not gushing blood "can be left open without dressings, because sealing the wound may allow air to accumulate in the chest cavity, causing partial or complete collapse of the lung (pneumothorax)." When applying pressure to a chest wall wound to stop bleeding, "make sure that the pressure does not completely seal the wound. If the wound is bubbling or making noise, do not completely seal the wound." All penetrating chest and abdominal wounds require immediate emergency call
Level of Evidence: B

Source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 256–257, 267–268; Thoracic and abdominal injuries section: "A sterile (or functionally clean) and wet dressing may be placed on open abdominal wounds where internal organs are visible" "If applying pressure to an open chest wound, ensure the pressure does not completely seal the wound. If the wound is bubbling or making noise, do not completely seal the wound."

Note: B is set because this is the accepted practice in the guidelines. Without randomized trials, the injured cannot be divided into two groups: "pull out" and "no pull out". When you arrive at the hospital, go directly to the priority table (pre-examination triage table) at the entrance of the emergency department and report "penetrating injury" instead of queuing at the registration window. According to Beijing’s triage standards, patients with severe bleeding and severe pain can be classified as Level 2 and must be admitted to the emergency room (see Section 24, Article 7 (Emergency Pre-examination Triage Table)). If the puncture is really punctured, call 120. Beijing’s plan requires emergency doctors to notify the hospital in advance to prepare for treatment of level 1 and 2 patients. How to apply pressure and apply a tourniquet on heavy bleeding, please refer to Article 12.

Case: Construction worker Lao Zhang accidentally fell from a height during construction. A steel bar penetrated his thigh and he was in critical condition. The workers did not pull out the steel bars, but immediately called 120 and used clean gauze to wrap pressure around the steel bars and fix the steel bars to prevent them from shaking. After being sent to the hospital, the doctor said that because the foreign body was not removed, uncontrollable massive bleeding was avoided, and time was bought for surgery to remove the foreign body and determine whether the blood vessels were damaged. Lao Zhang finally saved his leg.

items.title: If you suspect a fracture, don't move that part. Hold it still and apply cold compress for 20 minutes. Do not straighten it by yourself.
items.core: Injuries to the hands and feet should be treated as fractures first, even if they can stand and move. Keep the injured area still, support it with your hands or use a hard board to hold it in place, and apply cold compresses for no more than 20 minutes at a time. Don't straighten it yourself. If the bone pokes out of the skin, stop bleeding first. Don't press it back. X-rays may miss fractures. If the X-rays are normal but the doctor still suspects a fracture or ligament injury, follow the doctor's instructions for a review or MRI.
body: Cost: Nothing. Find a hard board, rolled up magazine, or clothing for support. Put cold things in a cloth layer.

Benefits: The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies has released the 2025 International First Aid Guidelines. It says "Any injury on the hands or feet should be treated first as a possible fracture." It also says, "The only accurate way to diagnose a fracture is to take an X-ray. If you're not sure, treat it like a fracture." The purpose of immobilization is to "minimize movement and pain." Apply cold compresses "for up to 20 minutes at a time to reduce pain; cold for longer than that may damage the skin." "When you injure a long bone like the femur, the bleeding from the bone itself can be fatal." If you have obvious pain or swelling, show signs of shock, have a fractured femur (thigh bone), or have a clearly incorrect limb position, you should call emergency services. For fractures that are bent into angles, two conditions must be met at the same time before they can be considered to be broken back to their original position (reduction) on site. One is that "the location is remote (or the conditions are limited), and the limbs below the angle are cold or white, or the emergency personnel cannot fix it for moving." Second, the rescuer is trained. For open fractures (where the broken bone breaks the skin), bleeding and infection must be stopped first. But just because the first X-ray didn't show it, doesn't mean there's no fracture. The UK's National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has a guideline on hip fractures. It says: If the X-ray is normal but a hip fracture is still suspected, "do an MRI (magnetic resonance)." If it cannot be done within 24 hours, consider doing CT. NICE's fracture guideline states: If a fracture of the scaphoid of the wrist is suspected, "after careful physical examination, consider an MRI first." The navicular bone is a small bone in the wrist. A summary of the literature by Cochrane states: "Initial X-rays cannot exclude fracture." In studies it included, the median rate of actual fractures among people with normal X-rays but whose doctors still suspected a scaphoid fracture was 20 percent. The American College of Radiology has standards for the examination of knee injuries. It states: If no fracture is visible on X-ray, but there is still suspicion of a hidden fracture or internal joint damage, an MRI is "usually appropriate" as the next step. It also writes that MRI is very accurate in detecting hidden fractures, meniscal and ligament injuries.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 301–302. National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2011). Hip fracture: management. NICE guideline CG124, clause 1.1.1. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg124/chapter/Recommendations>; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2016). Fractures (non-complex): assessment and management. NICE guideline NG38, clause 1.2.3. ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Acute Trauma to the Knee, Variant 3. American College of Radiology. <https://acsearch.acr.org/docs/69419/Narrative/>

Note: B is set because these are accepted practices. There is only one study that reviewed old medical records to perform traction and fixation on femur (thigh bone) fractures before being sent to the hospital, and the credibility of the evidence is very low. The results were fewer blood transfusions over 24 hours, shorter hospital stays, and differences in death and complications that were too small to tell. As for whether to reset (put the bones back to their original positions) or fix them as they are, no evidence was found at all. There are three common misunderstandings. Being able to stand and walk does not mean that there are no fractures. Use only cold compresses, not hot compresses, and do not alternate between hot and cold. Sprains will not be cured by "moving away", they must rest first. Don't quit smoking until your bones have grown, see Section 2, Item 1 (Quiting Smoking). Don’t expect to take calcium supplements or drink bone broth to make your bones grow faster. See Section 6, Item 30 (take calcium supplements after a fracture). The contraindications for moving elderly people with suspected fractures after a fall are listed in Article 2. If a leg becomes swollen after being put in a cast or lying in bed, be alert for blood clots. See No. 11. After treatment, please see Section 24, Articles 9 and 10 for whether you need to have a disability appraisal and whether you need to apply for a disability certificate.

Case: The aunt stepped down the stairs and her ankle was swollen and painful but she could still walk. She did not rub it or straighten it by herself. She held the injured area with her hands and fixed it in place with a hard board. She went home and applied cold compress for 15 minutes. She went to the hospital to take a film to confirm the slight bone fracture. After resting according to the doctor's instructions, she recovered smoothly without any sequelae.

items.title: After being sexually assaulted, go to a safe place and call 110 first; do not take a shower, do not wash clothes, do not clean up the room before the injury examination, and go to the hospital within 72 hours
items.core: The marks left on the body, clothes and in the house are the most important evidence to identify the other party. Therefore, try not to take a shower, wash clothes, or clean the room before the injury examination, and call 110 as soon as possible. Emergency contraceptive pills are available in pharmacies and are more effective the sooner you take them. Go to the hospital within 72 hours and let the doctor decide whether to take blocking drugs.
body: Cost: There is no cost to call the police. Emergency contraceptive pills are over-the-counter and can be purchased at pharmacies. A course of blocking drugs costs thousands of dollars. It is up to the doctor to decide whether to take them. See Article 38 of this section (get the blocking drugs within 72 hours). What was difficult was that it was difficult to speak at the time and I wanted to take a shower right away.

Gains: A prosecutor from the Beijing Municipal People’s Procuratorate said: “Whether a minor or an adult is violated, they should dial 110 to call the police as soon as possible.” Calling the police and seeking medical treatment in a timely manner "facilitates the investigation agency's timely investigation of the scene, extraction of traces of physical evidence, and fixation of evidence." The People's Daily Sexual Assault Prevention Handbook reprinted by the Guizhou Provincial Department of Civil Affairs states: "Once you unfortunately encounter sexual assault, the most important thing is to retain evidence." It is necessary to keep "evidences such as body fluids, hair, dander, communication records, etc." and "after being violated, do not take a bath, wash clothes, clean the room, or throw away things without authorization." If an acquaintance commits a crime, keep records of phone calls and correspondence. If the other party threatens or bribes you afterwards, you must also leave evidence. The Xicheng District People's Procuratorate of Beijing wrote: "Try not to take a shower before undergoing a physical examination." The World Health Organization says emergency contraception can be used "when a woman has been sexually assaulted without effective contraceptive protection." It is recommended to use it within 5 days, the earlier the more effective it is. Emergency contraceptive pills containing levonorgestrel, a progestin, have a pregnancy rate of 1.2 to 2.1 percent in women who use them. Levonorgestrel tablets sold in domestic pharmacies are over-the-counter drugs. The Wuhan Municipal Health Commission says: "Within 72 hours after unprotected sex, the sooner you take the medicine, the better the effect of preventing pregnancy." HIV-blocking drugs should be taken within 2 hours as much as possible, and no later than 72 hours (nationwide)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Beijing Municipal People's Procuratorate (2024). Watch dramas with Fayan丨Watch "The Prosecutor of Nine Parts" How should minors protect themselves in the face of illegal infringement? (Reprinted from China Central Radio and Television Station’s Voice of China). <https://www.bjjc.gov.cn/c/bjoweb/mtbg1/75046.jhtml>; Guizhou Provincial Department of Civil Affairs (2024). Minors Sexual Assault Prevention Manual, parents and children please check it out! (Reprinted from People’s Daily). <https://mzt.guizhou.gov.cn/xwzx/mzyw/202407/t20240723_85145012.html>; People’s Procuratorate of Xicheng District, Beijing (2018). Why are they no longer silent…. <https://www.bjjc.gov.cn/c/xicheng/xjjsl/320654084.jhtml>; World Health Organization (2021). Emergency contraception (fact report). <https://www.who.int/zh/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/emergency-contraception>; Wuhan Municipal Health Commission (2020). Safe and reasonable use of emergency contraception. <https://wjw.wuhan.gov.cn/ztzl_28/fyjkkp/szjk/202010/t20201009_1461161.shtml>; Beijing Municipal People’s Government. Can’t tell the difference between before and after? Six questions and six answers to comprehensively understand HIV pre-exposure/post-exposure prophylaxis. <https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/jhsyfwzdzx/sjazbr/fakp/202311/t20231110_3299397.html>

Note: The reason given is B because these are official case handling experience and medication recommendations. There is no figure on "how much higher the conviction rate will be after following these instructions." The beneficiaries are mainly yourself and your family. The 72 hours for emergency contraceptive pills is the standard in the domestic instructions. The World Health Organization says that it is effective within 5 days, but the later the worse, the worse it is. Don’t delay. If you are already pregnant, emergency contraceptive pills have no effect. When calling the police, tell the truth, without concealing or exaggerating. If the other party cheats on you, gives you money, or threatens you afterwards, keep a record of it and don’t delete it. You can call the police after you think about it, but the evidence will disappear over time. Regardless of whether you call the police or not, you must go to the hospital within the time limit. Sound Recordings See Section 8 Clause 41 (Recordings). If the other party uses photos or calls the police to blackmail you afterwards, it is also a crime. See Section 8, Article 32 (the other party uses calling the police or sending photos to ask for money). If something like this happens to a friend, go with him to the police or the hospital. Don't first persuade him to take a shower and rest. How to teach children normally, and how parents should respond to children’s comments, see Section 30, Article 19 (Understanding the Private Parts of the Body). If you still have nightmares and flashbacks a month later, see Section 29, Item 14 (Trauma-focused psychotherapy). For daily contraception after giving birth, see Section 27, Article 20 (breastfeeding does not equal contraception).

Case: After the victim, Xiao Chen, was sexually assaulted, she immediately went to her neighbor’s house to call 110 while the other party left. She did not take a shower or change clothes, nor did she clean up the room. She went to the hospital to have her injuries examined within 72 hours and took blocking drugs. The police quickly identified the suspect based on the biological test materials extracted and captured him.

items.title: If a baby under 1 year old chokes and cannot cry, lie down and pat the back 5 times, turn over and press the chest 5 times, take turns, do not press the belly
items.core: If the child can still cough or cry, let him cough on his own while you watch. If he couldn't cry and his face turned purple, he would be called 120. You lay your child face down on your forearm, tap the heel of your hand 5 times between the two shoulder blades, turn it over before it comes out, and tap 5 quick times in the middle of the chest. Do both in turn. Don't press the belly. If the child doesn't respond, switch to cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
body: Cost: No money. Watch the moves or take a baby first aid class, a few minutes to half a day. The difficult thing is to turn the child over and lay down first in a panic.

Benefits: The American Heart Association and the American Academy of Pediatrics have released 2025 guidelines for basic life support in children. The guidelines say: Asphyxia (such as foreign objects blocking the airway) "is one of the leading causes of death in infants and children." The most common thing babies choke on is liquid. If the child is still coughing and can still make a sound, it is mild. Let the child cough on his own while keeping an eye on whether it has gotten worse. A cough that is very weak, unable to cough or cry, or turns blue is severe. In severe cases, call first aid, and then "repeatedly pat the back 5 times and hit the chest 5 times until the foreign object comes out or the baby loses response." The guidelines do not recommend abdominal thrusting for babies because it may damage the organs in the belly. It is now recommended to use the heel of one hand for chest thrusts because it presses deeper than the original two-finger method. Start cardiopulmonary resuscitation when the baby becomes unresponsive, starting with compressions without feeling for a pulse. Visible foreign objects should be removed before insufflation. The guide clearly states "Don't pick it out blindly with your fingers." This is also true of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies’ 2025 International First Aid Guidelines. First, tap hard between the two shoulder blades for up to 5 times. If it doesn't work, turn the child over and press the chest for up to 5 times. If it doesn't work, call the emergency department immediately. It uses both hands to press on the chest and two thumbs to press. The Fujian Provincial Red Cross Emergency Rescue Training Center said that babies under 1 year old need "5 back slaps + 5 chest impacts." Place the infant prone on the forearms with the head lower than the torso during back patting
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Joyner BL et al (2025). Part 6: Pediatric Basic Life Support: 2025 American Heart Association and American Academy of Pediatrics Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care. Determining "big" profit depends on judgment: a completely blocked airway will stop the child's heartbeat within a few minutes. Almost all those who benefited were their own children. Children over 1 year old and adults should press the belly instead, see Article 26 of this section (choking, patting on the back plus abdominal shock). What technique should be used to massage the chest? Each family has different writing methods. The American guide uses the heel of one hand, the International Red Cross uses two thumbs, and the old tutorial uses two fingers. The 2025 U.S. Guidelines no longer recommend it because two-finger pressure is not deep enough. Keep small things such as coins and small toys out of the reach of children. What to do if the child becomes unresponsive, see Article 44 of this section (Infant CPR).

Case: A 9-month-old baby suddenly got stuck while eating peanuts, could not cry and turned purple. The mother immediately asked her family to call 120. At the same time, she laid the baby face down on her forearm, and quickly tapped the baby between the shoulder blades 5 times with the heel of her hand. If no foreign body was discharged, she turned it over and pressed 5 times in the middle of the chest. After about 3 rounds of alternation, the peanut is coughed up and the baby resumes breathing. He was sent to the hospital for examination and confirmed that there was nothing serious. The doctor said that what he did was completely correct.

items.title: If a baby under 1 year old does not respond or breathe normally, turn on the hands-free dial 120 and perform infant CPR: press 30 and blow 2 breaths
items.core: If there is no response or normal breathing by patting the soles of the feet, turn on the hands-free dial 120 without stopping. Put your hands around your chest and press with two thumbs. If you can't hold it, use the heel of one hand to press about 4 cm deep, about 2 times per second. After every 30 presses, cover the child's mouth and nose with your mouth and blow 2 breaths. Cardiopulmonary arrest in babies is mostly caused by being unable to breathe. If cardiopulmonary resuscitation with insufflation is performed, more babies will survive.
body: Cost: No money. Infant CPR needs to be practiced once in a class, for half a day to a day. The difficulty is blowing into the child's mouth and nose, and not being able to press hard.

Benefits: The American Heart Association and the American Academy of Pediatrics have released 2025 guidelines for basic life support in children. The guide states: The main cause of cardiac arrest in infants and children is breathing problems. Only 6.6% of babies who suffer cardiac arrest outside the hospital are discharged alive. Ordinary people who encounter an infant or child who is unresponsive, not breathing normally, and has no signs of life, "should start cardiopulmonary resuscitation immediately" and do not feel for a pulse. Compression depth should be at least one-third of the anterior-to-posterior diameter of the chest, which is "approximately 1.5 inches (4 centimeters)" for infants. Frequency 100 to 120 times per minute. When doing it alone, press 30 times and blow 2 breaths. When doing it with two people, press 15 times and blow for 2 breaths. The baby should be pressed with the heel of one hand, or with both hands wrapped around each other and pressed with two thumbs. If you can't hold it, use the heel of your hand. The practice of pressing with two fingers has been discontinued because it is not deep enough. The guidelines also write that for infants and children who suffer out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, insufflation in addition to compressions can improve survival. A U.S. registry counted 3,900 children under the age of 18 who suffered out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, 59.4% of whom were infants. For those present who performed CPR, the adjusted rate of being discharged alive was 13.2%, compared with 9.5% for those who did not. Adjusted odds ratio OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.25–1.96 (confidence range). In infants, cardiopulmonary resuscitation with insufflation is associated with greater survival, and those who survive have better brain recovery. If you just press the button but don't blow the whistle, the result will be the same as if no one does it. The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies has also produced the 2025 International First Aid Guidelines. It says: To see if the baby reacts, pick the baby up or pat the soles of his feet. If you are alone, put the emergency phone on speakerphone and make the emergency call yourself. If you don’t have a phone that can be pressed and dialed at the same time, perform CPR for 1 minute before calling. The Capital Institute of Pediatrics has a popular science article, which was reprinted by the Beijing Municipal Health Commission. It reads: "If only one person is present, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation for 2 minutes and then call 120 ambulance." The compression range is "baby 4cm". Insufflation under 1 year of age should be "mouth to mouth and nose"
Level of Evidence: B

Note: B is determined because survival numbers come from registry studies that only track records. Moreover, the calculation is for all children, and there is no separate number for infants in the summary. The "large" income is calculated based on the figures for all children: the number of children discharged alive is from 9.5% to 13.2%, which is a relative increase of about 40%. Almost all those who benefited were their own children. Compared with item 1 of this section (press the chest hard), there are three differences. The baby needs to blow. Just pressing without blowing will have poor effect on the baby. Press the chest with two thumbs or the heel of one palm, about 4 centimeters without stacking your hands. When one person cannot press and make a call at the same time, press first and then make a call. How long to press first varies from company to company: the single-person process of the Capital Institute of Pediatrics and the United States Guidelines is 2 minutes, and the International Red Cross is 1 minute. If your phone is hands-free, you don't have this problem. The European Resuscitation Council teaches to blow 5 breaths first and then press. The American guideline teaches to press first and then blow. Both are better than nothing. Old domestic tutorials teach two-finger press, but this technique has been removed from the 2025 US guidelines. If it is caused by choking, look into the mouth before blowing and remove visible foreign objects. See Article 43 of this section (Infant Choking).

Case: A 10-month-old baby got stuck after eating jelly. There was no response or normal breathing when patting the soles of the feet. The mother immediately opened the hands-free dial and called 120. At the same time, she put her hands around the baby's chest and pressed quickly with two thumbs. After pressing 30 times, her mouth covered the mouth and nose and blew two breaths. The operation was repeated until the ambulance came. The child resumed breathing on his own.

items.title: If a child swallows a button battery, or swallows more than two strong magnetic beads, go to the emergency room of a hospital with a gastroscopy immediately. Don’t wait for it to pull out on its own, and don’t induce vomiting.
items.core: A button battery stuck in the esophagus can cause severe burns in as fast as 2 hours. The child may seem fine at first. Two or more magnetic beads will attract each other across the intestinal wall and may push the intestines through. If you suspect that you have swallowed it, go to the hospital immediately to take an X-ray. Don't induce vomiting, don't wait for it to come out on its own, and don't wait for symptoms.
body: Cost: Free, the cost of emergency X-rays and removal is extra. Usually tighten the battery compartments of remote controls, electronic scales, and car keys. Keep spare batteries and magnetic beads out of reach of children. The difficulty is that most of the time no one sees the child swallow it, and the child may not have any symptoms at first.

Benefit: Figures from the U.S. Poison Database from 1985 to 2009 show that the rate of serious injury or death after swallowing button batteries increased 6.7 times. The most dangerous are lithium batteries with a diameter of 20 mm. Results were significantly worse for children under 4 years old and for lithium batteries larger than 20 mm in diameter. A battery stuck in the esophagus can cause severe burns in just 2 to 2.5 hours, leaving lasting effects. In 92% of deaths and 56% of serious injuries, no one saw the child swallow it. At least 54% of deaths and 27% of serious injuries were initially misdiagnosed because symptoms were atypical. After the battery is taken out, the injury will go deeper. Esophageal perforation, perforation of the esophagus and trachea or large blood vessels, and severe bleeding may occur after a few days. In another analysis of 8,648 cases, 61.8% of the batteries swallowed by children under 6 years old were taken directly from electrical appliances. The U.S. National Poison Control Center's disposal guidelines state: "Do not induce vomiting" if you suspect you have swallowed a battery. A battery stuck in the esophagus "can cause severe burns in as little as 2 hours", "don't wait for symptoms to appear." Anyone under 12 years old should take a photo and find batteries immediately. Product injury monitoring by the Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention shows that there have been nearly 100 cases of injuries related to accidental swallowing of batteries in the past five years, most of which were button batteries. 92.9% of injuries were to children aged 0 to 6 years. Moderate or severe injuries occurred in 39.3% and hospitalization was required in 25.0%. Its advice is to "seek medical attention immediately and never induce vomiting or feed your child on your own." The same monitoring report states that if Bucky balls (magnetic beads) are swallowed into the stomach, the beads in adjacent intestinal tubes will "attract each other and squeeze the intestinal tubes, thus causing intestinal obstruction or intestinal perforation." If swallowed by mistake, "you should be sent to a doctor immediately." A 2025 literature review included 130 children who had intestinal perforations (intestinal fistulas) after swallowing more than 2 magnets. Median age 3.3 years, 95.5% required surgery, 19% had postoperative complications, 1 died
Level of Evidence: B

Remarks: Defined B This is because the numbers come from poison hotlines and case registrations, and there is no comparison of "how many fewer deaths would be achieved by following these instructions." Determining "big" income depends on judgment: a battery in the esophagus can cause serious injuries in 2 hours, and most of the deaths are caused by misdiagnosis and misdiagnosis. Almost all those who benefited were their own children. Bring the same type of battery, packaging or electrical appliances together, and the doctor will need to use this to identify which battery it is. Chinese and foreign opinions differ on whether to feed honey on the road. The National Poison Control Center recommends that honey be given to anyone over 1 year old, less than 12 hours old, able to swallow, and if they happen to have it on hand. Feed 10 ml every 10 minutes up to 6 times. It's based on experiments on live pigs, and a 2023 summary said the evidence in humans is scant. Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention says not to feed. Children under 1 year of age should never be fed honey. Honey can only slow down the burn, not replace it. Don't delay going out to find honey. If the battery and magnet are swallowed together, the National Poison Control Center requires that the battery be removed if it reaches the stomach. The elderly can also swallow it: 15.5% of the 8648 cases swallowed the battery as a pill, mostly the elderly. Hearing aid batteries were swallowed in 36.3% of all cases. If the baby is choked and unable to breathe, first handle it according to Article 26 (back slap and abdominal shock) or Article 43 (choking the baby) of this section. For accidental ingestion of cleaning agents and drugs, see Article 20 of this section (Accidental Ingestion of Cleaning Agents).

Case: A 1-year-old baby swallowed the button battery in the remote control by mistake. When the mother found out, she did not induce vomiting or wait for the battery to pass out on its own. She immediately took the baby to the emergency department of a children's hospital with a gastroscopy. The doctor said that if it were one hour later, the esophagus might be perforated. After taking out the battery in time, the baby was in danger.

items.title: If someone is drunk, let him lie on his side and be watched by someone. Don't let him sleep alone. If he cannot wake up, has slow or irregular breathing, has convulsions, or feels cold, beat him. 120
items.core: A person who is so drunk that he falls asleep may choke to death on his own vomit, or his breathing may stop slowly. Let him lie on his side and have someone watch him at all times. Don't leave him alone in the house to sleep. If you can't wake up, your breathing becomes slow or irregular, you have convulsions, or your skin feels cold and blue, call 120. Don't pour coffee, don't take cold showers, don't pick your throat and induce vomiting.
body: Cost: No money. Someone had to keep watch for several hours, often all night. The difficult thing is that I drank too much and wanted to go home to sleep, but everyone thought "just take a nap".

Income: The symptoms of alcoholism listed by the British National Health Service (NHS) include: confusion, slurred speech, inability to stand, vomiting, incontinence, pale or blue skin, slow or irregular breathing, convulsions, and inability to wake up. If you think someone is suffering from alcohol poisoning, or if they are convulsing, losing consciousness, or stopping breathing, call emergency services. The thing to do is to stay by his side "because he might choke on his own vomit or stop breathing." Help him sit up while he is awake. The unconscious man was placed in a resuscitation position lying on his side to see if his breathing was normal. If you are still awake, able to swallow, and not vomiting, you can drink water in small sips. Keep him warm with a coat or blanket. Here are five things not to do. Don't let him drink again. Don't give him food, he will choke. Avoid coffee and caffeinated drinks, which can increase dehydration. Don't let him take cold showers or soak in cold water. He may freeze, fall, or pass out in the water. Don't try to make him puke. An article by an emergency doctor published on the website of the Shaanxi Provincial Health Commission stated that drunk people have weakened throat reflexes and are prone to inhalation into the trachea when vomiting. In severe cases, they can "directly suffocate to death." Emergency departments often receive dead drunk people who have a large amount of vomit sucked out of their trachea. In the comatose stage, if your face is pale, your lips are blue, your skin is clammy, your body temperature has dropped, and your breathing is shallow, you should call 120. At this time, let him lie on his side, "do not induce vomiting or feed food", cover him with a blanket to keep him warm, and turn over regularly. If the heartbeat and breathing stop, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation immediately. A hospital science piece reprinted by the Beijing Municipal Health Commission states: "Never let a drunk person sleep alone to avoid having no one to rescue the patient when he or she suffocates." An article by a pharmacist reprinted by the Fujian Provincial Food and Drug Administration said that drunk people "must lie on their sides" as hypothermia can cause cardiac arrest. According to statistics from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, from 2010 to 2012, an average of 2,221 people over the age of 15 died from alcohol poisoning every year in the United States, which is equivalent to about 6 people every day
Level of Evidence: B

Source: NHS. not try to make them sick". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/alcohol-poisoning/>; Shaanxi Provincial Health Commission (2022). What situations should not be delayed after drunkenness (Sun Peng, Peng Cao, Emergency Department, Union Hospital Affiliated to Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology). <https://sxwjw.shaanxi.gov.cn/ywgz/gbbj/202208/t20220825_2248211.html>; Beijing Municipal Health Commission (2023). Food poisoning, alcohol poisoning, and gas poisoning [Family first aid methods for critical and severe cases (6)] (Source: Beijing Chuiyangliu Hospital). <https://wjw.beijing.gov.cn/bmfw_20143/jkzs/jksh/202307/t20230706_3157010.html>; Fujian Provincial Food and Drug Administration (2022). Medication for alcoholism (reprinted from China Food and Drug Network, author Wang Shuping). Kanny D et al. (2015). Vital signs: alcohol poisoning deaths — United States, 2010–2012. MMWR 63(53):1238-1242. <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25577989/>; Taixing People's Court (2023). If someone drowns after drinking alcohol many times, the drinker should bear responsibility according to the degree of fault (National People's Court Information Network). <https://rmft.court.gov.cn/1150/jdal/3795.jhtml>; Supreme People's Court (2024). Guiding Case No. 227 Hu Moumou, Wang Moumou v. Demou Restaurant, Jiang Moumou, etc. Right to Life Dispute Case. <https://www.court.gov.cn/shenpan/xiangqing/433761.html>

Note: The reason for setting B is because these are official popular science and emergency experience, and there are no figures for "how many fewer deaths can be avoided by following these instructions." Determining "big" income depends on judgment: choking and respiratory arrest occur when no one is watching, and someone watching can detect it in time and call 120 in time. There is no consensus on inducing vomiting. Some domestic popular science says that people who can still walk and talk can stimulate their throats and induce vomiting. Those who cannot be woken up must not be induced to vomit. This is consistent with both China and foreign countries. The NHS does not recommend inducing vomiting at any time.
