The report urges vegetarians, especially pregnant and breastfeeding women, to find out how much B12 is in what they eat, or to ask a nutrition professional. A 2016 position paper from the American Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics states: "Vegans need reliable sources of vitamin B12, such as fortified foods or supplements." A 2017 position paper from the European Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition states that all infants should eat iron-rich complementary foods, including meat or iron-fortified foods. A vegan diet should only be followed under the proper supervision of a doctor or nutritionist, and parents should understand the serious consequences of not supplementing as recommended. The National Health Commission’s 2020 feeding core information requires that there should be no less than 4 types of complementary foods per day. This includes at least one animal food, one vegetable, and one cereal and potato food
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (2003). Neurologic impairment in children associated with maternal dietary deficiency of cobalamin—Georgia, 2001. MMWR, 52(4), 61-64. <https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/mm5204a1.htm>; Fewtrell M, Bronsky J, Campoy C, et al. (2017). Complementary Feeding: A Position Paper by the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) Committee on Nutrition. Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition, 64(1), 119-132. <https://doi.org/10.1097/MPG.0000000000001454>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2020). Core information on infant and young child feeding health education. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-08/01/content_5531915.htm>; Melina V, Craig W, Levin S (2016). Position of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics: Vegetarian Diets. Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, 116(12), 1970-1980. Source also from here )

Note: Controversy: The American Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics’ 2016 position is that well-planned vegetarian and vegan diets are appropriate for all stages of life, including pregnancy, breastfeeding, infants, and children. But it also states that people on a vegan diet need to have a reliable source of B12, such as fortified foods or supplements. The two sides disagree on whether vegans can feed babies, and there is no disagreement on "the need to supplement B12." Vegetarians who eat eggs and milk have a lower risk, but those who rarely eat eggs and milk will still be deficient. The mother of the second child in the report has been a vegetarian for 20 years and barely touches meat, fish and dairy products. The early symptoms of B12 deficiency are uncharacteristic, and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says anemia indicators are not suitable for screening. If your child grows slowly and cannot keep up with his development, you should proactively tell the doctor when you see a doctor that your family is vegetarian, and the doctor will decide what to check. Don’t refuse treatment given by your doctor just because you believe in folk remedies, see Section 16, Item 4 (Don’t stop regular treatment just to try folk remedies). For how to add complementary foods, see Article 4 of this section (Add complementary foods from 6 months onwards), and for folic acid during pregnancy, see Article 27, Article 1 (0.4 mg of folic acid per day).

Case: A breastfeeding mother on a vegetarian diet did not supplement B12. The exclusively breastfed baby had developmental delay and anemia when it was 5 months old, and was diagnosed with B12 deficiency. The doctor pointed out that insufficient B12 in breast milk was the cause, and the mother needed to supplement it and add meat and egg complementary foods to the baby.
tags: Popular group=pregnancy, infants and young children

items.title: Don’t buy a walker with wheels when buying things for your baby. If you want him to sit and play, switch to a play station or playpen without wheels
items.core: A child sitting in a walker can sprint more than 0.9 meters per second. Most of the time, adults are watching when they are injured. From 1990 to 2014, about 230,000 children were admitted to emergency rooms due to walkers in the United States. Ninety percent of the injuries were to the head and neck, and most of them fell down the stairs with the child in the car. A walker cannot teach a child to walk either.
body: Cost: No money, but also saves the cost of a baby walker. Play stations and playpens without wheels need to be purchased separately, or you can borrow them. The difficulty is that you have to be willing to throw it away if your elders have given it to you or you have already bought it

Income: From 1990 to 2014 in the United States, it is estimated that about 230,000 children under 15 months old went to the emergency room for injuries caused by walkers (accurate value: 230,676). 90.6% of the injuries were to the head or neck, and 74.1% occurred after falling down the stairs in a walker. 4.5% were hospitalized after the injury, and 37.8% of the children hospitalized had skull fractures. The United States has implemented mandatory safety standards for baby walkers since 2010. Over the next 4 years, the average number of injuries per year was 22.7% lower than in the previous 4 years. But the authors say walkers are still a significant source of avoidable injuries to children. A 2001 position statement from the American Academy of Pediatrics said 34 walker-related deaths were reported in the United States from 1973 to 1998. Warning labels, publicity and education, adult supervision, and stair gates have all been proven to be ineffective in preventing this type of injury. There are no clear benefits to baby walkers, so the society advocates a ban on the production and sale of wheeled baby walkers and recommends the use of fixed play stations without wheels instead. A note to parents from the academy reads that most walker injuries occur while adults are watching. A child sitting in a walker can sprint more than 3 feet (about 0.9 meters) in one second. Whether a walker can help a child learn to walk? The answer is that it cannot, but it may delay it. The evidence is not solid that it will delay walking. In a survey of 190 babies in Ireland, those using walkers were on average about 3 weeks later in walking independently (61.12 weeks vs. 58.14 weeks). The more you use it, the more late it becomes. But this is just a one-time questionnaire survey without group control. A small review in 2002 found two randomized trials, neither of which found a significant effect on the onset of walking. Taking the four studies together, the quality of the studies is low from 11 to 26 days late
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Sims A, Chounthirath T, Yang J, Hodges NL, Smith GA (2018). Infant Walker-Related Injuries in the United States. Pediatrics, 142(4), e20174332. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2017-4332>; American Academy of Pediatrics, Committee on Injury and Poison Prevention (2001). Injuries Associated With Infant Walkers. Pediatrics, 108(3), 790-792. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.108.3.790>; American Academy of Pediatrics (2022). Baby Walkers: A Dangerous Choice. HealthyChildren.org. Garrett M, McElroy AM, Staines A (2002). Locomotor milestones and babywalkers: cross sectional study. BMJ, 324(7352), 1494. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.324.7352.1494>; Burrows P, Griffiths P (2002). Do baby walkers delay onset of walking in young children? British Journal of Community Nursing, 7(11), 581-586. <https://doi.org/10.12968/bjcn.2002.7.11.10889>; Health Canada (2004-04-07). Minister Pettigrew announces a ban on baby walkers. News Release 2004-15. <https://www.canada.ca/en/news/archive/2004/04/minister-pettigrew-announces-ban-baby-walkers.html>; Canada Consumer Product Safety Act (S.C. 2010, c. 21), section 5 and Schedule 2 item 3. <https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/C-1.68/FullText.html>; National Standard Information Public Service Platform. GB 14749-2006 Safety Requirements for Baby Walkers. <https://std.samr.gov.cn/gb/search/gbDetailed?id=71F772D7639DD3A7E05397BE0A0AB82A>

Note: Canada has banned the sale, advertising and import of baby walkers since April 7, 2004. Second-hand ones are also not allowed to be sold at flea markets and garage sales. If you already have one at home, officials recommend tearing it down and throwing it away. The current Canadian Consumer Product Safety Act puts it on the prohibited list, and no one is allowed to produce, import, advertise or sell it. There is no ban on sales in China, and baby walkers are produced in accordance with the current national standard GB 14749-2006. Standards only care about the product itself and cannot control children rushing to the stairs. In the United States, since 1997, walkers have either been made wider than the door or equipped with brakes on the side of the steps, but the society still thinks this is not enough. Children can reach higher when sitting inside, pull down the tablecloth and spill hot coffee, grab the pot handle on the stove, or even fall into the sink or bathtub. The society recommends three alternatives: fixed play stations without wheels (with swivel and bounce seats), playpens, and high chairs. When sending your child to day care or another home, make sure there are no walkers in use there. Please refer to Article 11 of this section for the order of purchasing large items (large items are considered in the order of “borrowing, buying second-hand, and buying new”).

Case: My grandma bought a wheeled walker for her 8-month-old grandson. The baby immediately slid to the top of the stairs when he sat in it. The walker and the baby rolled down three steps. There was a 5 cm gash on his forehead and he needed 4 stitches. The doctor said he should never use it again in the future.

items.title: Feed your child 400 IU of vitamin D every day after birth, especially if you are breastfed, don’t miss out. Generally, there is no need to supplement calcium within 6 months of full term
items.core: Breastmilk contains very little vitamin D, and babies should not be exposed to too much sun, so they need to supplement it every day. In rural areas of Türkiye, 3.8% of the children who did not receive supplementary care got rickets in one year, while none of the children who did receive supplementary care developed rickets. Give the amount according to the doctor's instructions. Normal full-term children generally do not need additional calcium supplements within 6 months.
body: Cost: A bottle of vitamin D drops costs tens of yuan, and should be dropped once a day. The difficulty lies in remembering to feed him every day, at least until he is 1 year old

Benefit: A 2020 Cochrane review said breast milk is low in vitamin D, and babies fed only breast milk are more likely to not get enough. The American Academy of Pediatrics says children should be protected from the sun when they're outside for long periods of time, so all babies need vitamin D supplements. The National Health Commission’s core feeding information for 2020 reads: “Starting from birth, babies should be supplemented with 400-800 international units of vitamin D every day under the guidance of a doctor.” The same paragraph also reads: "Normal full-term babies generally do not need calcium supplements within 6 months after birth." The 2016 global consensus on rickets involved 11 international academic organizations. Consensus says 400 IU (10 micrograms) per day is enough to prevent rickets. All babies need supplements from birth to 12 months, whether breastfed or formula fed. This is a strong recommendation and the quality of the evidence is moderate. In a study in rural northeastern Türkiye, none of the children who received 400 IU per day developed rickets. Among children without supplementation, 3.8% developed new rickets in 12 months. The consensus also said that there are no reports in the world of infants who received 400 IU daily supplementation and were diagnosed with rickets by radiograph. China conducted a group study in 1992 in four cities in the north and south, supplementing 100, 200 or 400 IU per day. By 6 months, no child in any of the three groups had developed rickets. However, the vitamin D in the cord blood of newborns in the north is only about one-third of that in the south (12.5 vs. 35.0 nmol/L). The more you supplement, the higher the level at 6 months. The author recommends supplementing 400 IU per day
Level of Evidence: B

Source: General Office of the National Health Commission (2020). Core information on infant and young child feeding health education. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-08/01/content_5531915.htm>; Munns CF, Shaw N, Kiely M, et al. (2016). Global Consensus Recommendations on Prevention and Management of Nutritional Rickets. Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism, 101(2), 394-415. <https://doi.org/10.1210/jc.2015-2175>; Beser E, Cakmakci T (1994). Factors affecting the morbidity of vitamin D deficiency rickets and primary protection. East African Medical Journal, 71(6), 358-362. <https://europepmc.org/article/MED/7835254>; Specker BL, Ho ML, Oestreich A, et al. (1992). Prospective study of vitamin D supplementation and rickets in China. Journal of Pediatrics, 120(5), 733-739. <https://doi.org/10.1016/s0022-3476(05)80236-7>; Tan ML, Abrams SA, Osborn DA (2020). Vitamin D supplementation for term breastfed infants to prevent vitamin D deficiency and improve bone health. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 12, CD013046. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013046.pub2>; American Academy of Pediatrics (2022). Where We Stand: Vitamin D & Iron Supplements for Babies. HealthyChildren.org. <https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-Iron-Supplements.aspx>; Gallo S, Comeau K, Vanstone C, et al. (2013). Effect of different dosages of oral vitamin D supplementation on vitamin D status in healthy, breastfed infants: a randomized trial. JAMA, 309(17), 1785-1792. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2013.3404>

Note: B is determined because the figures for rickets prevention come from comparisons without randomization. Cochrane 2020 merged trials of supplementation in infants. Children who supplemented 400 IU per day were about 40% less likely to be vitamin D deficient (relative risk RR 0.57). But the experiments were small and could not tell whether rickets was rare or not. The income is determined based on judgment, because it is not known how common infant rickets is in China. There are mixed opinions about taking formula. The American Academy of Pediatrics says that drinking more than about 800 milliliters (27 ounces) of vitamin D-fortified formula per day does not require supplementation. The domestic core information states that all infants should receive supplementation, and it depends on what the doctor says. Don’t increase the dosage yourself: In a Canadian trial, the vitamin D in the blood of the group taking 1,600 IU per day was too high and was stopped early. There was no difference in length and bone between the 400 to 1200 IU groups. Adults who are not deficient in vitamin D should not take supplements for longevity, see Section 6, Item 3 (People who are not deficient in vitamin D).

Case: After the exclusively breastfed baby was one month old, the mother was given 400IU vitamin D drops every day. The bone density during the child care examination was normal and there was no rib valgus. The neighbor's child who did not take supplements was found to have moderate rickets at the age of 1 and started taking calcitriol.

items.title: When bathing a baby, first put cold water in and then hot water, test it with the inside of your wrist or elbow before putting the baby in; the instantaneous water heater that can set the water temperature should be adjusted to below 50 ℃
items.core: If the hot water of 65 ℃ comes into contact for 2 seconds, most adults will get third-degree burns, and the baby's skin is even thinner. Put cold water in the basin first and then mix it with hot water. After stirring well, test it with the inside of your wrist or elbow before putting the child in. Don't wash it under an open faucet. After a state in the United States lowered the factory temperature of water heaters to 49°C, the number of children hospitalized due to hot water burns was reduced by more than half.
body: Cost: No money. Spend an extra minute or two each time you shower to test the water temperature. If you want more stability, buy a water thermometer. Even when children are crying and adults are anxious, you should try it before releasing it

Benefits: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission says that most adults will suffer third-degree burns within 2 seconds of exposure to 150℉ (about 65℃) water. Burns can also occur if exposed to 140℉ (60°C) water for 6 seconds or 130℉ (approximately 54°C) water for 30 seconds. Even at 120°F (49°C), a 5-minute soak can result in third-degree burns. The WHO reports that infants and young children have thinner skin than adults and can be burned at lower temperatures, and the burns can be deeper. The American Academy of Pediatrics teaches parents: Test the water in the basin with the inside of your wrist or elbow to make sure it is "warm but not hot." "Never bathe your baby under running water." Because the water flows in the pipes, the temperature will rise and fall, and a slight change may cause burns. Washington State in the United States legislated in 1983 that new water heaters must be factory preset at 49°C. By 1988, the average temperature of hot water in homes dropped from 61°C in 1977 to 50°C. The number of children hospitalized for tap water burns has dropped from 5.5 per year in the 1970s to 2.4 per year. Burn areas, skin grafts, deaths, and hospitalization days were also reduced. This is a before-and-after comparison, not a group trial. Australia regulates bathroom hot water taps to a maximum temperature of 50°C. In New South Wales, hospital admissions for burns in children aged 0 to 4 fell by 13% between 1989 and 1996. Severe burn injuries requiring hospitalization for more than 10 days decreased by 30% in the two years after the second stage. In the three domestic statistics on children's burn hospitalizations, 87.6% to 90.6% were burned by hot liquids, with the highest number of children under 3 years old
Level of Evidence: B

Source: US Consumer Product Safety Commission. Avoiding Tap Water Scalds (Document 5098). <https://www.cpsc.gov/s3fs-public/5098.pdf>; American Academy of Pediatrics (2025). Bathing Your Baby. HealthyChildren.org. <https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/bathing-skin-care/Pages/Bathing-Your-Newborn.aspx>; NHS. Washing and bathing your baby (reviewed 2024-07-23). <https://www.nhs.uk/baby/caring-for-a-newborn/washing-and-bathing-your-baby/>; World Health Organization, UNICEF (2008). World report on child injury prevention, Chapter 4 Burns (the same page has the Chinese version of the "World Report on Child Injury Prevention"). <https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/43851>; Erdmann TC, Feldman KW, Rivara FP, Heimbach DM, Wall HA (1991). Tap water burn prevention: the effect of legislation. Pediatrics, 88(3), 572-577. Xu JH, Qiu J, Zhou JH, et al. (2014). Pediatric burns in military hospitals of China from 2001 to 2007: a retrospective study. Burns, 40(8), 1780-1788. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.burns.2014.04.003>; Zhu L, Zhang Y, Liu L, et al. (2013). Hospitalized pediatric burns in North China: a 10-year epidemiologic review. Burns, 39(5), 1004-1011. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.burns.2012.12.014>; Han D, Wei Y, Li Y, et al. (2022). Epidemiological and Clinical Characteristics of 5,569 Pediatric Burns in Central China From 2013 to 2019. Frontiers in Public Health, 10, 751615. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2022.751615>; World Health Organization (2007). Legionella and the prevention of legionellosis. <https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/43233>

Note: The number B is determined because the numbers come from before-and-after comparisons and medical record statistics, and there is no group trial. The income is determined based on judgment, because no separate figures for bathwater scalds in China have been found. There are two types of water heaters. For instantaneous gas water heaters, the outlet water temperature can be directly set to below 50°C. Storage-type electric water heaters are counted separately: WHO’s Legionella prevention guidelines recommend that the water outlet from water heaters should be kept at 60°C, and the hot water from faucets should not be lower than 50°C. Legionella is a type of bacteria that causes pneumonia. The same guide also states that anti-Legionella bacteria cannot increase the risk of children being scalded, and a thermostatic mixing valve can be installed at the water outlet. If it is not installed, just cool it first, then heat it, and then put it away. Don't leave when washing. The American Academy of Pediatrics says more than half of children who drown in bathtubs are under 1 year old, see Section 1, No. 12 (Keep water within sight). Don’t serve hot water while holding your baby: The WHO says that in high-income countries, burns from hot drinks in cups are most common among babies under 1 year old. If you are burned, take a shower with cool water first. See Section 13, Article 14 (Run with cool water after being burned).

Case: When a mother bathes her 6-month-old baby, she first puts cold water in and then hot water, and tests the temperature on the inside of her wrist before putting the baby into the basin. At a friend's house, she puts hot water in first, and when she turns around to get a towel, the baby sits in it, causing big blisters on her thighs.

items.title: Check the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ safety alerts before departure, and do not go to places marked “Do Not Travel Yet”
items.core: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs divides security risks abroad into four levels, with the highest level called "Do Not Travel Yet." From September 15, 2026, avoiding high-risk countries and regions will be written into administrative regulations. When applying for documents and going through customs, the staff will remind you and advise you not to go if necessary. It only takes a few minutes to turn the page before setting off.
body: Cost: Nothing. Open the China Consular Service website and browse through it. You can read it in a few minutes.

Benefits: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs publicly issues foreign security alerts based on risk levels. There are roughly four levels from low to high: "Pay attention to safety", "Strengthen safety precautions", "Go with caution" and "Don't go there yet". The new regulations, which will come into effect on September 15, 2026, also include personal obligations in administrative regulations. The original text is: "Chinese citizens should pay attention to foreign security warnings and travel destination safety risk warnings, and avoid traveling to and staying in high-risk countries or regions." The new regulations also require immigration management agencies (departments that issue entry and exit documents and manage border inspections) to remind people who are going to high-risk areas when applying for permits and exit border inspections. The original text of this article is: "Chinese citizens who plan to travel to countries or regions with the highest level of risk or with a high incidence of cases that seriously endanger personal safety shall be discouraged from traveling if necessary."
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2026). Provisions on Exit and Entry Management (National Order No. 841). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173.htm> (Article 2); State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (National Order No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (19, 21); Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Safety Reminder. <https://cs.mfa.gov.cn/zggmzhw/lsbh/aqtx/>; National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2018). Tourism Law (2018) (Revised in 2016, Articles 58 and 62). <https://zwgk.mct.gov.cn/zfxxgkml/zcfg/fl/202105/t20210526_924763.html> (Reprinted by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism Government Information Disclosure)

Note: Reminders will change according to the situation. This book does not copy the list. Check the page yourself before traveling. As of September 7, 2026, there are still these "Do Not Go" reminders in this column: Swaziland (2026-08-25), Palestine (2023-10-10), and Sudan (2023-04-17). The other four are Afghanistan (2023-02-17), Syria (2023-01-04), Peru (2022-12-29), and Somalia (2022-11-24). There are also special reminders for northern Myanmar and some provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Travel agencies also have a duty to inform. The Tourism Law stipulates that when signing a package tour contract, the travel agency must inform you of safety precautions, as well as the laws, customs and religious taboos of the destination. Package travel contracts must be signed in writing. Before joining a group, you can ask the other party to write down the risks of the destination. This is the author’s suggestion.

Case: Lao Zhang planned to go hiking in a certain country. Before departure, he checked the Ministry of Foreign Affairs reminder and saw that some areas of the country were marked "Do not travel temporarily" and immediately changed his route to neighboring countries. Traveling companions forced their way in without heeding the warnings and were trapped for three days in an armed conflict. They had to rely on the embassy's coordination to evacuate.

items.title: Save 12308 and the consular protection phone number of the local embassy or consulate in your mobile phone, make another copy and put it in your wallet, don’t wait until something happens to look for it again
items.core: When something goes wrong, call the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ global consular protection hotline first. From home, dial 12308; from abroad, dial +86-10-12308. The hotline has received more than 3 million calls since its launch. During the same period, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and overseas agencies handled more than 500,000 consular protection cases.
body: Cost: Nothing. Save two numbers, copy one more, a few minutes.

Benefits: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has a global emergency hotline for consular protection and services that is manned 24 hours a day. From within China, dial 12308. From abroad, dial +86-10-12308, or +86-10-65612308. Since this hotline was opened in 2014, it has received more than 3 million calls. During the same period, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and overseas missions handled more than 500,000 consular protection cases of various types.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Chinese Embassy and Consulates in Myanmar (2023). Consular reminder on the current security situation in northern Myanmar. <https://cs.mfa.gov.cn/zggmzhw/lsbh/aqtx/202311/t20231109_11176682.shtml>; State Council Information Office (2023). Regular briefing on the State Council’s policies to introduce the situation on consular protection and assistance. <https://www.gov.cn/xinwen/2023zccfh/11/index.htm>

备注：驻当地使领馆自己还有一个领保电话，通常比总台更快。 Before departure, search it by country on the China Consular Service website and save it into your mobile phone along with the main station number. If your phone is lost or out of battery, the saved numbers will no longer be available.所以再手抄一份放在钱包里，或者把号码写一份给家里人

Case: Xiao Li lost his wallet and mobile phone while traveling in Southeast Asia. He remembered the 12308 number he copied in his wallet before departure, and borrowed a passerby's mobile phone to call. The embassy and consulate contacted him half an hour later, issued a replacement travel permit, and returned home smoothly the next day.

items.title: Know what consular protection can and cannot do: you can visit, but you can’t extort people, and you have to pay the fees yourself
items.core: If you are arrested abroad, what the embassy or consulate can do is: verify the situation with the local area, demand fair treatment in accordance with the law, visit you, and observe the court session. It cannot change the sentence for you, nor can it take the person away. Others pay for food, accommodation, transportation, and medical expenses first, and you have to pay them yourself in the end. So prepare money and insurance before going abroad, and don’t think of “the country will pay for it if something goes wrong” as a plan.
body: Cost: Nothing. Take a few minutes to read this line clearly.

Benefits: When you are arrested, the embassy or consulate can do several things. Verify the situation with the relevant departments of the host country and request a fair and fair handling in accordance with the law. The original text of the regulations is "In accordance with the laws of the host country and the international treaties that my country and the host country have concluded or jointly participated in, visit or contact them to understand their relevant needs, and require the relevant departments of the host country to provide humanitarian treatment and fair treatment to the Chinese citizen." Translated into vernacular, the embassy or consulate will visit you, contact you, ask you what you want, and require the local government to treat you according to humane and fair standards in accordance with local laws and the treaties signed by the two countries. The embassy or consulate can observe the court session and request protection of your litigation rights. If you are injured or caught in a disaster, it can prompt local emergency rescue and help your family members deal with the aftermath. But the regulations on fees are equally clear: "Chinese citizens, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations that receive materials and services such as food, accommodation, transportation, and medical care provided by third parties during the process of consular protection and assistance shall pay their own expenses." If others pay for food, accommodation, transportation, and medical care first, it’s your turn to pay for it.
Level of Evidence: A
Source: State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (National Order No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (Articles 9, 10, 14, 26)

Note: If the embassy or consulate does not pay the fine for you, pay for your medical expenses, or buy your air ticket, it cannot change the conclusion of the court in the country where it is located. It can give you information about local lawyers, translators, medical and funeral agencies, and can also help you contact relatives and friends, and help you find relief channels. So prepare your own money and insurance before going abroad, and don’t think of “the country will pay for it if something goes wrong” as a plan.

Case: Xiao Chen was detained due to a misunderstanding and got involved in a fight overseas. The embassy and consulate visited him and asked for fair treatment, but they could not take him away. He paid $12,000 for bail and lawyer fees out of his own pocket, and his family also sold cars to raise money. This is a profound lesson.

items.title: Buy an insurance that covers overseas medical treatment and medical evacuation, don’t just buy flight delay insurance
items.core: You have to pay for medical treatment abroad. Domestic medical insurance basically does not cover it, and the embassy and consulates do not cover it. What can really bring down a family is not the outpatient fees, but the hospitalization after a serious injury, and transporting the person back to the country, which requires a special plane or medical escort. When buying travel insurance, there are two main limits: overseas medical expenses and emergency medical evacuation and repatriation.
body: Cost: A short-term overseas travel insurance costs tens to hundreds of yuan.

Income: You have to pay for medical treatment abroad. Domestic medical insurance basically does not reimburse overseas. Consular protection does not advance this money either, see Article 3 (What consular protection can and cannot do). The basis is Article 26 of the Regulations. What can really bring down a family is not the outpatient fees, but the hospitalization and medical transport after a serious injury. To transfer people back to the country from overseas hospitals, special flights or medical escorts are required, which is the most expensive category of self-funded projects. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, emergency transportation of patients from remote places to good hospitals may cost more than $100,000 if paid out of pocket. When buying insurance, give priority to two limits. The first is the amount of overseas medical expenses. The second is the amount of emergency medical transport and repatriation, which governs the maximum amount of compensation that can be compensated for transferring people to the hospital and sending people back to the country after an accident
Evidence level: C

Source: State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (National Order No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (Article 26); U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Travelers' Health: Travel Insurance: "Medical evacuation insurance covers emergency transportation from a remote area to a high-quality hospital, which could otherwise cost more than $100,000.". <https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/page/insurance>; The rest is the author's experience, no direct literature

Note: $100,000 is a lower limit, not a cost range. No official or industry published fee range statistics have been found, so this book does not write specific ranges. Check three things before buying. First, is the country you are going to covered? Second, are high-risk activities such as diving, skiing, and motorcycle riding excluded. Third, for claim settlement, should the insurance company settle the bill directly with the hospital, or should you advance the money and then reimburse it? The same goes for visa-free countries

Case: Ms. Wang broke her leg while skiing in Japan. The surgery and hospitalization cost more than 200,000 yuan. Fortunately, she bought an insurance covering 600,000 yuan for overseas medical treatment and 1 million yuan for transshipment before departure. The insurance company paid the full compensation and arranged a special flight back to Shanghai.

items.title: "Overseas high-paying recruitment" should be regarded as a scam. If you are deceived into committing electronic fraud, you may be restricted from leaving the country
items.core: The monthly salary is ridiculously high, no education or experience is asked, no formal contract is signed, you are asked to gather in a border city first, and your passport is kept for you. This kind of life is gone, and neither the person nor the passport is in his hands. If you make false documents when leaving the country, the border inspection will stop you and refuse to let you go. Those who commit illegal crimes abroad and endanger national security and interests may not be allowed to leave the country for 6 months to 3 years after returning to the country.
body: Cost: No money. The hard part is turning down a job that looks like a good job.

Income: The official characterization of this type of case is very straightforward. In recent years, there have been cases of "people being deceived and leaving the country or illegally leaving the country under false pretexts to engage in illegal activities such as cross-border gambling, telecommunications and network fraud, seriously endangering people's lives and property safety." It's about being tricked out, or making up excuses to sneak out, and go there to engage in gambling and telecommunications fraud. The new regulations are tightened at both ends to address this issue. On the exit side: "The reasons for applying for exit, entry and stay must be true and legal." If you submit false documents or tell lies, the immigration management agency has the right not to issue you documents or let you leave the country. Returning to China: "Chinese citizens who engage in illegal and criminal activities abroad and endanger national security and interests may... decide not to leave the country within 6 months to 3 years from the date of return." Those who are administratively detained for obtaining documents by fraud or illegal entry and exit are also not allowed to leave the country for 6 months to 3 years
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2026). Provisions on Exit and Entry Management (National Order No. 841). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173.htm> (Articles 3 and 4); Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Public Security, National Immigration Bureau (2026). Answering reporters' questions on the "Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Management". <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202608/content_7077270.htm>

Note: The identification characteristics are basically fixed: the monthly salary is much higher than the same position, no academic experience is required, no formal contract is required, you are asked to gather in the border city first, the visa is issued on behalf of you and your passport is kept. Special consular reminders have been issued for northern Myanmar. If you really go, your personal freedom and passport are not in your hands, don’t think you can leave if you want

Case: Xiao Zhou saw an advertisement for "Customer Service Recruitment with a monthly salary of 30,000 in Thailand" and smuggled himself into a fraud park. His passport was confiscated and he was forced to deceive others. He was deported back to the country six months later and was sentenced to a fixed-term prison sentence for illegal exit and fraud, and was not allowed to leave the country for 5 years.

items.title: Overseas cash withdrawals cannot exceed 100,000 yuan in a year, which is calculated by all the cards in your name; you can carry cash in and out of the country, the maximum amount of RMB is 20,000 yuan each time, and foreign currencies exceeding US$5,000 must be declared to the customs
items.core: Overseas cash withdrawals are based on the sum of all bank cards in your name, with a cap of 100,000 yuan per year, and you cannot withdraw more than that in the current year and the next year. Card consumption will not be affected. You can carry cash with you when entering and exiting the country, up to a maximum of 20,000 yuan in RMB each time, and any foreign currency exceeding US$5,000 must be declared to the customs. Failure to declare may result in fines, hiding it is considered smuggling, and cash will be confiscated.
body: Cost: No money. Before you leave, estimate how much cash you will need to withdraw for this trip, and you will need to pay the rest by swiping your card. The hard thing is to break the habit, don’t withdraw cash if you can swipe your card. If you want to take a large amount of foreign currency cash out of the country, you must first go to the bank to issue a certificate, which is an extra trip.

Income: Based on the "Notice on Regulating Overseas Large-amount Cash Withdrawal Transactions by Bank Cards" issued by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (Huifa [2017] No. 29, effective from January 1, 2018). Article 1: "When an individual withdraws cash overseas with domestic bank cards, the total number of bank cards (including supplementary cards) in his name shall not exceed the equivalent of 100,000 yuan per calendar year. If the annual limit is exceeded, cash withdrawals overseas with domestic bank cards will be suspended this year and the following year." Paragraph 2 of the same article: "Individuals may not circumvent or help circumvent the management of overseas cash withdrawals by borrowing other people's bank cards or lending their own bank cards." Article 2: The foreign exchange bureau sends the suspension list to the card-issuing bank every day. The card-issuing bank should start no later than 17:00 Beijing time on that day. People on the suspension list can use their bank cards to withdraw cash overseas. Article 3: People who are included in the suspended list can take their valid identity documents to branches of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange to check their overseas cash withdrawal details. Article 4: The daily upper limit for each foreign currency card is adjusted from the equivalent of US$1,000 to the equivalent of RMB 10,000; for RMB cards, the daily limit for each card shall not exceed the equivalent of RMB 10,000. Article 6: Card-issuing banks, domestic RMB card clearing organizations and individuals who violate the provisions of this notice shall be punished in accordance with the relevant provisions of the "Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations of the People's Republic of China". The State Administration of Foreign Exchange also clarified several points in answering reporters' questions. The "Notice" does not affect individuals' overseas consumption with cards. Regular transactions such as food, accommodation, travel, and purchases related to outbound tourism, business, and study abroad can all be paid with bank cards. These purchases do not take up the personal convenience annual foreign exchange purchase quota of US$50,000. The annual quota is calculated by the Foreign Exchange Bureau by aggregating data from various card-issuing financial institutions. Because real-time control will slow down transaction response, "the Foreign Exchange Bureau uses delay control methods" (not on-site interception). According to other statistics, in 2016, 81% of overseas cash withdrawals using domestic bank cards were less than RMB 30,000 (nationally). There are also rules for carrying cash in and out of the country. The back of the new customs declaration form that will be used from April 1, 2025, reads: "The RMB carried by each person for each entry and exit shall not exceed 20,000 yuan." When foreign currency cash enters the country, "if the value exceeds the equivalent of 5,000 U.S. dollars, a written declaration must be made to the customs." When leaving the country with an equivalent value of more than US$5,000 to US$10,000, you must first find a bank to issue a "Permit for Carrying Foreign Exchange Out of the Country" and then declare it to the customs. If the amount exceeds US$10,000, you must ask the Foreign Exchange Administration to issue this certificate. The regulations of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange state that outbound personnel "are not allowed to carry more than the equivalent of 10,000 U.S. dollars in foreign currency cash out of the country in principle." Customs regulations for the supervision of luggage and items stipulate that any currency or cash exceeding the prescribed amount must be reported to the Customs in writing when entering or exiting the country. If the written declaration has not been completed when the customs starts inspection, it will be considered as no declaration. If the goods are not declared but not hidden, the customs will give a warning and may impose a fine of less than 20% of the value of the goods. Hiding, disguising or concealing the report will be considered as smuggling, the cash will be confiscated, and a fine of less than the equivalent value may also be imposed
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2017). Notice on regulating overseas large-amount cash withdrawal transactions with bank cards (Huifa [2017] No. 29, Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7, effective from January 1, 2018). <https://www.safe.gov.cn/safe/2017/1230/21873.html>; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2017). Relevant persons in charge of the Foreign Exchange Administration answered reporters’ questions on issues related to regulating large overseas cash withdrawal transactions with bank cards. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2017-12/31/content_5251958.htm>; China UnionPay International. Overseas ATM withdrawals. <https://m.unionpayintl.com/wap/cn/serviceCenter/cardUsingInstructions/805.shtml>; General Administration of Customs (2025). Announcement on matters related to the declaration of luggage and items for entry and exit personnel (General Administration of Customs Announcement 2025 No. 43, Part 2 of the "Important Tips" on the back of the attached declaration form). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017195.htm>; General Administration of Customs (2025). Measures of the Customs of the People's Republic of China for the Supervision of Entry and Exit Luggage and Articles (General Administration of Customs Order No. 276, Articles 9, 10, and 11). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202502/content_7005697.htm>; State Administration of Foreign Exchange, General Administration of Customs (2003). Notice on the issuance of the "Interim Measures for the Entry and Exit Management of Carrying Foreign Currency Cash" (Huifa [2003] No. 102, Articles 3, 5, and 7). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2004/content_63085.htm>; People's Bank of China (2004). People's Bank of China Announcement [2004] No. 18 (the RMB entry and exit limit is adjusted to 20,000 yuan, effective from January 1, 2005). <https://www.pbc.gov.cn/tiaofasi/144941/3581332/3582861/2018072309595152720.pdf>; State Council (revised in 2022). Regulations on the Implementation of Customs Administrative Penalties (Articles 7, 9, and 19). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80818180e0a61301811e43f41f1fa2>; U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Money and Other Monetary Instruments: "Federal law mandates that when entering or leaving the United States you must report amounts exceeding $10,000" "the $10,000 threshold applies to the total amount they are carrying or sending collectively, not per individual”. <https://www.cbp.gov/travel/international-visitors/kbyg/money>

Note: The quota is calculated based on the natural year, and accumulation restarts on January 1. Only cash withdrawals abroad are stopped, and card consumption will not be affected. If you really need to use large amounts of cash abroad, you should purchase foreign exchange first according to the "Personal Foreign Exchange Management Measures" and then take the foreign currency cash out of the country. If the amount exceeds US$5,000, remember to apply for a carry permit and go through the customs red channel to declare. The destination country also has its own declaration threshold, so check it before departure. For example, U.S. Customs stipulates that if you bring more than $10,000 into or out of the U.S. at one time, you must declare it. If a family is traveling together, the total amount will be calculated. Cash regulations are as of October 14, 2026. There are still two pitfalls in withdrawing cash, which are clearly stated on the UnionPay International "Overseas ATM Withdrawal" page. First, the dual-logo card cannot be withdrawn through UnionPay channels at some ATMs in some countries. Second, some overseas ATMs will prompt an additional handling fee (surcharge) on the screen. This amount is collected by the local acquirer and "has nothing to do with UnionPay." The same page also states that "Since credit card withdrawals require overdraft interest, cardholders are advised to use UnionPay debit cards for overseas withdrawals." What to do if the card is lost, swallowed or stolen, see Section 14, Article 5 (if the card is stolen, report the loss and freeze it before calling the police). The limit for withdrawing and carrying cash is as of October 2026. The latest announcements from the Foreign Exchange Bureau and Customs shall prevail before departure.

Case: Xiao Wang traveled abroad and used three bank cards in his name to withdraw cash in installments overseas, with a total of 120,000 yuan withdrawn in one year. After returning to China, I discovered that the limit exceeded 100,000 yuan, and the overseas cash withdrawal function was suspended both that year and the second year. He originally thought that the limit could be spread among multiple cards, but in the end, all cards were restricted.

items.title: Take a photo of your passport, visa, and ID card and save it in the cloud. If you lose it, call the police first and then replace your travel document
items.core: If your passport is lost, the embassy or consulate can give you a replacement travel document for returning to your country, but you must be able to prove who you are. If you have the information page, photos of the visa page and entry and exit records in hand, it will be much faster to apply for a reissue. You must first call the local police to get a receipt. Many countries require this piece of paper for exit inspections and insurance claims. Mobile phones are often lost together with passports, so don’t just keep photos in your mobile phone.
body: Cost: No money. Take a few photos before heading out.

Benefits: If you lose your passport, the embassy or consulate abroad can issue you a travel document for returning to your country, but you need to prove your identity first. If you have clear photos of the passport information page, visa page and entry and exit records in hand, the speed of reissue will vary greatly. At the same time, you must first call the local police and get a report receipt. Many countries require this document for exit inspection and insurance claims. Find the entrance of the embassy or consulate, which is the two consular protection telephone numbers saved in Article 2.
Evidence level: C

Source: State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (National Order No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (Article 16); Author’s experience, no direct documentation

Note: The storage method is to take the photo and put it in two different places, such as saving one copy on a cloud disk and sending one copy to a family member. Print another paper copy and keep it separately from the original. Bank cards and prescriptions for commonly used medicines were also photographed. Mobile phones and passports are usually lost together. If they are only stored in the mobile phone, they are not saved at all. Cloud disk login requires a mobile phone verification code. If you lose your phone, you may not be able to log in. Before leaving, try logging in on another device to make sure it can be opened without the phone. ID photos are sensitive information, so it is safer to choose a storage method that can be encrypted. But the encrypted storage method cannot be opened by anyone if you forget the password, so you cannot save the copy sent to your family.

Case: Mr. Zhang’s passport and mobile phone were stolen while traveling in Europe. Because he took photos of the passport information page and visa page before departure and stored them in his cloud mailbox. After calling the police and getting a receipt, he quickly applied for a new travel permit at the embassy and consulate and returned home smoothly. His entry and exit records and insurance claims were not delayed because the materials were complete.

items.title: When driving overseas, first confirm whether the local area recognizes the Chinese driver's license. Most of the "International Driver's License" sold online are waste paper
items.core: The "International Driver's License" issued online is not valid in mainland China. That certificate is a mutually recognized translation between the contracting parties to the 1949 Geneva Convention. Among the 103 contracting parties, there is no mainland China. Therefore, no matter who does it for you in China, it will have no legal effect. Whether you can drive with a Chinese driver's license depends on the destination's own regulations. Don't drive without confirming it clearly.
body: Cost: No money. Check your destination’s regulations before departure.

Income: The so-called "International Driving Permit" (IDP) is a mutually recognized translation between the contracting parties to the 1949 Road Traffic Convention. This Convention was concluded in Geneva on September 19, 1949, and entered into force on March 26, 1952. As of November 4, 2026, the United Nations Treaty Library showed 103 Contracting Parties (countries and territories that are signatories). Mainland China is not on this list. Therefore, China does not issue this kind of international driving license. Any agency that "issues an international driver's license on behalf of others" in the country will not have any legal effect. Whether you can drive with a Chinese driver's license depends on the regulations of the destination country or region. Some recognize the Chinese driver's license plus a notarized translation, some require a local driver's license, and some do not recognize it at all
Level of Evidence: A

Source: United Nations Treaty Collection. Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 — status of treaties. <https://treaties.un.org/pages/ViewDetailsV.aspx?src=TREATY&mtdsg_no=XI-B-1&chapter=11&clang=_en>

Note: The driver’s license used for driving is not recognized by the local area, and the insurance may deny compensation in the event of an accident. This is the real cost. This sentence is based on the author’s experience. It depends on the policy terms and local laws. There are two ways to check: look for the "Instructions for Chinese Citizens" of the destination country on the Chinese Consular Service website, or directly ask the car rental company to give you a written confirmation. Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan and some countries have separate arrangements

Case: Xiao Lin spent 300 yuan online to apply for an "International Driver's Permit". When he rented a car in France, the police found it was a fake certificate. He was fined 1,200 euros for driving without a license and the car was impounded. The trip was ruined. The certificate had no legal effect in the country.

items.title: When looking for an agency to handle visas, study abroad, or immigration, first ask whether it has been registered with the immigration management agency
items.core: Starting from September 15, 2026, agencies that handle visas, study abroad, and immigration must register with the immigration management agency. Exaggerating propaganda to solicit customers, providing or assisting in providing false materials are expressly prohibited. Be careful when you hear words such as "guaranteed", "guaranteed", "we will help you make the materials".
body: Cost: No money. Ask more if it has been filed, and then keep the written materials.

Income: In 2018, the access permit for private entry and exit agencies was canceled (it is not necessary to obtain an approval document first to open an agency). Since then, the number of institutions has grown rapidly, and problems have arisen such that "the number of institutions is unclear, some institutions handle business in violation of laws and regulations, and harm the legitimate rights and interests of people entering and exiting the country." Officials cannot even count how many there are. Starting from September 15, 2026, this type of intermediaries will be subject to registration management. The organization shall report to the local immigration management agency within 15 days from the date of establishment. What has been done before must be replaced within 90 days from the date of implementation. The following types of behaviors are expressly prohibited. The first is "publishing false information, or soliciting service recipients through exaggerated publicity, misleading publicity, etc." The second is "providing or assisting in providing false materials, and assisting others to apply for visas, stay and residence documents, passports and other exit and entry documents or procedures in violation of regulations." The third is "divulging, selling, or illegally providing... personal privacy or personal information." The fourth is "organizing or assisting others to engage in cross-border illegal and criminal activities." Overseas enterprises and institutions are not allowed to provide such intermediary services in China
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2026). Provisions on Exit and Entry Management (National Order No. 841). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173.htm> (Articles 7, 8, 10, 12, 13); United States Code, Title 8, §1182(a)(6)(C)(i) Misrepresentation. <https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/8/1182> (Reprinted by Cornell University Legal Information Institute)

Note: An intermediary that talks about "packaging", "guarantee" and "we will help you with the materials" is doing something that is expressly prohibited. Once found out, the applicant will bear the consequences. If you make an unintentional mistake in filling out the form, you will usually be rejected this time. This is the author’s experience. If you use false materials and are found to have committed fraud, the consequences will be much more severe. Take the United States as an example. Immigration laws stipulate that foreigners who apply for visas by fraud or intentionally misrepresenting important facts are "not allowed to enter the country." Policy consultation and information inquiries that are not for the purpose of making money are not considered intermediary services

Case: Ms. Zhao went to an agency to study abroad, but the other party said, "We'll cover it, and we'll cover all the materials." They also charged 80,000 yuan. Later, it was discovered that the agency had not registered with the Immigration Bureau, and the fake materials used were found out. She was refused a visa, and she would not get her money back.

items.title: Don’t issue invitation letters for strangers, and don’t let people use your name to go through entry-exit procedures
items.core: If you issue invitation letters or application materials for others, if the content is untrue, the issuer will be punished. Individuals will be fined 5,000 yuan to 10,000 yuan, and any illegal gains will be confiscated. The unit is fined 10,000 to 50,000, and the person handling it is fined another 5,000 to 10,000. A favor, in exchange for paying for it myself.
body: Cost: No money. The hard thing is to turn down a favor in person.

Income: The person who issues the invitation letter is responsible for whether the content is true. The original text is: "If an individual issues a false invitation letter or other application materials for others to apply for entry, exit, stay or residence, the immigration management agency will impose a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan; if there is any illegal income, the illegal income will be confiscated." If the unit issues false materials, it will be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. At the same time, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel (leaders and handlers of affairs) will be fined not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan
Level of Evidence: A
Source: State Council (2026). Regulations on Exit and Entry Management (National Decree No. 841). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173.htm> (Articles 3 and 11)

Note: You cannot verify the details of a stranger, and you cannot guarantee whether what he says is true or false. But once the invitation letter is false, you will be punished by the person who issued it. This is the same type of risk as Section 8 "Not carrying things for strangers": the materials are issued in your name, and the consequences fall on you. If public officials or military personnel want to apply for foreign nationality or overseas residence status through an agency in violation of regulations, the agency will not only be unable to apply for it, but must also report it to the supervisory authority.

Case: Lao Liu sent a false invitation letter to a distant relative, saying that the other party was coming to visit relatives. After the Immigration Bureau found out, Lao Liu was fined 8,000 yuan in accordance with the rules and confiscated the 2,000 yuan "thank you fee" given by his relatives. He regretted it.

items.title: Before leaving the country, send your itinerary, residence, and people traveling with you to a family member, and make an appointment on how often you will be contacted
items.core: If a person loses contact abroad, the family can approach the embassy or consulate for help. The embassy or consulate will tell the family how to call the police in the local area, and will urge the case after it is filed. The premise is that someone in the country knows where you should be and when to contact you. Just send the flight number, address, phone number of the person traveling with you and how often you plan to contact them to a family member.
body: Cost: No money. Send a message before you go.

Benefits: When Chinese citizens’ whereabouts abroad are unknown, relatives can seek help from diplomatic missions abroad. The original text of the regulations is "Diplomatic agencies stationed abroad should provide local police methods and other information for obtaining assistance." After the local police file a case, the embassy or consulate will urge them to handle it in a timely manner. Whether these requests for help can be initiated depends on whether anyone in the country knows where you should be and when you should be contacted
Evidence level: C

Source: State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (National Order No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (Article 13); Author’s experience, no direct documentation

Remarks: It is enough to write four things clearly: flight number, residence address, name and phone number of traveling companions, and agreed contact frequency. If you are going to a place with poor signal or public security, make it clear that "call the police if you don't hear anything for a long time." The cost of this thing is close to zero, but the above rescue procedures must first have your family know your itinerary before you can start

Case: Xiao Li went to Thailand for a free trip. Before departure, he sent his flight, hotel address, and phone number of his companions to his sister, and agreed to make a video call every night. On the third day, his mobile phone was stolen. My sister contacted the hotel and the embassy and consulate according to the itinerary, and helped him apply for a travel permit for his return trip that day.

items.title: Check the destination regulations before taking medicine abroad: cold medicines and cough medicines containing pseudoephedrine and codeine, sleeping pills, psychotropic medicines and powerful analgesics, bring the original packaging, prescription or doctor's certificate, and only bring the amount for personal use
items.core: Pseudoephedrine exceeds 10%, codeine exceeds 1% Cold medicines and cough medicines are regulated as stimulant raw materials or narcotics in Japan, and you must apply for a license in advance. If you take sleeping pills for more than a month, you must apply for a license in advance in Japan, and in Singapore, you must apply in advance for medicines with controlled ingredients. Only by bringing the original packaging and a doctor's certificate, and only bringing the amount for personal use, can you avoid having the medicine confiscated, fined or even sentenced to jail time.
body: Cost: No money. Check the destination’s official website for a few minutes before departure. If you want to take controlled drugs, you have to go to the hospital to get a certificate and apply for it about two weeks in advance.

Income: Japan divides medicines into several categories according to their ingredients. Drugs containing more than 10% pseudoephedrine are considered "stimulant raw materials". Those containing more than 1% codeine are considered narcotic drugs. These two categories must apply for permission from the Narcotics Control Department of the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare at least 14 days in advance before entering the country. The medicine must be carried with you personally and cannot be mailed or asked to be taken by family members. Psychotropic drugs such as diazepam and triazolam do not need to be applied for within one month's consumption. Common medicines are also limited: prescription drugs are limited to one month’s dosage, and other medicines are limited to two months’ dosage. If you exceed the limit, you must first apply for an "Import Confirmation Certificate". The original reminder from the Chinese Embassy in Japan is: If you bring medicines into Japan illegally and in violation of regulations, "violators will be fined, detained or even sentenced, and contraband will be confiscated." The Health Sciences Authority of Singapore (HSA) stipulates that medicines that do not contain controlled ingredients can only be carried for a maximum of 3 months. Keep a copy of your prescription or doctor's letter with you. The medicine should be placed in the original packaging with the pharmacy label attached. For medicines containing controlled ingredients, apply for approval at least 2 weeks in advance. Medications that are more than 3 months old are not allowed to be brought in, nor are medications in the form of chewing gum. Bringing medicines for others is limited to immediate family members’ own prescriptions. Substandard medicines will be confiscated and may be subject to law enforcement. On the Chinese side, customs law requires individuals to carry items in and out of the country "limited to personal use and in reasonable quantities." For narcotic drugs and first-class psychotropic drugs, you can bring the maximum dosage in a single prescription with the hospital's medical certificate and identity certificate. Customs releases based on the principle of self-use and reasonableness
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Narcotics Control Department of the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare of Japan. Application Guidance: "When you enter/leave Japan carrying your medicine containing controlled substances in Japan for your own medical use, you need to get a permission in advance." "You should apply at least 14 days prior to your travel." as your family.". <https://www.ncd.mhlw.go.jp/en/application2.html>; Narcotics Control Department, Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare of Japan (2024). Controlled Substances List (December 12, 2024 version): "Ephedrine, Pseudoephedrine (*Any substances containing 10% or less of ephedrine or pseudoephedrine are excluded.)" "Codeine… (*Any substances containing 1% or less of codeine or its salt are excluded.)". <https://www.ncd.mhlw.go.jp/dl_data/keitai/cotrolled_substances_list20241212%20.pdf>; Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare of Japan. Information for those who are bringing medicines for personal use into Japan: "Poison, Deadly poison, Prescription drug: Up to 1 month supply" "Other Drugs, Quasi drugs: Up to 2 month supply". <https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/iyakuhin/kojinyunyu/topics/tp010401-1_00001.html>; Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare of Japan. Personal input of medical medicines, etc.: "Input of portable medicines for medical purposes (such as ジアゼパム, トリアゾラム, etc.)": If the amount of the injection is more than 1 month, it is necessary to carry the injection and input it in advance, and it is necessary to obtain the input confirmation certificate in advance." <https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/iyakuhin/kojinyunyu/topics/tp010401-1.html>; Chinese Embassy in Japan (2018). Please do not bring contraband when traveling to Japan. <https://jp.china-embassy.gov.cn/jbwzlmnew/lszcnew/LSBHYXZ/LSBHLBZN/201811/t20181113_9475556.htm>; Health Sciences Authority, Singapore. Bringing in personal medications: "You may bring up to 3 months' supply if no approval is needed and the medication is not prohibited." "Please note that imports of quantities "Failure to comply will result in your medication being confiscated or enforcement action may be taken.". <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab22b8a017abd719e0f05c0>; State Council (third revision in 2024). Regulations on the Administration of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Article 44). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081819c230ff2019c2d0fcaed641d>

Note: The regulations will change and each country is different. This book only writes about the method. Before departure, check the official website of the destination health department or customs, or the consular reminder from the Chinese embassy in the local area. The above regulations of Japan and Singapore are checked according to the official website on October 14, 2026. If the medicine contains these ingredients, look at the ingredient list on the package insert, and if you are unsure, ask the doctor who prescribes the medicine. It is best to bring medicines to the person taking the medicines themselves. In Singapore, only immediate family members are allowed to bring their own prescription medicines. This is the same as Section 8, Article 29 (Do not carry things for strangers). Take a photo of the prescription and medicine box and save a copy. For the storage method, see Article 7 of this section (take a photo and save a copy in the cloud).

Case: Before going to Japan, Ms. Chen checked the Food and Drug Administration regulations and asked to keep codeine-containing cough medicine in the country. She only brought a two-week supply of sleeping pills and kept the original packaging and prescription. After the entry declaration, she cleared customs smoothly.

items.title: When returning from abroad, don’t bring meat products (vacuum-packed ham and jerky are also included), cheese, fresh fruits and seeds. If you bring animal and plant products, go to the red channel to declare them
items.core: When you return to the country, you cannot bring meat regardless of whether it is raw or cooked. No matter how tightly packed ham, jerky, and sausage are, it will be the same. Cheese, butter, fresh eggs, fresh fruits, vegetables and seeds are also on the banned list. If you bring it, it will be returned or destroyed. If you fail to declare animal or plant products, you may be fined up to 5,000 yuan.
body: Cost: No money. Avoid these categories when buying specialties abroad, and go through your luggage before returning home. If you bring something you are unsure about, take the red channel through customs and wait in line for a while.

Benefit: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs and the General Administration of Customs announced a prohibited list in 2021. Everything you carry with you, checked in, mailed, expressly, and cross-border e-commerce direct purchases are all under its control. These are the categories that are most relevant to ordinary tourists. The first category is meat. The original text is "(raw or cooked) meat (including organs) and its products." The list does not make exceptions based on packaging. The second category is milk and eggs, including cream, butter, cheese, and condensed milk, as well as preserved eggs, salted eggs, and mayonnaise. The third category is "fresh fruits, vegetables" and fresh cut flowers. The fourth category is seeds, seedlings and other plant materials that can grow. The fifth category is live animals, except cats and dogs. Bird's nests are also banned, except for commercially sterile canned bird's nests. Article 29 of the Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine Law states that items on the list brought into the country will be "returned or destroyed." Animal and plant products not included in the list can be brought, but they must also be declared. The customs regulations for the supervision of baggage items state that if you carry animals, plants, or animal or plant products, you must make a written declaration to the customs. If the written declaration has not been completed when the customs starts inspection, it will be regarded as no declaration. The original text of the measure also says: "If you are not aware of customs regulations or do not know how to choose a channel, you should choose the 'red channel'." The penalty for failure to declare is stated in Article 39 of the Quarantine Law. Those who “fail to declare for quarantine” will be fined. Article 59 of the Regulations for the Implementation of the Quarantine Law sets such fines at less than 5,000 yuan
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, General Administration of Customs (2021). Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, General Administration of Customs Announcement No. 470 (List of animals and plants, their products and other quarantine objects prohibited from being carried or sent into the country by the People's Republic of China). <https://www.moa.gov.cn/nybgb/2022/202202/202203/t20220324_6393815.htm>; National People’s Congress Standing Committee (revised in 2009). Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine Law (Articles 29, 30, and 39). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf6ab3604e7>; State Council (1996). Regulations on the Implementation of the Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine Law (State Council Order No. 206, Articles 41 and 59). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f4086afae03c1>; General Administration of Customs (2025). Measures of the Customs of the People's Republic of China for the Supervision of Entry and Exit Baggage (General Administration of Customs Order No. 276, Articles 9, 11, 12, 25, and 27). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202502/content_7005697.htm>; General Administration of Customs (2025). Announcement on matters related to the declaration of luggage and items for entry and exit personnel (General Administration of Customs Announcement 2025 No. 43, Articles 1 and 3). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017195.htm>

Note: The list is verified according to the announcement on the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs on October 14, 2026. The two departments said they would "dynamically adjust" and check again before departure. There are a few exceptions. Dried and cooked aquatic products are not prohibited, such as dried squid and dried shrimp, but they still need to be declared. Those that have been approved and have an official quarantine certificate from the exporting country are not subject to the list restrictions. Each person is limited to one cat or dog, and must have an official quarantine certificate and vaccination certificate from the exporting country. When traveling abroad, many destination countries also do not allow meat products to be brought into the country. The inspection method is the same as Article 12 of this section (check the regulations of the destination before taking medicine abroad). Please refer to the official website of the destination customs or the consular reminder from the Chinese embassy or consulate.

Case: Ms. Chen returned from Germany with vacuum-packed ham and cheese in her suitcase, and did not declare through the red channel. During customs inspection, they discovered that these meat and dairy products were prohibited from entering the country, and they were all destroyed. She was also fined for failing to declare them, which was not worth the loss.

items.title: Check where the safety exits are before entering KTVs, bars, or secret rooms. If they are locked or blocked, find another one
items.core: According to regulations, when entertainment venues are open, evacuation passages and safety exits must be clear. Blocking, locking, placing things in the way, and covering signage are not allowed. Internet cafes are also not allowed to lock doors and windows. If you can't do it, it's illegal, and you can report it. If the private room is underground, has only one exit, and the aisle is full of debris, find another one.
body: Cost: No money. Look up for 10 seconds when you enter.

Income: This is the legal obligation of the operator. If you can't do it, it's illegal, and you can report it. The original text of the regulations: "During business, entertainment venues should ensure that evacuation passages and safety exits are smooth. They must not block or lock evacuation passages and safety exits. They must not set up fences or other obstacles that affect evacuation in evacuation passages and safety exits." The regulations also require that "clear indication signs should be set up at evacuation passages and safety exits, and indication signs must not be blocked or covered." Internet cafes are also required to "block or lock doors and windows, safe evacuation passages and safe exits during business hours" and "prohibit open flame lighting and smoking"
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2006). Entertainment Venue Management Regulations (National Decree No. 458, Article 20, 21). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297.htm>; State Council (2002). Regulations on the Management of Business Places for Internet Access Services (National Decree No. 363, Article 21). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_61788.htm>

Note: If any of the following items occupies one of the following, please change the location: the box is underground, there is only one exit, the aisle is full of debris, and the safety exit indicator light does not light up. When such places catch fire, there is heavy smoke, narrow aisles, and many people, most of whom are drunk. The time left for you to escape is counted in seconds. According to the regulations, the reporting hotline should be written on the warning sign in the venue

Case: Xiao Lin booked a secret room with his classmates. When he entered the store, he first looked for the safe exit. He found boxes stacked in the corridor and the exit was blocked by a curtain. He canceled the reservation on the spot and went next door. Later, the store closed due to fire protection issues.

items.title: A price list must be clearly marked before ordering. Entertainment venues must clearly mark the price, and "play now and calculate later" is not accepted
items.core: According to regulations, entertainment venues must clearly mark the price of services and goods sold, and they must take the initiative to show you the price list. The so-called "exorbitantly priced drinks" often occur when the price list is not read and the bill is settled based on the verbal quotation afterwards. When entering the private room, you first need to take a photo of the order, and after ordering, you will be asked for a confirmation list. If there is any dispute over the checkout, please call 12315 on the spot.
body: Cost: No money. Ask for an order once. The difficulty is that asking the price in front of others is a bit embarrassing.

Revenue: Original text of the regulations: "Entertainment venues that provide entertainment services and sell goods must clearly mark prices and provide price lists to consumers; consumers must not be forced or deceived to accept services or purchase goods." Violations of price laws and regulations will be punished by relevant departments in accordance with the law. A common situation in the so-called "exorbitantly priced drinks" disputes is that the price list is not shown, and the settlement is based on the verbal quotation afterwards. This sentence is based on the author’s experience and no official statistics have been found
Level of Evidence: A
Source: State Council (2006). Regulations on the Management of Entertainment Places (National Decree No. 458, Articles 29 and 53). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297.htm>
