Remarks: How to do it: Before entering the box, ask for a price list, either paper or electronic, and take a photo when you get it. After ordering, I asked for a confirmed list. For the "special" and "fruit plate" recommended by the waiter, always ask for the price before ordering. If there is a dispute over the checkout, call 12315 on the spot. Don't pay first and then defend your rights. It will be much harder for you to provide evidence after you have paid.

Case: Xiao Zhou asked for the price list and took a photo before ordering drinks at a bar. The waiter said, "Play first and then calculate later." He insisted on reading the order and confirming it item by item. There was no temporary service charge when checking out.

items.title: If someone hands someone "something" in the venue, he will leave immediately. Tolerating or providing it is not "helping a friend"
items.core: Drugs are not allowed to be sold or provided in entertainment venues, nor are people allowed to smoke inside. Violators will be subject to suspension of business for 3 to 6 months for rectification, and severe license revocation. Allowing others to use the private room or accommodation you booked may constitute the crime of allowing others to take drugs. Someone takes out unknown powder, tablets, or cartridges and asks you to try them, and leave on the spot.
body: Cost: No money. Get up and walk out. The difficulty is leaving in front of a table full of people.

Revenue: The regulations explicitly prohibit entertainment venues from "selling or providing drugs, or organizing, forcing, instigating, luring, deceiving, or allowing others to take or inject drugs." Employees are also not allowed to take drugs or provide conditions for customers to do the above things. In case of violation, the public security department will confiscate the illegal gains and illegal property, and order the company to suspend business for 3 to 6 months for rectification. In serious cases, the entertainment business license will be revoked. The regulations also require venues to display warning signs prohibiting drugs, gambling, and prostitution in prominent locations in lobbies, private rooms, and private rooms, and to indicate the reporting hotline. On the personal side: The Criminal Law stipulates that "anyone who allows others to take or inject drugs shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention or surveillance, and shall also be fined." The judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court lists the circumstances for criminalization, including housing multiple people at one time, housing multiple people within two years, housing minors, and housing for profit. Those who do not commit a crime will be detained for 10 to 15 days in accordance with the Public Security Administration Punishment Law and may be fined not more than 3,000 yuan. If the circumstances are relatively minor, the offender shall be detained for not more than 5 days or fined not more than 1,000 yuan. Those who take or inject drugs by themselves will also be detained for 10 to 15 days and may be fined up to 3,000 yuan
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council (2006). Regulations on the Management of Entertainment Venues (National Order No. 458, Articles 14, 30, and 42). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297.htm>; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 354). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Supreme People’s Court (2016). Interpretation of Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Drug Crime Cases (Fa Shi [2016] No. 8, Article 12). <https://www.sc.jcy.gov.cn/zlxx/sfjs/201606/t20160617_1809560.shtml> (Reprinted by the Sichuan Provincial People’s Procuratorate); National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2025). Public Security Management Punishment Law (revised in 2025, Articles 84 and 85). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>

Note: As long as someone takes out unknown powder, tablets, or electronic cigarette cartridges, please "try it" and leave on the spot. Don't stay to watch the fun. Your personal risk is greater than the venue. If you take drugs yourself, you will be punished by public security. "Letting friends use it here" in the private room you booked or at your own residence may constitute the crime of allowing others to take drugs.

Case: It was a friend's birthday in a KTV box. Someone took out an unknown powder and invited Xiao Chen to "refresh himself". He immediately took his friend away and contacted the clerk. The police later investigated the box and he was not involved in the case.

items.title: Don’t eat candies and snacks given by strangers, don’t drink drinks that are out of sight, and don’t accept cigarette cartridges from others
items.core: Today’s drugs don’t look like drugs. "Shangtou" e-cigarettes mixed with synthetic cannabinoids look similar to ordinary e-cigarettes. Some people give them to people to try in bars, KTVs, and hotels. Those who cheat others to smoke will be detained for 10 to 15 days and fined. Those who smoke themselves will also be detained. Those who are tricked into smoking may be given a lighter sentence or not fined. Change the drink once it is out of sight.
body: Cost: No money. Don't accept anything handed over by others. If your cup is out of sight, change it to another cup.

Benefits: Today’s drugs don’t look like drugs. Synthetic cannabinoid substances have been listed as a whole category since July 1, 2021, and this category is generally controlled as drugs. Some people mix it into e-cigarette oil to make "top" e-cigarettes. In the case reported by the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the investigators described the e-liquid as "can be changed into various colors and flavors by adding edible pigments" and "is basically the same as ordinary e-cigarettes in appearance." Sellers invite friends and associates in bars, KTVs, and hotels to promote the product and induce others to take it. According to reports, underage drug users accounted for nearly 40% of the drug abuse cases handled locally that year. Etomidate will be included in the Category II Psychotropic Drugs List starting from October 1, 2023. Cheating people to take drugs is an offense in itself. Anyone who induces, instigates, deceives or forces others to take or inject drugs shall be detained for 10 to 15 days and fined 1,000 to 5,000 yuan. Those who constitute a crime will be sentenced to less than 3 years, those who commit serious crimes will be sentenced to 3 to 7 years, and those who are forced will be sentenced to 3 to 10 years. Those who commit crimes will be given more severe punishment. Those who take or inject drugs themselves will be detained for 10 to 15 days and may be fined up to 3,000 yuan. If the circumstances are less serious, the offender shall be detained for not more than 5 days or fined not more than 1,000 yuan. The same law stipulates that those who engage in sex under coercion or deception will be given a lighter, mitigated or no punishment. They may also be ordered not to enter entertainment venues for 6 months to 1 year. Addict ordered to community detox for 3 years. Those who refuse community detoxification, or relapse during detoxification, will be subject to compulsory isolation detoxification for 2 years, which can be extended for up to another 1 year (National Public Security Administration Punishment Law will be effective from January 2026)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Supreme People's Procuratorate (2021). Wujiang District, Suzhou, Jiangsu: Prosecutors handling the case reveal new drugs disguised as trendy drugs. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202110/t20211011_531831.shtml>; State Food and Drug Administration, Ministry of Public Security, and National Health Commission (2023). Announcement on Adjusting the Catalog of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Drugs (No. 120 of 2023). <https://yjj.sh.gov.cn/qtgzwj/20230911/3b612c94e35b4b63abba314c972a2593.html> (Reprinted by Shanghai Food and Drug Administration, original page nmpa.gov.cn returns 412 in this machine); National People's Congress Standing Committee (2025). Public Security Management Punishment Law (2025) (Revised in 2007, Articles 20, 84, and 85). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; National People’s Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 353). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2007). Anti-Drug Law (Articles 33, 38, 47). <http://www.gd.gov.cn/zwgk/wjk/zcfgk/content/post_2520706.html> (Reprinted by the Guangdong Provincial People’s Government)

Note: It is not just entertainment venues, but also in front of schools, friends’ gatherings, and long-distance buses. It doesn’t matter whether you give candies, drinks or cigarette cartridges. Drugging is often followed by robbery, sexual assault and extortion. There are no public official statistics on this, and it is a judgment based on experience. It is much easier to change the drink as soon as it is out of sight than to pursue it afterwards. What to do when someone takes out unknown powders, tablets, or cartridges in the venue, see Article 3 of this section. Carrying something for someone else, see Section 8, Article 29.

Case: Xiao He attended a bar party. When she came back, she found that the cup had been touched by others and stopped drinking. The stranger said that the e-cigarette was "very high" and she refused to accept it. She took a taxi home that night, and then someone was sent to the hospital due to discomfort.

items.title: Don’t open scripted entertainment venues or secret rooms in residential buildings or below the second underground floor
items.core: The 2022 notice from the fifth department stated that scripted entertainment venues are not allowed to be opened in residential buildings, nor are they allowed to be opened on the second underground floor or below. Such venues are often dark and have narrow passages. Some are decorated with combustible materials, and evacuation passages are locked or blocked, making it difficult to escape in the event of a fire. Before booking, check the address and floor on the review page, and find another hotel if it doesn’t comply.
body: Cost: No money. Before booking, ask which floor the address is on.

Revenue: The special notice of the five departments in 2022 is very specific: "Scripted entertainment business premises shall not be located in residential buildings, or below the first basement level of the building (excluding the first basement level)." The notice also requires sites to implement the requirements of the Production Safety Law and the Fire Protection Law, "carry out fire risk self-awareness, self-inspection, and self-correction on a regular basis, and improve the ability to organize evacuation and escape in emergencies and to fight initial fires." The same notice also requires scripts to have age-appropriate cues. If the scene is not suitable for minors, minors shall not be allowed to enter. Except for statutory holidays, rest days and winter and summer vacations, scripted entertainment activities are not allowed to be provided to minors. The fire protection and cultural tourism departments of Shanghai's Qingpu District inspected 13 such places at the end of 2021. The notice stated that such places usually have dark environments, narrow passages, are decorated with combustible materials, and evacuation passages are locked and occupied.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Culture and Tourism, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, Ministry of Emergency Management, State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Notice on strengthening the management of scripted entertainment business venues. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-06/27/content_5698021.htm>; Shanghai Qingpu District Culture and Tourism Bureau (2022-01-10). Report on the special inspection of fire safety in "escape room" type places in our district. <https://www.shqp.gov.cn/tv/wlzwgk/ml/yw/20220217/913272.html>

Note: The Qingpu notice also said that some businesses made the rooms intricate for the sake of atmosphere, and also hid evacuation signs and emergency lights. Once something goes wrong, it is not easy for people to find the exit immediately. You can tell the floor on the review page before booking, and you can also tell whether it is a residential building. If you are not compliant, just go to another store

Case: Xiao Zhao booked a horror room and saw that the address on the review page was on the sixth floor of a residential building. He immediately canceled the reservation and changed the reservation to a mall store. Later, the original store was notified of rectification. Players said that the passage was narrow and the room was stuffy.

items.title: If your mood is bad enough to cause depression, just go for a walk or run. The antidepressant effect size (effect size) is directly proportional to the intensity
items.core: For people with severe depression, exercise, brisk walking or jogging will have the most obvious improvement. Followed by yoga, strength training, Tai Chi and Qigong, there is not much difference between them. The higher the intensity, the better the effect. Strength training and yoga are the easiest to stick to. The quality of the evidence in this area is low. What is certain is that moving is better than staying still. Choose the one you can persist in.
body: Cost: No money. About half an hour each time. The difficulty is that when you are in a bad mood, the last thing you want to do is move, so you have to push yourself.

Earnings: This is the result of 218 controlled trials that were randomized into two groups. Involving 495 groups, 14,170 participants meeting clinical criteria for major depression. Algorithms allow various movements to be compared with each other (Bayesian network meta-analysis). The comparison was between usual care and a placebo tablet (active control). The effect size is expressed as Hedges' g, with the more negative the number, the greater the symptom improvement. Brisk walking or jogging −0.62 (95% confidence interval −0.80 to −0.45, meaning the true value falls roughly within this range). Yoga −0.55 (−0.73 to −0.36). Strength training −0.49 (−0.69 to −0.29). Mixed Aerobic −0.43 (−0.61 to −0.24). Tai Chi or Qigong −0.42 (−0.65 to −0.21). The original text says that "the effect of exercise is directly proportional to the intensity prescribed": the higher the intensity, the better the effect. Strength training and yoga are the most acceptable and easiest to persist
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Noetel M, Sanders T, Gallardo-Gómez D, et al. (2024). Effect of exercise for depression: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. BMJ, 384, e075847. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-075847>

Note: Controversy. The author himself stated that only one of the 218 studies was clean enough and not easily biased by design. According to the popular scoring method, walking quickly and jogging only counts as "low" credibility, while the rest are "very low". Exercise cannot be hidden from the participants. When people know that they are exercising, they tend to feel better. This expectation cannot be eliminated. The conclusion direction is still available: moving is better than not moving, the intensity should not be too low, and choose the one you can persist in. This is an expansion of Section 3 "Get active first when you are feeling depressed" and cannot replace standard treatment after diagnosis

Case: After Xiao Zheng was diagnosed with mild depression, he started walking briskly for 20 minutes a day, and increased it to 40 minutes after two weeks. His sleep and mood gradually improved. During the follow-up visit, the doctor said that the score on the scale had dropped.

items.title: When anxiety affects your life, the effect of mindfulness-based stress reduction classes is not inferior to commonly used anti-anxiety drugs
items.core: People diagnosed with anxiety disorders take 8 weeks of mindfulness-based stress reduction classes, and the symptom improvement is almost the same as taking the anti-anxiety drug escitalopram. Nearly 80% of people who take the medicine have had adverse reactions, and some people have dropped out because of this. About half of the people who attended the class showed up, and no one quit. The course is a standardized 8-week course, and any meditation app does not count.
body: Cost: It costs a little to sign up for classes. The course lasts for 8 weeks, with classes once a week and daily practice at home. The hard part is practicing every day for 8 weeks.

Benefits: This was a trial in 3 urban academic medical centers in the United States to see if taking classes would be worse than taking medication (a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial). Two hundred and seventy-six adults with diagnosed anxiety disorders were randomly divided in half in a 1:1 ratio. One group took an 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction course. One group received escitalopram (10 to 20 mg flexible dose). 208 people completed the journey. At the end, based on the doctor's anxiety severity score (Clinical Global Impression Severity Scale), the mindfulness group dropped by 1.35 and the medication group dropped by 1.43. The difference between the two groups is −0.07 (95% CI −0.38 to 0.23, that is, the real gap falls roughly within this period; P=0.65, that is, there is no difference between this gap and no difference). The lower limit of this period does not cross the pre-drawn “not worse” line (non-inferiority margin −0.495). Side effects varied widely: 78.6% of the drug group had at least one adverse reaction related to the trial, and 10 people dropped out because of it. Mindfulness group 15.4%, no one dropped out because of this
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Hoge EA, Bui E, Mete M, Dutton MA, Baker AW, Simon NM (2023). Mindfulness-based stress reduction vs escitalopram for the treatment of adults with anxiety disorders: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA Psychiatry, 80(1), 13-21. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2022.3679>

Note: The trial used a standardized 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction course (MBSR), and any meditation app cannot be equated with it. It is intended for people who have met the diagnostic criteria for an anxiety disorder and should still see a doctor. If you have been putting off treatment because of concerns about side effects, there is another option with comparable evidence.

Case: Ms. Wang was too anxious to work overtime, so she signed up for the hospital’s standardized eight-week mindfulness-based stress reduction course, followed it every week and recorded it every day. After eight weeks, I fell asleep faster, palpitations decreased, and doctors assessed that my symptoms were significantly improved.

items.title: If you want to slow down on the spot, use 5 minutes of "cyclic sighing": inhale for two sections, and exhale for a longer period.
items.core: Doing breathing exercises for 5 minutes a day for a month will improve your mood and slow down your breathing better than mindfulness meditation of the same length. Among several breathing methods, "cyclic sighing" which lengthens the exhalation is the best. The method is to take a breath through your nose, take another small breath to fill your lungs, and then slowly spit it out through your mouth. This is just an experiment. It’s up to you to decide whether it’s good or bad, but you don’t have to spend any money.
body: Cost: Nothing. 5 minutes a day.

Benefits: This was an at-home, randomized, controlled trial comparing three daily 5-minute breathing exercises with the same length of mindfulness meditation for 1 month. The three breathing techniques are: cyclic sighing (emphasis on prolonged exhalation), box breathing (inhale, hold, and exhale for equal lengths), and cyclic hyperventilation with breath hold (long inhale, short exhale). Putting the data of each person and time together (mixed effects model), breathing exercises are better than mindfulness meditation, especially circular sighing, which is mainly based on exhalation. It was better at improving mood (P<0.05, that is, this difference is not like a coincidence) and decreasing respiratory rate (P<0.05).
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Balban MY, Neri E, Kogon MM, et al. (2023). Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal. Cell Reports Medicine, 4(1), 100895. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2022.100895>

Note: The method is to take a breath through your nose, take another short breath to fill your lungs, and then exhale slowly and long through your mouth. Repeat for 5 minutes. This is the only test that can be done at home. I have to fill in the questionnaire myself, and the number of people is not large. The effect is only slightly better than meditation, but it doesn’t really solve the problem. But it costs nothing, only takes 5 minutes, can be done anytime, anywhere, and is cost-effective

Case: Xiao Tang was so nervous before the interview that his hands were shaking. He followed the reminder and did a five-minute sigh cycle: inhale twice and then exhale long. After three rounds, my breathing slowed down, and my heartbeat slowed down a bit before I walked in. I was still nervous but could answer normally.

items.title: Think of "meeting people regularly" as a health expense, don't only see people when you are in a bad mood: people who rarely interact with each other have a higher risk of death, but it is not clear who is responsible.
items.core: People who rarely interact with others have a higher risk of death during the following years. The same goes for people who feel lonely, those who live alone, and more so among people under 65. These are all based on follow-up observations. It may also be that people with poor health are more likely to live alone.
body: Cost: It costs a little money and some time to meet. The difficulty is that you have to take the initiative to ask someone out when you are in a good mood.

Gains: This is the result of 70 studies that recorded and then followed together (meta-analysis), with a total of 3.4 million participants followed for an average of 7 years. Social isolation, loneliness, and living alone are all associated with increased mortality. After deducting interfering factors such as age and physical condition, the weighted average odds ratios are: social isolation 1.29, loneliness 1.26, and living alone 1.32. Effect sizes were similar among the three and were larger among those under 65 than among older adults
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Holt-Lunstad J, Smith TB, Baker M, Harris T, Stephenson D (2015). Loneliness and social isolation as risk factors for mortality: a meta-analytic review. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 10(2), 227-237. <https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691614568352>

Note: Controversy. These are all correlations observed from the population, not group controlled experiments, and it is indistinguishable who is the cause and who is the cause. People who are already in poor health are more likely to live alone and socialize less. The author regards social relationships as health factors of the same magnitude as smoking and obesity, but there are no randomized trials to prove that "increasing social contact can reduce mortality." This does not conflict with Section 3 "Reduce the relationships that consume you": that one, cut off the relationships that consume you, here you need to keep the ones that restore your energy.

Case: Lao Zhou seldom goes out after his retirement, so his children put meetings twice a week on their calendar. He regularly eats with his old colleagues and goes for walks on weekends. After half a year, he has a more regular schedule and has someone he can contact immediately when he is in a bad mood.

items.title: When choosing a place to live, take into account the surrounding green space, but don’t expect that “going to the park more” will extend your life.
items.core: The better the greenery within 500 meters of where you live, the lower the risk of death, not measured by the number of times you go to the park. For every 0.1 higher the vegetation index (a number that converts greenness), the risk is about 4% lower. People who live in areas with good greening tend to have more money and enjoy better air. So don’t think that going to the park will extend your life. Just take the surrounding green spaces into account when choosing a place to live.
body: Cost: Nothing. When viewing the property, take a look at the surrounding greenery.

Gains: This is the result of nine studies that tracked people over many years (a meta-analysis of cohort studies), involving 8.32 million people in seven countries. What we look at is the degree of surrounding greening within 500 meters of your residence, measured by the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI, a number that converts ground greening into a number). The pooled hazard ratio for total mortality was 0.96 (95% CI 0.94–0.97) for each 0.1 index increase in greenness. The risk of death is about 4% lower, and the true value falls roughly in the low 3% to low 6% range. Seven out of nine studies found that better greenery was associated with lower mortality, and the difference was not likely to be due to chance. There is no correlation between the other 2 items.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Rojas-Rueda D, Nieuwenhuijsen MJ, Gascon M, Perez-Leon D, Mudu P (2019). Green spaces and mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. The Lancet Planetary Health, 3(11), e469-e477. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2542-5196(19)30215-3>

Note: Controversy. The results of various studies are very different (I²=95%, the larger the number, the more inconsistent with each other). And it measures the greenness around your residence, not the number of times you go to the park. People who live in places with good greening tend to be richer, have better air, and love to exercise more. These factors are inseparable from the greening. Don't read it like "you can extend your life by going to the park." The usable part is to include green space when choosing a place to live, and the cost is zero. NDVI is close to 0 for bare ground and cement, and close to 1 for dense vegetation. So "0.1" is roughly the difference between moving from a bare block to a block with rows of street trees.

Case: When Xiao Liu was changing rent, he compared two apartments. The commute took about 20 minutes. He chose the one with street trees and a street garden downstairs. It was more comfortable to walk by every day, but he did not regard it as a guarantee of longevity.

items.title: Don’t go to hot springs or saunas after drinking alcohol, and don’t take hot baths when you get home.
items.core: In Finland, half of the people who die in saunas have been drinking. In Tokyo, about a quarter of those who died in bathing after autopsy had high levels of blood alcohol. In a record of bathtub drowning, drunkenness was the most common cause. Japanese officials list "Don't take a bath after drinking alcohol" as a key point in preventing drowning. If your companion drinks too much, don't let him go in there alone.
body: Cost: Nothing. After drinking, I would take a dip another day and simply take a shower when I got home. The difficulty is that hot springs and saunas are often the next event after a dinner party. Everyone at the table is going, so you have to say no.

Gains: Finland examined people who died in saunas from 1990 to 2002, case by case, using police and forensic reports. Such deaths are less than 2 in 100,000 per year, and the original article states that "overall 50% of people are under the influence of alcohol." The author said that the risk of alcohol is getting bigger, and the focus of prevention is to drink less and don't leave drunk people alone in the sauna. The Tokyo Medical Examiner handled 3,289 bathing deaths from 2009 to 2011. Of the 550 autopsies performed, 140 had blood alcohol levels exceeding 0.5 milligrams per milliliter, accounting for about a quarter. Another autopsy in Tokyo recorded 77 cases of bathtub drowning. Drunkness was the most contributing factor to drowning (25 cases), followed by heart disease (22 cases). A December 2025 reminder from the Japan Consumer Agency stated that 7,776 people drowned in bathtubs in Japan in 2024, including 7,363 people over 65 years old. Key points to prevent accidents read: Do not take a bath right after eating, drinking, or taking medicine. The Chinese Embassy in Japan reminds that "it is not advisable to bathe after drinking" because "bathing while drinking can easily cause cardiac or vascular system emergencies." According to popular science from the Shaanxi Provincial Health Commission, if you soak in hot springs after drinking, the high water temperature will dilate blood vessels, which may lead to hypotension, hypoglycemia, and even fainting.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Kenttämies A, Karkola K (2008). Death in sauna. Journal of Forensic Sciences, 53(3), 724-729. Suzuki H, Hikiji W, Tanifuji T, Abe N, Fukunaga T (2015). Characteristics of sudden bath-related death investigated by medical examiners in Tokyo, Japan. Journal of Epidemiology, 25(2), 126-132. Mishima S, Suzuki H, Fukunaga T, Nishitani Y (2018). Postmortem computed tomography findings in cases of bath-related death: applicability and limitation in forensic practice. Forensic Science International, 282, 195-203. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.forsciint.2017.11.030>; Consumer Geng (2025). At the end of the year and the beginning of the new year, please pay attention to accidents involving elderly people: "Bath after eating, bathing after drinking, and taking medicines, avoid bathing after eating". <https://www.caa.go.jp/policies/policy/consumer_safety/caution/caution_084/>; Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Japan (2015). Consular Reminder No. 17: "It is not advisable to bathe on an empty stomach, on a full stomach, or after drinking. Bathing after drinking can easily cause cardiac or vascular system emergencies." <https://jp.china-embassy.gov.cn/chn/jbwzlmnew/lszcnew/LSBHYXZ/LSBHLBZN/201503/t20150327_9475462.htm>; Shaanxi Provincial Health Commission (2021). Only by soaking in the right hot springs can you maintain your health: "Do not soak in hot springs after drinking alcohol or on an empty stomach. The stimulation of high water temperatures can easily cause peripheral vasodilation, hypotension, hypoglycemia, and even syncope." <https://sxwjw.shaanxi.gov.cn/ywgz/gbbj/202101/t20210111_2148844.html>

Note: B was chosen because these studies only looked at dead people. No one has calculated how many people who drink and go out have accidents, so it’s impossible to say how much higher the risk is. The income is determined as "medium" based on judgment: not many people die in saunas and bathtubs, but one-quarter to half of the dead have been drunk. Most of the people who drown in Japanese bathtubs are old people, but young people who drink can also have accidents in saunas. For the benefits of daily bathing and reminders on water temperature and duration, see Section 2, Item 36 (Take a bath if possible). How to look after a drunk companion, see Section 13, Article 46 (Someone is drunk).

Case: After several friends gathered for dinner and drinks, one of them insisted on going to the hot springs despite being dissuaded. He soon became dizzy and weak in the high temperature environment, and finally fainted by the pool. His companion found out and sent him to the doctor in time to turn the situation around.

items.title: Wear a helmet when skiing, snowboarding, roller skating, or mountain biking
items.core: People who wear helmets when skiing or snowboarding are less likely to suffer head injuries in falls and collisions, and the same is true for children under 13 years old. Wearing a helmet on a bicycle reduces head injuries, serious head injuries, and fatal head injuries. Wearing a helmet does not make your neck more susceptible to injury.
body: Cost: A few hundred dollars to buy one. Take a few seconds each time you put it on and buckle it.

Gains: Ski and snowboard numbers come from a combined analysis of 12 studies. Most studies compare people with head injuries to others who wear helmets (case-control). Helmet wearers had fewer head injuries, odds ratio OR 0.65 (95% CI 0.55–0.79). In studies including children under 13 years of age, the odds ratio OR was 0.41 (0.27–0.59). Neck injury OR 0.89 (0.72–1.09), not elevated. The cycling figures come from 40 studies and more than 64,000 people who have fallen or crashed. Wearing a helmet also resulted in fewer head injuries, with an odds ratio of head injury OR 0.49 (0.42–0.57). Severe head injury OR 0.31 (0.25–0.37), fatal head injury OR 0.35 (0.14–0.88). Facial injury OR 0.67 (0.56–0.81). Neck injury OR 0.96 (0.74–1.25), no association was seen. The Beijing Municipal Sports Bureau said that after the local standards for ski resorts in Beijing were revised in 2017, helmets are required to enter advanced trails.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Russell K, Christie J, Hagel BE (2010). The effect of helmets on the risk of head and neck injuries among skiers and snowboarders: a meta-analysis. CMAJ, 182(4), 333-340. <https://doi.org/10.1503/cmaj.091080>; Olivier J, Creighton P (2017). Bicycle injuries and helmet injuries use: a systematic review and meta-analysis. International Journal of Epidemiology, 46(1), 278-292. <https://doi.org/10.1093/ije/dyw153>; Beijing Municipal Sports Bureau. Reply to Proposal No. 1276 of the Fourth Session of the 13th Beijing Municipal Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference: "Skiers are clearly required to wear helmets before entering advanced ski areas." <https://tyj.beijing.gov.cn/bjsports/zfxxgk_/1421305/jytablgz/11180211/index.html>

Note: These numbers are based on the likelihood of head injury after a fall or collision. Wearing a helmet will not prevent you from falling. There are no similar merging studies on roller skating and skateboarding, so they were pushed over because they fall and hit their heads in similar ways. The helmet should be closed and the buckle should be fastened. If you rent it, try it on first. Please refer to Section 1, Article 2 (Wearing a Helmet) for wearing a helmet when riding a motorcycle or electric bicycle.

Case: A ski enthusiast lost control and crashed into a guardrail while skiing at high speed on a high-speed track. He only suffered minor scratches because he wore a professional helmet throughout the process. Doctors said that if he had not worn it, he would have likely suffered a skull fracture.

items.title: When you turn 50, pick up a hobby and keep doing it, but don’t use it as a substitute for treatment for depression.
items.core: People over the age of 65 had fewer depressive symptoms and were more satisfied with life during the years when they had hobbies than during the years when they did not have hobbies. People over the age of 50 in the UK are less likely to be depressed if they take up hobbies later in life. But these are track records. In two experiments involving the elderly singing chorus, in one the depression was reduced, in the other the depression remained unchanged and the loneliness was reduced.
body: Cost: It depends on how much you choose. Musical instruments, fishing gear, and handmade materials usually cost around a few hundred yuan to get started. Set aside a few hours each week. The difficulty is that during the first period of learning, progress is slow and it is easy to give up.

Earnings: Five older age follow-up surveys from 16 countries combined, totaling 93,263 people aged 65+. The algorithm is to compare the same person with himself to see how much difference there is between the years when he has hobbies and the years when he has no hobbies (fixed effects model). In this way, factors that do not change with time such as genes, personality, and origin are all deducted. The proportion of those who have hobbies is very different, with 51.0% in Spain and 96.0% in Denmark. After netting out confounders, the pooled coefficient for depressive symptoms during hobbies was −0.10 (95% CI −0.13 to −0.07, confidence range). Several results are converted to standard deviations, so this is equivalent to 0.1 standard deviations less, which is a small difference. Self-rated health was 0.06 (0.03 to 0.08), happiness was 0.09 (0.06 to 0.13), and life satisfaction was 0.10 (0.08 to 0.12), all in the good direction. Country-level factors explain less than 9% of the differences between country outcomes. The author changed the calculation based on the British data to an algorithm that considers the order of precedence. Depressive symptoms still decreased after having hobbies. The author writes that it is not just that people with a good mental state are more likely to develop hobbies, the two are likely to influence each other. Another British survey followed 8,780 people over the age of 50, asked every two years from 2004 to 2017, and also compared the same people with themselves. Taking up a hobby was associated with an odds ratio of depression of OR 0.70 (95% CI 0.64–0.76). For people who were not originally depressed and had no hobbies, the odds ratio of becoming depressed after developing hobbies was OR 0.68 (0.56–0.83). For people who were originally depressed and had no hobbies, the odds of improvement after developing hobbies was OR 2.72 (2.09–3.53). Changes in reading, socializing, and exercising only explained about 7% of this association. There were two experiments on grouping people, both choruses, and the results were inconsistent. A British study assigned 258 people aged over 60 in five centers to either a choir group or a life-as-usual group. At 3 months, the chorus group had 1.52 lower depression scores (95% CI −2.13 to −0.92) and 1.78 lower anxiety scores (−2.5 to −1.06). At 6 months, psychological quality of life scores remained 2.35 higher (0.06 to 4.76). A US study divided 390 people over 60 years old at 12 senior centers into two groups by centre. One group started singing weekly for 90 minutes immediately, while the other group waited six months before starting. At half a year, loneliness in the chorus group decreased and interest in life increased, with effect sizes of 0.34 and 0.39, between small and medium. There were no differences in the three main predetermined measures: depressive symptoms (PHQ-8 scale), executive function, and lower limb strength.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Mak HW, Noguchi T, Bone JK, Wels J, Gao Q, Kondo K, Saito T, Fancourt D (2023). Hobby engagement and mental wellbeing among people aged 65 years and older in 16 countries. Nature Medicine, 29(9), 2233-2240. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-023-02506-1>; Fancourt D, Opher S, de Oliveira C (2020). Fixed-effects analyzes of time-varying associations between hobbies and depression in a longitudinal cohort study: support for social prescribing? Psychotherapy and Psychosomatics, 89(2), 111-113. <https://doi.org/10.1159/000503571>; Johnson JK, Stewart AL, Acree M, Nápoles AM, Flatt JD, Max WB, Gregorich SE (2020). A community choir intervention to promote well-being among diverse older adults: results from the Community of Voices trial. The Journals of Gerontology: Series B, 75(3), 549-559. <https://doi.org/10.1093/geronb/gby132>; Coulton S, Clift S, Skingley A, Rodriguez J (2015). Effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of community singing on mental health-related quality of life of older people: randomized controlled trial. The British Journal of Psychiatry, 207(3), 250-255. <https://doi.org/10.1192/bjp.bp.113.129908>

Note: Controversy. The 16-country project and the 8,780-person UK project are both tracking records. The author himself states that observational data cannot determine cause and effect. If you compare the same person with yourself, you can deduct unchanging factors such as personality and origin, but for things that have changed over the same period, you can only deduct the few things asked in the survey. Of the two choral studies, the British study reduced depression at 3 months, while the American study showed no change in depression at 6 months. The evidence is all from people over 50, with no similar data available for younger people. The determination of "small" returns is based on judgment, because the difference under the most stringent comparison method is only about 0.1 standard deviation, and the two experiments are not comparable in terms of depression. The questionnaire asked whether you had any hobbies or pastimes, no matter which one. Pick something you can do with others, and it will be included in item 9 of this section (meet people regularly); pick something that needs to be active, and count it in item 6 (go for a walk or run). If you have depression or anxiety that affects your life, see a doctor first. For what you can do, see Item 6 (Depression), Item 7 (Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction), and Item 18 of Section 3 (What to do first when you are feeling down).

Case: A retired elderly man participated in a community choir for two years and insisted on rehearsing and performing every week. His original loneliness was significantly reduced and his mentality became more cheerful. However, he still cooperated with psychological counseling intervention for mild depression symptoms.

sections.title: What skills are cost-effective to learn

items.title: If you are under 16 years old, there is no option to "go work": the company that recruits you will be fined 5,000 yuan per month, and those who are willing to recruit are illegal workers
items.core: People who graduate from junior high school are generally 15 to 16 years old, and they are stuck in this line. If you are under the age of 16, it is illegal for the company to recruit you except for special recruitment in literary, artistic and sports units. Each child worker employed will be fined 5,000 yuan per month. Therefore, those who are willing to hire you are working in units that employ workers illegally. If something goes wrong, according to regulations, the medical expenses and compensation will be borne by this unit.
body: Cost: No money. Take a minute to figure out how old you are.

Income: Article 11 of the "Compulsory Education Law": "For any child who has reached the age of six, his parents or other legal guardians shall send him to school to receive and complete compulsory education." Article 14: "Employers are prohibited from recruiting children and teenagers of school age who should receive compulsory education." Article 58: Anyone who fails to send school-age children to school in accordance with the provisions of this law without justifiable reasons shall be criticized and educated by the education administrative department of the local township people's government or county-level people's government and ordered to make corrections within a time limit. Article 2 of the "Regulations on the Prohibition of the Use of Child Labor": State agencies, social groups, enterprises and institutions, private non-enterprise units or individual industrial and commercial households "are not allowed to recruit minors under the age of 16." Article 6: "Penalty shall be based on a fine of 5,000 yuan per month for each child laborer used." Those who fail to make corrections within the time limit will be fined 10,000 yuan per person per month. Article 7: Anyone who introduces child labor to find employment will be fined 5,000 yuan for each person introduced. Article 10: If a child worker is sick or injured, the employer "should be responsible for sending the child to a medical institution for treatment, and bear all medical and living expenses during the treatment period." If a child worker is disabled or dies, he or she must be compensated in a lump sum. Article 13 leaves only one exception: literary, artistic and sports units may recruit professional literary and artistic workers and athletes under the age of 16 with the consent of parents or other guardians (national)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2018). Compulsory Education Law (Second Amendment in 2018, Articles 11, 14, and 58). <http://www.moe.gov.cn/jyb_sjzl/sjzl_zcfg/zcfg_jyfl/202110/t20211029_575949.html> (published by the Ministry of Education); State Council (2002). Regulations prohibiting the use of child labor (State Council Order No. 364, Articles 2, 6, 7, 10, and 13). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_61798.htm>

Note: The beneficiary is yourself. It is legal to work after the age of 16. If you want to learn a trade before working part-time, you can go through the dimensions of Article 10 (Skills to Resist Automation) in this section first. The overtime pay, annual leave, and work-related injury benefits discussed in Section 19 all presuppose that there is a labor relationship and evidence. If a child worker is injured, according to Article 10 of the "Regulations on the Prohibition of the Use of Child Labor", the employer shall bear all medical and living expenses during the treatment period, and a lump sum compensation will be required for those who are disabled or dead

Case: A restaurant hired a 15-year-old junior high school graduate as a waiter for only two months. After the labor inspection department found out, it fined the restaurant 5,000 yuan per month in accordance with the law and ordered it to immediately stop using child labor.

items.title: Put "is there any use in studying" into the mortality account: for each additional year of education, the risk of adult death is reduced by about 1.9%
items.core: For each additional year of education, the risk of death in adulthood is reduced by about 1.9% on average. It's most pronounced among those aged 18 to 49, about 2.9% lower for each additional year, and only 0.8% lower for those over 70. People who can keep reading are usually in good condition. How much of this is due to reading itself, I can’t tell.
body: Cost: No money. It takes time and energy to study for several more years. For tuition fees, see Article 4 of this section (Secondary Vocational School Tuition Fees and Grants). The difficulty is to keep reading without giving up in the middle.

Benefit: Find and combine previous studies (systematic review and meta-analysis). The search range was from January 1980 to May 2023, and 603 studies, 70 sites in 59 countries, and 10,355 observations were finally included. Education and adult mortality (deaths from all causes combined) have a dose-response relationship (the more you read, the greater the decrease). Each additional year of education is associated with an average decrease in mortality risk of 1.9% (95% uncertainty interval 1.8–2.0, within which the true value falls roughly). For those aged 18 to 49, the decrease was 2.9% (2.8–3.0) per additional year. Those over 70 years old experienced a decrease of 0.8% (0.6–1.0). No difference was seen between men and women. Looking separately by national development level (socio-demographic index), no difference is seen
Level of evidence: A (controversial)

Source: IHME-CHAIN Collaborators (2024). Effects of education on adult mortality: a global systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet Public Health, 9(3), e155-e165. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-2667(23)00306-7>

Remarks: Controversy. The authors themselves reported publication bias (p<0.0001), meaning that studies with promising results are more likely to be published. Results also varied widely between studies. What is included is follow-up observation, not an experiment done by dividing people into groups. The number of years of schooling is mixed with family conditions, region, and occupation. How much of this 1.9% is caused by reading itself, and how much is due to "people who can keep reading are inherently good", this type of research cannot be separated. The reverse of cause and effect is also inseparable. People who have been sick and have psychological problems as children are more likely to drop out of school and die early. This can make reading seem more useful than it actually is. Therefore, it can effectively prove that "reading more and living longer are in the same direction", but it does not mean that "you can extend your life by 1.9% by studying". The magnitude of the benefit is set as small: readers usually face reading for another three or four years, which adds up to less than 10% at 1.9% per year, which is only small according to the boundaries of the whole book. The beneficiary is you

Case: In the same family, the average annual income of the elders who persisted in finishing high school is nearly 10,000 yuan higher than that of the elders who dropped out of junior high school. They pay more attention to health management in daily life, and the physical examination indicators after the age of 70 are generally better.

items.title: Before judging whether “academic qualifications have been devalued,” first look at the educational structure of the country: only 15,467 people per 100,000 people have a college degree (about 19% according to the 2020 census, and estimated in 2025 sampling)
items.core: At the time of the 2020 census, about 15% of the country had a college degree or above. The 2025 sample survey projects about 19%, a few percentage points more over five years. Both times, the majority of people had a junior high school education. People over the age of 15 have spent an average of 9.91 years in school, just past junior high school. Therefore, junior high school education is the one with the largest number of people in China, and it cannot be said to be scarce.
body: Cost: No money. Just take a look at the numbers below.

Benefits: The standard time point for the seventh national census is November 1, 2020. Among the national population, there are 218,360,767 people with university (college and above) education. There are 213,005,258 people in high schools (including technical secondary schools). Junior high school 487163489 people. Primary school population: 349,658,828. Compared with the sixth census in 2010, the number of people with college education per 100,000 people increased from 8,930 to 15,467. The number of high school students increased from 14,032 to 15,088. The number of junior high schools dropped from 38,788 to 34,507. Primary school enrollment dropped from 26,779 to 24,767. The average years of education for people aged 15 and above increased from 9.08 years to 9.91 years. The illiteracy rate dropped from 4.08% to 2.67%. The standard time point for the 2025 national 1% population sample survey is November 1, 2025, with a sample of 20.52 million people. Based on the sample, the national population is estimated to be 1,405.45 million. Among them, 272.33 million are in university (college and above), 242.72 million are in high school (including technical secondary school), 452.83 million are in junior high school, and 331.22 million are in primary school. The bulletin did not give a figure per 100,000 people. Calculated according to the total population, universities account for about 19.4% and junior high schools account for about 32.2%, which is still the class with the largest population
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National Bureau of Statistics, Office of the Leading Group for the Seventh National Census of the State Council (2021). Bulletin of the Seventh National Census (No. 6) - Population education status. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/tjgb/rkpcgb/qgrkpcgb/202302/t20230206_1902006.html>; National Bureau of Statistics (2026). 2025 National 1% Population Sample Survey Main Data Bulletin. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202605/t20260522_1963788.html>

Note: These numbers only indicate whether academic qualifications are scarce among the population. Whether studying is worthwhile for a specific person should be determined by the method in Article 6 of this section (how to calculate whether studying or working). Also note: the census counts the entire population of the country, including the elderly and children, not the labor force, nor your peers. The bulletin does not give numbers separately by age. From 2010 to 2020, the number of people with a college degree per 100,000 people has increased by more than 70%. The proportion among young people is likely to be higher than the national figure. This is based on the inference. Therefore, comparing national numbers with peers will overestimate one's own advantages. What it can illustrate is: Looking at the national population, college education is still a minority. The numbers in 2025 are estimated by sampling, while the census is based on a full count from house to house. The calibers of the two are different. Therefore, the two sets of numbers are juxtaposed without replacing the old numbers with the new ones. 19.4% and 32.2% are calculated based on the number of people in the gazette and the total population. The beneficiary is you

Case: A company mistakenly believed that a bachelor's degree was common when recruiting. After receiving a large number of resumes, it was discovered that the highest education level of most applicants was junior high school or high school. It eventually adjusted the job's academic requirements to junior college or above.

items.title: If you "can't afford to study", let's do the calculation according to the policy: Tuition fees for public secondary vocational schools have been waived for most rural and needy students, with a stipend of 2,300 yuan, and student loans of up to 20,000 yuan per year
items.core: In public secondary vocational schools, tuition fees have been waived for rural students, urban agriculture-related majors, and students from poor families. Bursaries for secondary vocational schools and regular high schools will be RMB 2,300 per year starting from spring 2025. When I go to college, the scholarship is 3,700 yuan per year, and the maximum student loan I can borrow is 20,000 yuan per year. When you don't have enough money, do the math first and then decide whether to drop out of school and go work.
body: Cost: No money. Before the start of the semester, go to the school's student financial aid management agency to inquire and submit the materials.

Benefits: Tuition exemption for secondary vocational schools is a policy starting from the fall semester of 2012. The original text is "Tuition is exempted for all rural (including county and town) students, urban agriculture-related majors, and students from families with financial difficulties who are in the first, second, and third grade of full-time formal students in public secondary vocational schools (except for students majoring in art-related performance majors)." Adjustments to student financial aid policy for 2024. The national scholarship for undergraduate students is increased from 3,300 yuan per student per year to 3,700 yuan. The National Inspirational Scholarship has been increased from 5,000 yuan to 6,000 yuan. Both are implemented from the fall semester 2024 (inspirational scholarships from 2024). The national scholarships for secondary vocational schools and general high schools will be increased from 2,000 yuan per student per year to 2,300 yuan, starting from the spring semester of 2025. State student loans have also been adjusted, starting in the fall semester 2024. "The annual loan application amount for each undergraduate student will be increased from no more than 16,000 yuan to no more than 20,000 yuan." For graduate students, the scholarship "has been increased from no more than 20,000 yuan to no more than 25,000 yuan." The interest rate is 70 basis points (0.7 percentage points lower) than the market quoted interest rate (LPR) for loans of the same grade during the same period (nationally)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Finance, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2012). Opinions on expanding the scope of tuition-free policy for secondary vocational education and further improving the national scholarship system (Finance Education [2012] No. 376). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2013/content_2332779.htm>; Heads of relevant departments and bureaus of the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, and Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2024). Responding to reporters’ questions on issues related to adjusting student financial aid policies. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202410/content_6983672.htm>; Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, People’s Bank of China, and State Administration of Financial Supervision (2024). Notice on adjusting and improving policies related to national student loans (Caijiao [2024] No. 188). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202411/content_6984812.htm>

Note: The beneficiaries are yourself and your children. The specific number of people covered by the tuition-free program and the different levels of scholarships are determined by each province. Private schools provide subsidies based on local public standards for similar majors. You still have to pay the difference yourself, so you need to check the local documents before enrolling. Student loans are loans, not subsidies, and must be repaid after graduation. But it separates "I can't afford tuition now" and "Is it worthwhile in the next few years" into two different things. Don't conclude that you don't have enough money. Section 7 has written about training subsidies and temporary assistance during the period of unemployment. If your family has really lost their income, apply for those first

Case: A rural secondary vocational student originally considered dropping out of school due to family poverty. After being reminded by the school, he applied for free tuition and a stipend of 2,300 yuan per year. He successfully completed the culinary major and found a stable job in a hotel.

items.title: Failure to pass the general high school does not mean that the road is cut off: secondary vocational schools have comprehensive admissions and separate examinations, and the recruitment of skilled positions in public institutions can also lower academic requirements
items.core: The Vocational Education Law of 2022 states: Vocational education and general education status are equally important. Secondary vocational schools can enroll students in conjunction with higher vocational schools, but higher vocational schools must also set aside enrollment plans or take separate exams to recruit graduates from secondary vocational schools. Employers are also not allowed to set up barriers for you just because you graduated from a vocational school. If your scores are not good enough to get into the general high school, you need to find another path, not stop at junior high school.
body: Cost: No money. Before filling out your application for the high school entrance examination, check the province’s vocational education enrollment platform.

Benefits: Article 3 of the "Vocational Education Law" (effective from May 1, 2022): "Vocational education is a type of education that has the same important status as general education." Article 37: Secondary vocational schools “may, in accordance with relevant national regulations, implement integrated enrollment and training in relevant majors with higher vocational school education.” Higher vocational schools "may recruit students in accordance with relevant national regulations and adopt an assessment method that combines cultural quality and vocational skills." Educational administrative departments at or above the provincial level should establish a unified enrollment platform for vocational education, summarize and publish school, major settings and enrollment status, and provide inquiry and application services. Article 53: "Vocational school students enjoy equal opportunities with ordinary school students of the same level in terms of further education, employment, career development, etc." Higher vocational schools and ordinary colleges and universities that implement vocational education "should determine corresponding proportions in the enrollment plan or adopt separate examination methods to specifically recruit vocational school graduates." "Employers shall not set application, recruitment, and employment conditions that hinder equal employment and fair competition for vocational school graduates." Positions with vocational skill level requirements in public recruitment "can appropriately reduce academic requirements" (National)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (2022). Vocational Education Law (revised in 2022, Articles 3, 37, and 53). <http://www.moe.gov.cn/jyb_sjzl/sjzl_zcfg/zcfg_jyfl/202204/t20220421_620064.html> (published by the Ministry of Education)

Remarks: The beneficiaries are yourself and your children. These are legal channels, not guaranteed admission. Which majors are included in the comprehensive training, the proportion of independent enrollment and retention, and which subjects are tested in the vocational education college entrance examination are all determined by each province. Before applying, you must check the province's vocational education enrollment platform and enrollment plan for that year, and do not rely on the experience of other provinces. When choosing a secondary vocational major, use the dimensions of item 10 in this section (skills to resist automation): Majors that require on-site visits and non-standard environments are more likely to be rejected. When choosing a school, it depends on whether it is included in the province's vocational education enrollment plan for that year. The certificate issued by it should be verified according to the three steps in Article 8 (check whether the certificate is in the directory). Do not accept those who promise "guaranteed distribution" and "guarantee" in the admissions promotion

Case: Students whose scores in the high school entrance examination did not reach the upper limit entered the CNC major of a secondary vocational school and were promoted to higher vocational schools through "3+2" comprehensive training. After graduation, they successfully applied for technical positions in public institutions with their skill certificates.

items.title: Think of "study or work" as a question: go to work first and earn three years' salary early, versus the difference in annual income in the following decades if you go to school
items.core: If you go to work first, you can earn several years' salary earlier, but this money is only taken once. If you continue to study, you will earn more every year than those who did not study, and you will continue to earn more for thirty or forty years. So we need to compare these two amounts of money together. For an extra year of schooling in urban China, one year's income is about 4.0% to 10.2% higher, but this is a figure before 2001, so we can only give a general idea.
body: Cost: No money. Sit down and count once, about half an hour.

Earnings: This is an estimate for Chinese cities and towns from 1988 to 2001. How much more income can be gained by studying for one more year is called the rate of return on education. The original article reads, “The rate for each year of education increased sharply from 4.0% in 1988 to 10.2% in 2001.” The increase occurred mainly after 1992. What it reflects is that the proportion of people who go to college earn more than those who don’t go to college (the higher education wage premium) is getting bigger. This is the local Chinese magnitude that can be used when converting "one more year of study" into the annual income difference. For global averages, see Item 7 of this section (global average returns to an additional year of education)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Zhang J, Zhao Y, Park A, Song X (2005). Economic returns to schooling in urban China, 1988 to 2001. Journal of Comparative Economics, 33(4), 730-752. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jce.2005.05.008>

Note: Before calculation, first deduct the free tuition and bursaries in Article 4 of this section (secondary vocational tuition and bursaries), as well as the account in Article 2 of this section (an extra year of education and mortality). The data, as of 2001, only covers cities and towns and cannot be directly used as today's data. The same goes for the global average of 9% in Item 7 of this section. What is given here is an algorithm, not an answer: if you really calculate it according to this method, the conclusion will vary from person to person. If the tuition is high, the major and position are not suitable, and the years of study are long, it may not be cost-effective. But that only means that this specific project is not cost-effective, and it does not mean that reading is useless. There are still a few things that don’t fit into the formula, but they do exist. See Article 5 of this section for the statutory academic qualifications threshold (through-entry admissions and separate examinations for secondary vocational schools), see Article 10 for resistance to substitution (skills that challenge automation), and whether you can change industries. The beneficiary is yourself

Case: Two junior high school classmates, one went directly to work in a factory with a monthly income of 4,000 yuan, and the other joined a technical position after completing higher vocational education and earned 9,000 yuan a month. Three years later, the former’s salary has basically not increased, while the latter’s income continues to grow

items.title: Remember the baseline first: with one more year of education, the global average private return (the part that falls on one’s own income) is about 9% per year
items.core: According to the global average, if you study for one more year, your personal income will be about 9% higher per year, and women's returns have always been higher than men. This number refers to formal schooling and cannot be applied directly to enrolling in a class. Use it as a yardstick: a course costs you 30,000 yuan and half a year. Just ask whether the change in income it brings is worth an extra year of studying.
body: Cost: Nothing. Memorize this number and use it as a yardstick to measure various "learn something" plans.

Gains: A review of 1,120 estimates covering 139 countries from 1950 to 2014 calculated that “the global average private return to an extra year of education was 9% per year.” The private return is the part that falls on one’s own income: studying for one more year increases income by about 9% on average. Private returns to higher education are rising. The social return to education (the part that falls on society as a whole rather than on the individual) remains high. The average return to education for women continues to be higher than for men
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Psacharopoulos G, Patrinos HA (2018). Returns to investment in education: a decennial review of the global literature. Education Economics, 26(5), 445-458. <https://doi.org/10.1080/09645292.2018.1484426>; World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 8402. <https://doi.org/10.1596/1813-9450-8402>

Note: This is the global average of "one more year of study". It cannot be regarded as the benefit of "enrolling in a class". It is not a specific figure for China. It can only be used as a reference. Its purpose is to give all training programs a yardstick. If a course costs you 30,000 yuan and half a year, you should ask whether it can bring about an income change equivalent to one year of formal education. Note also that global averages mask huge professional and country differences

Case: A worker The factory technician spent half a year and 30,000 yuan to participate in automation training. After graduation, his monthly salary increased from 6,000 yuan to 8,500 yuan. The cost was recovered in less than a year, which is far better than his colleagues who did not participate in the training during the same period

items.title: Before spending money to get a certificate, first check whether the certificate is in the National Vocational Qualification Catalog or the list of evaluation institutions registered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security.
items.core: The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security has specifically dealt with some institutions that run random classes, charge arbitrary fees, issue certificates indiscriminately, and pretend to be authoritative institutions in the name of new occupations and skill levels. Before signing up, follow the three-step check: whether this occupation is in the national vocational qualification catalog, whether the issuing agency is an evaluation agency registered with the human resources and social security department, and whether the certificate number can be found on the official platform. If you can't find it, don't report it.
body: Cost: Nothing. Check once, ten minutes.

Benefits: The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security has carried out nationwide governance specifically for this purpose. The chaos named in the document is that "some institutions and units randomly organize training, evaluation, and certification activities in the name of new professional qualifications, vocational skill levels, etc., charge arbitrary fees, and issue certificates indiscriminately; some institutions and units make false or exaggerated publicity, and even organize training, evaluation, and certificate issuance in the name of fake authoritative organizations." Governance measures include joint investigations with cybersecurity, public security, market supervision and other departments to "severely crack down on the evaluation and certification activities of counterfeit appraisal agencies and evaluation agencies registered with the human resources and social security departments." Illegal publicity on websites and new media will be shut down in accordance with the law. The document also requires "guiding the public to understand the channels and methods of certificate inquiry, and to judge the legality, compliance and value of the certificate."
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2022). Notice on carrying out special management of "copycat certificates" in technical skills. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-03/18/content_5679641.htm>

Note: Check in this order. First check whether the occupation is in the "National Vocational Qualification Catalog". If it is not in the catalog, it is not a national professional qualification. Then look at whether the issuing agency is an evaluation agency registered with the human resources and social security department. Finally, go to the official Skilled Talent Evaluation Certificate Inquiry Platform to check whether the certificate number can be found. Those that cannot be found will not be reported. Those with the words "international", "advanced" and "registered" and promises of "guaranteed" and "affiliation with income" have the highest risk. For "academic improvement classes" where you spend money to buy academic qualifications, see Section 31, Article 10 (only academic qualifications can be found on Xuexin.com).

Case: Someone spent 12,000 yuan to sign up " "International Registered Nutritionist" training class, but later found that the certificate was not in the national professional qualification catalog, and the issuing agency had not been registered by the human resources and social security department, so it could not be used for job hunting

items.title: For training, give priority to government subsidy channels. Don’t sign up for business classes at your own expense as soon as you start.
items.core: From 2025 to the end of 2027, the state plans to provide subsidized training for more than 30 million people. Money comes from employment subsidy funds, unemployment insurance funds, enterprise employee education funds, etc. Which type of job is in short supply and has higher training costs, the higher the subsidy will be. Those who are employed first ask their employer, while others first look through the subsidy catalog of the local social security bureau before deciding what to study.
body: Cost: No money, or it can be significantly reduced. The training itself takes time. The hard thing is to resist the impulse and sign up for classes at your own expense. Check the subsidy catalog first.

Benefits: The scale at the national level is clear: from 2025 to the end of 2027, "more than 30 million people will receive subsidized training focusing on high-precision industries, urgently needed industries, key employment groups, etc." Funding sources have been unified into a package: employment subsidy funds, unemployment insurance funds, industry development funds, east-west cooperation funds, enterprise employee education funds, etc. The level of the subsidy is determined according to the urgent need of the occupation (type of work) and the cost of training. Different types of work are different. Enterprises are also required to "withdraw and use employee education funds in full in accordance with regulations to ensure that more than 60% is used for front-line employee education and training."
Level of Evidence: A

Source: State Council Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection (2025). Guidance on carrying out large-scale vocational skills improvement training actions. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222.htm>

Note: How to receive it and how much you can receive are determined by each province. The entrance is the "Vocational Training Subsidy Catalog" and the public training base on the official website of the local Social Security Bureau. Section 7 writes about vocational training subsidies (the same person can enjoy up to three times) and social security subsidies during unemployment. Those who are employed will first ask about the unit’s employee education funds. It is much cheaper to check the subsidy catalog first and then choose what to study than to make a good choice first and then look for subsidies.

Case: After an unemployed young man checked the subsidy directory of the local Social Security Bureau, he participated in the government-subsidized electrician training for free and obtained the certificate. Three months later, he successfully joined a property company with a monthly income of 4,500 yuan

items.title: When choosing skills, give priority to "whether you need to do it, whether you need to judge on the spot". These types of skills are the most difficult to be eliminated by automation.
items.core: According to U.S. estimates, about 47% of jobs are at high risk of being taken over by computers, and later estimates based on specific tasks are much lower. There are three obstacles for machines: manual dexterity, coming up with new things, and dealing with people. Therefore, jobs that require on-site work, non-standard environment, and on-the-spot judgment are more difficult to be dismissed. Positions with fixed processes and mainly processing information are at the highest risk.
body: Cost: Nothing. Before choosing, live through what you want to learn based on this dimension.

Benefits: Estimate "how likely it is that this job can be left to a computer" (computable probability assessment) for 702 occupations in the United States. The result is that about 47% of jobs are in the high-risk range. What determines the level of risk in the model are three hurdles that the machine cannot currently overcome. The author calls them "engineering bottlenecks." The first is perception and operation, including finger dexterity, hand dexterity, and working in narrow spaces and awkward postures. The second is creative intelligence (the ability to come up with new things). The third is social intelligence (the ability to deal with people). Therefore, the probability of being replaced is always lower for jobs that have non-standard environments and require hard work and on-the-spot judgment. This is not an accident of individual professions. Jobs with fixed processes and focused on information processing are at the highest risk
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Frey CB, Osborne MA (2017). The future of employment: how susceptible are jobs to computerisation? Technological Forecasting and Social Change, 114, 254-280. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.techfore.2016.08.019>

Remarks: Controversy. This study is an unpublished paper in 2013. The score is "whether the entire profession can be taken over by machines." Later, some research changed to breaking down the estimates into specific tasks, and the calculated high-risk ratio was much lower. It also doesn't say in what year this will happen. When using it, don't focus on the 47% number, but look at the three places where the machine is stuck. This is why on-site installation, maintenance, and maintenance tasks are more resistant to substitution than pure paperwork. Therefore, when "learning a skill", priority should be given to those who need to go to the scene and face non-standard environments

Case: Wang Qiang, who graduated from a technical secondary school, did not choose the position of assembly line quality inspector, but learned industrial robot debugging. He is stationed in the workshop of the automobile factory and needs to judge the deviation of the robotic arm on site and calibrate it manually. Due to the non-standard environment and reliance on manual experience, his position has not been replaced by automation, and his current monthly salary exceeds 10,000 yuan.

items.title: Before learning, make sure whether the skill has a grade evaluation and whether the grade can be converted into money
items.core: The country is promoting the "New Eighth Level Workers", requiring companies to link job wages and skill levels. Employees with outstanding performance can also directly determine the grade without looking at seniority and seniority. This is the policy direction, and it varies greatly among local companies. There are national occupational standards and grade-level skills. Only in the future can we talk about salary increases according to grade. Check whether they are available before learning.
body: Cost: No money. Just check it once.

Benefits: The country is promoting the "New Eighth Level Workers" vocational skill grading system. The document clearly calls for linking grade and salary. The original words are to "strengthen the skills-oriented salary distribution system... guide enterprises to implement a distribution method that double-links job salary with job value and skill level." All localities should "increase the intensity and batch selection of senior workers and above". Qualified companies can evaluate the skill levels of their employees themselves. For employees with outstanding performance, "the conditions such as working years, grades, qualifications, etc. can be broken and the corresponding occupational skill level can be directly determined."
Level of Evidence: B

Source: State Council Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection (2025). Guidance on carrying out large-scale occupational skills improvement training actions. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222.htm>; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2021). "Skills China Action" Implementation Plan. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-07/06/content_5622619.htm>

Note: This is the policy direction, not the number of wages that have been realized. The implementation level of enterprises in different regions varies greatly.
