Earnings: All people born between 1968 and 2008 in Denmark and 1973 and 2006 in Sweden are included. Add to this the 89.3% of those born in Finland between 1987 and 2007. A total of more than 7.3 million people. Of these, 189,094 lost a parent before the age of 18. The mortality rate of this group of children from all causes combined was 50% higher than that of those who were not bereaved (mortality ratio 1.50, 95% CI 1.43–1.58, or about 1.5 times). The proportion of parents who died of unnatural causes such as accidents and suicides was 1.84 (1.71–2.00), which is about 80% higher. Deaths from natural causes such as disease were 1.33 (1.24–1.41), about 30% higher. It is highest when the child's cause of death falls into the same category as the parent's cause of death. The American Academy of Pediatrics' 2016 clinical report to pediatricians requires that when talking to bereaved children, clarify what happened and what it means, and correct misinformation and misunderstandings that children have heard. The report also provides recommendations on how to support children in attending funerals and other farewell ceremonies
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Li J, et al. (2014). Mortality after parental death in childhood: a nationwide cohort study from three Nordic countries. PLoS Medicine. Council (2016). Supporting the Grieving Child and Family. Pediatrics, 138(3), e20162147. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2016-2147>

Note: Don’t make up “traveling away” when telling your children, custody and support arrangements must be written down. No direct research or original guide has been found on whether to transfer schools or live elsewhere. The author's opinion is that it is better for children to have less changes in their lives. Giving B is not because the numbers are not hard. This is a tracking study of the entire population of three countries, and the numbers themselves are A-level. The reason for giving B is because there is no direct experimental evidence between this number and the specific methods of "how to tell the child and whether to attend the farewell". The authors also note that there is a lack of data on parent-child relationships and children's lifestyle after bereavement. Gao Li has both an innate physical component and the long-term effects of bereavement. Appointment of guardians and arrangements for property are provided in Section 17. See Section 18 for child support and schooling.

Case: The father of a 9-year-old boy died in a car accident. His mother did not hide it from him. She told him the story in words he could understand. She took him to choose a guitar that his father liked and put it in the coffin, and asked him to say goodbye only when he wanted to talk. Half a year later, the child was able to go to school normally without persistent nightmares or withdrawal.

items.title: If the grief is still there after half a year and you can't live anymore, go to a psychiatrist or clinical psychology department to register
items.core: About one in ten bereaved adults will be stuck. I have been thinking about it for more than half a year to the point where I can't eat, go to work, or take care of my children. I feel numb and feel that life is meaningless. It’s not that you’re not strong enough. It has diagnostic criteria and specialized treatments. Targeted treatment is 51% effective, compared with 28% for general psychotherapy, and it works faster.
body: Cost: Registration fee plus treatment fee. This type of treatment is done in sessions, with an average of 16 sessions over 19 weeks in the trial. The difficulty lies in taking the step to register this number yourself.

Benefit: 14 studies combined, looking at adults who had loved ones who had not died of violence and were not in psychiatric care themselves. The prevalence of prolonged grief disorders was 9.8% (95% CI 6.8–14.0), or approximately 10 per 100 bereaved adults. The older you are, the higher the proportion is. Another study tested the accuracy of this set of diagnostic criteria. 291 bereaved people were interviewed three times, 0–6, 6–12, and 12–24 months after bereavement. The core manifestation of the diagnosis is the intense longing for the deceased. Add at least five of these nine items. The top five are emotional numbness, shock, feeling that life has no meaning, distrust of others, and pain from the loss. The last four are difficulty accepting, not being able to recognize who one is, avoiding reality, and being unable to continue living. These symptoms must occur every day, or be so severe that they cannot do anything. And it persists at least 6 months after the death of a loved one, affecting daily life. There was also a trial in which 95 people were divided into two groups, doing 16 treatments for an average of 19 weeks. Treatment for complicated grief is 51% effective. Ordinary interpersonal psychotherapy 28% (P=0.02, difference unlikely to be due to chance). The former also works faster. Number needed to treat 4.3, that is, one more person gets better for every 4.3 treated
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Lundorff M, et al. (2017). Prevalence of prolonged grief disorder in adult bereavement: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Affective Disorders. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jad.2017.01.030>; Prigerson HG, et al. (2009). Prolonged grief disorder: Psychometric validation of criteria proposed for DSM-V and ICD-11. PLoS Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1000121>; Shear MK, et al. (2005). Treatment of complicated grief: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.293.21.2601>

Note: Don’t get stuck on the month. The real judgment is "it affects eating, sleeping, going to work, and taking care of children." If you are right, go and register. Departments are called psychiatry, psychology or clinical psychology, and they are available in public psychiatric hospitals. This diagnosis is called complicated grief or prolonged grief disorder in different sources. Different standards require different durations, some write 6 months, some write 12 months. This proportion of 9.8% comes from 14 studies with considerable differences in practices. The author also reminds that it may not be transferable to other groups of people.

Case: 8 months after the death of his wife, Mr. Wang still eats in front of the portrait every day, is unable to go to work, and has lost ten pounds. I went to a psychiatrist to be diagnosed with prolonged grief disorder, and received targeted treatment for 12 weeks. I was able to pick up and drop off my children again, resume work, and self-assessed that "I can think of her but not be held back."

items.title: Don’t spend money on grief counseling as soon as you get started, first check whether your grief is really stuck (the symptoms in No. 8)
items.core: Arrange psychological counseling for all bereaved people. The benefits are very small and will not be seen after a while, because most people will recover on their own. But for people who are clearly unable to adapt, treatment is as effective as treating other psychological problems. So first check Article 8 (Go to a psychiatrist if you are stuck in grief), and then spend the money if you are right.
body: Cost: No money, in turn save a consulting fee.

Benefits: 61 controlled studies combined. Psychological intervention is commonly used for bereaved people. The benefits are very small immediately after the treatment, and no benefits can be seen after a while. Interventions that only recruit bereaved people who are "clearly unable to adapt" are as effective as psychotherapy for other psychological problems. The results of studies without screening beforehand were not good because the group without intervention would have recovered over time. Another 14 lottery group trials were taken together: the treatment for people who already had problems was significantly better than the control after treatment and during follow-up visits, and the effect continued to grow after a period of time. Common preventive interventions for people who don't have problems yet are ineffective. Another study followed 205 people from before they were widowed to 6 or 18 months after they were widowed. This research breaks out into five directions. They are ordinary grief, chronic grief, chronic depression, getting better during bereavement, and resilience (bearing it). Among them, the resilient type is the most common, and the ordinary sad type is relatively rare.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Currier JM, et al. (2008). The effectiveness of psychotherapeutic interventions for bereaved persons: a comprehensive quantitative review. Psychological Bulletin. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.134.5.648>; Wittouck C, et al. (2011). <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpr.2010.09.005>; Bonanno GA, et al. (2002). Resilience to loss and chronic grief: a prospective study from preloss to 18-months postloss. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.83.5.1150>; Stroebe M et al (2007). Health outcomes of bereavement. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(07)61816-9> (review in the notes)

Note: What I say here is “not everyone has to do it”, not “don’t do it all”. High-risk bereavements of the type in Item 4 (where a loved one dies by suicide, accident, or homicide) are exactly what the evidence supports. No. 8 (Grief stuck, go to psychiatry) The same goes for people who are stuck. A Lancet review concluded similarly: Grief is not a disease and most people do not need professional intervention. We should focus our efforts on those at high risk. It is also used in people who are already experiencing complicated grief, post-bereavement depression and stress disorders.

Case: Ms. Zhao lost her mother two months ago, and her relatives recommended spending 8,000 yuan for grief counseling. She compared symptom No. 8 and found that she only shed tears occasionally, could go to work and take care of the baby, and was not stuck, so she did not spend the money. Four months later, she slowly recovered and saved money for her father's physical examination.

items.title: After separation and divorce, don’t cut off medical insurance and don’t use alcohol to support it.
items.core: People who were separated or divorced were significantly more likely to die early than those who were still married, with men and those who were younger being more likely to die early. This is not necessarily caused by divorce. Divorced people may have different health and income. There are two things you can control yourself: don't let your medical insurance cut off, and don't rely on tobacco and alcohol to support you.
body: Cost: Nothing. Renew your medical insurance and stop drinking. The difficulty is that it is easy to rely on alcohol during this period.

Benefits: 32 enrollment-then-follow-up studies combined, covering more than 6.5 million people, 160,000 deaths, more than 755,000 divorces, and 11 countries. Adults who are separated or divorced have a significantly higher risk of early death compared with those who are still married. Men and younger people rise more significantly than women and older people. The authors discuss four possible paths. The first is social selection. People with different health or conditions are more likely to get divorced. The second is that resources are interrupted, and income and security are cut off. The third is changes in health behaviors, and worsening of smoking and drinking habits. The fourth is chronic psychological stress (long-term tension)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Sbarra DA, et al. (2011). Divorce and Death: A Meta-Analysis and Research Agenda for Clinical, Social, and Health Psychology. Perspectives on Psychological Science. <https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691611414724>

Note: The original article only talked about "significant increase" and group comparison, but did not give a multiple that could be quoted, so I will not write specific numbers here. The magnitude of the income is determined as medium based on "the direction is known and there is no threshold drop that can be set". Property, debts and dowry upon divorce are discussed in Sections 8 and 10. Child support arrangements are provided in Section 10, Article 23 (the divorce agreement spells out support and visitation).

Case: After Mr. Chen agreed to divorce, he went to the Social Security Bureau to switch his medical insurance from work to flexible employment and renew it without stopping payment; when he was upset, he went for a run instead of drinking. Three months later, he was hospitalized for a cold and was reimbursed 70% of the time. During the same period, his divorced colleague paid more than 20,000 out-of-pocket due to the termination of insurance, and was also found to have worsened fatty liver disease.

items.title: If you need someone to talk to you, call 12356. For minors and teenagers, call 12355. If you need to see a doctor, call the psychological clinic.
items.core: If you want to talk to someone, call 12356, the national psychological assistance hotline, which is free. There is also a 12355 Youth Comprehensive Service Platform for minors and teenagers. If you want to see a doctor, go to the psychological clinic of a psychiatry department, a psychology department, or a clinical psychology department. When encountering family changes, unemployment, or schooling, community grid workers and social workers should take the initiative to find out.
body: Cost: Nothing. Both hotlines are free. The psychological outpatient clinic is registered as a general outpatient clinic.

Benefits: The 2026 plan of the National Health Commission and 25 other departments requires the improvement of the 12356 psychological assistance hotline working system. It is necessary to ensure stable operation and improve the connection rate. It is necessary to promote the establishment of a provincial 12356 information platform. It is necessary to strengthen the construction of linkage mechanisms with service hotlines such as 110. It is also necessary to build and make good use of the 12355 Youth Comprehensive Service Platform, and to collaborate with 12356. There are three goals by 2030. First, more than 80% of administrative villages and urban communities have psychological consultation rooms or social studios and provide psychological services. Second, public psychiatric hospitals at all levels and at least one hospital in each county (district) provide psychological outpatient services. Third, each province has established a provincial-level 12356 psychological assistance platform. The psychological crisis intervention and psychological assistance team is composed of psychiatrists, psychotherapy technicians, psychological counselors, social work professionals and volunteers. The plan also requires the three types of people to pay attention to it and detect it early. These three types of people are grid workers (staff responsible for each area in the community), social work professionals and volunteers. They must promptly detect risks of psychological crises such as family changes, unemployment, and school dropout (National, issued in March 2026)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National Health Commission and 25 other departments (2026). Notice on the issuance of the implementation plan for improving the psychosocial service system and crisis intervention mechanism (National Health Medical Administration [2026] No. 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065035.htm>

Note: The reason for B is that village and community consultation rooms and county-level psychological clinics are only to be built in 2030 and are not available everywhere now. 12356 and 12355 can be played now. Please refer to Section 1, Article 25 for the opening hours of 12356 and the number of hours it is available each day. Counseling and psychotherapy are not the same thing. Diagnosis and medication must be made by psychiatrists, and treatment must be done in qualified medical institutions. The "healing" and "spiritual consultation" that charge by the hour on the market are not included in this system.

Case: Xiao Zhou had insomnia all night after losing his job. He dialed 12356 late at night and talked for 20 minutes. The hotline taught him breathing techniques and made an appointment with a community social worker to visit the next day. His 14-year-old cousin was isolated by his classmates. He called 12355 and was continuously followed. Both of them later returned to school and stabilized with the help of the school psychologist.

items.title: In the first three months after the accident, all irreversible decisions will be postponed.
items.core: During this period, you have the worst judgment of various "opportunities". In the experiment, sad people were willing to take between 10% and 30% less money in order to wait for three months. If the amount exceeds one month's income, or if it is costly to regret, it will be postponed for three months. Tell it to someone who has no interest in the matter first, and don't make a decision on the same day.
body: Cost: No money spent, just pushing the decision back and possibly missing some opportunities. The difficulty is that at the time, I felt like opportunities were waiting for no one.

Benefits: Avoid making property dispositions that you cannot regret during the period when you have just been hit and your judgment is at your worst. Such things include selling your house, resigning, investing your pension or compensation money in one lump sum, hastily remarrying, and guarantoring for others. The amount of such decisions is usually in the order of tens of thousands of yuan to a house, so the income is set as medium. Official documents also list "family changes, unemployment, and dropout from school" as psychological crisis risks that the community must proactively investigate. The situation during this period is originally regarded as a situation that requires outsiders' help. The National Institute on Aging's (NIA) grief guidelines list "difficulty making decisions" as a common symptom of grief. It advises: If you have the choice, postpone major life decisions until you feel better. When you are sad and may not be able to think clearly, it is best not to make big changes such as selling your house or resigning. One study conducted three experiments. The researchers randomly divided people into groups, put some people into a sad state, and then asked them to choose "get the money now" or "get the money in 3 months." Compared to calm people, sad people were willing to take 13% to 34% less money to wait 3 months. This is sadness caused by the experiment, not real bereavement. The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) warned of a scam in 2023: someone pretended to be a funeral home and told the family that the funeral would be canceled if they did not make up the money immediately. The first method it gives is to withstand the pressure of "do it right away". A serious business will give you time to make a decision.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National Health Commission and other 25 departments (2026). Implementation plan for improving the psychosocial service system and crisis intervention mechanism (National Health and Medical Administration [2026] No. 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065035.htm>; National Institute on Aging. possible" paragraph, page updated 2026-01-26). <https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/grief-and-mourning/coping-grief-and-loss>; Lerner JS, Li Y, Weber EU (2013). The financial costs of sadness. Psychological Science, 24(1), 72-79. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797612450302>; Puig A, Federal Trade Commission (2023-06-15). Imposters prey on families preparing for the funeral of a loved one. <https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/06/imposters-prey-families-preparing-funeral-loved-one>

Note: If you don’t have such an uninterested person around you, just call 12356 and tell the story (see No. 11 of this section, call 12356 if you want someone to talk with you). You can also write it down yourself and read it again every three days. It's graded B because "Push Back" is supported by official grief guidelines and a randomized experiment. However, no studies have directly compared the financial outcomes of bereaved individuals who defer versus those who do not. NIA also only said "wait until you feel better" and did not give a time period. "Three months" and "more than one month's income" are the lines drawn by the author himself. Common scams targeting the bereaved and elderly are found in Section 17 (Investment for retirement, housing for retirement) and Section 6 (Fortune telling). The pitfalls of guarantees and IOUs are found in Section 8. There are several amounts of money that need to be dealt with proactively and are not included in the "postponement" list: provident fund balance, social security benefits, and work-related death payments. See Sections 25 and 19.

Case: More than a month after Ms. Liu’s husband passed away, someone advised her to sell her home at a low price to “save her money.” According to the rules, she postponed it for three months and told her cousin who was a doctor first. Three months later, house prices rebounded, so she kept the house and later rented it out for an extra 2,000 yuan a month. She had no regrets.

items.title: Don't use death as a way to pay off debts: life insurance will not pay out within two years, and work-related injuries will not be recognized. Debts will still be deducted from the inheritance first
items.core: Life insurance contracts will not pay out if you commit suicide within two years, and only the money that can be refunded in the policy will be refunded. They didn't acknowledge the work-related injuries, and they didn't get a cent of the three payments for work-related injuries. The debt you owe will be deducted from your inheritance first, and your family will only get the rest. Your spouse who borrowed the debt jointly will still have to pay it back. They also bear the health costs mentioned in Article 4 of this section (Bereavement due to suicide or violent death).
body: Cost: No money, just settle the account.

Income: Article 44 of the Insurance Law governs contracts in which the death of the insured is the condition for payment of insurance benefits. If the insured commits suicide within two years from the date when the contract is established or the validity of the contract is restored, the insurer shall not be liable for payment of insurance benefits. If the insurance company does not pay compensation according to this article, it must refund the cash value of the insurance policy as stipulated in the contract, that is, it will only refund the money that can be refunded in the policy without paying the insured amount. If the insured person is a person without civil capacity when he commits suicide, that is, a person who is legally unable to be responsible for his own actions, this exemption does not apply. The insured amount of life insurance is usually in the hundreds of thousands of yuan, so the income is determined to be large. Paragraph 3 of Article 16 of the Work Injury Insurance Regulations stipulates: Self-injury or suicide shall not be recognized as a work-related injury or treated as a work-related injury. Article 39 The three work-related death benefits were all in vain. The first is the funeral subsidy, which is paid for 6 months based on the average monthly salary of local employees in the previous year. The second is supporting relatives’ pensions. The third is a one-time work-related death benefit, which is 20 times the per capita disposable income of urban residents nationwide in the previous year. Article 1159 of the Civil Code stipulates: When dividing an estate, the taxes and debts that the deceased should pay in accordance with the law must be paid off, that is, the estate must be used to repay taxes and debts first, and then the rest can be divided. Article 1161 stipulates that the heir shall pay off the inheritance within the actual value of the inheritance, that is, he will only pay back the part he inherited and does not need to pay any more himself. Those who give up the inheritance will not be liable for repayment. Spouses should also read Article 1064 of the Civil Code: "Debts borne by a joint signature of both spouses or by one spouse's subsequent ratification, as well as debts borne by one spouse in his or her own name for the daily needs of the family during the marriage, are joint debts of the spouses." If the two people signed the loan together and borrowed it for the daily expenses of the family, the spouse himself is the debtor and cannot avoid giving up the inheritance
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (2015 revision). Article 44 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4060811>; State Council (Revised in 2010). Articles 16 and 39 of the Regulations on Work-related Injury Insurance (State Council Order No. 586). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm>; National People’s Congress (2020). Articles 1159 and 1161 of the Civil Code of the People’s Republic of China. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>; National People's Congress (2020). Article 1064 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>

Note: Only money is calculated here. This section and the other items in Section 1 say don't go this far. Article 44 of the Insurance Law only governs the first two years. It is written to explain all the provisions, not to provide a timetable. The health costs of family members are shown in Article 4 of this section (those whose spouses die by suicide have a 70% to 80% higher risk of developing new mental disorders within 5 years). See Section 1, Items 25 and 32 for what to do when thoughts arise, and see Section 1, Item 33 for the sequelae after being rescued. The standards for three amounts of money due to work-related deaths are set out in Section 19, Article 15. How to deal with inheritance and debts is shown in Section 25, Article 11 (the heirs only use the inherited inheritance to repay). For the money you should withdraw, please refer to Section 25, Article 9 (to withdraw provident fund and social security benefits one by one)

Case: Lao Zhou owed 300,000 yuan, so he bought a 200,000 yuan life insurance policy and wanted to walk away. He didn’t know that compensation would not be paid for suicide within two years, work-related injuries would not be recognized, and debts would have to be deducted from the inheritance first. Fortunately, my family stopped me, and I later restructured my debt and slowly paid it off, saving my insurance policy and the only home in my family.

items.title: After you have experienced a car accident, being beaten, or a disaster, don’t expect a one-time psychological interview immediately after the accident; if nightmares, flashbacks, and fear are still severe after a month, go to a psychiatric department for trauma-focused psychotherapy
items.core: After a serious incident, it is common to have nightmares and be easily frightened in the first few weeks, and most people will recover on their own. It's still severe after a month, and it may be post-traumatic stress disorder. Psychotherapy specifically targeting trauma has obvious effects. Immediately after the incident, you ask someone to tell you what happened. This kind of one-time interview cannot prevent this disease. In one experiment, people who did it were worse off three years later.
body: Cost: registration fee plus treatment fee, usually 8 to 12 times. The difficulty lies in the fact that therapy involves going back to the experience that you are most afraid of remembering.

Benefits: The National Health Commission's "Standards for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Mental Disorders (2020 Edition)" states that on average, about 8% of people who experience mental trauma will develop post-traumatic stress disorder. There are three categories of core performance. One is nightmares, flashbacks, and scenes of accidents popping up repeatedly. The second is to avoid touching topics, places and people related to this matter. Third, he is always alert, easily frightened, and suffers from insomnia. This diagnosis is made only when symptoms last for more than 1 month and seriously affect family, study, or work. The norm is written in the section on acute stress disorder. Most people return to normal after self-adjustment or acute crisis intervention. For treatment effects, please see a summary in 2020. There were a total of 114 trials divided into lottery groups and 8171 people. Trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy versus waiting list or usual care, SMD −1.32 (95% CI −1.57 to −1.08, confidence range), moderate-quality evidence. Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) was −1.23 (−1.69 to −0.76), low quality evidence. SMD and d are the same ruler, anything above 0.8 is considered large, and both are above this line. For ordinary supportive counseling and waiting ratios, no difference was seen (−0.43, −0.90 to 0.04). A 2013 Cochrane review by the same authors had 70 trials, 4761 participants, and was in the same direction. It was −1.62 (−2.03 to −1.21) for trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy and −1.17 (−2.04 to −0.30) for EMDR. But the quality of the evidence in that review was very low. This is how the UK NICE 2018 guidance is organized. Individual trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy is provided for adults with severe symptoms within one month of their accident. If the diagnosis is confirmed or the symptoms are obvious after one month, the same treatment is provided, usually 8 to 12 times. For trauma that is not caused by war and has not healed after 3 months, EMDR is also provided. If the symptoms are mild and not enough for diagnosis, the patient should be observed in the first month and make an appointment for a follow-up examination within one month. The following types of psychotherapy are listed in domestic norms: extended exposure, cognitive processing therapy and EMDR. A one-time interview immediately after the accident, looking at three pieces of information. A 2002 Cochrane review of 11 trials found that single individual interviews did not reduce suffering or prevent post-traumatic stress disorder. There was no difference at 3 to 5 months with an odds ratio OR 1.22 (0.60–2.46). One of the trials followed up 1 year, and those who had been interviewed were more likely to develop the disease, with an odds ratio of 2.88 (1.11–7.53). The authors conclude that interviews should no longer be forced on traumatized people. Another trial looked at patients who were hospitalized after car accidents and were randomly divided into groups. After 3 years, the interview group had significantly worse psychiatric symptoms, anxiety while riding in a car, pain, physical problems, overall functioning, and financial problems. People who had severe flashbacks and avoidance at the beginning still had symptoms 3 years later after being interviewed, while those who did not have recovered. NICE guidance states clearly not to provide psychologically focused interviews for the prevention or treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder. The reason is that no benefits have been seen from doing it individually or collectively, and there are signs of worse effects than not doing it
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Lewis C, et al. (2020). Psychological therapies for post-traumatic stress disorder in adults: systematic review and meta-analysis. European Journal of Psychotraumatology. <https://doi.org/10.1080/20008198.2020.1729633>; Bisson JI, et al. (2013). Psychological therapies for chronic post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in adults. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, CD003388. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD003388.pub4>; Rose S, et al. (2002). Systematic Reviews, CD000560. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000560>; Mayou RA, Ehlers A, Hobbs M (2000). Psychological debriefing for road traffic accident victims. Three-year follow-up of a randomized controlled trial. British Journal of Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1192/bjp.176.6.589>; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2018). Post-traumatic stress disorder (NG116), recommendations 1.6.4, 1.6.5, 1.6.15–1.6.19. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng116/chapter/Recommendations>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2020). Notice on the issuance of the Standards for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Mental Disorders (2020 Edition) (National Health Commission Medical Letter [2020] No. 945), Chapter 8 Trauma and Stress-Related Disorders. <https://www.nhc.gov.cn/yzygj/c100068/202012/b4305ace9e14440792eb76d29602c88a.shtml>

Note: A one-time interview is to call the person together or talk alone within a few days after the accident to let him tell the story and feelings at the time. Domestic standards also list group interviews in the psychological treatment table for acute stress disorder, which is inconsistent with NICE. This article is based on the test results. If you organize this kind of meeting after something goes wrong at work or school, you don’t have to talk about it if you don’t want to, and don’t force others to talk about it. The first few weeks are about being safe, eating, sleeping, and having people around you. Go to a psychiatry, psychology or clinical psychology department and ask directly if you can get trauma-focused psychotherapy. The logic is the same as #9 in this section (Don’t spend money on grief counseling right out of the gate). Not everyone needs professional intervention, but efforts should be directed at those who are still stuck after a month. Those whose loved ones die in accidents or homicides often have these symptoms, see Article 4 of this section (Relatives die in accidents or homicides). What to do first after being sexually assaulted, see Section 13, Article 42 (After Being Sexually Assaulted). Emergency rescue personnel such as police, medical staff, and firefighters get it due to their work, and it has been included in the catalog of occupational diseases. See Section 19, Item 10 (remarks on dust, noise, and chemical poisons) for details.

Case: Xiao Chen was pulled into a one-time psychological interview that night after the car accident, and the incident was told. A month later, he still had recurring flashbacks and was afraid to get in the car. I went to a psychiatric department for trauma-focused therapy eight times, and my flashbacks decreased. After half a year, I was able to drive to work alone without taking long vacations.

items.title: If your child says that there is sudden severe pain and it is getting worse, go to the hospital immediately and don't let him endure it until school is over
items.core: Some diseases are calculated by the hour. The boy suddenly suffered severe pain in one side of his scrotum, which may be due to testicular torsion, that is, the blood vessel connected to the testicles was twisted and the blood supply was cut off. When treated within 6 hours, 97.2% of the testicles were preserved, and when treated within 19 to 24 hours, only 42.5% remained. Don't wait until school is over for this kind of pain. Even if it hurts for a long time, you still have to go.
body: Cost: No money. Take half a day off to take your child to the emergency room.

Profit: According to the rules, 30 groups of case reports and 2116 cases of testicular torsion patients were found and combined. Among them, 1,283 cases are counted in 6-hour intervals. The rate of testicular preservation was 97.2% between 0 and 6 hours from the onset of pain. 79.3% from 7 to 12 hours. 13 to 18 hours 61.3%. 19 to 24 hours 42.5%. 25 to 48 hours 24.4%. 7.4% over 48 hours. Combined into large segments, 90.4% within 12 hours, 54.0% between 13 and 24 hours, and 18.1% over 24 hours. The authors concluded that retention could be longer than the commonly cited 6 to 8 hours. So even if you have been hurting for a long time, you still have to deal with it. Don't stop going because "it's too late anyway." In the three-year U.S. pediatric hospitalization data from 2000, 2003, and 2006, 2,443 boys aged 1 month to less than 18 years of age underwent testicular torsion surgery. There are two peaks in the age of onset, one in the first year of life and one in puberty.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Mellick LB, et al. (2019). A Systematic Review of Testicle Survival Time After a Torsion Event. Pediatric Emergency Care. epidemiology using a national database: incidence, risk of orchiectomy and possible measures toward improving the quality of care. Journal of Urology, 186(5), 2009-2013. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.juro.2011.07.024>

Note: Let me tell the boy in advance: If there is sudden severe pain down there, speak up right away, don’t be embarrassed. Testicular torsion is more common in boys who have just entered puberty. Many children are embarrassed to say it and just endure it. This is the author's experience. Also calculated on an hourly basis are acute appendicitis (which can perforate if delayed for a long time), diabetic ketoacidosis, and meningitis. This section has not verified the "how much damage will be done if it takes a few hours" one by one in this section. The author summarizes their common signals as follows: sudden onset, worsening, and different from any other time. How to recognize an emergency and how to call a car see Section 13.

Case: A 12-year-old boy suddenly suffered severe pain in his right scrotum during class. The teacher did not let him endure it until school was over, so he immediately contacted his parents and sent him to the emergency room. Ultrasound confirmed testicular torsion, and the testicle was surgically reduced within 5 hours. The blood supply to the testis was restored, and the reexamination was normal, thus avoiding resection and future fertility risks.

items.title: Don’t put off the treatment you need to do just to “wait until the exam is over.” Some windows follow bone age, not exam arrangements.
items.core: Scoliosis is a sideways curvature of the spine. The brace is a hard-shell vest worn on the body to support the spine. When the bones were still growing, 75% of the children did not bend to 50 degrees until the bones were grown, and only 42% of the children only observed and did not wear them. The time it can be worn will depend on the growth of the bones. If it does not follow the high school entrance examination and college entrance examination, you may miss it after the examination.
body: Cost: No money, all you have to decide is whether to do it sooner or later. Asking for leave and follow-up visits will take time, and the cost of the treatment itself will be calculated separately. The difficulty is that the brace requires wearing it for at least 18 hours a day, and the child has to endure it.

Benefits: A multi-hospital trial found 242 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients who were eligible to wear braces. Among them, 116 cases were divided into groups by drawing lots, and 126 cases chose whether to wear it or not. Success or failure is determined in advance: if the curvature grows to more than 50 degrees, the treatment will be considered a failure, and if the curvature has not reached this degree when the bone is finished growing, the treatment will be considered a success. Children in the brace group were asked to wear them for at least 18 hours a day. It is calculated based on which group it was initially assigned to, regardless of whether it was actually worn enough later. The odds were 75% for the brace-wearing group and 42% for the observation-only group (odds ratio OR 4.11, 95% CI 1.85–9.16). Calculating the two groups of people drawn by lot and those chosen by oneself, the ratio is 72% vs. 48% (after deducting the original difference between the two groups, the odds ratio is OR 1.93, 1.08–3.46). The more hours of wear per day, the higher the success rate (P<0.001, this relationship is unlikely to be due to chance). The trial was stopped early because the brace was indeed effective.
Level of Evidence: A
Source: Weinstein SL, et al. (2013). Effects of bracing in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1307337>

Note: Scoliosis is used as an example here because it has a lottery-based trial and a clear time window. It also happens to be one of the key items in the student physical examination (see No. 7). According to the author's experience, similar surgeries include strabismus, amblyopia, dental caries, and congenital heart disease, which can be performed at a time. The later they are done, the less effective or more costly they may be. This section has not been verified item by item. Please ask a specialist for the specific window. If you are afraid of delaying class, you can suspend schooling during the compulsory education period for up to 1 year, and your student status will be retained. See Article 11.

Case: A 13-year-old girl was diagnosed with mild scoliosis, and the doctor recommended wearing a brace immediately. The parents did not wait until after the high school entrance examination, but took advantage of the immature bone age to wear it for 20 hours a day, and cooperated with follow-up visits for adjustments. One year later, the curvature did not progress and stabilized at 30 degrees when bone age reached maturity, thus avoiding surgery.

items.title: If a child is bullied, report to school on the same day and ask for written handling. If a child is bullied, call the police directly if it involves beating, stealing money, or spreading rumors.
items.core: Children who are bullied by their peers are significantly more likely to have suicidal thoughts and engage in suicidal behavior. When the school receives a report, it must immediately investigate it. If it is determined to be bullying, it will be punished or punished. If it is serious, it must not be concealed and must be reported to the police. So I reported it on the same day and asked to go through the certification process and leave a written record.
body: Cost: Nothing. Contact the class teacher and the school's student bullying management organization. If you want to call the police, call 110. The difficulty lies in resisting the advice to "don't make a big deal out of it."

Yield: 34 studies, 284,375 children and adolescents combined. Being bullied by peers was associated with suicidal ideation, odds ratio OR 2.23 (95% CI 2.10–2.37). A further 9 studies with 70,102 people found that bullying was associated with suicide attempts, with an odds ratio of OR 2.55 (1.95–3.34). The results were the same across men and women, ages and the quality of the studies themselves. The association between cyberbullying and suicidal thoughts is stronger than offline bullying. Article 21 of the "School Protection Regulations for Minors" lists five categories of behavior: beating, kicking, slapping, scratching, pushing, and pulling; insulting, sarcastic, and insulting nicknames; robbing, taking, or deliberately destroying property; malicious exclusion and isolation; fabricating facts, defamation, or spreading rumors through the Internet. The article also stipulates that if a party with an advantage in age, body or number does these things intentionally or maliciously, causing personal injury, property damage or mental damage, it can be deemed as bullying. Article 22 requires faculty and staff to promptly understand and report any student's abnormal mood or physical injury. Article 23 requires the school to immediately investigate the report upon receipt, submit it to the bullying management organization for determination and disposal, and notify parents to participate. If bullying is determined, educational punishment or disciplinary action will be taken. Serious bullying that violates public security management or is suspected of committing a crime must not be concealed, and must be reported to the public security organs and education administrative departments in a timely manner (nationwide, effective from September 1, 2021)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: van Geel M, et al. (2014). Relationship between peer victimization, cyberbullying, and suicide in children and adolescents: a meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2013.4143>; Ministry of Education (2021). Regulations on the protection of minors in schools (Ministry of Education Order No. 50, Articles 21, 22, and 23). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-06/02/content_5614946.htm>; Ministry of Education and other eleven departments (2017). Strengthening the comprehensive management plan for bullying among primary and secondary school students (Jiaosu [2017] No. 10, 3 (1)). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2018/content_5294435.htm>

Note: The 22nd sign of roll call is obvious emotional abnormality and physical injury. If your child has an unexplained injury or is suddenly in a bad mood, ask first. This analysis, which combines multiple studies, only tracks records without group comparisons, so it cannot prove that bullying alone causes suicide. But the direction and magnitude of the risks are clear. The "Comprehensive Plan for Strengthening the Comprehensive Management of Bullying among Primary and Secondary School Students" also requires a strict distinction between bullying and playing among students. Therefore, the school has the obligation to make a determination and cannot just say "children are playing around".

Case: A boy in the second grade of junior high school was robbed of his meal money by his classmates at the school gate, and the rumor was spread to the class. His father took him to report to the class teacher that night and asked the school to issue a written record of the incident and call the police. The next day, the school conducted surveillance and interviewed parents. The money was refunded and the rumors were deleted.

items.title: Let your children stay outdoors for 2 hours a day. This is currently the only way to prevent myopia that is supported by randomized trials without spending any money or medication.
items.core: If the first grade of elementary school has an extra 40 minutes of outdoor classes every day, the number of newly myopic children will drop from about 40% to about 30% after three years. The amount given by the National Health Commission is no less than 2 hours outdoors during the day, or 14 hours a week. Cloudy days also count.
body: Cost: Nothing. But to make time every day, most of the time you have to squeeze it in from homework and online classes. The difficulty is that you have to do it every day, not just a few times.

Income: First-grade students from 12 primary schools in Guangzhou were divided into groups by lottery (952 students in the intervention school and 951 students in the control school, with an average age of 6.6 years). The intervention was implemented by adding a 40-minute outdoor activity class to each school day and encouraging parents to take their children outside outside of class. The proportion of new myopia within 3 years was 30.4% in the intervention group, or 259 cases among 853 eligible persons, and 39.5%, or 287 cases among 726 persons in the control group. The two groups differed by -9.1 percentage points (95% CI -14.1 to -4.1, P<0.001), with the true difference ranging from roughly 4 to 14 percentage points less. The deepening in power (spherical equivalent change) over 3 years was -1.42 D versus -1.59 D, ​​a difference of 0.17 D (P=0.04). The intervention group deepened slightly less. D is the unit of measurement. There was no difference in the growth of the axial length of the eyeball between the two groups (P=0.07). The "Ten Core Knowledge for Preventing and Controlling Myopia in Children and Adolescents" requires children and adolescents to engage in outdoor activities for no less than 2 hours a day, or a total of 14 hours per week. It indicates that outdoor activities have a protective effect even on cloudy days, and requires avoiding high temperatures and strong sunlight in the afternoon. There are also lottery tests for medication to prevent myopia. 474 Hong Kong children aged 4 to 9 who were not nearsighted were divided into three groups and received eye drops once a night for two years. The rate of myopia over two years was 28.4% for those who took 0.05% atropine, and 53.0% for those who took placebo. The rate for 0.01% atropine was 45.9%, and there was no difference compared with the placebo.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: He M, et al. (2015). Effect of Time Spent Outdoors at School on the Development of Myopia Among Children in China: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. Yam JC, Zhang XJ, Zhang Y, et al. (2023). Effect of Low-Concentration Atropine Eyedrops vs Placebo on Myopia Incidence in Children: The LAMP2 Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA, 329(6), 472-481. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.24162>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten core knowledge for preventing and controlling myopia in children and adolescents (National Health Office Maternal and Child Letter [2023] No. 278). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284.htm>

Note: This trial was only conducted for 3 years, and the children who participated started from the age of 6. The difference in the proportion of myopia between the two groups is 9.1 percentage points, which can only prevent some people from being myopic, but cannot guarantee that they will not be myopic. The same ten core knowledge items also provide several practices. Reading and writing require "one foot, one punch, one inch." After using your eyes at close range for 20 minutes, look far away for more than 20 seconds. For primary and secondary school students who do not use electronic screens for learning, the time limit shall not exceed 15 minutes at a time and the total time shall not exceed 1 hour per day. "Staying outside" and "taking physical education class" are not the same thing. Standing outside during class also counts. The author of the trial of atropine eye drops said that more trials are needed to confirm and to see whether it is safe in the long term. Ask your ophthalmologist whether to use it and which concentration to use. The author has not found any other methods that don't cost money and don't use drugs, such as lottery tests.

Case: A first-grade girl used to love reading indoors, but her mother changed it to riding bikes in the community after school, going to the park on weekends, and ensuring two hours of outdoor time every day. A year later, a physical examination showed that her vision was stable, and the doctor asked her to continue.

items.title: Screens should not be given to children aged 0 to 3 years old, and to children aged 3 to 6 years old. Screens should not be given to primary and secondary school students for non-study purposes for no more than 1 hour a day.
items.core: The National Health and Medical Commission requires that children aged 0 to 3 years old should not be given screens, and children aged 3 to 6 years old should try not to touch them. For primary and secondary school students who are not using it for study, it should not exceed 15 minutes at a time and no more than 1 hour a day. The reason is that looking at the screen at close range for a long time can easily lead to myopia early. The evidence between screens and myopia is not so strong. The real test effect is to spend 2 hours outdoors every day.
body: Cost: Nothing. What’s difficult is taking the screen away from children, and it’s also difficult for parents themselves to stop watching it in front of their children.

Benefits: The original words of Article 4 of the "Ten Core Knowledge for Preventing and Controlling Myopia in Children and Adolescents" are "Infants and children aged 0 to 3 years old should not use mobile phones, tablets, computers and other screen electronic products; children aged 3 to 6 years should try to avoid contact with and use of mobile phones, tablets, computers and other screen electronic products; primary and secondary school students should not use electronic screens for more than 15 minutes at a time for non-learning purposes, and the cumulative time per day should not exceed 1 hour." The same article states that "Using electronic video products at close range for a long time can easily deplete children's hyperopia reserve, which is an important reason for the early onset and high incidence of myopia in children and adolescents." The 2018 implementation plan of eight departments including the Ministry of Education has consistent requirements for parents, and also adds that "the younger the age, the shorter the time of continuous use of electronic products." The research evidence is much weaker: one systematic review included 33 studies, 11 combined, ranging from 3 months to 33 years old. Taking into account only mobile phones and tablets, the odds ratio for myopia was 1.26 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.60, I²=77%). Combined with the computer it is 1.77 (1.28 to 2.45, I²=87%). The authors concluded only that it was "possibly relevant" and noted that none of the 33 studies had reliable measures of screen time.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten core knowledge for preventing and controlling myopia in children and adolescents (National Health Office Maternity and Childhood Letter [2023] No. 278). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284.htm>; Eight departments including the Ministry of Education (2018). Comprehensive Implementation Plan for Preventing and Controlling Myopia in Children and Adolescents (Jiao Ti Yi [2018] No. 3). <http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A17/moe_943/s3285/201808/t20180830_346672.html> ; Foreman J, Salim AT, Praveen A, et al. (2021). Association between digital smart device use and myopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet Digital Health, 3(12), e806-e818. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2589-7500(21)00135-7> ; Madigan S, McArthur BA, Anhorn C, Eirich R, Christakis DA (2020). Associations between screen use and child language skills: a systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics, 174(7), 665-675. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2020.0327>

Note: B is set because the official regulations are divided into grades, not the numbers measured in experiments. The lower limit of the odds ratio given by the study is exactly 1.00, and the author only dares to say "may be related." So just think of it as a house rule that is easy to implement. Don’t think of it as “if you don’t look at the screen, you won’t be myopic.” What really holds up the draw test is Article 4 (2 hours outdoors). Preschoolers should also have their eyes checked. The same document states that refractive screening should be done regularly after 1 to 3 years old, 4 to 6 years old, and 7 years old to see how much hyperopia reserve is left. Please refer to Article 12 (Mydriasis Optometry) for the investigation method. A meta-analysis of the relationship between screens and children's language ability was conducted, which included 42 studies involving 18,905 people. More screen time was associated with weaker language skills (r=−0.14, 95% CI −0.18 to −0.10). But watching together and watching programs with educational content were in turn positively correlated (r=0.16 and 0.13). This is correlation, not causation. It only shows that it is not cost-effective to use a screen instead of talking to your children.

Case: A two-and-a-half-year-old child always watches animations before meals. The parents put away the tablet and changed it to puzzles and parent-child reading, and took sticker books when going out. Two months later, the child no longer chased for the screen, and half a year later, the physical examination showed normal vision.

items.title: Treat myopia as the damage it will leave behind: the deeper the degree, the more retinal detachment, macular degeneration, and glaucoma will occur in the future.
items.core: Myopia will not heal on its own, nor can the degree be reduced, nor is it just a matter of "wearing glasses". Compared with people who are not myopic, people with myopia are more likely to suffer from myopic macular degeneration and retinal detachment, with those above 600 degrees being the worst affected. Therefore, the deeper a child's myopia becomes, the greater the risk he will face in the future.
body: Cost: Nothing. There is nothing to do per se, the things to do are in items 4 and 5 (2 hours outdoors, age-specific screens).

Benefits: A systematic review and meta-analysis compiled studies before June 2019, divided into three categories according to degree: mild (−0.5 to −3.00 D), moderate (−3.00 to −6.00 D), and high (≤−6.00 D, above 600 degrees). Compared with those without myopia, the odds ratios for myopic macular degeneration were 13.57 (95% CI 6.18 to 29.79), 72.74 (33.18 to 159.48), and 845.08 (230.05 to 3104.34). Retinal detachment was 3.15 (1.92 to 5.17), 8.74 (7.28 to 10.50), and 12.62 (6.65 to 23.94). Posterior subcapsular cataract was 1.56 (1.32 to 1.84), 2.55 (1.98 to 3.28), and 4.55 (2.66 to 7.75). For open-angle glaucoma, mild was 1.59 (1.33 to 1.91), and moderate and high combined were 2.92 (1.89 to 4.52). The odds ratios of visual impairment for those over 60 years old were 1.71 (1.07 to 2.74), 5.54 (3.12 to 9.85), and 87.63 (34.50 to 222.58). The "Ten Core Knowledge for Preventing and Controlling Myopia in Children and Adolescents" agrees: above 600 degrees is high myopia. In this group of people, the incidence of blinding eye diseases such as cataracts, open-angle glaucoma, myopic macular degeneration, retinal detachment, and myopic optic neuropathy is significantly higher than that of other groups. Moreover, "myopia is preventable, controllable and irreversible."
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Haarman AEG, Enthoven CA, Tideman JWL, Tedja MS, Verhoeven VJM, Klaver CCW (2020). The complications of myopia: a review and meta-analysis. Investigative Ophthalmology & Visual Science, 61(4), 49. <https://doi.org/10.1167/iovs.61.4.49>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten core knowledge to prevent and control myopia in children and adolescents (National Health Office Maternity and Childhood Letter [2023] No. 278). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284.htm>

Note: The summaries are all observational studies, and the odds ratios are unusually large. The confidence range for high myopia versus macular degeneration ranges from 230 to 3104, indicating that studies vary widely. Numbers can only be used to measure magnitude and cannot be used as precise values. The figures for visual impairment in the income column are for people over 60 years old. The author infers from this that most of these consequences will not be apparent until middle-aged and older people. Myopia is not just a matter of wearing a pair of glasses, it is worth the effort to delay and control it. For how to review after diagnosis, see Article 12 (Mydriasis Optometry). Don’t buy products that claim to cure myopia, see No. 9 (Cure Myopia).

Case: A third-grade boy squints his eyes when looking at the blackboard, and his parents are worried about wearing glasses that will make him worse. Two years later, my dilated refraction was nearly 600 degrees. The doctor explained that high myopia would increase the risk of retinal detachment and macular degeneration, and required regular fundus examinations.

items.title: You should read the report form of the student physical examination every year by yourself. Any abnormal items should be taken to the hospital for examination that year.
items.core: Primary and secondary schools organize student physical examinations once a year. The report card should focus on overweight, obesity, malnutrition, abnormal spinal curvature, poor vision, and dental caries. Don’t just take one look at your height and weight and put away your list. If these items were abnormal, I took my child to a specialist to have them checked out.
body: Cost: Nothing. The medical examination fee for compulsory education is paid out of the school's public funds, and parents do not have to pay extra.

Benefits: The "Measures for the Management of Health Examinations for Primary and Secondary School Students (2021 Edition)" stipulates that primary and secondary schools organize a physical examination for school students once a year. Surgical examination includes the head, neck, chest, spine, extremities, skin, and lymph nodes. The eye examination includes eye appearance, distance vision, and refraction (the degree of nearsightedness and farsightedness). The report card issued to the individual should include the findings, overall evaluation and health guidance suggestions. Among them, overweight, obesity, malnutrition, abnormal spinal curvature, poor vision, and dental caries (cavities) must be the focus of guidance. The education administration department should establish files and follow up on students with health problems (write them down and follow up later). The cost of physical examination for students in compulsory education shall be paid by the school’s public funds, and parents shall not pay separately (National, issued in September 2021)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: National Health Commission, Ministry of Education (2021). Measures for the Management of Health Examinations for Primary and Secondary School Students (2021 Edition) (National Health Commission [2021] No. 29). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-10/21/content_5644100.htm>

Note: I gave it B because this is a document that stipulates what the school should do, not an effectiveness study. What it guarantees is "check these items every year, and follow up if any abnormalities are found." It does not guarantee that someone will take care of them if they are found. The physical examination is just a screening, not a diagnosis. If you have poor vision, go to an ophthalmologist for dilated refraction (Article 12). If you have abnormal spinal curvature, go to an orthopedic or spinal surgery department (No. 2, don’t put off treatment just to wait until the exam is over). Parents must take their children to these two steps.

Case: The medical examination sheet for a fourth-grade student said ‘abnormal spinal curvature’. At first, my mother only looked at the height and weight, and then she turned to the back and noticed. At that time, he was taken to the children's orthopedics department for a X-ray, and he was diagnosed with mild scoliosis, and corrective training was started.

items.title: According to the U.S. Prevention Guidelines, children aged 12 to 18 should be screened for depression. Do not use school psychological assessments as diagnosis.
items.core: U.S. prevention guidelines recommend screening for major depression in children ages 12 to 18, with insufficient evidence for children ages 11 and younger. Suicide is the second leading cause of death for children ages 10 to 19 in the United States. The school's annual psychological assessment is only a census and cannot be used as a diagnosis. If the child himself says he is uncomfortable, he will be referred directly to a psychiatrist or clinical psychology department.
body: Cost: 0 to tens of yuan, fill out a screening questionnaire in the community or hospital outpatient clinic. There is no charge for calling the two hotlines 12355 and 12356.

Benefits: The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force issued a recommendation statement in 2022. It recommends screening adolescents aged 12 to 18 years for major depressive disorder (category B recommendation). Category B means that the grasp is medium, the benefits are medium, and it is worth doing. There is insufficient evidence to screen children 11 years and younger for major depression (I statement, that is, the evidence is insufficient to make a recommendation). There is insufficient evidence on the benefits and harms of specifically screening children and adolescents for suicide risk (I Statement). How often should screening be performed? The working group found no evidence and the most appropriate interval is unclear. It states that repeated screening may be most useful in adolescents with risk factors for depression. Suicide is the second leading cause of death for people aged 10 to 19, the document states. The document also points out that severe depression in children and adolescents is closely related to many later problems. These problems include recurrent episodes of depression in adulthood, other mental disorders, and an increased risk of suicidal thoughts, suicide attempts, and death by suicide. The "Ten Measures to Further Strengthen the Mental Health Work of Primary and Secondary School Students" requires the establishment of a three-level service system of class teachers, full-time and part-time mental health teachers, and psychiatrists. Each student undergoes psychological assessment, generally no more than once per academic year. The document also calls for the advancement of mechanisms for referral to medical treatment for mental illness and for returning to school after recovery. It calls for the role of 12355 Youth Help Desk and 12356 Psychological Assistance Hotline (Nationwide, issued October 2025)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: US Preventive Services Task Force (2022). Screening for Depression and Suicide Risk in Children and Adolescents: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.16946>; General Office of the Ministry of Education (2025). Ten Measures to Further Strengthen the Mental Health of Primary and Secondary School Students (Jiaoji Office [2025] No. 2). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528.htm>; US Preventive Services Task Force (2022). Depression and Suicide Risk in Children and Adolescents: Screening (Screening Intervals). <https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/screening-depression-suicide-risk-children-adolescents>

Note: The rating is B because the original article gives a rating of recommendation strength, not an effect that can be converted into numbers. Screening once is the minimum recommended by the author, and those with risk factors for depression can be screened again after a while. It is still recommended by the United States, and there is no corresponding official screening recommendation in China. A positive screening result only means that another evaluation is required, but does not mean a confirmed diagnosis. See Section 1, Article 25 for treatment of suicidal thoughts. See section 29 for family responses.

Case: The school psychological assessment of a second-year junior high school girl showed that she was ‘normal’, but she had insomnia, cried for two consecutive weeks, and said that living was boring. My mother did not wait for a re-examination and went directly to the psychiatry department. After interviews and scale assessments, she was diagnosed with moderate depression and started treatment.

items.title: Don’t buy products and services that claim to “cure myopia” or “reduce myopia”
items.core: The State Administration for Market Regulation clearly stated that “myopia cannot be cured under current medical technology.” Those who promote terms such as "restoration", "lower degree", "myopia cure" and "degree repair" must be strictly investigated and dealt with. When you see such words, exclude them directly without comparing prices. Eye protection devices are considered medical devices, and e-commerce platforms have the responsibility to check whether sellers are qualified to sell them.
body: Cost: No money, and in turn, you save money.

Income: The special rectification action notice from the General Office of the State Administration for Market Regulation from November 2021 to March 2022 clearly states: "Under the current medical technology conditions, myopia cannot be cured." The notice requires that the use of misleading expressions such as "rehabilitation", "restoration", "dimension reduction", "myopia cure", "myopia nemesis", "degree repair" and other misleading expressions to market children and adolescents' myopia prevention and control products shall be strictly investigated in accordance with the law. The notice calls for intensified crackdowns, focusing on behaviors that deceive consumers by falsely using the name of traditional Chinese medicine or using traditional Chinese medicine theory and technology for marketing purposes. The notice also requires severe crackdowns on two types of false and illegal advertisements: those that use the name or image of patients to compare the results before and after diagnosis and treatment, and those that make guaranteed promises about the safety and efficacy of diagnosis and treatment. The notice requires e-commerce platforms to strictly implement the business qualification review responsibilities of medical devices such as eye protection devices and related special commodities (to find out whether the seller is qualified to sell) (Nationwide)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: General Office of the State Administration for Market Regulation (2021). Notice on carrying out special rectification actions for illegal commercial marketing and publicity of children and adolescent myopia prevention and control products. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-11/12/content_5650400.htm>

Remarks: The reason for giving B is because it is based on the identification caliber of the regulatory department when investigating and handling, and it is not measured by using the product for controlled testing. However, "myopia cannot be cured", the health department and regulatory authorities agree: "Ten Core Knowledge for Preventing and Controlling Myopia in Children and Adolescents" states that "myopia is preventable, controllable and irreversible". The two things with real evidence are in Article 4 (Outdoors) and Article 12 (Regulation of Optometry and Reexamination). For anti-blue light glasses, see Section 6, Article 16 (Anti-blue light glasses).

Case: My mother saw an advertisement for an eye protection device that said, "Reduce the temperature by 100 degrees in three months." Before placing the order, she found a regulatory notice that said, "Myopia cannot be cured." She asked the platform for medical device qualifications, but the seller couldn't provide it, so she gave up the purchase and reported it.

items.title: Sleep, homework, physical education and rankings are all clearly stated. If the school cannot do it, it can be submitted
items.core: The document states that elementary school students sleep 10 hours a day, junior high school students 9 hours, and high school students 8 hours. Morning classes in primary schools generally start no earlier than 8:20, and in secondary schools no earlier than 8:00. In 2025, it is also stipulated that physical activities should be no less than 2 hours a day, and rankings must not be based on test scores. If your child doesn't get enough sleep for a long time, you should take these measures first. Don't blame your child for being lazy.
body: Cost: No money. Just know the provisions and report it to the school or local education administration department if necessary. The difficulty lies in opening your mouth to mention it.

Benefits: The "Notice on Further Strengthening the Sleep Management of Primary and Secondary School Students" stipulates that primary school students should sleep up to 10 hours a day, junior high school students 9 hours, and high school students 8 hours. The morning class time for primary schools is generally not earlier than 8:20, and for secondary schools is generally not earlier than 8:00. Schools shall not require students to arrive at school in advance to participate in unified education and teaching activities. Primary school students generally go to bed no later than 21:20, junior high school students no later than 22:00, and high school students no later than 23:00. Training at off-campus training institutions must end no later than 20:30, and online live training must end no later than 21:00. Game services are not allowed for minors from 22:00 to 8:00 the next day (National, issued in March 2021). The "Ten Measures to Further Strengthen the Mental Health of Primary and Secondary School Students" also stipulates that comprehensive physical activity time for primary and secondary school students should be no less than 2 hours a day, and "15 minutes between classes" is encouraged. It also stipulates that students shall not be ranked based on test scores, and it is strictly forbidden to assign mechanically repetitive and punitive homework, and it is encouraged to set one "no homework day" every week (National, issued in October 2025)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: General Office of the Ministry of Education (2021). Notice on further strengthening the sleep management of primary and secondary school students (Jiaoji Department Letter [2021] No. 11). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-04/02/content_5597443.htm>; General Office of the Ministry of Education (2025). Ten measures to further strengthen the mental health of primary and secondary school students (Jiaoji Department [2025] No. 2). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528.htm>

Note: These two documents are issued by the competent authorities. The extent to which each school implements it varies greatly from place to place, so this article is assigned B. Their purpose is to let you know what the school should be doing, so that you have a basis for talking about it. Adult sleep accounts are provided in Sections 2 and 3.

Case: A fifth-grade child wakes up at 6:30 every day and goes to bed at 11 p.m. He is always sleepy in class. The mother talked to the head teacher about sleep and school attendance regulations. The school canceled morning readings and reduced evening homework at home. The child's sleep gradually approached ten hours.

items.title: A child can take a leave of absence from school if he cannot bear it any longer, and the school must keep his student status for up to 1 year
items.core: There is a formal system for suspension of schooling. Parents or other guardians submit an application, and the school confirms the application and reports it to the superior for approval. The maximum period is 1 year at a time. If you need to take a break at the end of the period, you can reapply. The school must keep the child's enrollment status during the break, and he will continue to attend when school resumes. Specific measures are determined by each province, so please ask the school's academic affairs office or local education bureau.
body: Cost: No money. Applications are made to the school by parents or other legal guardians. The difficulty is to first accept the child for a while.

Benefits: Article 16 of the "Measures for the Management of Student Status of Primary and Secondary School Students" stipulates what to do if you suspend your studies. Students should apply for suspension of study by their parents or other legal guardians. After confirmation by the school, it will be reported to the higher-level student status management department for approval. Schools should handle relevant procedures in a timely manner when classes resume. The period for applying for a leave of absence at one time shall not exceed 1 year. If you really want to take a leave of absence after the expiration, you should apply again. The school should retain the student's student status (student identity and location) during the student's leave of absence. Specific measures for suspension of study and resumption will be formulated by provincial education administrative departments (Nationally, issued in January 2025). The "Ten Measures to Further Strengthen the Mental Health Work of Primary and Secondary School Students" requires promoting the establishment of mechanisms for referral for medical treatment and return to school after recovery for mental illness, and guiding schools to formulate plans for handling emergencies of psychological crises on campus.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Ministry of Education (2025). Measures for the Management of Student Status of Primary and Secondary School Students (Jiaoji [2025] No. 1, Article 16). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202502/content_7002620.htm>; General Office of the Ministry of Education (2025). Ten Measures to Further Strengthen the Mental Health of Primary and Secondary School Students (Jiaoji Department [2025] No. 2). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528.htm>; Ministry of Education (2021). Regulations on the protection of minors in schools (Ministry of Education Order No. 50, Article 12). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-06/02/content_5614946.htm>

Remarks: According to the author’s experience, ask three things clearly before going to apply: what medical certificate is required, how to record the student status in the system during the period of leave of absence, and whether to return to the original grade or drop one level when returning to school. The reason for giving B is because the conditions for suspending school, what materials to submit, and how to resume school are all determined by the provincial education department. There is only a framework at the national level. Article 12 of the "Regulations on the Protection of Minors in Schools" also requires compulsory education schools to improve the reporting and filing system for students who drop out, suspend school, and take long-term leave. Therefore, suspending school is something that the school has done, and it is not a special case made for you.

Case: A boy in the third grade of junior high school was unable to enter the classroom for two consecutive months due to severe anxiety. His parents submitted a diagnosis certificate and application for suspension of school to the school. The school reported to the Education Bureau for approval and retained his student status for one year; after recuperation, he returned to school on time and returned to the original grade to continue classes.

items.title: If you detect poor vision, go to the hospital for dilated refraction, and then review it at intervals specified by the doctor
items.core: Mydriatic refraction involves first instilling eye drops to relax the muscles responsible for adjusting focus in the eye, and then rechecking the prescription. This is done in the hospital and is the most accurate way to diagnose myopia. The National Health Commission states that this medicine will not cause damage to healthy eyes and will return to normal after stopping the medicine. Don’t use a computerized optometry test at an optical shop as a diagnosis, and don’t refuse to buy your children glasses just because you’re afraid the prescription will go up.
body: Cost: tens to hundreds of yuan for examination fees and glasses fees. After the pupils are dilated, the child will be afraid of light and see things up close, and it will take half a day to a day or two to get over it.

Benefits: "Ten Core Knowledge for Preventing and Controlling Myopia in Children and Adolescents" explains what mydriasis and optometry is. Use cycloplegic agent first, then optometry. Cycloplegics are eye drops that relax the muscles in the eye that are responsible for focusing. Mydriatic optometry is a medical optometry performed in a hospital and is the “gold standard” (the most accurate method) for diagnosing myopia. Mydriatic drugs will not cause damage to healthy eyes.
