After taking the drug, short-term photophobia and blurred vision may occur, which can return to normal after stopping the drug. Once myopia is diagnosed, timely scientific intervention should be carried out to correct it by wearing glasses. Wearing appropriate glasses can effectively correct blurred vision and delay the progression of myopia. For those with normal vision when wearing glasses, preschool children and primary school students should be re-examined every 3 to 6 months, and middle school and high school students should be re-examined every 6 to 12 months. Whether to change glasses will be decided based on the specific situation. Children between the ages of 1 and 3, 4 to 6, and 7 years old should undergo regular refractive screening (check the diopter) and monitor the amount of hyperopia reserve (National, issued in July 2023)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten core knowledge for preventing and controlling myopia in children and adolescents (National Health Office Maternal and Child Letter [2023] No. 278). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284.htm>

Remarks: B is given because this is the approach given in official popular science documents, not original research with specific numbers. High myopia can lead to problems such as retinal detachment, so the review is not just for changing glasses. The "poor vision" detected in the student's physical examination is only the result of the first screening. Students must also go to the hospital for a complete eye examination, see Article 7.

Case: A sixth-grade girl had poor eyesight during a physical examination. She wanted to get glasses directly after a computer test at an optical shop. Her mother took her to the hospital for a dilated eye exam, and found that the prescription was fifty degrees lower than the results in the store. The doctor prescribed glasses based on the dilated results and made an appointment for a three-month reexamination.

items.title: Fissure sealing is done after the permanent molars grow in
items.core: Fissure sealing is to seal the groove on the biting side of the big teeth with resin so that food residue cannot get in. Two years after the treatment, the sealed teeth had fewer cavities, and the protective effect can still be seen four years later. The specific amount of reduction depends on the child's original risk of dental caries.
body: Cost: tens to one or two hundred yuan per piece. No anesthesia, no grinding of teeth, just a few minutes at a time. Many places have free programs for children of sufficient age.

Revenue: 38 trials, 7924 children aged 5 to 16 years, combined by Cochrane rules. Take the ratio of resin-based sealers to no sealers. The odds ratio for permanent first molars in children aged 5 to 10 years was OR 0.12 (95% CI 0.08–0.19) at 24 months. This one comes from seven trials, with 1548 people drawn and 1322 finally tested, and the quality of the evidence is moderate. The odds ratio cannot be directly regarded as the ratio of the proportion of tooth decay between two groups. How much less is actually possible depends on how many teeth would have been decayed when the seal was sealed. At 48 to 54 months, the odds ratio OR was 0.21 (0.16–0.28), with closed still showing fewer cavities. The authors concluded that resin sealants were more effective at preventing dental caries than no sealants at 24 months. Of the 4 trials in which adverse effects were recorded, no adverse effects were reported. Insufficient evidence as to which sealant material is better among glass ionomers
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ahovuo-Saloranta A, et al. (2017). Pit and fissure sealants for preventing dental decay in permanent teeth. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001830.pub5>

Note: The first permanent molar (the big tooth that will not be replaced) usually emerges around 6 years old, and the second one around 12 years old. Sealing should be done when the tooth has just erupted and is not broken yet. If it is already decayed, it can only be filled. Many areas list pit and fissure sealing as a free project for children of sufficient age. Ask the local Centers for Disease Control and Prevention or community health service center. This section did not find a national document that could be verified verbatim, so coverage and age groups are not included. The Cochrane abstract also gives several examples of two-group proportions, but the conversion using odds ratios does not match, so I do not copy them here. Dental caries is also a key item in the physical examination of students, see Article 7.

Case: The six-year-old child's teeth have just grown in. His mother took him to the dental department for examination. The doctor performed pit and fissure sealing on the four permanent molars. A reexamination two years later showed that most of the sealants were intact, the teeth were not decayed, and the doctor only repaired the missing one.

items.title: Children love to play games. First check whether sleep, homework and outing activities are squeezed out. Don't just focus on how long they play
items.core: There are about two or three out of every 100 people who truly have "gaming disorder". If the threshold of the questionnaire is set low and only young people are selected, the proportion will be falsely high. Looking at the real records of game companies, it is almost impossible to see that playing more and less will affect happiness. Minors are required to play only on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and holidays from 8 to 9 p.m.
body: Cost: No money. Pay attention once a week to what time the child goes to bed, whether homework is handed in, and whether the child goes out for activities.

Benefits: A meta-analysis compiled 53 studies, 226,247 people in 17 countries. The prevalence of gaming disorder was 3.05% (95% CI 2.38–3.91, confidence range). Counting only studies with more rigorous sampling, it was 1.96%. The results varied widely from study to study, with 77% of the difference being in which questionnaire was used. The sample is teenagers, the threshold score is low, and the sample is small, which will make the proportion higher. Another study obtained data from seven game companies and connected the real gaming time of 38,935 players over six weeks with their own happiness levels. There is little evidence that time spent playing affects happiness. The National Press and Publication Administration stipulates that game companies can only provide one-hour services to minors from 20:00 to 21:00 every day on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and statutory holidays (National/International, starting from 2021)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Stevens MW, Dorstyn D, Delfabbro PH, King DL. (2021). Global prevalence of gaming disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Australian and New Zealand Journal of Psychiatry, 55(6), 553–568. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0004867420962851>; Vuorre M, Johannes N, Magnusson K, Przybylski AK. (2022). Time spent playing video games is unlikely to impact well-being. Royal Society Open Science, 9(7), 220411. <https://doi.org/10.1098/rsos.220411>; National Press and Publication Administration (2021). Notice on further strict management to effectively prevent minors from being addicted to online games (Guoxinquan [2021] No. 14). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-09/01/content_5634661.htm>

Remarks: B is given because the prevalence rate changes too much with the questionnaire, and the study on happiness only followed six weeks. According to the author's judgment, the most common cost of gaming is the loss of sleep and outdoor time. No research figures were found for this sentence. See Section 10 (Sleep, Homework, Physical Education) of this section for explicit requirements for sleep. See item 4 of this section for outdoor use (2 hours outdoors per day), and item 5 of this section for screen time (not to exceed 1 hour per day for non-study purposes). For recharges and refunds, see Section 5, Article 9 (Rewards for children to recharge using mobile phones). When his grades, sleep, and family relationships all collapse, and he can't stop even with persuasion, he takes his child to a psychiatrist or child psychology department. Do not send them to closed-managed Internet addiction treatment schools, see Article 18 of this section (Internet addiction treatment schools). The beneficiary is the child.

Case: A boy in the first grade of junior high school claimed that he only played for one hour a day, but his parents discovered that he put off his homework until late at night and did not go out on weekends. Instead of just arguing about the duration, my father put away the equipment after 9pm from Friday to Sunday and arranged for a morning run. After two weeks, his sleep and homework improved significantly.

items.title: If a child says he likes the same sex, don't scold him, don't kick him out of the house, and don't send him to "correction": the attitude of the family is related to whether he will commit suicide.
items.core: Among domestic middle school students, those who like the same sex or both sexes are about 3 to 5.5 times more likely to have attempted suicide in a year. Foreign studies have shown that children who are strongly rejected by their families during adolescence are much more likely to attempt suicide later on. Many more have been sent to "correction" by their parents and have attempted suicide.
body: Cost: Nothing. The difficulty is that parents need to digest their own emotions first and not say harsh words right now.

Benefits: A domestic survey covered 506 middle schools in 7 provinces, with a total of 150,822 students from the first grade to the third grade of high school. Among boys who have attempted suicide in the past year, 2.2% only like the opposite sex, 6.9% only like the same sex, and 12.2% like both genders. The corresponding rates for girls are 3.1%, 8.9%, and 10.9%. Calculated, it is about 3 to 5.5 times that of students who only like the opposite sex. The researchers deducted factors such as age, academic pressure, family finances, and being bullied. After deductions, the odds ratios OR for boys were 3.13 (95% CI 2.28–4.28) and 3.83 (2.85–5.14) for the two groups. There are already few suicide attempts in a year, and the odds ratios and relative risks are similar. A meta-analysis summarizing 35 studies calculated that sexual minority adolescents had an OR of 3.50 (2.98–4.12) for having attempted suicide. A US study asked 224 gay and bisexual youth aged 21 to 25 to recall reactions at home during adolescence. Compared with peers with little rejection at home, those with high levels of rejection at home had an OR of 8.4 for having attempted suicide. In another study, parents who themselves tried to change their children's sexual orientation had an OR of 3.08 (1.39–6.83) for children who had attempted suicide. Parents also send their children to see a therapist or religious person, 5.07 (2.38–10.79) (China/Multiple Countries/U.S.)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Huang Y, Li P, Guo L, et al. (2018). Sexual minority status and suicidal behavior among Chinese adolescents: a nationally representative cross-sectional study. BMJ Open, 8(8), e020969. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2017-020969>; di Giacomo E, Krausz M, Colmegna F, Aspesi F, Clerici M. (2018). Estimating the Risk of Attempted Suicide Among Sexual Minority Youths: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics, 172(12), 1145–1152. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2018.2731>; Ryan C, Huebner D, Diaz RM, Sanchez J. (2009). Family rejection as a predictor of negative health outcomes in white and Latino lesbian, gay, and bisexual young adults. Pediatrics, 123(1), 346–352. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2007-3524>; Ryan C, Toomey RB, Diaz RM, Russell ST. (2020). Parent-Initiated Sexual Orientation Change Efforts With LGBT Adolescents: Implications for Young Adult Mental Health and Adjustment. Journal of Homosexuality, 67(2), 159–173. <https://doi.org/10.1080/00918369.2018.1538407>; National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2024 revision). Protection of Minors Law (Article 17). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081818f197cf001905e567af635a0>; National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2015). Anti-Domestic Violence Law (Article 2). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7f9d60889>

Note: The reason given is B because these are one-time surveys. The degree of family rejection depends on the memories of adults. It can only show that there is a relationship, but cannot explain who caused whom. Parents don’t have to agree immediately. Don’t do anything to hurt your children yet. Legally, parents are not allowed to abuse, abandon, or commit domestic violence against their children. Frequent verbal abuse and threats are also considered domestic violence. If the child is depressed and says he doesn’t want to live, call 12356 first, see Section 1, Item 25 (call 12356 if he has suicidal thoughts). You can also go to a psychiatrist according to Article 8 of this section (a depression screening between the ages of 12 and 18). "Correction" Why don't touch it, see Section 6, Article 28 (Don't do sexual orientation correction). The beneficiary is the child and you.

Case: After dinner, my son, a sophomore in high school, said he liked boys. His mother did not scold him or drive him away. She only said that he would live at home and chat slowly, and then accompany him for psychological counseling. After one semester, he was still in school, emotionally stable, and willing to talk about stress with his parents.

items.title: Don't hit your child, and don't yell, scold or call him stupid: Children who are often spanked and scolded have more behavioral and emotional problems.
items.core: Children who are frequently spanked have more aggression and psychological problems, are more estranged from their parents, and receive more severe spankings. Whether spanking can make a child obedient on the spot is unclear from the evidence. Children who are often yelled at and called stupid when they are 13 years old will get into more troubles and become depressed later on, and their parents can't stop them no matter how affectionate they are.
body: Cost: Nothing. The hard thing is to stop your hands and mouth the moment the anger arises, and you have to change your management method to neither hitting nor scolding. For alternative management methods, see Article 17 of this section (parent classes that teach specific methods).

Profit: Let’s see first. One meta-analysis only included open-hand spanking or spanking. It summarizes 75 studies, 111 effect sizes, and a total of 160,927 children. Thirteen of the 17 results were clearly related to being beaten, and all were in a bad direction. d is the effect size, with 0.2 considered small and 0.5 considered medium. Aggression in childhood d = 0.37 (95% CI 0.13–0.61, credible range). Explicit problems 0.41, referring to hitting people and breaking rules. Internalizing problems 0.24, referring to anxiety and depression. Mental health problems 0.53, poor relationship with parents 0.51, low self-esteem 0.15, and poor cognitive abilities 0.17. Physical abuse by parents 0.64. Antisocial behavior in adulthood 0.36 and mental health problems 0.24. The 111 effect sizes combined were d = 0.33 (0.29–0.38). There is no significant relationship between the child's disobedience on the spot and whether he is spanked (d = 0.14, −0.19–0.47), and this item has only 5 effect sizes. Another review looked only at pre- and post- follow-up studies, a total of 69 studies. Corporal punishment consistently predicted more behavioral problems later in life, and was not associated with any good long-term outcomes. Seven of the studies looked at the number of spankings, and five found that more spankings were associated with worse problems. Look at the yelling and cursing again. A US study followed 976 families with both parents. When the child is 13 years old, parents often yell, curse, and call the child stupid or lazy. Between the ages of 13 and 14, the child's trouble-making and depressive symptoms increase. Whether the parents are usually affectionate or not cannot offset this relationship. The reverse is also true: children who get into more trouble at age 13 get scolded more later on. Legally, parents are not allowed to commit domestic violence against their children. Article 2 of the Anti-Domestic Violence Law lists the methods of domestic violence: beating, binding, mutilation, restriction of personal freedom, and regular verbal abuse and intimidation. Article 12 of the law requires guardians to conduct family education in a civilized manner. If parents infringe on their children's rights, neighborhood committees and village committees must admonish and stop them, and report serious cases to the police. If the police, procuratorate, or court find out, they must reprimand the parents and order them to receive family education guidance (nationwide)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Gershoff ET, Grogan-Kaylor A. (2016). Spanking and child outcomes: Old controversies and new meta-analyses. Journal of Family Psychology, 30(4), 453–469. <https://doi.org/10.1037/fam0000191>; Heilmann A, Mehay A, Watt RG, et al. (2021). Physical punishment and child outcomes: a narrative review of prospective studies. Lancet, 398(10297), 355–364. Wang MT, Kenny S. (2014). Longitudinal links between fathers' and mothers' harsh verbal discipline and adolescents' conduct problems and depressive symptoms. Child Development, 85(3), 908–923. <https://doi.org/10.1111/cdev.12143>; Ferguson CJ. (2013). Spanking, corporate punishment and negative long-term outcomes: a meta-analytic review of longitudinal studies. Clinical Psychology Review, 33(1), 196–208. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpr.2012.11.002>; Larzelere RE, Kuhn BR. (2005). Comparing child outcomes of physical punishment and alternative disciplinary tactics: a meta-analysis. Clinical Child and Family Psychology Review, 8(1), 1–37. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10567-005-2340-z>; National People's Congress Standing Committee (2015). Anti-Domestic Violence Law (Articles 2 and 12). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7f9d60889>; National People's Congress Standing Committee (Amended in 2024). Law on the Protection of Minors (Articles 11, 17, 118). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081818f197cf001905e567af635a0>; National People's Congress Standing Committee (2021). Family Education Promotion Law (Articles 23, 53). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817cac3b2d017cac5a6c6f0109>

Note: Controversy. Almost all of these studies are just follow-up records without group control, and cannot explain who caused whom. In the spanking review, 72% of the studies only looked at whether the two events occurred together, or relied on subsequent recall. Another meta-analysis only included studies with before-and-after follow-up. After subtracting the child's original behavior, the correlation between spanking and explicit problems was only 0.07, and the correlation with internalizing problems was only 0.10. The author of that article thought the impact was minimal. Another review found that "conditional spanking" was more effective than 10 of 13 other discipline methods in reducing disobedience and antisocial behavior. It also found that hitting too hard or mainly hitting is worse than other management methods. Therefore, what the counter-argument can show is that a small amount and conditional treatment may not be worse than other management methods. Beating him hard, beating him often and scolding him often made both sides think it was worse. Occasionally hitting or yelling is not clearly stated in the law as domestic violence. It names beatings and regular verbal abuse and threats. The beneficiaries are mainly children. If a child is spanked at home, reporting to the police and applying for a protection order are described in Section 8, Article 43 (Personal Safety Protection Order). Anyone who sees other people beating their children for a long time has the right to dissuade them or report it to the public security, civil affairs, or education departments. For matters involving a stranger's home, it is enough to call 110 or tell the neighborhood committee. Don't go to the door to start a fight yourself.

Case: My father often slapped the table and scolded his son as "stupid" because he was procrastinating on his homework, and once even slapped the back of his hand. Three months later, the child avoided him, hid his test papers, and pushed his classmates in the class. After he changed his mind to leave first and calm down before telling the rules, the conflicts were reduced.

items.title: If your child is difficult to control and you can’t help but beat and scold yourself, go to a parent class that teaches specific methods.
items.core: Children are inherently difficult to control, but parents have taken classes that teach them specific methods of management. The problems of children hitting others and not obeying the rules have been reduced, and the parents' mood has also improved. Parents also beat and scold their children less often. It was most obvious when they first finished class. They still hit their children after one or two years, but they were much smaller. Shanghai has also tried this type of class and it was effective.
body: Cost: Parent schools run by schools and kindergartens and online parent schools run by governments at or above the provincial level are stated to be public welfare by law. Evidence-based classes are held once a week or every other week for one to two hours, ranging from four to twenty-four weeks. You should practice accordingly when you get home. The difficulty lies in persisting in finishing it and practicing every day.

Benefits: Cochrane compiled 13 trials, 10 of which were randomized, with a total of 1078 parents. The children, ages 3 to 12, all had behavioral problems. Incoming classes are held once a week or every other week, for one to two hours each time, at least three times. The short one lasts for 4 weeks and the long one lasts for 24 weeks. Parents who have attended classes have fewer behavioral problems in their children. The SMD was −0.53 (95% CI −0.72 to −0.34, confidence range) for parents’ own ratings and −0.44 (−0.77 to −0.11) for independent ratings. SMD and d are on the same scale, 0.5 is considered medium. Parental mental health improved, −0.36 (−0.52 to −0.20). There were fewer negative or harsh disciplines, with parent ratings −0.77 (−0.96 to −0.59) and others rating −0.42 (−0.67 to −0.16). The authors say these are short-term effects. Another meta-review only included trials of parent classes with children aged 2 to 10 years old. It identified 346 randomized trials, 60 of which measured behaviors such as spanking and scolding, spread across 22 countries. Hitting and scolding decreased at the beginning of class, d = −0.46 (−0.59 to −0.33). and −0.24 after 1 to 6 months (−0.37 to −0.11). It is −0.18 (−0.34 to −0.02) after 7 to 24 months, and becomes smaller the further back. Most of these data are reported by parents themselves. There are also trials in China. 81 parents in Shanghai were divided into groups by lottery, and some of them attended Triple P group classes. After the class, the children's adjustment problems, parents' management and emotions were better than those of the parents waiting for the class, and they were still there 6 months later. A rural kindergarten was attended by 191 adults with children, part of which was self-study online classes, plus two group discussions. After two weeks of schooling, they reported about 33% less child abuse than those who were only given books to read (IRR 0.67). Three months later, the children also had fewer behavioral problems (d = −0.40). The "Family Education Promotion Law" requires parents to consciously learn family education knowledge. Primary and secondary schools and kindergartens can run parent schools and regularly organize public welfare family education guidance. Neighborhood committees and village committees can set up community parent schools. Governments at or above the provincial level should open public welfare online parent schools and service hotlines. Family education guidance agencies are not allowed to organize for-profit training (national, effective from January 1, 2022)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Furlong M, McGilloway S, Bywater T, Hutchings J, Smith SM, Donnelly M. (2012). Behavioral and cognitive-behavioural group-based parenting programs for early-onset conduct problems in children aged 3 to 12 years. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (2), CD008225. Backhaus S, Leijten P, Jochim J, Melendez-Torres GJ, Gardner F. (2023). Effects over time of parenting interventions to reduce physical and emotional violence against children: a systematic review and meta-analysis. eClinicalMedicine, 60, 102003. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eclinm.2023.102003>; Guo M, Morawska A, Sanders MR. (2016). A Randomized Controlled Trial of Group Triple P With Chinese Parents in Mainland China. Behavior Modification, 40(6), 825–851. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0145445516644221>; Wang W, Zhang H. (2026). A self-directed parenting program to reduce the risk of child maltreatment in rural China: A cluster randomized controlled trial. Child Abuse & Neglect, 173, 107937. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chiabu.2026.107937>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Family Education Promotion Law (Articles 18, 25, 31, 38, and 40). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817cac3b2d017cac5a6c6f0109>

Remarks: A is given because of the combined figures from Cochrane and multiple lottery trials. The lessons in the experiment had several things in common. The person leading the class teaches specific methods, such as playing with the child, praising, rewarding and disciplining. Parents practice and drill in class and have homework when they get home. Classes that only distribute information or only discuss are excluded, so the evidence cannot control those who only listen to one lecture. What and how the public welfare parent schools in China teach vary from place to place, and may not necessarily be of this type. When choosing a class, check to see if it lasts for several weeks and allows you to practice specific methods. In the two collected experiments, common course titles are Triple P and Incredible Years. This book does not recommend specific institutions or paid products. The effect of less spanking and scolding will diminish after one or two years, and you have to continue practicing after class. The beneficiary is the child and you. If your child already has severe emotional problems, take him to a psychiatrist or child psychologist, see Article 8 (Depression Screening) in this section.

Case: In a parent training in Shanghai, parents repeatedly practiced giving clear instructions, praising promptly and yelling less. Parents with difficult-to-manage children report that their children hit others, grab toys, and contradict each other less frequently, and that their emotions are easier to stabilize.

items.title: Don’t send your children to closed-managed “Internet addiction treatment schools” and “special training camps”: The law prohibits the use of methods that harm children’s body and mind to quit Internet addiction, and some children have been imprisoned to death
items.core: The law expressly prohibits the use of methods that harm children’s body and mind to quit Internet addiction. A boy who had just been sent to a special training school in Hefei was handcuffed in a solitary room and died about 44 hours later. Nanchang Yuzhang Academy put students in solitary confinement and four people were sentenced. The parents asked for tuition compensation, but the court did not support it.
body: Cost: No money, but also save a tuition fee. The difficulty lies in the fact that when a child is at his most noisy, parents cannot resist handing him over to outsiders for "closed discipline."

Income: Article 68 of the "Law on the Protection of Minors" stipulates that no organization or individual may interfere with minors' addiction to the Internet in a way that infringes on the physical and mental health of minors. The following two cases have court decisions. The first one was in Hefei, Anhui. In August 2017, the parents of an 18-year-old boy signed an agreement with a special training school to send him to detoxify from Internet addiction. People from the school took him away by force, put him in a solitary room, and handcuffed his hands to the window bars. They restricted him from eating, drinking and resting, and also beat him. The boy died about 44 hours later. The identification concluded that high temperature, restricted position, lack of diet and trauma caused death from water and electrolyte disorders. On October 31, 2018, the Hefei Intermediate Court issued the first-instance judgment. The school director was sentenced to 16 years for intentional injury and unlawful imprisonment. The four instructors received sentences ranging from one year to eight years and six months. On December 28, 2018, the Anhui Provincial Higher Court upheld the original verdict in the second instance. The second-instance ruling stated that the school had not been approved by the relevant departments, and the defendants did not have teaching qualifications. The second case was in Nanchang, Jiangxi. Yuzhang Academy was opened in 2013 and closed in November 2017. During the school year, the school took some students into the "Depression Relief Room" and placed them in solitary confinement for three to ten days at a time. On April 28, 2023, the Anyuan District Court of Pingxiang City retried the first instance and pronounced that the five defendants were guilty of illegal detention. Four people were sentenced. Xinhua News Agency's original words were "fixed-term imprisonment ranging from two years and ten months to eleven months." These four people are also prohibited from engaging in education-related occupations within a certain period of time, and one person is exempted from criminal punishment. Parents requested compensation for tuition fees and round-trip transportation expenses, but the court did not support it (National/Anhui/Jiangxi)
Evidence level: C

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (amended in 2024). Protection of Minors (Article 68). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081818f197cf001905e567af635a0>; Red Star News (2019-02-20). Chasing hot spots: An 18-year-old boy died after being handcuffed and detained for two days, and five people from the Internet addiction treatment school were sentenced. <https://static.cdsb.com/micropub/Articles/201902/5b98283216ea5d2e8eef7f8cb7d4dbbb.html> (Web Archive <https://web.archive.org/web/20261005013030/https://static.cdsb.com/micropub/Articles/201902/5b98283216ea5d2e8eef7f8cb7d4dbbb.html>); Xinhua News Agency (2023-04-28). Jiangxi "Yuzhang Academy Case" Sentencing All five defendants accepted the verdict and did not appeal. <http://www.news.cn/2023-04/28/c_1129579126.htm> (Web archive) <http://web.archive.org/web/20230428212544/http://www.news.cn/2023-04/28/c_1129579126.htm>)

Note: It is given C because there are only individual cases and there are no statistics on the number of accidents in this type of school. There were only media reports on the Hefei case, which quoted the first-instance judgment and the second-instance ruling. The original text of the judgment could not be found on the court’s official website. The Yuzhang Academy case was reported by Xinhua News Agency as the court’s verdict. If your child loves to play games, first follow Article 14 of this section (Children love to play games) to see if sleep, homework and outing activities are squeezed out. His grades, sleep, and family relationships all collapsed, and he couldn't stop. He took his child to a psychiatrist or child psychology department for diagnosis and treatment by a doctor. Those who have been sent in, take the children back. The child said he was detained, beaten, and called the police. The beneficiary is the child.

Case: A boy in Hefei was sent to a special training school by his parents to cure his Internet addiction. He was put into a solitary room and handcuffed as soon as he arrived at the school. He died about 44 hours later. Afterwards, his family regretted it and the institution was held accountable.

items.title: Teach children to recognize the private parts of the body. If someone touches someone or is asked to keep it secret, they should go home and report it; if the child says "Let me know first, don't scold," take him to the police or a doctor.
items.core: Children who have attended sexual assault prevention classes are much more likely to take actions to protect themselves during the drill of pretending to be a stranger to seduce. What I learned is still there six months later, and the child has not become more scared. Whether it can really reduce the risk of infringement has not yet been determined. A high proportion of people who sexually abuse children are acquaintances, so they need to be taught where no one else can touch them, and if they touch or are asked to keep it secret, they should report it home.
body: Cost: No money. I usually teach you a few words when taking a bath or changing clothes, and then ask again after a while. It is difficult for parents to say that they are embarrassed to speak about body parts, and it is also difficult for parents to suppress their anger and not scold their children when they do say it.

Benefits: Cochrane in 2015 compiled 24 trials of sexual assault prevention lessons in schools, involving 5,802 pupils aged 5 to 18 years. Most of these classes teach a few things: safety rules, your body belongs to you, and what are your private parts. Also teach children what kind of touching is not allowed, what kind of secrets cannot be kept, and who to tell. Many classes also emphasize that it is not the child's fault if something goes wrong. First see if the child can protect himself. Researchers asked people to pretend to be strangers to lure children, 102 people in 2 experiments. The odds ratio for taking protective actions was OR 5.71 (95% CI 1.98–16.51, confidence range). According to the original conversion, for every 1,000 people who have not taken the class, about 390 people have achieved it, and for every 1,000 people who have taken the class, about 795 people have achieved it, which is about twice the number. Look at knowledge again. 18 trials, 4657 people, questionnaire score SMD 0.61 (0.45–0.78), 0.5 considered moderate. It is still 0.69 (0.51–0.87) half a year later. In 3 studies, 795 people saw the harm, and there was no increase or decrease in children's anxiety and fear (SMD −0.08, −0.22 to 0.07). 3 studies of 1,788 people looked at whether the child would tell. The OR for saying they had been sexually assaulted was 3.56 (1.13–11.24), changing from about 4 to about 14 per 1000 people. But children in the same class and school were similar to each other, and after correcting for this, the difference was not noticeable (OR 3.04, 0.75–12.33). The quality of the evidence was moderate for all outcomes. The author states that whether these courses can really reduce sexual assault requires long-term follow-up to know. Six United Nations agencies, including UNESCO, issued sex education guidelines in 2018. It recommends teaching children the names of body parts, including reproductive organs, between ages 5 and 8. Also teach your children which parts of the body are private. When someone touches him and makes him uncomfortable, say "no", walk away, and tell a trusted adult. The guidance states that sexual abuse is never the child’s fault. The same goes for things done by acquaintances, trusted people, or even family members. The People's Daily's Sexual Assault Prevention Handbook gives an easy-to-remember statement: No one is allowed to see or touch the areas covered by vests and shorts. Article 16 of the "Law on the Protection of Minors" requires parents to provide safety education to their children and improve their awareness and ability of self-protection. Article 40 requires schools and kindergartens to carry out sex education appropriate to the age of children. If sexual assault or harassment is discovered in schools or kindergartens, they must not conceal it and report it to the public security and education departments in a timely manner. Nine departments including the Supreme People's Procuratorate established a mandatory reporting system in 2020. Those who need to report include people from schools, kindergartens, hospitals, childcare institutions, neighborhood committees, village committees, hotels and other units. If they discover that their children have been or are suspected of being harmed at work, they must report the crime to the police immediately. Situations to be reported include: suspected abnormal injuries to the reproductive organs or private parts, suspected sexual assault, pregnancy, and miscarriage of girls under 14 years old. The reporter’s information must be kept confidential. If a dispute arises due to the report, the reporter shall not bear legal responsibility. In 2025, the procuratorate prosecuted 42,873 people for crimes of sexual assault against minors such as rape and child molestation, 5.5% less than the previous year. This represented 58.9% of crimes against minors prosecuted. Of the cases of abuse of minors prosecuted this year, 3,852, or 7.1%, had clues from mandatory reporting. The opinions of 16 departments including the Supreme People’s Court in 2025 stated that a high proportion of such cases were committed by acquaintances. Some young children lack awareness of prevention, and their guardians are negligent, and they do not even know that their children have been sexually abused (National/Multiple Countries)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Walsh K, Zwi K, Woolfenden S, Shlonsky A. (2015). School-based education programs for the prevention of child sexual abuse. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (4), CD004380. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004380.pub3>; UNESCO, UNAIDS, UNFPA, UNICEF, UN Women, WHO (2018). International technical guidance on sexuality education: an evidence-informed approach (revised edition). <https://www.unfpa.org/sites/default/files/pub-pdf/ITGSE.pdf>; Guizhou Provincial Department of Civil Affairs (2024). Minors Sexual Assault Prevention Manual, parents and children please check it out! (Reprinted from People’s Daily). <https://mzt.guizhou.gov.cn/xwzx/mzyw/202407/t20240723_85145012.html>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (amended in 2024). Law on the Protection of Minors (Articles 11, 16, and 40). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081818f197cf001905e567af635a0>; Nine departments including the Supreme People's Procuratorate (2020). Opinions on establishing a mandatory reporting system for cases of violations of minors (Trial) (Articles 2, 3, 4, 13, and 15). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202005/t20200529_463482.shtml>; Supreme People’s Procuratorate (2026). White Paper on Procuratorial Work for Minors (2025). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202606/t20260601_728630.shtml>; Guizhou Provincial Department of Civil Affairs (2025). 16 departments including the Supreme Law, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Civil Affairs jointly issued the "Opinions on Strictly Punishing and Preventing Crimes of Sexual Assault on Minors in accordance with the Law" (reprinted from the People's Court News). <https://mzt.guizhou.gov.cn/xwzx/mzyw/202508/t20250807_88423354.html>

Remarks: The number is B because the numbers are all from lessons in school. They measure knowledge and actions in drills, not how much harm has been suffered. Parents teach at home, there are no separate trials. The income is determined to be small because there are only these alternative indicators, and the number is really less than a few percent if there is no damage. The teaching method is as follows: use the original names of body parts to tell him where the private parts are. Then tell him that anyone who asks him to keep it secret and not tell his parents will have to go home and tell him, and he will not be scolded if he does. The child said, take it seriously first, don't ask if he made it up, and don't scold him. The law requires teachers and doctors to call the police if they are "suspected", and parents do not have to wait for confirmation. Tell him it's not his fault and call 110. Do not give him a bath or change of clothes before examining his injuries, see Section 13, Item 42 (After Sexual Assault). It doesn't matter who the other party is, relatives and teachers also call the police. The legal consequences if the other party is under 14 years of age, see Section 9, Article 18 (The other party is under 14 years of age). Your friend's child told you, tell his parents, and call the police together. For matters related to strange children, call 110 and hand it over to the police. Don’t go to the other party to settle the score yourself. The law states that anyone has the right to report to the police. The beneficiary is the child.

Case: The mother uses the parts covered by the swimsuit to teach her daughter boundaries, and makes an appointment with others to keep it confidential. Once, a neighbor's uncle touched her private parts and told her not to tell her. The daughter went home and told her mother. Her mother first called the police to take her for a checkup, and the matter was handled promptly.

items.title: Don’t let children under 12 years old ride bicycles on the road, and children under 16 years old ride electric bicycles on the road: if you hit someone else, your parents will pay, and you may also have to bear part of it if you are hit
items.core: You can only ride a bicycle on the road if you are 12 years old or above, and you can ride an electric bicycle only if you are 16 years old or above. A 14-year-old kid swiped his mother's ID number to ride a shared electric scooter, causing him to suffer a tenth-degree disability. The court ordered his parents to pay compensation of 187,000 yuan. If a child under age is hit by himself, even if the other party is fully responsible, some courts have ruled that the child should bear part of the responsibility.
body: Cost: No money, but you have to change the way to go to school, parents pick you up, take the bus or walk. The difficulty is that if all the classmates ride, the children will get into trouble.

Income: Article 72 of the "Road Traffic Safety Law Implementation Regulations" stipulates that "you must be 12 years or older to drive a bicycle or tricycle" on the road. The same article also stipulates that "you must be at least 16 years old to drive electric bicycles and motorized wheelchairs for disabled people." Violation will result in a warning or a fine of 5 to 50 yuan in accordance with Article 89 of the Road Traffic Safety Law. Those who do not accept the fine may have their vehicle impounded. The fine is not much, what matters is the balance after the accident. Article 1188 of the Civil Code stipulates that if a minor causes harm to others, the guardian shall bear tort liability. If the child has property of his own, compensation will be paid from his property first, and if the amount is insufficient, the guardian will compensate. The Lianjiang County Court in Fujian Province decided a case. In May 2022, the child who had just turned 14 scanned the QR code with his mother’s account and rented a shared electric bicycle. He collided with a man riding an electric bicycle, who was disabled to the tenth degree. The traffic police determined that the child was fully responsible. Rental companies and insurance companies say the user agreement requires over 16 years of age and the child is not a legal rider, so no compensation will be paid. The court awarded the child's parents 187,000 yuan in damages (accurately 187,017.83 yuan). The child himself suffers if he is hit. A judge in Beijing wrote about a case: A 10-year-old child was riding a bicycle after school and was hit by an electric bicycle and suffered a tenth degree of disability. The traffic police found that the other party was fully responsible. Article 1173 of the Civil Code stipulates that if the infringed party is at fault for the occurrence of the damage, the liability of the tortfeasor may be reduced. Based on this, the court found that the child was on the road under the age of 12 and the guardian did not stop it, and ruled that the child should bear part of the losses. The injury is also more serious. An Israeli trauma center admitted 337 children with traffic injuries from 2014 to 2016. Traumatic brain injuries accounted for 13% of those injured while riding electric bikes, and 3% while riding regular bikes. After taking other factors into account, people riding electric bicycles are more seriously injured, with an odds ratio of OR 2.56 (95% CI 1.1–5.88, credible range) (National/Fujian/Beijing/Israel)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: State Council (revised in 2017). Regulations for the Implementation of the Road Traffic Safety Law (Article 72). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f40f566c10e23>; National People’s Congress Standing Committee (amended in 2021). Road Traffic Safety Law (Article 89). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab231eb017abd617ef70519>; National People’s Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1173, 1188). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>; Guangzhou Municipal Justice Bureau (2024-11-28). A 14-year-old child riding a shared electric scooter actually hit someone and caused a tenth-level disability... (Reprinted on CCTV, etc.). <https://sfj.gz.gov.cn/ztlm/fzxc/yasf/content/post_9915896.html>（Web Archive <http://web.archive.org/web/20250421103222/https://sfj.gz.gov.cn/ztlm/fzxc/yasf/content/post_9915896.html>); Qin Pengbo (2024-08-29). How can "half-grown children" ride safely and compliantly. Beijing Politics and Law Network (Source: Beijing Law Network). <https://www.bj148.org/123/202408/t20240829_1667638.html>; Zmora O, Peleg K, Klein Y (2019). Pediatric electric bicycle injuries and comparison to other pediatric traffic injuries. Traffic injuries Injury Prevention, 20(5), 540-543. <https://doi.org/10.1080/15389588.2019.1608361>

Remarks: B is given because the law and two cases have been verified, but the number of injuries only comes from one hospital abroad, and no statistics on casualties based on age can be found in China. The Lian Jiangna case was reproduced from the legal popularization column of the Justice Bureau, and the original text of the judgment was not found. The high income was based on the compensation package of 187,000 yuan in that case. Not every accident requires such a large amount of compensation. The user agreement for shared electric bicycles also requires that people over 16 years old should not scan their account numbers for children. Wear a helmet when you are old enough to ride, see Section 1, Item 2 (Wear a helmet and buckle it up) and Section 22, Item 12 (Wear a helmet when riding a mountain bike). The beneficiaries are mainly the children, and the ones who lose money are the parents themselves.

Case: A fourteen-year-old boy swiped his mother’s account while riding a shared electric scooter. He hit a pedestrian at an intersection and suffered a tenth-degree disability. The court found that the minor was riding a bicycle and that the parents had improper management. It ordered the parents to pay compensation of 187,000 yuan, and the family was in debt for this.

items.title: If your child hits his head during exercise and then develops a headache, dizziness or confusion, do not play again that day; if he vomits again and again, becomes increasingly sleepy, and has a more severe headache, go to the emergency room immediately
items.core: Children who continue to play after a concussion take an average of 44 days to recover, and it takes about 22 days for them to leave the field. If something feels wrong after hitting your head, don’t do it again that day, and wait until the doctor says it’s okay. Continuous vomiting, getting sleepier and unable to wake up, headaches getting worse, slurred speech, and convulsions are all signs that you need to go to the emergency room immediately.
body: Cost: No money. Let the child leave the field and no longer practice or compete that day. The difficulty is that the game is busy, the child says "it's okay", and the coach and parents want him to continue.

Benefit: A concussion is a temporary disruption of brain function after a head impact, which is usually not visible on film. A U.S. study followed 69 athletes with concussions in sports, with an average age of about 15 years. The 35 guys who were dismissed had an average recovery time of 22.0 days. The 34 people who went on to get the shot with symptoms lasted an average of 44.4 days (P=0.003, unlikely to be a coincidence). For those who were beaten later, more of them delayed their recovery for more than 21 days. The original text reads "8.80 times more likely" and does not indicate which ratio it is. A consensus emerged from the 2022 Amsterdam International Sports Concussion Conference. It said that those who experience loss of consciousness, convulsions, unsteadiness, confusion, behavioral changes, or inability to remember things should be terminated immediately. These individuals should not return to competition or training that day. The exception is that experienced medical staff checked on the spot and confirmed that it was not caused by a concussion. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's guidance to parents and coaches is more direct: If you have suspicious symptoms, leave the game immediately and not play again that day until the doctor says you can play again. It also says not to judge the severity yourself, only medical staff can assess it. It lists signs that you should go to the emergency room immediately: convulsions, inability to recognize people or places, repeated nausea and vomiting, unusual behavior, and increasing confusion or agitation. After passing out, he becomes increasingly sleepy, unable to wake up, has slurred speech, and has weak or numb hands and feet. Then the headache becomes more and more severe and does not relieve, the pupils on both sides are not the same size or the vision is double (United States / many countries)
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Elbin RJ, Sufrinko A, Schatz P, et al. (2016). Removal From Play After Concussion and Recovery Time. Pediatrics, 138(3), e20160910. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2016-0910>; Patricios JS, Schneider KJ, Dvorak J, et al. (2023). Consensus statement on concussion in sport: the 6th International Conference on Concussion in Sport-Amsterdam, October 2022. British Journal of Sports Medicine, 57(11), 695-711. HEADS UP. <https://www.cdc.gov/heads-up/signs-symptoms/index.html>; CDC (2025). Signs and Symptoms of Concussion. HEADS UP. <https://www.cdc.gov/heads-up/response/index.html>

Remarks: B is given because the two groups of people who continue to play and leave the field are not divided by lot, and the number of people is small. The profit is determined to be large, based on the recovery days shortened by about half. The consensus also says that you should avoid looking at screens for the first two days and do light activities such as walking, and then gradually increase as tolerated after 24 to 48 hours. But for sports that involve the risk of collisions and falls, you have to wait for your doctor’s approval. Wearing a helmet when riding a bicycle or skiing is described in Section 22, Article 12 (Wearing a helmet when riding a mountain bike). If an old man kowtows for several weeks before problems arise, see Section 13, Item 10 (Old man kowtows too much). The beneficiary is the child.

Case: A second-year junior high school student said he was dizzy after being hit on the head by an elbow, but the coach still allowed him to continue playing in the second half. He then vomited twice and had difficulty waking up. He was sent to the emergency room and diagnosed with a concussion, and he rested for more than 40 years before resuming training.

sections.title: How many paths are there after the age of 18

items.title: Let’s first check the threshold: most of the age and academic requirements for the twelve paths are clearly written down
items.core: The thresholds for these twelve paths are mostly written in the documents. To work, you must be 16 years old, to serve as a soldier you must be 18 years old, and for college graduates you must be 24 years old. To take the civil service examination, people generally need to be between 18 and 35 years old and have a college degree or above. There is no age or education limit for self-study examination, but full-time students cannot apply. To be self-employed, one only needs to have "business ability."
body: Cost: No money. Spend ten minutes checking it out to see if you can get it.

Income: When enlisting in the army, read the Military Service Law: "Male citizens who have reached the age of 18 should be drafted for active service; those who have not been drafted that year can still be drafted for active service before they are 22 years old. The recruitment age for ordinary college graduates can be relaxed to 24 years old, and the recruitment age for graduate students can be relaxed to 26 years old." For civil servant examinations, please refer to Article 18 of the "Civil Service Recruitment Regulations". The application requirements include "age above 18 years old but below 35 years old" and "possessing a college degree or above." These two items can be adjusted appropriately with the approval of the civil service authorities at or above the provincial level. Article 19 of the regulations lists five categories of people who are not allowed to apply. For example, those who have received criminal punishment for crimes, those who have been dismissed from public office, and those who have been listed as targets of joint punishment for breach of trust. Firefighters read the "Recruitment Methods for Firefighters in the National Comprehensive Fire Rescue Team". Article 5 "Age must be between 18 years old and below 22 years old" and "have a high school education or above." Article 6 "Personnel with a college degree or above, retired soldiers of the People's Liberation Army and the Armed Police Force...the age can be relaxed to 24 years old." For military civilians, please refer to Article 9 of the "Regulations on Civilian Personnel of the Chinese People's Liberation Army". The basic conditions include "being 18 years or older." Article 19 of the regulations stipulates that the maximum age for first-time recruitment of lower-level positions is 35 years old. Lower grade positions are entry-level positions. For public institutions, read Article 8 of the "Personnel Management Regulations for Public Institutions" "Public institutions shall recruit new staff members through open recruitment to the public." For self-employed individuals, please refer to the "Regulations on Promoting the Development of Individual Industrial and Commercial Households", "Citizens with business capabilities... who register as individual industrial and commercial households in accordance with the law shall apply to these regulations." For self-study exams, please refer to the "Interim Regulations on Self-Study Examinations for Higher Education". Article 3 "Citizens of the People's Republic of China, regardless of gender, age, nationality, race or education level, may participate in self-study examinations for higher education in accordance with the provisions of these regulations." Article 20: "Students in full-time schools of all levels and types are not allowed to apply." Publicly funded normal school students should read Article 2 of the "Implementation Measures for Publicly Funded Education for Normal University Students Directly Affiliated to the Ministry of Education." It only recruits students at six normal universities affiliated to the ministry. They are Beijing Normal University, East China Normal University, Northeast Normal University, Central China Normal University, Shaanxi Normal University and Southwest University. The undergraduate and postgraduate stages are designed in an integrated manner and assessed in stages. After completing the undergraduate program, you can continue to study as a graduate student. The tuition and accommodation fees during the school period are borne by the central government, and living expenses subsidies are also provided. Article 5 of the Measures "Recruits public-funded normal school students and implements early batch admission", which means that students are admitted before the regular batch. Oriented medical students read the "Notice on the Employment Placement and Contract Performance Management of Rural Order-Based Free Training Medical Students". It reads: "After admission and before receiving the admission notice, an agreement must be signed with the county-level health administrative department...the human resources and social security department where the training school and targeted employment are located." If you want to work abroad, please read the Regulations on the Administration of Foreign Labor Cooperation. Article 5: To engage in foreign labor service cooperation, business qualifications must be obtained with the approval of the competent commerce department. Paragraph 4 of Article 7: "No foreign labor service cooperation enterprise shall engage in foreign labor service cooperation without obtaining the foreign labor service cooperation qualification certificate and registering it in accordance with the law." It is illegal for a company without this qualification certificate to organize people to work abroad. Paragraph 2 of Article 8: "No unit or individual may organize laborers to work abroad in the name of business, tourism, study abroad, etc." There is no legal academic qualification threshold for platform acceptance of orders and flexible employment. The basis for self-insurance and occupational injury protection is provided in Articles 11 and 12 of this section. The Compulsory Education Law for Part-time Workers: "Employers are prohibited from recruiting children and teenagers of school age who should receive compulsory education." Article 2 of the "Provisions on the Prohibition of Child Labor" states that persons under the age of 16 shall not be employed. For penalties, see Section 23, Article 1 (under 16 years of age).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (2021). Military Service Law (Article 20). <http://www.mod.gov.cn/regulatory/2021-08/20/content_4892491.htm> (published by the Ministry of National Defense); Organization Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (2019). Civil Service Recruitment Regulations (Articles 18 and 19). <https://www.12371.cn/2020/01/08/ARTI1578447606460158.shtml> (published on the Communist Party Member Network); Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, Ministry of Emergency Management (2021). Recruitment Methods for Firefighters in the National Comprehensive Fire Rescue Team (Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security [2021] No. 58, Articles 5 and 6). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-08/27/content_5633684.htm>; State Council, Central Military Commission (2022). Regulations on Civilian Personnel of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (Second Revision, Order No. 757, Articles 9 and 19). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181857bca5e01859ee5a6c06d62> (National Laws and Regulations Database); State Council (2014). Regulations on Personnel Management of Public Institutions (State Council Order No. 652, Article 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2014-05/15/content_8810.htm>; State Council (2022). Regulations on Promoting the Development of Individual Industrial and Commercial Households (State Council Order No. 755, Article 2). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-10/25/content_5721592.htm>; State Council (Revised in 1988, 2014). Interim Regulations on Higher Education Self-Study Examinations (Articles 3 and 20). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f415d64e5236d> (National Laws and Regulations Database); National People’s Congress Standing Committee (2018). Compulsory Education Law (Article 14). <http://www.moe.gov.cn/jyb_sjzl/sjzl_zcfg/zcfg_jyfl/202110/t20211029_575949.html> (published by the Ministry of Education); State Council (2002). Regulations prohibiting the use of child labor (State Council Order No. 364, Article 2). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_61798.htm>; General Office of the State Council (2024). Notice on forwarding the "Implementation Measures for Publicly Funded Education for Normal University Students Directly Affiliated to the Ministry of Education" by the Ministry of Education and other departments (Guobanfa [2024] No. 27, Articles 2 and 5). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202406/content_6957261.htm>; National Health Commission and 7 other departments (2019). Notice on the employment placement and contract performance management of targeted and free training of medical students in rural areas. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-11/13/content_5451684.htm>; State Council (2012). Regulations on the Administration of Foreign Labor Cooperation (State Council Order No. 620, Articles 5, 7 and 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-06/11/content_1091.htm>

Note: There are also some roads whose thresholds are not written down. The regulations of public institutions only require open recruitment. Please refer to each recruitment announcement for age and education. There is no legal academic qualification threshold for accepting orders on the platform. The age and academic qualifications for civil servants can be adjusted with the approval of the competent authorities at or above the provincial level. After reaching the threshold, you still have to pass the political conditions, physical examination and political assessment. There are no public scoring standards for these levels, and they cannot be found in the regulations. The entrance to the comprehensive enrollment of secondary vocational schools, technical colleges and vocational education is provided in Section 23, Item 5, and the subsidy when the family cannot afford it is provided in Section 23, Item 4. Being self-employed does not depend on academic qualifications, which does not mean that it is easy to open a store. Capital, personal guarantees and closing costs are provided in Section 12. A personal guarantee means that if the company doesn't repay it, you have to pay it back yourself. Whether you can borrow a loan with the state providing part of the interest for you to start with, see Article 16 of this section. The terms of public-funded normal school students and targeted medical students were decided on the day they filled in their application for the college entrance examination, and the price was written in Article 13. The threshold for working abroad does not lie with you, but with the company's qualifications. How do you understand Article 14? Which path is more cost-effective? I won’t compare each path for you. I only list the threshold and cost. You have to calculate it according to your own situation.

Case: A 17-year-old secondary vocational school student wanted to apply for a labor position, join the army and be a civil servant. After checking the announcement, he found that: you can apply for a part-time job if you are over 16 years old. Males must be over 18 to join the army. Most civil servants must be between 18 and 35 years old and have a college degree or above. He first chose a path that he could study in, and then supplemented his academic qualifications.

items.title: You must register for military service before October 31st of the year you turn 18; a compulsory soldier must serve in active service for two years
items.core: Military service registration is a legal obligation. It does not mean signing up to join the army, and registration does not mean you will go. Males who are over 18 years old must register online before October 31. If you do not register, the county will order you to make corrections within a time limit. If you do not make corrections, you will be forced to perform military service and fined. If you really join the army, you will have to serve in active service for two years.
body: Cost: No money. Registration is filled out online once and it takes just a few minutes. If you really join the army, the price will be two years of full-time service. During these two years, you won't be able to do anything else at the same time.

Benefits: To register, please refer to the "Regulations on Military Service Registration". It reads: “The military service agencies of the people’s governments of counties, autonomous counties, cities without districts, and municipal districts shall, before October 31 of each year, organize male citizens in their respective administrative regions who have reached the age of 18 before December 31 of that year to register for initial military service.” The same regulation also states: "Initial military service registration is mainly carried out through online registration, and is completed independently by citizens through the military service registration online platform." What will happen if you don’t register? See Article 57, Paragraph 1 of the Military Service Law. This section governs "those who refuse or evade military service registration." The punishment is "the county-level people's government shall order them to make corrections within a time limit; if they fail to make corrections within the time limit, the county-level people's government will force them to perform military service obligations and impose a fine." Article 15 of the Military Service Law stipulates that the first-time military service registration targets "male citizens who have reached the age of 18 before December 31 of each year." Paragraph 2 of Article 20 reads, “Based on the needs of the military, female citizens may be recruited for active service in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.” Article 15 of the "Regulations on Military Service Registration" states that "according to the needs of the military... qualified female citizens may be organized to register for reserve service." The Military Service Law also states that "the period of active service for compulsory soldiers is two years." "Citizens aged 17 or over but under 18 may be recruited for active service based on the needs of the military and their own volition." Sergeants who “have served in active service for twelve years or meet other conditions stipulated by the state shall be assigned work by the local people’s government at or above the county level in the resettlement area.” Non-commissioned officers “who have served in active service for thirty years or have reached the age of fifty-five or who meet other conditions stipulated by the state shall be placed for retirement.” Job arrangement means giving a job by the government, and retirement arrangement means retiring according to the retirement plan. The "Regulations on Military Recruitment" states that "priority shall be ensured for the recruitment of soldiers who are graduates of ordinary colleges and universities and have special requirements for political, physical conditions or professional skills." The regulations also state that "citizens who are full-time students or recent graduates of ordinary colleges and universities can apply at the place of residence or school location before enrollment" (National)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: General Office of the State Council, General Office of the Central Military Commission (2025). Regulations on Military Service Registration (Guobanfa [2025] No. 41). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202512/content_7051363.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Military Service Law (revised in 2021, Articles 15, 20, 25, 26, 54, and 57). <http://www.mod.gov.cn/regulatory/2021-08/20/content_4892491.htm> (published by the Ministry of National Defense); State Council, Central Military Commission (2023). Regulations on Recruitment (State Council, Central Military Commission Order No. 759, Article 5). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2023/content_5753313.htm>

Note: Registration and application are two different things, and the costs are quite different. The series of punishments of not being allowed to leave the country for two years are only punishable for those who renege after being drafted, see Article 3 (Rejection of Military Service). According to the law, only men are eligible for initial military service registration. Women are recruited according to the needs of the army, and they can also register for reserve service according to the needs of the army. The conditions for soldiers to pass military academies and for soldiers who perform well to become officers (promotion) are all written in the internal regulations of the army and cannot be found outside. The Military Service Law contains only two sentences: Active-duty officers are selected from "active-duty soldiers with outstanding performance" and other personnel, and military academies recruit students without age restrictions. The specific score lines and quotas are not given in this book.

Case: After Xiao Li turned 18, he logged into the National Military Recruitment Network to complete military service registration before October 31 of that year. He only registered but did not sign up to join the army. The system generated a record and the Ministry of Human Resources informed him that his military service registration obligation had been completed and he was not required to join the army.

items.title: If you refuse to perform military service after being drafted, you will not be allowed to leave the country or return to school within two years, and you will not be able to join civil servants or state-owned enterprises.
items.core: Those who sign up but refuse to join the military and refuse to change even after being ordered to do so will have a series of consequences. Civil servants cannot hire you, nor can state-owned enterprises and public institutions recruit you. They will not be allowed to leave the country within two years, and will not be allowed to enter or resume school. They will also be included in the list of persons who have seriously dishonestly performed their national defense obligations. So don’t sign up with the idea of ​​“submit it first and then take it back, if it doesn’t work, then return it.”
body: Cost: No money. The price is that before signing up, you have to think clearly about whether to go or not.

Income: Item 2 of Article 57, Paragraph 1, of the Military Service Law refers to "Citizens who are drafted and refuse or evade recruitment to serve in active service." The punishment is also "the people's government at the county level shall order them to make corrections within a time limit; if they fail to make corrections within the time limit, the people's government at the county level will force them to perform their military service obligations and impose a fine." Paragraph 2 of the same article: "Anyone who commits the second act of the previous paragraph and refuses to correct it shall not be employed as a civil servant or a staff member managed in accordance with the Civil Servant Law of the People's Republic of China. He shall not be recruited or employed as a staff member of a state-owned enterprise or public institution. He shall not be allowed to leave the country or return to school within two years. He shall be included in the list of seriously dishonest persons in the performance of national defense obligations and subject to joint punishment." Joint punishment means that multiple departments use the same list to jointly implement the above restrictions. Article 58: The same set of punishments shall be imposed on those who have already joined the army. If a soldier refuses to perform his duties or flees the army with the purpose of evading military service, the consequences will depend on the outcome. Anyone who is removed from the military, expelled from the military, or held criminally responsible in accordance with the law shall be punished in accordance with Article 57, paragraph 2. Those who are removed from the list will also be fined (nationwide, effective from October 1, 2021)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: National People's Congress Standing Committee (2021). Military Service Law (revised in 2021, Articles 57 and 58). <http://www.mod.gov.cn/regulatory/2021-08/20/content_4892491.htm> (Published by the Ministry of National Defense)

Note: What is counted here is personal freedom and employment qualifications, not money. This series of punishments only punishes two types of people. One type is "citizens who are drafted and refuse to evade conscription and serve in active service." The other type is those who were removed from the military, expelled from the military, and held criminally responsible after joining the army. Those who have not registered for military service are not included. Please see Article 2 for military service registration. The prerequisite for punishment is "refusal to correct", which will be determined and punished by the county-level people's government. Each locality decides how much the fine should be, and this book will not write about it. It’s up to you whether you want to go or not, but you have to decide before signing up.

Case: A college student voluntarily enlisted in the army. After passing the physical examination, he refused to report because he was afraid of hardship. The army and the county People's Armed Forces Department repeatedly tried to persuade him to no avail. Later, he was notified that he was not allowed to return to school, was not allowed to take the civil service examination for state-owned enterprises, and was not allowed to leave the country for two years.

items.title: Two of the most practical benefits for college students to serve in the military are: tuition reimbursement of up to 20,000 yuan per year, student status retained for two years after retirement, and special plans for postgraduate entrance examinations
items.core: If current students, recent graduates and freshmen serve in the military, the state will pay for your tuition for the years of study. The maximum annual allowance for undergraduate students is 20,000 yuan, and the maximum annual allowance for graduate students is 25,000 yuan, whichever is higher is the actual tuition fee or student loan. Students will retain their academic status during the military service and can return to school within two years after retirement. There is also a special plan to recruit only retired college students and soldiers for the postgraduate entrance examination.
body: Cost: No money. After retiring, submit application materials as required by the school and make one or two trips.

Benefits: The Ministry of Finance and four other departments announced in 2024 that college students who serve in the military will receive three benefits: tuition compensation, reimbursement of national student loans for tuition, and tuition exemptions. Reimbursement means that the state pays off the student loan for you. These three standards "are accordingly adjusted to a maximum of 20,000 yuan per year for undergraduate students and a maximum of 25,000 yuan per year for graduate students." The new standards will be implemented starting in the fall semester of 2024. The exact amount of the subsidy depends on this sentence: "It shall be based on the higher amount of the tuition fees actually paid by the students or the national student loans obtained (including the principal and the interest accrued before full repayment)." There is another sentence at the end that "No compensation, compensation or reduction will be given for parts exceeding the standard." Therefore, for the money you get every year, first take the higher one between the actual tuition fees and student loans, and then compare it with the upper limit and take the smaller one. If the tuition is 5,000 yuan per year, the supplement will be 5,000 yuan. The number of additional years is calculated based on the number of years of study, not the number of years of service. The 2019 Student Financial Aid Fund Management Regulations read: “If you complete the prescribed number of years of study before enlisting in the military, you will be entitled to tuition compensation or national student loan reimbursement; if you complete the remaining prescribed number of years of study after retiring from the army and return to school, you will be entitled to tuition exemption.” When fresh graduates go to serve in the military, they have to pay the tuition for the entire academic period. For student status, please refer to the Veterans Protection Act. It reads: "Active-duty military personnel who have been admitted to ordinary colleges and universities before joining the army or are students studying in ordinary colleges and universities will retain their admission qualifications or student status during active service. They are allowed to enroll or resume school within two years after retirement. They can transfer to other majors in the school in accordance with relevant national regulations." The law also states: "In accordance with the overall arrangements of the state, colleges and universities may recruit retired military personnel through separate plans, separate enrollment, etc." For the postgraduate entrance examination, please refer to the 2026 notice of the General Office of the Ministry of Education. This program is called the "Retired College Soldier Program." The notice reads: "It is issued separately and used specifically within the overall scale of the national master's degree enrollment plan. It cannot be adjusted to the general plan or other special plans. The admissions unit determines independently...the preliminary examination score requirements (generally not higher than the preliminary examination score requirements for candidates in the general program of the corresponding disciplines and majors of the unit)...candidates who have served for a long time under the same conditions will be given priority for admission." Separate row and special use means that these quotas are set aside separately and can only be used to recruit retired college students and soldiers. This plan will be undertaken by 532 ordinary colleges and universities in 2026 (nationwide)
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, People's Bank of China, State Administration of Financial Supervision (2024). Notice on adjusting and improving policies related to national student loans (Caijiao [2024] No. 188). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202411/content_6984812.htm>; Five departments including the Ministry of Finance (2019).
