Falagas ME, Vouloumanou EK, Plessa E, Peppas G, Rafailidis PI (2010). Inaccuracies in dosing drugs with teaspoons and tablespoons. International Journal of Clinical Practice, 64(9):1185-1189. Yin HS, Dreyer BP, Ugboaja DC, et al. (2014). Unit of measurement used and parent medication dosing errors. Pediatrics, 134(2):e354-e361. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2014-0395>

Note: Metamizole is not the drug of choice for adults. The instructions state that it may cause agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia and anaphylactic shock, and should only be used short-term when the condition is severe and there are no other effective drugs. The name of Zhongqingling sounds like ordinary cold medicine, and it contains metamizole. Ask your pediatrician or pharmacist what antipyretics your child should take and how much should he take according to his body weight. If a child under 3 months old has a fever, go directly to the hospital. See Section 20, Article 8 (go directly to the hospital if the temperature is 38°C). The number B is determined because the figures for Reye's syndrome come from surveillance reports, and the reduction in cases and the issuance of warnings are related to each other, not controlled trials. The benefit is set to be "large" because cases dropped from 555 to less than 36 per year after the warning.

Case: A two-year-old child had a fever, and the parents fed him aspirin as recommended by the elder. The child soon developed vomiting and drowsiness. He was sent to the hospital and diagnosed with Reye's syndrome. He was rescued before he was out of danger. During the follow-up visit, the doctor emphasized that children can only use acetaminophen or ibuprofen to reduce fever.

items.title: For those over 60 years old, who have had gastric bleeding, and are taking anticoagulants or hormones, ask your doctor before taking painkillers such as ibuprofen
items.core: Painkillers such as ibuprofen, naproxen, and aspirin can damage the stomach. In high-dose trials, people who took ibuprofen had about four times the risk of gastric bleeding and perforation than those who didn't take it. People who are older, have had stomach bleeding, are taking anticoagulants or hormones, and drink more than three drinks a day are at higher risk.
body: Cost: No money. Ask your doctor or pharmacist once.

Benefits: This type of medicine is called non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and the common ones are ibuprofen, naproxen, and diclofenac. A meta-analysis compiled 280 randomized trials of these drugs versus placebo, involving 124,513 people. Relative risk of upper gastrointestinal perforation, obstruction, or bleeding compared with placebo: RR 3.97 (95% CI 2.22–7.10, approximately 4 times) for ibuprofen, 4.22 (2.71–6.56) for naproxen, and 1.89 (1.16–3.09) for diclofenac. All such drugs roughly double the risk of heart failure. U.S. regulations require such over-the-counter drugs to carry a stomach bleeding warning. The drugs listed in the warning are "aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen" (aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen). The warning lists six types of people who are at higher risk: those over 60 years old, who have had gastric ulcers or bleeding, who are taking anticoagulants or hormones and other such drugs at the same time, who drink more than three glasses of wine a day while taking the medicine, and who eat more or for longer than prescribed.
Level of Evidence: A

Source: Coxib and traditional NSAID Trialists' (CNT) Collaboration; Bhala N, Emberson J, Merhi A, et al. (2013). Vascular and upper gastrointestinal effects of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: meta-analyses of individual participant data from randomized trials. Lancet, 382(9894):769-779. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(13)60900-9>; 21 CFR 201.326(a)(2)(iii)(A) Stomach bleeding warning. <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-201/subpart-G/section-201.326>

Note: The conclusion of the paper talks about high-dose usage. This article does not give a separate figure for the risks of taking it occasionally for a day or two and taking the dosage according to the instructions. Many compound cold medicines also contain this type of ingredient. If you take them with analgesics, it will be repetitive. Look at the ingredient list first. The doctor has asked you to take low-dose aspirin for a long time to prevent blood clots. Don't stop it yourself, and don't add another painkiller yourself. People with poor kidney function should take this type of medicine, see Article 14 of this section (poor kidney function). How to use this kind of medicine for dysmenorrhea and when to go to a gynecologist for examination, see Section 3, Item 25 (Take painkillers such as ibuprofen for dysmenorrhea).

Case: A 68-year-old man had a history of gastric bleeding. He bought ibuprofen and took it on his own because of joint pain. Half a month later, he vomited blood and black stool and was hospitalized again. Doctors point out that this type of painkillers can significantly increase the risk of gastric bleeding, and people with a history of gastric disease must consult a doctor before taking the medicine.

items.title: If children under 2 years old have a cold, do not give yourself compound cold medicines and cough medicines
items.core: The State Food and Drug Administration requires 14 types of compound cold medicines for children to add warnings. The warning states that parents are not recommended to use it on their own for children under 2 years old and should use it under the guidance of a doctor or pharmacist. In experiments on children, cough suppressants and anti-allergy medicines were no better than placebos.
body: Cost: No money, and you can save money on medicines.

Income: Announcement No. 57 of the State Food and Drug Administration in 2021 has revised the instructions for 14 varieties, including acetaminophen Mami oral solution, pediatric acetaminophen xanthanamine granules, pediatric acetaminophen alkamine granules, etc. The new warning is "It is not recommended that parents or guardians use this product on their own for infants and young children under 2 years old. It should be used under the guidance of a physician or pharmacist." The precautions are added: "Usage should be strictly in accordance with the instructions and dosage of the drug to avoid overdose." It also added that "the combined use of anti-cold drugs containing the same or similar active ingredients should be avoided." A Cochrane review included 29 randomized controlled trials, 10 of which were conducted in children. In trials with children, none of these drugs were better than placebo: cough suppressants, antihistamines (allergy-fighting ingredients), antihistamines plus decongestants (nose-clearing ingredients), and cough suppressants plus bronchodilators. Adverse effects were reported in 21 studies, more often with formulations containing antihistamines and dextromethorphan.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Announcement of the State Food and Drug Administration on revising the instructions for 14 types of drugs including Aminophen Asami Oral Solution (No. 57, 2021) and attachments. <https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/directory/web/nmpa/xxgk/ggtg/ypggtg/ypshmshxdgg/20210423105404141.html>; Smith SM, Schroeder K, Fahey T (2014). Over-the-counter (OTC) medications for acute cough in children and adults in community settings. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (11):CD001831. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001831.pub5>

Note: This 14 Many species have "aminophenol" in their names and also contain acetaminophen. If taken together with antipyretics, the situation is repeated. See Article 1 of this section (acetaminophen). One trial in that review found honey to be better than placebo, but honey should not be given to children under 1 year of age, see Section 20, Item 6 (Honey). The rating of B is because there are few trials of each drug category in the review, and the authors did not combine the numbers. The "medium" profit rating is based on judgment: this type of medicine has no proven benefits for children, and the main risks are overdose and duplication of ingredients.

Case: When a parent saw a one-and-a-half-year-old child with runny nose and cough, he gave him compound cold medicine. The child then became abnormally lethargic and refused to eat. After seeking medical treatment, the doctor explained that such drugs are prohibited for children under 2 years old. The antitussive ingredients are not effective for children and may damage their nerves.

items.title: Do not take painkillers such as ibuprofen after 20 weeks of pregnancy
items.core: Taking ibuprofen after 20 weeks of pregnancy may damage the fetus's kidneys and reduce the amniotic fluid. Among such reports received in the United States, there are cases of neonatal death. Low-dose aspirin prescribed by your doctor is not included.
body: Cost: No money.

Benefits: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a safety alert in October 2020. Taking NSAIDs after about 20 weeks of pregnancy may cause fetal kidney problems, leading to oligohydramnios. The warning covers both prescription and over-the-counter medicines, including aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac, and celecoxib. The FDA reviewed adverse event reports through July 2017 and found 35 cases of oligohydramnios or neonatal renal insufficiency, all with serious outcomes. Five of the neonatal deaths occurred, all with neonatal renal failure. In the literature, most cases of oligohydramnios resolve within 72 hours to 6 days after drug withdrawal. The FDA recommends that pregnant women not use these drugs after 20 weeks of pregnancy unless specifically advised so by their doctor. Low-dose aspirin (81 mg) prescribed by a doctor to treat specific problems during pregnancy is exempt from this restriction. When you need to relieve pain and reduce fever, the FDA mentioned that other drugs such as acetaminophen can be used. Please ask your pharmacist or doctor first.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2020-10-15). FDA recommends avoiding use of NSAIDs in pregnancy at 20 weeks or later because they can result in low amniotic fluid. Drug Safety Communication. <https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-recommends-avoiding-use-nsaids-pregnancy-20-weeks-or-later-because-they-can-result-low-amniotic>

Note: FDA reminds that many over-the-counter medicines for colds, flu, and insomnia also contain these ingredients. Please read the ingredient list. U.S. over-the-counter drug labels originally only warned about the last three months of pregnancy, but this time the limit has been moved up to about 20 weeks. Low-dose aspirin to prevent preeclampsia, see Section 27, Item 5 (Low-dose aspirin). The reason for setting B is that the number comes from adverse event reports, and we don’t know how many people took the medicine without any accidents. The "medium" income is a judgment: the outcome is serious, but it occurs rarely.

Case: A pregnant woman who was 24 weeks pregnant took ibuprofen on her own due to headache. The prenatal examination found that the amniotic fluid was low and the fetal kidney function indicators were abnormal. After emergency discontinuation of the medication, she followed the doctor's advice for monitoring. The doctor said that taking this kind of medicine after 20 weeks of pregnancy may damage the fetal kidneys and the risk is extremely high.

items.title: Buy omeprazole yourself for acid reflux and heartburn, and take it for up to 7 days; if you have difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools, go directly to the hospital
items.core: Omeprazole enteric-coated tablets can be purchased without a prescription starting in 2022, but the instructions state that you should not take it for more than 7 days, and do not take it again within two months. Do not eat if you have difficulty or pain swallowing, vomiting blood, bloody or dark stools, as these may be signs of something serious. This medicine may also mask the symptoms of gastric cancer and delay diagnosis.
body: Cost: No money. Eat according to the number of days in the instructions.

Benefits: The State Food and Drug Administration’s Announcement No. 68 of 2022 converted omeprazole enteric-coated tablets from a prescription drug to an over-the-counter drug, and also released a sample instruction manual. The indications written in the template are "short-term relief of heartburn and acid reflux symptoms caused by hyperacidity." Notes: Do not use for more than 7 days. If symptoms are not relieved, consult a physician or pharmacist. Do not take it again within two months. If symptoms recur, seek medical attention immediately. Do not use if you have difficulty or pain swallowing, vomiting blood, bloody or dark stools, as these may be signs of a serious condition. When alarm symptoms such as obvious weight loss, repeated vomiting, difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood or melena occur, malignant tumors must be ruled out first. The reason is that treatment may mask symptoms and delay diagnosis. If you are over 55 and develop new or changing symptoms, talk to your doctor. People taking clopidogrel should avoid taking omeprazole at the same time. For the reason, please refer to the instructions for clopidogrel (Plavix) in the United States. Omeprazole inhibits the enzyme (CYP2C19) that converts clopidogrel in the body. The instructions read "omeprazole was shown to reduce significantly the antiplatelet activity of Plavix when given concomitantly or 12 hours apart." When the two drugs are taken at the same time or 12 hours apart, the anti-thrombotic effect of clopidogrel is significantly weakened. These instructions are written for acute coronary syndrome, recent myocardial infarction, recent stroke, and peripheral artery disease.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Announcement of the State Food and Drug Administration on the conversion of prescription drugs of Omeprazole Enteric-coated Tablets into over-the-counter drugs (No. 68, 2022) and Appendix 2 "Model Instructions for Over-the-Counter Drugs". <https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/yaopin/ypggtg/20220826171517123.html>; Sanofi-Aventis U.S. (2025). PLAVIX (clopidogrel) tablets, US prescribing information, sections 1, 5 and 7 (DailyMed). <https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=de8b0b67-eb25-4684-83b5-7ad785314227>

Note: Clopidogrel is an anti-thrombotic drug, commonly used by people who have suffered from myocardial infarction and stroke. Omeprazole will weaken it, so people who take it should ask their doctor first. The reason for setting B is that these are the provisions of the manual. There is no research to calculate how many things can be avoided if you follow them. The “medium” benefit is based on judgment: it prevents gastric bleeding and gastric cancer, but most acid reflux and heartburn are not serious. For the practice of going to the emergency room on the same day as melena or vomiting blood, see Section 13, Article 49 (Tarry).

Case: Mr. Wang, a citizen, suffered from acid reflux and heartburn. He bought omeprazole and took it for half a month. His symptoms fluctuated but he did not seek medical treatment. Later, a gastroscopy was performed to detect early-stage gastric cancer. The doctor said that taking this kind of medicine for a long time would mask the symptoms, and self-medication should never exceed 7 days.

items.title: Don’t ask the doctor for antibiotics when you have a common cold
items.core: Taking antibiotics for a cold is no better than not taking them at all. For adults who take it, the risk of side effects is more than twice as high as if they don't take it. If the runny nose has been present for less than 10 days, there is no definite benefit from taking antibiotics.
body: Cost: No money, and you can save money on medicine.

Benefits: A Cochrane systematic review summarizing 6 randomized trials, 1147 people. There was no significant difference in the proportion of colds that did not improve or persisted when taking antibiotics and taking placebo (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.60–1.14, the difference was not significant). The risk of adverse effects was 1.8 times greater than in the placebo group (95% CI 1.01–3.21). Among them, the increase was 2.62 times in adults (1.32–5.18), and there was no increase in children (0.91, 0.51–1.63). For acute purulent rhinitis with purulent nasal discharge lasting less than 10 days, antibiotics have no clear benefit (RR 0.73, 0.47–1.13). There were more adverse reactions (RR 1.46, 1.10–1.94, approximately 46% higher). The authors concluded that routine antibiotic use is not recommended in either case.
Level of Evidence: A
Source: Kenealy T, Arroll B (2025). Antibiotics for the common cold and acute purulent rhinitis. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 11:CD000247. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000247.pub4>

Note: This edition is 2025 If it was republished in 2013, the abstract states that the literature search ended in 2013. Antibiotics are prescription drugs in China, and pharmacies must sell them with a prescription. Don’t take any antibiotics left at home for your own consumption. The "medium" income setting is a judgment: it prevents adverse reactions, not death. Do not ask for infusion if you have a cold, see Section 6, Article 35 (Ask for infusion if you have a cold or fever).

Case: He had a common cold at work and the patient forced the doctor to initiate sporulation. After three days of infusion, not only did the cold not improve, but he also developed severe diarrhea. He was diagnosed with antibiotic-related intestinal flora disorder. He gradually recovered after stopping the medication for a week.

items.title: If you have diarrhea, drink oral rehydration salt first to rehydrate. Children under 5 years old are not given antidiarrheal medicine
items.core: The most important thing for diarrhea is rehydration, not antidiarrhea. Drink oral rehydration salts mixed with water according to the instructions. Do not use fruit drinks instead. Too sweet will make people more dehydrated. If children under 5 years old are not given antidiarrheal drugs such as loperamide, severe intestinal obstruction may occur, which may be fatal.
body: Cost: A box of oral rehydration salts costs a few yuan to more than ten yuan. Keep a box at home.

Benefits: The World Health Organization's Diarrhea Treatment Manual states that "antidiarrheal" drugs and antiemetics have no practical benefit for acute or persistent diarrhea in children. They do not prevent dehydration or improve nutrition. The original words of the Chinese version of the manual are "Some medicines have dangerous and sometimes fatal side effects. These medicines should never be used in children under 5 years of age." Drugs like loperamide that slow down intestinal motility can cause severe paralytic ileus, which can be fatal, and can prolong infection. The manual also states that drinks with too much sugar, such as soft drinks and commercial fruit drinks, will absorb water from the body into the intestines, causing high-sodium dehydration. The WHO manual recommends a hypotonic formula with a total osmotic pressure of 245 mOsm/L. It resulted in 33% fewer unscheduled intravenous infusions compared to the old formula. A Cochrane review summarized 8 trials with similar results (odds ratio OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.45–0.79).
Level of Evidence: A

Source: World Health Organization (2005). The treatment of diarrhoea: a manual for physicians and other senior health workers, 4th revision. Oral rehydration solution for treating dehydration caused by acute diarrhoea in children. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (1):CD002847. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002847>

Note: When buying, read the osmotic pressure on the instructions and choose a low-osmotic formula. The handbook states that children with blood in their stools are most likely to have bacillary dysentery, and that they need to see a doctor for antibiotics instead of just rehydrating them at home. Determining the income as "middle" is a judgment: the number in your hand compares two types of rehydration salts, not drinking or not drinking.

Case: A 4-year-old child had diarrhea. The parents gave the child oral rehydration salt according to the instructions without giving antidiarrheal medicine. Three days later, the child's dehydration symptoms disappeared and the diarrhea improved. Another parent in the same community gave his 2-year-old child antidiarrheal medicine, which caused intestinal obstruction and sent the child to the hospital.

items.title: When you have a headache, don’t take painkillers for 15 days a month, and don’t take compound painkillers for 10 days, otherwise the headache may be caused by the medicines
items.core: If you have a recurring headache, take painkillers every day, and the pain may become worse the more you take them. The International Headache Classification calls this medication overuse headache. Pain for more than 15 days in a month, taking ordinary analgesics for more than 15 days or compound painkillers for more than 10 days, for more than 3 months, is enough to make a diagnosis. Most people get better after they stop taking too many medications.
body: Cost: No money. You should remember the number of days you need to take medicine, and you should also refrain from taking it casually.

Benefits: The 3rd edition of the International Classification of Headache Disorders of the International Headache Society gives diagnostic criteria: people who have original headaches have headaches for more than 15 days per month and regularly overdose on headache medications for more than 3 months. For non-opioid painkillers such as acetaminophen, aspirin, and ibuprofen, the overdose threshold is 15 days or more per month. The threshold for compounded painkillers is 10 days or more per month. Compound analgesics refer to two or more types of drugs that have analgesic effects combined, or with the addition of auxiliary ingredients such as caffeine, such as acetaminophen plus codeine. Several non-opioid analgesics are taken in rotation, and the number of days is added up. The classification description states that epidemiological evidence from many countries shows that more than half of people who suffer from headaches for more than 15 days per month have this type of headache. Most patients get better when they stop taking the overdose medication, and treatments to prevent headaches are more effective.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Headache Classification Committee of the International Headache Society (2018). The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition. Cephalalgia, 38(1):1-211. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0333102417738202>; ICHD-3 Online Edition 8.2 Medication-overuse headache (including 8.2.3, 8.2.5). <https://ichd-3.org/8-headache-attributed-to-a-substance-or-its-withdrawal/8-2-medication-overuse-headache-moh/>

Note: Painkillers with the word "caffeine" in the drug name generally add caffeine, and are calculated as a compound for 10 days. If you have more and more headache days in a month, go to a neurologist instead of just adding more medicine. The reason for setting B is that the classification standards give diagnostic thresholds, not controlled tests. The "medium" income is a judgment call: it buys you less headaches and does not involve death.

Case: Ms. Liu took painkillers whenever she had a headache. She took them for about 20 days a month for the past three months. Later, she had pain almost every day. The neurology department diagnosed her with medication overuse headache and asked her to stop taking too many medications. After two months, the number of headache days decreased significantly. Doctors say that taking compound painkillers more than ten days a month is more likely to cause the disease.

items.title: Regularly clear out expired medicines and unused leftover medicines, and throw the packaging into hazardous trash cans. Do not leave them at home.
items.core: In the United States, nearly half of the medicines accidentally taken by adults on children's backs are prescription pills. About 30% of prescription drugs accidentally taken were from grandparents. By clearing out unused medicine, there will be one less thing for children to dig into. The cleared medicines and packaging should be thrown into hazardous waste bins or handed over to pharmacies that collect used medicines.
body: Cost: Nothing. Go through the medicine box once a year for ten minutes.

Income: U.S. emergency department surveillance data estimates that from 2004 to 2013, children under the age of 6 accidentally took medicines behind the back of adults and visited approximately 640,000 emergency departments (estimated value: 640,161 times). About 59,000 times a year in 2013 (59,092 times). From 2010 to 2013, the most common was oral prescription tablets, accounting for 45.9%. The most commonly prescribed drugs were opioid analgesics (13.8%) and benzodiazepine sedatives (12.7%). Five poison control centers in the United States asked parents who called for help in 2017. Among children who mistakenly took prescription drugs, 30.7% took the drugs from their grandparents. More than half (51.5%) of prescription drugs were removed from the original packaging by adults before the children received them. The domestic "National List of Hazardous Wastes (2025 Edition)" lists waste pharmaceuticals and their packaging produced in daily household life as hazardous wastes in domestic waste. Shanghai’s classification guidelines classify waste pharmaceuticals as hazardous waste. The guidelines state that waste drugs include expired drugs, drug capsules, tablets, and inner drug packaging. "Waste drugs should be put out together with their packaging." Shanghai also stipulates that the market supervision departments in each district will set up temporary transfer points for expired and discarded medicines collected by pharmacies from households. The U.S. FDA says the best way to dispose of expired and unused medicines is to hand them over to recycling centers.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Lovegrove MC, Weidle NJ, Budnitz DS (2015). Trends in Emergency Department Visits for Unsupervised Pediatric Medication Exposures, 2004-2013. Pediatrics, 136(4):e821-e829. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2015-2092>; Agarwal M, Lovegrove MC, Geller RJ, et al. (2020). Circumstances Involved in Unsupervised Solid Dose Medication Exposures among Young Children. Journal of Pediatrics, 219:188-195.e6. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jpeds.2019.12.027>; Ministry of Ecology and Environment et al. (2024). National List of Hazardous Wastes (2025 Edition), Appendix "Hazardous Waste Exemption Management List" Item 1. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_11906/202503/content_7011162.html>; Shanghai Greening and City Appearance Administration (2024). Shanghai Domestic Waste Classification and Disposal Guidelines (2024 Edition) (Shanghai Lvrong [2024] No. 278). <https://www.shanghai.gov.cn/gwk/search/content/40b9feaa-53db-472f-8a6b-2c3cf0465def>; Shanghai Greening and City Appearance Administration, Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau, Shanghai Food and Drug Administration (2018). Notice on standardizing the full management of hazardous waste classification for domestic waste. <https://www.shanghai.gov.cn/nw12344/20200813/0001-12344_57440.html>; U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2025). Where and How to Dispose of Unused Medicines. <https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/where-and-how-dispose-unused-medicines>

Note: The garbage classification catalogs in different places are not exactly the same. The catalog posted in the community garbage room shall prevail. Shanghai classifies traditional Chinese medicine residues as wet waste and does not count as hazardous waste. Keep the remaining medicine in the original box, do not pour it into separate medicine boxes or other bottles, and keep it out of the reach of children. See Section 13, Article 20 (Accidental Ingestion). Don’t take leftover antibiotics at home for your own consumption. See Article 7 (Antibiotics) in this section. When there are no recycling points in the United States, people mix the medicines with coffee grounds and cat litter, then seal the bags and throw them into ordinary garbage. A few powerful painkillers are allowed to be flushed down the toilet. This is the practice in the United States, and domestic products are distributed according to local classification. The reason for setting B is that the numbers in the United States are just registrations, and there is no study to calculate how many times cleaning the medicine cabinet will reduce the number of accidental ingestions. The income is determined to be "small": the number in hand is the number of emergency visits, not deaths, and it cannot be calculated as the effect of cleaning up.

Case: Grandma left the antihypertensive medicine on the coffee table, and her two-year-old grandson mistakenly thought it was candy and ate half of it. He was sent to the doctor for gastric lavage before he was out of danger. Afterwards, the family cleaned up all expired and leftover medicines and threw the packaging into hazardous trash cans, eliminating safety hazards.

items.title: Do not drink alcohol while taking antibacterial drugs such as cephalosporin and metronidazole and within 7 days after stopping the drug, and do not touch alcohol-containing drugs such as Huoxiang Zhengqi water and cough syrup
items.core: Some cephalosporins and metronidazole and other drugs will make people blush, sweat, panic, have severe difficulty breathing, and drop blood pressure. Not only liquor and beer, but also alcohol-containing medicines such as Huoxiang Zhengqi water and cough syrup can cause it. Do not touch it while taking the medicine and for 7 days after stopping the medicine.
body: Cost: No money. Don’t drink alcohol for more than a week. Before taking other medicines, check to see if there is ethanol in the ingredients.

Benefit: This is called a disulfiram-like reaction. The Fujian Provincial Food and Drug Administration’s 2023 safety medication science popularization said that drinking alcohol before and after taking some cephalosporin drugs may trigger this reaction. Kopp said this "can seriously damage health and even endanger life." Symptoms include facial flushing, sweating, palpitations, and even difficulty breathing, decreased blood pressure, and anaphylactic shock. According to popular science, the drugs listed in the "Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China Clinical Medication Instructions" include cefazolin, ceftriaxone, cefoperazone, metronidazole, tinidazole, furazolidone, etc. Popular science states that "it is prohibited to drink alcohol and consume alcohol-containing drugs and food within 7 days after taking the medicine." Examples include wine-filled chocolate and Huoxiang Zhengqi water. The reason is that the enzyme inhibited by the drug often takes 4 to 5 days to recover. A hospital in Guangzhou compiled 82 cases over 2 years. 57 cases (69.51%) were caused by cephalosporins, and 10 cases (12.20%) were caused by nitroimidazole (metronidazole, tinidazole, etc.). Alcohol came from alcoholic beverages in 40 cases (48.78%) and from ethanol-containing medicines in 31 cases (37.80%). Oral medications include Huoxiang Zhengqi water, cough syrup, motherwort extract, etc. Among the 82 cases, 68 were mild, 9 were moderate, and 5 were severe. They resolved within 1 to 3 hours, and there were no deaths. The instructions for metronidazole in the United States require that you do not drink alcohol or use products containing propylene glycol during medication and for at least 3 days after stopping medication.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Fujian Provincial Food and Drug Administration (Fujian Provincial Drug Science Popularization and Supervision Data Center) (2023). Original popular science knowledge for the 2023 "National Safe Medication Month" - Why you can't drink alcohol while taking cephalosporins. <https://yjj.scjgj.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/kpzl/qgaqyyy/202312/t20231215_6334595.htm>; Fang Caifu, Tu Xing, Liu Tao, Huang Hongbing, Qiu Meng, Liang Weiting (2015). Analysis of 82 cases of disulfiram-like reactions in our hospital. Chinese Pharmacy, 26(29):4089-4091. <https://doi.org/10.6039/j.issn.1001-0408.2015.29.19>; Pfizer (2026). FLAGYL 375 (metronidazole) capsules, prescribing information: Contraindications, Interaction with Alcohol. DailyMed. <https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=a2883ca1-5a9a-4259-9d80-46ab67274384>

Note: Not every cephalosporin will be like this, but ordinary people can't tell the difference. It is easiest to do this for whichever type you eat. When the doctor prescribes cephalosporin or metronidazole, take the initiative to ask whether you have drunk alcohol in the past few days. The popular science article recommends not drinking 3 days before taking the medicine, and admits that there is currently no authoritative statement on this interval. Once you feel flushed and flustered, stop drinking alcohol immediately. Popular science says that you can recover on your own in mild cases, but in severe cases you have to be sent to the hospital. Do not drink alcohol while taking acetaminophen, see No. 1 of this section (acetaminophen). The decision is B because the evidence is a collection of cases and instructions without comparison. The benefits are considered "small": all 82 cases recovered within a few hours, no deaths occurred, and only 5 cases were severe. How to look after someone who is drunk, see Section 13, Article 46 (Someone is Drunk).

Case: My uncle took metronidazole due to periodontitis and drank two ounces of white wine at dinner. Ten minutes later, his face turned red, he felt panicked and short of breath, and his blood pressure dropped sharply. He was sent to the hospital for emergency treatment. Doctors remind you not to touch even alcohol-containing Huoxiang Zhengqi water while taking cephalosporins and metronidazole and within 7 days of stopping the drugs.

items.title: If you take cold medicine or anti-allergic medicine containing chlorpheniramine (chlorpheniramine) or diphenhydramine, do not drive, work at heights, or operate machinery while taking the medicine
items.core: Many compound cold medicines are mixed with anti-allergic ingredients such as chlorpheniramine and diphenhydramine, which will make you sleepy after taking them. The State Food and Drug Administration reminds you not to drive, work at heights, or operate machinery while taking this type of medicine. On a driving simulator, people who took diphenhydramine drove worse than those who drank alcohol. Just because you don't feel sleepy doesn't mean you can drive without any problems.
body: Cost: No money. When buying medicine, take a look at the ingredient list. During the days when taking medicine, take a car or take a taxi, or ask a doctor or pharmacist to change the medicine to a medicine that will not make you sleepy.

Income: The 2010 adverse drug reaction information report of the State Food and Drug Administration stated that Vitamin C Yinqiao Tablets contain chlorpheniramine maleate, also called chlorpheniramine. Its main adverse reactions are drowsiness, weakness, drowsiness, and dry mouth. The notice advises doctors and pharmacies to remind patients that they are not allowed to drive machines, cars, or boats, and are not allowed to engage in high-altitude operations, mechanical operations, or operate precision instruments while taking medication. The 2020 public medication reminder from the State Food and Drug Administration states that compound cold medicines contain anti-allergic ingredients such as chlorpheniramine and diphenhydramine, which can make you drowsy. People engaged in driving, operating machinery, and working at heights should use it with caution. A US driving simulator trial looked at 40 drivers aged 25 to 44 with seasonal allergic rhinitis. Each person was given one treatment every other week, prescribed for 1 hour each: diphenhydramine 50 mg, fexofenadine 60 mg, drinking to a blood alcohol concentration of about 0.1%, and placebo. Fexofenadine is a non-drowsy allergy medicine. The ability to keep up with the speed of the car in front was worst after taking diphenhydramine, but was significantly better after drinking alcohol and taking fexofenadine. The ability to stay in lane is impaired after drinking alcohol and taking diphenhydramine. When the car in front suddenly blocks the road, the reaction time is the slowest after drinking alcohol, with an average of 2.21 seconds, and after taking fexofenadine, it is 1.95 seconds. Taking fexofenadine is about the same as taking a placebo. The authors concluded that diphenhydramine affects driving more than alcohol. The driver's self-reported drowsiness level cannot tell whether he is driving well or not, so he cannot rely on "drowsiness or not" to determine whether he can drive.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: State Food and Drug Administration (2010). Adverse Drug Reaction Information Notice (Issue 32) focuses on the safety issues of the Chinese and Western medicine compound preparation Vitamin C Yinqiao Tablets. <https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/xxgk/yjjsh/ypblfytb/20100919162601498.html>; State Food and Drug Administration (2020). The top ten medication tips for the public in 2020丨 (3) Caution is required when using cold medications, and safety and rationality are key. <https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/xxgk/kpzhsh/kpzhshyp/20201111095256170.html>; Weiler JM, Bloomfield JR, Woodworth GG, et al. (2000). Effects of fexofenadine, diphenhydramine, and alcohol on driving performance. A randomized, placebo-controlled trial in the Iowa driving simulator. Annals of Internal Medicine, 132(5):354-363. <https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-132-5-200003070-00004>; Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (2021 Year revised) Article 22, Paragraph 2. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab231eb017abd617ef70519>

Note: The phenanfenamine, compound acetaminophen, and acetaminophen named by the Food and Drug Administration all contain chlorpheniramine. Please read the ingredient list before buying. What is expressly prohibited by the Road Traffic Safety Law is driving after taking state-controlled psychotropic drugs or narcotic drugs. Common cold medicine and anti-allergy medicine are not included, and the prohibition on driving is written in the instructions and reminders from the Food and Drug Administration. If you have to eat and drive, ask your doctor or pharmacist to change the medicine to one that will not make you sleepy. Many of these cold medicines also contain acetaminophen, see No. 1 of this section (acetaminophen). See Section 1, Item 9 (Stop and rest when you are sleepy) for other risks of driving while sleepy. The B was assigned because there was only one simulator trial with 40 people and no accident figures on real roads. The income is determined to be "small": the end point is the driving performance in the simulator, not accidents and deaths. In addition to yourself, the beneficiaries include your family members and other people on the road.

Case: Chen, an office worker, took a compound cold medicine containing chlorpheniramine after catching a cold. He consciously woke up and drove to work the next morning. On the way, he reacted slowly and rear-ended the car in front of him. A physical examination showed that his driving state was equivalent to drunk driving.

items.title: If you take drugs such as lipid-lowering drugs and antihypertensive drugs for a long time, first check whether grapefruit (grapefruit) is mentioned in the instructions. If it is written, do not eat grapefruit and pomelo, and do not drink grapefruit juice
items.core: Grapefruit will cause some drugs to rise several times in the blood. If the amount you eat does not change, it means you have eaten too much. One grapefruit or a cup of grapefruit juice has this effect, and if you take the medicine the next day, some of it will still be left. In severe cases, it may damage muscles, kidneys, or cause arrhythmia that may lead to sudden death. Grapefruit also has this effect, but ordinary sweet oranges do not.
body: Cost: Nothing. When you get a medicine that you want to take for a long time, read the "Drug Interactions" and "Precautions" in the instructions. For those who wrote about grapefruit, do not eat grapefruit, grapefruit, lime, lime, or drink their juice while taking the medicine. If you like to eat grapefruit, you can ask your doctor if he can change his medicine to one that will not affect it.

Benefits: A 2013 review by Canadian Pharmacologists said more than 85 drugs are known or expected to interact with grapefruit. 43 of these may cause serious adverse reactions. Severe reactions include torsade de pointes, a heart rhythm disorder that may lead to sudden death. There is also rhabdomyolysis (massive muscle destruction, which can damage the kidneys), bone marrow suppression, respiratory depression, gastrointestinal bleeding and kidney damage. The furanocoumarins in grapefruit bind tightly to an enzyme (CYP3A4) that breaks down drugs in the intestinal wall cells of the small intestine, rendering it permanently ineffective. The effect will wear off until the body re-creates new enzymes. Before oral medicine enters the blood, part of it is broken down in the small intestine and liver. This is called the first-pass effect. The enzymes in the small intestine are inactive, and less is broken down in this step, so more medicine enters the blood. One whole grapefruit or 200 ml of juice is enough to increase blood levels to clinically significant levels. When the antihypertensive drug felodipine is mixed with a portion of grapefruit, the amount of the drug in the blood is on average 3 times that of when mixed with plain water. Drinking the same 250 ml of juice varies from 0 to 8 times for different people. When the lipid-lowering drug simvastatin was mixed with juice at 200 ml per day for 3 days, the total blood drug content (AUC) was 330% of that when mixed with plain water. Atorvastatin with juice is 180% to 250%. Pravastatin, rosuvastatin and fluvastatin were not affected. Drink 200 ml of juice within 4 hours before taking the medicine for the greatest benefit. Half of it is left after 10 hours, and a quarter is left after 24 hours. Reviews say limes (commonly used to make orange marmalade), limes and grapefruits also work in the same way. Sweet oranges such as navel oranges and Volencia oranges do not contain furanocoumarins and do not have this effect. The US FDA's popular science named simvastatin, atorvastatin and nifedipine. It says that when you drink a lot of grapefruit juice, too much of the lipid-lowering drug is retained in the body, which increases the risk of liver and muscle damage, possibly leading to kidney failure.
Level of Evidence: B

Source: Bailey DG, Dresser G, Arnold JMO (2013). Grapefruit–medication interactions: forbidden fruit or avoidable consequences? CMAJ, 185(4):309-316. <https://doi.org/10.1503/cmaj.120951>; U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2021). Grapefruit Juice and Some Drugs Don't Mix. <https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/grapefruit-juice-and-some-drugs-dont-mix>

Note: Not all drugs are affected, and some drugs in the same category are affected. Among the commonly used drugs listed in that review are the lipid-lowering drugs simvastatin, lovastatin, and atorvastatin, and the antihypertensive drugs felodipine and nifedipine. There are also amiodarone, ticagrelor, tacrolimus, cyclosporine, domperidone, quetiapine, oxycodone, etc. Clopidogrel, on the other hand, will not work when exposed to grapefruit. If the instructions are not written and you are not sure, ask the doctor or pharmacist who prescribed the medicine. The review said people over 45 buy the most grapefruit and take the most medicine. When older people take felodipine and grapefruit, their heartbeat will speed up when their blood pressure drops. The number B is determined because the numbers come from pharmacokinetic tests that look at blood drug concentrations, and there are only case reports of serious consequences. The profit is determined to be "small": the end point is blood drug concentration, and research cannot tell how many accidents can be avoided.

Case: Li, a hypertensive patient, has been taking lipid-lowering drugs on time for a long time, and his physical examination indicators have always been normal. Recently, I drank a glass of grapefruit juice for breakfast every day. After a few days, my muscles all over my body ached and my urine turned brown. I went to the doctor and was diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis caused by drug accumulation.

items.title: People with chronic kidney disease or poor kidney function should not buy painkillers such as ibuprofen for long-term use. Ask a doctor first, and do not eat carambola and carambola juice.
items.core: People with poor kidneys are more likely to suffer from acute kidney injury if they take painkillers such as ibuprofen. Long-term consumption of painkillers by themselves is also related to kidney failure. For people taking diuretics plus sulfate or satan antihypertensive drugs, the risk of acute kidney injury is about 30%. People with poor kidneys may suffer from hiccups, confusion, and convulsions after eating star fruit. About 30% of reported cases of such poisoning have resulted in death.
body: Cost: No money. Ask your doctor or pharmacist before buying painkillers. If you are taking diuretics and antihypertensive drugs such as Prilim and Sartan, you should take the initiative to tell them. Do not touch the carambola or carambola juice.

Benefits: This type of analgesic is called nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and the common ones are ibuprofen, naproxen, and diclofenac. Acute kidney injury occurs when kidney function suddenly deteriorates within a few days. A systematic review summarized studies that only followed records and did not group groups in community populations. Among the general population taking these drugs, the odds ratio for acute kidney injury was OR 1.73 (95% CI 1.44–2.07). The odds ratios were slightly higher for people over 50 years old. Write an OR of 2.51 for the abstract, and an OR of 2.01 for the group analysis of the main text and Figure 4. The 95% CI is 1.52–2.68 in both places, and the original article is inconsistent. In people with pre-existing chronic kidney disease, the OR across 5 studies combined was 1.63 (1.22–2.19). The authors say that none of the studies gave an original incidence rate, so the absolute risk cannot be calculated. A British study followed 487,372 people taking blood pressure medication for an average of 5.9 years. Take diuretics plus Prix or Sartan antihypertensive drugs, plus these kinds of painkillers. Take the three together. When the three items were eaten together, the incidence rate of acute kidney injury was approximately 31% higher, 1.31 (95% CI 1.12–1.53). The highest incidence rate was found in the first 30 days when the three items were eaten together, with an incidence rate ratio of 1.82 (1.35–2.46). It was just a combination of antihypertensive drugs and painkillers, and no increased risk was seen. KDIGO's 2024 Chronic Kidney Disease Guidelines say people with chronic kidney disease may be more susceptible to kidney damage from medications. Practice Point 4.1.3 of the Guidelines requires that over-the-counter drugs and herbal medicines that may damage the kidneys be checked and limited. The guidelines state that indiscriminate long-term self-purchasing of such medicines is associated with a higher risk of kidney failure and should be discouraged. U.S. regulations require labels on such over-the-counter drugs to state: People with high blood pressure, heart disease, liver cirrhosis or kidney disease should ask their doctor before taking diuretics. The evidence for star fruit is a summary of cases. One review included 126 patients in 33 reports from 1993 to 2016. The most common symptom is persistent hiccups, occurring in 65% of cases. Delirium and convulsions are most often associated with death. No one with normal kidney function died. 36% of patients with chronic renal insufficiency who had not yet been on dialysis died, and 27% of dialysis patients died. People with normal kidney function ate much more star fruits when they had an accident. Another review included 136 patients, 69.1% of whom had poor renal function.
